product_title: Heng Long 3819 German Panther Tank (6mm Shooter) Scale 1:16 R/c
review_headline: The "value" offering in the Heng Long tank line
review_body: This is an "entry level" model in the Heng Long tank series.  But not a heavily stripped down one.  It includes many of the features of the more expensive Heng Long tanks, including engine, cannon and machine gun sounds, an operating main gun that can be remotely elevated and lowered and which shoots plastic pellets, a turret that can be remotely rotated , variable speed control and engine smoke.  That's the good news.  The tradeoffs for the lower price are slightly less detail on the model (molded as opposed to operating driver and radio operator hatches and muzzle brace) and the entry level drive train, which is plastic tracks and drive gearboxes with nylon as opposed to metal gears and drive sprockets.  If one wants to make the investment and doesn't mind doing some straightforward disassembly and replacement modifications, upgrade metal gear drive units and metal tracks are readily available for this tank.  I recommend adding the metal gear drive, it does make an improvement in operation and is doesn't strip as readily as the plastic gears do.  Heng Long enthusiasts tend to split on whether upgrading to metal tracks is worth the cost.  Some say they give the model tanks a more realistic feel when running, but others state metal tracks are much more likely to "skip" out the teeth of the drive sprocket.  I have stuck with the plastic tracks (which are not a molded strip but actually have realistic individual links) and find they work fine and haven't worn in use.  The one other element of all Heng Long tanks that tends to be problematic -- and which can only be permanently fixed by doing some modifications -- are the engine exhaust smoke units.  The stock ones employ a cotton wick and a very thin heating element, which create smoke when oil that comes with the tank is heated and fed out of the tank exhausts.  The problem with this system is twofold; the smoke created comes out in small unrealistic wisps and the combustible wick and lightweight heating element don't hold up very well, usually starting to disintegrate after just 3-4 uses.  The aforementioned somewhat  involved fix for this requires opening up the tank, removing the smoke unit and then modifying it by replacing the heating element with a 15 ohm  wirewound resistor,  the cotton wick with one made from Kevlar and adding a small 25mm fan to boost the smoke output.  That results in a reliable system that produces realistic volumes of chugging exhaust.  Lastly, this operating model can be vastly improved by "weathering" the exterior.  Real tanks that are in service end up coated with soil, soot, etc.  Some time spent using washes and drybrushing  to "dirty up" this tank (as shown in the attached photo) turn it from a somewhat toy-like unit into a realistic operating  model.

I bought this for my 4 year old daughter's birthday....she LOVES it! She and my older daughter love watching Teen Titans Go! and my four year old's favorite character is Raven, of course. review_body: Great introduction to the concept of Monopoly for younger kids. I bought this for my niece who was turning 5. I thought it might be too complicated to hold her interest long enough, but I played it with her and her 7 year old sister, and we managed to finish a whole game, which is pretty good. It is an extremely simplified version of the game: 3 players, only $1 bills (it get a little annoying counting out $20, but it's great for younger kids who understand counting but not necessarily math), no houses/hotels or anything like that. I feel I should point out that the cards have a lot of reading for the younger ones of the 5+ recommended age group....a group of 5 year olds might have problems playing without an adult or older kid.  I found it fun playing with the kids, though; as much as I am over the whole "Frozen" thing, it has enough elements of the adult game to make it more interesting for an adult to play than a lot of other kids' games out there.

product_title: ParkZone Sport Cub BNF Airplane
review_body:
Great, stable flyer. Only problem is that the included battery velcro came loose on my ~12th flight and the battery literally fell out of the plane. The foam at the nose completely broke off from the crash, however $5 worth of CA glue made the plane good as new. If foam breaks, remove electronics and soak broken parts in boiling water. Doing so will remove wrinkles (and slightly discolor the foam). Toothpicks also help to keep the glued pieces together while drying. I'm very happy with the propeller as it did not snap or bend when the plane crashed.

This plane flies great in less than 10mph wind and is easy to take off from the ground or by throwing it. However, taking off or landing on grass is kind of a problem as the plane flips over 4 out of 5 times on landings and every time on takeoff. This plane handles wind MUCH better than the smaller ~$100 planes (which crash at even the slightest gust of wind). Overall, this is a great plane. You must get extra batteries and a better charger if you plan to fly it often. The included charger (at least the one I got) only works with 12v car plugs. I tried getting a wall adapter but there are none that supply enough current (Amps). Get a 2/3 cell Dynamite charger for way better results and charge times.

product_title: Dxhycc 6pcs Temporary Fake Slip on Tattoo Arm Sleeves Stockings
review_body:
First, I received these sleeves free for the purpose of review. Hopefully my impressions and observations prove helpful to you in your decision making. If you have questions, feel free to post them in the comments section and I'll do my best to answer based on my own experience with the product.

What you're getting with this order:
(6) Tattoo Arm sleeves

What are these, and what are they supposed to do?:
These are flesh colored arm sleeves with realistic looking tattoo designs that when worn, are supposed to look like actual, full sleeve tattoos. Each order comes with 6 different tattoo designs. It should be noted that some of the designs, like some tattoos, are fairly racy, containing nudity.

Do they work?:
Yes and no. They actually do look pretty real, but this will depend some on your actual skin tone. The length is appropriate for a realistic looking sleeve, and once on it does make for an interesting conversation piece. However, they lack in two areas. First, they are very thin and thus they tear quite easily. The second time I donned one of the sleeves I put a huge run in it from end to end. Second, they are of a uniform size from end to end, meaning there is no adjustment for the upper arm. If you have very small and/or skinny arms these will be perfect. I'm of a normal build, and these are very difficult to bring over the upper arm without ruining them. They have to be pulled on slowly and gently and even then damage is likely.

Bottom line: These look quite realistic but being composed of ultra thin material and being of one uniform size thus not accommodating the increasing size of the upper arm, they end up being very fragile. They are inexpensive and if you need them for just one or two uses they might be what you're looking for. For me, they are a fun idea but simply don't fit and are too easily damaged.

product_title: Survive Escape From Atlantis 30th Anniversary Edition
review_headline: Great casual game with a good variety of gameplay
review_body:
This is our current favorite game! I like games where you feel that your strategy effects the outcome of the game. It's also good for a game to have some luck so that people of different levels can play and the outcome won't only be decided by strategy. I also like that a lot of the "luck" is actually other player choices. There is very little cooperative gameplay and there's no trading/collecting. It's all about getting the most of your men safe from a sinking Atlantis!

The game in a nutshell is one where you save your people, and depending on which people you save will give you a total score that you try to beat everyone else's total score. You can play with two people, but it's really a 3-4 player game (5-6 expansion available but I've not tried it). The goal is to escape a sinking island across the sea to the other islands at the 4 corners of the board. Every turn you get three movements to try and get some of your 10 people to safety. Also every turn you remove one of 40 land tiles. First you remove the sand, then the forest, and then the rock tiles. One of the 8 rock tiles has the volcano which ends the game. Once the game ends, everyone on Atlantis or in the ocean dies and you count up your tiles. Oh, and beware, there are whales, sea creatures and sharks in the water!

Pros:
-There's variety in the gameplay. Every turn you have up to five things to do and there is a different starting gameplay. You may be able to use a tile from previous gameplay, you get to move your people, you get to take a land tile from the board, you may be able to use that tile immediately, and finally you get to roll a die which lets you move a monster. For as simple a game as it is, there is some real variety in what you're doing! And there's not a single mechanic I dislike.
-You can surprise yourself! Each of your people has a different point value from 1-6 on their feet. You only look at the feet at the beginning of the game. If you don't keep track of where what point value is, you may have to wait to the end of the game to see what your score is! Nobody other than you knows the point values at all, so they have no idea how many points they need to beat you! Don't tell my wife, but I turn the biggest point value sideways...
-The end of the game has some randomness. Everybody knows the volcano end game tile is somewhere in the rocky ground. But it could be the first rock turned or it could be the last! That add some tension when you get to the rock tiles, and knowing there is an end coming keeps you from playing too defensive of a game.

Cons:
-It's possible to know you will lose halfway into the game and have to keep playing. You could lose your highest scoring people or even lose all of your people. Then you are supposed to keep playing till the end.
-There are a lot of mechanics that encourage revenge play. The players could all gang up against someone too. You can certainly play fair, but there's no mechanic to discourage these tactics.
-There are green tiles you can play immediately and red tiles you play your next turn. If you look carefully at the edge of the face down land tiles you can tell whether you're grabbing a green or red tile. I wish the very edge of the bottom of every tile was black so you couldn't tell them apart.

We love this game! The adults have played it regularly and the 8 year old son picked up immediately. I'm not sure if the six year old daughter gets it, but I didn't really expect her to. product_title: Marvel Avengers Age of Ultron Titan Hero Tech Thor 12 Inch Figure(Discontinued by manufacturer)
review_body:
If you are a regular reader of my reviews, you already know that my son and I have collected a number of the Titan Hero series figures from Hasbro. They all have at least five points of articulation, but in the case of Thor, he features seven total POA (head, shoulders, hips, and wrists). They usually feature just one (if any) accessories and in the case of Thor, Mjolnir is right at his side. The hammer is a cool accessory, but much like the recent Titan Hero Series figures of Star Lord and Rocket Raccoon, Thor has a hard time holding Mjolnir properly in his hand. Since this figure will primarily be a display figure (he's mine, I claimed him from my son, haha), that isn't too much of a problem.

Thor comes with a cloth cape which is nice. I'm not a very big fan of vinyl capes on larger figures, and I'm really glad that Thor got the cloth treatment with this figure. While it may not flow in the wind, it definitely looks good on the God of Thunder's back.

What sets the Titan Hero Tech series apart from the regular Titan figures is the added component of the figures talking and (at least in the case of the Age of Ultron figures) interacting with the Hulk Buster figure. Thor says multiple phrases in a voice that attempts (but fails) to sound like Chris Hemsworth. The phrases are cool and my son and I both enjoy them.

Overall, this is a pretty cool figure. I do plan on getting a few more of these figures in the future. I knocked off a star for the limited articulation on the head of the figure (hampered by Thor's golden locks) and the poor-fitting Mjolnir in Thor's hand. Other than those two setbacks, this figure is cool.

product_title: Concept Board Game
review_headline: Fun game that's better without scoring
review_body:
Have played this with a few different groups and find this works well with both experienced and casual gamers. During the game you'll identify key themes by placing colored exclamation marks onto various pictures on the board and sub-themes related to the key themes by similar colored cubes (also using the pictures on the board). You can use the cards provided or do as we often do and think up your own person, place, or thing.

Couple things we've added that aren't in the rules:
- a timer (usually set it to 5 minutes) to help prevent turns from taking too long
- eliminate scoring - found this game to be as enjoyable (maybe more so) without keeping track of score
- get rid of the reference sheets - found this helps speed things up and encourages creative thinking

If you're looking for a party game that plays well with a variety of people, definitely recommend this one. It's fun even when you fail as you get to see what the persons thought process was. Play around with the rules to find what works best for you. The less you restrict yourself with them, the more fun you'll have with this one.

review_body:
This game is incredibly complicated and really fun. There are a lot of different things going on, with the gears to put your guys on to wait for specific roles, then the resources to gather, the things to purchase, and the different abilities of the possible characters. There's no way to play exactly the same game twice. The gear mechanism is really inventive and adds a lot of mystery to the outcome.
I did paint my gears, because the light beige plastic that comes in the box isn't interesting to look at. I didn't have the patience for all of the detail that you can see in the user photos, but I still get compliments when we take it to a game party.
I've never won, because my husband is so good at keeping track of multiple goals and getting the resources just in time to buy the ability to build the better thing, but I love it anyway.

product_title: ERTL  Plymouth Prowler With Trailer Model Kit
review_body:
I received my AMT/ERTL (Racing Champions) #8588 Plymouth Prowler with Trailer today. It's been a long time since I've seen "Racing Champions" on model kit instructions.
Here is the pre-build kit review.
About 130 parts total, the 18 piece V-6 (I've never built a V6 before) seems straightforward with paint callouts for flat, gloss and semi gloss colors. The gray plastic parts are all in one bag except for the body which is bagged by itself. I don't see any flash on any parts.
There are 17 chrome parts bagged seperately. The body is bagged separately also and the engraving looks good.
I didn't see any ejection pin marks in bad places so there shouldn't be any filling required.
The rubber tires look great with the "Goodyear" raised letters and other tire lettering appearing sharp. I don't see any mold seam around the middle of the tire which will make it nice to not need to sand the tires other than lightly.
12 clear parts bagged separately also have no flash.
The strangest thing in this kit to me is the removable roof molded in clear. I can't say I've ever seen this before. Anyway, it has a nice "woven" pattern molded into it on the top which shoul still show under a light coat of paint.
A decal sheet with four sets of license plates and a chrome sticker sheet with die-cut two side mirrors and the interior mirror.
I paid $10.87 including shipping so I think I got another great deal from amazon. It has to take it's place in line and wait to be built.
I'll gladly take any comments from anybody who has built this kit. As for painting, I was strongly considering on giving it a "Harley-Davidson" paint job with silver on the lower and black on the upper body.'

POST ASSEMBLY REVIEW: The body is painted Model Master Sublime Green and the interior is Tamiya SF56 Metallic Gray with sublime green inserts on the door panels, seats and dash highlights. I detailed this model very similar to a picture I found on the internet only in a different color.
The engine is all Tamiya X18 semi-gloss black, XF1 flat black and Model Master sublime green.
This kit was the biggest P.I.T.A. that I have worked on in a long, long time. The engine went together without issue. The tires are well molded and have rotation markings on them. Attention must be made when assembling them to the chassis as the inner rings are different sizes. The trailer rims will not fit the car even though they are very close.
If you get this kit, check the straightness of the frame before you start. My frame, at the rear was twisted and, I found out at the assembly step of joining the body to the frame, the frame was at least 3/8" too low to mate with the body. My only option here was to break out the super glue and squeeze. I did hit the super glue with some baking soda to harden it and after three hours, it's still in place so I think it's a success.
The front bezels that hold the chrome headlight insert - the insert would not allow the bezel to sit in place correctly so a lot of sanding of the chrome back and the body frame were needed on both sides.
The steering was supposed to be positionable but because of parts not aligning properly they requred super glue to hold in securely.
The trailer body and top did not match but doesn't look that bad.
The windshield is a clear part in it's own bag and was detailed with Tamiya semi-gloss black.
The hood is a one-piece removable unit. No hinges are inculded. I needed to modify the areas where the four tabs on the hood hold it in place for it to sit properly.
The strangest part of this whole kit was why they molded the convertible roof in clear. I chose not to use this at this time so the interior can be seen but I may use it at a later date.
Overall, this kit needs a lot of reworking and patience. It looks great sitting on my shelf (I'm now out of display space) and after all the twisting, badwords and more twisting, it sits on all fours.
As always, any comments and criticisms are welcome.
I don't know why the pictures seem like two different colors. Tomorrow it will get a coat or two of Future and be considered finished.﻿words and more twisting, it sits on all fours.

product_title: Butterflies Mini Triangular Puzzle
review_headline: How difficult could it be ,all the same size and shape,give it a try.
review_body:
This is a great little puzzle.At the low price ,it certainly serves the purpose of a party favour.Somewhat like a mini Jigsaw puzzle,but a much greater challenge than first appears.There are 9 triangular pieces,all the same size and all have straight edges.All one has to do is fit them together in a large triangle,making sure all the pieces match.It seems to go pretty fast, 'till all of once, the pieces don't match.The pieces are well made and will stand lots of use.this puzzle is so small ,it can easily fit in a pocket and be used in a plane or otherwise waiting.It is small enough to fit on a tray or any table surface.It comes as a Butterfly SeriesThe one shown here has white,gold and black butterflies,called Hebomoia Glaucippe..On any puzzle all the butterflies are the same.I have one with blue and gold butterflies,called Prepona Buckleyana and another with green and yellow butterflies called Ornithoptera Goliath.
This puzzle is a miniature version of similar puzzles called Triazzle which consist of 9 triangles and when assembled result in a larger triangle 4 " high by 5' at the base.I did a Review for one called "JurassicTravel Triazzle" on Aug 13,2014,but there are other designs..There is also another version called "Scramble Squares" they consist of 9 squares and when complete make as 12" X12" square.I did a Review for one called "Scramble Squares Hockey" on Dec 22,2014 and there are many other designs.
All these type of puzzles seem easy to do,but it takes lots of patience and there is only one correct solution.
It would be great entertainment at a social gathering to give each person one,and see who could complete theirs first.

product_title: Swing-N-Slide Sherwood Playset
review_body:
Great playset for the price. My girls absolutely love it. It did take quite a bit of time to assemble mainly because there are so many pieces. The 100+ pieces of wood come in, I believe, 6 different boxes and you have to hunt through to find the required piece for the step you are on. For me that was the most frustrating part. In hindsight, I probably should have sorted all of the pieces before beginning, but we were ready to jump right in. All pieces fit perfectly, I was impressed.

I was impressed by the quality of the materials and the instructions were great as well.

My only knock (aside from hunting for pieces) is the roof. The roof is made of canvas and I imagine in a few years I will need to replace it with wood. Also, it was a pain in the neck to get on, although not impossible. It required quite a bit of pulling to get into a position for securing, but that could be due to the guy doing the assembling (this guy) not securing the eaves correctly or the tower not being perfectly square. Nevertheless it is assembled...

All things considered, this is a fantastic swingset that I would absolutely recommend! My girls love it, to me that's all that matters.

It scratches soooooo easily.  I can tell all the "appliances" are gonna be really scratched up a week or so after my daughter gets her hands on this.  There's already quite a few from when I was putting this together.  I'll probably just take the doors off and spray paint them in the future to remedy this problem though.  There's also the matter of the pegs against the backsplash.  I wasn't able to tighten the screws enough to where they don't move, I'm hoping that they don't come off easily. product_title: Indian Sport Scout Motorcycle 1-12 Testors
review_headline: Good looking when completed, frustrating piece of crap when building.
review_body:
First off, let me say that the finished model looks very good - not perfect, certainly not as good as a carefully-detailed kit requiring more builder input, but better than the average toy. Good thing, too, because the looks are the only thing saving this poorly-conceived kit from getting only a single star.

This Testor kit has the worst build quality I have ever seen in a "quick build" model. Pre-set screws need to be loosened to adjust part alignment, parts like the headlight had to be disassembled, realigned, and retightened because they weren't in the right place right out of the box, and absolutely NOTHING lined up in the rear end on the first try. I've been building models for over 40 years and there is no way I would have rated this model as a skill level 1. Any kid putting this together as a beginner's kit would have given up in frustration. The fit of the handlebar/front fork assembly is so crappy that this step, near the beginning on the instruction sheet, needs to be done last to prevent the front end from falling off repeatedly while the builder struggles with the ridiculously difficult rear tire placement.

The instruction sheet is brilliantly stupid as well. Completely devoid of any text, the tiny smudgedly-printed illustrations are hard to read and difficult to decypher. Seriously - by the time you're done putting together this "quick build" model you will have invested at least two hours and a lot of colorful vocabulary.

product_title: Hubsan X4 H107C 4 Channel 2.4GHz RC Quad Copter with Camera - Green/Black
review_headline: Was fantastic, then stopped recording after one video!
review_body: Updated: I went from a 5-star to a 3-star overnight! I got it to record the first time I tried and then it stopped working each time thereafter. I'm returning and debating whether I should try another one or look for better quality.   I am amazed at the value for the price. You should buy a micro schd card and the associated card reader (total of about $30-40) with the drone. It takes a while to get used to flying just to operate at a beginner level, but that likely comes with r/c flight regardless of the device.  I'm using this as a training tool and may get something more advanced. For now, I'm really happy with the quality of this hand-sized thing. It flies well and is extremely responsive (so be careful with the remote). The video quality is standard def at best, but it's still pretty cool to see from the drone's perspective. Short flight time (5-8 minutes) but there may be an extended-life battery available.  All in all, a great purchase. I've actually recommended it to friends already and will be taking to Iceland in a few weeks in hopes of getting some aerial footage of the sights.  Hope this helps!

product_title: 1:12 BMW F650GS Diecast Motorcycle Bike Model Toy New in Box Black Color
review_headline: Fine F650GS model, too delicate for rough play.
review_body:
This BMW F650GS Model by Automax is not a bad rendition of the bike. It provides some fine details of the bike and even includes some functional components like a working sidestand, centerstand, steering, rolling wheels, and even a working rear suspension!

Many of the components are rather delicate, however, and I would not recommend this as a toy as it wouldn't last too long under rough play. The mirrors, handlebars, stands fender and tail section are flimsy.

The finish is clean and sharp, it shows a detailed and accurate instrument cluster, and some good engine details.

While I think the Maisto branded models are a little higher quality, and come packaged with better protection, the Automax versions aren't too bad. I've had Automax models not survive shipping in their packages in part because the bits hanging off like mirrors and turn signals are very delicate, and the boxes are poorly designed. I've knocked off one star for this.

product_title: Square Enix Devil May Cry 3: Play Arts Kai Dante Action Figure
review_body:
Upon opening the box, I noticed right off the bat that the container holding the figure was opened at the top. I excused this for poor taping until I opened the flap and saw that one arm of Dantes was about a half inch longer than the other was while in packaging.

When taking the figure out, I noticed the longer arm was in fact a misaligned ball joint that cannot be moved or 'popped' back into place as I at first thought it could. Fidgeting with it a bit, the entire thing popped off. Although it went back in, the arm has limited mobility when it comes to posing and will occasionally come off on its own.

The feet of the figure has two swivels at the feet area for better posing, however one of these seems to be glued shut tightly with paint, while the other had to be forcefully turned to break it free.

Onto the better things about Dante.

The sculpt itself is very on point. The face makes him look young, albeit a bit serious (There were many parts in the game when things would turn into a serious matter, especially after Dantes' sleeve was ripped).

The jacket itself is a very nice crimson color, with an immense amount of detail. The same could be said about Dantes' abs, which looks chiseled and ultra-realistic (including belly button!)

Posability (minus the defunct arm on mine) is a pretty good range. There are joints located in the chest and waist area for bending naturally, and the joints in the ankles make it easier for him to stay upright.

Overall, this figure could've be given a five star rating, if only Play Arts Kai would crack down on their poor quality control. No one likes playing Russian Roulette with fairly pricey figures.

product_title: Magic The Gathering Commander 2014 Built from Scratch Deck
review_body:
I've had a very good time playing this deck. Red, for the most part, has been the worst commander deck due to various reason. This deck doesn't necessarily fix those holes, but it get around it by really being an artifact deck in the flavor of red. It takes a bit of practice to get the hang of how the deck plays, but the main jist of it is get artifacts into your graveyard, pull artifacts out of your graveyard and into play. I'm sure after making some upgrades, this deck will be amazing. There are some cards that are just filler and need to be replaced (like the handful of artifacts that don't do anything while coming into play or leaving, which is what this deck does... a lot).

Power ranking with the other 2014 decks, I'd place this one above Blue and behind White and on par or just slightly better than Green. I (nor none of my buddies) have the Black deck yet, so I can't compare it there.

product_title: Gund Grumpy Cat Plush Stuffed Animal Toy
review_headline: Grumpy Cat is everything and more than you hoped she would be....
review_body: It was with a bit of trepidation that I ordered Grumpy Cat for my 13 year old daughter. I had read the reviews and was concerned with the size, quality and condition of the product.  Well someone has listened to previous complaints. Grumpy Cat did not arrive shriveled up in shrink wrap. Nope! She was wrapped in an oversized ziplock bag that protected her from the elements yet still allowed her fur to lay naturally, then tucked into a secure envelope and placed in my mailbox to enjoy her last moments of peace before my daughter got her hands on her. Her size is purr-fection. She is the exact right size to nuzzle her head in the crook of my daughter's neck while sleeping and still leave ample body, legs and tail for cuddling throughout the night. She is actually the size of one of my full grown cats but doesn't shed all over my daughter's face in the night. It is hard to believe that a toy could have 'fur' that is this soft but she really does. I think the most amazing thing about Grumpy Cat is her eyes. Now, when I read previous reviews I thought they were going overboard on his point. Then, my daughter's Grumpy Cat arrived. It is unbelievable. They are so clear, so expressive, so calming and so darn cute! The more she is loved on by my daughter, the cuter and more expressive she becomes. It's as if she has this scowl that says 'leave me alone' but these eyes that say 'I'm here for you'. This is a STUFFED TOY I'm talking about as though it has the capacity for compassion and understanding!!! How totally bizarre is that!?! I would never have believed it, especially not from a product review, but that's just how amazingly well designed she is. I am including some photos with my review. Please note: these photos come no where near doing justice to the real thing and, I had to practically pry her out of my daughter's hands to take the photos so she appears a bit more 'loved on' then she normally would!

I bought this to use with my 2-almost-3-year-old with transitions and speeding up time on the toilet, brushing teeth, cleaning up, etc. I love the alert!

product_title: Red Dragon Inn 3
review_headline: The most interesting decks of all RDI -- secondary deck mechanics for everyone!
review_body:
RDI3 is my favorite complete deck set out of all the current RDIs (5 is not yet out). Each character is varied, possesses a secondary deck mechanic, and is well rounded. Unlike many of the other decks where one or more characters may feel underpowered, all four of these characters are fully flushed out. That said, I would not recommend this set for brand new players to RDI. The secondary decks may confuse users and blur core mechanics. Best for already-playing-RDI folks.

Character reviews:

Phrenk - Potions Master! He not only has a wide variety of potions, an interesting deck that has strong gambling abilities, heals and offense, his secondary Potions deck is as varied. It has heals, spikes, hit cards... and more than that, these cards can be sold to other players for Gold. Phrenk is fun, and a regular pick in our group.

Wizgelle - One of my all time favorite RDI decks. Wizgelle is a Critical Hit/Critical Miss character. As long as you're not afraid of wild cards, she's enormously fun to play. The majority of her cards require the use of a "Gear" card, which will change the affect of the card played. This can be really good or really bad. But that's part of the fun for me.

Kaylin - Probably the least super powered of this group, since she can have whole rounds (until her next turn) under the effect of a negative Wulfric card. Kaylin's secondary mechanic is a pet wolf deck, which gives a status buff for the duration of one round. Sometimes this is awesome, sometimes this is not awesome. She's also not super well versed in managing gold compared to the rest of the cast. But she is lots of fun, and has a card that lets her sit out an entire round (very strong when played at the right time).

Now.... Serena.
After playing with this deck for several years, my friends and I have a house rule--- we generally don't play Serena, because she is seriously overpowered. Serena players are generally ganged up on as a result (most often surviving anyway) which is a negative experience for everyone playing.

Why is Serena OP? Her Piety mechanic allows her to gain a scale of increasing/decreasing benefits from her cards depending on which side of the meter you're on. Most of her cards affect her Piety, either gaining or decreasing it. The problem is, I quickly figured out that it was not only very easy, but very advantageous to simply stay at max (8) Piety. Staying at 8 lets you use an incredibly large number of healing cards at their substantial benefit of 3 or higher. A smart player can literally go from near death to almost full HP, and such moves are completely within the card rules. In fact, a new Ally that came out (Brother Bastian) makes for some seriously long game play when Serena and he are both on board, if Bastian has enough luck to have received all of his prayer heals. Another house rule we have--- Serena and Bastian are not allowed in the same game.

To sum up everything.... If you're on the fence about RDI3, don't be. This is by far my favorite edition. The extra mechanics add a lot of value and fun for long time players. :)

product_title: Bruder Toys Man Garbage Truck Rear Loading Green
review_headline: High Quality Toy and Impressive Detail
review_body:
I purchased this Bruder garbage truck for my 4 year old nephew who is obsessed with garbage trucks. As with most toys, it is often difficult to tell exactly what you are getting based on images online, but this turned out to be exactly what he wanted. The truck is about 18 inches long, has significant detailing, and appears to be made of sturdy (the sellers keep saying ABS) plastic. The wheels are a denser plastic that feels like more like rubber. in the back is a small handle a child can turn which then turns two screw drives that force "waste" into the back of the garbage truck. Two cans are included and the rear gate can be lifted to dump their contents into the back. In addition, the back opens to allow access, the whole back end tilts up to dump all the waste, and the cab even tilts to expose the plastic "engine." The effect is a realistic looking garbage truck that seems tough enough for younger children, but with enough detail to make it much ore interesting than the clunky-chunky cheap stuff you find at most big-name department stores.

My nephew opened this and went BANANAS. He loves garbage trucks and this was clearly the coolest one he'd ever seen. :-) I was a little shy about the price, but must admit when my sister texted a photo of him asleep that night with the garbage truck in bed next to him, I felt just fine.

I would highly recommend this toy, and will look to Bruder for further purchases as I feel the quality is obvious. Oddly enough, we happened to be in a toy store in Ann Arbor that same day and saw the same truck for $25 more, so look for a good deal on Amazon.

product_title: Star Wars The Phantom Menace The Vintage Collection Naboo Pilot Figure
review_headline: A great figure for a meh movie!  Hasbro wins again!
review_body:
It's kind of absurd Hasbro made TWO headsculpts for the Naboo Pilot, but this did roll out for the Phantom Menace 3D release, so Hasbro was kind of going bonkers on character/figure updates.

It moved okay on the carpet but really moved on the hard wood floors. When it bumps into something, it spins around and goes the other way.

This is one of those toys that is really cute and your child will love, but as a grown up, you'll wish there was a sound control button.

product_title: LLSai- 2.4G Mini 2W Power Amplifier Module for Phantom 2.4G Radio Transmit in White
review_headline: Very poor solder work will put your RC craft at risk.
review_body:
This amp/antenna combination seems to work, however I have not been able to quantities how well yet. However there is a serious problem.
Very poor assembly. The two threaded connectors on either end of the "2W" amplifier are very poorly soldered. A minor bump to my antenna mounted atop this amplifier resulted in the top connector completely separating from the amplifier body. Removing the wrap revealed why. The ends of the connectors have five pins, one signal and four ground. Only two of the four ground pins were soldered and the joints of the pins which were soldered looked poor. I was able to re-solder the connector to the amp and re-solder the pins on the other end. The amp now seems to be working. If you must buy this amp I recommend inspecting the solder work on the connectors and fix them if needed. If you are not adept at fine soldering I would look for another product. Item available from other vendors at Amazon of less than half the price asked by this seller.

product_title: 14' G4 Enclosure Trampoline Netting Using 4 Poles
review_body: This net is very nice! For the sake of future readers, mine came from TrampolineParts Center and I couldn't be happier. It's been several years since we got the trampoline, but this net seems to be of higher quality than the original.The material is not quite as soft as the original net though, but that may come with time. It is described perfectly and shipping was prompt. It comes with the strings needed to tie the net down. These should be tied at each end and snaked through at the bottom every inch or so to keep the bottom tight. I don't care too much for tying all of the strings, so I just went to Lowes and got a 50ft paracord and fed it 25ft each way. There is a larger row near the bottom of the net where the string should be fed. I fed the paracord in and out every inch or so and under each spring. This seems to have worked even better than the individual strings. This seems like it would take longer, but it actually went much faster since I didn't have to tie each of the smaller strings twice. The only problem I had was that the net was a few inches shorter than my original net, which just meant that I had to lower each of the pole a few inches to accommodate for this. No big deal though. The zipper is also nice and seems like it will last a good time. I've only had it up for a few days, so I can comment on the durability at this point. I'll update my review this fall after the kids have beaten in up for a few months.

product_title: G.I. JOE Vehicle Cobra Stinger with Stinger Commander
review_body:
This product is a near-identical reissue of the popular Cobra Stinger from the early 1980s. Since it's a fairly simple Jeep-like vehicle, it doesn't have a ton of moving parts, but everything that's here is great. In addition to the missile rack (which rotates and elevates), it's got opening doors, a removable canopy, and a removable AK-47 that clips to the hood. The wheels have probably the smoothest rolling action of any toy I've seen in a long time--I don't know if it's the metal axles, but this thing just glides. It's much better even than the 50th Anniversary VAMP Mk. II. The only issue I have is that since this is a vehicle design from the 80s, the doors and passenger compartment are designed around the smaller classic-style figures, and are not designed specifically to fit the larger modern-era figures. Luckily the removable canopy makes inserting and removing figures easier, since most won't fit through the doors. Still, it would have been appreciated if Hasbro boosted the passenger compartment maybe 1/2 inch in each direction...it's not a deal-breaker, though. It would also be nice if the body had some sort of painted texture/patina or camo pattern, rather than simply being done in the same flat colors as the original. However, the 25th Anniversary vehicles were all designed to be the spitting image of their 80s counterparts, so it's a success in that regard, and still looks very classy with the choice of colors.

The Stinger Driver figure, like the 80s version, is a repaint of the Cobra Trooper (in this case, he's got the helmet and vest of the Bazooka Trooper variant). The color scheme is great, and he looks cool even compared to the newer sculpts of the Trooper. I was pleasantly surprised to see that Hasbro actually made the figure's "crotch" a bit narrower than other 25th Anniversary Troopers, which makes it a little easier to fold his legs into a seated position. The choice of vest wasn't a great idea, though, since the pistol holster on the small of his back makes it a bit harder to fit him into his seat. Luckily the vest is removable, though he'll still fit even with it on.

Overall, I really like this vehicle a lot. It's a classic, and deservedly so; even the slightly cramped passenger compartment does little to damage its appeal as a modern-era product. If you can afford the high price they go for nowadays (at least 3 to 4x original MSRP), then I fully recommend grabbing one of these.stol holster on the small of his back makes it a bit harder to fit him into his seat. review_headline: Fun slingshots featuring hand-carved wooden designs and a sturdy elastic band
review_body:
Very cool slingshots with a unique wooden animal design. I've only tried the normal, boring slingshots before so the beautiful hand-crafted and hand-painted panda and raccoon designs of these particular slingshots are much appreciated. I ordered these to sling treats across our backyard and at the dog beach for my two Siberian Huskies to chase after. They love chasing after things but unfortunately, I don't have a very strong throwing arm and therefore rely on these slingshots to launch the treats a farther distance than I normally could.

Overall, they work great so far as the handles (made of sturdy wood) and the elastic band both feel solid and dependable. The handle is easy to grip and doesn't hurt the hand despite being wooden, and the elastic band can be pulled pretty far back for long-distance launches (pretty fun to have treat launching contests since there are two slingshots in this pack). Overall, very fun product that has successfully fulfilled its purpose of making my huskies work a bit harder for their treats.

product_title: Android Netrunner LCG: The Valley Data Pack
review_headline: The One With Clot in it
review_body:
Last go around we went to the moon. After that we got a big box which made the Anarch faction a force to be reckoned with. And now here we are. The new cycle. Welcome to California. Welcome to the San San Cycle. As usual I will rate the cards based on a 0-5 scale showing whether they are epic or going to ride the binder till the end of time. So how essential a buy is it? Let’s get right to it.

*Adjusted Chronotype (4) Very useable card. Finally makes Wyldside a force to be reckoned with. Solid.
*Bandwidth (3.5) A five strength, zero rez cost code gate? Sign me up. Granted it falls into the same issue as Data Raven if they go tag me. But still, pretty sweet.
*Brain-Taping Warehouse (2) The rez cost is good. The trash cost is great. The ability sounds powerful on paper. But ultimately…meh. Think about it, if it hits early the runner can click through it. And if it’s late it doesn’t do much. I tried it, but never found it useful.
*Capital Investors (3) Magnum Opus for the corp is good for sure.
*Clot (4.5) This card has not been overhyped. Singlehandedly wrecking fast advance. But you know what’s really nice about this card? The fact it exists. Even if you are not running it the corp has to respect it. Run it in a deck with Personal Workshop or Clone Chip and watch the corp sweat.
*Cortex Lock (4) No more Click one – Mimic, click two – run, anymore. This card is amazingly good.
*Enhanced Vision (2) It’s neat! And that’s it. Binder fodder.
*Gene Conditioning Shoppe (3) Moderate use now. But why do I see a “Genetic Deck” in our future?
*Genetic Resequencing (2) It’s Ok. The best I can give you on this one.
*Jinteki Biotech – Life Imagined (The Brewery, The Tank, The Greenhouse) (3.5) Speaking of cool cards, this is pretty cool. Jinteki is proving themselves shell game masters. You can see what the runner is playing and choose which ID you want to try. The Brewery deals 2 net damage once in the game. The Tank shuffles your archives into your R&D. And The Greenhouse gives you 4 advancement tokens for free. It’s exciting, but hard to make a deck taking advantage of it’s strength. On the plus side though, 4 advancement tokens is cool. Interesting, but not the strongest ID. Jack of all trades, master of none.

*Negotiator (2.5) It’s not super terrible. But it is “Mimic-able.”
*Next Gold (3) This is designed very well in my opinion. It’s strong, but fairly costed. I like it.
*Paige Piper (4.5) Wow. Just wow. Talk about your deck optimization! She is a beast. And well suited for Miss Estevez.
*Predictive Algorithm (2.5) Theoretically it turns all agendas into mini- NAPDs. But in reality it only fires once per steal obviously. Also NBN is kind of top heavy in good currents anyway. I don’t see this card ever being a thing.
*Spike (1) Yuck. This card is just ugly all the way around. It’s weak strength and you have to trash it to use it. Not worth running even in Criminal.
*Symmetrical Visage (3) I think a huge debate could be made about whether this or Professional Contacts is better. On one hand it is way cheaper. But it also only happens once a turn (two if you are using the Gene Shoppe). Not to say that it’s bad though. Just not sure how good it is.
*Synthetic Blood (4) Make the PE deck cry!
*Tech Startup (2.5) A fine card. Nothing to write home about though.
*Traffic Jam (2) A neutral Clot! Yeah not quite. It is ok but not very reliable.
*Valley Grid (3) Tricky card to play, but good for killing the runner.

Final Score (4) This is a solid data pack. Both the runners and the corp got some solid includes. I think the runners slightly edged the corps out though. Clot, Paige Piper, and Adjusted Chronotype. Pretty sick. This won’t be one of the mandatory packs to pick up if you are new to Netrunner. But for someoneis has reached the mid-level of play, you need this one. Solid buy.is has reached the mid-level of play, you need this one. Solid buy.

review_headline: The shoes are not really flat like normal feet (imagine standing on ice skates/rollerblades)
review_body:
The model figure has to be built, which I wasn't really expecting, but I've done models before. Took maybe a couple of hours to assemble. A lot of the pieces need to be tight fit, so I had to spend extra time to shave off excess plastic that remained on a part from its holders.

Figure is taller than I expected. The shoes are not really flat like normal feet (imagine standing on ice skates/rollerblades), but it still balances decently.

As mentioned in some other reviews, the coloring is not exactly as what is pictured on the box. Some highlights are not there since each piece of plastic is either black, white, pink, dark pink. I may paint it later to try to add the highlights. Most noticable on the weapons (guns particularly are just solid white), tiara, skirt.

The figure's joints feel stiff, but in ways that is good for posing (they are able to hold a pose easier). The figure overall looks great, though it'd be nice if it were a bit cheaper (though it's the cheapest Phantasy Star Online model I've seen).

Hands fall apart super easily. I'd highly recommend glue-ing those together. You can still slide the weapons into the hands after they've been glued.

review_headline: A warning. I bought this kit from Amazon about ...

The black lead should be minus but on the ohms scales it is positive. If you test a diode put the red on the cathode end to see if the diode will conduct, then reverse and look for infinity. product_title: Minnie Mouse Pull Ribbon String Pinata
review_body:
This is a very cute design but poorly made. I have three kids and I've done a lot of pinatas--including pull string ones. It can be a real pain when the last kid pulls the string and nothing falls--so you have to shake the treats out. I guess to solve for this, the makers of this pinata created a series of slits in the cardboard around the edge, and there is only the tissue paper to hold the candy in. I suppose in theory this is great, but ours came with the tissue torn. Therefore, there was a good sized hole--in the bottom. That doesn't work for filling it with candy.

I included pics so you can see the problem. Like I said--I've done a lot of pinatas. Obviously if you do the kind you whack with a stick you won't have any of these problems. But I've bought lots of pull string pinatas that don't have the odd slits. I wouldn't recommend this pinata. I'm returning for our money back!

review_body:
I've read a few reviews on here and some other sites complaining this figure and her other figure are listed as six inches and the product is much shorter than that. The actress herself is 5'2" in real life. With all of the other figures standing taller and at, closer to, or taller than the 6 inch height, it makes sense that her figure is shorter. The line is correct in saying these figures are 6 inch scale. That doesn't mean all of them will be six inches. You wouldn't want a six inch figure of Tyrion, would you? She is a full inch taller than that figure as well, meaning the company is doing a dang good job at keeping to scale.

Now that I have that out of he way, the reason I docked a star is because the likeness could honestly be better. It also took me a few stores to find one with a good paint job. The one I bought still has its flaws with paint, most notably with her hair and cloak, but it was the best I could find. Joints are super stiff, but I currently have her standing on one side of my Iron Throne replica with Tyrion on the other side. These are my two favorite characters on the show. product_title: Barbie KEVIN Doll Cool Boyfriend of Skipper Doll (1990)
review_body:
I acquired this doll back when they were still in production, 20+ yrs. ago, because even then they were relatively rare and hard-to-find. The description is slightly inaccurate. Kevin stands closer to 11" tall (a good 10¾" without shoes, to be exact); and as such is slightly taller than the Life in the Dreamhouse Skipper dolls that are popular today. He does come with all the clothing and accessories pictured here, including a pair of white socks; although from my personal observation his black dress pants were not sewn well (one outside leg seam ripped after a few changes). The tennis shoes are just decorative cloth covers (matching the reversible T-/dress shirt) that fit over top his hard plastic dress shoes (included).
In case anyone is wondering, although Kevin's overall build seems pretty solid and durable (good weight for his size, not overly hollow, cheap or flimsy), the articulation on this doll is very poor. His arms and legs are hard plastic and do not bend at all; nor will they move sideways (laterally) at shoulders, waist or hips. For comparison, he's not quite as stiff as the Model Muse adult collector edition Barbies; but (contrary to his description as a "cool boyfriend") neither would he make an ideal surfing, horseback riding or roller skating companion for Skipper. Kevin's hair is molded plastic (not rooted); and his head moves from side-to-side only (not up or down). He sports the wide cartoonish-looking eyes popular on some Barbie dolls designed during the late 80's - early 90's.
Since he is shorter and of considerably slighter build than the standard issue Ken, most Ken clothes will probably not fit him well; although some of the shirts designed for the Barbie Fashionistas Ken Cutie - http://www.amazon.com/Barbie-Fashionistas-Ken-Cutie-Doll/dp/B004NIF53M and similar "slim"-style Kens do seem to fit okay.

product_title: Marvel Avengers Age of Ultron Captain America Star Launch Shield
review_body:
This toy is as much fun as it looks in the TV commercials. My grandson had been attracted to it when he saw it and I was delighted to have it offered on Vine.

Knowing how commercials tend to exaggerate, I was a little skeptical that it could live up to the hype. Surprisingly, it does provide plenty of excitement and the toy functions just as we saw in Nickelodeon. The ring does shoot off the shield with great force.

Some of the virtues of the toy, such as the efficient and rapid way it dispatches the star rings can also be faults. It shoots hard and far and high. This is very good from one point of view but it has its downside as well. It’s hard to find the right place to use it without losing a ring or hurting a bystander. It’s perfectly safe for the child using it, but it can hurt someone in the way of the projectile or (as happened to us) it can get stuck in a tree or a roof. I was able to get one off the roof using a step ladder and the pool brush but I’m waiting for the gardener to come again to get the one that is stuck on our live oak in the front yard.

The path of the ring is also a little bit hard to control. The slightest breeze or variation in the angle in which it’s being held and it swerves off what you expect would be a straight trajectory. The only safe place to stand is behind the child shooting it.

This is not a toy to use indoors. The best place I’ve found is my brother’s back porch which runs the whole width of the house and has nothing breakable and nothing on which the rings can get caught.

Another con is that it only comes with two rings. Given their propensity to travel fast and high, it is not unlikely that in the near future one will get permanently lost.

But all of the above are adult concerns. My grandson loves it. His friends love it. The construction, functionality, design, and colors are just right. It has been used intensely and often by different children (ages 6 and 7) and a couple of so-called adults and there is no noticeable wear or deterioration. If we manage to hold on to the rings, the toy (and the excitement) should last for a long time.ages 6 and 7) and a couple of so-called adults and there is no noticeable wear or deterioration. As a side note, Twilight Sparkle doesn't have anything to do with the vampire books.

+You can pose the doll in a ton of different positions
+High quality clothing
+Her hair is very nice for doll hair
+Fun and exciting

Cons:
-The box doesn't have any instructions or background on why the pony is in human form

review_body:
Ordered this for my 3 year old, returned it shortly after opening the box. Went with the " Swing N Slide Summit Slide - Green " instead, which is much stiffer and better. Highly recommend that.

In short, this "cool wave slide" slide is way too flimsy to be a good, safe slide. This was surprising, as the Amazon product description as well as the color brochure that came in the slide package said "250 lbs limit." After pushing on it myself with my arms, I noticed it bowed way too much (4+ inches with ~20-30 lbs pressure.) Then i notice the assembly instructions said "105 lb limit." Quite different from the 250 lbs advertised!

Honestly, with the flex and the bumps, and the relatively low side walls, it would just be a matter of time before my kid or someone else kid bounced or flew off the side of it...and I don't want to have to watch over them waiting for that to happen!

product_title: Estes Proto X Nano R/C Quadcopter-p
review_headline: Hefty Small Stable and Tons of Fun!
review_body: Teeny tiny but rock solid in the air!  I am not a very good heli pilot but it did not take long for me to get used to this quadcopter's controls.  It charges fairly quickly and will stay in the air around 5-6 minutes.  I've only used this indoors and it can get blown around by the central air but it has more than enough power to counter the air currents.  The LED lights are very bright and easy to see in a room lit by sunlight.  Removing dog hair tangled in the blades does not take long to do.  Just pop off the blade, pull the hair out and replace the blade back on the motor shaft.  Removing from the wife's hair takes a bit more coaxing to calm her down before removing the rotor blades from their iron grip with her hair.  No experience removing from the coat of a live dog.  The construction is very solid and it has a good weight to it, which probably contributes a lot to the flight stability.  The quadcopter is very durable and has sustained quite a few crashes that would have bent the main rotor shaft of my heli's.  The worst crash from 12 feet up onto carpet only popped off a single rotor blade.  Worst crash on a laminate floor was probably from 6 feet up and with a good amount of ground speed due to a loss of spacial orientation and still only lost a rotor.  A swat from the wife did not result in any blades being removed.  The gray motor blade is sometimes hard to find on a light brown carpet, but it does not usually go more than a few feet from the crash site.  Wife said it did sting a bit when the blades made contact with skin.  Confirmed her statement with my cheek.  The controller is comically small but is surprisingly comfortable in my grasp.  The battery cover is held in place with a screw so there is no chance of batteries falling out of the remote while flying.  The controls are easy to use and provide a lot of micro adjustments.  There were times when the quadcopter started to drift to a side and even with full controls in the opposite direction it continued to do so.  A quick 360 wiggle of the right stick usually corrects this drift in the air before contact with the ground or wife occurs.  I am definitely impressed with the cost/performance ratio, nice job Estes!

product_title: DC Sideshow Collectibles 1/6 Scale Figure Harley Quinn
review_body: It isn't often I think that Sideshow may have possibly surpassed Hot Toys in the 1/6th scale arena.  But Harley might be the exception.  The level of detail is incredible, in particular on her clothing.  In comparison to the other figures in this line, Batman, Catwoman, and Joker, Harley doesn't come with as many accessories.  But, she doesn't really need to.  The few she does come with are highly detailed and are really all she needs.  If I had one complaint, it would be the frilly bodice piece they wrapped around her waist, I don't know if this was to kind of tie in a little of her look from the popular Batman Arkham game series, where she wears a corset top, it's just that it's not really her traditional comic book appearance.  However, this piece is removable, but it's not exactly easy to do so.  You literally have to unlace it to take it off.  However if you want a more traditional look you can do so, leaving her in her the full body spandex suit she normally wears.  The only other possible one is that the frilly wrist cuffs are molded plastic that stay on by being wedge against the hands.  Why they didn't go ahead and have these be the same fabric as whats on the bottom of the corset and actually be stitched to the sleeves of her suit I don't understand, unless it was a design constraint.  But, really that's just nit-picking.  Her two head sculpts perfectly capture two of her more common facial expressions, and again like with Catwoman, the teeth and mouth area look eerily realistic.  Overall an excellent piece and a must for your collection whether your a Batnut like me or just a Harley fan.  This is the best representation of her in a collectible 1/6th scale out there, which isn't hard being the only other 2 are the Tonner doll (ridiculously overpriced and too Barbie-ish) and the Medicom RAH Hush version (ridiculously overpriced for how cheaply it feels it was made in comparison to this one, yet Medicom expects you to pay about the same price).  I suggest picking it up as soon as possible as these only go up in price!cking it up as soon as possible as these only go up in price!

product_title: Arrma Granite BLX 4600mAh NiMH 8.4V Vehicle
review_body:
Not the quality that I expected out of a "Big Squid RC" 2 time Basher Truck of the year. The fit/finish of the RTR model was pretty good. Nothing was loose and everything appeared to be set correctly. The ESC was already set for the Lipo cutoff so I had to change that so I could run the NiMH battery which was included.

First run the battery lasted me about 25 minutes as I was being very gentle on the throttle as I got used to the Granite.

Second run with the included 4600 mah NiMH lasted 10 minutes when I decided that this model could go off a 7-9 inch high curb. Well as soon as it landed it blew the dog bones out and popped off the part that attaches to the rear hub carrier. After finding the dog bones I was able to pop everything back in.

3rd run overall - first with a 2S Venom 5000 mah lipo - 6 minutes into the battery the truck blew out it's dog bone again and this time stripped the bolt that is in the rear hub carrier AND it completely bend the supposedly "captured" rear hinge pin.

Just from pressing the throttle it somehow generated enough force that it smash a hinge pin through the special "captured" system.

Totally disappointed that a machine I've seen launched repeatedly off a 2nd story building is already broken while I wait the week for the part to come in. This wasn't some hopped up battery or anything, standard 2S.

The part availability is slim to none as there are no approved aluminum hop up parts despite Arrma's website showing there are. They are not for sale anywhere on the internet.

I would give it 1 or 2 stars because of the fact this junk broke that quickly without a single crash, bad landing or anything. Just a wheelie.

I gave it 3 because once I spend 50-100 bucks on buying parts and using a dremel to custom fit all the upgrade parts from other RC vehicles, I should have a truck worthy of being a basher. This truck has power, great pull with NiMH and even more with Lipo. Just sad I'll never actually be able to use the full power as it snaps everything that comes on the stock vehicle.

Outside temp. when I ran this was 50-65 degrees and at 6500 elevation.

Contacted ARRMA and haven't received any response regarding my seeking warranty replacement for the broken items.

product_title: SwingNSlide Wind Rider Glider Swing
review_body: Perfect addition to your swing set. Kids needed something different to spruce up the swinging experience so we got this and a disk swing. At the time our youngest was 2 and wasn't as sure of it as I had hoped. The following summer, age 3, she wanted to ride it but had to be pushed because it took to much work for her to get any movement, this year at 4 she is perfect on it and enjoys it very much. It is not large so I would say the best age range (when we bought it our kids were....9, 6, 2 and infant.....it has been 2 years) based on my average sized children is 3yrs to 8 yrs. after that their legs are so long when they put their legs in the foot holes their knees stick up pretty high. This isn't to say a 2 yr old or 9 yr old can't use it or wouldn't enjoy it....I am just speaking in terms of a really good size fit. I think the perfect age is 4-6 maybe 7. Also, the swing is hard, very hard plastic....so they need to be comfortable "feeling" that against their back as there is no give. The movement comes from the arms and legs like any other glider. The plastic is "slippery" which is why I say 3+ because at 2 they just couldn't stay put well enough because if their feet can't reach the foot holes then they are less stable. The swing hangs like a normal swing so that is nice that it doesn't require anything special on your set to hang it. The kids can get it going quite high and all have enjoyed it. I would recommend it and buy it over again.

product_title: Easy Playhouse Set
review_headline: We extended the fun for awhile and its great, but not without limitations.
review_body:
We have a 2.5 and 4.5 year old girl and boy and prior to introducing this to them, we really played everything up by having them watch castle themed shows like Cinderella and Sophia the First as well as looking at some kids DK Castle books and even building a Lego Castle. So when we asked them what it would be like to have their own castle, they obviously freaked out. Not only that, but they could decorate it with stickers, pens, crayons..whatever. So we gave one of them one half and one the other. But we didn't let them decorate that until a week after we introduced it to them so we got extended play out of it. Indeed it is flimsy and we really haven't found a solution for that yet. I think if you found a good spot outside for it, you could get some bungee cords and attach them to some stakes in the ground. It would be nice to see it come with something like that similar to a Blow Up Santa Claus.

It's too big for play inside generally so wait for a sunny day and play it up with the kids for the surprise and don't let them decorate it until the 2nd week. Then let them decorate the other side a different week. That's 3 weeks of great fun! You can decide for yourself if the price is worth it. You are not buying a heavy-duty plastic castle and overall if you got 3 weeks good use it would be about $15/week. Is that cheaper than other things you would do with your kids like take them to the zoo or local play date location? More than likely.

product_title: Marvel Avengers Age of Ultron Iron Man Arc FX Armor
review_headline: Meh. This toy could have been much better than it is. Why not give kids TWO gloves that work instead of one?
review_body:
Well, this is a little gimmick toy that will be very attractive to young boys. What little boy wouldn't want to be Iron Man?

This toy is marked as being for kids ages 5 and up. My son is currently seven years old, and these gloves fit him pretty well. There are seven different sound effects that can be activated by pressing the "repulsor" disc on the right glove. Sorry. No blasting from both hands! Only the right glove lights up and makes sounds. (AAA battery is included.) Yes, I think this was a bad idea. It would have been far more fun if BOTH gloves made sounds and lit up, but I guess Hasbro decided that they would be cheap and only give you one working glove. Boo! Also, no mask is included in this pack, so your kid(s) will certainly be asking you to buy them the mask, too, if you give them the gloves. Again, this might be a good marketing ploy, but it sucks for the parents. As fun as these gloves may be, I think they could have been much better. As such, I give this toy only three stars.

product_title: Toynami Diecast Chogokin Voltron 30th Anniversary Light up Collector Set w/Base
review_body:
The closest most of us will ever get to owning one of those classic Matchbox or Popy diecast Voltrons. Toy aim did a superb job. The weight is solid. You can feel every ounce of metal. It is a stunning display piece. And it has much of what the classic Matchbox version lacked. Weapons. At least Voltrons melee weapons. Still no sign of his missiles sadly.

The resulting figure is fairly posable, balances better than I expected (much better than the Mattel giant collector subscription one.) and has the really nice electronic base. The lions legs are all heavily chromed plastic which can wear and easily break. So this is a display piece and adult type toy for occasionally swooshing. Not so much a full blown plaything. This is for your inner 9 year old. Your actual real life 9 year old can wait till he is 40 to get his own.

It's not quite to the caliber of Bandai's long running Soul of Chogokin series. But it's pretty close. Here's hoping Toynami blesses us with a matching scale recreation of Vehicle Voltron / Dairugger XV soon.

review_body:
Fantastic figure of Cody Rhodes. Spot-on detail from every angle. I love the 'angry'-looking headscan, personally. Great detail on the tights design, also.

As a customizer, I would highly recommend this figure due to it's decent price and the several valuable parts it comes with. I bought this one for a second time to put together a Finn Bálor custom- and, depending on your customizing skill level, it is very easy to turn this figure into Finn without switching out many parts. The torso, pelvis, upper legs, shoulders, arms and headscan can all easily be modified to make a very nice Finn Bálor figure.

As for Cody Rhodes- as I stated previously, this figure is very well done. The accessories it comes with are nice accessories to have. The jacket and sleeveless t-shirt are detailed and fitted perfectly. I enjoy having this figure in my collection, and would recommend to anyone interested in either customizing, or having a nice Cody Rhodes figure.

product_title: Little Tikes Clearly Sports Bowling
review_headline: Terrifically durable little bowling set - no shoe rental required!
review_body:
In my experience, I've found that Little Tikes makes such sturdy little sports toys for youngsters - we'd purchased this little bowling set for our oldest grandson when he was 2 years old (now 7), and even though it has only six pins, it enables you to give your youngster the basic concept of the game - though, if your little one is anything like our (now three) grandsons, he/she will start their enjoyment of this set out by simply banging the pins together for the sound effects and watching the enclosed balls spin around, or using the bowling ball to roll back and forth to each other. (Just be careful... that 6" ball is made of a very hard plastic, and definitely has the potential to injure - people, pets or objects - if thrown, so if your youngster's into a "throwing" stage, best to keep it out of sight until they're past it.)

While this is a color change of our set (which had a blue bowling ball with red, green and blue balls inside of the pins), it's the same set. The pins stand @ 9-1/4", and are @ 3-1/4" thick, and it's been so funny to watch them at play with them... sometimes they're all lined up, single file rather than triangularly, and our middle grandson still thinks walking right up to the pins, ball in hand, and knocking them down is a much better idea, probably not being able to figure out why his Big Brother and grandparents stand so far away and roll it - his average is much higher than mine, I can assure you! We've used this for other games as well, like spacing the pins apart and seeing who can roll the most balls in between the pins withOUT knocking one over. Our youngest grandson is just 7 months old, and even he enjoys being on his stomach and moving the pins around with his hands to make the balls move (just realize the age recommendation is 2+ for good reason... the pins are hard plastic as well, and though they're lighter weight than the ball, you wouldn't want to leave a baby alone with them - he/she could grab hold of one, bop him/herself in the head and get a good sized lump.)

product_title: LeapFrog Sing and Play Farm
review_headline: Best farm for your little one!
review_body:
This toy is perfect for a child that loves to press buttons and carry toys around. I can't even tell you how many times my son has walked up to me carrying this toy around like it is his favorite lunchbox. The toy is a great purchase and in my opinion a must-have in your arsenal of toys.

PROS:

1. Improves dexterity. Unlike a lot of other toys, this toy has a bunch of different things that are only activated by using certain hand motions. Your kid can learn how to turn a light switch on and off. The best part is that the toy says, "LIGHTS ON," and "LIGHTS OFF." Gets your kid associated with basic vocabulary and basic motor functions. You have to slide things. The button at the top pops open the window. You have to turn a key for the tractor to start and it lights up. My kid is fascinated with the functions and is always trying to figure out the turning of the key. So many things that normally you wouldn't think of and this little farm has it.

2. It's very mobile. The handle on the top makes it a perfect toy for your little one to carry around and believe me, they will!

3. You can turn it off and it has two sounds settings, which is nice to choose from.

4. It's educational. It teaches your kid the animals and gets it familiar with the noises they make. It also sings.

CONS

1. The toy can be loud. Use the sound setting.

2. The repetitive sounds and tunes can be annoying, but that is going to be the case with any children's toy.

All in all, this toy is a great toy, especially for the price! My son has had it for months and he still plays with it all of the time.

They nearly went through the entire deck, and what was supposed to be the opening of our game night turned into the main event.  In a lot of ways that tells you the kind of game this is.  It's a party game that starts a conversation.  It's devilishly simple. (The rules, in their entirety are printed on the back of the box.) The whole thing is the question, "would you date someone with this awesome quality, and this...probably not so awesome quality?" That's all. But it's all but guaranteed to generate a moment you and your friends will be talking about for the rest of the week. Like when you try to explain to your friend why he could never deal with a girlfriend who was constantly drinking his tears. The game itself is clever and funny, but the best thing it does is get out of it's own way, and allow the players to come up with the real joke. The card has some awesome lines about why it's be cool to date someone with their own robot, but knowing that your friend has admitted that she'd date Shia if it meant she could meet Optimus Prime, and getting to announce that is a moment to be remembered.  If you're played out on Cards Against Humanity, try this.  Personally I think it's even better.

product_title: Mars Attacks The Dice Game
review_body:

Instead of a board, it's played with cards, and it's kind of fun to play. There is no skill involved, just rolls of the dice. That is nice for a party game when you don't want to have something that'll go until 2 a.m. Or maybe you do want to have something that will go until 2 a.m.; this one is adaptable.

The main attraction to play this particular dice game is the Mars Attacks graphics on the cards. If you enjoy games of chance and old matinee style sci fi movies, you'll enjoy this game.

product_title: 3-in-1 Skidoodle Sketcher
review_body:
with an almost three year old in the house, little tikes is a brand i'm well familiar with. i've never had a single problem with little tikes products...until this. i received an email from little tikes advertising that this product was do for release, so i snapped it up thinking it would be a great Easter gift for my daughter.

issue #1: i was under the impression from the email that dry erase markers would be included; instead of markers, crayons are used for the dry erase board. sensible, given the age range for the product, but impractical for use--you have to scrub--i mean, SCRUB--to get the crayon off of the dry erase board. *i* had trouble removing the crayon with the "magic cloth;" imagine the trouble a child will have with this.

issue #2: "stand it on a table!" you do that by folding the blue doors back. flimsy, flimsy, flimsy. the sketcher falls down when you apply any pressure to it. that makes using the dry erase board pretty impossible.

issue #3: "storage pouches to take art supplies on the go!" flimsy, flimsy, flimsy. after one use--ONE--you can't store anything in them as the plastic seams have completely cracked open. i would expect that to happen to plastic that was several years old, not brand new.

issue #4: the door hanger. little tikes could have gone with a less bulky door hanger; to shut the door on this thick, curvy hanger, you need to slam the door.

i'd rate this lower, but my child enjoys it, which is enough for me. all things being even, though, little tikes had a great concept but fell short on the manufacturing. not the quality i expect from them.

product_title: 25T M3 Metal RC Servo Blue Arm Horn for Futaba Savox Xcore HL HSP HD Power 3-20kg
review_body: Well I finally got around to using these servo horns and it's like they say, you get what you pay for.  First off I had to clean out a few spots where in the milling process some aluminum was left behind and made it hard to get onto the servo.  After that it went on a bit easier.  Then the top screw for tightening it down with stripped out on both servo horns.  It's like the threads where not deep enough or something.  I've never had an issue with tightening down those screws with other brands.  It is longer than most of your standard horns which on the lower hole gives you a bit more turning if  your rig can handle that.  If not you will have to adjust your end points or move it up to the upper hole where most servo horns tend to be at.  There is no need for a lock nut on the back of this either.  It is thicker.  A bit of lock tight and you are golden.
