product_title: Fun Express 12 Hawaiian Ruffled Simulated Silk Flower Leis Novelty (1 Dozen)
review_body: Based on the product description and photo, I expected to receive 1 dozen 36" leis in an assortment of realistic colors. However, only 1 in the pack is 36" long, while the rest are 30" –  40". I found the colors even more disappointing. First of all, several of the leis are rainbow colored and have significantly smaller flowers than the others, making them look completely out of place. I ran across these rainbow colored leis while shopping and specifically chose not to purchase them in favor of more realistic colors. Secondly, almost all of the realistic colors I did receive, with the exception of the 1 yellow & orange lei and 1 blue & white lei, are some combination of purple and pink so they look almost identical. A couple of the leis look like they're missing 30% of their flowers, so they look very bare next to the others. Unfortunately, I am unable to contact the seller directly so I'm going to have to return these and make another purchase, which is very frustrating. As another reviewer mentioned, these flowers shed like crazy. In the short time it took me to take them out of the package and check them all out, I ended up with little fibers all over my black pants. There are a few positives. The flower size of the realistically colored leis is about the same as most live flower leis and the colors are quite pretty. If I had received a better assortment of realistic colors (NOT rainbow colors) with more uniformity in number of flowers and length, I would've been quite satisfied. I'm not quite sure how to rate this product because I'm not sure where the problem occurred – with the manufacturer or with the seller. It seems as though someone had a huge pile of different size and color leis and just randomly grabbed 12 and stuffed them in a bag without paying attention to the product description.  Note: The leis are very flat upon arrival. After spending the night looped over a hanger, they fluffed out nicely.t randomly grabbed 12 and stuffed them in a bag without paying attention to the product description.

product_title: Sick Bricks Double Pack Theme 1 Action Figure
review_headline: This game really sick, full of bugs and need doctor badly.
review_body:
Write this review based on one week of play time on my iPhone 6+. Purchased Sick Bricks 3-in-1 Power Up set Action Figure which come with 5 figure and a set of Double Pack Theme One which come with Silence Shadow and Hiro Thunderbutt, a total of 7 figure and 3 power up set.
In the beginning, it is a very good game experience, I would give it a 5 stars. Few hours into the game, the power scan start messing with the game play since it only work half the time. And the mix brick scan also don't work some of the time. The more you play and level up, the more patient your will loss.
Once your finished the regular level, you move on to the silver and gold power brick which basically is playing all the same Hideout at a more difficult level, a very redundant and boring process same as the power up scan. However, it get worst because of too many bugs in the game. The most unforgettable one is the Goon Armory in the City, which do not let you in the room to complete the hideout. And countless other times when you are lock out in a room or trap with no where to go except shut down the app. I have experience that at least a dozen of times.

Currently, I have all the figures at level 10, but the XP counter or bar will not be fill at level 10, it will always be at 0 or empty no matter how long your play it.

What frustrated me the most is I have 21/20, yes 21/20 stars in the City Center neighborhood and yet I cannot finished it because of the glitch in Goon Armory. Finished the Ninjas at 20/20, 18 stars for Space, and 19 stars for Monster. With 3 extra key to unlock new neighborhood, which the app always pop up to remind you when there is no more hood that can be unlock, another major glitch. Only 4 neighbor to play.

Don't waste your money and time. Developer should do a better job before releasing the game. What a disappointment.

product_title: Fascinations Metal Earth Apollo Lunar Module 3D Metal Model Kit
review_body:
Out of 8 models I've build this one is probably as hard if not harder than the Model T. The biggest problem with this is the order they have you install some of the items, the thrusters for one are so tiny and fragile - for them to have you install them right off the bat then have to work around building the rest of the structure without knocking these out was a challenge. There were many other components too that I ended up installing toward the end to avoid bending/braking. The biggest challenge though for this was it has you right away bend the shape of the major section, this wouldn't be a problem except in order to install the other panels you have to open this back up. I ended up opening and closing this so much that the panel actually snapped off, fortunately with all the tabs twisted in the end you could never tell this broke.

It is an amazing model and I highly recommend this to anyone with patience, I do stay study the instructions first and ask yourself - is this step adding a small prone piece, if so can it be added later, and before I bend this will this inhibit me from adding another part without having to reopen it. If you do decide to do this I would also highly recommend buying Xuron 450BN Bent Nose Plier, 5 Inch Long Reach Needle Nose Pliers Jeweler Hand Tool, and Hakko CHP-170 Micro Soft Wire Cutter, 1.5mm Stand-off, Flush Cut, 2.5mm Hardened Carbon Steel Construction, 21-Degree Angled Jaw, 8mm Jaw Length, 16 G. These tools made it that much easier to bend the tabs in the smallest places.

One more note on these is when bending a part for a wheel or to be round, use a nail, pen, Sharpie, highlighter, etc to use to bend the metal around, this will help keep the parts in the round form. My first model I did, the Model T I didn't think about this and the wheels didn't turn out as well as they could've.

This model probably took me about 10 hours (I could be exaggerating here but it seemed like it), some of the other models such as the 747 took 45 minutes.her models such as the 747 took 45 minutes.

product_title: Easy Playhouse Set
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:2c1a9535abebde0ca951613c5f98babe]] So we all know how much kids love playing in boxes. So give credit to the people behind the Easy Playhouse Castle who manufacture pre-cut cardboard boxes that look like castles and charge around $40 for them. Yes, that's what you're getting when you buy this - a pre-cut corrugated cardboard sheet.

Is it sturdy? Not really. There are also very sharp cardboard edges that will cause papercuts. It won't survive children who plan to replicate castle invasions given that it's only about as strong as the last shipping carton you received from Amazon.

I suppose if you're really busy and don't have time to cut up card board boxes this might be a time saver. But I really can't recommend anyone spending this kind of money on a perforated cardboard box that you can get for free from just about any appliance store. You might even have more fun with your kids designing and building a castle out of that vs. spending $40 of their college savings on this.

Fourth, I wear a 44R suit jacket and the Large is large on me. Not too large if I'm wearing it over a couple other layers, but too large to wear alone. Though it is tailored like a shirt and is as thin as a heavy shirt, and thus begs to be worn as a shirt, I'll have to wear layers underneath.

product_title: Dark Horse Deluxe Mass Effect: Metal Earth 3D Laser-Cut Model: SX3
review_body:
This is by far and away the most frustrating model that I have ever attempted to complete.

I purchased this model and a pre-built plastic replica at the same time directly from Dark Horse at Comic Con Seattle. The plastic version is nice although small for the normal price tag. I figured, hey, why not have a couple variations to display.

My wife has assembled a model of this sort in the past of the Space Needle and although it was challenging, we do have it on display and it looks good. I went in to the project knowing that it would not be a necessarily easy task. This proved to be an understatement.

First off, if you are going to attempt this or any similar model of its type, I highly suggest getting a set of jewelers’ pliers to include the snips. This makes it a lot easier to remove the pieces from the stamp and not mar or crease them. The fact of the matter with this whole thing however is how fragile these pieces are. Yes, they are meant to be that way for pliability and no I was not expecting any real rigidity. The thing here is that even the slightest slip of the hand once a few layers were assembled resulted in parts that were not easily repaired or glued to break off. I genuinely wanted to enjoy putting this together. I seriously wanted to display it alongside the plastic version that I purchased. After numerous scratches, cuts and even stabbing a tab in to my finger while trying to bend another and ultimately breaking one of the aforementioned pieces, I was forced to concede defeat and disposed of it. I suppose if you have the patience required to skillfully and masterfully build a small time piece then you may be able to pull this off. And for you, I commend you and mentioned to my wife that I may consider buying one pre-built. For me however, as much as I wanted to enjoy this model, this experience has led me to report my very first truly negative review. I would not purchase to attempt again, I have removed similar items from my wish list and I regret having purchased similar items for family members.

The advertised age on the packaging states 14+. Personally, again unless you have very small hands and time bending patience, I would not recommend you purchase for anyone that you care about even a little or are at least sympathetic to.

product_title: Newisland 3x3 Pros Speed Cube Optimum Structure Great Corner Cutting Eco-Friendly Plastics Puzzle Cube Lightning
review_headline: Great cube, though lack of reverse corner cutting requires practice
review_body:
Out of the box, this cube felt a bit tight. After tensioning it to my preference, it's a great cube.

Turning: 4.8 - The cube doesn't turn half bad. It could be better, though it's not really noticeable. Overall, it turns great, and I was not disappointed.

Noise: 4.3 - The cube is a little noisier than most I've seen. It's still a relatively quiet cube, but there is a bit more added noise when turning, though it isn't all that noticeable.

Corner cutting: 4.9 - My current main cube is a MoYu AoLong, which corner cuts great. MoYu is known for their 45 degree corner cutting, so I wasn't surprised that this cube didn't quite match that. I was able to corner cut almost the full 45 degrees, as opposed to MoYu's slightly more than 45 degrees.

Reverse corner cutting: 3.7 - Reverse corner cutting isn't all that great. Again, my MoYu AoLong will corner cut more than 45 degrees reverse as well, so again, I wasn't surprised to see this cube fall short of that. With roughly the same force I need for my MoYu, I was able to reverse corner cut only about 2/3 of a cubie, roughly 20 degrees or so.

Speed: 4.5 - When attempting a solve, I clocked in roughly the same as my AoLong, though the lack of reverse corner cutting requires a bit of technique with quick R U' R' or L' U L. With a bit of practice, it was no harder than my AoLong, however.

Overall, I give this cube a rating of somewhere around 4.8. It's a great cube, and while its lack of reverse corner cutting was a problem right out of the box, tensioning and a but of practice made it as good as my MoYu AoLong. This is a great cube, and I hope to see more products from you guys in the future!

product_title: Mars Attacks The Dice Game
review_body:
This Mars Attacks Dice Game will appeal to young children. In it, the players defend American cities or monuments before they are nuked. It reminded me of the movie of the same name. However, it could become somewhat repetitious after a few games. There is no board, and its makeup is quite simple. There are tokens you use to keep track of the progress on the State or Monument cards. There are eight die. One can roll nukes, aliens, and laser guns. Basically, if you have enough nukes, you can get nuked. However, if you are nuked enough times, you can defend a monument. If you have guns, you can defend a city. The winner is based upon the points gained for each acquisition.

Sadly, I found the game easy enough for children, but it was the directions that were vague and, consequently, somewhat difficult. I wonder if a ten year old could follow them.

review_headline: I enjoyed the game and its Seafarers expansion quite a lot
review_body: I enjoyed the game and its Seafarers expansion quite a lot. I play it with my adult children and son-in-law. The rules are simple enough that my son with a cognitive disability is able to understand the game and plan his strategy with only a little support, but the game play is sufficiently variable to keep the rest of us interested. It's rare to find a game that the whole family with a range of interests and abilities can enjoy. The production values are good. review_body:
This was my first (and only) experience with the Aircore series and I am pleasantly surprised. The model accepted the Aircore power plant (not included) easily and positively with a simple magnetic "click" and needed no adjustments in trim or CG.
The speed envelope for such a small plane is impressive. I was able to loll around in flat circles at 1/3 throttle doing fly bys and admiring the scale shape, but when I pushed the throttle forward, the thing became blazing fast and the roll rate and climb out had me grinning and my heart thumping.
In the past, I've been frustrated by scale warbirds which were too small to enjoy because of their diminutive size-disappearing out of sight too quickly, OR too large to easily transport by car and use in a small field. This format is quiet, decent sized, and had smooth characteristics. This is NOT a beginner plane, but for the experienced pilot, offers a great scale looking craft fully capable of reasonable speed OR "Holy Cow Ballistic!" if your skills are ready.

product_title: Liquid Ass T-Mister Tex-Ass Stink Spray Novelty
review_body:
I originally started with a lone bottle of Liquid Ass that I bought on a whim several years ago. Little did I know that my purchase of mega stink would lead me to actually getting legitimate use instead of just for practical jokes.

I have Tex-Ass, Barfume, and the original Liquid Ass and they all get used rather frequently. My husband and I live in an apartment and have all of our married life. What once began as going to the mall and spraying this stuff in a doorway has turned into a perfect noisy neighbor repellent. We had our neighbor across the hall from us move in to her apartment at 10PM. This continued for three days. By day three, hubby and I were sick and tired of the banging, the loud talking, and the cussing in our apartment complex hallway. So, we waited for the group of them to go out to get more stuff. 15 pumps were unloaded into the momentarily calm and quiet hallway. We then watched out the peephole and waited. The chaos, the grimaces, gagging, and exasperated expressions on their faces when they came back in the building was too much for us to bear, and we had to run into our bedroom to permit gut-busting laughter. They stopped moving furniture and called it a night right after that. That was one of the many successful times we have had to use it out there in the hallway (usually on the same neighbor).

This stuff seriously is a must if you live in close quarters with rude neighbors. I've used it in the hallway when a neighbor put her child and their 3 friends out in the hallway to play. This stuff has sent annoying cellphone talkers that think the hallway is their domain swiftly behind locked doors. I cannot tell you how many times I have heard air freshener cans being sprayed out in the hallway. Our apartment complex has a mystery 'stink' problem on occasion, but no one can figure out where that wretched ass smell comes from. All three of these sprays are amazing, potent, and lethal.

My next test will be making retching sounds in the hallway, pour a can of clam chowder in the hallway, and spray some barfume out there. Apartment living can be hell, but Liquid Ass can make things oh so much better!

Note: I did NOT receive this product for free or a discount. I paid for this product in full with my own money.ur a can of clam chowder in the hallway, and spray some barfume out there. product_title: 1 To 6 Balance Charger Cable for Walkera Hubsan X4 RC Quadcopter Remote Control Toys Parts
review_headline: Adaptable for use with the iMAX B6AC.
review_body: I bought this cable and added banana plugs to it to make an iMAX B6AC compatible adapter cable for my Hubsan batteries. I got sick of charging them one at a time, and went looking for something to help speed things up. I found a 3x adapter like this, but even charging 3 at a time wasn't quite enough. I examined the wiring on the 3x adapter and figured out how to modify this one to work. All you have to do is add a red banana plug/wire to the pin where only 1 red wire connects to it, and a black banana plug/wire to the pin with only 1 black wire. All of the 5 pins in the center have 1 red and 1 black wire going to them, so the pins I'm talking about are on the far end of the connector from each other. The charger will see the pack connected to the negative-most end of the plug (with the black banana plug) as Cell 1, and the pack on the positive-most end as Cell 6. It's not terribly important, but I stuck little number stickers on each Hubsan connector so I could tell the difference. I of course used heat shrink to cover the bare wires, and then a larger piece of heat shrink to sort of fuse all the wires together to have a convenient place to pull when removing it from the charger.

product_title: Herpa Wings Dan Air Comet 4 Model Airplane
review_headline: A Fine Replica of an Historic Airliner
review_body:
On October 4th, 1958, a British Overseas Airline Corporation (BOAC) airliner made a nonstop flight from London to New York. Normally, that would not have been an extraordinary event, except that this aircraft was not like the others that proceeded it. Powered by four Rolls-Royce Avon engines, it was the first jet aircraft to perform this feat, beating Pan American's then brand-new Boeing 707. The aircraft that made this historic flight was G-APDB.

Delta Bravo had a short but interesting career. By 1960, the prestigious London-to-New York route would be taken over by BOAC's own Boeing 707s, which were much closer in capacity and speed to that of other carriers plying the North Atlantic route. The Comet would take over services to the Near and Far East, and Africa. Delta Bravo was leased to Malaysian Airways System for a short while, appearing in that fledgling airline's colorful yellow and black scheme, wearing registration 9M-AOB. She soldiered on at BOAC for a while longer and was put into storage by1964, eclipsed by the much larger Boeing 707 and the brand-new British Vickers VC-10 (and even the more-powerful Comet 4C). Her historic flight, largely forgotten, the aircraft languished for another half decade.

A young British charter operator, Dan-Air London (named after its founders, Davies, And, Newman), was eager to trade its piston-engine aircraft for jets. The stored Comets, gently used, with low mileage and airframe hours, would fit the role just fine. Dan-Air, in 1966, purchased its first examples, the second independent British airline (after British United) to do so. In the interim, Britain's own British European Airways (BEA) retired its Comet 4Bs as more-economical Hawker-Siddely Tridents and BAC-111s came on line. Delta Bravo got her lucky break in 1969 and joined fellow Comets on that airline's European charter services. Dan-Air was the largest operator of the Comet, operating the three main commercial variants (the 4, 4B, and 4C) She flew with Dan-Air until 1974, when the airline started phasing out the noisy, fuel-thirsty Comets for more economical BAC-111s and used early-model Boeing 727s.

Most of Dan-Air's iconic Comets were sold for scrap; three, however, were preserved for posterity. One of these was G-APDB, the subject of our model. The old lady is a proud part of the outstanding collection of the Duxford Imperial War Museum. The aircraft was restored to its original BOAC scheme but later reverted to this, the early Dan-Air scheme.

Now, onto our model. Off the bat, Herpa is to be congratulated for issuing a replica of this extremely important and interesting aircraft. As of this writing, none of the other three surviving Comet 4-series aircraft have been issued in any scale. I am thrilled to have it in my collection! Overall, the shape of the model is well executed, as are the markings. One thing I do not like about Herpa's offerings are the company's use of plastic for the tail surfaces (vertical and horizontal stabilizers). At least, unlike Dragon Wings, the main wings are diecast metal. Many of the early Herpa 1:500-scale offerings were somewhat crude by today's standards. I am glad to say that the company's newer offerings, this one among them, represent a vast improvement in quality, especially in the execution of the landing gear. The gap between the wings and fuselage is somewhat noticeable, but it is not as bad as it appears in the stock photos. The scale of this model, 1:500, is currently manufactured by only two companies; most prefer the larger 1:400 scale. And as of this writing, a new 1:200-scale Dan-Air Comet 4B, in the airline's final scheme, has appeared. The real De Havilland Comet was not a large aircraft, even for its time. As such, this model, in 1:500 scale, is a small bird, at about 2 3/4 inches (68 cm) in length, with a wingspan of about 2 5/8 inches (66 cm). Overall, this is a fine little replica, and she fits inwell with my small collection of much-loved airliners in that same scale. product_title: KMC Hyper Mat Sleeve Black (80-Pack) + 100 Pochettes Card Barrier Perfect Size Soft Sleeves Value Set !
review_headline: KMC Hyper Mat came highly recommended, but I was disappointed
review_body:
KMC Hyper Mat came highly recommended from Tolarian Community College on Youtube for double-sleeving cards, and while I can see how well these products work together, I just do not like KMC Hyper Mat. The sleeve edges are *extremely* sharp making shuffling uncomfortable to begin with, and the sleeves do not slide together well at all in that classical "mash shuffle" style, further exacerbating the issue. The cards stick and resist each other while weaving them together. You'll be bouncing your deck in your hand to get it to mash shuffle, and you will notice cards sticking during a chop shuffle. It should not take me 15 seconds to complete one shuffle. If your hands sweat at all, it definitely will.

I recommend Dragon Shield sleeves over these. They shuffle together more smoothly and don't feel like they could cut you open. For double-sleeving, pair Dragon Shields for the outer sleeve with Ultra-Pro's Pro-Fit for the inner sleeve.

The way The Professor gushed about these sleeves, I'm wondering if he's ever tried pairing Dragon Shield with Pro Fit, or if I got a bad set of KMC sleeves.

product_title: Nerf Zombie Hammer Shot
review_headline: An overall review of a great short and mid-range gun for your arsenal
review_body: This is a great gun. I love the new hammer action instead of the pump. The hammer helps you achieve and maintain better accuracy by letting you stay in the same position. The "faster firing" ability is awesome too. The only downfall to the new ability is user error by slipping off the hammer and having a premature release creating a short firing dart.Tested accuracy (on a cool night with slight breeze) is excellent at 0-20ft, fair from 20-35ft (you still have the ability to adjust for the wind and distance to have better accuracy), poor from 35-55ft (the accuracy is extremely low but the dart has power and makes the distance just fine), and bad from 55-75ft (the distance/power is almost gone and the accuracy is next to nothing). The weight is distributed about the same as the old Maverick Rev-6 if not better. The only thing I haven't liked (but I'm getting used to) is the handle/grip. This gun will, of course, fire the suction darts and the "whistler" style darts. Be sure to remove your darts when not in use. (the instructions say this) I can only figure this helps the darts stay snug in the chamber longer.

The major disappointment of this truck is that it has no tail gate! The bed is flat and there is nothing to keep the load in the truck from dumping out when the child pushes it around. I understand that this makes it actually dump the contents out better, but even just a small rim to keep the load inside the dump truck would be better, in my opinion. product_title: Upper Deck Legendary: A Marvel Deck Building Game
review_headline: A fun strategy card game that will keep you coming back and wanting more expansions (and the fan-made app is super helpful)
review_body:
This is my first intro into the deck building genre, but I have to say that I am pleased. My wife made fun of me for obsessing about the game until I got her hooked on it. Then one day I came home and she had the game set up and ready to go :) I now own the base set (marvel legendary) and the first expansion (dark city). The base set is solid and has enough variety to keep you coming back again and again, but I suppose if you play it over and over enough you'll get a little tired of it and will start wanting the expansions--a good thing I guess? As a Marvel, comic book nerd this game does have many things in it that will make you proud to own it. (As an example Deadpool has a card entitled "Here hold this for a second," and the action of the card permits the player to hand over a bystander to a villain of choice. The caption reads, "Hey, Abomination makes a pretty good baby sitter." This fits Deadpool's insane persona). In other words the actions of the cards and the feel of the game and characters seem to be true to the Marvel universe.

That being said there are a couple of minor weaknesses/ irritating elements to the game--perhaps especially being a Marvel fan, and as such I may have given this game a rating of 4.5 stars.
1) Spider-man is FAR too weak. How on earth is Black Widow more powerful than Spider-man?? (Perhaps this is even more disappointing because I'm a Spidey fan. But my impression is that the "Paint the town red" expansion helps to even these odds. I'm not sure though.
2) I felt that the game would have been even stronger if the outcome were held in suspense throughout the entire game. At some point during the game play, however; it becomes fairly obvious as to whether you (or your group) will win or lose. I feel like this is a minor weakness because the ending can feel somewhat anti-climactic.

Also, I found the fan-made app super helpful. The app randomizes the scenarios for you and cuts down on a lot of unnecessary card sorting. This is a huge recourse for this game. Check it out here: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.ctgilley.marvellegendaryrandomizer&hl=en

Bottom line: you won't be disappointed (especially if you're a Marvel fan), and your excitement will make you want to get the expansions.

product_title: JJRC H9D 4CH 2.4GHz FPV RC Quadcopter with 6-Axis Gyro 0.3MP Camera Golden RTF
review_headline: Cheap and flies terrible. It barely has enough jizz to lift the ...
review_body: It is a real piece of poopie friends.  Cheap and flies terrible.  It barely has enough jizz to lift the camera if you take the landing gear off, then it will fly about 5-10 feet high on full throttle but is barely controllable.  Perhaps I was spoiled by my Syma quad, but what is the point of FPV if you can't fly high enough and stable enough to take your eyes off of the copter?  I really wish I had never purchased this POS, but really wanted FPV and this was affordable.  You definitely get what you pay for here.  The quad does not even have an On-Off switch, you have to open the battery compartment to turn it off.  RIP OFF is too gentle of a word for this piece of garbage.  The only upside is the FPV camera and remote, which appear tons better than the actual quad itself.  The FPV camera will plug into the camera port on my Syma but I haven't figured out if the remote can operate the Syma quad.  So far...no.  On the JJRC H9D the camera mount is so loose that the camera keeps falling off if you change directions too suddenly, and the quad is so unstable that happens frequently.  Best bet is just to send this back and make a down payment on a Phantom.  Better solution would have been to never have wasted my money on the JJRC-H9D.  My brother purchased one off EBay and the FPV camera did not work.  He got his money back but it took a long time.  As pictured without the landing gear attached, it barely flies.  With landing gear, not higher than 2 feet.  This quad is really not a good buy.  I wish ZERO STARS was an option.

product_title: Step2  Naturally Playful Sand Table
review_headline: We are completely happy with this sand table
review_body:
We are completely happy with this sand table. It's a great height. My daughter is quite small and she was able to play comfortably at it when she received it on her 2nd birthday. My niece (8) plays with it sometimes and kneels, which works out just fine. It's been almost a year since her birthday and the sand table still looks great, despite having sat outside in the elements entirely unprotected.

The lid isn't completely water tight but so long as you keep it covered when not in use, we haven't found it to be much of a problem. We are in Houston so lots of rain. It's sometimes a bit damp after a really hard rain, no shock there with our humidity, but not so wet as to prevent my daughter from playing in it. It is deep enough for her to enjoy but not so deep that it takes very long for the sand to dry out if you do forget to cover it.

If you are deciding between this and a combo sand/water table, I'd get this. My friends combo tables are always dirty messes since the sand ends up in the water (of course!). You can't just fill up one side or the other very easily (what are you going to do with 50# of sand if you want to put it back in the table?). Many of the combo tables don't have a cover. We have a separate, inexpensive water table and I'm really happy that it worked out like this because it's easy to just keep the lid on the sand table while the water table is in use.

review_body:
This is an interesting toy. When I received it I would not expect my baby to like it, however even though she did not use it for its primary purpose, she liked the spinning wheel a lot.

In its original idea, this is a speedway for a car (or more if you buy the extra sets), and a learning / response toy at the same time. When you place the car in position and hit the lever, the car is lowered into the spinning platform. Additionally there are three buttons, marked, 1, 2, 3, that has circle square and triangle shaped. Depending on the level (there are three) it will either tell you what the buttons are, or ask you press specific ones, and so on.

Unfortunately we have better toys for learning shapes / numbers, which makes this unattractive in that manner. However the spinning wheel was very fun for the baby. This was more so after she started experimenting with it with more toys (small balls are especially good for this).

Overall this is a fun little toy. Works well, but the learning part seems lackluster.

review_body:
Looking at publicity photos of this doll line online, I hadn't been sure if I wanted to get one or not; it's always so hard to tell until you've seen one in person. But then a fellow collector posted some of her own shots and mentioned that the doll line's own website had them on sale (presumably to make way for the new line that will come out soon) and I decided to take the chance, and picked up this one, and I must say that I feel the money was well spent. The doll is cute, she has absolutely gorgeous glass eyes, and her clothes are mostly made of jersey, so they feel like a real person's clothing, unlike the doll clothes on...well, almost every other doll in my collection. (I don't even want to think about how many dolls that is, btw.) The plastic she's made of feels a bit rubbery compared to other dolls, but it's not a bad thing, just something that's a little surprising at first. Looking at her photos, I kept thinking she'd be about the size of the Moxie Girlz Teenz dolls, but she's more on the Barbie scale, though just a bit larger, so there's no chance of her being able to wear Barbie's clothes. In fact, that's probably the biggest downside of this doll line at this time: the options for finding clothes for them are pretty much nil, apart from having them trade outfits with each other. I think the only doll in my collection who could trade clothes with this doll would be the BeGoths I just recently got, only I think hers would be too large. (Not to mention that the style is a bit of a mismatch for this doll!)

I've seen reviews on here for one of the other dolls in this line complaining about the hands breaking off, and I must say that I can definitely see that happening if the doll is given to a young child: the wrist joints seem a little less well made than the other joints, so that is probably something to keep in mind if you're thinking of gifting the doll to a very rambunctious youngster. Her head doesn't turn quite as much as I wasexpecting, either, but I think it's probably plenty for a child's plaything. (It's more a case of not being able to tilt it at an angle than not being able to turn it, as such.) As a collector, my only complaint is that her stand isn't quite right: either the two pieces don't fit together properly, or it's just a tiny bit too long, but whatever the reason for it, if she's in her stand, then her feet are dangling just a bit above the ground, which looks awkward to me, so I have her sitting on a shelf instead.

One last note: because these dolls are apparently sold only online, and never in stores, the package was one of the easiest to open I've encountered in years. The twist-ties were only there to hold her in place and protect her from sliding around during shipping, so there were only as many as were needed. And best of all, no universal annoyances stuck through the back of her head! (That is my biggest pet peeve with standard fashion doll packaging. Trying to get rid of those things without damaging the doll's hair...ugh, nightmare time.)

product_title: Munchkin Deluxe
review_headline: A game for all but the most Prudish
review_body:
As a long time Gamer I found this game to be quite enjoyable. The term ‘Munchkin’ harkens back to the days of old when meeting younger new players at gaming club meetings. They always over-read the rules and found any loophole to take advantage of. Hence, they were dubbed “Munchkins”. That spirit of crazy do-anything-no-matter-how-illogical-to-win spirit is captured herein.

I originally bought this game to play with my daughter. She won't play serious dungeon/adventure board or card games, but after reading a few cards of this game she eagerly agreed to a simple two player learning game, and now we are hooked! This game is written with good humor, which we both enjoyed. As an old school player myself, I found the humor of the Steve Jackson Games Team welcoming like an old friend. My daughter just thinks the cards are fun; Boots of Butt-Kicking, the Duck of Doom, etc. These are great fun! They are loaded with imaginative humorous puns!

Some might find a card or two inappropriate for younger players. I feel you either have to be easily offended or think children should be raised in a bell jar until they are twenty one to find this game objectionable. If you are the kind of person who is offended by the terms “Sneaky Bastard Sword” (a play on words), “Horny Helmet” (A helmet with huge Horns), or “Kneepads of Allure” (Not explained), then don’t complain, simply DON’T BUY THIS GAME FOR YOUR KIDS! Yes older, adult players may get the subtext of the artwork on the “Leather Armor” card, but a ten year old probably won’t see it. Take a chill pill and let your kids mature a little.

Now, the game play is simple, very simple. This is no huge strategy game. Gameplay is literally as easy as; Kick the Door in, Kill the Monster, Grab the Treasure, and Go up a level. Get to level 10 first, and you win. There is some strategy added with helping and hurting the other player. There are times when it is advantageous to both hurt and help an opponent in the same turn. (See my definition of Munchkin above). The final stages of the game almost always end very cutthroat, and pulling out all the dirty tricks you can to stop your opponent. If your kids or you can’t handle this; don’t buy!

Playing time 30-60 minutes, 3 Players recommended, but 2 player games are possible just less fun. It will take several playing sessions before you experience all the cards, and should you find they get boring or predictable, there are eight expansions with new cards, new concepts and new variations on the game. product_title: Nerf N-Strike SnapFire Blaster
review_headline: This is a pretty awesome blaster
review_body: This is a pretty awesome blaster despite some reviews ive seen elsewhere. Its slightly more expensive than a jolt but its accuracy and power make up for it. It appears to be much more accurate and slightly more powerful than my jolt. The seal in the barrel is basically perfect, no air escapes past the dart. If you are looking to mod this by removing the air restrictor, it's relatively easy, just remove the plunger assembly, take a screw driver and put it in the barrel and tap the whole air restrictor and plunger stop out the back. From there, i took a dremel and opened up the hole where the dart post is and once it was open, the air restrictor popped out. I put the plunger stop back in along with the plunger itself and its good to go! Replacing the spring is very simple. I put the stock spring from a retaliator in it and it works amazingly well. Definitely recommend this if you are looking for a single shot blaster.

product_title: The Resistance (The Dystopian Universe)
review_body:
Who ever thought accusing your friends of being a spy could be so much fun? The creators of The Resistance obviously did and they were spot on. I saw this game on Tabletop a while back and decided to give it a try. The first night playing this my friends and I spent 2 hours (probably 10-15 games) playing this addictively fun quasi-micro game.

The game is based on a system that pits players against each other but forces them to work together. The members of "The Resistance" don't know who is friendly and who is truly a "Spy" but the "Spies" know the identity of their fellow agents. Each round one player must form a team with a preset number of members varying from 2-3 (for 5 player games, with team sizes adjustable for up to 10 players). The lead player during that round tries to pick his allies without picking the spys (unless that player is a spy). All players vote on the makeup of the group, this is where the fun begins.

During the voting process players will try to persuade the current "Leader" who to take and who not to take. Accusations fly, insults are hurled and laughs are had by all. This part of the game is so fun we had to put an argument timer in place to keep things moving (my friends and I are expert arguers!). Once a team is finalized each chosen member chooses if the mission will succeed or fail. Missions succeed as long as all participating members choose the succeed card but the mission fails if even one player chooses the fail card. The cards are placed face down on the table and the "Leader" shuffles and reveals the outcome.

The game is won when either side has reached 3 wins (3 failures for the Spies and 3 successes for the Resistance). One of the best aspects of this game is that the more you play the better your lies become and the more outrageous the accusations become. My friends at one point believed me to be the spy simply because it had been 3 or 4 games without me being the spy so odds said I was due to be one soon. It turns out I was a regular resistance member the whole time (until the next game of course... mwa ha ha ha ha ha hahahahahahaha!)

Buy this game, play this game, weed out the spies and VIVA LA RESISTANCE!

product_title: SJ230/SJ250 2 Speed 3.5 Channel 9 Inch Long Super Anti-crash RC Helicopter with Built-in GYRO (Black)
review_headline: Comparison of SJ130 at $14.99 vs Syma S107/S107G at $19.99
review_body:
Previously purchased Syma S107/S107G. Then saw this one and thought it was the same only cheaper so bought for my son. There were a few differences and a few observations:
1. Con?: It appears to be a Chinese knockoff of a Chinese knockoff, I had never considered that!
2. Con: The battery it comes with is crap, make sure you buy the battery upgrade.
3. Con: The upgrades are crap so make sure you buy 2 of them, saves frustration when one fails to charge.
4. Pro: Does not use the same battery as the Syma product.
5. Pro: Battery actually has a plug so is designed to be replaced. This is a plus since the original battery is crap.
6. Pro: Battery is easier to replace because it does not require the tiny phillips screwdriver which wasn't included with Syma product either.
7. Pro: Control unit only uses 4 "AA" batteries instead of 6 like the Syma. That is good because the batteries are probably worth more than the Helicopter.
8. Pro: The control unit does not require the tiny phillips screwdriver like the Syma product did, but which was not included anyway.
9. Pro: Remote Control is apparently somewhat more sophisticated. Even has something called a "Demo" mode.
10. Con: The instruction manual is so bad that you are given no clue what "Demo" mode does. The manual is probably the worst I've seen yet
11. Pro: The controls are pretty basic so the manual is not really necessary except to figure out why charging is so difficult. Helicopter must be in the "ON" position to charge, unlike Syma.
12. Con: Basic controls = "Not Much Fun to Fly". It hovers and it creeps forward, that is about it
13. Con for both: this is an indoor toy, outside forget it. Light or wind, either one and it is even less fun than "Not Much Fun" above.
14. Con for both: Blades are freakin' dangerous.
15. Pro for both: Much quieter and less annoying to my wife and daughter than my Nano which sounds like a mosquito on steroids. These just hum a little, but the pitch is tolerable.

Summary: for $14.99 it is probably about as good as it gets and is definitely a better product than the Syma S107 I think. Only time will tell whether it will last as long or longer since both have now flown several times. After reading other reviews, I feel blessed to get 2 that actually work. They are so cheap that it isn't even worth the time to send them back. That said, the Nano is a lot more fun and damages less when it crashes into stuff. These actually contain metal, so I am amazed they are so cheap. The Syma contains even more metal, probably why it costs more. I sort of wish I had not bought the replacement parts pack, because when these die I doubt I will take the time to even repair them. 5 minutes with these and you are good. Been there, done that. Yawn...

product_title: Melissa & Doug 25 Wooden Shape and Color Magnets in a Box
review_body:
Love these magnetic shapes, for the most part.
I have never had to question the durability of any Melissa and Doug product... Until now.
The description states that the product is made of wood, however this is not entirely an accurate description. Most Melissa and Doug products have the colors painted on them, so I assumed that this would be the case with these magnets as well. The "color portion" is sturdy cardboard (think the consistency of a board book), so the product is a wooden shape with this cardboard on top, and obviously the magnet on the back.
I have learned that no matter now old some children are, things still go in their mouths. After sticking the corner of one shape in his mouth, my son had successfully moistened, then in turn, peeled the thick cardboard off the shape in only a couple of minutes.
If these shapes had a painted color top instead of a cardboard one, they would be perfect!
Had the product description correctly stated that they were made with wood and cardboard, we would not have purchased them.

review_body:
My nearly 5 year old grandson is nuts about Thomas the Train, as well as any toy set that involves tracks of any kind (for trains or cars), and he loves playing with this set. I helped him get it set up initially and I installed the batteries (2 AAA size, which are NOT included), and the first time he played with it he was absorbed for nearly two hours.

The train itself is about 4 1/2" long. The train and all the parts are well-built for a relatively inexpensive set, and overall the set and packaging are Fisher-Price quality. As far as toy sets with tracks of any kind go, this one is on the small side, which has its advantages in terms of how much space it takes up when in use and when stored. (Fisher-Price invites you to expand it by purchasing other Track Master sets.)

product_title: Fisher-Price Dora and Friends Play It Two Ways Guitar
review_headline: A fun toy guitar for a toddler to play
review_body:
This is such a cute little fake guitar. It is push button rather than anything with real strings. You play it by pushing the button where you would normally strum the guitar and you do "fret" work by pushing down on the interior of the fret section of the guitar. There is a flip section that alternates the music between electric and acoustic.

My grandson is almost 18 months old and doesn't really know who Dora is as he watches very little on TV (and then only a couple of specific DVDs.) We do, however, play a lot of instruments amongst the family - just in my house along there are over a dozen different instruments. He even has a small ukelele of his own at his house that he plays with. He grabbed the Dora guitar as soon as I showed it to him and showed him which buttons to push. He "played" guitar all afternoon - carrying it around with him everywhere. He would stop and start dancing and shaking his head to the tunes or would drop the guitar to clap - and then realize that he had to play it again to make the music continue.

The final move of the day was when he put it in his pop-up castle (along with his much beloved Fisher-Price piano keyboard) where it will wait until next week when he comes to my house again. He loved it and played with it for hours. His smile was so big, I wondered if it hurt his face to keep it up all afternoon. I'll probably pull out one of my guitars and then we can rock out together.

This is a really cute toy guitar and I recommend it highly. I don't know why it is recommended for 3 years and up. I don't see any small pieces that could be a hazard and my little guy loved it at 18 months.

review_body: Great flyer if you use a transmitter that can reduce the aileron and elevator throw.  I use about 60% for each, and tie them to toggle switches on the Spectrum DX6i.  When I want to have snappy rolls, or tight loops, I just switch the reduction off.  Without some restriction, the plane is hard for me to keep up with, even with reduced power.  I landed in the water several times, and found a few drops in the electronics section.  I blew it out and few again, but on the fifth flight the motor controller section of the control board smoked.  I bought a second one, and after a serious crash, I moved the newer control board into the first plane, and am flying it almost daily with great success.  I land in the grass, however.

product_title: Fisher-Price Soothe and Glow Seahorse
review_headline: Best-selling toy, now ostensibly redesigned to address consumer concerns
review_body:
So, did Fisher solve the fire hazard in the battery case with this new version of their extremely popular baby lullaby and nightlight toy? I could find no official word, but the product has been renamed (they’ve removed the words “Ocean Wonders” from the name) and the battery pack redesigned (it used to take three batteries, now it takes two). Ostensibly, this redesign solved the fire hazard that many consumers complained about with the former version.

The former version was the seventh most popular toy for young babies and tots until news got out that some of the toys were heating up and smoking when their adult users changed the batteries. There was never an official recall ,and as far as I know, no babies were hurt, but there was an avalanche of negative reviews and many negative consumer watch news stories in the media.

That was last year. Turn the calendar ahead and we now have the new Fisher-Price Soothe and Glow Seahorse. It looks exactly the same. It plays the exact same music. The only difference was a redesign of the working battery pack mechanism inside the Seahorse. I think, as consumers, we can assume that the problem has been resolved. That’s good, because, this product was a clear winner for all those parents and babies out there who used it and didn’t experience any fire hazard problems. If you look at the reviews for the old version, there are actually far more over-the-top positive five-star reviews for the product than there were one-star reviews warning about the potential fire hazard.

So, in some respects, the consumer won; the product was redesigned.

I gave this to my niece and her six-month-old baby. She phoned me to report that both of them absolutely adore it! She’s so happy with it; she says, “It works like magic! The baby took to it immediately…and so did my two year old.” Evidently, the older one loves the glow light as much as the music.

So how does it work? When the Seahorse’s soft yellow plastic belly is squeezed, it starts glowing and soft soothing music comes out through the fabric of the toy. The music is synthesized instrumental music. In the background, very faintly, there is the constant sound of water, either the sound of gurgling, or the sound of water lapping against a boat or shore. There are eight melodies. The Seahorse plays a few phrases from each tune in a slow, measured, and unembellished fashion; the musical emphasis is entirely on calmness and serenity. Each tune tapers off in pitch and tempo after a short time, then there is a soothing lapping water sound, then a bit of silence, then another tune begins. The entire repertoire lasts six-and-a-half minutes. Finally, after the last song tapers off, the glow light flickers off and the cycle is complete. Every time the Seahorse is squeezed, it goes through the exact same repertoire. If it’s squeezed while it is in the middle of its repertoire, it ignores the squeeze and continues till the end of the cycle. If, for any reason, you want to turn the device off in the middle of its repertoire, all you need to do is to hold the squeeze extra long until it shuts off. Remember this: it is not in the instructions, and I learned it only by accident, but it works perfectly every time.

For those of you who are interested in exactly what music your child will hear, these are the melodies:
1) Petzold’s “Minuet in G major (made popular fifty years ago as "A Lover's Concerto" and given lyrics that begin “How gentle is the rain);”
2) The popular English lullaby, "Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star;"
3) Beethoven’s “Ode to Joy;”
4) The lullaby “Golden Slumbers;”
5) Bach’s “Jesu, Joy of Man’s Desiring;”
6) The lullaby “Sleep Baby Sleep”
7) Pachelbel's Canon in D; and
8) The French nursery rhyme, "Frère Jacques" (in English, translated as “Where is Thumbkin?”

The music has two settings of loudness. The glow light is soft and reassuring, definitely designed gently to sweep fear out of dark corners, but not to be so bright that it might interfere with sleep. There is nothing about the Seahorse that could serve as a choke hazard. The electrical mechanism can be separated from the Seahorse if the fabric part needs cleaning. You’ll have to remove the electrical mechanism eventually to insert two AA alkaline batteries when the original batteries start to fail. The instructions now emphasize (with bold print) the use of alkaline batteries. There is a Velcro closure at the back. It may take some effort to make sure the two Velcro strips are fully matched so no Velcro remains on the outside to detract from the overall furry softness and appeal of this cuddly calming creature.

I can see absolutely no reason not to give this enjoyable, and very useful, toy an enthusiastic five-star rating.music has two settings of loudness. The spiral 'ramp' can be placed going up around the cone as a true spiral or down as a roundabout circling the cone. Connecting with the other sets, this is a very cool addition. There is also a little garage, that doubles as a ramp.

The sets that are compatible include many launcher sets. These launchers have a button that the child can push/ punch and send a car racing forward. Connect a launcher to this set and you have a very cool stunt ramp.

Alone, this isn't the most fun and I am unsure if its staying power. But when connected to the other sets in the series, this creates an extra fun Radiator Springs happy fun place.

product_title: Bandai Hobby HGUC Gundam F91 Action Figure
review_headline: I loved putting together this kit
review_body:
Let me start by saying that this kit is SMALLER than the average 1/144 kit. BUT that's because the F91 was designed as a smaller mech, so scaling it down is accurate!
I loved putting together this kit, as I do with almost every Gundam kit I build, but there was just something about this kit that made me ecstatic. It was a simple kit, a bit of everything you expect from gundam, and extra parts for your style of posing. 2 head designs, 1 beam rifle, 2 beam sabers, 1 I-field shield, and 1 Nuke Launcher (at least I think that's what it is, never watched this particular part of the UC stuff) make up the added gear. Attached to the back is the variable beam cannons, and they can be posed in several ways as well.
All in all, I'd say this was the most satisfying kit I've built to date.

product_title: Chuggington: 4 Seasons 4 x 35 Piece Puzzles in a Tin
review_body:
We purchased the Chuggington 4 Seasons 4 in 1 puzzles. The purchase arrived within a couple days (Sunday Delivery!)

My Granddaughter just loves Chuggington and loved the puzzles.

The puzzle pieces seem to be thick enough for 3+ year olds'. We like the storage tin also.

Slightly disappointed with the 4 puzzles not being marked on the backside to differentiate which piece goes to which puzzle (1,2,3 or 4), and the tin was not divided to keep the 4 puzzles separated so the pieces don't get mixed up, which you know is bound to happen with little kids!

Took the puzzles pieces out of the packing bags (one at a time) and the silica gel packs were broken open on two of them, and you cannot see them very well, and of course the silica beads went all over the place, so use caution unpacking it (I think I am still finding the beads!). I took a Sharpie and wrote the puzzle # on the back of each piece and placed them in Ziplock sandwich bags and that works well. I also put the puzzle # on the pictures that are shown on the top of the tin so we could reference the completed picture by number.

Aside from the packing consideration, the puzzles were pleasing and reasonable!

review_body:

First of all, the dress was COVERED in fine glitter, which coated every surface in my house the first ten times she wore it. It was a bit too long for her, and in the two months she's owned it, the bottom of it has completely fallen apart. The seams are ripping at the bottom and shoulders, and the bottom of it is fraying. I guess you get what you pay for.

But the most disturbing part is that yesterday, she somehow managed to fall/sit on the dress while she was carrying it, and landed on the snowflake medallion. It actually put a hole in her pants and left a decent sized wound on her rear end that bled. I'd never noticed how sharp and pointy the snowflake was before, and this probably was a freak incident, but I'm so glad she wasn't hurt more seriously. I'm considering that this dress may need to go away now.

product_title: NFL Electric Football Game
review_headline: Old School Fun. We had Electric Football Leagues when I was ...
review_body: Old School Fun. We had Electric Football Leagues when I was a kid. Still have my old team, and have found that there are still many leagues and organizations throughout the country and people who customize boards, players, and teams. With research you should be able to find some in your area, especially hobbyists. In any event, the football players move across the field due to vibration. The bristles on the bottom of the bases the players stand on  react to the vibration from the board for movement. Some of the bases have radialknob controllers to help with that movement. Some people have complained about the movement of the players. Well, the movement can be adjusted by manipulating the bristles (just slide your fingers across them). Also, upon delivery, due to production, some/many of the bases will have flashing (excess material) on the bristles. If so, this should be removed and the bases will then operate/run more effectively. Lastly, not a big proponent of the passing component of the game. Typically, our league back in the day (vanity won't let me say how long ago) utilized only running plays. But passing can be done, but takes practice. For an overview of the game see the video on the link here http://www.tudorgames.com/electric-football.html . Also note, this is not for small-kids as the pieces are breakable. So responsible 6 year olds or better yet, 8 and up. I hope this helps. And by the way, ask Dad or Grandpa, you might get lucky and they may still have their old treasured team tucked away in the attic.  Addendum: Bought the larger board, but the same should apply. First of all, for any old-school players of Electric Football, this board is not made of metal. Playing field appears durable though. Also, the new remote motor system is novel. However, utilizing it will revolve looking for the sweet spot on the board before applying it. Tip: put motor on top to try to locate a good running spot (typically near the corners. Also, the new remote system utilizes batteries rather than plugging in. This offers a convenience of easily transporting the board and/or playing while tailgating, but the dependency on batteries has its downsides as well (i.e. strength of vibrations, more temperamental motor dependent upon battery strength). Finally, the major upside is the new teams are painted well (although no center notches in the bottom for older style rookie bases) and yardsticks and other accessories are not dependent upon magnets. And best of all, although it takes some getting used to, the new invisi-bases are great. They run decently in comparison to the older style bases. So all in all, lowered one star because I don't like all the new features (miss being able to plug in). But all in all, nice to have new boards.

review_headline: So much fun you won't even know you're learning science and math concepts!
review_body:
Lots of fun! Easy to follow directions and literally 100+ projects that build on one another. The projects have some informational rational at a basic level so you actually understand what you just did, why it worked, and how it was important. Can apply basic physics at a young agel!!

My electrician husband loved helping my son, 6, work on projects. product_title: Playskool Sesame Street School Bus
review_body:
My 20-month old son attends a music class and when the teacher does the "Wheels on the Bus" song, she brings this bus out. There is always a fight amongst the kids for who gets to hold it and play with it (this doesn't happen with any of the other toys she uses). I figured I would lessen the mystique of this bus by buying my son and his classmates their own buses for home. As every mom knows, new toys and someone else's toys are the best and if it's something they own, it might as well be chopped liver. Well, I was wrong! This toy still reigns supreme at music class! At home, my son plays with it every day and it's one of the first things he looks for every morning.

Now, in terms of bells and whistles, this bus doesn't have much (there's a button to open the door and The Count turns toward the open door). But maybe the lack of music,lights, etc. is what encourages imagination and continued play. Whatever it is, this is one of my son's favorite toys and for that reason, I would highly recommend it.

product_title: World of Nintendo 4" Samus [Metroid] Figure with Mystery Accessory
review_body:
Samus Aran, star of the Metroid franchise, is the latest offering from the World of Nintendo line. If you're like me, you appreciate that the World of Nintendo series is an affordable opportunity to possess some of your favorite Nintendo characters in action figure form, as some of the Japanese imports can become quite expensive.

Samus here stands roughly 4 inches tall and is made of the typical plastic you find in most action figures. She sports 14 points of articulation. The head, arms, biceps, and ankles are swivel joints, with the knees, elbows, hips, and abdomen a nice ball type joint. Due to the sculpt, some of the range of motion is limited, and this is especially true in the hips. Despite this, Samus remains a very poseable figure, one which can easily be put in a wide array of poses.

The sculpt is very good. It looks like they've taken design cues from how her armor appeared in Metroid Prime, and there is a nice level of detail. The only possible complaint is the paint applications, which while effective, seem minimal on her abdomen. It also would have been nice to have a metallic sheen to this figure, but as it is, the figure looks very much like the plastic toy which it is. The figure appears a bit different from the one pictured, as Samus's head is much more nestled among her shoulder pads.

Play-wise, Samus looks like she could stand up to a fair amount of play, although if handled too rough, there might be issues with her knee and elbow joints as they appear a bit fragile. The mystery accessory Samus comes with is her ball form which she uses in the game. There's really not much to it - it's a roughly as round as a quarter, has appropriate detailing, and is made of a harder type of plastic. WARNING: If you plan on giving this to a child, the ball might pose a choking hazard.

All in all, this is probably the best figure the World of Nintendo has done to date, as it's superior to both the Link and Mario figure in my opinion. Be warned that this figure retails for about $7.99 - quite a difference in price from what most on-line sites are asking for it. There are approximately two Samus Aran's to a case, so she is fairly rare, but can be found with a bit of diligence. If you're a Metroid fan, or just a fan of Nintendo in general, I recommend this figure.s figure retails for about $7.99 - quite a difference in price from what most on-line sites are asking for it. There are approximately two Samus Aran's to a case, so she is fairly rare, but can be found with a bit of diligence. If you're a Metroid fan, or just a fan of Nintendo in general, I recommend this figure.

product_title: Redcat Racing Hurricane XTR Nitro Buggy, Yellow/Flame, 1/8 Scale
review_headline: Such a waste of time and money, Do Not Buy!
review_body: Bought one and felt very durable. Engine break in went fine, Ran once and was amazed, It was fast, fun, and smoked the competition. 3rd tank, not so much, would start randomly going full throttle, idle, and off. Engine would not tune at all, even the slightest adjustment caused the engine to die and not start. Took to a professional, $45.00 later he said non of their employees could tune it, and to send it back. (This is an experienced r/c shop where they race R/C Daily). So I sent it back and ordered a second. Started break-in of the motor, worked 30 sec, then went randomly full throttle, idle, and off. Restarted, and it idled 5 sec, went max throttle (on it's own), and a very loud Bang! Instantly stopped. Tried to start, and the friction was too easy and felt metal grinding on metal. Called redcat, they said I could only file a warranty claim online. So I painstakingly did. 48 hours later I finally get an email asking further info. The claims website they sent me to failed 8-9 times. Another 24 hours and no call, no response. I loved the car(s). But the motors failed on both, and their customer service at redcat needs a serious overhaul. There is no reason a simple phone call could not resolve the issue, but they won't deal with warranty issues on a phone???? What I will say, is I loved the car the one time I actually got to run it, but between bad parts and no customer service, DO NOT WASTE YOUR MONEY. Especially if you like to resolve a problem the quick, simple, old-fashioned way.

product_title: Perfect Barrier Card Sleeves
review_body:
KMC is a brand known for making top quality products and this is no different. For those of you who are unfamiliar with this product, this is the inner sleeve for double sleeving. These are similar to penny sleeve except they fit your cards almost perfectly; snug, but not to tight.

To double sleeve properly you would put these sleeves onto your card upside down (opening at the bottom of your card) then insert into your normal sleeves like normal (opening at top). I highly recommend either a KMC sleeve (especially super matte) or Dragonshield outer with these. These seem to fit the best together and also if you're going to be using an inner sleeve, why use a crappy outer.

These are designed for normal sized playing cards (Magic, Pokémon, etc) so if you're looking for Yugioh sleeves these are the wrong ones, though KMC does make them smaller for games sized.

product_title: TAIGEN 1/16 SCALE 2.4 Ghz SHERMAN M4A3 75MM (BB) by TaiGen
review_headline: As perfect as you can get for an RC Sherman
review_body:
For a long time I had a fascination with remote controlled tanks and a while back I had bought a $30 Heng Long 1/30 scale Sherman. While it was a great RC Tank for the price you paid, it still felt like a rather cheap toy and definitely was not durable enough to use outside. I wanted something that was larger and very well built. After doing my research I had decided on Taigen's 1/16th scale Sherman, and while yes it is quite an expensive piece compared to similar products on the market, I feel based on the outstanding quality of the tank it really is worth the extra price.

The construction is absolutely fantastic. A large percentage of the tank is made of metal which adds a surprising amount of heft to the model (it weighs somewhere in the neighborhood of 12 pounds). All of the tank's guts reside in a single piece metal 'tub' that makes up the lower chassis. The entire drivetrain is made of metal and the treads are very strong and downright gorgeous as well. All in all a very well designed and solid RC vehicle.

All of the unique features this model has really makes this tank even more worth it. The 360˚ turret rotation is fantastic and accurate to the real thing (most other tanks on the market only have around a 320˚ turret rotation range). The airsoft cannon and smoke unit work excellently and add a lot of fun realism to the tank. The onboard sound module really brings life to it and can be adjusted from whisper quiet to a shockingly loud roar (the speaker is of good quality too- definitely doesn't suffer from the 'tinny' sound other tanks have. It's nice and loud and bassy). Top speed is quite decent and it is also capable of a nice slow crawl as well.

The only thing that worries me with this tank is that due to the significant heft of the model I fear that the motors will face a lot more stress than the plastic versions. However because of how this tank is designed it looks to be extremely easy to work on, and a lot of replacement parts and upgrades are available from the manufacturer should anything fail. For instance, I am very interested in swapping out the stock 3:1 gearbox and putting in the 4:1 gearbox offered by the company to get more low end torque to climb over obstacles.

All in all I couldn't be more pleased with my purchase. The metal construction, all the realistic features, and the ease of maintenance make this pretty much the best remote controlled Sherman on the market. I was hesitant at first when I saw the price tag as there are less expensive options on the market, but after receiving my Taigen RC tank, I know it was worth every penny from how much I gained with this model. The only thing I need now is a Tiger or T34 that I can give to a buddy so we can have backyard tank wars!

review_body:
I'm impressed how fast these did the trick and got our son riding. I wish these toe clips would have come with our Kettler tricycle. My son was having a hard time keeping his feet on the pedals as they went around or would not continue to pedal. This is when the free wheel feature worked against us. A fixed pedal would force his feet around when pushed, to get him used to the motion. But he would just let his feet sit on the pedals and they free wheel.

These install easily. I tried another reviewer's suggestion to strap the velcro around the back of his sneakers, so he could not pull his feet out. That is definitely the way to go. He spent a few minutes pretty upset with me when he realized he was stuck in the clips and just stomped the pedals back and forth into the brakes. Then, after the first time he accidentally went forward, his eyes went wide open and he got quiet. Another 30 seconds of experimenting and he was flying around, having a blast. It took a few more sessions to get the reverse and K-turns down.

If I had known it would be that simple, I would have spent 3 times as much for these on day one.

product_title: The Lord of The Rings Confrontation
review_headline: One of the most fun 2 player Euro board games!
review_body:
We purchased this due to an employee recommendation at Guardian Games in Portland, Oregon. Big hug guys for the great recommendation!!!

The very first thing one should note is the designer of this game: Reiner Knizia (Ph.D in Mathematics). He has designed such terrific games as Lost Cities, Samurai, Tigris and Euphrates, and many more. Every game he designed which I have played combine a wonderful mix of accessibility and long term strategy. Much like Carcassonne, the strategy in these games is not quite obvious at first, but with time, one learns that there is much more to be learned while novices can still play an expert player and present a challenge.

This is a two player game.
The setup time is minimal (less than 5 minutes).
The game time is between 10 and 20 minutes each round.
Short learning curve, lots of additional strategies to learn.

The game plays out as follows: the players choose their side - Fellowship or Mordor. Each side has strengths and weaknesses. The Fellowship wins if Frodo enters Mordor or if no Mordor characters remain. Mordor wins if Frodo is defeated or if three Mordor players enter the Shire. The Fellowship character abilities focus on defeating particular Mordor characters or fleeing battle in various ways while the Mordor characters tend to rely on overwhelming strength or additional movement bonuses.

Each player takes turns moving a character. The characters are set in plastic holders so the opponent cannot see which they are until they are engaged. When an opposing player advances into a realm held by the other player's character a battle ensues. Unless there is an ability resulting in automatic defeat of another or retreat, combat ensues. Each player chooses an attack card, reveals it at the same time and players modify battle based on the text or the strength number of the revealed card. The character with the higher strength wins the battle, though there are cards which end in other results such as Noble Sacrifice which the Fellowship can play to end in defeat for both characters. The cards are discarded after use. Play continues until a result ends in a win for either side.

What makes this game unique are the variations in character abilities, card abilities and other little factors (such as the Fellowship characters able to use the Anduin River or the Mines of Moria to bypass certain regions). The Fellowship characters tend to have a bit better luck if they don't press the attack on the forces of Sauron, many abilities are used when defending against attackers and others have skills which defeat certain characters which makes it a bit foolhardy to randomly attack Sauron characters until you know who they are.

I typically recommend playing once as each side in a sitting. There are also a few tweaks which can be used to make the game easier or more challenging including a variant game. You can leave your discards facing up in a row so the opponent can see which cards you no longer have, or you can discard face down relying on their memory. Same goes for characters defeated in battle, you can leave them exposed or turn them upside down.

There is a lot of strategy and cunning - very similar to chess in a way. I won once with only two characters left, but my opponent rushed in and attacked Frodo who escaped sideways allowing a straight shot into Mordor but no opposing characters could attack him on the way to Mordor. Other things can be interesting and fun, such as putting a Mordor character on Caradhras and watching the Fellowship player squirm wondering if it is the Balrog or a different character who doesn't auto-kill anyone passing through Moria.

It is simple on the surface, quick and easy to learn, yet complex and fun to play over time. This isn't a game that gets old quick. Each game is a little different due to different character placements and different strategies.I recommend this for players 12 and up, or perhaps some younger players with adult guidance.

Fun: A+
Learning Curve: B+
Setup: A+
Replay: A

If you like fun 2 player games check out Rivals for Catan, Race for the Galaxy (incredibly complex), or Samurai (by Knizia also).I recommend this for players 12 and up, or perhaps some younger players with adult guidance.

product_title: Cheerson CX-10 Mini 2.4G 4CH 6 Axis LED RC Quadcopter Toy Drone
review_headline: Amazing how far technology has come
review_body:
Only $20-25 for an awesome toy! Be sure to calibrate accelerometer before first flight (place copter on flat surface, click left stick until 3 beeps, then move left stick to lower left and right stick to upper left until copter lights flash). Mine didn't fly correctly until I calibrated.

Very stable flight, and extremely nimble. I recommend flying in advanced mode (click left stick until 3 beeps) for full acceleration in all directions. You can even toss it randomly up in the air and when you apply throttle it will automatically stabilize itself right-side-up. Reasonably tolerant of hard crashes. My blades have been bent a few times but I could just bend them back... haven't needed to use any of my 4 spares yet. The flipping feature is very fun and reliable. Flies for about 5 - 10 min depending on how aggressively you fly, recharges in about 12 min.

Great value for the price, and a great gift!

product_title: 7 Wonders
review_headline: The game is good, but I'm not a big fan of competitive ...
review_body:
The game is good, but I'm not a big fan of competitive games. I really hate playing chess, for example. Any game that requires me to actively play against someone else (as in, doing things in the game to hurt or slow down the other player(s)) is a problem for me. This game is, of course, competitive but it is complicated enough that I feel I often can just play what is best for me and not feel like I am handicapping myself for not playing something that hurts another player. That's why I can give it three stars for me instead of less, but those lower ratings are not a sign of a bad game, just one that doesn't fit my style.

With that out of the way, I can say the game does seem to be very good. Almost everyone else I have played with has enjoyed it (but I play with a bunch of people who like competitive games and dislike co-operative games). The rules are a little complex and most new players ask the same questions many times their first game, but after their first game they really enjoy it and want to play another. My now-eight year old daughter (seven when I got this) likes the game and also only took the one play-through to fully understand the rules, however she still doesn't understand much of the strategy of the game and tends to be one of the low scorers.
I do like how many players it supports (7). That (combined with the other players' bias towards competitive games) is often why I bring this game out in place of others I have. That said, it plays two players as well but the "neutral city" seems to just be a dumping ground, with neither player actively thinking like that city and playing what is best for it.
