product_title: Vocaloid Hatsune Miku Kagamine Rin Len plush doll 11
review_headline: Wonderful Len and Rin dolls~!  Note that they are NOT authentic.
review_body:
First off, the Len and Rin Kagamine dolls that this listing is selling are knock offs. I can't find the real versions for sale so this was okay by me, although I normally like to buy licensed products as this encourages them to make MORE products! I just don't want anyone to be let down. Now on to the dolls! Please note that since I don't own the authentic plushies, I don't know if the things I describe are also present in the those as well.

First Len because he's my favorite. Len looks pretty good with embroidered eyes and facial features. His hair is felt except for his front tuft and his ponytail in the back. His little outfit looks pretty good considering the expected quality of a knock off. The only thing missing is that he doesn't have his belt, which annoyed me because with how short his shirt is, you can see that he is missing one. He DOES have the decorative belt that hangs down on the side which is nice. His little leg and arm warmers - computer terminal/speaker things are removable and look pretty good. His headphones are also felt and are nicely attached to his head.

Rin also has embroidered eyes and facial features. She has felt hair and barrettes and her bow is stuffed and nice and fluffy. Her clothing is also well done considering that she's a knock off with the exception of one little detail. Instead of a treble clef mark on her shirt, she has Len's bass clef. Weird. Rin DOES have a belt that looks nice as well as the decorative one. Her little leg and arm warmers -computer terminal/speaker things look just as good as Len's but aren't removable on mine. Rin's headphones are just like Len's.

All in all, I am very glad I bought these two. I really love Len and Rin and these can be loved on once I find the authentic ones. I highly recommend them for adult, teen, and older child collectors. Since these dolls have felt decorations that can be pulled off, I don't recommend them for young children due tosafety concerns.

product_title: 1 Ct. Card Sorting Tray for Sports - Gaming -Trading Cards
review_headline: Pretty much a must have if you have lots of collecter/trading cards.
review_body:
I've been trying to sort through my MTG cards for a while now. I tried just making stacks on a large table, but it was a nightmare cards got mixed up stacks fell over and I ended up more frustrated every time. Buying the card sorting tray really makes everything immensely easy.

PRO:
It has lots of slots to sort cards in quickly and easily I never seem to run out of room.
The four deck slots to the right are great for dividing up sets of cards like separating spell and creature cards.
The plastic while not invincible is sturdy enough for the job and you don't have to worry about breaking it in daily use.

CON:
While there are plenty of spots to sort cards the flat right corner doesn't do anything for the product and is wasted space considering you could have fit at least three more deck sorters in the same space.
I suggest either leaving the sticker on or covering it with a laminate or tape. I tried pulling it off and it left the space sticky from glue and trying to clean it with adhesive remover, just made it tacky and speared. I wouldn't want to place my cards on that spot now even if it served a purpose.

All in all a great product and essential to any card collectors/traders

On the more deluxe track sets, where you have multiple levels of train track, and mountains the cars go through, the animals stick out too far and prevent the train from going underneath the raised levels and the tunnels in the mountain pieces. The drive unit also doesn't have enough power to push the entire set up the ramp leading to the elevated levels. So, a bit of misinformation means a star is removed. product_title: Bandai Hobby #86 RX-93 Nu Gundam HGUC Action Figure
review_headline: This Nu Gundam isn't just for show.
review_body: For an older High Grade that came out in 2008, I've got to say that the Nu Gundam in 1/144 scale is a pretty solid build. It has no loose parts when I assembled it and I think it is the best adaptation of the mobile suit from the movie, \\"Char's Counterattack\\" (I own the Nu Gundam ver. Ka). It has a wide variety of movement and poseability but don't expect to get the range of its Master Grade variant since it has no inner frame. It can also hold all its accessories at once without trouble. It already looks good by itself but with some yellow and black paint to touch up the arms, legs, and waist armor, it would look even better.    Pros:  -Solid feel  -Accessories: beam rifle, new hyper bazooka, shield with missiles and beam cannon, beam saber, large beam saber, and its signature fin funnels (6x)  -Requires little paint and panel lining  -Anime accurate  -Can have 12 funnels attached to backpack if you have another HGUC Nu Gundam  -Fin funnels are secured when attached unlike the MG  -Joints are colored in a gunmetal color and not the typical gray of other kits    Cons:  -A bit back heavy and leans a little to the left when the fin funnels are attached which is natural  -Only comes with 2 sticker decals for the shield and shoulder (not a problem if you're looking for the anime look like me)  -No effect parts for funnels or stand to display them in action    Final Thoughts:  I would highly recommend getting this kit, it is not a hard build and the final product is solid whenever you hold it. If you're a fan of Amuro Ray, this is his final canon mobile suit in the anime and should be in your collection.    P.S. For a little bit more, you can get HGUC-93 which contains this kit with all accessories I listed as well as extra parts (armor, new rifle, and new shield).

product_title: Nerf Zombie Strike SlingFire Blaster
review_body:
This is a cool blaster. Not the best, by a long shot, but it is fun to play with. I recently had a Nerf battle with my nephews and used one of these for the majority of the time.

Pro's: lever action is really fun and compared to some Nerf blasters it allows you to get quick follow up shots off. It looks really cool. Size is good for most kids 7+ and also good for adults (the lever may not have a lot of space for fingers though). Fairly inexpensive, making it a good value. It feels well built.

Con's: Not very accurate, granted most Nerf blasters aren't accurate... however, this one is less impressive than most front loading $10 blasters. I shot a lot of darts (new ones, not old worn out ones) through it and on average about 1/3 went fairly straight to the point you could hit something. Comparing that to my $7 Doublstrike pistol, I would say it shoots as straight (or straighter) about 5/6 shots. The range is also a little underwhelming. I realize they design these for children, but I am sure Nerf could make these things shoot over 50 feet level and 100+ feet with an angle right out of the box if they wanted to do so. Several cheaper Nerf blasters outranged this and had better accuracy at our Nerf war, including some that cost half as much or less. Nerf also needs to start including more darts, its foam and rubber... I doubt they will lose a fortune by giving 2-3 times as many as they currently include and it would certainly make people much happier with the purchases. Larger magazines in this blaster make it look awkward in my opinion. The operation may be difficult for children to understand fully, causing them to get frustrated. You have to make sure the lever is all the way down/forward to get magazine in/out. The magazine release button is not designed well, it feels out of place and feels like it could work better for doing such a simple task. Sometimes when you pull the lever forward to cock the blaster it feels like you have it all the way forward and you still have to go another 1/2"+ to cock it. This blaster did jam more often than other blasters at our Nerf war, not entirely sure why, the ammo didn't appear defective nor did I load it differently. From my research, modifications don't add much of a performance increase like other blasters. If you want a mechanical blaster I would recommend some of the cheaper pistol style blasters (Doublestrike, Firestrike, Hammershot, Strongarm, etc...) or shotgun style blasters (Raider, Rampage or Roughcut), if you want electric I would recommend the Stryfe. All of those outperformed this and in the case of the magazine fed blasters, had less jams as well.

Overall, I do like the blaster and love using the lever action design. I think Nerf could improve on the design and make it a little more effective in the future. product_title: Cosmo Fleet Special Gerubadesu class Coleoptera combat Carrier Darorudo
review_headline: The other half of an awesome desk diorama.
review_body:
Pros: Pre assembled, great paint job with decals and panel lining, and cool accessories. Wow, these parts are stiff. OK, be very careful rotating the cannons by the turret (with your fingers) and do not push the 3 barrels. Only the 4 large cannons, all the other ones are glued down. The combat decks come as accessories, be very careful to pry off the deck by lifting the front enough to slide a fingernail underneath and sliding from front to back on one side, then the same on the other side. Continue lifting one millimeter at a time and sliding, front to back, until it pops off. Do the same with the rear deck. Before you install the rear combat deck, look at the underside of the deck and view the slot the cannon fits into. Push the center of the cannon up with your finger nail and swivel the cannon around to loosen it and point it at the back of the model in line with the other rear cannon, this will make it easier to install the deck.
On a side note: Ordered on a Sunday and received it on a Friday. Keep the box, by the way, it is a great transport and display at work. Also buy the Yamato, it makes a great mini diorama on your desk. Plus a separate drill missile comes with it, besides the heavy bomber -missile attached- to put into the wave motion gun.
Cons: Price, I know buyers remorse, but the Yamato is 15 bucks cheaper and the same size. Plus the Mecha size model was just released, is 5" long and around 8 bucks, while the 1:1000 scale model is 10 bucks cheaper and over a foot long.
As far as collectables go I cannot endorse this higher. It is a piece of art. If I could give it 3/4 of a star more I would. It also makes a great paint scheme template for when I build the other red models.

product_title: ThreeZero Game of Thrones: Tyrion Lannister Figure (1:6 Scale)
review_headline: Great addition to a diverse collection!
review_body:
From the moment I first saw a prototype of this figure, I knew it was a "Must Have" for me. And, I was glad to discover that the final product looked even better than I'd hoped.

I'm used to the highly stylized design of the ThreeA figures, so I was excited to see ThreeZero taking the photo-realistic approach to this figure. Based on initial prototype photos, I was worried there could be a stylized aspect of this figure ... something which I've found the Star Wars & G.I. Joe figures from Sideshow Collectibles having. The final head sculpt for a SC figure winds up a great representation of an artistic view of the character itself; but still retains that toy-like look.

While Tyion's head-sculpt falls just short of what you would expect from a company like Hot Toys, the realism of the face is definitely there ... with the expression being a good representation of the character. It's not a blank expression (like the HT Mandarin or some of attributed to the HT Black Widow). I think it's the paint on the hair that just comes up shy of making the hair look right even though I feel they made a good effort. Two of the recent SC figures I have (Baroness & Commander Wolfe) don't even have paint apps and are just single-colored hair ... which is why they have a much more toy-like quality to them. So, whereas I keep my SC and HT figures separated since I just don't think they look right together ... Tyrion fit in perfectly among the HT crowd. That, to me, is what determines if another company's final product is in the same league or not. Whether or not the product can hold it's own with the reigning champ.

The quality of the outfit just knocks it out of the park, in my opinion. I've read that the maroon fabric for the tunic could have been thinner ... to make it in-scale with the character ... and I can certainly see where that's coming from. The thickness of the fabric is something I might expect for a garment in 1:1 scale. Infact, it's roughly as thick as the fabric of an Eddie Bauer flannel shirt I have … which is significantly thicker than the fabric in my slacks or jeans. So, scaling the approximately 1/16" thick coat up to 1:1 scale would make it 3/8" thick. I just checked my leather motorcycle jacket ... and even the thickest area I could find (the heavily reinforced neck/collar) was still half that thickness. That means that 1:6 scale Tyrion is wearing some seriously thick/padded clothing. If the tunic could have been made to use fabric half as thick, that would have made for a more natural look. But, fabric thickness aside, the quality of the fabric is top-notch. A 1:1 scale tunic made from that fabric would be awesome. It just looks like the fabric from the real actor's costume was used for this miniature costume as well.

The hands are another common thing for people to point out. In-person, I didn’t think they look as bad as the photos I’d seen. Some photos I’d seen did make it look as rough as rough-sculpted clay. I see more defined details than that. But, the details are “stylized” and “linear” rather than realistic (i.e, details made by very distinct lines instead of more subtle plays of light/shadow, and texture). Up-close, they’re going to stand out. But, looking at the figure as a whole on display, I think they just blend in. There’s just so much else to like and don’t feel they distract from that.

While the dagger with the ThreeZero exclusive version certain adds some extra flair to his look, I am pleased with the inclusion of the goblet and the book. I’ve read that he’s the most “non-action” action figure you can have … which is certainly arguable. HT Alfred, business suit Bruce Wayne, Bruce Banner, and a business-suites Lex Luther all certainly come to mind as other good examples of that inaction figure model. And, I site those others not to put them down … but to illustrate that a character doesn’t have to look like an action figure to be cool. Mr. Lannister has a keen intellect. As the character essentially acknowledges in the show, he knows he’s not going to be the biggest, the strongest, or the fastest. But, he’s learned the importance of being the most intelligent person in the room. That's his strength. And, that’s why I like when these types of characters are created in figure form. If Tony Stark was just a man in a suit of armor, HT would only be making the armor. But, it’s the man inside the armor that really makes the character, which is why they wind up releasing different workshop figures. He’s a tinkerer. Literally a Mechanic. Mr. Lannister is a scholar from a family of great influence and wealth; all of which I feel this figure strongly conveys. While he did wear armor in the series at one point, this figure wouldn't have looked as good like that ... because the point of that portion of the storyline was that it was an absurd role for him to be thrown into ... even though it was a great way to show just how much fortitude he did have. This shows the character when he's in his element. Knowledge, libations, and finery.

I’m also glad that ThreeZero started with this figure. Not just because it’s my favorite character from the GoT series … but because it’s nice to have even more diversity in the 1:6 landscape. While I saw that Sideshow had previously released Frodo and Samwise figures, didn’t see where a Gimli was ever released. We’ve had 3 movies about The Hobbit … featuring a Hobbit and a multitude of Dwarves … but no 1:6 figures yet that I’m aware of. I understand that custom tooling is expensive … especially at that scale (3-3/4” remains the one scale composed of the broadest diversity). But, it still seems like with a massive multi-movie series available … whose LOTR series already proved to be a huge success … there was enough to warrant the creation of a buck for a little person. So, I applaud ThreeZero for taking the initiative and making it happen. Perhaps others will follow suit … or be able to work out an arrangement to use the same buck themselves.

Hands and cloth-thickness aside … I couldn’t be happier with how this figure turned out. And, can’t help but marvel at how such a high-quality product could be released for what’s fast becoming an unheard of bargain. As one review remarked, despite the character’s size, the overall cost of the figure production would have been the same as a 12” figure … but yet the figure was significantly cheaper than what’s becoming the baseline price for a HT figure. I know licensing costs can be a major factor (my ThreeA Halo Spartans are significantly bigger than a HT Iron Man but actually cost much less) … but I also suspect it’s a case of economy-of-scale. ThreeZero may be a smaller company by comparison and therefore have less overhead cost; therefore allowing them to sell product at a much lower cost.

Only thing to watch out for … because it just happened to me … is, if you pose Tyrion holding his book, be careful when you’re carrying him from one table to another; being sure to support the book. Mine just slipped out of his hand, landed on the corner of the table, and took out a chip along the corner of the book; right where it's visible as he holds it. Will need to see what I can do to correct that. But, it did reveal the type of material it’s made out of can be chipped if you’re not paying attention.

If you’re a fan of the series … and in particular of this character, I would highly recommend this figure. The exclusive edition with the dagger will be more expensive naturally on the secondary market if that’s the edition you are most interested in. But, if you look to see if anybody starts parting out the figure, you may actually find that it’s cheaper to buy it separately and just add it to the regular edition of the figure (I was able to do that with the HT Dark World Loki and the exclusive Ether accessory).

I personally like how his royal look makes him stand out when among modern-looking characters. But, I found his look to be a great visual pairing with the HT Angelica figure … or with the Dark World Thor (cloaked) and Loki ... to display him with similarly-dressed characters.

It adds another dimension to any already diverse 1:6 scale landscape that ranges from diminutive character like Yoda to a gargantuan character like Hulk. Different heights. Different builds. Lots of variety. Each figure being a good representation of the character and actor they reflect.

product_title: Munchkin Panic
review_body:
I really enjoyed Munchkin Panic after a few two player games. While the game initially seems confusing due to the sheer number of pieces, rules, and 'order-of-play' steps it ultimately is a very simple game.

Munckin Panic is a mashup of two existing games, Castle Panic and Munchkin. I have prior experience with Munchkin games and that was the driving influence in selecting this product. In practice, I would describe the game as a social, lane based, tower defense game.

Essentially, the game spawns enemies of various strength in different lanes. The monsters each turn move one space forward. The board is divided into three colored sections. The player uses 'treasures' and 'heroes' to combat the encroaching monsters. Players win by killing all of the monsters and collecting the most 'trophy points' from the slain monsters. Monsters win by destroying your castle at the center of the board. These 'treasures' and 'heroes' all have various limitations that allow them to only attack certain parts of the board. This limitation is the key design mechanic that drives the social aspect of the game.

Central to the social game play is a 'negotiation' step, whereupon players are allowed to assist each other during the 'attack' phase. This is essential to defeating the monsters and winning the game. The rules are open ended and the game actively encourages players to be creative. So you can negotiate for any sort of reward whether it be an in game or out of game reward. So players must balance the good of the group with their own self desires to be the overall winner.

Ultimately, Munchkin Panic will be only as much fun as your friends. The game is pretty dry when played solo. The game play is basic and threadbare. The game humor will wear thin after a few plays. But, the social aspect will never get old if you have a good group of people to play with. So, for anyone that fits that criteria, I would definitely recommend Munchkin Panic.

review_headline: This looks like the original Mold we used

I used to make these for the show! This looks like the original Mold we used.
Exact Accuracy is 2" Tall by 1 5/8" wide! product_title: Melissa & Doug Water Wow Activity Book - Alphabet
review_body: My daughter loves to color, but she's still young enough that this means scribbles a crayon over a drawing and moves on. She's also a bit of a perfectionist, and gets mad when her drawings don't turn out right. We have a picture of a potato somewhere that looks like someone took it to the shooting range and fired crayons through it, because it didn't look *enough* like a potato.    These \\"coloring\\" books are a great deal, especially for on-the-go. Unlike other \\"magic picture\\" type books, these use simple water pens. You fill them with water and the brush-nib dispenses it. There are no special pens that dry out, and the images come out in color (as appropriate), instead of that grey color. The books can be re-used when dry, though it is hard to find an elegant way to dry them at once. The pages curl a bit, especially if you have an over-saturator, but are sturdy and last well.    The only design flaw - and this is a miniscule little quibble - is that, while the book has a nice little snap-on case for the water pen, it's located smack in the middle of the front cover. It would be nice if it were located in some other way so that the books are easier to stack, or slip into a bag. Still, they do keep the water pens right at hand for travel. And if worse comes to worse, a cup of water and a Q-tip might work as well.

review_headline: Excellent Basic Math Skills and Number Tracing For Toddlers
review_body:
I have five kids aged 2-7 and found that this game is well-suited to my younger kiddos.

The games revolve around sorting by size, counting, basic measuing by "ruler", dragging lines to make basic shapes and more.

The games are definitely geared toward younger learners. The recommended age is 3-5, but you might get away with a bit younger, and the higher end of that age range would be pushing it.

One of the games, for example, gets kids to pick which of three options is a number versus a letter. Others have you tracing lines to draw the number. Those skills in particular are aimed at very young kiddos.

Not to say that's bad; just know what you're getting into by buying this. I thought it was great for my 2 and 3 year old and would definitely recommend it for anyone in that age range!

I was concerned about that before purchasing it; I didn't want something that would encourage him to just sit and watch. With this set, he is constantly getting up and down, stretching, turning, and even running around the track to beat the train to the gates. Our padded 8' x 12' area rug in the family room is perfect for this purpose and can be see from the kitchen so mom can keep an eye on him while cooking and cleaning.

This toy has turned out to be his favorite. Not only does he love to help the train go around the track by putting gates up and down, trying to turn the crank (which we must help with), loading the cargo, etc. but his very favorite thing to do is put the track together himself. He will play for an hour or two putting it together and taking it apart, all the while happier than a pig in mud, lol! At bedtime, we literally have to take it away, which he's not too happy about.

There are several configuration options with this track and the hand cranked ramp does not have to be included in all of them, which can encourage independent play for the young ones.

I am purchasing more vehicles and the add-on tracks simply because he enjoys this toy so much. Way to go, Vtech!

product_title: Scalextric 1:32 Curved Curbs and Barriers
review_body:
This set serves really 2 purposes
A) Helps protect cars from damage after coming off the track
B) Significantly improves aesthetic appearance

Some points to setup.

The borders clip onto the track. The barriers slot into the borders.

to be clear. You should
A) use the black tabs and plug in the barrier to the black tab. Put the black tab to flat side down.
B) Space the tabs so that a barrier post fits into each.
C) Once you have 3 barrier posts plugged into a tabs (Each barrier has 3 posts) then snap the tabs into the outside of the track.
D) the kerbs are designed for scalextric 'C' size curves. The most common.
E) Spacing is tricky to work out, each curb runs the length around a single 'C' size track, although the barrier is longer, therefore you tend to have a loose piece of barrier unless you have some straight kerbs to hook it too. So its not perfect. but not a bid deal.

I deduct a point because of lack of decent instructions and the typical mis fitting of barrier to kerb to track as described above

product_title: The Learning Journey Match It! Games
review_body: These matching puzzles are great for kids learning to read. My 3 year-old loves the First Words Match It!. She had a little trouble at first because she just wanted to put them together without matching them up. Then I showed her that each one had a word that matched and she was fascinated. I would have to say I don't think all children would be that fascinated with it. She enjoys guessing what a word says and then telling people but she's always enjoyed words. When she was 2, she loved to sit down with the dictionary, point at words, and pretend to read it even though she couldn't read the words. I know, it's a strange thing for a 2-year-old to do. But my 1 year-old daughter and 1 year-old niece both enjoyed playing with them too and looking at all the pictures. They are very sturdy, great quality. The box they come in is also sturdy for a cardboard box and it has a handle on the top so your child can put them all away and carry it around like a suitcase. There are 30 matches (60 puzzle pieces) and they are all different so each puzzle piece can only be paired with its matching piece.

review_body: One of my gaming group's favorites is Catan. We played through C&K a few times (and I have played with C&K rules several times on PC) but the original is much more fast paced and fun. If we want complexity or depth, we play something else. If you're looking to add variety for Catan, the Seafarers expansion adds a lot of options without adding a ton of new rules. I purchased this expansion first, but in retrospect, I wish I would have just gone with Seafarers instead. Also, as a side note, I really hate the marketing scheme that is used for Catan's 5-6 player line of expansions.

product_title: Bora Bora Strategy Board Game
review_body:
We've had great fun playing Bora Bora in my household. The game has a very nice mix of Eurogame mechanics and American dice rolling. I'd say the game is more complex than Settlers of Catan but with the help of several good online tutorials we were playing in an hour or so.

The game is really beautiful The board is full of color and geographically interesting land forms. As mentioned in another review, the board has no writing on it which I think is a plus. The symbols will be readily recognizable by many gamers and are easy to pick up. All of the components are good quality and chalked with theme. All of the game mechanics are well thought out and very tight. There are many paths to winning and players can focus on various strategies to win.

I'd say this game is most like Puerto Rico, another game we love. Also, Bora, Bora scales well to two players. If you are looking for Monopoly or Clue, this game isn't for you. If you are interested in delving more deeply into the world of Eurogames or gaming in general, this game can be allot of fun.

product_title: Learning Resources Pretend & Play Calculator Cash Register
review_headline: Concept and feature set great, but quality and execution lacking.
review_body: This is potentially a great learning toy that can grow with a child for a long time.  Unfortunately a few things keep it from reaching it's potential.  First of all, it only beeped when pushing a button for a couple of days before it stopped working.  I replaced the battery with a new, $5 battery, and it still doesn't work.  Secondly, it's great that the calculator is solar powered, but it really needs to have a battery, and perhaps a back light.  This thing only works well in direct, BRIGHT light.  The money that you save not buying a $1 AA battery once a year is more than offset by having to have all of the lights up bright in your house to be able to play with this toy.    Positives:  Great for teaching math and money skills.  I love that the drawer can accommodate real-sized money.    I just wish that it would work without having to keep it pointed at the sun, and that the beeping feature would hold up more than one weekend.    Waiting for a replacement.  I'll update review if the new one works better.

product_title: Deadzone
review_headline: Great skirmish game that hits all the right notes.
review_body: Mantic is doing a great job making the type of games that Games Workshop used to. Deadzone is a skirmish game that pits small gangs/squads of different factions against one another, similar to games like Infinity (from Corus Belli) or the Venerable Necromunda (from Games Workshop, based on Warhammer 40K Second Ed.).  Let's get the negatives out of the way first. I put these up front, becuase there are VERY few and i'll admit they are a bit nitpicky -- there is much to like!  First, The diecut tokens for the game are a bit on the cheapish side, so if you're spoiled by Fantasy Flight-grade cardboard bits, you'll feel a little 'meh' about these. The punch on mine was so bad that I had to take up the X-Acto and trim many of them out, to prevent them from tearing.  Next, If you're not an experienced modeler/painter, the figures are going to be a bit daunting. The figures are not injection molded plastic, but cast resin. There are no instructions for assembly and the minis require a moderate-to-high amount of prep to assemble (the resin requires a lot of trimming, clean up and reshaping before you even can get to the point of gluing them together and painting).  and that's it for the negatives, seriously!  The Great:  * Playmat is genius, it's like a giant Mousepad. More games should use this concept. It helps with shaky models and it won't slide around the tabletop. * The plastic terrain is fantastic. Mantic could go into business selling this modular terrain alone.  The rules are fast, simple and spot-on. Deadzone distills aspects from the tactical games genre and finds simple solutions for mechanics that can be needlessly complex in other systems. The way Deadzone handles movement, cover and line of sight is pitch perfect, in my opinion. The small play area gets units into the frey quick and once you get the rules down, you can easily play a game in an hour time frame.  ADDENDUM: Knocked a full star off, due to the fact that my copy was missing the Captain & Specialisttroops for my enforcer faction. product_title: Rokenbok ROK Works Construction & Action Set
review_headline: A hit for girls and boys, Easy operation, Fun for all ages, Teaches Engineering and Physics through play
review_body:
We were watching various review videos one day and our five year old daughter decided that this toy was the one she would ask Santa for. At first we balked at the price, and if we did invest it would need to be a joint gift for both of our children. We decided that this starter set had the most bang for buck with the structure, controller, and vehicle (and ours came with an additional block building set as part of a bonus holiday special [[ASIN:B00PBB0MSI Rokenbok Maker Gadgets]]). Our daughter is too young yet to put the structure together herself, but was excited to help sort and hand-off pieces to her dad as he built. It was she who learned how to work the controller before anyone else, and she taught her two and a half year old brother how to use it. The controller's red light makes aiming very easy for both of them. Though it is hard to hear, especially on carpet, the vehicle beeps when it backs up! He tends to over work the vehicle so we tend to steer him to keeping the conveyor full. The rocks are pretty tough as I've sucked up a few in the vacuum and retrieved them unscathed. Though our children are not mouthers, it is reassuring that the rocks have an open design for airflow -- really clever since it makes them lighter using less material and makes them safer.

Except for the vehicle, this set can be played with without batteries (and we built a few awesome things with the bonus blocks we got which has no electronic components). It has been so popular with us big kids too, that we decided to invest in another set for the toddlers next birthday. Because of his age, we are going to focus on the vehicle that pushes rather than has a lift or dumping action to keep it simple for him (and to curb the arguments over the one controller). Be advised that though the set is not hard to put together, it is more complex than Leggo blocks and will take time. However, it is well designed and we love that there are no on off switches since it powers down on its own, and the conveyor stops when empty. This really saves on batteries, but we strongly suggest investing in rechargeable batteries. They will more than pay for themselves.

Really our only minor complaint (or a wish) is that the vehicle had free-wheeling mode so it could be pushed along manually. Other than that we are pleased that this toy is designed to grow with the kids and they will have it for years, which makes the investment well worth it.

Tip: Laminate the instructions so they'll last. We go economical and use clear contact paper.its own, and the conveyor stops when empty. product_title: Hanabi Card Game
review_headline: Exercise in frustration and too much work
review_body:
I am always on the hunt for good 2 player games. After reading so many great reviews I went ahead and purchased this at a local game shop. Unfortunately this game has ended up being an exercise in frustration and I find that it requires so much concentration and memory that it is tiring to play. I'm not sure how so many people have loved this game, but for me it has not been an enjoyable game to play. I find that my memory is not that great (or perhaps I don't have a good strategy to remember the clues) and therefore I get frustrated with myself and forget clues. I get frustrated when a card is discarded that ends a fireworks series. There is a lot of logic and deduction involved which I find taxing. There is no winning or losing but just how many points you are able to get at the end so I find the end of the game to not be very satisfying.

We also own Lost Cities which also ends up being a frustrating game to me and evokes similar feelings. If you don't have the right cards at the right time, you end up having to discard and lose some points. I find that Hanabi has that same element and therefore ends up being a game that is more frustrating and less enjoyable.

For some people it seems this game is great, (and even won a Spiel des Jahres which I find surprising) but for me it is definitely not my cup of tea. If you are like me and don't enjoy having to do a ton of memorization, logic, and deduction during a game, then I don't recommend this game.

review_headline: After I was comfortable with the controls I flipped it into expert mode ...
review_body: If you're used to just flying something that just kinda hovers there this is something that has far more control even in normal mode. It took me a couple of days to get used to flying it as often as I could to get it to just hover, and to get it to land where I wanted it to.  So worth it though! After I was comfortable with the controls I flipped it into expert mode and wished I'd done sooner, this thing is extremely agile and will really take off and stop itself on a dime.  The only complaint I have is our current battery technology that doesn't keep up with this quad copter.  240mAH will only go for a few minutes and 380mAH last a few more but also make it a little more sluggish to fly.  The Hubsan X4 was recommended to me for beginners and as a beginner I found that it's the perfect quad copter to start out with before you buy or build something that costs hundreds or thousands of dollars.  5 stars from me!

product_title: Fascinations Metal Earth Star Wars: AT-AT Model
review_headline: Tricky to build, but awesome result.
review_body:
I snapped up all of the Metal Earth Star Wars models last week because it seemed like they were becoming scarce. This one was not the first model I built, but it was very tricky. I'm pretty meticulous, but I made a few mistakes which resulted in a broken AT-AT head. Luckily, I was able to finagle it back into place and no one will notice but me. I also broke some tabs off one of the leg pieces just removing it from the metal sheet. Again, I just kept going because I figured no one else would ever notice. They really ought to warn you better about "do this before that" type situations... if you seal up the body before attaching the head, there is no way to get the head attached! Sounds obvious, but it isn't clear in the instructions.

TL;DR: other reviewers are right, the pieces are fragile and the instructions are unclear, but man I love seeing this AT-AT on my shelf.

product_title: Mega Bloks First Builders Build'n Go Wagon
review_headline: Good basic wagon for a small toddler
review_body:
My son got this as a one year birthday present. He is now 16 months and enjoys it. The wagon is big and because it has big wheels, it is easy for him to push on many surfaces (we have carpet and this does fine on it). It goes over bumps easily. It can hold more blocks than what it comes with. Really, even though it is compatible with Megabloks and has places to attach those, he enjoys more putting other things, like stuffed animals, into it. He also tries to climb into it, but since the bottom of the bin is narrow, he gets uncomfortable and fusses when he makes it in. It shouldn't be used to hold a child. It's sturdy to hold up to toddler play, but light weight and just not designed to put a child in.

Overall, this is a good wagon for a very small child. They can put things in and out of it and then use it to push or pull those things around.

product_title: 100 Piece Dinosaur and Cave Man Prehistoric Playset with Play Mat and Storage Container by Imagination Generation
review_headline: Buy this is you want broken and cracked dinosaurs
review_body: I was really disappointed by how it was packed and by the actual item itself.  As another reviewer noted, this was not packed well.  The item arrived with only one square of "air pack" that was totally busted so there was no cushion at all for the product inside the box.  I am not sure if this contributed to the broken items inside the bag of dinosaurs.  As another reviewer experienced, I also had quite a few dinosaurs that were damaged with large cracks in the tail and body.  In addition, this set came with almost more trees than dinosaurs and many of the dinosaurs were duplicates (i.e. doubles and triples of the same dinosaurs).  There were a lot of very small dinosaurs and only 6 "massive" dinosaurs.  I don't think "massive" is an accurate description, but at least they were big enough to hold.  Too bad most of them were cracked.  I ordered this for my 1 1/2 year old for Christmas and he was really excited to play with it, but since the small dinosaurs were so small, I had to take those and the cavemen away since they were choking hazards for him.  For nearly $40, I was really disappointed with the quality of the dinosaurs and the trees and cavemen.  I felt like I paid a lot for a big bag of cheap plastic pieces most of which arrived broken.  The dinosaurs are hollow, so if anyone steps on one by accident, it will break easily (2 of them have met this fate within the first week of owning this).  If this item were $10-15 dollars, then I wouldn't have been so disappointed.  I would consider buying a different dinosaur pack that had better quality dinosaurs (i.e. not hollow, cheap plastic that cracks).  Hopefully the seller will do a better job of packing this item for anyone that decides to purchase this.  It is possible that the poor packing job also contributed to the items inside being broken.  The concept was nice, but the execution was not.  Save your money for a higher quality dinosaur set.  This one was way overpriced for what it was.The pics are much more impressive than what you actually receive.

product_title: Timeline - Americana
review_headline: Time for some fun with time
review_body:
Timeline - Americana is based on a simple concept: the players compete on the basis of their knowledge of American history across a broad range of categories. There are 110 cards in the game pack. One side has a historic event, such as when Facebook was founded, when did Jackie Robinson sign with Brooklyn Dodgers, when did the elephant become a symbol for the Republican Party, etc.; the other side has the year the event happened. Illustrations on the cards add to character of the game.

Gameplay is relatively simple. Players are dealt a selection of cards, keeping them face up, and then one card is taken from the remaining draw stack and placed date side up. Players go around the table (the game suggests 2-8 can play), with the first taking a turn to place one card from their selection next to the card that begins the game. If they think the event on their card is earlier, they put it on the left side; later, they put it on the right. Only then do they turn it over to see if they're correct.

If correct, play passes to the next player with the new card remaining on the table in what becomes the timeline as more cards are put down. If wrong, the player puts the card back in the box and draws a replacement card from the draw stack of remaining cards. Then the next player takes their turn. As more cards are added to the timeline, each new card has to be placed where it is between all those that have earlier dates and all those that have later dates. (Matching years can be put on top of a card already in the timeline.) The first player to successfully place all of his or her cards in the correct order on the timeline is the winner. If the stack of remaining cards in the draw pile runs out before that happens, the cards in the discard pile can be reshuffled into a new draw stack.

This is deceptively simple at first - but it gets harder as new cards are added to the timeline and it gets longer. Info with the game suggests it can be played out in around 15 minutes. 4 cards per player are suggested for a normal hand, but when there are fewer players, more cards can be dealt initially to extend game play. A player who gets cards spread over a long date range may have an easier time placing them than a player who gets cards in a cluster of events - so luck of the draw is a factor as well. The rules list the game as being suitable for ages 8 on up - but older ages may have problems with the small size of the cards and the print on them. (Which suggests a large print edition as a possibility?) The reason for the small card size is to keep the space needed for a growing timeline to a practical minimum. The game can be played anywhere there's a flat surface to build the timeline on.

The educational aspect of the game is obvious, but it's still fun; having to place the cards in the correct time sequence helps create an awareness of how events in American history fall across time, something just playing with flashcards wouldn't. There's a broad enough mix of events in different categories that there should be things to interest every player. While it is possible a player could memorize all of the cards over time, there's still a lot of gameplay before that should happen.

All in all, a simple but fun game, packed in a nifty metal case. Will there be expanded card packs in the future, or decks for different areas of world history? product_title: Bandai Hobby #02 Gafran "Gundam Age" 1/144 - High Grade Age
review_headline: easy to build;  difficult to pose without a stand;  not many colors
review_body:
This was my second gundam model, the first being an HG Genoace II. I chose this model because it's likewise from Gundam AGE line and because it was less than $10 ($9.69 when I bought it; $8.31 as of the writing of this review), which in my mind is a great deal with it's eligibility for prime shipping.

Construction took longer than the Genoace II, on the order of three-ish hours, although some of that may be attributed to the fact that my eyes were dilated during the construction process. I had no trouble with the stickers, although there were a few times where I installed pieces backwards and had to disassemble/reassemble. Unlike the Genoace II, there were no leftover pieces on the sprues after construction.

The completed Gundam shows a lot of blue and grey, with the single trans-green chest piece almost entirely hidden, and the green sticker for the head barely visible. I wish they could've thrown in some more colors, maybe a lighter shade of grey to make it pop more, but it's not too bad as is.

The height of the model is slightly greater than that of the Genoace II, due to the Gafran's longer legs and taller head. In general, the poseability of the model isn't great, but isn't bad. The ankles are sorely limited in their degrees of freedom, and most ground poses will involve at least one of the feet not flat. The wings/skirt do get a little in the way, but not too much. The elbows don't bend much more than 90 degrees, but the hands aren't meant to hold weapons (they are the weapons), so the limited articulation there is acceptable. The tail cannon has little articulation side to side, so it's hard to make it point anywhere other than forwards or a few degrees left or right from forwards with some altitude. The articulation of the hand cannons is a really nice feature considering the size and grade of the model.

The transformation into flight mode is pretty nice, with a few exceptions. The wings and boosters get in the way for any pose in which the wing surface is parallel to the body, and the elbows just seem a little unnatural when they bend forwards. The shoulders also look a little awkward. The head articulation and fold out canard wings are very nice looking in flight mode, and the flip out claws on the back legs is a nice touch. In the absence of a stand, posing the Gundam in flight mode provides mediocre results at best.

In general the Gundam holds together pretty well, although my open hands somewhat consistently fall out of their sockets and moving the legs too much while posing can knock the skirts off. The tail/spine and wing/spine connections are a bit flimsy, and have the tendency to slide out a bit during posing.

I have yet to try panel lining, but I don't feel as if it'd be very effectual considering the already dark colors of the model. I've experienced no broken pieces yet. Overall, I consider this Gundam a great deal for it's price, and am considering purchasing another to double the size of my enemy force

product_title: Scattergories Game
review_headline: A game full of fun and laughs!
review_body:
I received this product from House Party in exchange for a fair and honest review.

Scattergories is one of my families favorite games. What I like about it is it is not too complicated for the younger kids (as long as they can read and write, so I'd say it's perfect for 7 and up) but just as fun for us older folk too. There are 12 category cards. You start by picking a number, and all players flip to that card. The dice is rolled, and whatever letter it lands on, you have to think of words that start with that letter and match the category. Say the dice lands on M and the category on your card is animal. You would write something like "monkey". It's fairly simple, but so many laughs can be had when you hear what other players come up with! I would highly recommend this game to anyone who likes to play board games!

review_body:
Not at all what the photo shows. You would assume the cable would be of the semi-rigid type, but it is a very poorly thrown together product. A reach out from the seller with an offer of a replacement would be nice, but I won't press the matter and will likely go with a different brand.

EDIT: Today the connector and coaxial cable came loose. These are the \\"crimp down\\" connections, apparently, and aren't even crimped properly. product_title: Pioneer Custom DIY Play Set Hardware Kit (wood not included)
review_headline: It's OK but the price is a tad bit high for the finished project.
review_body: Ok...so you are looking for a swing set and see this puppy for $69 or so dollars and think...Wow, that's cheap.  Well, think about this.  1) the slide does not come with the swing set...you get to pay more for that later, and 2) All that wood, well that's extra too!.  So my cost was around $69 for the basic swing seats, chains and hooks, $175 for the wood, $12 for a bucket of 3 inch screws, $24 for two sets of stabilizing brackets (highly recommended) and $0 for a slide....I ran out of money and opted to not put a slide in.  Instead, I created a lower deck and left it for a play house/platform.  You won't need to stake this thing down because it is so heavy.  Best part of the experience was when the granddaughter ran outside and seeing for the first time said with a stutter "Amazing".  Not bad for a 3 year old.  Make sure you have someone to help you lift, screw and bolt the project together.  I also recommend drilling and counterboring the main beam and installing the swing hooks before you put it all together.

Two is that at several points I looked down at the play cards and realized what I'd had were pretty boring - that is to say, there are certain topics that are heavy on the questions in that range - sex naturally high among them.  I really did like that there was a sort of strategy as to which play cards you might want a certain erson to answer or that you might want to return as you yourself might not want to have to answer.  In the end, we sat around and just pulled play cards and answered them and talked about it, and that actually was a hoot!

product_title: Bandai Tamashii Nations "Mazinger Z" Super Robot Chogokin Action Figure
review_headline: A great Mazinger Z for your money
review_body:
This is Mazinger Z from the Super Robot Chogokin Collection. This is an incredibly sculpted and articulated figure based on Mazinger Z from the original series. This figure only stands at 5.5\\", but you get a lot for your money with this figure.

The sculpt of this figure is short of awesome. This figure is die cast in metal and plastic. His arms are removable and can be used with the Mazinger rocket effects included in the Mazinger Weapon Set, sold separately. The fists can also be removed and replaced with any of the extra 6 hands included in this set. The back of the robot has a hole to attach a Jet Scrander included in the Mazinger Weapon Set or from other figures of the Super Robot Chogokin Collection.

The paint job is very well done and it matches the coloring scheme of the original show. Mazinger Z is painted red on chest plates, black on upper torso, shoulders and waist, deep blue on forearms, fists, legs and feet, and silver on arms, lower torso and thighs. Even the tinny pilder is painted red, with blue on the windshield. No run offs to be seen.

The articulation is also amazing:
- ball-jointed head, ball-jointed neck,
- double ball-hinged shoulders,
- double hinged and swivel elbows, ball-jointed wrists,
- ball-jointed upper torso,
- ball-jointed lower torso,
- ball-hinged hips, swivel tights,
- ratchet knees, ball-jointed ankles.

This figure also includes a lot of accessories:
3 open right hands (1 holding weapon, 1 open and 1 dramatic open)
3 open left hands (1 holding weapon, 1 open and 1 dramatic open)
1 reinforced right forearm
2 reinforced right hands (1 fist and 1 dramatic open)
1 sword
1 hover pilder in docking position
1 tab (for posing base not included)

Overall, this figure screams quality. There was no pose I could not achieve with this figure. On top of that the price point at ~$40 is really good. And if you later want to get the rocket effects, you can buy them separately for less than $12, which is a good deal all around.ter want to get the rocket effects, you can buy them separately for less than $12, which is a good deal all around.

product_title: Fascinations ICONX Notre Dame Cathedral 3D Metal Model Kit
review_body:
This was an interesting build due to the larger sized sheets and the number of pieces. I did it over a period of three days, working on a few steps at a time. I'd estimate it took four hours total. For the most part it went okay but there were a few issues.

First, there are three different pics of this model. The one on Amazon (also on the top back of the box) is not what this looks like. That one is less detailed for the most part except for the steeple. The one on the front, inside and lower back of the box is the way the model is supposed to look. This is different than the 360 degree pic on the Fascinations website as that has the two little pointy top pieces in the rear instead of the front of the tower tops. They are supposed to be in front. This means steps 11 & 12 in the instructions have piece 32 on the wrong side. Unfortunately I did not realize that until later. As a result, the two 32 pieces are on the back side of my towers as instructed in step 19 (which also has the labels "Step 15" & "Step 16" reversed). The person who built the model used for the 360 degree pic possibly realized the towers would be backwards and rotated them but that left the pointed pieces on the wrong side. All this could have been avoided if Fascinations had left all four sides the same. So to sum up this issue use the pic on the front of the box as your reference. As a side note, a few of the "teeth" at the tower tops are missing, which is also the case in the website's 360 degree pic.

The other two issues involve the flying buttresses. First, the top ends do not attach or at least fit into slots so they are OCD cringe-worthy as I can spend all day trying to adjust them to look perfectly straight and lined up. Second, many of them were attached to the metal sheets in terrible places causing removal and aesthetic issues.

Despite all this moaning and groaning it is a really nice model that looks great when finished. It was a bit challenging but not too much and yes it was repetitious forming all those buttresses and twisting all those tabs. But it was definitely worth it. I took two stars off due to the issues above but added one back due to how nice it looks finished.

product_title: Wahii WaterSlide 75 - World's Biggest Backyard Lawn Water Slide!
review_headline: Great Fun but a lot of work
review_body:
This slide is incredible fun. Everyone loves it, we've had 3-year-olds on it and 60-year-olds. Anyone who is not riding is usually video-recording and howling with laughter!

***Some important notes on setup: It is secured to the ground using the included "hardware" (U-brackets & plastic cards) AFTER you connect all the cards to the slide using Tape. This is a tedious and time-consuming process. Each time you set it up, you'll need to replace some tape. The old spot where the tape was is now covered in adhesive and old grass. Plan more than an hour the first time you set it up, and 30 minutes each subsequent time.

Tape is REQUIRED for use. I have only had success using the "Tough & Wide" Gorilla Tape. You need about 18" of tape for each of the 15 (I think) fasteners, so have a full roll on hand. That's about 20' - 25' of tape! You'll need a few more feet each additional time you set it up.

Also, plan multiple sprinklers to keep it watered! Bottom Line: Tons of fun and tons of work!

product_title: Great Planes Bench Topper Workbench Organizer
review_headline: Good product design, terrible execution with poor quality die cutting used throughout.  Buy the pre-assembled kit instead.
review_body:
The kit design and product features are good. This is why I bought it. It has great features to store and organize the tools you use most regularly to build kits.

The build quality of the kit, however, was extremely poor. The wood is plywood and they used die cutting throughout. The quality of the die cutting was extremely poor. In most instances the cuts only go half-way through the thickness of the plywood. This means that you will need to cut every edge of every piece using an xacto knife. Cutting through plywood with an xacto knife is extremely tedious and time consuming. It is tough on your hands, and you will likely wear out many blades. Doing this for several circular cutouts was extraordinarily difficult.

Because the die cutting was so poor, when you do finally cut out all of the pieces you will find that many of the edges are semi-crushed, and part of the edges of the plywood are torn out. This makes gluing the pieces together more challenging than it needs to be. Bottom line for me is that I would not recommend that you buy this kit unless you see that they have switched to laser cutting the pieces. Until then, buy the pre-assembled version of this kit if you must have this.

product_title: LeapFrog LeapTV Educational Gaming System
review_headline: Not a sponsored review! Disappointing. HDMI only output. Poor design choices.
review_body: This started out as a three star review but as I've revised it downward as I write. This system looked so cool. I think I was more excited for them to get it then they were.    And, now, not so much. It's just a big let down, even if it's relatively inexpensive for a video game system.    And read the 5 star reviews! Lots are from people who were GIVEN a system to review. Yeah....that's not biased.    I'm really disappointed with this. It only does HDMI output, so I need to get an adapter to the work with the old playroom TV. This is a big design flaw since I think a lot of people would want to attach this to an old \\"retired\\" TV.    I find this whole thing frustrating for kids. Leapfrog made a good effort to explain things well, but the hardware is really touchy. The controllers are finicky and the motion sensor camera requires really perfect placement and the proper lighting. There is also no good way to tell the player one and player two controllers apart.    Also, it encourages kids to stand up and play, but it's so easy for them to walk too close or to move too far away and then the motion camera stops working and preschoolers are too young to understand what's wrong. Also, it's very easy for someone to move in the background and mess up the players game. And since they are ALREADY frustrated....    The operating system isn't great for young kids either. You have to log in as a particular player and that player is always player 1. You have exit the game to switch players, and even then, it's hard to do. We've had lots of fights over who gets to be player 1 and who has which controller.    My youger son has a hard time using it and he quickly gets bored and frustrated. My older son can work it better, but honestly, I can tell he will outgrow it quickly. Some of the games are rated up to 7 or 8, but I think most kids that age would want a more advanced system. He plays it because he wants to play video games and doesn't know that the games are badly designed.    I've played a lot of video games in my life, and the race games are needlessly hard for kids. The physics are bad and kids slalom wildly back and forth. I could hardly stay on the skateboard track with the thumb stick and I have fully-developed fine motor control which no one in this target age group has.    Oh! And lots of the games (like Pixar and bubble guppies) are 1 player games!    We love leapfrog and my kids are into learning, but the \\"power ups\\" that you get by answering questions feel like interruptions to the game instead of part of the game.    So it's like \\"ok, put up with these three, too-easy question to get something arbitrary and THEN you can play!\\"    It's REALLY a shame, because I think it has great potential. My kids love iphone games and they are interested in video games so this seemed like an excellent option, but it's not. It doesn't work well and by the time they are old enough to manage its tricky controllers, they will be old enough to use a wii.    I'm really regretting this system after a week and hope they get tired of it because the only person more frustrated by it than my kids is me.

product_title: E-accexpert® Bright Blue Head Light Kit for DJI Phantom 2 Vision Vision+ Quadcopter
review_headline: I like it but don't like it. Read details.
review_body:
I like it and don't like it at the same time. There are a few drawbacks. Before you buy this, make sure you have the Phantom 2 and higher, this isn't made for the old phantom.

Good:
- This thing is INCREDIBLY BRIGHT. Seriously, do NOT stare at the L.E.D. circle directly, it will bleach the crap out of your eyes. I couldn't see without the black/white dot for probably 20 minutes after I accidentally stared directly at it.
- It barely pulls any power, I noticed no [negative] impact on my flight time.
- It makes your phantom looks bad ass.

Bad:
- The connectors do not contact the battery. Once full power is applied, the vibrations inside the airframe cause the light to go on and off or completely go OFF all together. This is BAD...very, very bad.
- Designed for the front of the Phantom, yet it is not concave to snugly fit into the front. Its supposed to be shaped like ) but instead its like | .
- It doesn't keep running! (see first point). It turned off 20ft into the air due to incredibly POOR connections.

Suggestion:
If you can come up with a way to snugly fit this to the battery male connectors, this is a PERFECT product for you. If you cannot, well, then enjoy your bright light whilst your Phantom 2 is sitting pretty on the ground (Hopefully not crashed).

Cheers!

product_title: Sky Viper Camera Drone
review_headline: Great until arm broke on 2nd day.
review_body:
PROS:
Stable flight. My 10 year old was able to consistently control it after 10 - 15 attempts.
Decent video and pictures.
Good range and speed.
Very cool stunts.
We have a MAC and no problem viewing pics and vids, that recorded (see below).

CONS:
Power cable is VERY difficult to remove once clipped in.
Video and pictures did not record for one full session - missed saving footage of some great indoor stuff we shouldn't have been doing.
Battery keeps coming loose after crashes. It doesn't disconnect or shut off, but it is a drag to have to keep putting back.
Rotor gears dislodge on crashes. This does prevent flight but they are easy enough to put back. Still a drag.
Dirt will clog the rotor gears.
Arm broke and now it's useless. This pretty much ends the discussion of pros and cons.

We flew it for a good 20 minutes with multiple charges on a baseball diamond, in my house and also in my backyard on the lawn. It bounced like hell a LOT of times with no permanent damage. But then the arm snapped off at the body joint and now it's junk. On that flight it fell from about 15 feet.

Overall we liked it but now... who cares? If you are lucky and it works longer for you, here are some tips:
Watch out for dirt. On the baseball diamond the little gears jammed more than a few times. The same goes for very long carpet.
After you put the pics on your computer, if you clear out the drone's drive, the next set of pictures will have the same numbers as the first. It's a drag to have to rename them each time you clear the copters drive and start from pic0001 again. But this is probably them same with every copter I'm guessing.

It really was a cool copter and we're pretty bummed out it's done.

I don't know about those whom complained about the instruction manual that came with it, it was easy to read, VERY informative in regards to instructions, and there are others that purchased the F3 that has video's on YouTube showing how to fly this! It was an easy matter of charging the batteries, installing batteries in controller, installing charged battery into helicopter, syncing controller and BAM! We were out there flying it in minutes! Highly recommend this toy if you want to step up from the S107G and play outside like we did. It's not just an outside flyer, you can also still fly it indoors no problem! : )

product_title: Myth Board Game
review_body:
... I'm sadly forced to agree with those who gave the game low ratings.

If you buy just this box and nothing else, be prepared to struggle playing this game. It will be difficult to play out of the box (because of the terrible state of the rule book and cards. They are missing important info and are inconsistent in their terminology). If you're an experienced RPGer you can probably wing it and house-rule your way to a coherent game and enjoy it because the game system is AWESOME! I don't think there's any other co-operative dungeon crawler that plays quite like Myth available today.

However, if you're not an experienced RPG'er... ALL IS NOT LOST. The game production is superb. Easily in the top 10% of all miniature board games like Descent 2nd Ed., Claustrophobia, etc. Slightly better than the D&D Adventure games (Drizzt, Ravenloft and Ashardalon). Great minis, components, tiles, tokens, etc. You have great components for a game. But ... oh, those rules...!!!! :-(

So I suppose a final recommendation is:

1. If you are looking for a dungeon crawl-type game, but like to have clear rules, a clearly laid out play sequence and clearly laid out objectives and scenario set ups, I have to admit you'd be better off playing games like Descent 2nd Ed., Claustrophobia, the D&D Adventure System games (or Gears of War or Escape: Fighting for Freedom if you prefer sci-fi). Myth will probably not be for you.

2. However, if you're OK with setting up your own scenarios (within the provided guidelines), or following some of the provided adventure scenario (there's still a bit of DIY needed, even with these)... and you don't mind downloading the latest updated version of the rules and cards online and watch the (very good) game-play videos on YouTube... and you enjoy a more free-flowing sequence of play where players are free to do anything they want (within certain constraints)... and there's more uncertainty about when the Darkness (the enemy) will act, and what it will do... and you want to play with heroes with very widely differing skills and abilities... but whose abilities will allow you to pull off some incredible moves that can change a losing game in an instant, and that will have you talking about it long after the game has ended... then maybe Myth is the right game for you.

Hope this helps! :-)

PS. There's just barely enough enemy minis in the retail box to provide for a full game. You don't need to buy any extra, but you DO have to be careful with your set-up limits. Just go for the lowest number of enemies in each set-up, and download the variant card for the mini-boss Yardu from BGG so you can play him without needing to buy anything else.

review_body: I was really excited to get this cash register for my kids for Christmas (ages 3 and 4), especially with all the great reviews.  But I am really disappointed in the product I received.  Because it is only solar-powered, it barely works.  The only way we can get the solar-powered part to work is by shining a flashlight directly on the panel.  Without that, the calculator will not work at all.  We tried putting it directly under our lights, and I've turned an extra lamp on directly over the cash register, but we can still barely see the numbers.  My 4-year-old has been so diappointed that she can't get the buttons to work.  She was also upset that the credit card doesn't beep when it swipes, and even when we shine a light on the solar-powered panel to get the numbers to show, the buttons make no sound.  Aren't they supposed to make a sound?  As much as I don't want to deal with having to send something back to Amazon, I'm afraid I'll have to return this toy.  I've been trying to find the good in it, but all-in-all, it has been nothing but a disappointment.

product_title: Christmas Tree Train Set
review_headline: Brings Back Memories....Fun Addition for Christmas
review_body:
We have had this tree train for about 20 years until last year when I forgot to remove the piece that attaches to the tree before I threw away our old tree to make way for a new one. Even after 20 years we still got steam from the engine every once in a while. When I saw it being offered less than I paid for it 20 years ago I had to buy the replacement.

It is fairly easy to put together, but the most important thing to take into consideration is where to put the sleeve you attach to the tree. It has to be in a spot where the tree branch lengths are not so long that the track is lost in the branches or so short the track sticks way out past the tree. Finding the sweet spot is the trick. Putting the posts that hold the track can also be a bit tricky. They take a fair amount of pressure to put them into the sleeve and then to attach the track. I was always afraid I was going to break the plastic putting it together, but with some care never did. Also, make sure the track is level as the little train really can't go up hill.

You can set the train to continuously circle the tree until you stop it (and it whistles as it goes), or you can set it to make about 2 1/2 trips around and stop until you press the button again.

Overall, good value for the money.

product_title: Corolle Mon Premier Pacifier Doll Set
review_headline: Sew paci to the doll's outfit for safety!
review_body: Bought these to go with our Baby Cailin boy doll.  I agree with other reviews, they are incredibly small - an entire pacifier (the mouthpiece plus the handle) is about the size of a half-dollar coin.  The mouthpiece alone is about the size of a nickel, maybe a tad smaller.  It has to be slightly forced into the Cailin doll mouth, though it isn't terrible.  I can do it without a problem, it just takes a little push, and my 26 mo old daughter is getting close to figuring it out though she tends to ask for help.  I sewed the ribbon of the pacifier onto the front of the doll's outfit like it is displayed in some online photos if you google them.  That way it cannot be lost because it is attached to the baby and I don't have to worry about my daughter swallowing it.  If you are keeping the pacifiers  loose, I would definitely not feel comfortable using them with ages 2 and below.  The first thing my daughter did when she saw it was try to put it in her mouth like a regular paci, even with it sewn onto the doll's outfit!  She hasn't done it since, it was like she was trying it out for size, but it made be extra thankful I had sewn it on in the first place!  Overall I am happy with the purchase, it is a nice little addition to the adorable doll.

product_title: Nerf Rebelle Rapid Red Blaster
review_headline: This is the best nerf gun out there for females (unless you are ...
review_body:
This is the best nerf gun out there for females (unless you are very strong and prefer the CS-18 that has C batteries in it.) Not being sexist, that is just the way it is, fair/equal does not mean exact same) It is light and extremely effective and the handle is small (painfully small for adult males). How effective? Its rate of fire EXCEEDS the CS-18 if you know how to use it and can trigger pull fast enough (paintball players will own with this--I cleared 12 darts in 4 seconds, that is 3 dps--CS-18 was 12 darts in 5 seconds). Girls (at least ours) do like the colors and the secret agent/message aspect as well. Some may complain "it only has a 12 dart clip, no fair!" Once again, it is a size thing. And guess what? The gun is compatible with 18 dart clips and drums as well. Not sure if the darts it comes with are actual elites, but once again, it is fully compatible and slings them very forcefully and surprisingly accurately.

If your gun seems Dead On Arrival (DOA), try adjusting the batteries a few more times. Our second gun on Christmas morning seemed this way. I actually tried fully pulling out the batteries and swapping them THREE times and even pulled out a digital multimeter to test all my brand new batteries (even knowing the odds of new batteries being bad is infinitesimal just to be sure) before I got them all to seat properly. The way the battery compartment closes, two batteries have to pop into the holes to make the connection.

Fantastic gun, highly recommend.

review_headline: Be prepared to source your own hardware....
review_body: The overall quality of the frame itself is good, the Carbon fiber plate is of good quality, and the edge finish is great.  Where the kit fails is in its hardware: the bolts supplied are all M2.5 x 8.  That's fine for the 16 that go through ONE plate into the aluminum standoffs. But for the 16 that pass through THREE plates to attach the four arms, they aren't long enough to reach the nylon on the locking nuts (<2mm).  They need to be at least 10mm for safe attachment (M2.5 x 10).  So, if you buy this kit, you''ll need to do one of two things: either supply 16 M2.5 hex nuts and use locktite OR replace 16 bolts with M2.5 x 10 to use the supplied locknuts.

product_title: Magna-Tiles 02148 Solid Colors 48 pc DX set Toy
review_headline: Magnetic tiles in general are among the best open ended toys out there
review_body:
Magnetic tiles in general are among the best open ended toys out there. Bought 2 huge translucent sets for my Family Child Care program, and with 10 kids had to go get another set! They are in constant use. One of the best investments ever. Kids can begin to put them together around 2-3, and quickly learn all the ins and outs of the mechanics of them. But over several years of having the kids use them each and every day, I have never seen the same structure twice. Sometimes they astound me with their ideas.

This opaque set was bought in particular for a little boy with vision challenges. He was able to build with them more easily, as they have great contrast. He quickly moved to the translucent ones as he gained mastery with these.

Over say 7-8 or more years of daily use with these toys, with a large group of kids happily sharing them, we have lost one magnet, and had no tiles break. This is a high value toy when you consider how many hours of play for how many dollars of purchase price. Kids will play with these for years and years. Not a toy that will sit on the shelf.

product_title: Graphic Skinz Design Studio Skinz Bundle for Girls 3 Assorted Packs 18 Transfers per Pack for Use with Motorized Vacuum Chamber
review_headline: Lots of Fun, Not Sure How Long Lasting.
review_body:
This set would be a lot of fun for kids. There are several objects in the kit you can skin and you can skin other objects, like phone or iPod cases. I was thinking it might be good for other arts and crafts projects, but I haven't really found a good use for it yet on that front. I think you could use the skins like decoupage, but I haven't tried yet. I think it would be a lot of fun for kids to play with, but I think after they skin everything, they'll be done with it. I don't see it taking off like the loom bands.

A few other downsides: Not much fits into the vacuum chamber, and the chamber seems cheaply made. However, you can apply the skin with a damp sponge to areas that are too large. I am not sure how long the chamber will hold up, but it will probably hold as long as the skin pack holds. The key item is the skins, and they are a little bit pricey.

I do think this is a good idea and kids love to personalize things. The objects included i n the kit (a box, and some figures) are pretty cute too. I am going to give it four stars because I am not the target audience, but I was pretty impressed.

product_title: Deck Box: Ninja by Legion Supplies
review_headline: Great design; highly recommended + buy the matching card sleeves (may need 2 packs for most decks).
review_body: Bought this as a Christmas gift, but took a good look at it when the package arrived. There isn't much you can say about a deck box, but I will say that the design alone is worth the cost. product_title: Pirates of the Spanish Main Game Booster Pack
review_headline: Fun to collect and to play!
review_body:
I've never really been one for collectable strategy games, but Pirates of the Spanish Main (and its other Pirates versions) is the exception. Each pack contains two ships, it claims you can play with only two, but you need at least 6-8 ships in order for it to be any fun. The game itself is very fun to play, although a little slow paced for a kids game, make sure you have at least a couple hours before starting a game. Even if you don't play the game, the ships are still fun to collect. Most ships share the same 5 simple designs (as expected since they all assemble from 2d punch out cards) but each ships has very nice printed details making each feel unique. These ships are very fun to collect and, if you have the attention span, the game is quite fun too!
I don't really want to think about how much I've spent on collecting these things, but my 40+ ship armada looks really good on my shelf so I'd say it was worth it.
