product_title: Cypher Game
review_headline: Great Microgame, Cool Theme, Plays Well With 2 to 4 People
review_body:
I really like micro games like Love Letter as they are easy to carry around. The biggest problem with Love Letter is that it's so random, and decisions are so simple that there's just not much to it. Cypher still uses only a handful of cards (about 20), but the way it's mechanic works, you end up with more complex, meaningful decisions each turn. Each turn, you end up with 3 cards in your hand—you play one, then draw another, and pass one to your left and one to the right. So you're balancing what to play, what to give to your opponents, and what to keep.

This is interesting because you get some idea of the cards your opponents might have. Plus you're building up a tableau which adds some momentum to the game that Love Letter just doesn't have. It's really fun in this game when it enters the final round, and you think you have the cards necessary to play to win, but you might not.

A lot can change quickly, and while it's definitely got more meaningful decisions than Love Letter, it's still pretty light and fairly random. But the theme is great, the cards work well and seem well balanced, and, again, unlike Love Letter, it actually plays well with 2.

product_title: Edushape Marbulous Marble Run - 82 Pieces plus Bonus of 50 Marbles -  Total of 132 Pieces
review_headline: Time and Multiple Re-assembly Required - Could be a waste of money
review_body: It took me hours to put this together. I got this marble run to help entertain my nieces coming over for Christmas. However, be aware that kids will definitely NOT be able to put the whole set together. To elaborate, if your kid is only interested in a small scale, then he or she , with adult supervision, may be able to stack several pieces together. Yet, I wanted to use all the pieces and build the same model they have depicted on the picture (model 102 pictured on the piece of supposedly \\"instructions\\" in the box). The pieces can be snapped together but once I started building it up, certain pieces would not stay put. Several times the structure collapsed on me while building it. The model was top heavy and I opted to glue certain pieces together at about 6-7 areas in order for the structure to stay put.  In addition, the colors are not exactly the same as they have in the pic.  It would have been nice if they identified all the similar parts with a corresponding letter or number instead of just showing a pic of the piece that did not totally look like the actual piece or show a picture of the item with a different color than the actual piece    Yet, once I built it, I was happy with the way the marbles went through the maze. Im sure my nieces will like it. It was just a struggle to put it together and I know now that certain parts will have to kept glued together or maybe I wont bother disassembling it anymore.    Adding to my earlier review. My 3 nieces attempted to play with this marble run Christmas eve at my place and it immediately tumbled over the first time they tried to use it. After a frustrating attempt to re-assemble this thing, they gave it another run. After only a couple of attempts, the whole thing toppled over again. At that point, I had to give it up and did not bother reassembling.   Reminder that the model I attempted was the one shown on here which used all the available pieces It was TOP heavy and will NEVER stay put unless you glue most of the pieces together. Like I said they do snap together but they they should have the portion that inserts into the groove of each piece longer for it to possibly stay put.

review_body:
This toy is well built and sturdy enough for its intended use but too fragile for kids that would want to use it as just a ball to through around. It takes a steady hand and a good bit of thought to make it all the way through the maze. As a bonus the designer has broken the maze into three stages with three entry points so if you can get through the first two thirds of the maze but want to work on the last third you can enter the maze at that point.

About the maze, what fun! The kids (Age 3 and 5) love it. It is recommended for 8 and up but younger ones can find it interesting. It can actually hold my kids attention longer than most anything else without batteries or WiFi. Some times it is difficult to figure out which direction you have to go to get to the next checkpoint but in my humble opinion that is the point of this kind of toy.

This toy can teach problem solving, hand eye coordination, concentration and deductive reasoning. We highly recommend!

product_title: Syma X5C Explorers 2.4G 4CH 6-Axis Gyro RC Quadcopter With HD Camera
review_body:
This quad is incredible value. It is very stable, which makes it very easy to fly and a wonderful platform for taking movies and pictures.

The quad comes with two modes, Basic and expert. It instructions describe these as mode 1 and mode 2. If you're learning to fly, mode one is good as the reactions are very subdued. This mode is also preferable for video, as the direction changes have less "impact" on the footage. The disadvantage of mode one becomes apparent if there is a little wind, or one want to have a little fun. In mode one it's impossible to overcome the drift caused by even a mild breeze. Mode two is where the action is, and f you want this quad to have some fun, that's the mode to choose.

Because the instructions are fairly poor, finding how to switch modes is a challenge. There is a button on the top left of the remote control. Press that to switch modes.

The quad comes into it's own when taking photographs and video. The quality in both is surprisingly good. Being able to take photographs from viewpoints that would otherwise be unaccessible is a big advantage, and gives this packages surprising value.

We have numerous kites that live in the trees close by. They are curious birds, and it's evident from their behavior that they're trying to figure out what this invader is. There is the prospect of some great photos and video.

There are better quads out there if your only interest is having fun, but if you're keen on getting some unusual photographs (or videos), as well as having some fun flying, this is amazingly good value.

product_title: Piano Lacquer Backgammon Game Set with Wood Inlay 13”
review_headline: So much potential, marred by poor QC and some shoddy components.
review_body:
Let me start by saying that overall I've been a happy customer with my past YMI purchases. They offer generally hard to find items in the USA (like go stones) at good prices. However I have to say I'm pretty disappointed with the backgammon set I received. Its very possible that its just a QC issue with mine, but here is the rundown:

Pros:
- Nice material overall, decent weight but not too bulky.
- Patterns on the wood are pleasing and not much in the way of obvious knots, etc.
- The deep contrast on the pip marks is nice. I'm not sure what the actual wood type is but its a very nice contrast in both color and grain and makes for a beautiful playing surface.

Cons:
- The actual playing area of the board is about 11.5-12 inches deep, not 13. I'm not sure if the standard way to measure backgammon boards counts the border thickness, but based on how this one is measured I wish they had a "piano lacquer" set at 15 inches.
- The pieces are very plain, and two white pieces had some deep dents on one side.
- Would have been nice if the dice cups were a bit deeper. They look nice but its too easy to shake die out of them by accident.
- The dice are HORRIBLE (cheap, light, uneven, different sizes). DO NOT PLAY WITH THEM. As another reviewer said, there is no way these are rolling fair. Pick up some small dice separately or grab some extras from another game in your collection.
- Board is glued together which is normally fine, but there are places in the seams where the glue is obviously visible because they used too much. I may end up taking an exact-o knife to it.

Overall its an okay set but the accessories are lacking in comparison to the overall beauty of the wood and finish. The glue being visible along seams is unfortunate and I would have expected better. If you replace the dice and if the glue wasn't visible I'd be very happy with this purchase because there is nothing on its own that is majorly wrong with this set, but the little things all add up. For a little more money I think you can probably get much better.ajorly wrong with this set, but the little things all add up. For a little more money I think you can probably get much better.

138 Red
135 Blue
101 Green

Lastly 95 foreign cards which I didn't include in the colors above and also encompassed all 25 of the artifacts I received)

product_title: T.S. Shure Wooden Magnetic Map of the USA Puzzle
review_headline: At first this item seemed like a home run
review_body:
At first this item seemed like a home run, five-star product. VERY sturdy and good quality, educational, fun, and my kids LOVED it. My 6 year old kept saying, "This is AWESOME!" The kids played with it ALL DAY LONG. It even has pieces for the Great Lakes! How cool is that?!
When I sat down to play with them though, I noticed a couple deal-breakers for me. First is that several of the states are strangely misshapen. I'm not saying they need to be Rand McNally accurate, but really... look closely in the pictures at Texas. And Arizona. And New England. And Washington. And Mississippi... it's a little disturbing. I want my kids to have some tactile fun, but i ALSO want them to build some recognition of state shapes, and this is counter-productive! The pieces also cross over state lines several times to make even weirder shapes that make the actual state shapes even more ambiguous. But truthfully, given the amount of fun that my kids had I was willing to overlook this annoying flaw.
UNTIL....
Until they were done and it was time to put it away. I thought that it would be fun to hang it one the wall in their room, it even has a built in hanging cord on it! No big deal, right? WRONG. With just the slightest jiggle half of the states FELL OFF when held vertical. UMM... what? Isn't the whole point of a map with magnets that is designed to hang up vertically that the magnets STAY ON IT? So now what? What am i to do with this gigantic wooden map that can't hang up? I guess i have to take all the states off and store them in a separate bag so they can get lost? I'm disappointed to say the least. It's a shame because the quality of the materials are the best I've seen in a product like this, and my kids loved it. Great concept. Poor execution.

product_title: Marvel Heroics Tiny Miniature Figure <1" Hero's Vary - Quantity 1
review_headline: **ONE** HERO BALL FOR $10?! RIP OFF! DO NOT BE FOOLED! **These cost $1.00 each in stores!**
review_body:
Normally, I won't comment on sellers in reviews, or leave a one star review based on a seller, because reviews are for the product and the seller page is to comment on the seller.
HOWEVER, when I see such a gross attempt at a scam as this I feel I MUST speak up on the product page!
As another writer has stated these miniature toys cost $1 each anywhere else you can find them (Wal-Mart, Rite Aid, CVS, Walgreens). Do NOT waste $10 to purchase just *ONE* 1" tall action figure (especially when you don't know who you'll get)! The seller of this toy is just trying to make an outrageous profit by preying on consumer naivety!

Now, the miniatures themselves are absolutely adorable and fun. If you can find them elsewhere for the proper price I highly recommend them. I have a Batman from the DC line that is fantastic. The "painting" is a little goofy looking in spots, but what would you expect from something so tiny for $1? LOL.
If I was rating the actual toys I would give THOSE 4 stars at least, but as I want to bring this rip off to the attention of others, I am rating them a 1 star here.

product_title: Elf on the Shelf:A Christmas Tradition (brown-eyed girl scout elf)
review_headline: The new modern tradition to indoctrinate our children into accepting global surveilance!
review_body:
In our modern age of global and domestic terrorism, and the growing need for the government to monitor all of our activities from sun rise to sun set, there is no more important role of the parent than to teach their children to be accustomed to having peering eyes always looking over their shoulders. And this is why the Elf on the Shelf is the best Christmas Tradition to have come about since somebody included a naught and nice list in Santa's arsenal.

This cute little elf reminds children that they no longer have any reasonable expectation of privacy. Not at church or classroom, and not in the kitchen or bathroom. Instead, as a playful exercise they should always be looking out for wherever those spying eyes may be, and instead of becoming furious with their loss of personal space, they should laugh in glee at where those eyes might be.

This is a great new addition to our family Christmas tradition, along with our annual burning of copies of Fahrenheit 451 and 1984 that we do to remind our children how free thought and expression are only for the wicked.

product_title: Gund Animated Fortune Monkey Plush
review_headline: Gotta get this adorable Gund- it's a cheeky purple monkey!
review_body:
I'm partial to Gund stuffies, but generally prefer the non-animated/battery operated toys for their attention to detail, soft fur and perfect amount of stuffing.

This is the exception. It's a purple monkey. It's cheeky and a bit sarcastic in a non-mean way. The crystal ball lights up and the mouth moves and it's so very cute that it's a good whimsical gift for some adults as well as being a nice one for kids.

More details about the toy:
The soft plush feather does not stand up like it does in the photo, it's not wired and mine is curved over the top of the head from shipping. It still looks good.
The mouth moves minimally and because it's shallow and closes softly it's not a danger to tiny fingers.
The metallic covered crystal ball lights up pretty brightly in a succession of colors. It's very nice looking.
The voice is great, and the recorded answers are fun. Best for yes or no questions.
Press the hand to turn it on, ask the question, press the foot for an answer. It does shut off automatically after a short time, and you'll repeat the process to ask another question.
It's not too loud- I appreciate toys that are reasonably quiet.
It takes 3 AAA batteries- the battery compartment is easy to access through a Velcro strip on the back. You'll need a Phillips screwdriver to change batteries. You can also switch the monkey off on the battery compartment.

I'm just tickled by this little monkey. It's an award winning cutie and the silly answers to silly questions brought a lot of laughter in my family.

product_title: Ravensburger Santa Needs Directions - 1000 Piece Christmas Puzzle
review_headline: Momma in her kerchief, the dog gave a nuzzle, we settled in cozy to this Christmasy puzzle!
review_body: Exactly what I have come to expect from Ravensburger. All the pieces were included, and no duplicate pieces. The pieces were moderately sturdy, interlocked nicely, and most importantly, only two or three pieces even remotely fit together that were not \\"supposed to\\" (meaning, some pieces looked alike, but they did not fit together, whereas in lower quality puzzles, two or more pieces will both look similar as well as fit similar, causing confusion as to which piece is correct). My only semi-complaint is that I typically buy Ravensburger puzzles due to the impeccable detail within the picture itself. Of course, this makes it's easier for me to do the puzzle, and perhaps I should embrace the extra challenge this one offered. This particular puzzle was slightly more \\"blurry\\" versus \\"crisp\\" in terms of the picture on the puzzle. Again, this does not affect the functionality of the puzzle, and adds to the challenge, so I do not think it worth demoting the number of stars. If there were anything at all I would change about Ravensburger puzzles, it would be this: please have less blue dust in the packaging! But again, I suppose dust comes with the territory of packaging puzzles. I think the blue backing is lesser quality than the picture side of the pieces. Occasionally, there would be extra blue paper attached to some puzzle pieces, if that is a picking-point for anyone. Overall, an enjoyable Christmas puzzle and festive for the holidays. Clear off the dining room table, warm some mulling spices on the stovetop, play Christmas carols on the stereo, and enjoy this lovely puzzle!

product_title: A Game of Thrones: The Board Game Second Edition
review_headline: Best Board Game I've ever had.
review_body:
If you are a manic fans of GoT (and if you like playing RISK), then get this board game! This game is so challenging. Credit to George Martin for his brilliant concept, this game is realistic and strategically correct. Take House of Greyjoy for example. Strategically, it's located near winterfell, therefor it is easier for greyjoy and stark to clash in combat compared to the other houses. As for for house of Mattel, since sunspear is way below on the map, it will take time for them to reach or being reached by other player.

This board game contain many small parts, so best invest in a good small compartments for the tokens. I personally use small plastics with seal to store each type of token. And the board itself is quite large, so you'll need some space to play this. Don't play near babies or infant! Choking hazard!

The game rules is a bit complicated but learning it worth the effort. Some rules are unclear though, but fine by me since that means it is open for negotiation.

Been playing it several times and still this game never looses it's thrill and excitement. For a sore looser (like myself, lol) be warned. Playing this game can seriously wound your pride, especially when other player starts to making coalition with each other, or betraying any established faction, choosing different side etc. Thus I encourage you to play this with your closest friends... or not. Up to you!

And do spare lots of free time while playing this. Setting up the game itself takes about 10 to 15 minutes for me. More if you are unfamiliar with the map and the houses. As for playing time, it could take more than 4 hours until we've got a winner.

product_title: Takenoko Board Game
review_headline: Cute, light game, but does not deliver on an exciting experience
review_body:
I was very excited to get this game, I was thrilled to open it up and set it up. The panda is adorable, the instructions are funny, and the components are magnificent. The game works well, there are no bad mechanics, and the game is generally balanced. Players can keep up with their opponents and stay relevant to the game for the most part. The game starts out quite fun, but does not stay that way permanently.
The game does little to stimulate competition and the game is highly static. Players cannot influence its outcome significantly, they just keep on drawing random objective cards toward the end and wait for things to happen. Unless the objective has already occurred (which is likely) players often must use two to three of their turns to achieve them. Failure to complete an objective carries no penalty whatsoever.
The physical aesthetics of the game does carry some charm, but it is not enough to keep the game engaging for all ninety minutes or so it takes to play.
I don't hate this game, it is fun in small doses and I will play it, the game however just does not deliver what I am looking for and is not as strong as plenty of other games in the same price range with the same depth and playtime. For pretty artwork, this game is fantastic, for a great gaming experience look elsewhere.

product_title: Star Wars The Black Series Luke Skywalker #21 Figure 3.75 Inches
review_headline: Knobby Elbows Don't Stop The Fun With This Luke Skywalker
review_body:
In the realm of collectors I'm generally in the minority with this one, but I loved this Black Series Luke Skywalker figure... Almost 10 years ago, Hasbro cranked out a Dagobah Luke that was essentially a pre-posed statue with 2 sets of arms for two static poses. Cool? At the time it was unique, for sure, and I appreciated it for what it was, but it never satiated my desire for a truly nicely articulated Dagobah Luke for putting into all his action poses while he was abused and ridiculed by Yoda on Dagobah.

Flash forward and Hasbro cranks out a figure with more articulation than maybe they should've crammed into one figure (or at least his arms), and scads of extra bits and pieces! Essentially, what I wanted almost 10 years ago, they threw my way, and I really was pretty pleased with it!

Luke rocks a pretty great sculpt overall, and the head/face (while not the best likeness), is passable. They've done better Mark Hammil likenesses, and they've done worse.

The figure comes with a pistol, lightsaber, lightsaber hilt, a removable belt (with a working holster for his pistol on it), and EXTRA HANDS! OOOOoooo Yes, extra hands. Two hands are gripped to hold a weapon or accessory, while the other two hands are "jazz hands", and are intended for you to pose the figure doing his infamous handstand force training scenes. BOTH sets of hands are articulated at the wrists with ball joints too, so you have ample flexibility to try and balance that handstand pose. It isn't all that hard to do it, and looks just really cool.

Luke sports scads of articulation, which actually is where his drawbacks are. He's got what would could estimage to around 16 points of articulation, but they're almost entirely ball/socket joints, and so the range of movement makes him easily one of the most poseable Star Wars figures in the 4" line since it was created in the 70's. All of the joints are nicely hidden save for the elbows. I'd dare say it works perfectly, save for the elbows.

Now, why do collectors disapprove? Well, the joints on the arms, while plentiful, are pretty hideously obvious and just ugly to look at. Luke's elbows are double-hinged, and stand out like a sore thumb, and maybe possibly make the arms look slightly longer than they should be. They're definitely distracting, but they're made this way so he can interact with the Yoda backpack the Black Series Yoda figure comes with. The arms can pull tight to his chest, and he can hold the backpack straps, and be posed in yet another iconic pose from the films.

Now, will kids care? I think not. The poseability would be nothing but appealing to any kid playing with this figure I think, and it really is a fun figure to set up on your desk running around with Yoda on his back! Collectors and their tastes, are a weird balancing act for Hasbro. Aesthetics with poseability don't always work well together, and in my book I'd take the poseability. It's a toy first. Hasbro, in my opinion, has a great figure with this Dagobah Training Luke. If you want the lesser articulated figure, it exists and is quite inexpensive too. I'll take this one instead!

product_title: Robotech RPG Tactics Starter Board Game
review_headline: All in all not a bad little game
review_body:
All in all not a bad little game, certainly for a company's first attempt. It's not perfect however.

Gameplay: Rules are quite simple for the most part, most complex thing to worry about is is building your force, and a basic dice roll with an added value compared to another value (Say, shooting, D6 + Gunnery needs meet or beat Armor). Turns move fast, with players able to act and react to oneanother in various ways. Missiles coming in on you? Use anti missile weapons or burn command points to dodge, or if another model is close it could try and take some of the damage for you. You can steal activation from someone (And prevent it) to throw a spanner in the works for someone, though it's not easy. Each of the three factions have unique rules, Human pilots want to be the top gun and one up each other, letting you get more shots if they see their mates taking out the enemy. Zentrati care little for their men, as they know they have millions more at their disposal, Their rule lets them call in re-enforcement waves when units die close to commanders (So long as they have a rule called Life is Cheap), the same rule lets you ignore the normal restriction that would keep you from shooting allies, letting you take out your own men (you can always call on more afterall) if they would be blocking line of sight to the rest of your forces, or let one poor guy pin someone down in hand to hand combat before raining fire on the two. Included in the book are a number of scenario options, almost all of which are modular to create unique missions and goals for the game, in addition, there are fully fleshed out campaign rules for running extensive, interconnected games with branching paths.

Creating your army is done through unit cards that have listed stats, special skills/weapons, point values and upgrades, though the book doesn't have the point values or the faction rules, so dont loose the cards! Get some protectors, they will be used a lot. That said, the cards are dry erase, with boxes to note the amount of health each unit has and ammunition for certain weapons.

Miniatures are a bit of a mixed bag though the human models are incredibly fiddly, having 12+ parts in some cases for a model that is only a few inches tall, some of which look to be as thin as a pin. Zentrati models fare better here, but they also have some very small guns. If you have experience with miniature building then you can find a way, but if not then you will struggle. This is made all the worse with spurs that are not labeled, letting you know which arms go to which pose, or which head may be the match for your mech. The instructions are little better, having no step-by-step guide and providing only one view, something which may not show the direction the feet are facing. It's not easy, but after you build a couple you will get the hang of it.

Included in the box are two sets of custom dice, one for the Humans one for the Zentrati, a template, rule book, tokens for the command points, the needed cards for units, characters and detailed stats and decals.

Overall, the fun you have playing makes up for the bad, but there is room for improvement. The company is new to this, though they are old salts at RPGs, and it shows with the way many of the stats and information is handled.

And yes, the kickstarter was handled rather poorly (At the time of writing this, there are still a number of EU backers that don't have their pledges despite the company now selling it in the states and canada) and they didn't handle information or shipping well. That shouldn't impact the game itself, so try to keep that in mind if you see negative reviews from kickstarter backers. Gamers are a passionate bunch, we want what we want, when we want it (like many) but I'm not reviewing their handling of the launch or their business practices, this is just for the game.

Bought two boxes when the set was initially released, and did pull a Qliphort Disk in one and a Virgil + Ult Shekhinaga in the second. Easily paid for the boxes with those pulls but I would not recommend purchasing a NECH box anymore. Price has gone up a bit after release (as expected), but the main thing is that the Super Rares in the set will be reprinted in Dec. 5's release of the NECH Special Edition. product_title: LEGO DUPLO My First 10552 Creative Cars Building Set
review_headline: Another great set from Lego. Great addition to your Duplo collection.
review_body:
I bought this set for my son because I love how versatile it is. He’s a little young for it, but my nephew is 2 and is here all the time and wants to play with these. We have some other Duplo sets and the cars fit in well with the others. With Lego sets, the more you have the more possibilities there are. We have about 4 various sets we throw in a big tub, so there’s plenty to go around. We made some very tall, colorful cars with this set, which my nephew thinks is hilarious! It’s funny how the adults start playing with the kids and start getting into it.

In general I try to buy toys that encourage learning and imagination. I LOVE that Lego does that! I much prefer blocks over electronics, loud, or flashy toys. Lego’s also truly hold their value and are extremely hardy. We play with the Lego’s in the tub and take them outside. They never show any wear. I love that they can just be washed off and are good to go. The price is great for how many pieces the set comes with. Lego’s aren’t cheap, but they can be passed down and never go out of style. My grandparents have had the same Lego’s since I was a kid and my daughter loves going over and playing with them.

product_title: Building Bricks - 1000 pc Bulk Blocks w 54 Roof Pieces and Better Variety - Tight Fit with All Brands
review_headline: watch as the piece breaks the first time i use it
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:a903edd789c603ba40a3a85ca28326db]] I was very hesitant about buying off-brand legos but after seeing the prompt and attentive responses by the toy manufacturers to other customers, I decided to take a chance on them. The results are a mixed bag. The majority of pieces work okay but the plate pieces are incredibly easy to break, as you will see near the end of the video.

12-12-14 update: i am removing another star for this product for two reasons: First, i noticed cracks in some of the normal bricks, and not just the plates. This is very disappointing, seeing as i've owned this product less than two weeks. Also, the fit of the bricks is very inconsistent. Some are fairly loose while others are way too tight. The video i posted showed a test of just a handful of bricks, but if i were to go through a few dozen or more you would see that this becomes a problem. The second reason i'm downgrading my review is the unfulfilled promises from the manufacturer to replace the defective pieces. As you can see in the comments, they offered to replace the problem pieces, but when i asked how i was supposed to go about doing this, they never responded. Am i supposed to send all 1000 pieces back to them? What would be the point if they just send me another bag with the same flimsy pieces? They talk a big game but offer no real support that i can detect.

In conclusion, i would NOT recommend this purchase to anyone. i'd rather get used genuine Lego bricks from ebay, or pay just a bit more for new ones on Amazon.

product_title: White Wizard Games Star Realms Deckbuilding Game
review_body: This is essentially just Ascension with a space theme.  It is a deckbuilder with a central row of cards and players take turns playing the cards from their hand to accumulate two resources, attack and buy power, and acquire cards from the center row to make their deck stronger.  Pretty much the only difference between this game and Ascension besides the theme is that attack power is used to directly hit your opponent instead of monsters in the center row and the winner is the person who drains the opponent's life total.  Even that really just is a minor difference from attacking monsters in the center row to accumulate victory points.    Even many of the factions serve identical roles to Ascension.  The red faction in this game (I forget the name) has cards that provide a lot of attack power and trash cards from your hand and discard pile, just like the purple faction from Ascension (I forget that name as well).    With it essentially being the same game unless you really dislike the theme from Ascension or really like the theme from this game there's really no reason to play this over Ascension.  Ascension has been around a lot longer and has a lot of additional content.  This game just came out and will get boring pretty quickly seeing the same cards over and over again.  Even comparing base sets this game is a lot more boring, none of the cards do anything exciting, just the same stuff with different numbers.m back to position 6 without actually touching him.  Too bad you so rarely get to engage in fun practices like that because of the bad game design.

My 4-year-old needed a lot of help with the winding but stayed interested long enough to make (well, mostly watch me make) dozens of beads and then string them onto a necklace and bracelet by herself.
Screwing the winder onto a bottle, as suggested is a nice option but actually a bit pointless because it makes the winder harder to use, especially for small hands that can't grasp the bottle. Far easier to use the winder by itself so you can hold it really firmly.

review_body: This is a great card game for age 4+ starting to learn phonetic words. It is very similar to crazy 8's game. This set is the level 1 consisting of consonant-vowel-consonant words (there are 6 levels in total with increasing phonetic complexity).  It contains 50 CVC word cards (10 cards per vowel) and action cards such as draw a card, skip a turn, turn-around, etc. It also comes with a color instruction sheet that has the playing instructions and illustrated examples. Each game takes 2-8 players and about 10 minutes to complete.    Crazy A's is actually a new name for the existing game called \\"Whizizzle Phonics\\". The back of the cards still carry the old branding on them. It is still the same game, easy to learn and fun to play.    In addition, the CVC cards can be used as flash cards for teaching and learning. The game doubles up as a great teaching tool.    One problem with this game is that the vowels are color coded. It's easy for the youngsters to match the color instead of the vowel on the cards. One mitigating way is to have them say the c-v-c sounds out loud.

product_title: Cash N Guns Second Edition
review_body:
I generally lean toward strategy games rather than party games, but occasionally I find myself hosting a group of friends who aren’t particularly into board games and just want to do something fun. That’s where Cash N Guns comes in. This is a game about a group of mobsters dividing up their loot, so if you don’t approve of violence in games, you’ll obviously want to stay away from this one. Its standout feature is its large foam guns. Each player has one and on the count of three, everyone points their gun at the person they want to shoot for that round, in an attempt to eliminate rivals and get more loot for themselves. The ridiculousness of this moment is what makes the game work; the foam guns add an element of silliness and get everyone laughing. Again, you have to appreciate this sort of humour and not take it too seriously, but if that sounds good to you, then you’ll probably have a lot of fun here.

This isn’t a serious strategy game and can be enjoyed without much thought about strategy at all, but if you do want to get a bit more thinking in, there’s room for that too. There are meaningful decisions to be made about who to shoot and which loot to take from the pile when it’s your turn to choose. This would never be my top choice for a serious board game, but I’m glad that it’s not completely random. If you’re playing with a diverse crowd of people, I think this is a great game. You can strategize or not strategize as you see fit, and there will be lots of laughter regardless. It was a big hit with my group of friends.

About every two minutes the connection between the remote and quadcopter would go out, requiring that the battery be unplugged, reconnected, and the remote turned on and off. Oh, and how stupid is it that there isn't an on/off switch on the quadcopter? To power it on and off you have to literally connect and yank the cord.

I had a hard time flying it -- no matter how much I tried, I could not get it to just hover. As others have noted, the scant directions provide no help with how to fly it.

I'll concede that I may just stink as a quadcopter pilot, but the connectivity issue is reason enough to junk it.

product_title: Brain Fitness Pathwords Game
review_body:
If your interested in a fun mind strengthening game that brings the fun of Tetris and word searches together Path Words is the game for you. This is a single player game with; 80 spirel bound challenges, and 8 colorful puzzle pieces that resemble the pieces you would see while playing Tetris. The game is very difficult at times, but is even more fun and addictive.
This game targets ages 12 to adult; but may be suitable for a slightly younger age group if they have good vocabulary skills. The point of the game sounds easy enough; the adjective is to move your game pieces over the words making one complete word that can be read either forward or backwards, using up all the game pieces and covering all the letters so the word shows underneath the game pieces. Again I can't express that this is not an easy task; not to worry just start out playing the beginner level and work your way up to the more advanced levels.

This is such a fun, creative way to give your brain a mental workout. This maybe a single player game, but I sat around the table with my husband competing with one another to see who can find each word first truly taking word searches to the extreme!

This is made for road trips, vacations; or just when you want to strengthen your memory, sharpen focus, speed up your thinking process, or even reduce stress.
And another benefit to buying this game, is the fact that this game is 100% re-giftable. After your finished you can pass it along, or even donate it.

This is such a fun game, and can give hours and hours of individual brain fitness, or group/team strategy learning. I would recommend buying this for your household, or for a gift; perfect for that college student, teenager, or any adult.

product_title: Eyekepper wedding dress costume cosplay girl (120cm, Blue)
review_body:
After researching every "Elsa" costume I could find I settled on this one because it looked more authentic, imo. My daughter is a petite 5 1/2 yr old. I bought the 5-6 and it fits perfectly. She is 43" tall and it hung to the floor so that you couldn't see her shoes but she didn't step on it either. It is silky and has a nice flow. We both liked the finger loops at the end of the sheer sleeves. The sheer part feels fine and can easily be worn without a shirt underneath. The bodice of the dress comes up high enough to cover everything that should be covered and is silky material on the inside. It was cold on Halloween so she wore a white long sleeved shirt underneath and it looked fine. I assume the loops on the cape are for the arms/shoulders so that it can hang down in the back but we just tied them like a cape at her neck and it worked perfectly. Also, it's beautiful. It's sheer and "flowy" and covered with silver, glittery "snowflake-ish" patterns. We got lots of compliments on it while out trick-or-treating, although as a side note, we forgot both it and the crown at home for 1 event and all the girls still immediately recognized her as Elsa just by the dress (even with her dark brown hair.) That's how pretty the dress is. And yes, the crown is just a foam piece with jewels glued on it but it worked perfectly and was comfortable. It's more like a headband then the usual uncomfortable plastic crowns with combs. My daughter loves it!

I can't speak to how long this dress will last because it does seem fragile but, to be fair, every princess dress she owns has rips somewhere so I know it's only a matter of time. She played with it several times before Halloween and then had 3 Halloween events and it's holding up just fine so far. I am very pleased with this purchase.

product_title: Syma X1 4 Channel 2.4G RC Quad Copter Helicopter - UFO
review_headline: but overall I am extremely pleased. This was for my 7 year old son ...
review_body:
I don't have any other RC copter experience to compare to this, but overall I am extremely pleased. This was for my 7 year old son and it was very easy for him to control right off the bat. In no time he was doing flips in our living room with 8 foot ceilings. The included USB charger was really nice and one of the selling points for us. I am very sick of these battery powered battery chargers that a lot of kids toys come with! Flight time is about 15-20 minutes on a full charge.

Unfortunately, it did not last that long (about 9-10 months). First, the remote would not connect (you have to push the knob up and then down to initiate the connection and it gives two confirmation beeps, one for up and one for down). It would give the initiation beep for the up but not the down. I fixed that by filing out a notch in the remote so that the knob could be pressed further down. Now it won't connect again. I am not sure if it is a problem with the remote or the copter.

Regardless, for the price and how much my son played with it, it was a worthwhile toy! Would (and probably will) buy another one.

product_title: Pokemon Metal Key Chain Holder Klefki Limited Pokemon Center Japan
review_body:
[UPDATE (2016): This Klefki is now out-of-production, so as you can see, the price to purchase a new one is outrageous. I got mine for $25 in 2014, but it is sadly impossible to find one this reasonably-priced now. It is a valuable collector's item and one of a kind. If you are absolutely desperate to add this to your collection and spend $70-$100+ on it at this point, just be aware that this Klefki is very small and delicate, and cannot be handled roughly. Attaching keys to it will scrape it up, and the paint wears off easily.]

This is a very special limited Pokemon collector's item. It's a real Klefki! This little fairy key-ring can hold keys, or any key chains, and it is absolutely adorable! It is detailed and beautifully designed, made of sturdy, shiny metal. It also makes the most unique and cute accessory! Like another reviewer mentioned, I too like to use a smaller key-ring or carabiner to clip my Klefki to my belt loop or my coat pocket zipper to show off my Pokemon love.

Just a small warning though: the paint might wear off if Klefki is scraped up too much, so be careful.
Also, the face part is heavy, so it will slide upside down if you clip it to your belt loop, etc.

$25 may be a bit pricey for a key chain, but I personally think it is definitely worth it! I love this little guy! I was elated to receive it in the mail, all the way from the Pokemon Center in Japan. Don't miss out on this awesome Pokemon treasure!

review_headline: not grayish like one of the reviewers said
review_body: This is the coolest idea that Hasbro company came up with! It's a small white pony, not grayish like one of the reviewers said. At first, I thought it was a little small for my taste, but now when I look at it more, I do like the size. It's like most other ponies. Good size. It even comes with a small brush too, which is an added touch. It's unpainted too, so I matched mine to match my pony. I'm an artist so I can tell you what paint works. Any OUTDOOR acrylic paint that comes in a small plastic bottle in the craft section of most arts and craft stores. I use "Folk-Art" paint that is for Multi-surfaces, which means you can paint on glass, metal, stone, concrete, plaster, ceramics/porceline, wood, and yes, plastic! I tried it and the paint is very thick, and sticks to the plastic very well, It's permanent and weather proof. I'd give it overnight to dry. 24 hours to cure, but longer is better. For the hair I used the same paint. What I did was first wash the hair with some mild soap and warm water. Rinse. While the hair is still damp, I added the paint strait to the hair and using a very fine comb I combed the color through. Then when all the strands look coated enough, I pressed the hair between layers of paper towel to squeeze out the access paint. Let dry and set in completely. When the hair is dry with another comb, or even the same comb (after washing the comb)or brush it comes with, comb the hair so the strands don't stick together. It takes some attempts but really, the hair looks beautiful when you get it all straitened out. They don't stick together much and not hardened paint. I'd say try not to wash the hair too often, unless really neccessary, but I don't think the paint would wash out. After all it is permanent, weather-proof paint. Hope this helps.

review_headline: Great looking, but some design flaws.... and lots of pieces to lose
review_body:
This is a hard action figure to describe, because it looks SO great, but has some serious design issues that make it hard to enjoy as a toy.

LOOK: The look is fantastic, with the bright, eye-catching armor and the cuddly unarmored figure. Your kids will take one look and want to play with it, assembling the armor and having adventures.

USE: Now that your children want to play, the challenge begins. The unarmored form has trouble standing on its own, but it can be done after a little experimentation. The armor snaps on, but it is hard to make the panels *stay* on if you are moving the arms and legs for action poses. Also, there are a LOT of pieces of armor, so a lot of bits that might get lost or go missing.

Overall, because of the look, it will delight your Big Hero 6 fan, but it loses a point for the playability issues.

review_body:
This is a last resort item if you can't use die or a RNG app... A reasonable person would expect the inside surfaces between the two rings to be smooth to facilitate smooth gliding, but it may as well be sandpaper on this spinner. Even after washing and lubricating I could feel it grind as I manipulated the wheels, and when spun it instantly grinds to a halt instead of smoothly spinning down.

Additionally, the markers on the larger, inside ring are stamped into the metal and not just painted on. Unfortunately the smaller ring has matching marks where the tool accidentally made an impression (on mine it was on the 3). This leads to a neat trick where if you desire a 3 on a roll you need only lean the ring to the left or right and the markers will catch each other, giving you a predictable roll every time. Nice trick.

The material it's made of is fine, and the small cloth bag it comes with are nice. The numbers are stamped in nicely.

👍👎As always, whether you vote up or down, thank you for taking the time to let me know if my review helped you.

Instead of the typical handset with joysticks and buttons you press to control the movements, you have a controller that fits into the palm of your hand and through your fingers. It's a pretty good size controller, so it's not going to be fully hidden in the palm of a kid's hand (in case they're wanting to make it look like they really are using the Force to move the ship).

With practice, my 13 year old son got the hang of controlling it and sending it off into a mob of action figures. One button for forward, one for reverse and another to use the ship's blaster. The blaster works by the the ship splitting open and large tinted green clear plastic balls pop out.

The set comes with a little plastic Luke Skywalker, Darth Vader, three Rebel Soldiers, and three Stormtroopers. It's enough to get you started, but you may want to fill in more with an extra set of Star Wars figures as well. My son added an infantry of plastic army men to the battle, and the Destroyer barreling through with it's blaster was quite a bit more entertaining when it had targets to hit.

The Destroyer can be a bit delicate. It moves around like a remote control car, but doesn't handle crashes like one. The "force" can move this ship forward a short distance with a bit of speed, and if it bumps into things (walls, chair legs, etc) parts come popping off and it will have to be docked for quick repairs before it is again ready for battle. It doesn't break, just comes apart and needs snapped back together.

product_title: LX Deck Case, Black
review_headline: Weaker construction, but an unexpected benefit.
review_body:
Almost exactly the same size as the ultra-pro ones. However, there are two cons and one pro when comparing them:

1. The leather-like material that forms this box clings to card sleeves, keeping the last card of my deck in the box even when I overturn it. I have to reach in and basically scrape it off. It's not hard, but sometimes I forget it and play 1 card short.

2. The magnets that keep this closed aren't firmly anchored. As a result, they move around, bulge out of the leatherette and put stress on the material. It makes me think it's going to break, although it hasn't yet.

And one pro:

Because the magnets aren't firmly anchored, you get a solid shut even when the materials don't quite fit. This is important because both brands of boxes don't actually fit top-loaders, despite those being an extremely common way of holding the deck commander when playing EDH! If you leave a toploader in an Ultra-Pro box, even in the front. the flap will be a few MM off and it will seal only very weakly (turning the box over will break the seal). If you leave a toploader in this one, no big deal, the magnets will shift a bit.

product_title: Air Hogs RC Rollercopter - Red
review_body:
We were excited to receive the Air Hog RC Rollercopter for free thanks to BzzAgent.

It was like Christmas at my house when the box arrived and my 8 year old read everything the Air Hog would be capable of doing. He had plenty time to read because it took a couple minute to remove the toy from the safety packaging which was fine because it provided great stability for shipping.

The Air Hogs takes 6 AA batteries which isn't written in plain site on the packaging so we had to borrow batteries from other items around the house which was all good because we were ready to put this bad boy to task. We were ready to see some wall climbing action! Then we had to wait for it to charge. Still excited and gave us time to look over instructions.

After a couple practice attempts at getting it to climb the wall it was a success! Then on the second flight the one of the arms that was holding the helicopter in the protective cage broke and could not be repaired. Bummer! So we thought "hey it a helicopter right" So let's use the remote to fly it without the cage!!".

That's when we found out the cage also provides stability. The helicopter is not made to sit on any surface without falling over. So my suggestion to the manufacturer is to make stronger supports for the Rollercopter AND make the toy stable so that if the cage supports are broken the copter will still be operational.

All in all my son spent about 5 minutes enjoying the toy in the cage and 5 minutes trying to get it to fly after the supports broke.

product_title: Disney Planes: Fire & Rescue Oversized Blade Vehicle
review_headline: Propeller Blades Don't Spin Freely, Resulting In A Frustrated Son.
review_body: This toy looks great, feels solid as it's mostly diecast. But the biggest hang-up has been the propeller blades being directly connected to the hoist which is stashed in the side of Blade Ranger behind a sliding plastic door. The concept is sound: pull the hoist cable out, the blades spin... and then spin the blades the opposite direction to retract the hoist back into Blade Ranger. The issue: my son cannot freely spin the propeller blades like he can with his other Disney Cars helicopters, as it will get to a point where the blades are pulled too tight against the wound-up hoist inside Blade Ranger.  This has frustrated him to no end. So while the hoist makes it more interactive and realistic, its consequence is the inability to simply spin the blades.  I've used my son as my guide for my two-stars - he only likes this toy for about 1-2 minutes and then gives up on it completely, moving on to a different Planes or Cars toy.

review_body: My daughter got this and the Spinning Tops one as a gift (They were purchased from Amazon but not by me,) and is obsessed with them. But as far as this kit goes, she's not quite 6 yet and is able to do these projects without a great deal of help, though she does need some. The projects are broken down into fairly easy steps so kids can follow them, but you do have to pay very careful attention to make sure you choose just the right part, and it might take older child or adult hands to put some of the pieces together firmly. There are more projects online, and you can come up with stuff on your own, plus the kits all work together, like Legos, so you can come up with more ideas and do more the more kits you have. She wants the rest of the kits now - thankfully Christmas is coming up. The parts are high quality - they feel very solid. The stories feel a bit silly to me but my daughter likes them and wants them read over and over. If your daughter likes this, make sure to check out the book Rosie Revere, Engineer.

product_title: Fisher-Price Thomas the Train - TrackMaster Avalanche Escape Set
review_headline: Looks fun but has it's downfalls!
review_body: Okay I'm going to be entirely real here. I got this set free from fisher price to try and review. I was so excited when I found out I was selected to try this item. I have a four-year-old son who absolutely loves anything Thomas the train. The day the package arrived at my doorstep I immediately got my four-year-old and told him we were going to set this up. When I first opened the box honestly I was kind of scared, there was a lot of pieces, but being a 6 foot long track of course there was going to be a lot of pieces. The next thing I did was pull out the directions and honestly I was not impressed at all by them. It didn't give step by step directions like one would expect and I ended up setting the directions aside and used the image on the outside of the box instead. So after 2 1/2 hours of set up, it was finally ready to be used. My four-year-old loved the way it looked, it was huge, Thomas moved by himself, and it just looked really neat. Well, the very first attempt at sending Thomas around the track was a fail. 1) it was hard to get Thomas aligned right on the track 2) no matter how hard I tried and realigned the pieces that "move" I couldn't get them lingned  up right to where Thomas would just move through it without getting stuck. When the train made it to the top it would get stuck and I'd have to hold it together to get the train to move on to the piece that falls to the other side. 3) when the train makes its way through the fall and heads downhill, the cart attached to the back of the train either comes off the track or causes the entire train to derail. Don't get me wrong my son does like the set but it's not what I thought and it's doesn't function like it should. Sometimes the train goes through the entire track flawlessly, but not very often.

product_title: Spin Master Games Quelf Board Game
review_headline: Great party game!  Easy and so much fun!
review_body:
I got this game as a gift from my mother last year. She thought it looked like the kind of game I would like (I'm in my early 30's). After reading the description on box, I suspected she was right. Despite that, this game gathered dust on a shelf until I FINALLY opened it up at a Halloween party a couple of days ago and played it for the first time. It was a blast! Super easy to learn. Super easy to play and HILARIOUS! It made it even funnier since we were all in costume, I think. Good for a diverse age group. My 12 year old daughter even played with us and had fun. Later, some more pre-teens showed up and wanted to play when we were finished.

One guy who was playing was falling on particularly hard (and hilarious) bad luck. At one point in the game, he was not allowed to bend his arms or legs until the rule was extinguished. We took multiple colorful straws and put them together to make one big straw so he could still drink his drink. Then, before that rule was over, he had to try to find 3 items in the room that could be found in a survival kit before a sand timer ran out. Let me tell you, it was a riot watching him try to hobble around the room without bending his arms or legs all while wearing a monkey costume and an oversized banana necklace. That was probably even more hilarious to watch than his wife having to stick her finger up her hose and yodel until she rolled 3 two's, or another person only being able to refer to himself in the third person or suffer the consequence of going back a space for each slip up (even though it was so much fun tricking him into messing up). I highly recommend this game to anyone. If you have the right group of people, it is most definitely a good time.

product_title: LeapFrog LeapTV Educational Gaming System
review_headline: Educational, Active, Fun that inspires Children to Love Learning
review_body:
I received a LeapTV for the purpose of review and testing to share out honest opinion. I'm a mother of a 6 yr old and 8 yr old that love gaming. The LeapTV was really easy to hook up to our television and easy to get started. I swear the kids are more techy than I am. The LeapTV is plug and play game play in a matter of minutes. There's 3 ways to play: body, controller and point play.

There's a wonderful selection of games already loaded for kids to chose from and my 6 yr old immediately went for Spiderman game. I was really impressed with all of the game play within this one game. He sat and played with the controller, then stood up to play another part and even had to answer educational questions to move up to the next level within the game. They were perfect for his 1st grade level. He's an okay reader but the narrator made it easy for him. There was a few times where he needed words to be repeated and we weren't able to figure out if that was an option but we guessed and most of the time he was right. with the answer. I was so impressed on how he was able to answer the questions. Fact is this was probably the very first time I've seen him excited about learning and answering questions. When the game asked for him to change the position of the controller to move on to the next part of the game he knew exactly what to do. product_title: 20A 2-4S Brushless ESC for RC Quadcopter Multicopter Tube installation
review_headline: Needs short leads, but provides smooth reliable control of a brushless DC and good safety features
review_body: The controller arrived quickly with minimal documentation. It turned out to be very important to keep the total length of leads short between the motor and the controller -- this includes both the motor leads and the leads on the ESC -- less than 5 inches. Otherwise it stuttered and stalled. Once the leads were shortened, it worked fine - providing smooth reliable control of a brushless DC motor at 2-3 amps. I haven't tested it at higher currents.  The ESC can be controlled with the standard Arduino servo library as long as you hold it at zero for 1 sec to \\"arm\\" it for use.  It uses the Simon-K firm ware.  When it starts up, it estimates the number of cells and beeps to let you know what it found.  It then monitors voltage and smoothly fades out when battery voltage goes below 9 volts on a 3S pack.  In the future, I might have ordered a model with a BEC to provide 5V for servos, but it fulfills its designed function perfectly.

product_title: Bolt Action Starter Game BOX - D-Day Firefight
review_body: I am a fan of WWII board/miniatures game and have several games like tide of iron, memoir 44. Here, Bolt Action D-day firefight is my first miniature WWII games. In comparison to board game, for example, tide of iron that has lots mini and components, I do feel Bolt action D-day firefight is a little bit on the pricey side. The game comes with 30 28mm infantry mini plus one half track and several pieces of terrain on plastic sprue that requires assembly. The rulers and pin markers are printed on a thin cardboard paper with the reference sheets. There is no instruction on how to assembly the models, the only instruction is one for the half track printed on the side of the game box.  On the positive notes I do find the miniatures is very detailed and if painted properly, could look pretty neat. The rule books by osprey publication is excellent with realistic scenery. Interestingly, the 10 six side dices can be either in green or white colors, depending on which version you get. Overall, I give this game a 4 star not 5 due to high price point and plus or minus one star depending your paint skills.

product_title: Estes 4609 Syncro X Nano R/C Quadcopter-p
review_headline: ...works even better if you use the Hubsan X4 controller
review_body:
Great quadcopter which is hampered by a so-so controller. I applaud Hubsan (Estes is their distributor in the US and uses the Estes brand on these Hubsan Q4 nanos) for making a controller with the same size as the quad. The boards in these nano-controllers are exactly the same as in the Hubsan X4 controller, with a few functions disabled. The function I really want (and I'm not sure exactly why they disabled this) is the 'Expert' level. This basically gives the sticks 100% range (rather than about 30% on the basic level). You need this extra range on the nano because it tends to drift due to its light weight. [[ASIN:B00IZC6C8E Hubsan H107L X4 Mini RTF RC Quadcopter]] controllers pair with the Estes Synchro X Nano with no problem. Using the bigger controller allows you to do flips, which are actually easier indoors than with the Hubsan X4, because the light nanos don't drop as much during a flip. Overall a well engineered and implemented toy that is cheap and lots of fun.

Suggestions: purchase extra blades from RCSuperstore.com ($2.38 a set) and extra batteries (~$4 ea.) The batteries are taped to the board, but you can just pull them off and substitute light velcro, leave the top off and swap out batteries just like you do with your X4. The batteries need to be secured in place in the nano, or they would constantly cause drift. If you travel, take a phone charger to charge up the battery. In general, these batteries will wear quickly unless your charger has power management. Buy an [[ASIN:B00IBDOB5I Anker® 40W 5-Port Family-Sized Desktop USB Charger with PowerIQ™ Technology for iPhone 5s 5c 5; iPad Air mini; Galaxy S5 S4; Note 3 2; the new HTC One (M8); Nexus and More (White)]]and your batteries will charge much faster and last much longer.

review_headline: Swiping raises the difficulty, revert to classic mode if it frustrates you
review_body:
Our family gatherings have adults and kids in a wide range of ages, so I thought this \\"new\\" Simon would be a fun way we could all play together. As expected, it was a great way to pass the time with a mixed group---once we reverted to using the classic (tap) mode exclusively.

Even the adults who had previous Simon-experience had difficulty doing the correct swiping to satisfy the machine. I think we would have gotten the hang of it eventually, but it was too frustrating for casual party use. I do think the swiping and swiping/tap combo play is a neat way to raise the difficulty for those who want a real challenge. We ended up using just the classic mode, and everyone then could play and still have fun.

It's a neat \\"upgrade\\" to the old tried-and-true Simon game, but there is a definite learning curve to using it.

product_title: ALEX Toys Craft Color a Rocket Children's Kit
review_headline: Lots of fun, but pricey for what you get, and somewhat fragile.
review_body:
This could have been much better, and for $30-40 it should have been.

Assembly was frustrating. Part of the problem was that there are creases in the cardboard so it could be folded up inside its own box, but these creases are not part of the final rocket and it kept bending at these creases during assembly. It does not stay together using just its tabs and slots, but some clear packing tape solved this problem nicely.

The door started to rip during assembly and continued to rip with play. The bottom of the door frame ripped off after 45 minutes of play and unfortunately is important for stability.

The concept is nice and my children love it. They like drawing on it and playing inside of it. It does not hold up well to two kids fighting over who goes inside and even less so when they both get inside.

The markers are very nice. Each has two different points, one on each end. There are 6 different colors. They are somewhat washable. 90% came off of cotton pants in the washing machine. 50% came off of skin with soap and water. They do not wash off flat (porous) wall paint (be warned). My kids did all of this spontaneously.

I would have liked it better if it were less expensive, since in my house, it won't; last long. Alternatively, a stronger material than cardboard would have been appreciated.

product_title: Mega Bloks Halo UNSC Broadsword Midnight Strike (Discontinued by manufacturer)
review_headline: If you are a "Halo" Mega Bloks fan, the UNSC Broadsword Midnight Strike set is AWESOME!
review_body:
I have to say that the Halo Mega Bloks sets have been one of the most awesome sets in the entire Mega Bloks line. With super poseable figures with interchangeable armor systems and a pretty solid offering in terms of vehicles and figure sets, this is no doubt a series that separates itself from Lego sets.

Granted, hardcore Lego fans will either accept Mega Bloks or never accept them, for those with an open mind, will find the "Halo" sets to be exciting and fun.

But I have to admit that the "HALO" UNSC Broadsword Midnight Strike looked a bit challenging. For one, there are many parts that I have seen in a Mega Bloks set so far and wasn't sure how difficult it would be (considering I have worked on difficult "Batman" and "Star Wars" projects before).

But for the most part, the instructions were easy to follow but what I found important was to organize parts before working. There are a lot of small parts and while listed for 8+ and at 716-pieces, this is one set I recommend a parent assist their children with, as I can see my son getting a bit nervous with too many small parts that may be easy to lose.

But for the most part, this set was pretty awesome as you get three character figures: The Master Chief, Didact and Cortana and the UNSC Broadsword Midnight Strike.

Overall, this Mega Bloks "Halo" set is pretty awesome! You get your bang for your buck with this set and "Halo" fans should be happy with this huge set. It's one of the more challenging in the "Halo" Mega Bloks set but also one of the coolest!

Recommended!

product_title: 1/10 2.4Ghz Exceed RC Electric AceTiger Rally Car Ready to Run (Black)
review_body:
I've had this car for a couple weeks now and wanted to put it through it's paces before leaving a review, upon the first box opening, I was floored at how feature filled this car is! As someone who hasn't been in hobbyclass RC for about 5 years, I remember when I had to pay $200+ for a Traxxas (cheapest brand you could get at the time) Stampede with a mechanical speed control, Ready-to-Run, with one battery and a charger. This little car? $119.00.

2 favorite features
-Remember the days when you had to buy different radio crystals to run with your friends? Not anymore! Thanks to the new radio technology, you can run a bunch of these immediately out of the box without messing with additional crystals.

-Throttle adjustment on the controller. When I was a kid, I had tons of "toy" R/C cars because I didn't have the skills needed to drive the hobbyclass ones at speed, this led to my parents buying tons more R/C cars as I got older. With this controller, I can dial the car down enough for my 4yr old nephew to drive it. I wish I could've captured the look on his face when he got to drive Uncle Rob's race car. Priceless

-Durability. Just this past weekend I had the car running around a large piece of land at our 2nd home, the car had no problem slicing through wet fresh cut grass, mulched leaves, sticks and other debris. The biggest debris of all? My brother's great dane though the car was a squirrel and gave chase, he eventually caught the car as the battery lost it's juice and sank his teeth in. The lexan body cracked a little bit on the roof, and there are some tooth holes in the side, but we continue to run the around (away from the Great Dane this time) all weekend long.

Bottom Line: If you're new to Hobbyclass R/C, this is a great way to get started. Your age doesn't matter (with the ability to dial down the throttle), I will be buying one of these for my nephew so he and I can enjoy them together.

If you're returning to Hobbyclass R/C, like me, I've been wanting to get back into R/C for a long time, but with all of kits out there and with all the new pricey technology, shopping for one can be overwhelming (not to mention costly) if you don't have the right advice. This is a great way to rejoin the hobby and not kill your wallet. This one is the first in my fleet as exceed has bunches of cars and trucks both gas and electric powered. product_title: Educational Insights Surfside Scramble Word Game
review_headline: Build Vocabulary with Your Kids - Show Off Your Vocabulary with Your Friends
review_body: I am an elementary school teacher. I received this game from a former colleague of mine who is now at Educational Insights. I played this game with my 10-year-old son first and he became frustrated that words had to begin with the last letter of previous words, at first. Once he got the hang of it, he had more fun but he said it just made him want to play Scrabble. When I let my 6th graders play, they were confused and frustrated with the game as well. I sat down with them and we played together and then the fun began. They were able to see what I was doing and they caught on rather quickly. Without prompting, they also said that it was like Scrabble but less fun. My students felt that it was a game that was "trying too hard to be educational." I love the concept of the game so I played with a group of other teachers. We had a blast! No one was confused and we were able to have fun with our words and we became very competitive, very quickly. It is a fun and compact game that I would take with me to parties, but the downside to using it in the classroom is that I would need to be actively playing the game with the students in order for it to be utilized.

It’s a slippery slope when you bring one Barbie in the house. First, she needs more clothes and then she loses her shoes all the time. Then she needs a closet. product_title: The Learning Journey Techno Gears Marble Mania Vortex 2.0 Construction Set
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:mo3IA27AAX1BUGN]]Overall, I think this is a great toy for the right age group (children who are into building things and old enough to follow lots of instructions). It is much more labor-intensive to put together than other marble runs I have owned. It comes with hundreds of little pieces, of different shapes and sizes (each labeled with a small number that coincides with the instruction booklet). The base pieces are kind of neat how they fit together like a puzzle. They are marked in the exact place to start building the marble run, as you follow the instructions. The instruction booklet is BIG. If your kid loves putting together Lego sets and following all of the directions, they will probably love this. It took my husband about an hour to assemble the whole set. A lot of the fun of the set and a lot of the time spent will involve putting it together. We have yet to discover how well you can make up your OWN configuration instead of following the exact directions, but since there were a LOT of extra pieces after building it, we assume it is possible.

Some good things about this toy:

-Lots of pieces for the older child to put together - if they enjoy that sort of thing!
-The automatic marble launcher is pretty neat! No need to feed the marbles in manually each time - it automatically shoots them back up, accompanied by pinball-like sounds.
-Lots of marble fun! It really is a neat toy.

Some bad things about this toy:

-Lots of pieces :) If you buy this for a younger child, just know you are going to spend a lot of time assembling it.
-It isn't the sturdiest-feeling toy ever. Especially as you take it apart, it sometimes feels like some of the smaller pieces are going to break easily.
-It kind of hurts your hands as you click all of the pieces together.
-The marbles sometimes fly off of the ramps; it just needs some slight adjusting to fix the problem though.

Despite the few cons, I do think this is a fun toy! It's definitely not perfect but has some great features., I do think this is a fun toy! It's definitely not perfect but has some great features.

product_title: My Monopoly Game
review_body:
I got a copy of this game for free from BzzAgent. I am normally not into photo personalization but fortunately, my in-laws are VERY into this stuff, so I made my copy of the game into a grandchildren-themed board.

Pros: You can put your own pictures and labels, some people love this stuff (like my in-laws), kids love seeing their picture on the game! Software was ok to use, I had to create an account because I didn't have any accounts that they link to. It worked fine for me, I noticed some people have problems with an iPad but I used a normal computer and it was fine.

Cons: The photos cover up the normal "game messages" (so instead of "you won $700 in the lottery", you put your own photo label). The pictures on the box showed labels like "Abigail's birthday" but I thought that was weird .Unfortunately the words take up a lot of space covering the photos and the font can't be made smaller, so you can't even replicate the original labels on your own photo personalized game pieces. That was a bit disappointing to me. I didn't particularly like how the game tokens are modified to accept a photo, some people may love it but I'd rather have a normal game piece and not a ginormous photo card sticking up from the scotty dog.

Summary - great for kids, great for people who love photo products, not so great if you just want to play a normal game of Monopoly!

product_title: The Resistance Avalon Card Game
review_headline: Deep game with great replay value
review_body:
Deep game with great replay value, but be prepared to lose some friends. I first played this several months ago, and was struck by the simplicity, and the way it builds on games such as Mafia, Werewolf, etc.

In brief, there are 2-4 "bad guys", who know who is good and who is bad, and 3-6 "good guys," who don't know anything. One of the good guys is "Merlin," who knows the bad guys and the good guys. The good guys try to "pass" the majority of five quests, and the bad guys try to "fail" the majority. To go on a quest, the leader, who changes every round, selects 1-3 other people as specified by the board. The team is voted on, and if it is approved, each team member votes "pass" or "fail," with any number of "fail" cards leading to a failed quest. Throughout is intense discussion, accusations, and deception - you won't be able to trust your friends after a few rounds. If the good guys pass three quests, the bad guys have one last shot by guessing who Merlin is. If they succeed, the bad guys win.

The benefits are that this can be played with a smaller crowd, since no players "die" and there is no moderator required, as in Mafia.The game also scales in difficulty as the people you play with get more experienced. You find yourself adjusting and thinking of ways to convince others of your innocence, and trying to "get into" the heads of those you're playing with. You'll get extremely good at lying.

Some negatives are that the game can be unbalanced for smaller groups (five people), since the bad guys have a 1/3 shot of guessing who Merlin is. The other is that as you get experienced, it's better to play with experienced people, because they are less likely to obviously give away their allegiance - it can be frustrating teaching new people to play or playing with people who are just not good at deception or logic.

review_body: Replacing the batteries in Wall-e is easy. All you need is an exact-o knife or a razor blaze. Cut his bottom right where the Disney Tag sits. You will then see where the batteries sit in the talk-box. Then take a small Phillips Screwdriver and unscrew the battery holder and slide the plastic latch upwards. You will then find three Pakco L1154H Green Cell Batteries that operate Wall-e's talk-box. Find a retail store that carries this particular model of battery or order a whole bunch online. My suggestion would be to go to Joanne's Fabric or Micheal's and buy some Velcro so when the batteries need replacing again, you can just un-Velcro Wall-e and replace his batteries to last a lifetime. product_title: ALEX Toys Craft Hip to be Square Crochet
review_headline: I am disappointed.  My search continues for a nice beginners crochet kit.
review_body:
This craft kit is such a cute idea, learning how to crochet by making a granny square and then tying all the squares together to make a purse, scarf or hat, but.........

the instructions appeared simple until I got to step 2 in the Granny square. The instructions say to do a double crochet, but they don't give instructions for doing a double crochet prior to that!! So although this is a cute set, learning how to do to a granny square with only this instruction booklet is not possible for me, let alone my daughter. I haven't crocheted in years so I will have to learn to crochet (from another source) just to be able to use this kit and teach her. The instructions are in 4 different languages and color-coded, and also shows diagrams for left and right handed people, in the beginning at least. We did fine on the chain stitch and the slip stitch but then we headed into double crochets and shells without any examples.

The tin is nice for storing the project and yarns, but the top uses a see-through plastic and is not made out of tin as the rest, although it seems sturdy enough to me.

However, I'm a bit disappointed that my daughter can't use this to learn crochet, as it's just too difficult.
