product_title: Spacerail/Spacewrap Level 9 ,200ft of Rails - New Arrival - Special Edition, Limited - Hardest Level for Genius Kids
review_headline: Fit for the likes of Sisyphus
review_body:
Simply incredible.

This thing is a beast.

As many other reviewers have said, this is not for the faint of heart. The instructions for this, even if they were perfectly translated into English, are merely a novelty really and only give the builder the general idea of how it is supposed to go together.

If you are the type of model builder that requires explicit step-by-step instructions and hand-holding along the way, or get easily frustrated when something doesn't look or work right the first time, this is not the kit for you.

However, if you are the type of model builder or artist who can look at a subject, dwell on it, and intuit the proper method on your own based on planning things out, careful observation, and a LOT of trial and error then you will find this extremely satisfying to build.

There have been some negative reviews about the condition of these when they arrive, so at first I was a bit skeptical but have had prior good experience with their other kits, albeit from a few years ago.

Standard shipping was what we paid for, with an estimated delivery date a little over a month out from the date of purchase. To our surprise, we received a text from DHL indicating it was scheduled for delivery just one week later. The package was well padded and aside from some very minor creasing of the box all of the contents were received in good order.

All of the pieces had a minimal amount of flash, there were no improper fills or deformed/broken pieces, and many of the parts (the ones marked with a + after the quantity on the parts sheet in the instructions) had 5 or 6 extras included.

When compared to purchases of similar products in the past (both recent and back in the 80's), these kits are an exceptional value. They are still being manufactured, so that helps too.

Get one.
You won't regret it.
Even if you never finish it as shown on the box:
It will grow on you, and you will get lost in it like a Doozer on Fraggle Rock... with roller coasters!

product_title: Disney Sofia the First Tea Party Picnic Doll
review_body:
There is a lot to this play set so please forgive the long review. At this price you should know as many details as possible. There are several cute touches that point to attention to detail which make the price more acceptable. It is a Mattel product, so it does have years of quality products behind it.

When I first saw the play set I knew it would be a huge hit. My 4 year old granddaughter loves Sofia the First and playing tea party. She has a little dollie stroller that she fills with her own little tea party toys and pushes to the car when I pick her up. Now she has this adorable set to play with when she comes over.

It is smaller in size than I imagined. It is for ages 3 and up. There are a lot of small items so if you have younger children in the house, please keep track of these small choking hazard pieces. For example, the teacups are 1 1/4" in diameter and 3/4" tall, and the cupcakes are 1" tall and 3/4 " in diameter. It comes with 3 AA batteries. Yea! The amulet around her neck flashes when activated, if that is important information for you to know.

You can't drink from the cups. They are tiny and solid. So if you want a real tea party, for the humans in attendance you will need cups.

The pink in this set is more of a hot mauve pink, not a cotton candy pink. The doll is about 9 1/2" tall with the larger head that is popular today. The arms articulate at the shoulder. That is the only movement. The face is beautifully painted, she has big blue eyes, and the skin is smooth to touch. The hair is a light auburn brown color and a bit stiff. It is not very long. The dress is cute like a princess but not overdone. She has white pearlescent molded gloves that do not come off, perfect for a tea party. Her hat is mauve. Her shoes are lavender and come off. There is a "charm" attached to the from of her skirt. I assume that is what it is. The instructions mention there are additional ones for purchase???

The bunny is gray plastic with a blue bow tie. His head moves and the arm that can hold a tea cup raises. The ears are fabric. He does not talk. His voice comes from Sofia as part of a conversation with her when her sensor is activated, regardless of which piece activates it. His voice is different than hers. It is actually well done.

The accessories are good quality as far as plastic toys go. I was expecting thin, cheap, poorly painted plastic but this set has a nice feel and the colors are slightly pearlescent. They will last with the proper care. There are 2 cups, 2 saucers, 2 cupcakes, a teapot, a pastry stand for the cupcakes, a picnic basket and a checkered picnic cloth. Only the cupcakes, tea cups, and bunny activate the voice sensor when in very close proximity to her amulet.

I love that the handles for the 2 tea cups fit perfectly around the doll's and rabbit's hands. Not so easy to lose. When Sofia raises the teacup to her mouth, it gets close enough to activate the sensor and she speaks.

The picnic basket opens, and the small items fit inside. I love the attention to detail with the accessories: the swatch of fabric hanging out the corner if the picnic basket, the raised design on the tea cups, the cherry on top of the cupcakes, and the pastry stand - very thoughtful. The table cloth is just the perfect detailed touch to make the picnic tea party fantasy complete.

Sofia's and the bunny's voices are activated either by pressing the purple amulet around Sofia's neck (which flashes) or by bringing the bunny, teacups, or cupcakes very close to the amulet. The amulet is easy to press with little fingers. Another thoughtful touch. The voices come from a hard plastic purple box, shaped like a ruffled slip under her gown. Another cute detail. product_title: Barbie and The Secret Door Pink Unicorn Doll
review_headline: Translucent pink unicorn with colorful hair extensions
review_body:
Although my daughter has seen the Barbie movie "The Secret Door" (sold separately) from which this Barbie comes, seeing the movie isn't necessary to being able to appreciate this unicorn.

My kids love all things Barbie, and a unicorn (in pink, no less), can only make Barbie better. The unicorn looks just okay in the product picture, but is beautiful in real life. It's mostly translucent pink with a whitish back and flowers, butterflies, and other designs on her hind end. The mane and tail are pink and purple, with the colors fairly evenly distributed.

My daughter loves playing with the unicorn's hair and hair attachments. I thought the orange, yellow, and blue clip in extensions were a little too Punky Brewsterish, but my daughter loves them. She also loves that there are two flower clips that she can use on the unicorn or on her own hair. I love that these accessories are big and functional enough to keep with the unicorn, so I don't have a ton more loose Barbie pieces all over the house.

While the unicorn isn't articulated at all, she does have heart designs molded onto the body that distinguish her from typical Barbie horses. And, of course, she's got her horn. I was a little concerned about the potential for injury, but the horn is a rather soft rubber or silicone that keeps its shape but has a lot of give. You could poke an eye out with it, but it would take some effort. Although the pink unicorn is a character in the movie, I'd love to see another come out in blue and/or purple.

review_body:

I put it together myself so I can promise you that a fifty something can do it. But I also found myself having to use a lot of patience and I'm contemplating superglue right now. The plastic is sturdy. I think that it would take a bit of force to actually break it, but I honestly haven't kid tested it yet. It does seem to fall apart pretty easily. In fact I am seriously considering putting it on the top of a bookcase out of reach as a display piece

This is a compromise rating. As a toy for a five year old to play with I wouldn't rate it highly, probably two stars. As a collector's item I would probably give it four.

product_title: Plan Toy Baby Walker
review_body:
We bought this for our first child when he was starting to cruise at about 9 months. He loved this as the transitional item as starting around 10 months he would cruise, then take a few solo steps, then grab this. He would push it when he wanted to go somewhere too far to walk when he was just starting to walk independently. The blocks are great, and have gotten much use in the last 3 years.

I've deducted a star because this does not work as well for our second baby, now a cruiser herself. It is not sturdy enough for her to use it to pull herself up (it tips over and throws her off balance), and when she's standing she can't push it if the wheels are tight (which they need to be for it to be safe for her). I'm sure it will be great in a couple months, but I was hoping it would provide the same independence for her that it gave her brother at this stage, and it doesn't quite.

However, the materials, construction, and colors are all great and have held up well over 3 years of use.

product_title: Taby Tray Home School Car Vehicle Kids Children Activity Play Fun Desk
review_body:
We purchased this for our toddler for a long road trip. He's in a Diono car seat that's forward facing. The tray was fantastic and kept our sons toys/snacks/books/etc on the tray. I didn't have to keep reaching back or picking up fallen toys.

There is a small lip around the entire tray. I kind of wish it were a little taller as the hotwheels can easily roll off with a little force. But I was okay with that. The tray works well, even without having armrests on the car seat. There's a strap, included with the tray, that has easy-to-use snaps on both sides of the tray so you can detach one or both sides. Plus, the straps can be easily tightened so that was a good fit. It is durable plastic and doesn't bend, so it can fit lose on the car seat/lap or a little more snug.

I highly recommend this if you are looking for some sort of tray. It does. It move around once you have it clipped into place.

product_title: Classic Mega Sketcher Toy
review_headline: My 4yo was not happy with it. Neither was I.
review_body:
I read all the glowing reviews, and was enticed. The two sided pen. The smooth, non-segmented writing surface. The different shapes. It all sounded good. But my 4 year old was not happy.

- First, it's big. I know, it's called a "mega" sketcher but the frame around the surface area feels bulky. It's harder to cram into a book bag to take in the car.
- The writing surface seems to be a film, not a surface. And my son repeatedly tried to peel it off. I thought there was one of those clear "peel off" decals on top to protect it as if it was in a store. But no. That's just the way it is.
- There's a gap between the writing surface and the edge of the frame so when my son was using the plastic shapes, they kept getting caught underneath the edge, between the surface and the plastic border.
- We have two other Fisher Price "magnedoodles" and the contrast of the Megasketcher is much lower. My son would scribble repeatedly trying to make the image darker. It doesn't get any darker. It's just sort of a middle grey as opposed to a near black on the Magnedoodles.
- The pen on ours was not 2-sided. There was no "fat" line. Only the thin tip worked.
- Erasing the image is a PITA. First of all, its oriented he opposite way of the Fisher Price models (probably has to be to avoid getting sued) so the travel is shorter (yay!) but the bar is longer making it harder to push across the surface. It's a torque issue. And the longer rod means it needs more push to go across.
- Secondly (yes, more erasing), it takes numerous passes to erase an image. I will grant that the Megasketcher does a better job, in the end, of completely erasing the image compared to a Magnedoodle, but it takes many passes to get there. Slow passes work better than fast ones but you can't tell my four year old that. He's used to doing two passes with the Magnedoodle- zip-zap- and get right back to drawing. He would do several passes, butthen get frustrated when his hand slipped off the knob because his other hand was on the drawing surface and there simply wasn't enough torque (see above) to get the eraser to pass underneath.
- The shapes don't have magnets under them to hold them in place. Again, probably to differentiate it from the Magnedoodle. The shapes have little plastic clips on the edges to hold them in place. I'm an adult. _I_ had a hard time getting them to clip into place correctly. Unless they clip correctly, they fall out when you walk around. When a 4yo loses the _one_ icon he wants to use, it's not pretty.

So this is not the product for my 4 yo boy. I thought it would be better than it was. I thought it would be better than the Magnedoodle. But for the way my boy likes to draw, the higher contrast, stronger writing surface, stiffer edges, easier erasing, and the magnetic, drop-in shape holders all contribute to a better user experience for my little boy.

It's not a one star because I can see a more patient 8 year old appreciating the detailed surface, and not getting the shapes caught underneath. But overall, I think the changes they made, so it was different enough from the Magnedoodle, to be brought to market, greatly hampered the product it could have been.

product_title: LeapFrog Roll and Go Rocking Horse
review_headline: Very cute!  Best suited for babies just learning to crawl or walk...
review_body:
This horse is very cute and colorful, and very attractive to young children. There are 3 main ways to play with this. The child can rock the horse from side to side, push the saddle which lights up, and roll the toy across the floor. Everything that little ones do to this horse will cause lights and sounds, or even a few songs to play. The horse talks to baby and asks baby to rock him or push him again.
Each time baby swipes at the horse it will rock and possibly move away, which makes this a little difficult for a crawling baby to grab. That is good, because as it moves away it encourages baby to move and crawl after it. This toy is definitely good at coaxing little ones to move more as they learn to crawl and learn to walk.
It's also fun for adults to sit on the floor with little ones and push the horse back and forth on the floor, almost like a ball.
I also liked that it came 'ready to go' out of the box with batteries installed.
I would recommend this for babies and very young children. Particularly children who are learning to crawl or possibly learning to walk. Once a child can walk well, run, and jump they might not be interested in this for very long. I would say a good age range for this is 6 months to 18 months.

product_title: Doctor Who 11th Doctor Sonic Screwdriver
review_body:
Dooctor Whoooooo *flails wildly*

Let me explain to you how much I am obsessed with this show. Okay. Maybe not here and now. But Doctor Who has added to my pile of good things in so many ways.

To the screwdriver review thingie. I've had mine for a short while. Been using it sparingly for several weeks now. Was thrilled to get it during a sale, to replace my pipsqueak five inch sonic screwdriver flashlight that doesn't even make noise.

The real thing is so much better. Oh my giddy aunt, it is better. The box stated "Twelfth Doctor's Sonic Screwdriver," which is accurate I suppose considering Capaldi!Doctor is still using his predecessor's version, but Smith!Doctor fans must not be alarmed. This is indeed what most people recognize as the Eleventh Doctor's screwdriver.

As well as a clever toy, this is an extremely convincing prop. Plastic but weighty, and nicely detailed, the true coloring and texturing make this a classy accessory to your Doctor Who cosplay.

The sonic-ing actions work thusly: when the screwdriver is retracted, you can either use the lower side button or the red button at the bottom (under the hinged cap) to activate the light-up and sound. The sound is a quite respectable mimicry of the screwdriver's most common bzzzzzing sound that continues indefinitely for as long as you press the button, and it alternates between a higher and lower pitch each time you press the button.

To extend the screwdriver you press the upper side button and it SNAPS into epic full length. When extended, the side button WILL NOT WORK to activate the light and sound. You have to use the red button. This makes it a bit fumbly, because the side button is much more convenient. But you can just fist the end of the screwdriver to conceal the fact that you're pressing the button on the end (which is what I do in pictures).

I hope this thing takes batteries that are sold in America, because I wouldn't know what to do otherwise. I love my screwdriver, and this purchase was twenty dollars I won't be sorry about spending. Just one more thing: it does NOT DO WOOD. Gosh, wouldn't you think that somebody would fix that. However, it's still just great for disabling a Dalek's eyestalk.

The quality of the cards is fairly nice. They're not super rugged, but they're not flimsy either. It's similar to ordinary playing cards. The fact that they're round is novel enough to make them a little more interesting. The small metal tin that holds them is a really nice touch, and makes the game easy to toss into a purse or bag for nights out at restaurants or traveling when you need an activity.

It's a fun little way to practice word recognition, and the tie-in to Pixar films ought to make it a lot more attractive to kids who might not be huge fans of reading otherwise. (I remember watching an experiment where they showed that kids would want rocks over food for breakfast if you stuck Dora the Explorer stickers on the rocks... Might as well use marketing powers for good as well as evil.)

product_title: K’NEX – Plants vs. Zombies Wild West Skirmish Building Set – 219 Pieces –  Ages 5+ Construction Educational Toy
review_headline: Cute Details with Some Issues to Overcome
review_body:
My kids really enjoy the Plants vs. Zombie video games, so they can appreciate the theme of this set. The detailed zombies are great until you try to stand them up...It's very tricky. We could only get the prospector to consistently stand on a brick platform. The other two zombies carefully stand on the floor or on the spinning middle stand.

The arena is imaginative with various targets-some of which you can hit and make spin. This is VERY hard to do. I would recommend using more building blocks for simple targets alongside the zombies to increase playability for younger children.

The plant shooter was fine for my son's shooting style (he only touches the head of plant). However, when I tried to shoot (putting slight pressure on the base), the plant and its long, brown bench (sliding on the K'nex rods) kept breaking apart.

Full-color directions show the plant shooter being fired from two thin rectangular bricks forming a square on the floor. Unfortunately, these green pieces are not included in the set, so I took apart the two unused (brown) Lego-type benches with the same rectangular shapes and used that as a shooting base for the plant. This provided a much better experience.

Caution: This may not be the best choice for the recommended 5+ yrs. of age, especially without adult supervision. The shooter is fast and the balls are hard...Consider backing this set up to a wall to discourage children from getting behind the target scenery (in the line of fire) and to minimize losing ammo under beds, dressers...

review_body: I received two Littlest Pet Shop style sets free from Hasbro for my daughters to try out, The Pet Shop Style Set and the Say Ahh To the Spa Style Set.  This was not one that we received for free.  After playing with the two we had, my daughter saved up her allowance and purchased this one on her own because she loves the sets so much!  The new style design of LPS really promotes more creativity and imagination.  This Fun room set is adorable!  It comes with tiny hamsters, a tube, rocking ball, and even tiny little hamster water bottles that hang on the wall.  My 7 year old picked it out and loves it.  She had no problems putting it together by herself.  The directions are very easy to understand and the set can be taken apart and rebuilt over and over again.  That's one of her favorite parts of the new design.  It came with a sheet of stickers which my daughter loved decorating with.  It also comes with deco bits, which are tiny colorful decorations that can be stuck into the side walls and on some of the accessories for decoration.  My daughter loves changing around the deco bits every time she play with it.  My 7 year old has no problem putting the deco bits into the holes, but it is to hard for my 5 year old.  The sets are like a town of dollhouses for animals that you can collect and put together, and my daughters love animals, and dollhouses.  Also, Hasbro came out with an app to kind of go along with the play sets.  Some of the pets have a paw print on their backs.  The paw print can be scanned into the app so then the child can play with that pet in the game.  My daughters both love scanning the pets and playing games with them on our tablet.  Both of my daughters and I are really happy with the new design of the LPS line.  They have a lot of fun with them, even together, and I love that it's been a month and a half since we started collecting them and they are still playing with them regularly.  We already have 5 sets and I'm sure that there are more in ourfuture!

Recommended!

product_title: MAYFLASH Universal Adapter For Xbox360/Ps3/Ps2/Ps Vita Tv/Pc Usb
review_body:
I purchased this device so I can use my Dualshock 3 on an XBOX 360 for an Ultimate Marvel vs Capcom 3 tournament (West Coast Warzone 4). In order to use a PS3/PS2 controller on an XBOX 360 you must have a Microsoft wired XBOX 360 controller, 3rd party controllers do not work. This controller will work best: http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B003ZSN600/ref=cm_cr_ryp_prd_ttl_sol_1
First plug in the adapter into the XBOX 360, plug in the MICROSOFT WIRED XBOX 360 controller into the adapter, the adapter will light up and indicate which player you are, unplug your XBOX 360 controller, then plug in your PS3/PS2 controller. This device worked perfectly no dropped inputs, no extra inputs, no pauses/disconnections, and no lag. I used this device the whole weekend, on about 5 different XBOX 360s, and it worked fine. I also tested it with an XBOX 360 controller on the PS3, just plug n play and it works fine. The same goes for a PS2 controller on PS3 just plug n play. I purchased this device in May 2014 and it is still working fine.

PS: I wouldn't take negative reviews very seriously most of them are from people who failed to follow basic instructions. However, if you're still confused on how this device works just YouTube it and you'll be good.

product_title: Zoomer Interactive Puppy - Shadow
review_body:
I received Shadow free through BzzAgent for my family to try. It couldn't have come at a better time as my 6yr old has been asking if we can get a dog. The way this toy move is exceptional and impressive. The commands are simple and easy to learn. Everyone who we have shown this toy to has been completely amazed with how it works. There have been some negative reviews on the battery life. We haven't had as issue with this yet. It seems he works long enough for my kids (two boys ages 6 and 2) to play with and hasn't run out of battery before they were ready to let him rest.

Since Shadow arrives as a "puppy" and needs to be "trained", he is a little disobedient at first. While all the adults finds this an extremely clever addition to Shadow's personality, my 6 year old found it a bit frustrating and has caused him to put Shadow away a few times.

Shadow has many commands and even some hidden ones that you can find on your own. My son's friend was over and told Shadow to "get down" and he started dancing. That was a big hit! He sits, sings, plays dead and yes he even hikes his leg and pees!

All and all I think Shadow is a great toy. He's cleverly made and entertaining for all ages. I would say the ideal age for use would probably be about about 8-9 having more patience to "train" him. He is definitely a great alternative if you're not ready for a real puppy yet.

product_title: Dragon Caster
review_headline: VERY fun, original game with one moderate problem.
review_body:
I missed out on the kickstarter campaign for this game, but got a hold of it not long after its release. Dragon caster is about dragons and magicians, two themes my 14 year old son loves. We play a wide variety of games (Smallworld, Eclipse, Dominion, LOTR TCG, Smash Up, Descent, Waterdeep, Power Grid, etc.) So we aren't new to this arena. I was a little skeptical of a first release kickstarter game, but thankfully was pleasantly surprised.

The game employs a fascinating, and as far as I know, original play mechanic. It is fun, it is relatively short, it pulls you into it's theme incredibly well. It has (for me) the right mix of luck and logic (I lean a bit more to the logic side). It is fast paced, and holds the interest VERY well.

So why four stars instead of five? The instruction manual. I'm not new to this arena, and it really took a while to work through this book. Information is not well organized, and there are a number of conditions that can occur in the game that simply were not explained or barely touched upon. If you read through the book several times, then read the rules forum on Board Game Geek, then watch a couple of walkthroughs on Youtube you'll be able to put it together. Still we shouldn't have to go to those measures. A little clearer explanation on a number of points (the worst being Elder dragons) would have gone a long way. The game designer is VERY quick to answer questions on the board game geek website, but again, we really shouldn't have to rely on this.

Is this game worth playing? ABSOLUTELY. If you are a board game geek like me, it is WELL worth the effort to learn the rules. Let me tell you why:

The concept is fascinating. You have a "Caster" who can move left and right on your side of the board. He casts dragons and mana onto the play area between you and the other player's caster on the opposite side of the board. The grid between the casters is a hex layout (I'ma sucker for hex grid games), and the dragons fly across, trying eventually to kill the caster on the other side. The dragons must move forward, and can pick up mana to give them special powers. Upon encountering other dragons, battles ensue (The dice play a role in this, so luck is involved). Still, the types of dragons you cast, the battles you take on, and your strategy to get to the caster on the other side are very much skill based.

The mechanic for casting dragons is one of the coolest, most original ideas I have seen on a board game. You have this "Casting Chart" with a 3 by 3 grid of numbers one through nine. You roll two dice, and take the total number, dividing it any way you want to cover numbers on the chart (so a roll of nine could cover a 1 and 8, or a 2 and 7, etc..). I know this won't make much sense until you see the game, but what this means is that even though what you cast is based on a dice roll, you have a lot of choice in terms of how you use that roll to cast dragons and mana. The choices you make are as important as the dice roll, so you never fully feel at the mercy of the roll.

My son and I play this game a LOT. It is best with two players, and we knock through games in less than 30 minutes. There is a ton of replay value here around this engaging concept and fascinating mechanic. Take the warning about the instruction manual to heart, however. You'll have some research to do if you want to get the most out of this game.

review_body: I was using Suburb/Barcode style tires on the rear of my RC10T4 with ribbed fronts. The surface of my practice area/track near my house is a mixture of rough asphalt and loose dirt, so some of the dirt gets onto the asphalt portions of the track making for a varied and slippery surface. No jumps, so it's more like a rally course. With the Suburbs it's like driving on ice, with my fastest laps in the low 21 second range. I put Gladiators on the front and rear, and it's a night and day difference. Within 10 minutes, my fastest laps were in the low 19 seconds (2 seconds faster). Not only was the car more planted in the turns, I could run down the long straights at full throttle while keeping the car in control. With the suburbs, full throttle at any point on the straight would cause the back end to break loose. Highly recommend for loose dirt, bashing, and asphalt.

product_title: Doodle Quest Game
review_body: I found this game fun for a variety of ages and skill levels, and different than anything I've played before. Each round is a separate drawing challenge (getting through a maze, circling some things without touching others, etc.) They'd be very simple except that each player completes them on their own blank drawing space. The clear overlays can then be placed over the challenge for scoring. While it's hard to explain, it's easy to grasp the concept of the game once you have it in hand.    Note that this game really isn't about drawing, art or creativity. It does use spatial skills and hand eye coordination. It's doodling in a loose sense, with squiggly lines, circles, and the occasional use of included stencils.    This was fun for a family, including adults. It's probably a game adults will enjoy with kids, though, and not the latest craze at adult game night. I think the age guideline of 6+ is accurate. Our almost-five-year-old player needed lots of guidance and sometimes didn't quite get it. However, not all players need to know how to read. It'll be good for lots of play; materials are all reusable and challenges should each be fun to complete multiple times.

review_headline: Impressive But Overpriced With Inadequate Instructions
review_body:
I got my Imperial Probe Droid directly from Sideshow this week. My first impression is that it's bigger than what I was expecting, especially with the antennas extended. I was hoping to add it to a curio cabinet that houses my 1/6 scale Star Wars figures, but it's simply too tall. Oh, well... I'll have to display it outside the cabinet. I was expecting it to be dark grey or the color of metal, but it's black with grey scuff marks. (Perhaps my memory of the old Kenner Probot is why I thought it would be grey.) It's also lighter than what I was expecting because it's made of hollow plastic. Anyway, the figure is highly detailed and looks nice with the Hoth base cover under it. There's lots of articulation in the legs, and the head and turret gun swivel. The light has 2 modes (white and yellow), and the sound effects are authentic to the film. Overall, it looks and sounds impressive.

There's definitely room for improvement, though. The instructions show you how to put the figure together and where the batteries are located, but they fail to point out where the separate on switches are for the light and sound effects. After consulting others' video reviews on Youtube, I finally found the on switches, but the product still wouldn't work. Then suddenly after 4 hours of the unit not working, the light and sound began to function. I don't know what I did to cause them to work, but thankfully everything is still working. The legs and body are numbered so you know where each leg is supposed to attach, but several small pieces don't attach well to the body because the holes their pegs are supposed to go into are either too small or too big: with the small holes, you have to carefully force pieces into them and hope they don't break; with the large holes, pieces fit so loosely that they sometimes fall off the body. I would have preferred a clear support post over the black one to convey the idea that the probe is hovering (or at least a white one to blend with a snowy backdrop). Another option would have been to include a couple of different posts to suit customers' preferences. Finally, for what Sideshow is asking for this figure, I think it should have been made of a light metal (or $100 cheaper).

product_title: India Rails
review_body:
I love all the Mayfair Rails games!

But if you are only going to buy one, chose either Empire Builder or European Rails. This one has some issues.

First off, like most of the first-run editions, it's all in black and white. The playing pieces all have little stickers that you have to apply to them - and they are missing some. They say there are 2 circuses and 5 pilgrims in the game, but there are only stickers for 1 circus and 3 pilgrims. Since the stickers are all on one sheet, and the sheet wasn't ripped or damaged, this must be a flaw in the game.

Second, the board is A LOT SMALLER. Most of the games, the puzzle playing board is six pieces, and the country is large enough to read the cities and towns. This one, although India is a large country - and the game includes the surrounding countries of Bangladesh, Pakistan, Nepal, and two others I can't think of right now, the playing board is only four pieces. The board is thinner - substandard quality, and it warped. We have ours sitting under a set of books right now to try to flatten it out. The spots are smaller and closer together, so I know it won't wear well. We literally played the SPOTS OFF our Empire Builder game and have to replace it! But that took years of playing to do. I'm not sure that India rails will last that long. And because the spots are smaller, and the towns and cities are smaller, they are harder to read.

I do like the addition of some newer products.

I will play this game again. But I really LOVE Martian Rails! We own Empire Builder (USA), Eurorails, Lunar Rails, Martian Rails, Nepon Rails (Japan), China Rails and India. I would place India as my least favorite of them all - but that's like saying, "what's your least favorite flavor of ice cream?" I love all ice cream!

review_body:
Our 17 month old boy is attracted to this Laugh and Learn Laptop. He keeps going back to it and pushing the buttons. I like this toy because it really captures his attention with the cool retro bulb dot matrix display!

However one of his favorite buttons is the Level button, so he keeps changing the settings and then the learning stage is not consistent. It would have been better to make the Level button hard for the toddler to change (this is a common issue I see with many early baby electronic toys -- on the other toys he changes the volume or turns them off entirely because the switch is so easy to access).

Sometimes he closes the lid and then can't figure out how to open it. So I leave it completely folded open, face up on the floor rather than with the screen tilted at an angle, this way it is less likely to close.

The fact that this looks like a laptop makes it cute for adults as we watch. But from the baby's perspective this might as well be a simple box with buttons on it. Overall this is a nice interactive toy and maybe satisfy his urge to push the keyboard on my work laptop.

product_title: Fisher-Price Little People City Skyway
review_headline: There are no battery requirements which is great. And this also means there is no issue ...
review_body:
Thanks to Fisher-Price and BzzAgent I and my two children were given the opportunity to try this toy for free. In return I get to give my review of this toy. When we got it in the mail we were very excited to get it out of the box and get playing with it. I was a little overwhelming to see all of the pieces at first, but with the step-by-step instructions it was very simple. You do need to have a Phillips screw driver for screwing in certain pieces. I was a little concerned a first with the screws and small children, but once it was together I was confident that the screws were not going to be a issue. This is a toy that will last. There are no battery requirements which is great. And this also means there is no issue with loud noised for little ears!

My children love this toy! It is so tall. It has become the focal point of the room. It gets played with everyday. The love all of the little details that Fisher-Price has added to the tower. At the base there are paw prints in the 'cement', an apple core, a dropped ice cream cone and a chalk drawing. the have also found the ducks flying and the hot air balloon. Two cars with 'Little People' inside the driver seat come with the tower. It is very colorful and great for different learning experiences. It has the traffic light and the switches for the different directions for the cars to go. Only one car can go down at a time. It won't allow cars to go down at the same time for a race. I find it really sturdy and seems solid in construction once you have it all together.

The only negative that I found was that on the tracks there are slots all the way down the middle. Which make other toy cars get stuck along the way. With kids and there imaginations, in my house this toy is not just for 'Little People' cars it has become many other things and no other cars will go down the track unless the wheels fit just like the 'Little People' cars do. The Little People® City Skyway has offered many hours play and becoming many other thing than just a 'City Skyway'.nd becoming many other thing than just a 'City Skyway'.

Rather than include software in the box, users are required to use an app from the Apple App Store or for Android from Google play. In lieu of that you are referred to www.mymonopoly.com. The website www.mymonopoly.com is merely an ad for the product featuring a link for where to buy it. Eventually I discovered another site
https://na.mymonopoly.com/ which is the one where the software is. There you will find a list of supported devices and browsers. You are required to register to use the software in a browser. As most of the photos I wish to use are on other computers, I'm leery about registering from the one I'm currently using. I presently don't have access to an app capable device so do not know if you have to register that way as well. Regardless I find it an invasion of privacy.

product_title: 4D Vision Velociraptor Anatomy Modely
review_headline: This makes a pretty good display once you get it all together
review_body:
This makes a pretty good display once you get it all together. There are issues with fit and finish on some of the parts. If you want to get it to fit right you will need an X-Acto knife to trim some of the tabs and holes just a little bit. There are also some nasties on a couple of the parts where they were removed from the parts trees before painting. So you can trim those off with an X-Acto knife too.

Be very careful what you are buying. This company makes two velociraptors. One is smaller and one is larger. Same thing with the T-Rex. It's easy to order the wrong one by mistake. The two products have different looking packaging. This issue is made more confusing by the fact that quite a few of the product pages on Amazon picture the small version when they are selling the large version. I have seen this issue for both the velociraptor and the T-Rex. The box for the small dinosaurs is green and blue. The box my large velociraptor came in was white. But this is not much help since many of the product pages show the wrong box.

Furthermore, based on some of the reviews I have read it's obvious that some customers bought and paid for the large t-Rex and got the small one. It's easy to see how a seller could make this mistake. The small version should cost around 25 and the large version should cost around 50 and upwards. If you get your model and it is not the stated dimensions, send it back because they sent you the wrong one by mistake.

More advice about assembling this model: It's a snap kit, and the parts are made to be removable, in theory. But some of them are really hard to get off without breaking them. Especially the clear skin. So it's worth it to take your time and make sure all the other parts are in place and fitted just like you want them before you put the skin on. Because otherwise you are going to have to get the skin off to refit some of the internal parts.And getting the skin off is really tough to do without scratching something or breaking off one of the pins.

It's important to take your time. You should allow about two hours to put this model together if you want to do a good job. I don't recommend this for young kids because it's a little difficult to put together due to fit and finish issues, and that could be frustrating unless you have some modeling experience.

Overall this is a really cool display piece. I have one quibble about the base. The label on the base says "Discovery Channel" when it should say "Velociraptor" and maybe the genus and species name. This is kind of cheesy and they missed an opportunity there to show a little class.

I did have trouble with some loose wiring. Our bear turns on and off if you drop it and the on/off sensor floats around in the back instead of always being in a set spot. product_title: The Learning Journey Techno Gears Marble Mania Vortex 2.0 Construction Set
review_body:
My son, 7, is a big lover of anything he can build. Legos, K'nex, Tinkertoys, Erector Sets, architectural blocks, Citiblox, old-fashioned models ... You name, and if it involves intricate assembly, he's all over it. He's also a fan of marble runs, and can spend several hours with our [[ASIN:B00BJEYLOC Hape - Quadrilla - Vertigo - Marble Railway in Wood]] creating and executing various runs.

I assumed this Vortex set would be similar. It's not. First off, it's not reconfigurable. It can be assembled one way, and one way only. And assembly isn't easy either. He struggled to push the support parts together, as they look in the pictures like they might grooved K'nex like pieces, but actually have plastic ridges you must push until they click into place ... Or break off, whichever comes first. I didn't snap any while helping him, but it sure felt like I would.

And, yes, a parent will definitely have to help most kids under 10 assemble this, for sheer hand strength if nothing else. Mine can easily put together 1,000+ Lego sets labeled 14+, but simply lacked the patience and precision needed to snap these not-so-well-made parts together.

The instructions were OK, and easy enough for even my son to understand on his own, it was just the physical assembly that required my help. I'd say he did half and I did half and it took us about an hour.

Oddly, the pieces that don't snap together are the ones that will need to be the steadiest: the marble run itself. Which actually just lies in the frame work and stacks on top of each other, making it way too easy to knock a piece out and also creating little ridges the marbles can get stuck in, or pushing them over the sides of the inadequately deep ducts. It also makes it basically impossible to move this run intact. Overall: very bad design!

The motorized launch mechanism seems wildly unnecessary. It's loud, sounds like it's grinding grain, and awkward but, without it, the marbles get stuck, so if want to do the run, you have to use it.

The \\"glow in the dark\\" feature was also a bust, as turning out the lights didn't elicit any real sort of glow. One piece--the long drop--KIND of slightly glowed, but it's the least impressive glow-in-the-dark effect I've ever seen, so don't buy it for that.

At this price point, a solid wooden (heirloom-quality) Quadrilla set, which doesn't require batteries, is endlessly reconfigurable, very creative and far more long-lasting, would be a much wiser investment.

product_title: Ever After High Cedar Wood Doll
review_headline: Perfect addition to my expanding EAH collection
review_body:
I Love Cedar! She has such lovely wood grain details and adorable clothes.

Her face makeup is perfect. Her eyes are brown and she is wearing a light silvery eyeshadow. Her lipstick is only in the center of her lips to represent a "puppet" like style. Her hair is brown and curly, the curls are lightly gelled. The front has lavender streaks that are braided around her hairline. She has a wood grain detail all over her body.

Her dress is primarily purple. It has a wood grain pattern on the bodice with cute little scalloped sleeves and collar. She has a pink suspender/lederhosen detail on the bodice. The bodice overlays over the skirt slightly. The skirt starts off the pink color on top and fades into black on the bottom. It has lavender and gold detailing.

She has socks that go up to her knees. They are sand colored with shiny gold "specks" throughout them. They have lavender across the top with lavender ribbons hanging off them. Her shoes are beautifully detailed. They look to be made out of sticks and leaves. They have pink straps that also have wood grain detailing.

For accessories she has a green grasshopper hair clip. Little gold "swirly" earrings that I think are supposed to represent the rings of a tree. A gold charm bracelet that has a donkey, whale, fairy, and leaves for charms. And a blue fairy ring. She also has a purse that opens up. It has wood detailing and a purple yarn looking strap.

She comes with a black key hairbrush and clear stand with a black base. Also her storybookmark. The box, like all the others, resembles a storybook.

My few complaints with my doll are: The socks are uneven.....and that's it.

She is a wonder addition to the Ever After High line. She is probably my favorite doll as far as detailing goes. I just love the texture of her arms and legs. And the nods to Pinocchio are just perfect.

Your little one can drive an ambulance, which is also the tote for all the gear. There are a bunch of "tools" your little one probably recognizes: a stethoscope, a thermometer, an otoscope (which they all know from all those ear infections. What a pity they didn't add a bottle of the "pink stuff.") and lastly, a syringe, which is useful for giving (not getting!) zillions of pretend shots.

My daughter had the Fisher-Price kit when she was small, and loved it. However, she saw this and agreed with me that it's nicer than the F-P version. The little ambulance makes all the difference. The little smiles on each piece make them all so cute, and the ambulance is much nicer than the plastic "purse" in the F-P set. A great gift for any kid from 18 mo to 4 years old!

product_title: ThunderCats Tygra 8" Collector Figure Classic
review_headline: Well constructed figure with minimal paint. Too big to fit in with other "classics"/collector figures.
review_body:
In short, I expected a "collector" grade figure, but this is more of a toy. If you go in with the right expectations, you'll be happier with what you get.

First off, I was disappointed by something that was entirely my own fault: I had assumed the ThunderCats Classic figures would fit in with my Masters of the Universe Classics figures. There's no reason they should, of course, being made by different companies, but it seemed so obvious that Bandai would play off the popularity of the MotUC line by making them the same size. But no, these are 8", while MotUC figures are 7" (as are DC Direct figures), and thus they tower over the He-Man figures.

As you may imagine, MotUC was my benchmark here. As far as articulation goes, they are comparable, possibly better, which is very nice. Sculpted detail is good, especially on the head. Elsewhere it's simpler, but that's appropriate for the character. Accessories are also well chosen. No outstanding surprises, but complete enough for the character.

Where this really falls down is in the area of paint. There are no washes or airbrushing to bring out the detail on the figure, which is disappointing, and makes it look very flat. The figure is entirely molded in two shades of blue plastic, so the head, neck, forearms, hands, and toes are completely covered in generally glossy, thick looking paint.

Worse than that, there is a notable color matching problem on the orange paint used. Most areas are a bright, vivid orange, but the collar area appears much duller, spoiling the illusion of the collar and neck flowing together. Also notable is the fact that the wrist joints are unpainted blue, which looks odd between the orange forearm and cream-colored hand.

One positive area to mention, however, is that on the fine details that are present, especially the face, are crisp and well applied, and generally look excellent.

product_title: Traxxas 1/10 Slash 4X4 Brushless Short Course Truck (Platinum Edition)
review_body:
Well, I finally caved in and got the vehicle everyone I know has but me....a Slash. I am a basher, but a race track has opened nearby, so I wanted a vehicle that could hit the track, but still hold up to bashing. I bought this platinum edition surprisingly because of price. At the time of my purchase, a Slash 4X4 RTR cost $550. I paid $400 for this Platinum Edition, and $80 for a standard Traxxas transmitter/receiver combo. I saved $70 and got a tougher truck right out of the box!

I haven't taken it to the track, but the common opinion is the Slash isn't great for serious racing, at least not without some serious modifications throughout. But for me, an occasional trip to the track for some laps, and bashing, this truck is awesome.

The truck is very stable, it doesn't flip over easy. And although some advanced RC enthusiasts will tell you a 2 wheel drive is more fun for bashing, I respectfully disagree. I drive my Slash through gravel, loose dirt, mud, and grass. When winter arrives, I will drive it in the snow. Having 4WD is very beneficial in that it has extra traction. Plus, having the front wheels powering also facilitates control in the air. Having all four wheels to control makes the truck respond much better than a 2WD in the air. While a 4X4 will cost more, both initially and for repairs, I simply feel that there is more fun to be had with a 4X4.

I won't discount 2WD vehicles altogether, I have a Rustler VXL, and I really like that truggy. But I digress, I am really liking this Slash. Figure out what you want to do, race, bash, or both. Think of the terrain you'll be driving through, and how much you're willing to pay (more for a 4X4, or a 2WD and mod it for racing, etc.) and pick your Slash. This truck isn't a master at anything, but it's a jack of all trades; It can handle bashing and racing.

product_title: Berg Buddy Pedal Go Kart
review_headline: Ongoing problems make this cart unacceptable
review_body: In general this is a very well made cart.  I purchased it for my 3 grand daughters, the largest of whom weighs 74 Lbs.  In the year since I purchased it 3 of the tires have failed.  The failures are not from wear of the tire, but rather from the tire popping off the plastic rim.  I have inflated them to the proper pressure.  Most of the failures have occurred when the cart was just sitting there not being used.    The store owners have been most helpful in contacting the manufacturer.  The manufacturer has sent me 3 replacement wheel assemblies, but all of the replacements have failed as well.  The last one wouldn't even hold air right out of the box!  It was never installed on the cart.    It's my opinion that there are 2 fundamental problems with these wheels.  The first is a problem with the plastic wheel which tends to have the flange where the tire mounts spread open in time.  This causes the tire bead to pop off the rim causing the tube to protrude and pop.  The second seems to be that the tubes are very thin and poorly made.  A heavier tube might not pop as easily.    This was a expensive toy to purchase, and it's sad that in general it is very well made, however because of the ongoing failures of the wheels the cart is useless.

product_title: The Settlers of Catan
review_headline: The Most Overrated and Pretentious Board Game... EVER!
review_body: The Settlers of Catan gets credit for jumpstarting the great board game revolution that's been happening in the United States these past few years. It is a German game translated into english, and features simple and easy to understand rules. But the game has one major problem.    I hate it!    I don't even take any pride when I say I hate it. If anything, I'd love to enjoy this game and have the experience many people talk about, but it's just not there. I'm confused why this game is such a big deal, but hopefully that will be answered before this review is done.    Settles of Catan is played on a board made of hexagon tiles which (as may people have said) are a bit of a choir fitting together. There is no player to player combat. You must win by building towns, cities and roads on the board until one player reaches ten victory points. To put it bluntly, there is very little variety to this game. At the start of your turn you must roll dice. If the dice match a number on a given space, then all players (not just yourself) get to collect the resources produced by that space. You will get a collection of sheep, wood, bricks and other materials. This brings me to my first complaint.    You can go as many as five, six or seven turns where players produce NOTHING! All resource production depends on die rolls, and it doesn't matter who rolls the dice either if every player produces resources at the same time. But of course, you can also trade resources, which takes me to my next complaint.    Trading is extremely BORING! It will be pretty much the extent of your player-to-player interaction. If there is a resource you desperately need it is frustrating if players won't come up with a fair agreement. Trading with the game itself is also unfair because the game will take two of your resources and give you one in return (and it's very specific what it would like to trade for). Of course, resources are important because those are necessary for building your settlements. Andagain, this takes me to my third complaint.    Building your settlements makes NO sense! For example, you need bricks, wood, grain and sheep to build a house. Bricks and wood make sense... but sheep? Why? And it goes without saying, this game has NO replay value. You can collect all the resources you want but there are only 3 things you can build with them. The only thing you can spend stone on is a city. Research and development is non-existant. Soldiers give you victory points if you have the largest army... but they don't do anything besides that.    In this game, developing a settlement is not about experiencing the frontier, creating a new life for people or even teaching you history. The game is about hurrying to get victory points. And getting victory points is hard because the mechanics are so poorly balanced and fellow players are not inclined to help you with trading because they themselves will put all their effort into getting ahead of you and not making mutual benefits.    This... this is a terrible board game. There was no effort put into the thought behind it. The strategy is not inventive and it is slooooooooooow! Just when you've built up a settlement and think you've got a strategy going, you'll probably be up to 10 victory points and then the game ends when you thought it was just getting started. Yes! It's that bad. I do not know why people put this game so high on the pedestal. I'm mean, I'm willing to listen, but I have never once found myself enjoying this game. Maybe it's a personal thing for many people, or maybe fans of this game just haven't realized there are far better board games out there. But either way I don't believe there's any way I will ever enjoy this game.

review_headline: Worth the money and time investment
review_body:
I can't stand Agricola (even though I admit it's one of the best games out there -- just not for me), but I love Caverna. Compared to Agricola, Caverna is much more fun, the scoring makes a lot more sense, there are more options, and most unlike Agricola, Caverna has multiple paths to victory. Did I mention that it's more fun than Agricola? It's more fun than Agricola.

The artwork is the same as Agricola (which is very good) and the component quality is excellent.

If you've never played Agricola, then this game is about equal to it in complexity, which is pretty high. It's not a first-time gamer's game. You may want to start with something like Stone Age if you've never played a heavy worker placement game. But there's a huge reward for putting the time into learning a game like this. If you visit the Board Game Geek web site (Google it, you'll find it) and search for Caverna, you can find all sorts of tutorials, videos, and people eager to help you learn the game.

It's an expensive game for sure, but well worth the money.

product_title: Pictopia-Family Trivia Game: Disney Edition
review_headline: Who's the leader of the club that's made for you and me?
review_body:
I love trivia, everything about it. I watch Jeopardy on TV and actually surprise myself how many questions I get right. On the other hand I am not much for board games; in fact this is the only one I own. Cutting to the chase - I love this game. It is rated as being for ages 7+ but this is no kid's game. Based on Disney trivia from their animated classics and blockbuster movies, theme parks and TV shows it will test the knowledge and experience of most adults.

The game offers an unusual twist to typical board games in that the players encounter guess-my-answer questions that reveal how much the players know about each other. We are already planning a Disney-themed backyard party of close friends in which each will dress as their favorite Disney character, prepare a Disney-inspired food dish and use this game as the focal point of our entertainment.

The product itself is first-class and worth the selling price. Packaged in an attractive Disney character box the game board, game pieces (of which there are many) and game cards are all substantial quality for many years of use.

If you like trivia and also happen to be a Disney fan this is a must-have game. Highly recommended and worthy of 5-stars.

product_title: Harrisville Designs Style B Easyweaver
review_body: I am a complete weaving newbie and I like the loom.  I got one secondhand and had a lot of fun with it last weekend.  It seems sturdy and is easy to use.  It came pre-warped, but I did not like the yarn that came with it so I cut that off and with a little YouTube guidance, warped it with some cotton yarn I had laying around. This will be a great way to whittle down my yarn stash. The strips of Velcro on the back and front beams were a big help in stringing the warp.  I put on a 6-foot-long warp without too much trouble and it didn't take much longer before I had woven several inches of real fabric!  The little latches which hold the tension are pretty rudimentary but seem to work, and while the 8-dent heddle which came with the loom is all right, I wish Harrisville made heddles with different dent sizes for this loom--a 10-dent would be very helpful. That is the primary reason I am taking a star off. (BTW, I asked them, and they don't make other heddles for it.  I may have to rig something up with a heddle from another manufacturer.)  If I decide to continue with weaving, I will eventually want to move up to a loom that is a little larger and has more bells and whistles, but this is a good starter loom.

product_title: PLAYMOBIL Private Jet
review_headline: Typical Playmobil perfection, a favorite toy in our house
review_body:
I'm starting to really love Playmobil toys. I remember playing with them when I was a child, here and there at a friend's house. Now that I have a six-year-old, I'm learning once again how great their toys are.

This private jet toy by Playmobil is a lot of fun. My daughter LOVES flying it and playing with the little people. It was very easy to put together. I think older children who also like Legos would love the assembling aspect to the Playmobil toys. Seeing as my kids are 3 and 6, they still need my help to get it done. But assembling this private jet is, literally, a snap.

It was a matter of snapping on the wings, the tail, the wheels, putting the handles on the briefcases, and snapping in the windows. I love the little clear windows on the plane. A lot of kids toys would just leave them open. It feels like a pretty realistic toy! My daughter loves taking it on trips around the house.

This set comes with three little people, a pilot and two passengers. The pilot's hat and the hair of Playmobil characters are often removable and can be switched from person to person. There are little coffee mugs so the business people can sip while they fly, and there are cup holders in the plane. Their breifcases also fit nicely. I do worry about losing such little pieces, but oh well. That happens.

The top of the plane is made to be easily removed by a child. So it stays in place for realistic looking flight, but comes off with little effort in order to play with the inside of the plane. It's a decent sized toy plane, and comes in a large box. We gifted it to my six-year-old for her birthday and she was immediately smitten with it. I also got her some other Playmobil sets, and I love how the sets can be played with together. All the Playmobil people have the same curve to their hands, so the private jet folks can visit the horse ranch and ride the Playmobil horses before asking the horse lady to carry the briefcases onto the plane for them. You know? The more Playmobil sets you own, the more versatile your child's play can become. It's fun!

I'd definitely recommend this toy for a child as a gift or a fun surprise. Children who have parents who travel for work might especially enjoy it. As for us, my children have not yet been on a plane--believe it or not!--so I think they were so excited to get to play with one at home. Great toy, typical Playmobil.r them. You know? product_title: Elenco  350 Piece Pre-formed Jumper Wire Kit
review_body:
I didn't buy these at Amazon but did purchase the same kit. I have breadboarded many circuits over the years using solid wire. Breadboarding, in itself, can be problematic due to mis-wiring and loose jumpers. Since it's difficult to strip both ends of a short jumper, homemade jumpers tend to be longer, get in the way, and can cause signal problems. For anything but a relatively simple circuit, use of homemade jumpers quickly looks like a forest! These jumpers are certainly good for initial breadboarding, but they are equally valuable when building a hard-copy of your design. There are several suppliers, including those on Amazon, who offer what's called a "proto board". This board has hole and bus patterns like a breadboard except that there are copper pads on the back. So, once you have a working breadboard design, it's easy to duplicate it on a proto board, soldering the same length jumper you used to breadboard. I find this a great time saver for one-of-a-kind designs. The only thing you have to be al little careful of is where one jumper crosses another at the stripped ends. You could have a short.

There is a little confusion in the description. There are 14 different lengths including a short, no insulation, jumper. The box has only 12 compartments so 2 of the lengths are shared with other lengths. I have found "refill" jumper kits, not Elenco branded, that contain about 140 jumpers for about $3. Interesting, the lengths and colors of the refill kit jumpers correspond with those in this kit.

As a hobbyist, I have found that the least pleasant aspect of electronics is building hardware. Using these jumpers during both the design
and build process is a time saver and reduces the chance of mis-wiring over the old "haywire" process.

product_title: Golem Arcana Base Game Set
review_body: Very interesting game and for those that always wanted to try miniatures games, but are unable to keep up with the vast amounts of rules, measuring, and time needed. There's a lot to talk about, so lets start with what this is:    Golem Arcana base set is essentially a 2 player (for now, app updates will change this) board game on a tileset you play by using an Android or iOS app to augment the experience. It is a not a requirement, but you would have to memorize the entire ruleset (can be found in app or online) and play it correctly. The entire point of the app is to tell you where/how you can move, how various curses and blessings affect the tiles, and what the combat results will be. To do this the game comes with a bluetooth stylus that allows you to tap on various objections to immediately get the screen to show things like attacks/tiles/golems/stats/etc. The entire package working together is very interesting and allows for jumping in and playing very quickly.    So whats in the box?  - 6 tiles each broken into a 3x3 grid with various art representing different types of cover  - 2 factions each with 3 golems and their associated cards (DOES NOT COME WITH RELIC CARDS, ONLY THE XPACK DOES)  - 2 dice in case you don't trust .random() on your tablet/phone and rather roll yourself  - The stylus itself  - 2 \\"Menu\\" and \\"Dice\\" cards to help control the app without ever touching the device    General Gameplay...  Much like most miniatures games, this is very much an army builder with a point system played against another person who built an army on a tileset to do something to score victory points. Not familiar with that? Points are the general strength of your army and are used to keep things fair between two players and should be comparable or meet the requirements of the scenario. The base game gives you two factions worth roughly 500 points or less if you play them with two people. The game gives game types for 500, 1000, 2000, and 3000 point armies. Note the lorehas two factions against each other and 2 mercenary factions that can be their own team or part of the other two factions. You cannot combine the factions in the box to make a single faction in the army builder. You must buy expansions that contain more units.    There is a wonderful tutorial that gets you started extremely quickly. Since the rules are in the app, there isn't much to read before actually playing the game. Once you learn how the stylus/components interact, you're well on your way to learning the more advanced rules. Each player on their turn has a set number of Action Points to use. This is affected by the army size at the 500, 1000, 2000, 3000 point levels. Each movement/skill uses AP and once you run out, you end your turn. You can use the same skills as many times as you want, but they come with a \\"cooldown\\" cost. As you use them they double in cost and the cost doesn't reset until the cooldown is set back to 0 and your cooldown is reduced by 1 at the start of your turn. You must choose carefully or you may not be able to use your skills on that golem the next turn.    Attacking/moving/skills are all handled using the app telling you which numbers you need to roll in order to hit correctly. All stats like health/dodge/armor and also handled for you to simplify having to remember everything using a million tokens. Victory points are obtained by doing what the scenario says your team needs to do to claim them.    Game Modes...  Tutorial missions, king of the hill, destroy certain units, and a lot more to come. There isn't a scenario builder, but they claim one is coming.    Army Building:  Each golem has a point cost, size, pilot (knight 1 or more), and relic card it can carry into battle. Each golem has different stats, each knight gives a passive/active bonus, and each relic provides a unique ability for that golem. All of these option cost varying points and depending on the final number you end up in one of the 4 point categories (You can alsoplay in the higher ranks with less points, but never the lower ranks). As mentioned before there are 2 main factions that are never on the same team and 2 mercenary factions that can make their own army or are part of the two main factions.    About the Stylus...  The stylus works by pairing it with a device, then tapping on cards/powers/tiles/the golems themselves to get stats and confirm what kind of movement/powers you want to do on the board. The game then immediately tells you if this is legal, your chances of hitting, and what effects are on the board in various places. Extremely handy.    I used the stylus on the latest (as of August I'm sure a new one is around the corner) Ipad Mini. I was able to connect it without any issues using the their signup process when you first open the app. The stylus had no issues connecting and registering all of my \\"taps\\". It is extremely important that you tap so that the camera end is parallel (flat with) the area you are scanning. Don't hold it like a pen, hold it more like a stamp. Very rarely did I see parts of the card or entire cards not work correctly. Currently the creature based Relics like Tree of Life and the Bone Totem both do not register for me after summoning. That is extremely aggravating.    The App..  This is where I knock off a star. While the wondrous part about this game is it is a living breathing entity where most of the game mechanics can be patched up in an app update, as it currently stands you can get into issues and nasty bugs occasionally. Tapping too fast leads you to sometimes wait for the app to catch up or get gets confused. Everything is represented very cleanly, and the entire game can be played using your miniatures/cards/tiles without every touching the devices. Very cool. This is a long review, but hey, every game needs at least one!    Compatibility...  I tried the app/stylus on an Ipad Mini (Retina latest), IPhone 5s, Nexus 5, and LG G3. First of all, playing on a small screen like theIphone sucks horribly. This game definitely needs a Tablet/Phablet (Like the G3/Note) to allow for playing correctly. As you're sharing screens between players, it helps to have something big enough for all to see.    The Iphone 5s had some issues keeping up with the artwork and slowed down slightly. The Nexus 5 had pairing issues and would lose connection mid game. G3/Ipad Mini had no major issues while playing and only the occasional stall or crash when clicking/tapping too fast. All in all, Android devices are all over the place and you need a rather current one with updated Android OS with stable bluetooth. I'm sure there will be many phones that will not like the app.    Overall...  This game takes a lot of rule fiddliness out of the general flow and adds in a new layer of interaction that worked well for me. The balance is good and the app can be updated to fix balance issues. This may make the writing on the cards obsolete in the future as the app is always right versus what is written on the cards themselves. I enjoy playing this game a lot and do not feel like this is a silly or poorly augmented tablet app. They play together nicely.    Some notes:  - This game and the expansions are very pricey, but the everything is pre-painted and fairly sturdy. I did find some pieces not glued right and had to fix them myself  - As of now there is no way to buy another stylus without buying another base game. You can connect two stylus so each player gets their own.  - The base game does not come with relic cards for the two factions. product_title: The Melancholy of Haruhi Suzumiya 2 Playing Cards
review_body: Sorry, not the best header; I considered 'Fun cards not to be played with', but couldn't break from my usual play (hah!) on 'The something of' of the book and anime series titles (see my other Haruhi product reviews), though I suppose the joke may be wearing a little thin...    Anyway, here we have a standard deck of playing cards emblazoned with gorgeous pictures of Haruhi, Mikuru, Yuki, et. al, 27 in all (the same set was used for spades & diamonds and hearts & clubs, and high school & middle school Haruhi appear on both jokers), while the backs feature Haruhi in her ubiquitous 'pointing' pose, with her infamous 'mysterique sign', the SOS Brigade logo.    Parental Warning (sorry, kids):   Some of the pics are slightly saucy, with the girls (only, sorry, yaoi fans) in bikinis, gym clothes (in Japan the girls' PE uniform is a T-shirt and brief 'bloomers', purely for ease of movement of course), disheveled jammies, and nekked under a rumpled bed sheet (the latter two cases in somewhat suggestive poses), and of course Haruhi and Mikuru appear in their trademark 'bunny' outfits (as in Playboy, not Easter); the magnificently moe Mikuru has a card of her own, featuring her in her bunny suit, nurse's uniform and Battle Waitress outfit (from Haruhi's arts festival film, The Adventures of Mikuru Asahina Episode 0, included on vol. 1 of the DVD release, well worth buying from Amazon, plugitty, plug, plug; seriously, for, like, 8 bucks you can get the Limited Edition with two character song CDs; for about $15 you can have the LE of vol. 3, which comes with a double-sided chara pencil board and SOS Brigade logo pillow case & iron-on, not to mention a bonus disc with eps. 6 - 10, subbed only, in original broadcast order, and full Japan presentation [the regular episodes have English credits and such] with the original previews--well, never mind; that's an issue too complex to cover here, and anyway, I'm s'posed to be reviewing the Haruhi cards, not pitching the anime DVDs).The beautifully repro'd illos are by Futoshi Nishiya, Shoko Ikeda, and other Haruhi anime production artists and designers.  All of them can be seen in much larger form, along with a slew more, in Udon Entertainment's English text versions of Haruhi Suzumiya Illustrations Spring & Summer and Autumn & Winter, available from you-know-who.    In conclusion (or is it?), this deck is a must-have for Haruhi fans, and would make a great gift for same (and the same for the illustration books of course, or pretty much anything with Haruhi and the gang on it, for that matter).      Dunno if something like this will ever be a valuable collector's item, but just in case, why not buy two, one for display, the other to play with, and what the heck, even if you're not a collector, you'll need two decks to play... that card game that requires two decks--canasta? never mind, I prefer spades or hearts--ahem!         And now, gang, I think I'll go check out the Spring & Summer book again--just for drawing references, mind (thinking of doing some manga-style web comics), so,    See you next review! (Figma's Tsuruya-san, I reckon; see 'Two heads are better than one'--bet that's got ya intrigued, huh.)

I have a color printer and have printed many things in the past. I've printed business cards and return address labels all with no problems. However while printing the stickers to personalize my game, I had problems. The first two rows would print evenly but the rows below printed 'off' and it got worse as the rows went down. By the last row, half of the picture was on the bottom portion of the sticker in the row above. I don't know if my printer is making the mishap happen or if it's something to do with the program on the mymonopoly website but it's something that made personalization not desirable.

review_body: As a guy with a 3 year old daughter i have bought many cheap plastic tiaras from disney. My daughter took it off after a few more minutes of wearing and the top part promptly snapped off. Dont waste your money on this one this is literally the same tiaras you can buy at oriental trading for party favors for $10.50 a dozen. the only difference is these have a small frozen sticker on them and cost $10 for 1 as opposed to $10 for 12. This is by far the lowest quality item ive ever gotten from the disney store.

product_title: My Little Pony Pinkie Pie Cutie Mark Light up Plush
review_headline: Perfect! Only problem for me was it says Pinkie Pie in the description and I received Rainbow Dash instead...
review_body: I bought this for my daughter as a Christmas present for this year. I saw it in Wal-Mart for $25, but there was only one on the shelf and I couldn't find it anywhere on Wal-Mart's website to order it, so when I found it here for a little less than Wal-Mart's price I jumped on it. My only problem is the description said Pinkie Pie and I received Rainbow Dash. Now, my daughter is only 2 1/2 so she doesn't really have a particular favorite at the moment. She just likes all the pretty ponies, lol. But, for an older child who does have a favorite this could be a little disheartening. Especially if it's bought as like a treat for good grades and they know what they're getting they might be a little disappointed to see they received a different pony than the one they had ordered. But because my daughter is so young and doesn't really care which pony she gets (and I really wasn't trying to order a particular one) I didn't see where it was a reason to give it any less than a 5-star rating. I felt like the price was appropriate, especially in today's market. Most people would probably try to charge $40+ for this, but I got it for $23 and some change plus free shipping. So it was perfect. I ordered it on the 10th, and I just received it today (and I got the free 5-8 day shipping so it arrived very quickly!) and it lit up and sang like it was supposed to. The box was torn in one spot, but that could happen at any store or even when you get the toy home from the store so it really wasn't a big deal. I'm very happy with my purchase and I'd buy it again. Just be wary if you're hoping to receive Pinkie Pie that that may not be the one you get.

Easy to install in your drain plug and routing the wires was/is a breeze....unless your bilge is buried.  mine is not and I just clip it on the trolling battery when i want to use it.  I actually didnt want to review it so no one else buys it and ruins the wow factor, but man this thing is super cool bling for you boat and the creator deserves to make money on it.  + side effect of the wires is you can not lose it in the drink....like i did to my orig plug which is how i found this on Amazon, searching for a new one.  Only downside would be if you remove your plug all the time.  Eventually I can see the wires getting twisted to point of failure and then your going to pop the fuse that comes with it if it shorts.  My fuse was actually DOA but I wont take a star off for that.
