product_title: DC Collectibles Designer Series 1 Batman by Greg Capullo Action Figure
review_headline: The best Batman figure yet! But there is a thing about quality control--
review_body:
When DC Collectibles first announced these figures, I knew I had to get them. Not only are they the first of the Nu52 figures to actually have the best articulation, but also the design and look of Greg Capullo's pencils? That was a sure fire sell!

I'd like to get out of the way saying that there is almost nothing that bothers me with the design and sculpt of the figures. They are actually the most visually amazing ones they've made. It is with the quailty of joints, swivels and hinges.

I've got a frozen ab crunch on my Batman-- his elbow joints are locked that they constantly click when I bend them (Which I stop in fear of them breaking). The feet swivels were actually loose on his left foot. The knee joints (Which are Double Jointed) gave me a bit of a problem at first, but they worked out well after a little while of displaying him.

My major problem comes from the plastic case the figure is held in. The hole for the cape is not nearly wide enough for you to pull it out-- so it may require a bit of tricky cutting, but you should be carefully pulling it out-- as the cape is actually connected near the head and in a square peg in his upper back.

The Bat-a-rangs are a bit of a trouble to fit in and might be easily lost if you drop them.

Over all, this is a good step in the collectibles department of DC Collectibles, I only hope as they advance on with this line-- they learn from this wave on how to package and control the quality of the figures.

product_title: Transformers Age of Extinction Stomp and Chomp Grimlock Figure
review_body:
This is a really impressive toy as far as the final transformations go.

It's awesome to see this giant transformer standing next to a tiny Optimus Prime when in robot form however there are a couple of downsides.

The first thing I noticed was that the transformation wasn't extremely smooth. This was a little inconvenient but for the price, it made sense.

The edges are also pretty pointy so obviously this is a toy for older more responsible kids.

Also, Optimus Prime has very little detail/has barely any moving parts.

Aside from that, this toy looks amazing and makes really cool sounds.

If you're looking for a toy that's fun to look at and slide around (big robots legs don't move too well), then you're not going to be let down.

I thought the arm mobility was decent which is great considering they hold that giant sword.

Long story short, any kid or even adult will love this toy if they look at the big picture and see it for the awesome gift it is.

review_headline: Great way to introduce money, money management and fun to kids!

I received the Pretend & Play Calculator Cash Register in exchange for my opinion. However, my views remain my own and are 100% honest.

We have owned a couple of other pretend cash registers since the girls were smaller, but they always had a cartoonish quality that did not engage the girls, nor did it have the realistic money to help them learn. The Pretend & Play Calculator Cash Register is realistic in style and even includes a working, solar powered calculator so that children can begin interacting with a calculator! The money included is all real-size currency that children can easily identify and learn with. I love that they even have the presidents on them so that we can take our learning to the next level with talking about who is on the bill or coin!

The Pretend & Play Calculator Cash Register is a fun and exciting way for children to work on math skills, recognition and basic money handling. Our girls have set up a shop in the kitchen and each morning “ring up” our breakfasts as though we were in a cafeteria. Some days my prices are more comedic than anything – but I love the combination of imagination play with learning and skill building.

product_title: Himoto Centro 1:18 Scale Rtr 4Wd Electric Power Truggy W/2.4G Remote
review_headline: Runs ok while the battery last.
review_body:
Here is the good part...its actually pretty fast for this size. About 20mph right out of the box. Controller is not bad. A little big so if this is for a child, the controller will be too big for them. Overall very fun car.

Here is the bad....Battery pack only last 15- 20 min max. 6+ hours to charge. The tires are nice and grip well but wore out to almost bald within the first week of use. The shocks are nice and tight but they seem to get stuck a lot. You have to compress than decompress them several times to loosen up. There is an odd jitter when the battery gets low. It will move than stop, move than stop...over and over. I found out that if that starts to happen, adjust the trim a bit and ease into the throttle. This stops it from happening. The car is a lot smaller than I though it would be. Its ok though, I was looking for a small RC but did not expect it to be this small.

Overall, its fun to drive for the few minutes the battery last. Takes a long time to charge. Tires are a joke (even though they grip well). Would I buy this one again....probably not.

product_title: BOOMco. Whipblast Blaster
review_headline: The Whipblast Blaster isn't just for kids!
review_body:
This is a way cool toy that’s not for kids only. Big kids like them too and I’m pleased that no windows will be shot out in the process. Not long ago we replaced a couple of windows that fell victim to a BB gun years ago. The Whipblast is way cool and does have a lot of power, but because the darts are hollow and lightweight, no windows will be blown out in the process.

Eye gear is cool and should be used in battle. There are shields on either side of the Whipblast that can either be used to deflect or capture an opponent’s darts. There is a holding capacity for four darts in the end of the gun, but it’s not like a magazine. Only one can be primed and shot off at once while the other three are stored.

The priming is a process that almost looks like something the Rifleman would do. The gun whips around, primes and then can be shot. Most definitely could use some extra darts because a handful will never do. I consider them to be almost like a bonus that comes with the gun.

I thought it would be a cheapo given the price point because some toy guns I’ve got are much more expensive. This is a toy that kids from eight to eighty will love. It’s cool, it’s fun, well-made and designed, and won’t blow out a window.

product_title: Goodman Games 5070 Dungeon Crawl Classics Rpg Hc
review_body:
Subject: Adventure as 1974 intended you to.

Goodman, you had me at \\"funnel\\", but this blurb really did it for me:

Remember the good old days, when adventures were underground, NPCs were there to be killed, and the finale of every dungeon was the dragon on the 20th level? Those days are back. Dungeon Crawl Classics don't waste your time with long-winded speeches, weird campaign settings, or NPCs who aren't meant to be killed.

---

Some of the reasons I love DCC:
- Races are classes. This speaks a lot to the idea of recapturing the nostalgia of discovering RPGs for the first time. I've been listening to a lot of Podcasts and it seems folks have not been able to articulate why this is so cool. I think it boils down to the magic of discovering Dwarves, Halflings, and Elves for the first time. As an example - pretend you're a kid and you start playing a game where you're a Fairy Godmother. You don't automatically think of separating Fairy Godmothers into jobs like paper-pusher or wand-maker. And just so with non-humans. You're either a Fairy Godmother or you're not dammit. And that's magic.

(If you're looking for a mechanical answer it's probably this: it works because the race-based classes are so awesome that you're happy you got it. And it's not over-powered because of why everything in DCC is cool - our friend, Random.)

- Creating character backgrounds from whole cloth has become a habit, enjoyable to some but not by me. The funnel allows players to create character backgrounds on the fly as part of playing!

- OSR-ish but with its own sensibilities.

- Magic is magical once again, because of our buddy, Random.

product_title: Clash of Wills Shiloh 1862 Board Game
review_headline: Great sequel, but consider the original first
review_body:
Clash of Wills Shiloh is a sequel of sorts to Mayfair's other Civil War battlefield game \\"Test of Fire: Bull Run\\". It uses essentially the same game mechanics as the first game, while adding a few new features. New rules or changes to the old rules are very helpfully marked out in green in the rulebook, so it is very easy for players who have played Bull Run to adjust to the new game. In terms of complexity, the game is not too terribly complex and experienced board gamers should have no problem picking it up and playing fairly quickly even if they are new to the series.

The game mechanics are simple, but I found them very elegant. A game turn consists of rolling dice which determine what actions a player may take: Drawing cards, firing their artillery or moving units. The actual battle system is very interesting, with the defender firing first and then the attacker. In this way, it can sometimes be very difficult to dislodge an enemy from their position, especially if the defender is on a hill. However, this tends to give the game a very authentic feel, as maneuvering a massive army through the crowded forests around Pittsburgh Landing can be a pain. Armies are not instantly wiped out, but instead companies are first depleted being eliminated.

For those who have played Test of Fire: Bull Run, the most significant additions are cavalry tokens, which are more maneuverable than infantry but possess less firepower and veteran infantry, who fight better and are easier to move around on the battlefield.

The artwork of the game board and pieces, while not overly impressive, is very nicely done. The two-sided tiles used on the board feel just right in terms of representing your army, and the art on the cards also fits the tone of the game very well.

All in all, Clash of Wills is an excellent game, but I would recommend anyone who does not own Test of Fire to buy that one first. Not only is it a little easier to grasp,but I found it to be a slightly superior game due to its replay value. Clash of Wills attempts to portray the surprise attack on the Union Army through its setup of the first turn, and in this regard it succeeds. However, in attempting to make the game recreate history so accurately, it hinders the player's strategies to the point that you end up using the same tactics each game. Its still very fun, but I've found that I play Test of Fire more often because it is a little more open-ended in terms of how you can approach the battle.

product_title: Barbie Life in The Dreamhouse Pet Boutique and Doll Playset
review_headline: A fun pet set that my girls like, though my black daughter is disappointed that this set only includes a white Barbie
review_body:
Let me start by saying that all the little pieces to these Barbie sets still drive me nuts, but the new design in our three latest Barbie sets in which many of the small pieces snap to the set itself = GENIUS. It helps little hands, like those of my two 7-year-old daughters, play without having to pick up perpetually knocked over pieces, and it helps most of them (though not all, because some still don't snap in) avoid getting lost. But still? This set has 20+ pieces, many teeny tiny, so yes, it still drives me a little bonkers.

Now to this set specifically...
My girls love the pets and potential to dress them up and the toys accompanying them. They are into Littlest Pet Shop and My Little Pony and real-life animals too, so this is perfectly crafted to our girls' interests. The set includes:
- a frame for the shop/boutique itself with a pop up awning
- a two tiered display for the boutique, with spots for little accessories to snap in
- a counter with a faux display (via a sticker already on it, showing pet food, snacks, brushes, collars, shampoo, and toys for sale) that flips up to provide a pet bath area
- a beige cat with a pink dress/cape
- a brown puppy - some sort of toy breed - with a purple bow on its head and pink clothes
- a white toy poodle with a purple and blue snap on outfit
- a purple food dish
- a blue bone
- a box of dog treats (that's actually a plastic rectangular prism with a sticker on it, so not a real open-able box)
- a bunch of small accessories, including a play mirror, pet brush that slides on Barbie's hand and another brush that slides on in a different way, a trophy for pet shows, a pair of fake scissors for grooming, a circular toy, a bear toy, and a couple other items that aren't really clear as to what they are
- one Barbie wearing a dress that has a pink skirt portion attached to a white bodice with black polka dots and pink, yellow, and orange flowers
- an orange checkout that looks like an iPad checkout with a side swipe, and a matching orange hand scanner for the register

One pet peeve: In all three of the Malibu Ave. playsets, the box show two Barbies, while the set includes the typical blond haired, blue eyed, pale skinned Barbie we all know. Meanwhile, in the box, the paper backdrop shows a darker skinned friend.

In. ALL. Three. Sets.

C'mon, now. Can't at least one of the three sets include a Barbie with a little more melanin? I know the traditional Barbie is the one in each set, but times have changed. Diversity matters. Unfortunately, Mattel hasn't yet gotten that memo.ange checkout that looks like an iPad checkout with a side swipe, and a matching orange hand scanner for the register

product_title: SOS Titanic (Kartenspiel)
review_body:
Excellent game that can be played solitaire or cooperatively. The main mechanic of the game is based on the card game Klondike (aka. patience or solitaire). Players try to line up cards numerically in order to move them onto the lifeboats (ie. the aces in Klondike) and save the passengers. There are lots of decisions to make that add to the tension of the game. All of this is done as you turn the pages of a book showing a side view of the Titanic gradually sinking (you turn the pages as you run through the deck of cards). Very thematic and good game. The components are top-notch. The cards are very well made with a heavy linen texture and the artwork is great.

One issue when buying the game...check which edition you are buying. The game is not language dependent to play, but the rules may not be in English. This also is not a major problem because the publisher of the game has downloadable, full color rules in multiple languages on their website (http://www.ludonaute.fr/?page_id=2761&lang=en).

product_title: Hubsan X4 H107C with HD 2MP Camera 2.4G 4CH 6 Axis Gyro RC Quadcopter, Mode 2 RTF
review_headline: Review for Hubson 107C HD 2MP, and for the seller, The Little One's Choice
review_body:
I have to say this drone is simply brilliant!! The video quality is amazing for such a small package, and the tight, precise control over this drone is far beyond my expectations. Be sure to get a crash pack (great value for the props, the rest of the stuff is icing on the cake!) as you'll lose some props. At the time of this writing, prop packs (5 sets) are about $16, and a crash pack (4 prop sets, 2 motors, 2 LEDs, spare battery, replacement body) is about $20, so grab a crash pack, you'll be replacing a few props as you learn :)

Also, I have a short story about the seller here, and some of the other sellers here, who are all selling this item.

My first 107C I purchased here on Amazon a few weeks ago, randomly chose The Little One's Choice! as I placed it into the cart. It was fulfilled by Amazon and I'm Prime. Received it and LOVED it! Unfortunately, like Icarus, I flew too high while taking a video, the wind caught it, blew it out of range, and it landed somewhere in a densely wooded and very private neighborhood. Gone. :(

Ordered a replacement, and it randomly chose Bullzeye Precision as the seller, also fulfilled by Amazon. Received it, and while everything looked the same physically, it wasn't the same. The drone flew very erratically, and I was unable to get a good trim on it. Even worse was the video. Even though it did 720P resolution, it was clearly different than the one I received from The Little One's Choice!. The video was granier, jumpier, and even saved into a different directory structure and file naming convention than the first one I had.

I then compared the video output from the first one to the second one using a program called GSpot. The one from the Bullzeye purchase had frame errors and other errors, lots of avi overhead, etc, while the video from the "lost" drone showed as perfect, no errors, appropriate fps and avi overhead.

It was clear that the drone from Bullzeye was different at the camera level, and there was something amiss about the controls being so off and jerky as well. I'm not going to make any assertions, and simply will point out that I returned it for a refund, and purchased another one from The Little One's Choice!.

I received that one today and indeed it is just like the one I lost. The video is in the same format, the video is crisp and clear, it saves in the same folder structure/file naming convention as the first one that's now lost. GSpot shows the video is perfect and 30 fps.

Hope my review helped some of you, going to order another from TLOC for my son before you all scarf 'em up! :)

product_title: BOOMco. Twisted Spinner Blaster
review_body:
BOOMco. Twisted Spinner Blaster

Tough packaging to get the blaster out but it was worth the hassle.
This blaster comes with a target and shields that the darts stick to. The shields pop out around the side’s just press the button and they pop out, cool!
The darts are excellent at sticking to the target. The darts only stick to the shield and target so they won’t stick to glass or walls. I’m not sure this is a good thing or a bad thing. It’s a powerful blaster providing speed and distance.
I found two flaws, but two flaws I could work with. The first being this blaster is difficult to aim accurately. The trick to firing with accuracy is to pull the trigger slowly.
The second flaw is that the drum the darts are in can sometimes spin too far or not far enough and miss the air chamber that enables the dart to be ejected, so occasionally it will misfire. This problem is easily fixed, all you have to slightly turn the drum into place. If you are in a “battle”, this will put you at a disadvantage.
Overall this is a really fun blaster and while on a shopping venture we bought more darts. I noticed different gun and attachment for sale. My kids are all for buying those. So this is a hit for my kids- 11 and up!

product_title: Kagerou Project Mekakucity Actors Enomoto Takane Ene Cosplay Wig Blue Hair
review_body:
This is an excellent wig.

Shipping: Less than two weeks after the order date. 5/5.

Density: The main wig is medium; no netting shows through at all, but I’ve still had thicker bases, so that was slightly disappointing. The twintails are very, very thick, and thus a bit heavy. But I suppose having a thin base makes it easier for the butterfly clips to grab onto your real hair underneath. The fibers are very soft and silky, and it barely sheds. The cap of the wig may be small on those with larger heads, but it fits me fine. 4/5.

Color: Matches the picture in most lighting, but in some of my own pictures I’ve taken with it, it’s ranged from baby blue to dark blue. I don’t think this is a problem, as Ene’s hair also varies between the PVs and the anime. All of the fibers are the same hue. 5/5.

Style: Matches the picture. The twintails are pre-styled, but you’ll need to cut the bangs and put some hairspray in the main wig. The twintails tangle easily with wind or extended wearing, but a brush smooths them out easily. The twintails also clip in securely. 5/5.

(My head is small, my hair is of medium thickness and waist-length. I’ve used both a wig cap and simply pinning my hair up, and both have worked well.)

product_title: BRIO: Harvester
review_body:
This is a nicely detailed combine harvester. The reel is made from a fluted, wooden dowel, and it rotates as the combine moves along which is a nice touch. In addition to that, the arms that hold it also pivot so that it stays in contact with the ground even over uneven surfaces, which is an even nicer touch. It's really well thought out. The whole thing looks sharp, and it just works. Lots of play value here.

The undercarriage and reel are wood. The main body and the cutter arms are molded plastic. There's a magnet on the back.

My only real complaint with it is that it uses a lot of plastic, which seems to be the trend with BRIO these days. I'd not get too worked up about it, but the harvester also has this ugly flash mark in the center of its back, where the plastic piece was separated from the mold. This is really tacky and not at all typical of BRIO's normally high standards. They couldn't put the attachment point somewhere that's not visible in the final product? Come on, people. Think it through.

review_body:
The figure is an excellent likeness of Sean Bean and very well made, The only problem with the figure is that the sword blade is separately made and it will take a little time to make it fit properly. Why? Well, the prototype figure and the blade were undoubtedly made of the same material. The production blade is made of hard plastic and the figure and its clothing of softer materials. As they cooled after being made, the blade shrank less than the figure. It will fit eventually, but you will need to cut parts of the \\"tang\\" off until it fits nicely between Ned's hands and the \\"ground\\" of the base (no need for an Exacto knofe, use a nail clipper). On your first try to install it, you will find it does not fit and the blade will bow.

The figure is excellent and worth the time required to make the blade fit.

product_title: Barbie Sisters Life in The Dreamhouse Camper (Discontinued by manufacturer)
review_headline: Dreamhouse Camper Is My Children's Favorite Toy
review_body:
When I received this item, to say my 3 children were excited is an understatement. While I had never seen this Barbie set before, the kids seemed to know exactly what it was and were very excited.

I began assembly and putting stickers on the unit. From beginning to end, to assemble the camper and put all the stickers on took 46 minutes. I found assembly fairly easy, but a bit tedious. A few pieces took me a little time to figure out exactly where they went, but assembly went smoothly overall.

Being that I do not particularly care to play with Barbies, I turned the camper over to my three children to evaluate.

10 year old: The only complaints they had was that the chandelier came apart on them once, though they were able to reassemble it. They also mentioned it was difficult to store the dishes and snap them in place. They loved the fact there were a lot of beds and the camper came with food. They specifically mentioned how they liked the lemonade dispenser and how it looks like it drains. They gave the camper 4.5 stars

8 year old: They informed me that they really liked the fact there were lots of beds, but thought there should be 4 beds instead of 3 as there are 4 Barbie sisters. They thought it would be nice if the bathroom was a bit bigger and wished the camper set included a doll. They liked how the food and such snapped into place so it would not move. They loved how everything folds up and can be stored in the camper, but indicated that it can be hard to arrange everything so it all fits. They gave the camper 4.5 stars.

6 year old: They loved the set overall, but wondered why there was only 1 blanket for 3 beds. They brought up an interesting point that when the camper is folded up, there is no floor or bottom. They told me that sometimes when the camper is closed up, sometimes things will fall out the bottom while they are playing with it (I did not notice this at first, but there definitely are gaps in the bottom). They gave the camper 5 stars.

Again, while I did not play much with the unit, I will say that my initial impression of the Dreamhouse Camper was quite positive. I thought the unit was well designed and constructed very well. The only thing that I did not do it for me was the detachable cab. The kids like it, but it seems to be a strange aspect of the design to me. I noticed that even after having the Dreamhouse Camper for several weeks, the kids are still playing with it on a daily basis and is one of their favorite toys. I give the camper 5 stars.

Overall, I think this is a great toy and one my kids love! With as much fun as my 3 children have had with this toy, I feel that the Dreamhouse Camper is well worth the current price of $90. Averaging my family's ratings together, I get a mean rating of 4.75 stars which I will happily round up to 5 stars!ely are gaps in the bottom). They gave the camper 5 stars.

review_headline: ... used very many sock poi in the past (maybe like 3 or 4 pairs) but I think these have ...

Under blacklight I would say on a scale of 1 to 5 for brightness they are probably a 1 whereas neon poi are more like a 5. This is okay for me personally because I tend to prefer not to be the brightest spinner at a party or club where blacklights are involved. More focus can be placed on finding flow and less on who is watching.

One annoyance I noticed after a few days of spinning was that they are slightly ripping at the seam on one side. I'm spinning with tennis balls 75% filled with rice (not that heavy). product_title: Sparkfun Redbot Arduino Compatible Programmable Robot Kit
review_headline: Kits are Incomplete - lacking in hardware
review_body:
I recently purchased one of the RedBot Kits, the following lists what was to be included and the quantity I received.

1x RedBot Mainboard 1 - recieved
1x Magician Chassis 1 - set (upper and lower)
1x Accelerometer RedBot Sensor 1 - received
3x Line Follower RedBot Sensor 3 - received
10x F/F 6" Jumper Wire 10 - received
4x Sticky Tab 4 - received
2x 4-40 ¼" Phillips Screw (10 Pack) 2 (10 pack) - received
4x 4-40 1-¼" Flat Head Screw 4 - received
4x 4-40 Hex Nut 4 - received
3x 4-40 1-½" Aluminum Hex Standoff 3 - received
4x 4-40 3/8" Metal Standoff 4 - received
6x 4-40 1" Metal Standoff 6 - received

So everything is fine, or is it? Absolutely not!
Now for the instructions for installation of the Line Followers (which is part of this kit).
There is no hardware to do the installation. As per their assembly instructions we are to use the following parts, which
by the way are shown in their on-line store description of the kit.

3x 4-40 1" Phillips Screw
3x 4-40 ¼" Phillips Screw
6x 4-40 Nylon Standoffs

Without these parts the line followers (which they advertise as part of the kit) can not be added.

Now, on to the battery holder. None of these parts were included, which are need as per their instructions to
attach holder to the chassis piece.

2x M3*10 Flathead Screw
2x M3 Nuts

Again these are shown in their on-line catalog ad for the kit.

This is extremely disappointing to me because I had heard only good comments about SparkFun, apparently
these comments were incorrect.

product_title: Little Tikes Rocky Mountain River Race Inflatable Slide Bouncer
review_body:
We upgraded to the double slide with mountain climbing wall – the Rocky Mountain River Race - three years ago.

The Rocky Mountain River Race can handle my family's 4 kids (my kids and my sister’s) for weekly use – they are between the ages of 3 and 8. And I can easily see it handling the entertainment of a small birthday party – 7 to 8 kids.

What I love about the Rocky Mountain River Race is that it has the two slides, so more kids can zoom down at a time. Plus the mountain climbing wall, with footholds and straps, can handle two kids climbing at a time. Then there is a sizable wading pool on the bottom for the kids to slide into and splash. There is also a bucket over the mountain climbing wall that can fill with water and splash kids as they climb up. It works best with some assistance, my niece found out. She waits up top, filling it with water to dump on her brother.

The Rocky Mountain River Race works like this. First you unfold it on a flat surface. Do not put it on cement, have it on grass or the soft dirt. Remove stones and twigs. A tarp will help keep it even safer. The material is not like a cheap playpool. The material is thick, heavy and tarp like – but you don’t want to take a chance that it will tear OR that your kids will get hurt if they fall on a stone under the slide. You want to make sure you are near a hose and an electrical outlet. There will be water pouring continuously out of this inflatable, so pay attention to the location of the electrical cord and the placement of the air motor. We keep the air blower on a container, off the ground. You attach the air motor to the inflatable and tie up the extra air release tube. You will also need to attach the sprinklers to the top of the inflatable. Turn on the hose and you’re ready for play. This inflatable is so huge that it does take around 3 minutes to fill.

The inflatable is taller than my husband. The Rocky River Mountain River Race is 8 feet and 9 inches high! It’s length is and it is 13′ 7″ wide. If you go to the store, the image you see on the box is accurate and not blown out of proportion, which I notice competitors do. Or you can just view the pictures I’ve taken to get an idea of how it looks and works!

Putting it away is the hardest part. All inflatables are challenging to put away, but we always manage to do it. You need it to dry before putting it away. We leave it out in the sun right side up and upside down trying to get all the wet patches. Then we fold it, decompress it to get the air out and roll as tight as possible. Once it’s folded and rolled, we start pushing it back into it’s carrying case. The last time we did this (which is challenging) we still managed to have enough room to put the blower in too! Sometimes we just leave the blower out, though. We used to put the tube in the carrying case too, but I find it gets kinked like that. So now we just leave it out and next to the carrying case. Remember, this is a heavy inflatable, but I can carry it …. it is just over 60 pounds. But really, it’s worth the carrying and folding! I just love it so much and so do the kids.

If you have any questions about the Rocky Mountain River Race or Slam ‘n Curve Slide, just let me know! I’d be happy to help! You can see it in action here: http://youtu.be/mcb_93L_ook

product_title: Fisher-Price Nickelodeon Dora and Friends Cafe
review_headline: DORA DOUBLES THE FUN WITH CAFE' & CHARMS
review_body:
This Dora And Friends Cafe' set will not only bring lots of playability to your child, but with the darling charms and charm bracelet, you'll find your child fast becoming a charm collector. The Dora And Friends Cafe' is called the Arco Iris Cafe' and has everything on it's 2 floors Dora and her friends will need to have lots of fun with good eats, dining, lights, music and dancing.

The Cafe' has a front door and windows upon entering where you can see a drink area where you can choose which fruit you want for your drink, then mix it in the spinning blender, there is also a shelf of pastries, pies, cakes and treats to view. You will also see a take out window next to a refrigerator full of fruit, drinks and goodies.

Once you pick your food, you can climb the stairway to the upstairs. Here you will find a table and chairs for dining in and a very colorful stage with music and lights for dancing. The stage is decorated with palm trees on each side of a colorful holographic rainbow. The charms light up in a lovely light pattern to the music. Only Dora comes with this set, along with 3 charms- a guitar, microphone and flower.

There is also a charm bracelet for the child, as well as a cupcake, drink and bananas for Dora. Also included are a food tray, cake cover and register. You will hear Dora speaking using both English and Spanish words as the lights flash with music and singing as well. One thing you will have to buy extra with this darling set are the other Fisher Price Dora And Friends figures with Explorer Charms. They cost $7.99 each here on Amazon and you will find Alana comes with sports and animal charms, Kate comes with art and dance charms, Naiya comes with Science and astronomy charms and more.

The Dora & Friends Cafe' is 5 Star fun when you add more friends and charms. It will fast become a favorite with your child, as when the Cafe fun is done for the day, you'll see the charm bracelet being worn always. product_title: K'nex Titanfall - Atlas Titan Building Set
review_headline: Good model - not to be played with.
review_body:
First off you're probably wondering how this guy can review this set when it isn't in stock yet. Well, I purchased the set though another big name retailer, who had it in stock in their online store. I received it today and I was excited to build it and review it immediately.
When I first heard of Titanfall K'nex I look around where I could get it as soon as possible. I'm a huge Titanfall fan (G10 Prestige), and I'm also a huge building block fan. While Lego would have been my preference, I have worked with K'nex before with K'nex Mario Cart race track sets. For those of you who haven't worked with K'nex before they are more like the Bionicle and Hero Factory Lego than the traditional Lego building sets. In addition, working with K'nex is a bit harder, because you have to put a little pressure to snap the pieces in place, so I do not recommend it for younger kids.

The set looks neat once it is built, but there are many flaws that make it difficult for me to rate it high. While I knew how K'nex snapped in place, while a little difficult at times, it snaps on very sturdy. There were other parts of the build that I really didn't like. If you take a look at the picture, there are flaps on the side of the thighs. The clamps are very thin and short that it doesn't attach properly. Every time I would move the legs those things would pop off. In addition, the jet pack on the back is only secured by one connector and it isn't that tight so the jet pack also pops off frequently. Next the male socket part of the shoulder is twisted on to connect to the body. However, the ball connected to the arm is so tight when you move the arm the socket connector comes out, instead of the ball joint moving. As a result the whole arm comes off.
With these flaws I'm sure anyone playing with this would get frustrated. While it will be a good display piece, I can't recommend it for play.

Now this doesn't affect my rating, because K'nex isn't the only one who does this, but I am frustrated that manufactures chose to have stickers for their models instead of printing it directly on the piece. There are some pieces that have been painted, so I don't see why they can't print on the images. From my experience, stickers eventually harden and crack, even when it is not being played with.s this, but I am frustrated that manufactures chose to have stickers for their models instead of printing it directly on the piece. There are some pieces that have been painted, so I don't see why they can't print on the images. From my experience, stickers eventually harden and crack, even when it is not being played with.

product_title: Marvel Dice Masters: Avengers VS X-Men Dice Building Game by Wiz Kids
review_headline: Great potential for customization...lots of fun.
review_body:
Having spent an evening playing this with a friend, I am very intrigued by this game. Without getting into the rules here (you can find them elsewhere), I have to say that the level of customization gives this game awesome potential. It's pretty much like Quarriors, but with several important changes which give it great depth. First players have to decide not only which heroes to utilize, but which "flavor" of hero to play, as well as the max number of dice they will be allowed to use in total. Open ended rules allow for adjustment to HPs each player has to vary length of game. Tweaking each of the attributes can allow for significant differences in the games played.

Additionally, the artwork is great on the cards and the dice are of improved quality over that of Quarriors. The dice bags are actually just paper envelopes, which was a little surprising.

All in all, at a $15 price point this game is a no brainer buy.

review_headline: The extras make the camera worthless.
review_body:
We bought this for my twin boys when they were 2.5. The camera is super sturdy, and both boys enjoyed holding it up to their faces and saying "cheese". For about ten seconds. Every now and then, we pull it out again, and they enjoy it for another ten seconds. The problem with this camera is that it's more than a camera. Putting games, photo editing capabilities, etc on the camera might make it seem like it's worth more, but it doesn't. Who wants to play simple, silly games on a camera when you can play any awesome game you want on Mommy's iphone? A kids camera should be JUST a camera. Make it easy to take and review the pics taken. That's it. I regret this purchase.

product_title: Banpresto Sheryl Nome Coscro2 Macross 30th Anniversary SQ 8" Action Figure
review_headline: Lovely fashion aesthetic and quality - slightly disappointing face
review_body:
I collect anime figures as a pretty serious hobby and I'm particularly fond of prize figures like this one and have several in my collection - I own 10+ Banpresto figures as well for quality comparison.
This Sheryl is a bit heavy and arrives in a windowless box and requires a little bit of assembly but it's very simple to piece the parts together. I was very impressed with the quality and weight of the plastic as well as the paint job of her legs, stockings, shoes, and dress. The shoes are very lovely with small roses on the back. The legs are thick and attractive, supporting the top-heavy figure. Her panties are average, there may be a few scuffs or paint transfer there.
The dress however is absolutely gorgeous. It is not a gothic lolita dress but the dress clearly is heavily inspired by it which attracted me to the figure in the first place. The ruffles are detailed in the skirt and the weight feels evenly distributed. Sleeves are nicely done and the same rigid plastic as the dress. Her hands are not the most detailed but they are attractive. On my figure, she doesn't quite hold her dress exactly - but for just being a prize figure that's a normal quality-hiccup and nothing to worry about and it's not very obvious. The bow on the back waist of the dress is a rich dark purple and the only piece I suspect will/can cause paint transfer - especially to the hair. It may also be the only tricky piece in assembly due to the angle - I recommend removing her head from the body, placing on the bow, and then putting the head back on.

Her hair is quite a lovely color with a mix of a warm blonde and rich pink undertones. She also has a white hair ribbon on the back of her head. You may find her head strange to look at because of how huge the back of her hair goes back to make a strong anchor point for the hair and bow - displaying her facing forward makes this less noticeable. The headdress is cute and detailed with a black base, white ruffles, and small purple bows on the side.

Now the reason I only gave this figure 4/5 stars...her face is very weird. I'm not honestly a fan of the character or show (or the show's artstyle) and just got the figure for the fashion aesthetic, so maybe there is a little bias present. But the face is very oval in shape and round instead of wider and a bit more square like most anime figures have. The lips are alright, painted in an orchid-ish color like a lipgloss. The eye decals are the biggest offender looking rather lackluster and not as beautiful as Sheryl's eyes can look in other art work - and they don't hold even a match light to the eyes of any of my other Banpresto prizes.

Finally, her base. It is a base of white plastic with an attractive decal of...I believe the ship from the show in silver? It's attractive either way. There is a single support stand that seems to prop up just under a portion of her skirt. I did have a little trouble getting her onto the base due to how the support pegs were designed. Just be careful and maybe prop it on your knee while getting her feet down so the pegs don't drop out of the base.

I would recommend this figure if you could get her under $25, and she is mostly very lovely. I recommend looking up pictures of her on MyFigureCollection to get a better look at her face before you purchase her - just so you know what you're in for if you're particular about that sort of thing!

product_title: Bandai Hobby #15 RG Gundam Exia Model Kit (1/144 Scale)
review_body:
This is relatively simple as far as RG's go, looking quite similar to the HG exia. The obvious advantages over the RG exia have to be the chrome plated weapons and the blue ribbons. They're nice extra details which add a little flair to this exia.

However, what it lacks in complications it makes up for in simplicity. Unlike most RGs this thing is pretty solid. The only issue is, like usual with Exia models, the weak connection between the GN blades and the hips. It's "okay" but it doesn't stay on too well. The shield doesn't stay on very well either, but it's quite nimble and easy to get on compared to some of the other RG models.

Also, if you're worried about the chrome parts looking ugly, take a deep breath. One of the nubs is hidden completely, and the other is on the edge of the blade. If you're very careful, it only leaves a small line of dull gray, about a millimeter long, on each of the chrome parts. It's not noticeable at all unless you know exactly where it is and are within arms reach to it. This advice applies to all 3 of the blades.

product_title: Marvel Select Ghost Rider Action Figure
review_body:
Lets face it, what you want to know is can it be posed, right? What good is 1000 points of articulation if 99.9% of poses exposes the joints and makes it look just plain silly, right? Some characters look worse than stick figures no matter what you do. So let me set your mind at ease; this sculpt is so detailed and superbly painted, it is easy to pick a creepy or action pose and have it look natural, or as natural as a supernatural action Figure monster can look. Crouching, standing, full front or twisted torso with outstretched hand, it all looks good; not an easy task for the majority of figures out there.
Not perfect, mind you. Curiously, they chose to include the Belt and buckle with the torso rather than the lower part so that no matter where his crotch faces, these point in the same direction as his chest. considering everything else, this is easily overlooked. I'm happy with it.

product_title: Captain America Marvel Legends Soldiers of A.I.M. Action Figure Baron Von Zemo, 6 Inches
review_body:
The Captain America Series Marvel Legends Baron Zemo figure is a nice update to the previous figure released a while back. In accordance to the comic books, this is actually the first Baron's (The one Captain America originally fought in WWII) son.

He has a ball-jointed neck and can move it up and down, shoulder joints, bicep swivel, double-jointed elbows, swivel and ball jointed wrists (gloves hinder movement slightly), ab crunch joint, swivel waist, ball-jointed hips, swivel thighs, double-jointed kneecaps, swivel calf muscles, and ball jointed ankles.

As far as accessories go, he has his trusty Luger with a leopard decor on the handle, and a longsword. The sword has a hole on his belt that it can slide into but it is a very tight and awkward fit. He also comes with the right arm of the Mandroid BAF from this wave.

Overall, a fantastic figure for tons of adventures against Bucky and Captain America or along side The Red Skull, Armin Zola, or the Winter Soldier!

product_title: LEGO City Coast Guard Patrol 60014 (Discontinued by manufacturer)
review_headline: Fun set, better for kids than adult collectors
review_body:
Not the best set for adult collectors, though my kids did like it for all the animals included within -- a dog, a crab and THREE sharks! The build for the Coast Guard boat is okay. It's designed to be a bathtub toy, so the base of the boat (the entire white area from the deck on down) is just one gigantic plastic piece. The lettering and graphics you see are stickers as opposed to being printed on, and I can't imagine they'll last long after being played with in water.

The set does have a lot of play value, again making it better suited for kids than adult Lego fans. The submersible robot and helicopter are both sturdy builds and fit well on the boat (which transports them). The lighthouse is grossly, hilariously out of scale, but I won't complain about a blue plate getting tossed into this set. The minifigs are pretty standard, though I like the radio headset the one Coast Guard minifig wears.

Oh, and I should just mention one more time -- SHARKS!

product_title: Edushape Marbulous Marble Run - 82 Pieces plus Bonus of 50 Marbles -  Total of 132 Pieces
review_headline: Use your imagination to build bigger and better courses
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:mo1970EC27BBXDG]]Marbulous is a lot of fun for both kids and their parents. I don't mind saying that, since my wife and I had a great time building some of the marble courses shown in the user guide, plus designing a few of our own. The number and variety of pieces just begs for a kid's imagination and inventiveness to be let loose to design bigger and more creative courses.

The user guide shows five sample courses ranging from 35-102 pieces. Each sample course also shows a detailed breakdown of which pieces are used and how many of them. Each piece has an identifying code, which makes me think that the manufacturer may one day sell individual pieces like Lego does. That would be great for kids who design their own courses and can determine what pieces they need.

The \\"T129\\" pieces are used as bases. These bases are about 3\\"x2\\", so it helps to stagger them as much as you can to make the course as stable as possible. Even so, I recommend building courses on a hard surface like a tabletop instead of a carpet, where a course would be more prone to overturn if it gets bumped. But the pieces fit together tightly enough that if a course does overturn, there's usually little or no repair needed.

Note 1: The product description says the recommended age for Marbulous is age 4 and up. The user guide has a choking hazard warning for children under 3 years old. In any case, the set does contain marbles and other small parts that could be a choking hazard.
Note 2: The product description indicates that the set contains 101 pieces. The box that the set is packaged in shows 102 pieces.

A product sample was provided for review purposes.

product_title: Dragon-i Toys Wild West Gunslinger
review_headline: Great for children young and old.
review_body:
We saw this type of play set first at a neighborhood gathering. It had gathered up all of the little kids and they were having a great time.

With a birthday coming up we went searching and found this here on Amazon.

It is great fun and it gets play with a ton.

How it works:
- There are little spring loaded posts in the top of the "log". These are pushed down and lock into place.
- A "target" is then placed on top of this post.
- You turn on the gun and point it relatively accurately, and when the trigger it pulled it makes a stylized gun firing sound.
- If you are "on target" the spring loaded pin is released and the bottle or can that is the target gets flung into the air.
- There are claps and cheers and shouts of I did it that then ring thru the house.

The good:
- Kids of all ages love it.
- Even the littlest ones can push down the spring loaded target resting points. Yet when they go off things are flung nicely.
- It has worked very reliably with no problems, issues or failures.
- You can you use other targets. Many things can be set on top of the spring loaded pins and will get flung into the air.
- It works from a pretty good distance. So we have different distances setup for kids of different ages.
- The batteries seem to last for a very long time. We haven't had to replace any of them yet.

The bad:
- After the littlest one pulls the trigger the millionth time while just wandering around the house that sound gets to be a bit annoying. :)
- The base for the targets is a little narrow. The hard plastic targets are a little challenging for the little ones to balance on it. I recall when we first got it thinking that the one we had seen was wider and that they balanced more easily. We addressed this by looking for other things to act as a target. For the younger set we have taken to using carpet sample squares that we got from HD. These balance easily and pinwheel thru the air when the target goes off. You can also put the plastic targets included on the squares and they balance a bit easier. Lots of fun has been had trying different targets.

The bottom line: it is a fun little toy that everyone seems to enjoy playing with.

product_title: Fun Express Superhero Gliders (2 Dozen)
review_body:
I agree with all who found assembling the gliders puzzling, so I'd like to share a few tips that I found helpful.
(Try to gently press the parts together and not force them into place to avoid bending the glider).

1. Poke out the 4 slats - 2 in the body, one in the tail, one in the cape. A table knife works well.
2. Slide the plastic "nose" on the fist.
3. Slide the cross tail into the back section, matching colors.
4. Wiggle-Slide the cape through the middle - the space between the 2 slats is slit open to accommodate the cape.
This is the trickiest part - make sure the slit in the back fits the slat of the cape from an aerial view. The top of the cape
is 2-toned, the underside is the solid color with text.
5. Be sure to assemble a few gliders BEFORE the party so you can help others.

Go have fun!

product_title: Anki DRIVE Starter Kit (Previous Version)
review_headline: Melding generations of gaming for some good fun
review_body:
This is not your Dad's slot racer or your kid's video game - it's a melding of generations of gaming into a very fun hybrid. Yes, it's expensive and yes, there are still some kinks to be worked out - but it sure is a good time. Like slot racing, you don't have to worry too much about steering control of the cars - just tilt to choose your inside/outside lane position and the car does all the driving for you. Like modern gaming, there are upgrades, achievements and objectives beyond the lapping wins.

The implementation is good and I hope subsequent software iterations will continue to improve performance. We have cars that seem to lose their minds sometimes and head the wrong direction, and cars that go zooming off the track (problematic when playing on a table). Given the high-tech nature of the cars, I remain concerned about these flying leaps, but so far it hasn't been a problem. I would imagine this has something to do with the relatively basic, ABS-heavy styling.

FYI, the system is based on Bluetooth-LE (low energy), which is why older iOS devices won't work, regardless of their processors. Overall, it's a great time. The cost of melding generations of gaming is not low.

She will get very very pricey in the future. My guess is she will hit about 450, which is as much as the rare mass effect liara goes for now. Give it about a year, maybe less. Get her now at a normal price, you will be glad you did, she is worth every penny and will grace your shelf beautifully!!

product_title: DC SUPERHERO FIG COLL MAG #101 MON-EL - Eaglemoss
review_headline: Display model missing packaging passed off as "new"
review_body:
The picture of this product was incorrect, but the description and item matched what I had wanted, however it was not what I ordered since the item was supposed to to be new.

I contacted the seller because the item I received had been opened and was missing the plastic/poly bag that these types of figures are sold in (I've bought them before). In some areas, it is illegal to sell this type of item without the overall packaging because the figure is made of lead (although I guess this would be sort of appropriate for a Mon-el figure) and it is required to be sealed and have a lead warning on the packaging - which this item did not have. The seller stated that it was new, but then told me it had been a display model. Display models have been handled and are not new, and a good test of this is that I could not resell this item for full price without the packaging and the lead warning intact. If a company is going to sell a display model, then they should be honest about it and not try to pass it off as "new." Also, I happened to know it is made of lead - suppose this had been sent to a child where the family did not know about the lead content and the packaging and warning label were missing ?

The company offered me a refund, but I would be required to pay for all shipping charges, which means I won't be returning it. I am very displeased with the company.

product_title: Magic the Gathering Conspiracy Booster Box
review_headline: Wonderful fun for multi-player drafts and Commander/EDH
review_body:
Drafting Conspiracy proved to be the most fun I've had drafting--ever! [And, for the record, I was not the winner.] The cards will be welcome additions to my Commander decks, and have provided for some fun and entertaining kitchen-table matches with family and friends.

This set is intended primarily to support multi-player draft events, where players then participate in three-, four-, or five-player matches (often called "pods"). It's secondary purpose is to provide cards that are beneficial in multi-player formats (e.g., "free for all" matches).

For those not familiar with drafts, each player starts with three booster packs. All players open one pack, select a card, and then pass the pack to another player (first pack to the left, second to the right, and the third to the left). Players keep picking one card and passing until all cards are gone. [You can search for detailed draft rules online.]

Conspiracy includes many cards reprinted from many sets, as well as new cards specifically created for draft and multi-player formats. The draft-specific cards include many that introduce actions during the draft, like the ability to take a second card from a pack or the ability to look at a different pack. The mult-player focused cards themselves have two types: traditional cards (creatures, instants, etc.) with abilities that impact other players (or the whole board), and a special class of cards (with the "Conspiracy" card type) that affect the game but cannot be removed from the game (they reside in the Command Zone). Conspiracy cards convey a benefit to their controller--perhaps a creature enters the battlefield with Haste, or a specific spell costs one colorless mana less, or you might even have a Conspiracy card that allows you to be the starting player!

Note that cards with the Conspiracy card type are not legal (at this time) in sanctioned formats like Standard and Modern. They are intended for Conspiracy drafts, but you may use them with "house rules" and kitchen table (informal) games, though all players should agree to their use before starting a game. Other cards first published with this set are similarly restricted. [Visit the Wizards of the Coast Gatherer website if you have questions on the legality of any specific card.]

***** RECOMMENDATION *****
---------------------------------------------
IF YOU LOVE PLAYING MAGIC IN A MULTI-PLAYER FORMAT, I STRONGLY RECOMMEND PICKING UP A BOX.

PICKING UP A BOX IS ALSO A GREAT WAY TO HOST YOUR OWN DRAFT WITH YOUR FAMILY AND FRIENDS.

Some final notes for collectors:
---------------------------------------
The boxes I've seen opened thus far have held a significant amount of value (based on current prices at the time of this review). Brainstorm is available as a foil in this set. The new Planeswalker carries a premium price. There are many value cards, including Exploration, Stifle, and Misdirection. Each box I've seen opened has netted value well above the purchase price. I also used a grey sharpie on the whites of the eyes to make them look more sunken in and realistic. Use the same brown sharpie for the gums/ teeth. You can Also use an exacto knife to seprate the teeth to make it look REALLY realistic. If you use some black acrylic paint and and dry brush it on his claws, hands, feet and parts of the body, you end up with a top notch looking figurine that would easily sell for much much more. I am sure most 2-year olds will be able to reach the pedals, but my LO is quite petite for her age (she weighs 21 lbs and is just now fitting into 18 month clothing - not sure how tall she is, probably 30-31 in). I love that the Radio Flyer allows her to enjoy the trike without me breaking my back to push her.

product_title: Sluban F117 Stealth Bomber 209 Pieces Building Blocks
review_body:
First, this is a decently sized plane when done. Don't let the 209 pieces fool you, it's bigger than many Lego brand planes I've built.

The overall quality of the plastic bricks is pretty good. If Lego is a perfect 10 these are an easy 7, maybe 8.

There were two small mistakes in the instructions. I believe step 7 there is a piece that is "greyed out" like it is something you should placed in an earlier step- but it isn't supposed to be grey- you place the piece in this step. Also there is a place where a line that should go over the graphics is printed behind them so you can't see where it is supposed to point.

Other than that no real problems. The wheels are cheaper then Lego brand wheels. Hard plastic, not rubber, and the axles the wheels snap into are a bit thin and week, but they held for me.

The larger pieces had a dirty film on them- hard to explain- but the kind of thing I made sure to wash my hands thoroughly after putting the set together. Probably good practice in general but nothing I ever felt I needed to do after finishing with real Lego pieces.

I still very much enjoyed the build and will be happy to put this next to real Lego sets I already have.

product_title: Fate : System Toolkit
review_headline: Neat ideas and a great overview for magic using the Fate system
review_body: Fate Core (which is absolutely necessary for this product, introduced a refined RPG system that focuses on story above all else. Your characters are tough and are nearly-unkillable but the can be maimed to the point of uselessness and it might be time to make a new character while your old one retires to a background character or a source of quests for revenge due to their injuries. Fate allowed players and the GM to create worlds and scenarios together leading to a great overall understanding of the universe everyone was playing in and the broad and simple rules made it a snap to learn. The big rub was that SOME things NEEDED depth, how magic works, how cybernetic enhancements would change characters, and the negative aspect of using too much of these things with one character. While Fate Core touched on how to balance stuff like this, the Fate System Toolkit refines it and offers much easier source material to fine craft the universe you and your players game in. Not only a good GM tool, the System Toolkit is best shared with players to get a good idea on how to handle the game more fluidly.

But, it really does handle quite nicely once you trim it out properly.  Very attractive in the air, pretty aerobatic, can be flown in relatively confined areas once you get it dialed in.  I fly it on our cul-de-sac when the wind is calm.  It's a cheap foam air-frame to be sure but it can take a bit of abuse,  guerilla glue and packing tape can keep it flying a long time.  And when the airframe is no longer worth repairing, then the fun really begins, because you've still got the famous ParkZone "brick", the compact receiver/servo/electric motor controller with which you can convert just about anything into an RC model.  An amazing value for $100.

product_title: Transformers Prime Cyberverse Command Your World Commander Class Series 2 Ironhide Figure
review_body:
As an avid collector of Transformers and a father who buys Transformer toys for my two children ages 5 and 8, I would highly recommend staying away from all "Cyberverse" Transformer toys. They are small, not well constructed, and the paint job stinks. It is easy to purchase them because they are priced cheaper and I do not feel Amazon or any other online retailer does a good job articulating the actual size of these toys. For example, this one says "5.5 x 8 inches." If you broke the limbs off of the toy and lined them up you might get five inches, but in real life this toy is a "mini." Think the same size as the original G1 minibots from the 1980s.

Parents, the Cyberverse toys easily break when your kids play with them and the little weapons get lost easy. I highly recommend the Transformer "Prime" series which are much larger, better made, and can easily be found on Amazon for a few dollars more. They are superior toys, your kids will be happy, and they are modeled directly off the Prime animated series.

Collectors, the only reason to purchase the Cyberverse line is if you need some miniature figures to arrange around your "Titans." I've seen a few collectors arrange these mini versions around their Omega Supreme or Metroplex to make them look bigger. This is a cool visual, but be forewarned that the Cyberverse toys have sketchy paint and design. I would skip them in general.

product_title: Educational Insights 10-Pack Smencils
review_body:
I love these pencils. I am a music teacher, and I use pencils nearly all day; why not make it fun?

This pack of pencils comes in a vinyl zip-tube for easy storage, and each pencil comes in its own labeled, biodegradable corn plastic tube for "scent isolation". I try to keep these pencils in their tubes when I am not using them, and will rotate them out from time to time. They have kept their scent extremely well for me.

The pencils themselves are made out of recycled paper and lead. I love that the paper used still has printing on it; when you sharpen the pencil you can see that these are old newspaper. The lead works very well, it is a solid piece of lead, not that cheap glue-y lead that some pencils have. The erasers are also functional and hold up for a long time.

If you are looking for a way to make writing for yourself (or a young family member) fun, these would be the way to go. With fun scents like root beer, orange, and grape, who wouldn't enjoy writing more?

The product is described as responsive by Yomega and has "silicone sticker return system", but buried in the description is the phrase "the Maverick requires a bind to bring the yo yo back to hand", i.e., the very definition of an unresponsive yo yo.

So is it responsive or unresponsive? I've watched video reviews showing it as a responsive yo yo. Many reviews here state that it is responsive. But some customers are complaining that it "sleeps forever" no matter what they do. I purchased one of these for my daughter and it has been very frustrating as it appears out of the box the one we bought is absolutely, entirely unresponsive.

Based on their marketing material and almost complete lack of support options (seriously, check out their website), I get the impression that Yomega doesn't have a clue what they are selling and doesn't really care one way or the other. Even at $20 I expect better quality control than this.

review_body: Series six rotten egg trashies are amazing!! They come hidden inside purple plastic eggs that pull apart at the side into two pieces. There are ancient eggs-hibits which include dino poop, boggy bonfire, and scum scorcher (also a fire character). There are scrambled animals including the very cool battered bat, puking primate, rotten tooth tiger, and soft boiled sloth to name a few. One of my favorite kinds of trashies in this series are the puke eggs. These are a clear chartreuse egg shaped outer shell with a tiny solid trashy trapped inside. These characters include a poached spider, baked bug, and waste wasp and many more. There is hard boiled trash which feature a speckled, granite like finish. There is eggs-cavated trash which look like fossilized critters stuck in a broken open rock. Some of the characters include sewer slither (a snake), soiled shrimp, oozy octopus, and runny roach. product_title: Traxxas LaTrax Rally 4WD Rally Car, 1/18 Scale, Assorted Colors
review_body:
The car is very cool, no doubt. I bought 2 of these so my kids can race them, but my 5 year old doesn't drive hers a lot. But, I have a 9 year old who runs the car a considerable amount and the differential gears were skipping within 3 days. I took it apart and put ball bearings in it and it seems to work better. The nylon bushings that come with the car just aren't sufficient and soon they will allow a lot of 'slop' in the mechanisms. The wheels bushings were worn, and pretty much worn out within 24 hours. The thing is, when you have a powerful R/C car, you really need to have metal internals. I imagine this car will be fun for a long time, but I will be fixing and upgrading it...alot.
There are plenty of parts and kits online and at my local shop to upgrade this car into a useable R/C car that will last and be fun, but it's not going to last out of the box.
Remember that you get what you pay for, so anything in this price range is going to be sketchy and basically the same.
My son has been into R/C cars for quite some time and knows how to drive it, does not crash it into things, etc. There is no misuse going on here.
Traxxas needs to pull this product, do a quick redesign on the gears and bushings and then it will be worth the money. Until then, pass on this one, unless you know what you're getting.

product_title: Nerf N-Strike Elite: Stryfe Blaster, Colors may Vary
review_body:
This blaster is an excellent toy for children. Very simple to use and lots of fun. Unlike a few other Nerf Guns that I have owned, this one never got jammed up. The blaster includes tactical rails above and below the barrel as well as the option to add a stock (sold separately). This blaster includes the same six round clip that most other Nerf brand blasters use, but can be used with the larger size clip or the drum clip. Rate of fire on this is as fast as you can press the trigger. There are three safety interlocks on the blaster between the batteries and the motors, so if you don't have all of them depressed, then the motors won't spin up and you can't fire (closing the jam door is one, inserting a clip is two, and the small button below the trigger is the third). Note that you must hold down the button below the trigger when you want to fire, this will send power to the motors and allow you to pull the trigger. Blaster needs four AA batteries that are not included.

I personally purchased two of these to turn into automated turrets powered by Arduinos. I used them atop a robot for a collegiate competition where we needed to fire nerf darts at a target. The blasters are quite consistent and very simple to wire up and fire.

I like these and would certainly recommend these for kids of all ages.

product_title: 100 Coin Safe Square Coin Tubes for 40 NICKELS
review_body:
I've tried the clear plastic round tubes and now these. I prefer these Square tubes over the round

Clear Plastic Round Tubes
The clear plastic are nice in that you can see through them but that niceness is limited by you can only see the bottom coin and the edges of the rest but because they are round they easily roll off the table. The clearances are a bit tight and sometimes the coin gets stuck in the tube especially if there is any damage to the edge of the coin.

Coin Safe Square Coin Tubes
These coin storage tubes will not roll around, arrange easily next to each other. The clearances is such that supposedly you can put a whole coin roll in them. That is perfect for storing my uncirculated coins from the US Mint in their original US Mint rolls. This coin store while not necessarily completely airtight, has a lid seal that appears it would keep most of the air out. The only con I can think of is when all of these tubes are in the box they came in loaded with coins, it's hard to get one of them out. Since they are square, no room to get your fingers in to pull one out.

product_title: Play-Doh Sweet Shoppe Cake Mountain Playset
review_headline: Nice quality, lots of options - could have better storage
review_body:
We babysit a few times each month, and the house looks more and more like a day care center. We like to have something new or different each time she's over. Since she's now into Play-Doh, this was the perfect "next thing."

There's minimal assembly. Just snap on the top and snap in the cake mold base. The cake itself has three main pieces - the top with the mold, the middle with the lever, and the bottom. The bottom can also be used separately and has spots to put the "candles" and has more press-in shaped areas.

Typical Play-Doh dual use - the lever for the cake is also the top half of a mold - the bottom half is beneath that. Put in the Play-Doh, stick in a candle (they double as handles), press down - Play-Doh lollipop!

You get three different cake molds that snap into the top (to swap these molds, press the top button and pull the mold out - almost no effort!) Also included are (is?) a roller, plastic fork and knife, two "plates", an "icing" syringe, and Pal-Doh Plus. It's a version of Play-Doh that takes less effort to press out and mold.

So why 4 stars? Well, the base is hollow. It's an ideal place to store all the pieces - but there's no way to do so. The molds, plates, etc. have no storage or places to put them. I can see them getting lost quickly. The middle section has spots to hold the other pieces knife, fork and some candles. The base has spots for the roller and syringe to stand up - but they fall off if you look at them funny.

product_title: Armory Spray Primer (Black)
review_body:
Tried this on a mixed batch of plastic and metal minis from Reaper. And I almost ruined them all using this inferior product. I don't usually leave one star reviews, but this primer is simply unusable.

I thought, maybe you didn't shake the can enough. So while I scrubbed the awful, thick, textured sludge off of my test batch of minis ( I used mineral spirits and a soft brush) I decided to try again.

Test batch number two, three full minutes of shaking the can. Seventy degrees outside, no wind, spraying into the same box I used for a hundred minis before.

One pass left the exact same sludgy detail spoiling sticky mess that my first test did.

One last time, on a mix of plastic and metal junk figures. One more time, despite following the directions, and shaking it even longer...it did the same thing.

I should also mention that this product eats glue. In addition to being as thick and chunky as a can of Dinty Moore, it made several figures fall apart and caused the glue on the bases to break down.

Maybe there are bad batches of this product. I dunno. I can tell you that my experience was exactly the same as the other one star review. Avoid this product. It may be a third the price of the other brands, but it is 0% useful.

product_title: Dragon Models M103A1 Heavy Tank (1/35 Scale)
review_headline: Inaccurate, deceptive packaging and engineering errors.
review_body:
The problems with this kit have been very thoroughly documented elsewhere on the net. The kit does not come with a mantlet cover as depicted on the box cover. I bought this thing before I read those reviews, and had I done otherwise, I would have saved myself 80 bucks. Here's what I wrote on another forum:

I simply decided to correct what I think are the simplest things to correct: the issues with the bustle. You really need to address this even if you're building it out of the box because built stock, *there is no way for the bustle to clear the exhaust shroud.* This means that the turret will never be able to rotate a full 360 degrees.

Please refer to Pawel "Vodnik" Krupowicz's site because I didn't think to take pictures during this process. I trust your imagination is sufficient enough to visualize what I'm describing.

You'll note that the middle of the bustle does clear the shroud, but the sides of the bustle don't. use the middle of the bustle as a guide, break out your Dremel and start progressively shaving the sides of the underside of the bustle down until it looks flat. Start testing its clearance against the shroud (everything loosely tacked in place with white glue). I found that coating the top curve of the shroud in graphite and attempting to rotate the bustle over it tells me where all of the contact spots are. The re-shaping and carving on the underside of the turret should also address (to some extent) that annoying kink in the "line" the underside of the bustle makes where it meets the turret ring. You can see what I'm talking about on Vodnik's page. God how I wish I had seen that before I shelled out 80 bucks for this kit, but Caveat Emptor. But I digress...

Once you've flattened out the underside of the bustle, fit the exhaust pipes into the shroud and then snip off the bottom part of the exhaust pipes that contact the hull, and trim the sides of the shroud to be flush with that. With all of that in mind, the shroud and bustle SHOULD have enough clearance to rotate freely.

While you've got your Dremel out, chop off half of that bulge underneath the turret. Fair over the hole with Bondo and plastic sheet and you're done with that part. I didn't fret too much about things being perfectly shaped, because no matter what meatball surgery I did back there:

1. It's on the underside of the bustle and it's hard to see
2. The rest of the kit is so hilariously bad that I reasoned that anything I did must be an improvement.

Oh, there's another issue that you need to be watching for: THE BARREL ON MY KIT IS WARPED. There's a noticeable BEND in the barrel, like a parenthesis. Maybe your kit is better, but I blanch at the thought of hacking up a barrel to lengthen it and correct a curve. I'm fixing the barrel and mantlet in place with white glue and waiting for a turned barrel, if anyone ever bothers to release one for this kit.

Eh, if you look at it like a caricature of a M103A1, it ain't so bad. There's just obvious quality control issues that need some power tools to overcome. Think of it as an expensive test mule for practicing your Dremel techniques.

product_title: Minecraft 3" Figure Hangers Blind Pack, Series 1
review_headline: Cute blind bag toys perfect for any Minecraft fan.
review_body:
I used to do the blind box thing when I collected Dunny and Vinylmation figures, and now my daughter's getting into the craze with the new Minecraft hangers. These are basically key chains or bag clips with a Minecraft figure attached. If you aren't familiar with blind bag/box figures, it's a toy that comes in a box or package, but you can't see what you're getting. It's a surprise every time you buy one, and even if you bought 4 or 5, there's a chance you could end up with the same figure in each one. It may seem dumb, but if you have friends that collect them too, you can use extras to trade for ones you want. And before you get any ideas, these are packaged in a way that you can't just feel around and know who's inside.

My daughter ended up getting her favorite character- the Creeper, and he looks great. It's basically a smaller version of the Creeper figure that came out not too long ago. He stands at a little under 3 inches tall from head to toe, and has a matching green clip. His little feet and head can be moved around too, just like the bigger toy. One thing I'll mention is that you should pay attention to the clip before pressing around to open it. The clip is on the thin side and could easily break if you were to press it in the wrong direction. Otherwise, there's not much to worry about with the figure, aside from the fact that the head can be popped off, but attaches again easily.

Kids will love to put these on their backpacks or keys, and there's always fun in wondering who you're going to get next. Just keep an eye out for chase figures like the red sheep! As others have already mentioned, you can get these for a little cheaper at the big red bullseye store. If you have a birthday party with a couple of little Minecraft fans, these would make great party favors.
