product_title: Transformers Age of Extinction Generations Deluxe Class Autobot Drift Figure
review_headline: A Small Wonder ~ These aren't your childhood Transformers!
review_body:
I pride myself as being a kid who grew up on the original Transformers in the 80's. I had a many of the original toys and I even taped the movie when it aired ~ Optimus Prime's death really upset me, and I got really upset again several years later when someone taped over it...

Fast forwarding to today...this particular Autobot, Drift, plays a role in the upcoming Transformers Age of Extinction film. (If you pay attention to the official trailer, you can see a fuzzy outline of Drift in his Bugatti form!) As a member of the \\"Deluxe Class\\", this figurine is one of the smaller ones, but it's still movie-accurate and requires several steps to transform. The larger classes include \\"Voyager\\", \\"Leader\\", \\"Supreme\\", and others. There are other Transformer toys including non-transforming and One-Step models, but at least to me, anything below the \\"Deluxe Class\\" isn't really a proper Transformer. Unlike it's previous films, Hasbro seems to be focusing more on younger audiences this time around, and unfortunately, it appears to be producing fewer Deluxe class and above models.

Compared to the Transformers of old, these new-generation incarnations are much more detailed and have many points of articulation. More impressively, they look surprisingly good in either Robot or Vehicle mode, though with each shoulder, hip, elbow, and knee graced with a ratcheted swivel hinge joint, the transformation can get quite involved. In what I believe to be a triumph of computer-aided design, if you are so inclined, you can even coax poor Drift into something resembling a Tree pose. The biggest weakness in terms of articulation are the ankles ~ they're a simple hinge with only forwards and backwards movement and they're turned slightly inwards. As a result, you won't be able to pose Drift in many difference stances, though I think this is only a minor gripe in terms of playability.

Overall, I liked this toy quite a bit. I brought it to work and it now resides on top of my desktop with swords in hand. My coworkers generally had a good time trying to transform it between Robot and Car modes ~ though it should be noted even seasoned engineers needed a few iterations to master it. I think the build quality and materials are pretty good and I believe the toy can stand up to mindful play, though due to the complexity of transformation, I would not recommend this for younger kids. Older kids (including ones from 80's) should have a blast.

Notes:
1) The swords can store on Drift's chest in Car Mode but there is no storage for the daggers.
2) The rear wheel didn't roll particularly well which does negatively affect perception and playability.
3) From the back, Drift somewhat resembles a Ninja Turtle...n top of my desktop with swords in hand. product_title: Transformers Age of Extinction Generations Voyager Class Galvatron Figure
review_headline: I'm really surprised by this figure, heavy duty plastic, loads of articulation, figure has some heft to it, backpack forgivable
review_body:
I'm a long time Transformer collector. This new simplified line for Age of Extinction has to be taken with a grain of salt. Yes these are toys designed for kids, but there are still a lot of kids at heart out there. I wanted to really dislike this figure. I purchased from hasbrotoyshop.com at $24.99 as he is not available on Amazon yet. I came home today to find the figure waiting for me. I could tell when I picked up the box from the front porch that he was heavier than I expected.

Paint Apps- paint is lacking all around on this figure...a cardinal sin I usually don't overlook, the paint on the figure is of good quality and has been placed well

Articulation- This figure has 360 degree arm rotation, ankle 360 degree/pivot, ball jointed head that looks up/down/left/right, no wrist swivel, there is a 90 degree arm curl thanks to transformation, the collapsed backpack doesn't hinder movement at all, there is no waist articulation, I was able to get the figure in several solid fighting poses with thanks to the ankle swivel and foot pivot joints, the hips have a nice range of motion as well as the knee bend...it is hard to see either in stock photo

Truck Mode- the mode is very good and the figure looks good posing next to Evasion Mode Optimus Prime in truck mode, noticeable robot legs in truck bed but it still works

Play factor- I think the kids will have fun with this one and enjoy the ease of transformation at 17 steps

From a collector standpoint I'm happy with the figure for what it is. Thankfully this figure did not get the chrome treatment like many others. I do wish there had been a more silvery gray type of paint scheme and more paint on the figure as a whole. I also do not like the lack of weapon storage and the overall weapon appearance as a whole. The figure will sit proudly on my AOE movie shelf in robot mode for now, but he looks really good in either mode.

review_body:
My wife and I are both big fans of Settlers of Catan, and we wanted to try to help our boys (ages 5 and 7) get the idea so that they can play with us in a few years. After playing our first game, we found:

* Although the trading concepts and what things cost was a bit of a hard concept initially, even our 5 year old got it by the end.
* With the way the starting points are done, people have a very balanced chance.

So we all had tea and the demons eventually abated after playing a few games and deeming it "not tasteful". Those demons are really sensitive...

Anyway, it's a fantastic game. And me and the boys still play it. Their mother went missing in the woods about a week ago but she'll be back soon.. Or not.

product_title: Fisher-Price Little People Tow 'n Pull Tractor
review_headline: This is a really dumb and annoying toy!
review_body: My Dad is a dairy farmer, so I thought this would be a great toy for my grandson.  Boy, was I wrong!  As soon as the tractor is pushed, the Old McDonald's Farm immediately starts playing, very loudly, and doesn't stop until it's finished.  What's more, the instant the tractor is moved, the song starts all over again.  The music is incessant and totally annoying!  The animal sounds are attached to the posts in the wagon, so if the child puts the chicken on the lower post, the chicken will moo, or the cow on the upper post, the cow will crow.  There is plenty of room to put the cow on the top, by the way.  There is no tongue connecting the wagon to the tractor, so even though the wheels turn, the only direction it will easily roll is straight.  There is a bale of straw, but no place to put it in the wagon while the animals are there, and there's absolutely no point to the fact that the tailgate can be dropped.  Luckily, I bought this on Amazon's 40% off sale, but it wasn't even worth that much!  There isn't much here that will stretch a child's imagination, much less offer hours of playtime.  If you're looking for a great toy for your baby, get the Earlyears Roll n' Swirl Ball Ramp.

product_title: Star Wars Signature Series Force FX Lightsaber w/Removable Blade - Obi-Wan Kenobi
review_body:
I won't lie, it's pretty well made. It's a solid product, looks alright and works as advertised. This isn't some cheap toy model, though I'm not sure it's worth the $100+ pricetag. It is obvious that time and thought were spent in creating this item, but it is still misleading. The black and tan sections in the Obi-Wan lightsaber are just plastic, though a very durable plastic. Reading the dimensions of the product and having it in hand are also two different experiences. Overall, the lightsaber seems Oversized, too wide and too long, with the plastic sections representing a majority of its construction. It's a decent replica, but it still comes across as a Prop item, rather than a strictly modeled replica. Hanging from a belt, it is unwieldy and looks not quite right. The included belt hanger is pretty well-made, except for the plastic belt clip, which is thin and not very strong.

I'd meant to use this item as an accessory for a Jedi Costume I'm working on, but after receiving it I think I'll have to find something else. Though both the 501st Legion and Rebel Legion's accept this for their costuming standards, it doesn't meet my own.

product_title: Transformers Age of Extinction Generations Deluxe Class Dinobot Slug Figure
review_headline: A Dino by any other name...
review_body:
Slug is the most recent redesign of the Dinobot formerly known as Slag. The Dinobots for Transformers 4 are a bit of a mixed bag. While Slug isn’t the top of the heap, there is a lot to like about this Triceratops. The first big thing that old school fans will recognize are the red and purple plates that make up much of Slug’s dino form. Each of the new dinobots has its own primary color in the new toyline, from slug to scorn to Snarl. You’ll also notice the design choice where Slug’s body is much more segmented, in contrast to his G1 likeness. It really pops around his head crest.

In robot mode, Slug is a part of this knight aesthetic that flows from Optimus on down through many of the supporting characters. The dino head splits to become two massive shoulder parts and is even attached with a screw where the eye would be in dino mode, which is a fun choice. I will say I’m not overly crazy about the way his tail dangles off the back of the robot mode, but its not horrible. He’s got some nice articulation and looks really slick standing next to both Scorn and Grimlock. If you can pick him up for under twenty dollars, he’s an easy add. Much more than that, and I’d be inclined to look at some of the other TF4 toys first.

product_title: Ricky Bobby #26 Laughing Clown Malt Liquor/talladega Nights 1996 Monte Carlo 1/24th Diecast
review_headline: Before he drove with a live cougar, Ricky Bobby drove the Laughing Clown Chevrolet
review_body:
Every die cast car collection has to have something interesting in it. Maybe it's a rare, limited edition run, or maybe it's a model of your first car. Or, maybe, just maybe, it's the number 26 Laughing Clown Malt Liquor Chevrolet.

As a die cast model, this is middle of the pack - not outstanding quality or realism, but also not something you'd let a 2-year-old play with. Hood and trunk open, front wheels turn and are connected to the steering wheel and the rear wheels are connected to a single axle. It is a genuine scale model and fits right in with 1/24 scale cars.

Other than that, what really makes it special is the sponsors, some real, some imagined and the storied racing career of its driver, as only Hollywood could tell it.

It's a good model, but a better story.

product_title: Myth Board Game
review_headline: Not as bad as some say...
review_body:
Just wanted to put in my 2 cents about Myth.
1. Could the rule book be better, yes. Is it a terrible mess, no. If you are an old school role player, part if the fun is figuring out the rules as you play. Without a DM, it means you discuss it and move on. Remember this is a game, have fun!
2. As this is a starter set, you do not get everything that was in the Kickstarter stretch goals. Megacon Games will be releasing add on packs throughout the next year. As the Crawlers (insect) do not have a "mini" boss, the Shamblers (undead) "mini" boss is included instead. One of the "mini" bosses powers only activates when there are other Shamblers to raise.
3. Quest cards. Yes, there are some quest chains are not finished in the base set. Yes, there is a "quest expansion" that will be available to complete those "chain" quests. As it is, you can play the quests or free form tiles with just the base game.
4. An online starter quest and FAQ is available on the Megacon Games website. There is also a clarification sheet for the starting 5 characters decks, for questions regarding their cards.
5. This is the starter portion of the game. If you were to package everything from the Kickstarter campaign into the game box, no one would afford it. Yes, there was great value in the Kickstarter, but that was for the funding to get this game out to retailers too.

As with any new game, when playing you might not get all the rules right the first time, but as long as you are having fun, it's a great game. This is such a game. I feel that the ability for the "game" to play the darkness role without having someone be the bad guy is a great direction to go. It allows everyone to be the hero, and everyone to have fun.

product_title: Myth Board Game
review_body:
The rule book is ambiguous at points and can frustrate rule lawyers. If you want to get a solid understanding of the rules you need to read the official FAQ and watch the videos MCG is putting out. There is reference to pieces that need to be acquired in expansions, such as the only mini boss in the game summons soulless which is not included.

All that being said the game play is awesome. Each character plays differently and adds to the team and when you don't play as a team you will get rocked. It is up to the group on how hard you want to make each game session and what you want that game session to be. Will you free form, play an act or a story? I also enjoy the progression mechanic for both the characters and the treasure bag.

Make no mistake this is a miniature and board game hybrid and you will want to add more to get the most out of the game. If you do decide to purchase have patience to learn the rules (which will seem overly simplistic once you get them) and understand that this is your game and you can make judgement calls when you like, the designers intended for this. It is not a rigid structure like most hobby games on the market and can lead to some players yearning for more direction.

I would personally recommend this to all of my friends.

review_headline: Fun game that will have everyone laughing!
review_body:
This game is a lot of fun. I make my French students make the French animal noises, of course. It looks like it would be too easy, but once you start playing, you figure out that it's not so easy! You have to first look at everyone's cards to decide if you should be making a noise, or not. Then, make the correct animal noise. There is a lot of saying the wrong noise, or saying your animal's noise when you shouldn't. My students love this game; I've played it with 1st-4th graders, and I also enjoyed it myself, as an adult. It's hilarious when you or another player makes a silly noise. For example, when you flip over a duck, you're supposed to say coin-coin (quack quack), but one student kept saying "duck duck" and of course the hand motions going along with the noise are even more funny. You and your students or children will laugh uncontrollably. It gets much more difficult with 4 players, I prefer only 3 players. Also, the children will need to be highly supervised for several goes before they learn and follow the rules.

Character development is involved; students must be principled (honest) because if they weren't first to make their animal noise, they lose the card to the person who was first, and must admit that they weren't first. As the teacher/judge, I had to stop playing so that I could pay attention to who was really first in making the noise, and with 4 players, it's pretty difficult to tell; that's why I prefer only 3 players.

product_title: Max Factory Persona 4 Arena: Aigis Figma Action Figure
review_headline: Excellent figure, weapon attachment makes posing difficult.
review_body:
This figure to me seems like a great improvement over the previous Aigis in the figma series, however, I still wouldn't recommend this figure for pure fans of Persona 3's Aigis. While this figure has a much higher quality, the difference in hair style along with a few other small differences lose the nostalgic touch from the original game, despite making her look(in my opinion) a little better. If you liked her in Arena as well, or already have the original figure and can afford a second, this one is a must grab.

The only pose I've personally tried is her three weapon pose, where one of the weapons goes into a hole in her back, and the other two attach to that weapon. Usually, when posing I'll put my finger on the small of a figures back to get them to bend and adjust the way I want, with this figure, there is no safe or easy place to grab. Posing her(at least with any of the external weapons attached) turned out to be a much bigger challenge than before.

That said, she poses excellently, and there are only a few things not completely clear by her design. The handle from the Gatling gun escaped my attention at first, then the fact that she actually wasn't supposed to hold it in the pose mentioned above. Once you figure out these things though, she's a wonderful addition to any collection.

product_title: Intex Inflatable Stars Kiddie 2 Ring Circles Swimming Pool (48 inches X 10 inches) [Assorted Styles]
review_headline: Ugly printing but good size for toddler
review_body:

The pool is small enough that you can fill it easily in warm weather and, in colder weather, you can put in boiling or hot water to make the water warm. Our grandson loves it and he crawls in and out easily over the soft sides. He's 14 months old and wants to be in the pool several times per day. It's a great diversion for tired grandparents!

There's plenty of room for him to have several toys, including a big foursquare ball, in the pool with him. My husband is a little worried that he may bite through the sides but this doesn't seem to be a problem with others so I trust the plastic is strong enough.

There are ugly black printed warnings in different languages around the entire outside of the pool. It's not a big deal but I don't like the printing in my photos. I gave the pool 4 stars because of the printing. If I buy again, I'll spend a little more and get a wading pool without the printing. Just saw one at Target today that was a little larger but very attractive for $12.

Some people complained that the pool is not round. My experience is that it is not completely round when filled with air but, when filled with water, it becomes round.

product_title: Bandai Hobby HGBF Gundam Exia Dark Matter Model Kit (1/144 Scale)
review_body:
This is a pretty cool looking kit, though it's not without its flaws. Most notably the "rib cage"-like armor pops off the ball socket joint it's attached to, it's not a huge problem, more of an annoyance than anything.

Cons:
-There are some parts that are loose and can pop off easily. Some can be fixed with glue (those foot spikes for example), and some cannot (the rib cage I mentioned earlier).
-The backpack can be large and cumbersome to pose at times, I've spent more time trying to keep it out of the way than I have actually posing the model itself.
-The kit uses polycaps rather sparingly, which leads to a few areas being stubborn when posing.
-Aside from swiveling at the waist, there is almost not pose-ability in the upper torso

Pros:
-Even without paint, this kit looks great. If you decide to use the provided stickers you only really need to use the one for the eyes to make it look good. Of course, a bit of paneling never hurt either!
-Despite the lack of polycaps making the kit difficult to pose, this also means that it's rather sturdy too. The swords can be kind of heavy, yet only the wrists really give way to their weight.
-Comes with some nice extra hands, weapons, and other alternate parts

All in all, I think it's a really great kit. I'm usually wary of buying kits from or derived from the Gundam 00 series since the kits feel like they are made from a cheaper plastic that the HGUC kits, but this is definitely not the case for the Gundam Exia Dark Matter.

product_title: Lamentations of the Flame Princess: Weird Fantasy Role-Playing Grindhouse Edition Box Set
review_body:
This game has re-invigorated my interest in P&P role playing.

Most of my recent D&D experiences have felt bloated and pointless. Character creation has become inordinately complex. Your characters gain power and their +1s become +2s and +3s and so on, and the numbers get bigger in inverse proportion to the WEIGHT and substance of the game-world. These simple rules burn away all that encroaching tabletop bloat...

This game gets you straight to the fun, and the fear. Character creation is FAST, which is a great way of discouraging over-investment. Don't get attached, they'll likely be dead soon anyway.

So, what's the point? The point is story, and meaningful engagement with your companions. Your characters can easily die -- but that means that when you succeed it actually feels worthy.

All this isn't to say that a competent DM couldn't make a good experience with other rules -- but the core simplicity here, and the embedded emphasis on darkness, dread and powerlessness are, in my opinion, a much better starting point for a good roleplaying experience than the Disneyland products being churned out elsewhere.

Highly recommended.

review_headline: Came with multiple issues, the seller is great though.
review_body:
So I bought this Rally car in the hopes of having a 1/24 scale car of decent quality to mess around in the house without having to buy a Losi. Once again, in the hobby grade game you get what you pay for and this car is no different. It came with a defective battery that smoked as soon as I started to charge it and got very hot. I contacted the seller and they were surprisingly quick about sending me a replacement battery (which the positive terminal was loose from the plug). After charging the new battery I noticed one of the rims wasn't spinning correctly. After close inspection I concluded the factory had improperly installed the rim onto the axle causing the "D" shaped hole to the car to strip into an O. Of course this caused the car to work improperly. Since this car is a 4WD vehicle, the one tire without power affected the car's performance.

I wouldn't blame this on the seller, they were good enough to send me an extra battery and tried to make things right with me. It's the Quality Assurance department of Exceed that really should get their act together. I still would buy from this seller again, just not this car. Buyer beware!

The quality of the grass, eggs, ears, and toy bunny are average, and as one person said in their review, \\"something you can buy from the Dollar Store.\\" But as I said, for $14. review_body:
5/ 5 ENGINEERING
This stuff is designed how a gamer would design it. The pieces clip together flush. The 'removable' levels automatically align with the level below. The room sizes are varied, but standardized. The wall heights are standardized. It all builds together very intuitively. It is very modular. The sets interface with each other very well.

5/ 5 ARTWORK

5/5 PRICE FOR VALUE

Easily enough to build out several connected encounter areas. Although this product is not as durable as the thicker D&D tiles, it is much more useful.

5/5 INTERFACE WITH THE OTHER SETS
I now have three sets of cardboard and two sets of clips. All of it works very well together.

4/5 CLIPS
Don't forget the clips.They sell the plastic clips separate from the cardboard floors & walls. Without the clips the terrain is about as useful as the flat D&D terrain tiles. With the clips, attaching walls & removable levels is a snap. And remember, you don't need a clip at every 'clip slot'. My minor disappointment with the clips is that they distract slightly from the great artwork. On the upside, the clips do work (with a little bit of force) with the slightly thicker D&D tiles, but the utter lack of D&D tile walls make this only a minor perk.

Tip: glue on the bottom with clear glue and it will be invisible when dried. I didn't find the doors stood very well unless I glued them to their small supports. product_title: GERMAN Elspeth vs. Tezzeret Duel Decks Magic the Gathering Card Game Gift Set
review_body:
I first played this deck when in the process of teaching a friend to play the game (after using some simpler decks, he was ready for an intermediate level challenge, which this provides). The Tez deck is helpful for getting the idea of how to play an artifact-based deck, and of course the Elspeth deck provides the \\"white weenie\\" experience, but with a mana curve up to 6WW (for Angel of Salvation). A dissatisfying aspect here is that rarely do you actually draw the planeswalkers; it's obvious why Wizards only included one for each deck ($$), but this is a shortcoming of all the Duel Decks put out by Wizards.

So enough about that: Why buy German? Well, it makes sense if you speak German (or are learning the language), but that's not why I bought it. You'll pay maybe twice as much for the English version of this set, yet the chase cards in German will still fetch a good price on the secondary market, and sometimes even more than English. As of April 2014, the English values are as follows:

Elspeth, Knight-Errant (M) $18
Steel Overseer (R) $11
Tezzeret the Seeker (M) $10.50
Master of Etherium (R) $5
Swords to Plowshares (U) $4.50
Mishra's Factory (U) $3
Darksteel Citadel (C) $2.50
Seat of the Synod (C) $1.50

In this set you get 2 Swords to Plowshares in the Elspeth deck, and the artwork on this version of the card is by Terese Nielsen (the same version was again used in From the Vault: Twenty). You can't go wrong with Terese. The Mishra's Factory from the Tez deck is currently the only version with this artwork, which is a relief if you don't like the style of the Foglios. There are of course plenty of mediocre cards in this set too, but overall this is a propitious purchase at $25.

It seems to also work when I get mad or intense about something. If I start ranting that ball goes crazy. Thank you Learning Resources for providing me with a ViewScope, free of charge, for review on my blog, Ahh~Mazing Reviews. These are my own honest opinions.

Learning Resources is one of my favorite places to get educational toys for my son. Their toys are fun, educational, sturdy, and durable. We have not had a single toy from Learning Resources break, even though my son can be rather destructive. My son has so much fun with his toys from Learning Resources, and learns a lot while playing with them!

Learning Resources recently sent me their Primary Science ViewScope for review.

This ViewScope is like a microscope made just for kids. It includes a clear case for viewing specimens, so you could even put bugs in the case so your kids can see the bugs up close and personal. The viewer detaches for on-the-go discoveries, or attaches to a stand. The ViewScope focuses well with an easy to turn knob that my son can manage easily on his own.

My son has had so much fun looking at plants and other small items with his ViewScope! I can see this as a great teaching tool for a few years to come, until he is ready for a real microscope. It is quite durable and has held up well even though my son has been a little rough with it, but I’ve come to expect that with Learning Resources’ toys.

This game is way fun!!!! Now, if you are stuck on Superman has to be the only person with x-ray vision, this game is not for you. Any person can have any superpower; all you need do is draw the card. The benefits to that are the game is always different. As long as you can manage to break out of the comic universe mantra and delve into having fun and mixing it up a bit, this game is a blast. The box says ages 15+. My 8 year old plays it just fine. As long as the kid can read, they can play it.

So, if you are not a hard core gamer, not a die-hard (we can never change the comic universe, despite the hundreds of alternate universe comic book series that out there) DC universe person, this game will be good for you. It is a great introductory game to card playing and to the DC comic universe, so, no, you do not have to know anything about comics to play this game. I would recommend this game for all.

product_title: Disney/Pixar Cars Action Shifters Flo's V8 Cafe Dragstrip Playset
review_headline: Fun for a Cars fan, but poor quality track compared to Hot Wheels
review_body:
The Flo's V8 Cafe Dragstip race track playset from the Disney/Pixar Cars Action Shifters sets is cool playset for a child who love the Cars movies, but the fun is limited because of the poor build quality.

For starters, the lack of instructions is pretty bad (particularly for the decals/stickers). However, after you finally build this race track you will immediately notice that it's not made of quality plastics and won't hold together if kids are aggressive when they play.

What I mean by that last part is that the track pieces come apart very easily and don't snap together securely like a typical Hot Wheels track playset.

Also, you can tell that the person who designed this toy was trying to cut costs anywhere possible: The included car is cheaply made plastics (like the other cars in the "Cars" family of toys). Even "cool" features are limited, like the car racks where you can put other cars in the playset to "cheer" for the two racing cars ... only one side of the playset has the parts to make the other cars move, so only one side "cheers" for the racers.

For me, the biggest problem is that the playset keeps coming apart and has to be put back together. The only time I have to fix my son's Hot Wheels track is if he trips on it while running and pulls some of the race track apart. This playset comes apart when your kids are just playing with it.

I can really only recommend this if your kid LOVES the Cars movies.

product_title: Congo Monkey Playsystem #1 with Swing Beam - White and Sand Low Maintenance Play Set
review_body:
Overall, we are happy with this set. It looks great, and the vinyl is such a bonus. Staining a playset every year is not something we wanted to deal with. Avoiding slivers and sharp edges are also nice. Not having to stain though was the biggest selling point for us. We also bought the optional monkey bars. My kids love it, and the slide is SUPER fast.

I do have a few complaints, but I have kept them in perspective because I think many of them are complaints that nearly every playset seems to share when you look at reviews.

The first with most playsets is poor instructions. These were ok, but there were several areas where they could be improved. For example, we bought the wood roof option. The instructions did not warn you that you had to put some space between each of the planks rather than butt them right up next to each other. And, since it is not a flat surface, it's not like you can lay them out before you screw them in. We did one whole side wrong before figuring out that they needed to be spaced. The instructions should have told us to space them around 1/2 inch each or so. The instructions for the floor on the second level could have used some similar advice, giving some instruction about how to best space the planks.

The second issue with most playsets is cheap hardware. Most of this was fine, but we really hated the bolts with the sharp edges that had to be hammered in. They just didn't work the way they were intended. If you don't get it in just right and at just the right angle, then the bolt won't go in properly. I think these were the biggest frustration with the hardware.

We did lay out all the hardware in advance, and place them in labeled ziploc bags. That really helped us when we put it together. We were missing two big bolts and since we had only a certain window to get the set up, we had to buy the bolts locally.

Our wooden roof came with several planks where the vinyl was cracked and split. The company sent us replacements without any hassle.

The head room over the slide and entry points (like the rock wall and fire pole) are very low. Even my small 6 yo has to duck his head when going under the slide. Adults...if you want to slide, you'll need to be pretty limber to get your head under it.The company sent us replacements without any hassle.

review_headline: Fun, quick game. Great for any collection

Quite the fun game. As of right now, I only have the base game, and not any of the expansions.

Things don't generally drag on to long. There is a decent strategy to the game, with a hint of luck for people to catch up or make surprising wins. And best of all, it is really COOL! You are a giant monster taking over Tokyo, fighting other giant monsters. Growing limbs, getting fire breath, emitting poison. Quite fun. I would recommend it for basically any board game fans. It's a nice family game, but definitely good enough for any serious gamer's collection.

Bottom line: buy it, you won't be disappointed.

My 2 year old can't figure out how to do this on is own; it would've been a much better design to just leave it as a regular hill, but I guess they had to accommodate because the train is actually an electric train who's wheels move on their own (unlike the other smart wheels vehicles).

But besides the awkward hill, this toy is great. My son SITS STILL and plays!!! (Amazing for a VERY busy, active, on-the-go guy...) :) he loves the tunnels and turns and the track works with any other Smart Wheel vehicles or tracks. He even puts his other non-VTech cars and trains on there :)

Note: it takes up quite a bit of space when assembled, so unless its in a bedroom or playroom, be prepared for it to take up your entire living room :) but it's worth it!

product_title: The King Commands
review_body:
Camelot has fallen! King Arthur is dead, Merlin is missing and the castle has been looted. You and your friends are the last remaining knights of the round table and you have decided to duel for the few remaining bags of gold. But as all knights know money is not everything, whoever walks away with the best story is the true winner. I can’t say that I was expecting too much when I first heard about The King Commands. I had seen the name come up on a number of online forums and figured I should give it a chance. When I saw it at Board Game Revolution I was taken back by the size and simplicity of the game. I took out the cards and saw absolutely no writing on them and figured there must be something brilliant in the mechanics of this game to make it so simple. The rules were really easy to read and it didn’t take long at all to grasp the concept of the game. Basically, players compete to acquire glory through their run ins with other knights. You know it is a good game when the moment you finish everyone says ‘we have to play at least one more time’. I give The King Commands a solid four dice bordering on five.

Cons

1.) Impression – The game is fun. It is simple in its mechanics but brilliantly crafted. Unfortunately the game is pretty simple and will most likely never be a game that people rave about. I feel like it takes a trained eye to recognize the beauty in its simplicity. There will most likely always be other games that people remember and value over this one. Sad, but this may go forgotten someday. It simply lacks a small amount of impressiveness.

2.) Confusion – There was a certain amount of confusion about the bags of gold and how to acquire them. As far as we could tell, acquiring the bags of gold was only possible by attacking a player who had a bag of gold in their hand. If you have a bag of gold in your hand the only reason you don’t want to lose it is because it will go into somebody else’s hand. Otherwise, you hope you don’t draw gold because it is entirely useless for you. Perhaps if there was some way to place the gold into your own discard pile after a certain amount of time then there would be more motivation to keep your gold.

Pros

1.) Artwork – The artwork is simple yet powerful. Not only does the artwork give you something good to look at, but it manages to enhance the game play by making it easy to organize and reference the cards in your hand. Definitely lends itself to the rummy-style game play.

2.) Simplicity – The game is rather simple and this is a huge pro in my book. Anybody can make a game with insanely complex rules because you simply implement a new rule anytime you run into a hiccup. Simple and powerful, this game covers its bases while employing a minimum number of rules. Fantastic.

3.) Convenience – The King Commands, for lack of a better word, is convenient. The game provides a style mixed with length and difficulty that isn’t found in many other games. I find the theme unique and the gameplay familiar, yet refreshing. I like to have a variety of games in my arsenal and this fills a specific situation that not many others do. Refreshingly unique.

4.) Surprise – This isn’t normally a pro that I attribute to a game but there seems to be an impressiveness in concealing the winner until the end. This mechanic accomplishes two things: it keeps people playing fully invested the entire game, and it makes the end tallying of scores rather exciting. Bohnanza is another game with this interesting mechanic.

product_title: Dixit (Cover Art May Vary)
review_headline: Beautiful, but any fun really comes down to the players
review_body:
We received this as a gift recently. As a fan of other similar \\"socially creative\\" card games (Balderdash, Wise and Otherwise) and as someone with an art background, I was eager to give this a try.

Unfortunately, it totally bombed. The artwork and design is fantastic, but that's the best part of it. Because it's much more personal than similar games--the clues are based on what's meaningful to *you*--the game can often succumb to inside jokes, giving certain players an advantage over others. During our initial foray into it, one player was completely left out because other players were repeatedly citing films that only they and their friends had watched.

This is just one of the game's struggles with creative balance. If players aren't very imaginative or clever, they either opt for the aforementioned inside jokes or present something far too bland and obvious. On the other hand, getting too clever or creative with your clues can lead to nobody guessing the correct answer (which in this game actually costs you points). I found myself struggling to find the fun when half the clues were inside jokes, a quarter were far too obvious and simple and the rest were too convoluted and obscure.

The game practically requires a group with very similar backgrounds, say siblings, or a tight-knit group of friends... or a more basic level or players (e.g., children). This will not work as well at something like an adult gaming party. For me, this is a two star game, but it has the potential to work for the right group of players, so I'll give it three.

product_title: Krosmaster Arena Board Game
review_headline: My Favorite Board Game So Far
review_body:
As an avid gamer, this is one of my favorite board games of recent years. The figurines are simply fantastic. No one can argue that they did not dedicate a ton of time and energy making a beautiful brand of japanime style characters with personality. The games that I played can go in between 45 minutes to 2 hours depending on how you roll and what strategy you commit to. I've realized that the games where people summon minions/companions usually take much longer than otherwise. The arena style combat is both simple to understand and difficult to master. It is because of the simple nature of grasping the game that anyone (including children/wives/and non-tabletop gamers can really get into the game.

The packaging itself is smart and leave enough slots for all of the tokens to fit snugly in place without a whole lot of hassle. The only thing I can say is that the game is designed to get additional Kromasters (figurines), but the box does not leave much room for too many more figurines, at least not safely.

Here's a link to me Unboxing Krosmaster Arena
http://youtu.be/E2G-YBe5cd8

My son says: It's really tough. It's fun fun fun fun fun fun fun. It goes good. (It really does have good traction).
We'll keep you posted as we use it this summer.
Update: well, after almost a year, this is still a big hit. The traction has been really good, even in light snow. It has power to get up the hill we have. Our six year old is tall for his age, and the design on this is good for him (his knees don't have to bump his knees). Even our two year old has started driving it!! (With us right next to him, of course!) He will probably be driving it all by himself next year.
We have had no issues with this dune buggy.

product_title: Katamino Pocket
review_headline: Underwhelming as a logic puzzle and implementation
review_body:
I bought a bunch of pocket-sized logic puzzles to try them out. This was one of them.

I can see the value of pentominoes variants for children in terms of understanding geometry, symmetry, and basic problem solving, but it's not clear to me that there is any real logic involved in this solitaire puzzle for adults. Sure, the pieces have to fit, but it quickly devolves into a trial-and-error brute force problem. There are no internal constraints, such as in Sudoku variants, that allow logical thinking to exclude a branch of possibilities. There are no real strategies for starting a puzzle. Thus, you're left to try out each possibility iteratively. In this sense, harder puzzles are hard only because it takes on average longer for brute force to discover the solution. This also implies that you don't really get better at any logical skill as you progress through the difficulty stages. It's all just trial and error, and that doesn't really involve thinking. You might as well be rolling 10 dice until all of them come out as 6s.

Having said that, there is a certain zen-like quality to mindless packing.

The physical design also leaves something to be desired. The bottom tray for 2 thin pamphlets is much larger than it needs to be, and so the whole puzzle feels unnecessarily bulky especially for a pocket edition. The lid is also not exactly secure when closed. Compare for example with the more compact designs of IQ Twist/Fit/Link from SmartGames.

review_headline: Good Price, a few flaws. I'd still buy it again.
review_body:
The description I read said it came with a carrying bag and it did not. However, I didn't need the bag anyway so I didn't freak out over that. I will say for the price the items were awesome and my son loves them.
The triangle is good and makes a great sound.
The bells are fun. I do wish they adjusted but who cares at this price?
The cymbals are a good size and my son has a lot of fun with those but they don't have the greatest sound. He loves them so I don't really care because it's not like he is in a professional cymbal playing band at 18 months old.
The rubbing sticks do not make a great sound either, the undulations on the one stick are not wide or deep enough to get a good sound on it.
The wooden "soprano" thing was really a let down because as others have stated it was over varnished. Because it was over varnished the slits on the side connected on the end but I took a file and fixed that issue. It sounds better but that was annoying to have to do that.
The tambourine is fun too. The top part can be used like a drum and it takes a good beating. A lot of drums these days are covered with that "plastic" that others were complaining about. Mine was clear and not white like the pictured set.
The sticks for hitting the drum and the soprano stick are exactly the same. You get three of those. They aren't the greatest. My son prefers hitting the drum with the rubbing sticks. The tambourine drum has held up well to it.

All in all the set was a winner with my son. I would recommend this set as long as you do not mind having to do a little "fine tuning".

product_title: Tamiya 58346 The Grasshopper RC Car
review_headline: Best RC car I ever got my kids!!
review_body:
I have purchased countless $50 or $100 RC cars. I wish I got this one first!! I had a grasshopper as a kid and eventually sold it (because I was stupid). Would have saved me so much money if I kept it. I know it would still be running. Sit down with your kid and put this car together. Follow the directions carefully and plan on at least a few hours to do it. Don't start in the middle of the living room floor. Use a project board or a location that can be secured. You probably wont do it in 1 sitting. The work is tedious but worth it! You can replace any part that breaks on this car! I made a mistake putting the gear box together but when it acted up I knew what I had done ... because I knew it inside and out!
If your kid will sit make them do the build with you. They will get a great education out of it and a respect for the car knowing they will have to do the repair if they break it.
My 10 year old has slammed this full speed into walls, jumped it off of 5 foot high jumps into end to end rolls, run it into mud and water... I have not replaced anything yet!
If your kid it 5 or older just get this one and avoid buying cheap ones over and over again. You will find yourself out there playing with it! So much fun!

product_title: No Stress Chess
review_headline: Makes chess less overwhelming for a kid
review_body:
Though I know how to play chess, I was never good at strategizing and winning a chess game. As a kid, I used to play it just to show off that I know how to play, I frankly never enjoyed playing chess. May be that is why, I never bothered to teach my daughter how to play chess all these days. She is 6.5 years old now and she herself recently asked me if I can teach her how to play chess. She was curious because couple of her friends play it.
I wanted to make sure I don't transfer MY lack of enthusiasm with the game to her. Also, I was not sure how I can simplify the game for a beginner so that it does not overwhelm her. I browsed on amazon to see if I can buy any teaching books. That's when I bumped in to this 'No stress chess'. As all the good reviews say, this is an awesome teaching tool. The first thing a beginner needs to learn is the moves. We cannot overwhelm a kid by teaching her how to come up with a strategy to attack the king. So, this game simplifies it by providing a deck of cards from which you draw which piece the next player has to move. It does not make the game completely brainless. For eg, if the next player draws a 'Knight', he has to think which is a better move among 2 knights and 8+8 possible positions those knights can move to. This is a great deal for a 6 year old beginner!

My daughter and I got hooked on to it. She asks me to play it with her all the time! Now, even I am becoming a big fan of chess! Once my daughter masters the different moves of the pieces and gets a hang of the game, I will look for more teaching tools to teach kids strategies. I realized any game/art/studies becomes easy and enjoyable when you learn it the right way!

product_title: 100 20" Lumistick Brand Glowstick Necklaces Assorted Colors
review_headline: Exactly what it says on the tin
review_body:
They're glow necklaces. What more can you want?

I use these when I'm going to be out and about after dark in my manual wheelchair -- lighting the necklaces and threading two or three through my wheels makes it more likely people will notice me coming and not walk straight in front of me and stop dead. (They also amuse little kids when they see my wheels lit up and are eye-catching enough that the kids are less likely to run straight in front of me or cut me off.)

The only thing knocking them down from 5-star is that they're slightly less long lasting than some other glow necklaces I've ordered for the same purpose. Their most vivid glow only lasts for less than an hour before settling into a softer and less visible glow, and they're pretty much finished entirely by the 4 hour mark. I'm more used to 2-3 hours of bright glow and then another 4-5 of soft glow for 6-8 hours total.

product_title: Doggone Crazy
review_body: I would recommend this game to dog trainers, humane societies, animal shelters, rescue groups.  Would also recommend to families - your children will interact with dogs, whether or not you ever have one (at friends' house, walking down the street, etc.).  The game is set up so that whoever earns the most bones wins.  Bones are earned by correctly answering questions and correctly identifying dogs (from a deck of card pictures) that are safe to approach/interact with.  I do not always agree with the interpretations about which dogs are safe, which is why I gave 4 stars instead of 5.  Panting is considered a sign that the dog is relaxed and a closed mouth is considered a possible sign of concern.  Really??  Many nervous, stressed and/or frightened dogs pant and should be left alone and many relaxed dogs keep their mouths closed!  However, this has become another valuable learning tool.  As my 7 y/o and 10 y/o daughters and I play, we discuss the "correct" answers stated and whether we think these are right.  Overall, this is a great game that teaches kids to approach dogs safely and cautiously and handle dogs in appropriate ways (no hugging, interacting with dogs while eating, etc.).

review_headline: Good Value, Nice Assortment, Size Is As Stated But Not Large
review_body:
In the 12 pack of dinosaurs, I received all 8 dinosaurs that are pictured and 4 duplicates. The dinosaur 12 pack is a good value since it ends up costing about $1.30 per dinosaur. At that price it's hard to go too wrong. The dinosaurs are made in China. They are durably built and have no problem taking abuse from both my young boys who love dinosaurs.

In the product title it says "Large, Large Jumbo Plastic Dinosaurs" and in the product description it states the dinosaurs are approximately up to 6". If you didn't read the product description I can see where you would be misled by the product title because the dinosaurs are definitely not large. My kids have many Schleich and Papo dinosaurs. My kids' Papo Baby Mammoth is about the same size as these dinosaurs so I would consider these dinosaurs to be small. However, the length of them from nose to tail is accurate; several of them are just under 6" long.

The 12 pack offers a nice assortment of dinosaurs. The dinosaurs look identical in modeling and color to those in the product picture. The modeling, detail, and painting of the dinosaurs is what I expected based on the price. It is fine for the price but nowhere near that of Papo, Schleich, or Safari Ltd dinosaurs which are significantly more expensive. It's worth noting that all of the 2 legged meat eaters have a tendency to fall over on their side unless I bend their legs and tail.

The dinosaur 12 pack is a good value, has a nice variety of dinosaurs, and is sure to please kids who love dinosaurs. Just be aware that the dinosaurs are not large. They are small, measuring just under 6" in length.

Note: A product sample was provided by the seller in exchange for a fair, unbiased review.

product_title: The Learning Journey Match It! Games
review_body:
I bought this Spelling puzzle for my very smart 3 year old nephew who loves puzzles, and already has been working on his reading/spelling. I was actually afraid when I bought it that it might be a bit juvenile for him, but luckily it seems it'll take awhile before he reaches that point.

The only thing I didn't care for, but it's no big deal, is that when you open the box, it's just one huge mass of jumbled puzzle pieces. Wayyy too overwhelming for this purpose. So I helped him by doing most of the work, then giving him partially-finished words for him to work on. By the time we were done, they were all complete, so I tied them in a stack. Now his parents can break up one puzzle at a time and give him the pieces, rather than making him hunt through an entire box for the right cards, which would definitely not hold his interest. When one puzzle becomes too easy, they can break up 2 puzzles, and give them to him, and so on. I definitely suggest this method to keep the kids from becoming "bored" by actually just being overwhelmed. He definitely was disinterested and "bored" when I first opened the box. It was only when he saw the pictures coming together that it sparked his interest. So don't give up too early.

From what I could tell, the pieces were well-made. But as another reviewer stated, they ARE cardboard (albeit hard cardboard), so I wouldn't recommend this for under 3, due to the possibility of them putting them in their mouths. These pieces won't withstand much of that.

All in all, I think it's a very cute idea, well-made, and the price is right.

product_title: Aeroplanes: Aviation Ascendant
review_headline: Competing in the Golden Age of Commercial Aviation
review_body:
I must caveat this review by admitting to being a fan of games designed by Martin Wallace, of which I own about a dozen. In my opinion, he rarely disappoints.

Here Wallace provides us a network-building/pick-up-and-deliver game that offers several strategic options not unlike some of the traditional railroad games designed by Wallace and competitors. Players begin with a base airport somewhere in Europe, and gradually expand their network of air routes by strategically constructing new airports across Europe, and then over to Africa, Asia, North Amerrca, and South America. Driving this expansion is the need to deliver passengers (assigned randomly each game) to global destinations -- the farther the connection, the more profitable the delivery.

Players also purchase aircraft rated for distance and passenger capacity, and beautifully rendered on cards . They represent actual commercial aircraft of the '30s and '40s, and players continue to buy them throughout the game to upgrade their airline fleets and service the ever expanding enterprises. Players can use other player's routes to deliver passengers, but must share the profits; this means that there are advantages to being the only airline serviciing a particularly location if one or more passengers are seeking to go there..

Investments can also be made in a variety of one-time or permanent supplemental capabilities that can enhance airports, increase plane capacity, improve navigation (distance), and more.

This game was not one of Wallace's biggest sellers, but I think many of its critics may have been comparing it to his earlier game Automobile, and expected this to be a grade higher. One criticsm is the random determination of turn order each round; a die is rolled at the beginning of each round to determine the first player. I think it does work in this game in as much as it reduces analysis paralysis. It's not better than Automobile; it's very different, andan excellent strategy game its own right. Additionally, the beautiful artwork -- particularly the authentic airplane cards -- evokes period flavor and is sure to satisfy aviation historians and enthusiasts.

That said, it may be a big learning leap for gamers more accustomed to Monopoly and other family games -- this is not a light game. It will take about 2 hours to play (a bit longer while learning), and I do not recommended for young children.

product_title: Chozokei Soul DragonBall Z Vol. #9 (One ~2" figure in randomly selected blind box) (Japanese Imported) by Bandai
review_headline: Bandai Soul of Hyper Figuration Volume 9
review_body: I bought a complete set of 9 of these guys a few months back and I was more than pleased.  Being familiar with the Soul of Hyper line already, I knew to expect small, highly-detailed figurines that came with transparent, black/grey bases that feature their names in Japanese on them.  However, all of the Soul of Hyper figurines I had bought previously had been simply solid figures with no assembly required.  Not the case here.  Some figures must be assembled (like Cyborg Frieza whose legs and tail must be snapped onto the figurine and Goku whose Power Pole-wielding arms must be snapped on as well) while other figures have interchangeable parts (Turles features two interchangeable arms, one holding a piece of fruit from the Tree of Might.  Vegeto comes with two different heads, one regular and one Super Saiyan; just to name a couple).  There are two different versions of each figure.  Colored (pictured) and monotone.  The monotone versions are easier to find and are generally cheaper, so don't pay a premium price for them.  If you're a fan of Dragon Ball but are yet to dip into Soul of Hyper collecting, be warned: these figurines are highly addictive and cover a vast array of characters over several different assortments.

review_body:
What kid doesn't like an Easter basket full of surprise eggs and candy? This cute basket made of purple and yellow woven reeds is ideal for a preschooler or elementary school age child -- and the adults can nab the Lindt bunny when the kid isn't looking. It's not a big basket -- 9\\" at the longest and 5\\" deep -- but it's plenty big enough for goodies. The rabbit ears headband is adorable, but the stuffed toy rabbit is less so, albeit a nice addition. The included plastic Easter grass is just the right amount to fill the basket. One important note, though: loose jellybeans and small candies will fall through the bottom openings, even with the grass in place, so use the included plastic eggs to hold those kinds of candy.

The only included candy is the Lindt hollow chocolate bunny, which means that you have to supply the candy, coins, or small toys to fill the 12 plastic eggs. I wish that more candy had been included, making it easier to complete an entire Easter basket. I really like that shrink wrap and ribbon are included, so that when you get all your goodies together, you can enclose them in a nice looking gift-basket. The shrink wrap requires the use of a hair dryer.

The incompleteness of the goodies makes it a not-so-great gift for a grandparent or other family member to send to a child, but it does offer versatility to use preferred treats or toys. This is basically a DIY basket to present to a child on Easter day. Note: I received a sample for review.

product_title: Murder Mystery Party Games - Pasta, Passion & Pistols
review_body:
We bought this for my daughter's 14th birthday party. Thankfully, we had enough people to play all 8 roles. There was little guidance on how best to play with fewer than 8 players.
The setting is 2009 but we changed it to 1920s (that worked for the most part) and invited the girls dress up. We had antique hats for them to wear and fake mustaches for the male roles. We also had a red velvet cake with white frosting and caramel sauce with red food coloring to look like blood in a splattered pattern from a knife sticking out of the cake.
The content of the game was adult oriented but not unlike many of the drama-filled television shows targeted at teens. I felt comfortable with the age group we had. I would not recommend this for kids under 13.
The game takes a good 3 hours to play out. The girls couldn't help but ad-lib for the fun of it. They had a lot of fun getting into character! That may have extended the time. We did the dinner first, then Round 1, cake, Round 2, presents, Round 3 and the conclusion. For older participants, the breaks in between rounds may be distracting but for my group of young teens, it seemed to be a nice break and they used it as an opportunity to joke around and discuss the characters/situation.
I really liked how well thought out the included party planning guide was. It even broke down the preparations to when best to do certain activities. There are also recipes you can use for meal planing. It does give suggestions on ways to modify the game, for instance despite there only being 8 roles, more people can play by observing the characters and participating in the conclusion by identifying who they think the murderer is and why. I also liked how even the host can play as the murderer is unknown to everyone except the person who ends up with that role at the start of the game.
Drawbacks include how the script was written and not being clear on how to play with fewer than 8 people.
Each round has Dialog and Questioning. The Dialog is written like a script and was easy to play out. However, the Questioning is written in second person. It was difficult for the girls to come up with what to say in lieu of what was written and to change those lines to first person. I know it was not meant to be read verbatim but I wasn't exactly hosting a group of experienced thespians.
This game is really not for fewer than 8 players despite the Amazon description saying otherwise.
All in all, everyone had a great time playing this game and overwhelmingly asked if we would do this again. It was definitely worth the purchase and time.

review_body:
First off I want to say that I am 19- for an age reference. I am a camp consular during the summer and when the kids went to bed sometimes some of the adult would stay and play this. This game has the same concept as Apples to Apples. When I received mine, I played it with my twin sister and best friend and we really enjoyed it. There are 90 blacks cards and 460 white cards. This is a HUGE difference so after playing a few times you remember what the black cards are...for me it made it less fun; however, there are extensions you can purchase that you can get more black cards as well as white ones. I might purchase those in the future but for right now I am good.

I received the package on time and in tact - no complaints. The box is sturdy and hard. The directions are not some thin piece of paper. If you are on the edge of buying this I would recommend of watching some youtube videos of people playing to see if it is something you would enjoy as for many things are controversial.

Enjoy!

Ok we splurged and bought this unit 6 years ago as a gift to my then 3 and 4 year old. We love this because it's so easy to steer for the little ones much easier than the cheap powerwheels. Time and time again neighborhood kids come to ride it and attempt to destroy it but it's still going strong! THIS WAS WORTH EVERY PENNY. If my kids where still younger and this broke down I'd buy another the next day. Now that it's lasted 6 years if it died I'd have to get a real dune buggy.

my only complaint is the battery is hard to get to quickly. You need to unscrew the seat to charge it and after a month of unscrewing the seat the screw was stripped (no biggie).

If your kids love going fast get this unit.

product_title: ITALERI 556068 1/72 WWII German SS ITAS6068
review_headline: Good attention to detail such as the MP43/StG44 gun
review_body:
The now standard arrangement of three matching sprues of 16 poses has been used again here, and it must be said that a lot of the poses are very similar. There is more variety in the lower rows, although this is largely due to the heavier weapons being used. Several of the poses are almost identical to the first Italeri German Infantry set, which was a reissue of the old Esci product. The poses are OK if rather dull and bland.

As the war went on the German army assimilated a wide range of clothing, this set the theme seems to be cold weather as the men wear an variety of greatcoats, parkas, tunics and smocks as well as over trousers, while several also wear the toque. In some cases the position of the arms makes a definite ID of clothing impossible, but in all cases the clothing has been sculpted correctly. There is a good range of weapons on show here, and again the emphasis is on the later war years, with such weapons as the MP43/StG44 Assault rifle. The men are fairly lightly kitted, with most just having their field flask, entrenching tool and gas mask case, plus the appropriate ammunition pouches of course. In general the moulding is excellent, with plenty of detail in the one place that really needs it, the weapons. One place where this is not true is the base of the mortar. In this the piece is just a featureless slab of plastic and not even the right shape, although the mortar support, which is a separate piece that requires gluing on, is properly done. Also, both the heavy machine guns have had their bipeds twisted through 90 degrees, which allows them to be molded but was not possible in reality. The other machine gunner has found a box to rest on, although this has a side missing (for purely production reasons).
The SS men are more practically dressed and are clearly late war and in a cold environment - images of the Eastern front spring readily to mind. Although there are differences with the winter sets from Revell, this is not anything particularly original, but should work well with both those products. The uninspired poses and accuracy problems we have discussed are the main let-down’s here, which is a pity when the quality and sharpness of the sculpting is generally so good. Many have marked down this set for the reasons outlined, but for me this has to be one of my all-time favorite hence my marking.particularly original, but should work well with both those products. We were able to reset it but a couple of weeks later it stopped functioning and there was no way to fix it. We were able to exchange it for a new one, so far it's working fine. The other Furby started malfunctioning 2 months after purchase, we can no lo longer return or exchange it. My daughters have been very careful with their Furbies and they were both defective. product_title: Personalized Name Puzzle
review_headline: over 60 days to ship and size not as promised
review_body:
Extremely upset and have not been told the truth about this gift. This item was ordered on December 12, 2013, as a Christmas gift for my granddaughter. It was not shipped in time for Christmas. The first delay was when ababy.com called to ask the name for the puzzle. This was in spite of the name I had put in the block on the order form. I was next sent an e-mail that stated the puzzle would be shipped on or about December 30, 2013. On Thursday, January 9, 2014, I received a call from someone who identified themselves as being with customer service. They told me that they would be sending me an e-mail that showed that my item had shipped. This e-mail would go out to me before January 12, 2014, because, they said, “Amazon has a policy of cancelling orders that are not shipped within 30 days.” They asked when I needed it. I told them that I needed it for her birthday party on the next Sunday, January 12. The representative told me that they could not ship it by then, but they would ship it as soon as possible.
On January 16, 2014, I called again to check on the status of the puzzle. I was told that it had not been done yet. They guaranteed that it would be done and shipped by Friday, January 30, 2014. On February 6, 2014, the puzzle was still not here. So I called. I was told that they would check with the warehouse to see when it would be done and shipped. At first it was to be a Christmas present, then a birthday present, now it was not be here even in time to be a Valentine’s Day present. I cannot tell you how disappointed I am that I have spent the time and energy on this. The company did credit one-half of the purchase price back to my credit card.
On February 6, 2014, the company promised that the puzzle would be shipped by Friday, February 14, 2014. It was not. It was shipped UPS from Florida for arrival in Ohio on February 24, 2014.
The puzzle, when it finally arrived, was not as promised. The entire puzzle is 9 inches long and the letters are just over 2 inches high. (the Amazon listing says that it will be a minimum of 16 inches long, depending on the length of the name [ours was 5 letters] and the letters will be 3 inches high.) The letters are packed so close together that a child cannot get their fingers between them. Also, contrary to a question from a shopper, the letters ARE NOT raised above the surface of the puzzle.
I should also have checked on line reviews of this company before I ordered.

product_title: Dungeon Roll Game
review_headline: Quick, Light, Fun, Replayable, and High Quality Components - a perfect fit for us!
review_body:
Just after purchasing Dungeon Roll my daughter (14 yrs) and I enjoyed about ten quick games. I own both Zombie Dice and Martian Dice (I enjoy Martian Dice better). I'm reasonably sure that, for us, Dungeon Roll will replace both.

There is (not surprisingly) a lot of luck in this game, but you have plenty of opportunities through using hero abilities and treasures to influence the outcomes. This is certainly not a deep strategic game. It is very light, fun, and quick to play. It presents enough interesting choices to make us want to immediately play again. Replayability is key for us since we often only have short slots of time to game. We're both having fun with this one.

We have only tried two different heroes each. Her favorite is the Enchantress - so rolling scrolls is key. My favorite so far is the Mercenary, although I might move on to another hero soon (I'm having terrible luck rolling hardly any fighters).

At least once or twice a game we've both felt the tension of deciding to delve deeper (knowing the Dragon will show up soon) or bailing out back to the tavern. Or we've confidently progressed deeper into the dungeon with no sign of the Dragon, only to roll 3 immediately!

This game is by no means deep - there are no complex strategies and combos. But I'm not looking for that in a 15-20 minute game. I'm also quite satisfied with the solo and 2-player experience. I imagine that 3-player would be fine too, but beyond that this game would take too long (much like a 4+ player Zombie dice or Martian Dice experience).

Our scores have been generally low so far (17-20 range) but games are always close. Our final game this morning was the best; it ended 28 to 27, she only beat me by one! Perhaps it's time for me to take a different hero role!

Component quality is top notch. It's a dice game so you'd expect the dice to be high quality - they certainly are. And the game comes in a treasure box - how coolis that? Our only complaint is the experience (XP) tokens. They are double-sided with different numbers on the back. Accidentally flipping them over can mess up your experience count. We've already pimped out the game by replacing the XP tokens with small wooden green cubes (= 1 XP) and wooden yellow stars (=5 XP).

For us this one is a hit!

product_title: Fisher-Price Thomas the Train: Take-n-Play Spills and Thrills on Sodor
review_headline: Toddlers would rate it five stars, I'd only give it 1.
review_body:
My three year old twins (particularly the son) LOVE Thomas, so I was super thrilled to get this track set for them to play with. They have several of the take-n-play engines, but this was the first track set, so I was as excited as they were.

First, assembly was awful. The directions are line drawings, and the parts aren't labeled, so it took a bit to figure out which pieces of track went where. I had to add an additonal 10 minutes to the assembly time because the drawings aren't very detailed, and the pieces aren't labeled, so I put the side bars on backward. The pieces aren't meant to be taken apart once snapped together, so it took me an additional 10 minutes to use a precision screwdriver to carefully seperate the pieces and assemble them correctly. So, after a total of 20 minutes of so, the track was ready to use. In case you don't know this already, this track will NOT stand up on it's own, it has to lean up against a wall. We have hardwood floors and the track kept sliding down, but we moved a throw rug over by the wall and it provides traction to keep it in place.

As for the "accessories" to the track, the first piece, (not including the stop gate) is a yellow "crane" type thing that the train is supposed to swing over edge of the track as it goes by. This works piece works, WHEN the "crane" will stay snapped in place, but it usually flies off the first or second time a train passes by. I usually don't put it back once it falls off unless one of the twins asks me to. The small red "bridge" stays in place, but I'm not 100% sure what the purpose of it is. The small yellow crate that is supposed to be "slid" down the track falls off constantly, usually before the train even gets to it. To tell you the truth, I'm not even sure where it is now, it's probably in the bottom of the toy box. Last we have the paint shop, which is adorable and thankfully, actually works. Even though my toddlers just turned 3, they are able to fit the "paint splash" into the area where it belongs so that Thomas can get "painted." However, the paint only works with Thomas (who is included) so the paint wont' "stick" to the other trains. While the paint splash works, the paint "shop" tends to fall off the track with regularity.

As for the "track", the turns are quite sharp, and it is not unusual for a train to derail by the second switchback. I'm also not buying the "take and play" aspect of this thing....adding a hand hold at the top does not make something "portable." This thing is too big to be easily packed up and carried anywhere.

My twins love this track, and usually at least one of them plays with it every day. On the other hand, they just turned 3, and are quite happy letting the trains roll down the track, and don't really mind that the "accessories" don't really work. I think a child that was a little older would get very frustrated with the parts falling off and having to replace them each time a train went down the track. Personally, I would give this item 1 star, but since my babies do enjoy it so much, I decided to give it three stars, meaning it's "OK." product_title: LED Light Weight Magnifier with 5 Lenses 1x, 1.5x, 2x, 2.5x, 3.5x
review_body:
I just received these and opened the package to check them out. I didn't expect great packaging or quality since you usually "get what you pay for", in other words, these were very low price and my expectations were not terribly high.
I was very pleasantly surprised! The packaging was top notch (I know, it's just packaging... But when even the packaging is higher quality, that says something right away!). I opened them up and right away there was something I didn't remember seeing in the description, a head strap in case you wanted to wear them that way. The glasses frame seemed to be very sturdy and when I put it on it was actually very comfortable. The LED light had a insulator strip that had to be removed so the light would work (Another small detail that shows quality. Without it the batteries would probably be depleted by the time they got to you.) LED's were not extremely bright, but they're definitely sufficient for up close detail work. The lenses were in a separate nice heavy duty case, all separated so they don't get damaged and they appear to be glass (I'm not sure, but I do know they feel heavy like glass and seem to be great quality also.) The only negative thing that I could say about these is that the clip for the lenses seems to be very tight (Which may wear in after a while so I'd rather have them tight than loose!).
I wouldn't normally write a review for something so simple or inexpensive but I think that these warranted a review as I was VERY impressed with everything about them! I would DEFINITELY recommend them if you're looking for some magnifiers!!!

product_title: Militants Gordian (japan import)
review_headline: Dont waste your money on this...
review_body:
I recently got into collecting action figures (specially robots from old cartoons - 70's & 80's) and since it's so hard to find a "Gordian" figure I decided to get this while I try to get a real one from eBay or something (since Amazon doesn't have any). By "real one" I mean an actual action figure that looks decent enough to put it in a display case - this one isn't even close. First of all I didn't know exactly what I was getting because there was no description in the product's page. I had a slight idea based on the pictures (or so I thought).. so I was unpleasantly shocked when I got it - I didn't think it would be this bad. Toys that come free with kid's meals are better quality than this.

This is actually a plastic assembly kit where you need to take the parts out of a flat plastic mold and "glue" some of them together and "hope" that they will hold. Not all of it needs to be glued together, in some cases there are little plastic pins that are supposed to hold some parts together (some times they just don't work). The instructions come in Japanese only so I had to figure it out based on the diagrams and actually used google translate to confirm that the instructions specified that some parts needed to be "glued" together (cause I couldn't believe it at first).

Enough ranting, the reason why I dislike this product is mostly because of it's low quality. Obviously it is plastic, but lets just say that I just finished assemblying it and a piece already broke. The figures themselves DO NOT look at all like they do in the box once assembled E.g. Gordians helmet is ALL blue (no eyes, no white piece nothing). Same thing goes for Derringar (helmet is all red - no details) but the worse is protesser.. the entire figure is white.. no color at all (same goes for Daigo). Of course since it is plastic you could probably paint them (I'm thinking about painting protesser). The figures have no articulation whatsoever.

Bottom line is that this product is NOT worth $50. I wouldn't even pay $30 for it - maybe $15 (but in all honesty I wouldn't buy this product ever again).

The concept was nice (obviously based on the anime) but the execution is terrible. Like I said one piece already broke (derringar's shoulder) so I can't even put the robots inside the next because it is so fragile that the whole thing would just come apart (the glue, the pins everything). Protesser is actually the sturdiest because it's the smallest so it just uses 2 pins.

Not only did I waste $50 on this.. I also spent my weekend putting it together (waiting for the glue to dry etc).

I hope this review helps somebody out there and I can save you some money.

product_title: Undernail Writer - Swami Gimmick
review_body: Once for ounce, this is probably the most powerful magic gimmick in the arsenal.  Tiny, practically invisible.  But they need to be adjusted to your thumbnail when they arrive.  The little wings go under the nail, and the barrel and lead go above it.  Tighten it up until the barrel is pressing down and the wings are pressing up and it "pops on."  If you can take a tiny needle nose pliers and bend up the very tips of the wings (parallel to the nail edge) to dig into the underside of the nail, it'll hold better.  And maybe make a groove on the underside of your nail to give the wingtips something to grab.  Adjustments tend to loosen the barrel and the lead can slide around, so just touch it with superglue and it'll hold still.  Don't let the glue run onto the writing end or it will have to be sanded off before it will write again.  The all brass construction means that it will "spring" on like a champ for a long time!
