product_title: Ouija Board - Pink
review_headline: Pink Ouija Board Not Just For Girls!
review_body: Ouija BOX (front):  The box to this Ouija board is all pink and says the following:  "Ask the questions Girls want to know. With carrying case! Now with Question Cards 72 fun things to ask! Only at Toys-R-Us. Parker Brothers, Ages 8 +"  The box has a cut-out that makes the carrying case visible from the front.  Ouija BOX (back):  The back of the box is purple and pink and says the following: "Girls have questions...Ouija has answers! It has always been mysterious. It has always been mystifying. And now Ouija Board is just for you, girl! With 72 fun questions included, you'll never run out of things to ask... Who will call/text me next? Will I be a famous actor someday? Who wishes they could change places with me?"  "Gather your friends around, draw a card, place your fingers on the planchette, and ask you question. Concentrate very hard...and watch as the answer is revealed in the message window."  "Or make up your own questions! Ouija Board will answer. It's just a game--- or is it?"  "Contents: Ouija Board, message indicator (planchette), Crad deck with 72 Questions, Carrying Case with storage pockets, Instructions."  "Includes cool carrying case! Take it to parties, sleepovers, and more!" The box shows exactly what the box contains in pictures right on the back!  Ouija CARRYING CASE:  The carrying case is pink and is made out of vinyl and plastic. It has the sun and the moon in the top corners. The bottom corners have a graphic of a girl with purple hair and puckered lips as if ready to give you a kiss. It has a very large graphic of the Ouija Mystifying Oracle and a large graphic of the hot pink Planchette. The back has a very large graphic of the Ouija Mystifying Oracle and pretty graphics of flowers in each corner.  It feels fairly durable for something that is mostly plastic. The case has two shoulder straps that are a thick plastic and it looks cheap. There are zippers on both sides of the carrying case and zips and unzips fairly easy. On the inside of the case it has a compartment for the Ouija board, Planchette, and Question cards.. Everything fits snugly inside this case.  Ouija BOARD:  The Ouija board is very nice and is pink with purple letters. The "sun" and "moon" symbols are in yellow and baby blue. The layout of the board is exactly like the boards from the past. This board is very durable and is made out of the usual "Masonite" and is not cheap cardboard. The back has flowers surrounding the OUIJA Mystifying Oracle brand name. Very girly and nice looking board!  Ouija PLANCHETTE:  The Ouija Planchette is in hot pink and has a different shape than the usual planchettes that come with standard Ouija Boards..it reminds me of Valentines day candy hearts. The window is plastic with a tiny pointer that sticks out under the window. It feels cheap but is perhaps more durrable than the classic planchettes included in standard Ouija games. It has rounded corners and has the Ouija Mystifying Oracle graphic printed on the top.  Ouija QUESTION CARDS:  There are 72 Questions on 36 cards. They each have the Ouija Mystifying Oracle graphic on the backs. The fronts are decorated in pink flowers on a white background. The questions range from silly, to serious and some actually "test the Ouija Board" Questions include but are not limited to the following:  "Will (name someone) be my best friend when I grow up?", "Ouija Board, are you real?", "What cartoon character do I resemble?", "Which animal best matches my personality?", "What is my worst habit?" "Will I climb MT. Everest someday?" "Who wishes I would sit with them at lunch?" "Will I ever be on reality TV?" "What is my best physical feature?" " Who will ask me to go out with them next?", "At what age will I get married?", "Will I be president someday?", "Who has a crush on me?", "How many children will I have when I grow up?",  "Will I ever skydive?", "If the Ouija Board could rename me what would my name be?", "If I have to choose will I choose love or money?", "Does (name someone) want to go out with me?", "If I have to choose, will I have a career or stay home with my kids?" "Am I a good dancer?", "Will I ever volunteer for the Peace Corps?", "Where can I find burred treasure?", "Test the Ouija board.. What time is it now?",  and my personal favorite....  "Will I be a famous writer someday?"  Ouija INSTRUCTIONS:  This version of the Ouija Board has the most in depth instructions I have ever seen included in a Ouija Board game. It is a single sheet of paper that folds in half vertically. The instructions state the following:  "Ages 8+/ for two or more players."  "The Ouija Board (pronounced WEE-JA) has always been mysterious and mystifying. Ask it a question and it will respond by spelling out your answer in the window of the message indicator (Planchette). And now included---Question cards! Ask the Ouija Board what girls want to know!"  "SET-UP: 1) Before using the Ouija Board, wipe it with a dry cloth to remove dust and moisture. 2) Sit opposite another player or gather around the board if more than two are playing. 3) Set the Ouija Board on the players laps or on a small table between and within reach of the players. 4)Additional players are encouraged to look on and take note of the Ouija board's responses. 5) Set the planchette in the center of the Ouija Board. Place the cards face down near the board. 6) Place your fingers lightly on the planchette. Or, you and another player place the fingers of both hands very lightly on either side of the planchette. 7) Now concentrate."  "ASKING QUESTIONS USING THE CARDS: Players take turns drawing cards and choosing a question to ask. Ask only one question at a time. Ask your question slowlyand clearly. Allow the planchette to "float" across the board to reveal in the window either yes, no, a number, or letters of the alphabet. It may help to start by choosing yes or no questions.  Once the Ouija board is "warmed up" you can ask more complicated questions, and wait to see what the planchette answers. If your question has a blank, the Ouija board will spell out the answer for you. Some questions "test" the Ouija board to see if it can correctly answer your question. If nothing happens, try asking another question. Allow one to five minutes for an answer to come."  "ASKING YOUR OWN QUESTIONS: Be creative. Ask the Ouija board anything you want! Just remember to have fun. After all, it's just a game...or is it?"  "STORAGE: When finished, store the Ouija board in the handy carry case, and store the planchette and card deck inside the inner pockets of the case."  Ouija COMPANY MERGE AND CONTROVERSY:  In 2008 Parker Brothers and Hasbro Toys merged together to make a Ouija Board just for girls. This was an experiment between the two companies to see what marketing techniques they could employ to increase the sales of an already dwindling toy, the Ouija Board game. Despite their efforts to do away with spooky propaganda and to introduce more kid friendly play, the Ouija Board pink came under fire from religious groups and parents alike.  The controversy stemmed form the belief that makers of Ouija Board pink were exploiting little girls to get interested in the occult and there was quite an upset concerning some of the questions included on the cards. The concern from many were the questions themselves..many had an adult themed element and this upset many parents. Shortly after Hasbro bought the rights to the Ouija Game from Parker Brothers and quickly decided to pull the plug on Ouija Board pink.  Only a couple hundred were ever produced and Ouija Board pink would go down in history as the worst concept ever devisedby a toy company.  Ouija PERSONAL EXPERIENCE:  Oh where do I begin? First of all I love this version of Ouija Board not only are the ideas clearly thought out but the product itself is very high quality. The carrying case and planchette have some quality issues certainly but the issues are very small and ultimately minute. I attempted to play the game with my family and had boys and girls ranging from the age of 9 and 14 join in. The boys were a little apprehensive at first because of all the pink but soon wanted to get involved with the rest of us. The girls seemed to have the most fun with the carrying case and used it to put their dolls and what have you inside of it.  We did try to use the Ouija Board to contact "spirits" but this didn't last long as both the boys and the girls quickly lost interest. We probably had the most fun using the question cards and took turns answering the questions. We tried to re-invent the game by having the kids guess what answers their playmates might answer...but in the end this had a life-span of about 30 minutes.  Personally I think this Ouija board is one of the most innovative and creative design concepts attempted yet by Hasbro or other companies who owned the rights to Ouija Board in the past. I did not find anything that I would call "inappropriate" for young girls or boys alike. This edition is very rare and has a hefty price tag that only a collector like me would be willing to pay. All in all I love my Ouija Board Pink and wish that Hasbro will continue to explore other concepts like this in the future!

product_title: Pokemon Center Sylveon/Nymphia 10" Plush Doll
review_body: I found myself doing maybe a little too much extensive research on the best ways to minimize your chances of buying a fake Pokemon plush.  I bought this plush from UJC Mart Japan, which is fulfilled by Japan, and as far as I know, it is a legitimate one.  It seems like some people are getting ones that either don't match the picture or they're fake (or both).    The best rule of thumb is to be weary of stores that either ship from China or do not post where they ship from, since China is NOT licensed to sell Pokemon Center plush.  They DO manufacture them though, which explains why a lot of the \\"oops\\" plush come from there.  You might have to pay more to ensure that you're getting a legitimate one, but I think it's worth the price, since you probably will not have an easy time trying to get a refund from a knock-off.    Aside from that, the plush itself is adorable.  The left ear (without the bow) is a little hard to balance to stay up, and it usually flops in either direction if you try moving the plush afterwards.  The \\"ribbons\\" on it are sew on, so you are limited in ways you can pose it.  Once again, it is super cute! :)    Edited just to add a picture of the plush:  [...]

product_title: Dixit (Cover Art May Vary)
review_headline: Fantastic, thoughtful game that brings people together.
review_body:
Now, I should start by saying I'm very left-brained. I'm 27 years old, and when I first sat down to play this with some friends of ours, I was very skeptical. Seeing the very creative but very fantasy-based pictures on each card had me wondering if 1) this was really a game that adults would enjoy and 2) whether or not I'd be good at it, since I don't consider myself to be very creative or artsy. I'm very practical and logical by nature, so I was worried I would fail miserably at this or that it may not be much fun for me.

Wow, my first impressions were wrong! This game brings out so much creativity in everyone. It's all about interpretation - of not only the way you view your own cards but of the way that other players may be viewing theirs. It's a very simple game to learn but truly great for all ages (we played this with grandparents over the holidays and it was a memorable experience for everyone). We've played this with friends who have many different professions and interests, and it just adds to the fun. Highly recommended. We've already bought one expansion pack. My only critique would be that the expansion cards cost just as much as the original game, and you really do need more cards if you play a lot.

The games are expensive. They are the same cost as buying a cartridge game would be which to me seems steep.  They do run sales every once in a while, but it's nothing spectacular.  I was really expecting a little more out of the LeapPad Ultra- especially with the camera and whatnot.  You can't download Netflix or Skype or anything like that.  I think you can download movies and music but it all has to be from LeapFrog.  It's kind of annoying. That being said, my daughter does really like it.  She gets very excited about playing on her LeapPad and learning new things that it can do. I do feel that the games that I put on it are helping her learn her letters and numbers.  I wouldn't buy this again and in hindsight would recommend it as a gift either. To me, the cost just isn't worth it when there are so many free games to play online at Nick Jr. or Disney Jr., etc.

product_title: Syma S111G 3.5 Channel RC Helicopter with Gyro
review_body:
A friend of mine had the S107G at his place and I fell in love with flying it around. I became particularly interested in using it as a potential toy with my cats. I have two cats - one of them is more skittish and runs away as soon as it hears the rotors, but the other one can not get enough of it. The helicopter has held up well to repeated paw smackdowns and the cat has held up well to the propellers (which automatically stop as soon as they meet any resistance). Flight time to charge time ratio is decent.

My only gripe with this particular helicopter, vs. the Syma S107G, is the landing gear - the S111G has three plastic nubs that look like wheels but they can be bent easily by anything other than a soft landing. The helicopter tends to fall over on its side when it lands, which makes subsequent take offs more difficult. When I get another one of these (and I will, they're so gosh darn fun) I'll probably get something with two bars or more traditional landing gear. Compared to the S107G, this helicopter also seems slower (but perhaps a bit more stable, because of it).

product_title: 1775 - Rebellion
review_headline: Finally!  A wargame for people who don't like wargames
review_body:
I got a chance to play this game at a convention (somebody liked the game enough to bring their own copy). I'm not heavy into war games..in fact I really don't like them very much, BUT THIS GAME WAS SO MUCH FUN!!!! It doesn't even play that much like a board game, as it has elements of area control games mixed in. Think of it as Risk meets El Grande.
The game is designed for 2-4 players, and we played the 4 player game which seemed especially good because you play as two teams. Each of the factons has their own unique deck of movement and event cards as well as their own unique diec. In addition to those teams. there are Native Americans that will join forces with either side once recruited (but will not fight against other Native Americans), as well as some French and Hessian troops show up here or there. They all come with their own dice as well.
The idea of the game is to control the most states and Canadian Provinces at game's end, which occurs either after 8 game rounds at the end of the turn in which one side declares a truce. There is movement and conflict in the style of 'Risk', but with more diversity (keeping the game very interesting). Each die has sides that have bulls-eyes on some sides (counts as 'Hits'). The blank sides aren't treated as 'misses', but as 'Command Decisions', giving you a choice to have a troop remain in the fight or to retreat (if possible) to a neighboring friendly or neutral territory. Some faction's dice have an addition symbol for 'fleeing', where a unit is removed from the battle and placed in an area for reassignment on the next turn.
The only gripe I have - albeit a small one - is the use of the generic euro-cube to represent troops. In the one hand, they ARE easier to count and to move than the tiny little infantry figures of 'Risk', but being a game based on historical events, it's seems kind of callous to represent these people with wooden cubes. That being said, it doesn't make the play of this board game any less fun. And this IS a game, not a historical re-enactment!
It's refreshing to see a game of conflict that gets it right for non-wargamers and goes beyond the endless dice rolling while struggling for world domination. My son and I were giving each other high-fives for our teamwork having eeked out a tie against a more experienced team. product_title: Vampire Spike 12 inch Figure from Buffy the Vampire Slayer
review_body:
I bought this for my girlfriend, who is such a Buffy fan that she can recite dialogue from every single episode! And since her favorite character from the show is Spike, it was a no-brainer that I buy her this one.

The packaging itself is very well done, with the front showing an extreme close-up of the vamped-out Spike figure's face; and the front opens like a door, showing the figure and accessories through a clear plastic window. My girlfriend spent several minutes just looking at Spike and his items, and words like "This is so cool" and "I love this" would periodically escape her lips.

The figure itself is pretty impressive; Spike's vamp face and hair is very detailed, right down to the scar on his left brow. And the clothing he wears is surprisingly well done and fit on the character well; not all bulky or out of proportion as is often the case with 12' figures.
It comes with a broken human skull accessory, a replica of the necklace he wore in the series finale, a replica of the shotgun Spike had planned to use on Buffy in the episode "A Fool For Love." and a display base to display the figure on (complete with stylish Buffy logo on the base) All of these items look great; but instead of the broken human skull, I think it would have been cooler to have a "normal face" Spike head which you could attach to the figure.

Overall, I was very impressed with this purchase, and feel it would be a worthy addition to any Buffy fan's collection. My girlfriend, who is the hardcore fanatic give it "Two Stakes Up!"

product_title: Village Board Game
review_headline: Very fun and unique game for us!
review_body:
Village entertains both my husband and me very much! Our 9 yr old son is begging us to play with him (he watched us play once and thinks it looks super fun!). And, he's right. It is super fun.

You essentially send your family members out into different areas of the "world". Then, you have to make choices on which people remain involved to get you things (which lead to Victory points) and which players, ever so sadly, die. It's strategic decisions that dictate who dies and when (also a way to get victory points is to strategically kill off your family members so they get a place in the village chronicles.....so, dying can equal loads of victory points!). Of course, it's difficult to sum up how to play a game like this ina review. The main point is, it's fun and it's different. We have a great time with this one!! I think the expansion (The Village Inn which is essentially a pub with some other extras) would be very fun! I look forward to getting that at some point.

Play mostly 2 player. Probably takes somewhere between 1 and 1.5 hours to play, depending. And, not a terribly difficult learning curve. You do have to read the manual and have a trial game, of course, as is the case with all of these types of games.

100% recommend Village!!

Just an FYI...A few of our other favorites are Castles of Burgundy, Rialto, Tzolk'in, Dominion, London, Thurn and Taxis, Legacy, Seasons, 7 Wonders, Bora Bora, Keyflower, Le Havre...(ok, we have a lot of favorites!)...and we are eager to learn Trajan, Terra Mystica, Among the Stars, Puerto Rico, Shadows over the Empire and Euphoria. product_title: The Settlers of Catan
review_headline: Fantastic, and one of the most entertaining, thoughtful and engaging games I've ever played
review_body: Catan is a blast.  I've already played it a number of times with the kids, and each time there's some clever nuance or strategy to pick up.  The board is colorful, sturdy and, much to our delight, can be rearranged for different styles of gameplay.  The painted wooden pieces are a great touch, and have a throwback feel like the classic Risk game.  The game cards feature detailed paintings and add a unique feature to the game.  What impresses me is how well-balanced the elements of the game are: resources tend to be equally distributed, players all seem to get a chance to develop and advance, and when someone finally wins, unlike a game like Monopoly, there isn't really a player who's been skunked in the game completely, but everyone seems to have a good chance to earn victory points.  The pace is great, it's fairly easy to learn, and there are some great educational opportunities nestled into the game as well.  Highly recommeded - one of the best games I've ever played.

product_title: Tzolk'in: The Mayan Calendar
review_headline: SO unique and VERY fun!! It's a must buy :)
review_body:
Tzolk'in....is amazing. And beautiful. And creative. And fun. And very different for a worker placement game.

The shifting of the calendar makes this game different. The look, feel and play of the game is quite unique. My husband and I learned it and then had to play it over and over again to try new ways of playing.

We've only played 2 players and it takes roughly 1-1.5 hours. I think this would be a good one to play with more than 2 (as well as being super fun with 2!) because each turn is pretty simple. Either you place workers on or you take workers off. So, it would still play relatively fast with more people.

I think it's a must buy to add to any board game collection and, I think it's a must buy for anyone just looking for a few good games to play! There's no way you could buy this, learn it and play it without falling in love with it. Sure, that can be a challenge ;)

We have come to adore Stefan Feld games. I'm pretty sure he must be a genius. Which, I certainly am not! Nor am I a huge "gamer" by nature. I am a newly conformed gamer because I love my husband and he's a pretty big nerd at heart. (You know, super smart, loves to think, learn languages, read, and would love to play video games for hours but can't because he has 3 kids...lol). So, when he wanted to start playing these longer, more intense euro-style games, I rolled my eyes for a few months at the thought. BUT, then he returned from a deployment and tricked me into picking out several games on my own accord. I came across Castles of Burgundy, bought it and allowed myself to learn it with him. LOVED IT and fell in love with euro-gaming. (=super happy husband!).

Just an FYI...A few of our other favorites are Bora Bora, Castles of Burgundy, Rialto, Dominion, London, Thurn and Taxis, Legacy, Seasons, 7 Wonders, Bora Bora, Keyflower, Le Havre...(ok, we have a lot of favorites!)...and we are eager to learn Trajan, Terra Mystica, Among the Stars, Puerto Rico, Shadows over the Empire and Euphoria. product_title: Chutes and Ladders Super Hero Squad
review_headline: The Pros & Cons of Marvel's Chutes & Ladders
review_body:
If you like the original Chutes and Ladders, chances are you'll like this one, and for the price, it's one of the least expensive games out there for kids aged 2-4. I'll be making comparisons to the Chutes and Ladders I grew up with in the early 90s. I don't know how the \\"regular\\" Chutes and Ladders of this decade compares.

You should know, my 3-year-old requests to play this game every. single. day. I'll give the pros and cons from my point of view, but he'd give it a hearty 5 stars--two and a half Time Lords--because he loves it so much, even if he doesn't quite understand the gameplay yet.

Pros (or should I say...Ladders?):
1) Superheroes, obviously. I'm not going to pretend to know all of the names of the characters on the board, but the characters you can choose between for game play are Spider-Man, Hulk, Iron Man, Silver Surfer, Wolverine, Captain America, Thor, and Phoenix.
2) I got really excited that there were plastic protective cases and EIGHT characters to choose from. In the game I grew up with, you got four flimsy cardboard pieces and four little plastic stands that they needed in order to stay upright. Invariably the tiny plastic pieces get lost and/or eaten. This is an improvement! But...see #1 of the cons below.
3) This game is pretty open ended and can be educational if you're creative about it. Lessons: Consequences and rewards (something kids seem to need to learn more now than ever), counting, number recognition, addition up to 100, and of course, sportsmanship / not being a sore loser or winner.
4) This game can last forever. Seriously, I think we played a 90-minute game. It was a bit tortuous for us adults--When will it ever end?--but my son seemed to enjoy it. He also had no idea who was losing or winning and didn't care.
5) The consequences and rewards are really...weird. Some of them don't make much sense at all. In that sense, it's pretty similar to the classic game. These illustrations are just more ambiguous. I'll list them below the \\"Cons.\\"

Cons (Chutes):
1) There are only 4 plastic cases for eight characters, which means you either have to pop them out and replace them consistently, or you double up the characters. To separate the plastic casings, you have to bend the big piece back, and then the smaller piece will pop off. We doubled up the characters into pairs that made sense to me. Four Avengers paired with the four other characters. Our set up: Iron Man / Wolverine, Captain America / Silver Surfer, Hulk / Spiderman, Thor / Phoenix.
2) There's still only one girl character, and it's Phoenix. I'm betting most girls and boys are more familiar with Storm than with Phoenix, but that's just me. I don't watch the shows or anything. Is there a TV show? I know nothing.
3) Like the original game, you really have to pay attention which direction you're supposed to be moving on the board. Little ones who don't know the order of numbers will need help knowing whether they are supposed to go left, right, up, or down at any given time. My husband and I will go the wrong way pretty often, too.
4) I'm not really sure what lessons are supposed to be taught by this game. For one, everybody in my family thinks that slides are more fun than ladders, so that's confusing, morally. \\"Yay! I get to go down the slide! Oh, wait, that's bad in the Chutes & Ladders universe.\\" Might give you an opportunity to discuss alternate realities with your children, I suppose.
5) I can foresee my (older) kids yelling out \\"CHUTE\\" whenever they land on one. I find double meanings amusing, but some parents might not agree. \\"Magneto is riding his bike dangerously? CHUTE! He broke his bike!\\"

Spoiler Alert? I'm going to list the chutes and ladders illustrations as I interpret them. Maybe someone else can shed some light on a couple of these.

The Ladders:
1: A flying man holds a bone out to a dog he may or may not be acquainted with. -> Dog has bone. Man is hovering above him.
4: Storm is mixing batter. It's pink, of course, because she's a girl. Duh. -> Storm has a finished cake and attempts to...levitate it? My son was apparently confused by her hand gestures. Our exchange went like this: \\"Yay! Look! Now she has a cake!\\" \\"Why is she not happy?\\" \\"She is happy. She has a cake. Look, she's smiling.\\" \\"She's NOT happy.\\"
9: Cyclops uses his laser vision to torch a roast bird. -> He seems to be chewing a mouthful and is holding a drumstick in each hand.

Chutes
16: An angry-looking guy is holding a skateboard and a mace. -> Now he's sad, and his skateboard is broken.
48: Magneto is riding a bike, wearing a helmet even, with both hands on the handle bars. -> He angrily holds up the pieces of a broken bike. (I think the point here is that he rode the bike DOWN THE CHUTE, but this might need to be explained to kids who don't infer that.

product_title: Star Wars Edge of The Empire RPG Core Rulebook
review_headline: Finally, it feels like I'm playing a Star Wars RPG again!
review_body:
I held off writing a review until my group had a chance to play the game for a while. Having waited, here are my impressions:

1. The book itself is beautiful. The artwork is really nice, the book is well organized, and the pages, covers, and binding feel like they are really well put together.

2. The game system is fun and fast. I don't know how well it would work for a non Star Wars game (or space opera style), but it really captures the Star Wars feel. I've played all of the versions of the Star Wars RPG's over the years, from the first edition of West End Games to the Star Wars SAGA rules, and I like this system the best. My players have been really surprised at how much the game captures the feel of the movies (original trilogy). Part of it is the setting, to be sure, but also, the dice system has a certain feel to it when playing. You can succeed, and still have something minor go wrong. Or you can fail, and still pick up on some advantage you can use later. We have 5 PC's in our group, and with the skill tree system, we don't really have much skill "overlap". For the first time in I don't know how many years, I haven't had players try to figure out what the group "needs", they are just playing what they want. This system puts story and character ahead of dice rolls and complicated rules. That's what really gives it the "Star Wars" feel.

3. The dice. I thought this would be the biggest hurdle with my group. We are almost all long time gamers, and really, who wants to buy yet MORE dice for their game? We each have about 5 pounds of d6 dice for Shadowrun, a full set of dice for D&D, Storyteller dice (regular system AND Exalted dice). But Fantasy Flight Games did something really cool here-they made their own app for iOS and Android, at a reasonable price, for the specialty dice the game uses. I recommend buying the app for $4 vs a dice set for $14, plus, since the company actually made the app, it works the way it should. The app has options to factor out opposing successes and failures, and gives the player the net total. It really speeds up the game.

The book is worth the price. But let's face it, I've read some of the other reviews, and if you're in love with one of the previous versions of the Star Wars RPG, they I would suggest playing what you like, that's the point of a RPG in the first place-fun. If you haven't quite found a system you're happy with, or you are just curious, I would recommend you buy this book. I think you'll really like it.

product_title: Estes Proto X Nano R/C Quadcopter-p
review_headline: Amazingly fun, but these things are NOT built to last
review_body:
I had a hard time flying it at first, and I thought my quadcopter was defective. But, alas, no. After almost 30 flights, I have now mastered this thing. It's so freaking cute and awesome. My only complaint is I wish it could run longer.

edit:

An update to my previous review. So, after just 30+ flights, one of the motors is completely dead. Hopefully, Estes will replace it. I've read that these motors were not designed to last. But, I'm pretty shocked to see one fail so fast.

edit part deux:

The second one (replacement from Estes) died on me with less than 30 flights too. This time, the back two motors (black props) are going. They were getting stuck and I had to flick them to get them going. Now, one is completely dead and the other is barely hanging on at full throttle. I don't know if I'm just unlucky, but there are lots of others on the radio control estes forums complaining about this problem. I really hope this second one would have lasted atleast a 100+ flights like others are claiming.

edit part three:

So, I am on my third Proto X. And, this time, I flew this one really easy and hardly crashed it at all. After 43 flights, the rear motor is going out. It's pretty much stuck dead in the water. I cannot emphasize enough how much these things are really not meant to last. I am very surprised by people saying they have flown them for 100+ flights.

last edit:

So, after just under 2 months of owning three proto X's, I've cannibalized 8 motors to keep flying. That's right. EIGHT MOTORS FAILED IN JUST UNDER 2 MONTHS. Although, to be fair, I do fly this thing several times a day. Hopefully, motor parts will be available soon.

product_title: Transformers Masterpiece Soundwave 2013 Exclusive
review_headline: Poor quality, recommend purchase of Takara version instead
review_body:
For a 200 dollars purchase, this is one big disappointment. When compare to Masterpiece Optimus Prime, Hasbro Masterpiece Soundwave seems like a poor knockoff. You will notice right away how much lighter and cheaper it feels compares to Masterpiece Optimus Prime.

Furthermore it has very bad paint apps which gradually scrape off over time. Not to mention Hasbro's poor quality control. For example, my figure's leg joints were put on the opposite way and had to be fix with a screw driver. Also due to the imprecise ratchet joints, this figure cannot stand straight, it either leans forward or backward. The solution is to rotate the legs 90 degree, but then that would expose the poorly painted side of the legs.

That aside, the cassettes are amazing though, so I would strongly recommend you to get the Takara's version of Soundwave instead and purchase the cassettes separately. Together they would also cost only about 200 dollars but you will get a much better Soundwave quality wise with a cartoon's accurate visor (red instead of yellow).

product_title: 5 x Upgraded 25C 3.7V 380MAH Battery For Hubsan X4 H107 Ladybird RC Quadcopter
review_body:
These batteries (380mAh) are 1.7 grams heavier and 7mm longer than the 240mAh battery supplied with the Hubsan X4 (240mAh). You can't really fit the cord plug/jack in the back of the copter with these batteries in (which throws off the weight-and-balance and aerodynamic form of the copter a bit). The agility response of the X4 is a tiny bit slower with the weight of these batteries added.

I broke my last propeller right when I was testing the life of one of these batteries but I got 5 more batteries now so I'm not gonna be worried about battery life. I imagine that the battery life is the same as other reviewers say. I don't know yet but you may only get 3 more minutes of flight out of these. If that is the case, considering the weight penalty, you'd probably be better off just buying 5 smaller ones.

When I plugged the Hubsan-supplied battery and USB charger into an iPhone 4 charger (the small charger: 5V, 1A), plugged into standard US 120 VAC house electricity, the battery would charge in 27.5 minutes. I imagine these batteries would charge in between 35 and 45 minutes.

On the product review of this product from another seller, someone had wanted to cut off the blue heat shrink to save weight (it only takes away 0.2 grams). However, he found that the advertised mAh capacity that the battery was being sold at was labled as such on the shrink wrap but on the inside was labled as lower. He seemed pissed and only gave a one star rating for the deception. I did not find this with these batteries (I could have them tested though). There is no printing at all. If its safe for the battery (with chafing and wear and such) and if it doesn't allow the battery to fall out, I'd recommend cutting the shrink wrap off. It seemed the battery was harder to stuff in the compartment than the original.

The shipment was fairly timely and all five were there.

review_headline: Great toy! I'd give it 4.5 stars
review_body: I don't understand the reviews on this toy. This toy takes time to put together, do not buy it as a last minute gift that needs to be put together RIGHT NOW. And consider your attention span as well as the attention span of whatever child you are thinking about buying this for and REALLY think about whether you are going to put this toy together by yourself or with the child you are buying it for. I'm pretty sure putting this together with more than one child of any age is a bad idea! I actually got this toy from a thrift store, read the Amazon reviews, and face palmed asking myself what I'd gotten myself into. This toy is incredible! It had already been put together several times before I bought it. I disassembled any parts that had been previously put together, grouped together all parts with the same part number,  and started assembly. I paid close attention to the instruction booklet as to part orientation and double checked after I finished each page and again after I finished each section but I finished the build in a little less than 2 hours and with the addition of a plank of wood nailed under the base plates, this toy is very sturdy. My kids are almost 4 and 5 and a half so they weren't old enough to help me with that long of a build but they had a blast playing with it the first time out and they were pretty rough with it. They knocked off various ramps but those are easy enough to put back on. We played with it again tonight for an extended period of time and this time there was only one piece that fell off. And I have to say I had a REALLY good time putting this thing together. It was like a puzzle but a lot more interesting, 3 dimensional,  and it made me and my kids happy when I was done. One major negative, the auto-lift is a complete and utter waste of time.  Cool idea but too slow for human beings. A sturdy hand crank so that they can compete to see how fast they can get a marble to the top would be so much better. Also,  this is an early version ofthis companies gears and they are poorly designed with sloping horizontal surfaces so the gears just slide around,  go over and under each other and stop working every 20 - 30 seconds.  I'll be taking the motor and gear section apart and redoing it with the better constructed gears they made later that I already own from another toy set. I do think it can be reconfigured for additional fun and I look forward to taking this apart and rebuilding it with my kids help when they are just a bit older.

product_title: Incan Gold: Quest for Riches in the Ruins
review_headline: Great for people who enjoy game theory
review_body:
This game is heavily game-theory based. I.e., you have to know your opponents and anticipate their moves, as everyone takes their turn simultaneously. This makes it a great game for up to eight players, as gameplay isn't bogged down by turn-taking. The dynamic is extremely simple, and it only takes a minute to learn how to play. If you made a misstep while learning, there is solace in the fact that the game will be over in 10 to 20 minutes and you can start afresh.

The only downside to this game is that the "decision cards" each player uses to decide whether to go onward in the game or go back to camp are a bit confusing. Almost every game we play, someone accidentally flashes the wrong card, and we have to decide whether to let them slide (which can then upset other players) or stick with their mistake (which can throw off the whole game, since it's impossible for other players to anticipate the move of a player who made his or her move mistakenly). Hammer home the difference between the decision cards before the beginning of play and you should be fine.

review_body:
One of the hot toys for the 2012 Christmas season was Skyrocket toys Illumivor R/C Mecha-Shark, a very cool, light up and radio-controlled shark. What kid wants to control a car or truck when you can have a giant, jaw-chomping shark running around the house? Skyrocket is back this year with another cool R/C toy that kids will love.

The Illumivor Mecha-Pede is even creepier than the Mecha-Shark. Afterall, no one finds a shark in their house when moving an old box in the basement but we’ve all had a nasty, multi-legged centipede scurry across our feet when we least expect it. The Mecha-Pede is powered by four AAA batteries and the remote control requires one 9 volt battery. The Mecha-Pede can move forwards and backwards as well as right or left with the simple R/C controls. The figure has 14 sets of legs which skitter with movement but the toy actually moves on wheels on the bottom which makes it ok to use on shorter carpets but for ideal movement you definitely want to be on a harder surface like a tile floor or cement.

The real fun begins when you shut off the lights and all of those legs, antennae, forked tail, and ridges on his back light up. This gives the toy a truly eerie quality and if you hate bugs like I do, it makes the hair on your arms bristle! The toy is designed for kids ages six and up. It works quite well and there is an adjuster switch to make sure the toy moves straight. Very cool toy and another sure winner for Skyrocket toys!

This is my fourth rocket from Estes, the Maxi Alpha 3. The other three: Sky Dart, Far Side, and Blue Ninja builds went well. There are several quality issues with this build, some of which are not a big deal, but two diffidently are.
1. Part C did not fit into part G, (a ring fitting into a tube) but some simple sanding of part G took care of that, not a big deal.
2. Part F, a yellow spacer tube was not in any of the packages, it was totally missing. I had to make my own spacer out of a large dowel. Not too big of a deal, but still??
3. The engine mount assembly has TWO sets of measurements for the engine hook, the diagram shows 2 1/4 inches, and the descriptive part has it at 3 1/4 inches. Quote: "Cut a slit at 3 1/4 mark" per the instructions. I used the 3 1/4 inch mark (of course, it's the wrong one) and now because the engine hook sits deeper inside the engine mount tube, I CANNOT use the longer E-engines! That is why I bought this rocket!
4. I have emailed Estes twice about this,it's been over a week and no response. Very poor customer service!

I am very disappointed with the quality of the build (missing parts) and the poor instructions.
Phil

product_title: La Boca Game Board Game
review_body:
Number of players: 3-6
The game works well for any number of players.

Time: 40 minutes
Even though players will sit out rounds, this game goes so quickly there is no time to get bored.

Play: In this game, randomly selected pairs of players work cooperatively to build a three-dimensional structure using blocks. Each player can only see a two-dimensional picture of their side of the structure. Players earn points for completing the structure quickly. Each player gets a chance to play with every other player twice, and the player with the most points at the end wins.

Review: This game is fast-paced and fun, even for people who claim not to like spacial reasoning problems. Players end up developing strategies for building the structures quickly and deciding what information needs to be passed to their partner quickly. Once this gets too easy, there is a second difficulty level (which adds another block) to keep the game challenging. Because the structures must be completed in less than two minutes, there is a minimum of waiting around for other people to play. The nature of the game is such that you can't tell who is winning until the end, and it's enjoyable even if you lose.

product_title: Bandai Tamashii Nations D-Arts Black Zero Megaman X Action Figure
review_body:
First, Black Zero =/= Nightmare Zero. Second, 'nightmare' was an accurate title after the experience I had with it. Third? Aaauuuggh!

OK, so, D-Arts Black Zero is just that, a black repaint of D-Arts Zero Ver.2, with a bonus face plate depicting a very manga-esc winking face. If you already have Ver.2 Zero and prefer red over black, then pass this one up, because it's the same figure. It didn't deter me, since I love the series and this character.

However, this one didn't feel as sturdy as the red Ver.2. His knees and elbows felt loose and made posing him a chore, his neck was so stiff that it felt like it would snap off if I wasn't super careful, his hair felt like it was liable to just fall off during posing, and I found it impossible to disassemble any of the swords. The instructions clearly depict that the beam sword parts and the bottom of the hilt come off to allow easier gripping of the weapon, as well as the addition to 'sheathing' one of the spare swords at his back. As per usual, the figure came with multiple replaceable hands for both the left and the right hands; two closed fists, two dynamic hands and two hands for either giving Zero's iconic thumbs up or for gripping his weapons. The fists and dynamic hands pop on easily, but the other two have significantly smaller ports than the bit used to hold them on; I suppose it's to allow better hold for when weapons are held (and the third dynamic saber slash is heavy), but it's very difficult to put them in in the first place. A grown man had difficulty, people. And lastly, the right forearm. It doesn't stay on, at least on my figure. The arm cannon part was what the figure came assembled with, and that, as long as the left forearm, fit just fine. The right forearm will not connect to the right arm -incidentally, it fits perfectly on the left's arm. Because of this, I had to settle with poses featuring the arm cannon. Personal preferences aside, if a figure comes with interchangeable parts, it's fair to assume they should fit, right?

Positives, it is a very nice-looking figure, it can be posed in a very wide range of poses, its legs and feet are nice and sturdy and handle the back-heavy hairpiece fine, and the face plates are a snap to swap out. It has a lot of neat accessories (when they work), and the other D-Arts effect parts work just fine with this one. Design-wise, it would be my favorite of this line, especially since the repainting didn't just stop at the red-to-black, Zero's gold parts received a bit of a tarnished 'white-gold' look, and the saber went from blue to violet in the transition. Personally, I would have liked a violet gem on the helmet and red eyes, but the rest of it more than makes up for it. It looks sweet and right at home on my shelf.

I can't let the faults I experienced drag the score down too far, since it is a nice figure all-in-all. The cons made it weaker than I would've liked, but the pros helped it stay afloat, so it gets a solid three stars from me.

This screwdriver is a nice toy copy of the one in the TV series, has a nice weighty feel to it, good strong green light and some nice sounds. But. Yes I have a few niggles with it. Secondly, when the clamps are open you have to press the red button at the bottom of the base to make the green light go on, the original button does not work when the clamps are open. On top of that the little flap that covers the red button is kind of flimsy and ours just hangs open all the time now. If I was to add anything I would ask that the green light also emit from the middle of the device like in the TV series, that is after all what the Doctor is staring at half the time whenever he's using the screwdriver.

product_title: LEGO Lord Of The Rings 79005 The Wizard Battle
review_body:
I always appreciate it when Lego produces small, affordable sets that depict recognizable scenes and include new minifigures. In these respects, Wizard Battle is a great small set because you get two figures--Gandalf without his hat, and Saruman the White. Both of these characters are also available in bigger sets, but at $12, this is a great way to get them on the cheap.

And this set is really just about the minifigures. The build itself is very simple--just a throne and Saruman's palantir (which looks great with the Eye of Sauron in it), but it evokes Isengard and the scene from the movie quite well because of the black angular pieces. My only criticism of this and other recent Lego sets is the inclusion of action features that don't really add much. Although this is a small set, we get 2 action features: a flick rod feature that lets you eject Saruman from his chair, and a knob that spins the palantir around. Both work well, but the chair ejection feature really just enables you to faceplant Saruman onto the floor, and seems ill-suited for depicting a wizard duel. The flick rod is also tan colored, and detracts from the rest of the throne when Saruman isn't seated in it.

The spinning palantir is another useless feature, unless you want to give Saruman and Gandalf carousel rides. Sometimes, a little imagination is best, instead of forced action features.

product_title: Fisher-Price Little People Growing Garden and Farm Stand Playset
review_headline: Great Addition to the Little People Village!
review_body:
I got this to put next to the Little People Happy Sounds Home and my 21 month old daughter loves it! The set comes with a girl, a pop up worm, windmill, farm stand, lettuce, carrots, buttons to pop up the veggies in the ground, a watering pump, and a hose to "water" the garden. She loves the worm that when you sit him on one of the sections for the veggies in the farm stand, he pops up from the apples. I love that the set is interactive in that you can push the water pump and the sunflowers pop up in 3 increments and when pushed again, they go down, she can "water" the veggies and see them pop up, spin the windmill, and she can pretend to run the farm stand. I also like that the buttons and water pump teach cause and effect to the child and also helps teach the process of how food grows in the garden.

My only very minor complaint about this set is that sometimes the 3 buttons to pop up the veggies gets stuck. I do wish that when you press the buttons that the veggies stayed up because as soon as you let the button go, they go back down. But we love this set and it makes a great addition to our Little People village!

Accessories are good, it comes with a different set of legs for flight mode, a second head (that honestly looks a lot better), and the standard weapon complement. The flight wings attach instantly to the back but can be removed.

Aries is light and easy to pose with a stand, has the ability to plug into one although I am just using the generic Act 3 which works well.

The mobile suit is very photogenic and overall I am very very satisfied. Entirely possible that I'll be getting another to act as a wing man, for right now I'm using it as a Noin stand in alongside the Tallgeese.

product_title: Firefly: The Game
review_headline: The most fun strategic board game I've ever played!
review_body:
Though an extremely card heavy game (like 13+ decks!), the Firefly board game is an absolute blast! It's thought provoking, creative, and thrilling. It's also competitive, but easy for anyone (and I mean EVERYONE) to get a hang of. Play times are long, but the game doesn't try to hide that. Actually, the challenge card (stating the objectives of that particular game) tell you the estimated play time right on them — usually between an hour and two. Expect your first few games to be a bit longer (our first was 4+ and we didn't even finish!). Reading the entire manual (don't worry, it's not at all dry!) before hand will help speed up the process and you'll learn to how to move the game along faster between turns. And make sure, especially if the first game is played just between a husband and a wife, that both parties read the rules to avoid extreme frustration! (If not both, at least make sure the wife is the one who knows them =P). As the wife in my situation, I can say with confidence that this is a valuable tip for your marriage! The rules are plenty and sometimes a challenge; there are some minor, rare situations that my husband and I still aren't clear about handling. But at that point, we just establish a house rule!

Also, as a female, I recognize that a lot of women (not all) aren't into strategic board games. A few of the girls in our group of friends are definitely like that. But this game has proven an exception, especially if someone has watched Firefly and Serenity! Comparing the Firefly game to other intense board games I've played, these are some of the main points: it's more mentally stimulating than Risk but you don't need to have a mind for war tactics to win; it's more exciting that Settlers and you don't depend so much on luck; there's a lot more going on than in Small World, but it's not just about fighting the other players to win — it's more about beating the game; a race to win the challenge first. You can be a passive or an aggressive person, a peace-keeper or combat-oriented, yin or yang — I haven't yet found someone who didn't enjoy this game!

I bought it for my husband for Christmas and we played almost every night for nearly a month! Really, this is so much fun. You'll find yourself searching for some of the best (or your favorite) characters from the show just to make the most amazing crew. There is some element of luck, but as I said earlier, MUCH less than most games; really, luck only comes into play for your dice roles and drawing cards. The game is much more about efficiency and knowing how to work your jobs. Before long, you'll be working the 'Verse like you've been doing it for year! A great party game for an evening in--I can't wait to get the expansion!

Be sure to buy a plastic dinosaur with the game! And definitely go online and print off some sheets of Firefly's Chinese profanity!

product_title: LEGO Creator Expert 10243 Parisian Restaurant
review_headline: LEGO's Parisian Restaurant - Ooh la la!
review_body: LEGO's newest of the modular buildings, their Parisian Restaurant, is an absolute delight. Both the interior and exterior are loaded with the kind of detail dear to the LEGO fan's heart. Built to line up with the other buildings in the Modular series, it has three floors. The first has inside and outside seating and a complete kitchen, the second has an apartment with a Murphy bed that folds into the wall, and more exterior seating, and the top floor has an artist's garret complete with easel and finished paintings. I really enjoyed the intricate building components, especially the window designs and top floor medallions. LEGO has gotten more and more detailed with each Modular building they produce, and I appreciate finding new ways to combine various bricks for different effects. I'd say that the Parisian Restaurant, along with the Palace Cinema, are now my two favorite Modular buildings, and the restaurant is a great addition to the 1930's-ish downtown that the buildings can be combined to create. There are also five minifigs that come with the set, including a young man proposing to his girlfriend with a gold ring. There's even a nifty little motor scooter. I'm very happy with this set and recommend it highly (although you'll get a better price going through the LEGO website or store, rather than ordering on Amazon!).

product_title: Radiometer
review_headline: Wanted one of these since I was a kid!
review_body:
When I was about 13 or 14, I saw one of these sitting on a shelf at a friend of my mothers home. Her husband showed me what it was and moved it into a sunny spot so I could see it spin. At that moment I wanted one for myself! Fast forward a couple decades and I'm walking through a store full of old vintage toys. That trip made me wonder if I could find some of those same old toys online so I did a bit of searching. One of the recommendations caught my eye as soon as I saw the picture!

I'd always assumed these were fairly expensive so seeing the low price made it a no brainer for me. I am very pleased with what was delivered. It's definitely not a children's toy and should not be handled by them. It's fairly fragile and would not stand up to being tossed about.

It took a bit of experimentation but I finally found a nice sunny window in the house where it could sit. It definitely needs direct sunshine for best results. At the best time of day, it whirls quickly and works exactly as expected. I'll probably pick up a second one to have at work. I work with a lot of techy, nerdy people and it will be quite the conversation piece.

With no prior RC flight experience, I found Sky Viper to be fairly easy to learn to fly inside with sensitivity turned down and just now making outdoor flights with sensitivity turned up. Definitely better to learn to fly this $45 RC copter than paying $100 for a flight simulator program or buying a more expensive $500-$1,000 copter and crashing and damaging while learning to fly RC copters. When you learn to fly this copter, you can transition to a more expensive copter with camera and stabilized Gimbal and GPS. This is a great learning toll for public school science and technology classes where students can receive STEM classes disguised as a fun RC model plane class which actually teaches kids about the science and engineering needed in the aviation world. I encourage public schools to use teaching tools like this Sky Viper to create excitement for STEM classes.

review_body:
Has every single check mark of fake as noted on the official rainbowloom's site.
Sharp edges. No red arrow. No embossed logo on blue holding pieces. Spelling and grammatical errors in manual.

Everyone who has one of these purchased through Amazon's sellers needs to check the official rainbow loom PDF on how to spot a fake.
I'm not just being overly careful here. There's a number of shortcuts to be made in the manufacturing of plastics that can obviously include the use of lead to make shiny colors.
These are bands our kids are keeping in contact with their skin for extended periods of time.

Check yours and file a complaint with Amazon if need be.

product_title: Bandai Tamashii Nations Sailor Moon S.H. Figuarts Action Figure [Resale Editon]
review_body:
I received Sailor Moon here for Christmas. As a die-hard fan of this series, at first I was thrilled. I got the first edition run, which comes with two extra faces. However, when I opened the box and tried to play around with the posing options, I was really disappointed by what I found. You are supposed to be able to change Sailor Moon's face by removing her bangs, and then the face plate beneath it. However, in my model the bangs are stuck so tightly in I can't pry them off. I can't even get my nails into the crack, so sadly I can't change her faces. That's a huge disappointment, since she comes with so many face options. (By comparison, I also have Sailor Mercury and have no trouble removing her hair and faces.)

Also, some of her hands don't fit. When you remove the hands she comes equipped with, you see that there is a tiny peg at the end of each wrist. Her extra hands have tiny holes on their undersides so you can slide them onto the pegs. However, the holes on some of the hand options are too small. I can't get them to fit into the holes on the hands, and I'm afraid of breaking the pegs off entirely if I try to force them.

I was really disappointed with my figurine. Overall, the modeling and paint job on Sailor Moon is really nice, but due to these issues she is not nearly as customizable as the pictures would suggest. Maybe I was just unlucky and got a defective model.

product_title: Snap Circuits Extreme SC-750
review_headline: Contents seem ok but box was incomplete.
review_body:
Package arrived on Christmas eve but the lower half of the box was missing. The contents are sealed in two cellophane packs and appear to be complete but without the full outer box the components and parts will end up scattered once I break the cellophane seal. This is so disappointing as it is normal to store a game or a play set in its original box. I tried to contact the seller about this but the auto-options were limited...either return for refund with postage at own expense or return due to missing part then have postage reimbursed upon receipt and then wait for a new set to be sent. I only want the missing box so it hardly seemed worth it especially as we wanted it in time for Christmas and it took two weeks for the first order to arrive.
Given the cost of this I feel let down.

product_title: Furby Boom Figure (Straight Stripes)
review_headline: Greats for kids annoying for parents
review_body:
My 9 year old daughter loves this toy. She likes playing with it and the interaction between the toy and the player is nice.

The toy is very loud and annoying if you are not the one playing with it. There is no on/off button. The way to turn it off is by putting it to sleep by pulling its tail. Then the toy powers down.

You need the ipad application to truly enjoy this toy. One of your ipads need to be dedicated to Furby when you child wants to play with it. You can download a free app and this app syncs with your Furby. Then you can hatch new eggs, have new virtual Furbies, take care of your Furby and find out about its health status etc.

2) teaches how to follow along, and how to interact one toy with another. Teaches cause and effect.

Cons:

I would have returned it except for that it was his main "big" gift and I could hardly do that to the poor kid. review_headline: Looks pretty simple, but the curves and circles make this a fun challenge

The Leaning Tower of Pisa was probably my 20th MetalEarth 3D model I built and the curves and circles made this a difficult, yet fun challenge to build. The railing parts were very flimsy and delicate, which made the curve less perfect, but once the tabs are in place you can bend them for a better fit. The main core of the model was very sturdy and was on of the most rigid models I have built to date.

A tip for this model is to match all the seams so they all line up in a single line. Figure out which side you want displayed and place this seam in the back. Plan ahead for this part and do not bend or twist the tabs until you have figured this placement. It's a pain to undo the tabs once they are twisted or bent.

product_title: Takenoko Board Game
review_headline: Takenoko Review by Dad's Gaming Addiction
review_body:
Takenoko: 2-4 Players, Ages 8+, Average Play Time = 45 Minutes

Highly thematic doesn’t begin to describe “Takenoko”. The kids and I were simply blown away by the look and feel of the components. Of course, the panda figurine was the star of the show and even attracted the fourteen year old, Carolyn, to come over to the table. The rules were laid out well and the player boards really helped to keep everyone organized. There was a little bit of a learning curve, though most of it seemed to revolve around what a player could (and most probably should) do at any point in time…having a lot of options served to confuse the youngest a bit, but he quickly got the hang of things.

Along those same lines, there is a ton of strategy to consider while playing. Having three different ways to score points (via the three objective card types) really affects the way the game can play out, as not everyone will always be going after the same objectives as you. The gardener objectives, for example, task players with growing bamboo so many spaces high on a cluster of plots. The panda objectives, on the other hand, encourage players to eat said bamboo. These conflicting objectives can set players back a bit if they end up fighting over a particular area. The plot objective cards simply task players with building plots in a certain color scheme and shape, so that particular objective type is a tad less conflicting. Some colors are more rare than others too, so there’s that to consider as they appear during the game.

There’s also a little bit of randomness going on at the same time, though I wouldn’t consider that a bad thing in this case. Players are limited to strategies based on the objective cards they draw. If they draw gardener objective cards that all point to a particular color, for example, they’ll be forced to focus on that or run the risk of not scoring anything at the game’s end. The weather die further adds to the chaos, granting some type of random ability or action. To be fair, I did find the action useful most of the time, no matter what I happened to roll. If I rolled a storm and wasn’t focusing on devouring bamboo, I could instead play the panda offensively and devour bamboo I knew that other players were trying to build up to satisfy a gardener objective.

Overall, the kids and I really enjoyed playing “Takenoko”. It’s got just enough of a learning curve to be interesting, but is easy enough for younger kids to get the hang of with the assistance of an adult. There’s a lot of strategic depth in “Takenoko”, so there’s no shortage of thinking required in order to pull ahead of the competition. The fact that the game is pretty and well themed is just icing on the cake. I highly recommend this game to both families and hardcore gamers alike. “Takenoko” is easily one of my favorite games of all time.chaos, granting some type of random ability or action. The active language play can also be explored with the homes involved like, "What is the house like, what color is the door, who do you think lives there, where is the house," etc... product_title: MindWare Trebuchet by Keva
review_body:
got this for my 5 year daughter knowing full well it needed full assembly with glue. she loves building things and was right there helping me put it together. complete assembly from opening the box to firing for the first time was about an hour and a half. we were able to cut some time because we would glue some pieces together for one part, set them aside and glue pieces together for another part, and then be able to go back to the first for more gluing.

as far as firing, it does take a lot of practice and playing with. we used the change from one of her piggy banks as counterweight and it works very well. as far as projectiles to use, we've found that the balls it comes with are pretty useless as they are essentially painted ping pong balls and are far too light to get any decent distance. messing around with her other toys, i did find that the smaller bouncy balls you can get from vending machines work very well; they're a nice size and have a decent amount of weight to them, and they are, so far, non-lethal (but some barbie dolls have learned to hide when the war machine comes out).

a very nice project for a parent and child - girls included - and you get a fun toy to enjoy together.

product_title: Firefly: The Game
review_headline: Prepare for session that's long, but worth it.
review_body:
In the spirit of the much-loved yet short-lived tv series, you are the captain of a Firefly class spaceship, trying to earn an honest (and not so honest) dollar cruising the 'verse. Taking on jobs, ferrying passengers and cargo (both legal and illegal) from world to world, all while keeping your crew happy and avoiding entanglements with both the Alliance and the dreaded Reavers.

Okay, straight off the bat I'll say that the advised play time of about 2 hours for this game is extremely under-estimated. Our own session (of 3 players and following the recommended story option) was still in full swing 4 hours after we started, and even given a good hour or so to get familiar with the mechanics of gameplay we could have been there for a couple more easily.

The game looks great, although the 'American Style' volume of pieces, cards, cash and tokens can seem a bit overwheliming at first. These are colourfully printed on good card and paper stock and the player pieces (4 Fireflys, 1 Alliance Cruise and 1 Reaver ship) are well cast with good detail. The board itself is of decent dimensions, although you'll be wanting a large size playing surface (dining table or thereabouts) to cope once everything is set up.

From a boardgame standpoint, the gameplay consists of players competing to meet the conditions of an overarching 'storyline' chosen from half a dozen existing ones. They do this by taking on jobs from a variety of characters to increase their cash, acquiring crew and upgrading their ship. Jobs usually involve transportation of goods from one location to another, and often (especially in the case of illegal jobs) require the resolution of events using dice rolls against three 'skill' values. All the while players must balance fuel reserves, arrest warrants, the number and happiness of their crew and their cash to keep flying. I wouldn't say there's anything particularly groundbreaking in the mechanics here, but there are some great ideasincluding the need to balance profit returning cargo and passengers with ship essential parts and fuel, and the way that crewmembers of a moral persuasion can become disgruntled if you take on illegal jobs.

From a Firefly fan standpoint there is plenty to recommend this game. It is absolutely packed with references to Joss Whedon's opus. All the major and many minor characters are here with some great touches (such as three seperate cards for Yolanda, Saffron and Bridget!). Successfully completing a job makes you 'solid' with the person who gave it to you, resolution events come on 'Aim to Misbehave' adventure cards, and the active player token is a cutout dinosaur (although the makers recommend you swap this for a real plastic dino). :)

If you're neither a fan of the show, or of American style games with involved rules and more pieces than you can shake a stick at, this is probably not the game for you. But if you are a fan of one and don't mind the other, or better yet a fan of both, then this game is an absolute must. It promises hours and hours (so many more hours than the makers expected!) of fun and entertainment for the big damn hero in all of us.

product_title: Daron Flying Skyhawk on a String
review_headline: Not too shabby. Will delight a young aviation buff.
review_body:
This Flying Skyhawk On a String feels cheaply made and is a little short on detail, but it is colorful and functions decently. The instructions leave a little to be desired, and I suspect some people will misread/misunderstand them and be (unduly) disappointed in the toy's functionality as a result.

First, you have to assemble it and apply the included decals. This takes about 3 to 5 minutes.

Then, you have to mount one of the included swivel mounts to your ceiling with three screws. This part is a bit frustrating, since I was hoping installation wouldn't require a drill and screw mounts. So you have to be pretty sure about where you want to mount it, and then once you do, you'll have a length of fishing line dangling there semi-permanently (fortunately, you can at least unhook the plane to save your head from bumping into it). This is one of the main reasons I deducted two stars. It should be possible to unhook the fishing line from the mount, so that you can leave the mount screwed into the ceiling without having a dangling line. Instead, to remove the line, you'll have to unscrew the mount--leaving behind three holes in your ceiling.

Once the mount is screwed into the ceiling, you hook on the plane, turn it on, and give it a push in a \\"clockwise direction.\\" Here is where the instructions feel most confusing (another reason I deducted stars). Since it's hanging overhead, I bet most people will think of \\"clockwise\\" as moving in a circle from left-to-right AS YOU LOOK UP AT THE FLIGHTPATH. But actually, they mean clockwise AS YOU LOOK DOWN (FROM ABOVE) AT THE FLIGHTPATH. Of course, trial and error will fix it. After two minutes of watching it fly in a pathetically angled (almost sideways) attitude, I tried pushing it in the opposite direction and suddenly it was flying beautifully.

A final word of caution: You'll need about a six foot diameter UNOBSTRUCTED space for this to fly. Since we have a ceiling fan in our daughters' small bedroom, it was tricky but we found one corner where it could fly without hitting the wall or the ceiling fan (though the fishing line swings unnervingly close to the latter). And as the plane flies, ours emits noticeably whirring as well as a rattling noise. I would expect a toy this simple to function more quietly (yet another reason I deducted stars).

All in all, not a bad purchase if you have a budding aviation buff, like my one-year-old daughter, who squeals with glee when she sees a plane. You get what you pay for and this is adequate, but some more detail, a detachable fishing line (from the mount), and less rattle as it flies would make it substantially better.' small bedroom, it was tricky but we found one corner where it could fly without hitting the wall or the ceiling fan (though the fishing line swings unnervingly close to the latter). product_title: Monster High Password Journal 8
review_headline: My daughter loves it!!! Don't be afraid of the bad reviews.
review_body:
I got this for my six year old and she absolutely loved it. She is a monster high junkie so when I saw it was LESS expensive that the same one in just plain pink I had to get it even though all the reviews on it being unable to open after the password was set were there for me to read.

Well she was able to set it up all by herself! She loves the feature that allows her to record a greeting for when the password given is incorrect. Hers says. "Nice try brother..now get lost!"

Now I do believe that the trick to making sure no one gets locked out of their dairy is to make the password one word and something simple. It may seem like it defeats the purpose or takes the fun out of it but lets be real, it's more of a novelty item than a real technologically capable device that is going to recognize a lengthy or difficult command.

So after I read the reviews I explained to her it had to be something simple and she just uses the letter of her first name and it opens up every time without issue.

She really enjoys this and it was well worth the money spent in my opinion. She loves that she can record greetings and she love love loves the "magic pencil" and being able to write invisible entries. the only thing I think would be better is if they sent a replacement one because that's a big part of the charm of this toy and anyone with kids knows that it is going to be the first thing to get misplaced.

Hope this helps anyone on the fence.

product_title: Anki DRIVE Starter Kit (Previous Version)
review_headline: Great concept -- cars are great. Software is frustrating to the point of wanting to take a hammer to the cars.
review_body:
Okay, the cars whiz around the track with amazing intelligence. That part is great. Shooting and disabling the enemy (i.e. wife and daughter) is great. Think laser tag with little cars. They shoot invisible beams at each other (actually calculated by your Ipod or Iphone) and disable each other while whizzing around the track. HOWEVER, the game concept is stupid. It appears that the designers of the software got stuck in the "power up and attain magical abilities" video game paradigm. In theory this sounds great. Here's the theory: as you play and win, you get points. You can trade the points in for upgrades to your cars. These upgrades include powerful armor (that makes you harder to kill), stronger weapons to counter armor, and the ability to do U turns and sudden stops. I've got to admit the U turns and stops are cool.

Apparently the game theory is that serious gamers will buy the cars, upgrade as much as possible, and then compete with each other. But as I explain below, this theory makes the game NOT FUN for families or other casual players. At $200, plus $70 per extra cars, this is a lot of money for something that's frustrating.

So what's the problem? The software designers forgot this isn't a video game where you're playing against a computer AI. (You CAN play against AI controlled cars, but that's not a lot of fun compared to playing real people.) The problem is that you can't remove "fixed" special weapons from the cars, and you can't remove armor. For example, to start, we had three cars, two whose special "fixed" weapons are tractor beams, and the third whose special weapon is a shield. The tractor beam slows down the car in front so you have a better chance of shooting it. The shield lets you take a lot of hits without being disabled. It quickly became clear that whoever had the shielded car had a huge advantage over the 2 cars with tractor beams. You could basically shoot the shielded car forever without disabling it. As you can imagine, this caused some bad feelings! We tried to compensate for this by saying that the weakest player always got the shielded car. But this was a lame solution.

The obvious problem to the upgrade model is that 1) someone gets more points, 2) they upgrade, 3) this gives them a big advantage so they get still more points, and 4) they win more games get more points, upgrade more, etc. So they basically run away from the competition and become unbeatable. For example, our sneaky daughter, after racking up thousands of points, upgraded her armor a lot, making her car almost unkillable at the weapon levels of the other cars. The weaker cars had to use the dubious strategy of running around the track as fast as possible like small terrified rodents.

So essentially The designers created a game that isn't really a family game, or even a game for friends, because you can't level the playing field. They need to develop software that allows the players to reset the cars to defaults, where everyone is even. Or better yet, allow adding and removing weapons and armor without the stupid point system. This way it would be easy to level the playing field, or assign handicaps to better players by giving more abilities or weapons to poorer players (like poor old dad, who, after all, foots the bill). It would be fun to play a game in which one person said, "I want to play this game with no shields, a powerful weapons, and the ability to stop dead." And another player says, I'm going for powerful shields and the ability to U turn." It's sad that such a potentially awesome game is crippled by the myopia of the developers.

They did just release a software upgrade that does allow removing some upgrades. But the critical special weapons and armor is still not removable. I'll upgrade this review if they do a significant upgrade of the software.
