product_title: Madame Alexander 18" Urban Cowgirl - Favorite Friends Collection
review_headline: Such a Beautiful Doll! Amazing Quality! Very happy.
review_body: We purchased this doll for our 5 soon to be 6 year old daughters birthday. She specifically chose this doll off of the internet.  I showed her a few to choose from, an american girl doll made to resemble her, a my twinn doll 18" designed to resemble her and this madame Alexander that already somewhat resembled her. ha! She loved this one the most. She doesn't know she will actually receive her as a gift though.  I have taken the doll out of the box and inspected her to be sure she was in perfect shape before wrapping her for my daughters birthday. I also wanted to make sure her feet fit into the doll shoes that I have bought for her that are supposed to fit american girl dolls and other 18" dolls.  The shoes all fit perfectly. I've held up multiple pieces of doll clothing that all appear they will fit well. I did try a coat and little doll cowgirl hat on her to be sure they would fit and they fit her perfectly.  I would say her size is perfect and she will fit into all other 18" doll clothing and shoes.  I read reviews about her hair being a frizzy mess upon arrival, this was not the case for us.  The dolls hair is gorgeous and so soft, maybe finer than other doll hair however.  I have read online that you can mix fabric softener and water to make a nice solution that will moisturize and smooth unruly doll hair, so I plan to try that if her hair does ever become a mess.  The downfall to this doll are the boots.. VERY difficult to get off and not much easier to get back on.  I would really recommend taking them off and taking some strong scissors, sharp knife or wire cutters is what I used and just put a slit up the back of the boots to make them easier to take on and off. I did not cut all the way down the back, only to the top of the line of the heel.  MUCH BETTER now. I still have to push her feet forward by the heel a little with my thumb to get them into the boots but now I can push them in there without much effort.  They come off much easier and Iam not so worried I will break the dolls legs out of the joints. HOLD ON to the leg while pulling those boots off, they are tough. Otherwise the doll is gorgeous! GREAT quality. Her head moves in all directions, up down side to side. Her upper shoulder and chest are vinyl so that when you put a tank top on her you cannot see her stuffed body but her skin.  Her tummy and all under her chest line is a nice soft body and her legs are articulated (they go out to do splits,forward and back) so she can ride a doll horse or do gymnastics. Her arms are also articulated and move up down and around. Awesome feature. Her eyes open and close. Very Very happy with this purchase and I cannot wait to give her to my daughter.

"Pathfinder Adventure Card Game: Rise of the Runelords" is a new card game experience from Paizo Publishing that is designed to play like a traditional role playing game but without the need for a game master. Instead, the game itself largely creates the adventure that you and your friends will embark upon. A cooperative game, you and up to three others will search various locations for villains and encounter treasures, monsters, and various other items and perils along the way.

One mechanic that is really interesting here is just how cards function in the game. Each character gets a set of several cards from his deck to act as his hand. Theoretically, this would mean that characters with most cards in their hands are stronger- this is not necessarily so, as your deck also acts as your hit points. The more cards you hold in your hand, the less you have to lose if you take a hit point. It's a really fun and unusual mechanic that balances characters out nicely.

I have never played the "Pathfinder" role playing game, so I cannot comment on how well it translates into this card game. As it stands, the base game is a lot of fun, and future expansions should only increase the variety and game play choices available. "Pathfinder Adventure Card Game: Rise of the Runelords" is not going to be for everybody, especially hard core RPG gamers. But for those of us who never really got into RPGs, it definitely scratches a certain itch.

product_title: Lionel Polar Express Remote Train Set - O-Gauge
review_headline: Love the train but first one was DOA
review_body:
If this review was about Amazon customer service It'd be 5 stars for sure. First the bad, I ordered it and got it before Christmas - yeah! Had it all wrapped up and ready. My son opened it on Christmas day and we set everything up, plugged it in and the lights came on, turned on the remote and then nothing.............. We called around and read reviews online and found out that some of the kits remotes do not work, so I tried calling Amazon on Christmas day. Their service department answered and sent me a new one to my doorstep on the 27th. The good, the second one worked like a charm.

Observations: Metal engine and pretty much all the other cars are plastic. Detail level is adequate but far from the best I've seen. Definitely a beginner set. Comes with a large Santa's sleigh bell (if you have seen the movie you know that it symbolizes the spirit of Christmas and can only be heard if you are a believer) that is not used on the train more of an ornament (well made). It also comes with 4 characters, the 2 train engineers, the conductor and the main kid character (not quite to scale but good enough). A small bottle of smoke fluid, a transformer and extra passenger car light bulbs. The sounds come from the coal car behind the main train, but is controlled by the remote. Unfortunately volume is not adjustable. The main engine has a working headlight and all the passenger cars are lit with silhouettes of passengers and puppets based on characters in the movie. I've ran the train full speed forward and backwards without any derailing. The smoke generator works really well and left my room with quite a bit of smoke after running it a while. The train set is easy to setup the fast tracks snap together intuitively and the transformer plugs into a straight section. Make sure you set it up close to an electric outlet.

Some Quirks: One hassle is the lack of an on/off switch. You basically need to plug and unplug the transformer every time you play. It should be easy enough to retrofit or connect to a switched outlet. The smoke generator can be turned on and off while the train is on but make sure you have fluid in the generator. The chugging switch that mimics the trains chug chug and idle steam sounds can also be turned on and off however you need to unplug/plug the transformer (reset the system) for it to take effect. Not sure why it was designed that way. It should just be a simple open/close circuit to turn on/off sounds. The last quirk is if you leave the power on but do not run the train with the remote for an extended period of time, the train goes into a sort of a sleep mode. The lights stay on but the train does not respond to the remote, so when you turn on the remote and try to run the train it won't work. At that point you need to unplug/plug the transformer (reset the system) for the set to work again. It is by design. The remote has its own on/off switch which is a nice touch.

The set uses a bit of power so you may need to upgrade the transformer if you add additional tracks or trains on the same track. When the train is in a turn, it slows down a little, press the horn/bell buttons, to add audio and it slows down even more. When the train is running slow enough turning on the horn sound around the curved portion of the track can bring the train to a halt due to the weak transformer. Usually I run it at mid-speed and the issue is less noticeable.

For me this train will serve as a Christmas decoration for my kids probably with a small village underneath the Christmas tree (not to scale), so I don't expect to expand this set much. For this purpose I think this it great. Ample details and functionality. For a complete town try the smaller HO or N scales.

product_title: LeapFrog LeapPad Explorer Carrying Case (Works with all LeapPad2 and LeapPad1 Tablets)
review_headline: Don't store games in it: will break screen if Dropped.
review_body:
I have an engineering background and this is a terrible design.
-Parent placed Leap Pad in protective gel case, then placed in this padded case made specifically for the Leap Pad. The gel case makes it a slightly more snug fit, but that isn't the design problem. One game was placed in the lid as designed. My child dropped it once and screen was broken.
--The lip of the games is a perfect stress-point that directly impacts the edge of the glass.
--Additionally, the strap is attached to the zipper pull. Anyone ever seen a zipper designed to hold two pounds hanging from it as it is swung around by a child? Didn't think so...
This case could be useful as long as it is NEVER used to store games and the strap was clipped off so it had to be hand carried instead of the zipper being torn.

This is one parent very frustrated that I buy two protective items for the particular device and it is still broken on the first day.
LeapFrog voided the warranty and is going to send me a replacement Leap Pad after I ship this one back to them at my cost.
Their design problem caused the break. Not a happy camper.

product_title: McFarlane Toys The Walking Dead TV Series 4 The Governor Action Figure
review_headline: READ THIS REVIEW BEFORE YOU GO AND GET A REPLACEMENT BECAUSE OF THE BROKEN HEAD!!!
review_body: Here is my review for the McFarlane Walking Dead Governor action Figure. Paint, the paint is sloppy in numerous places but in all the other places it's GREAT!!! Sculpt, the Sculpt on this guy looks a lot like David Morrissey, but then in other ways it doesn't. Articulation, the articulation is typical for McFarlane's Walking Dead figures, and as usual the hips suck at moving around. Accessories, he comes with the alternate eye patch head, a knife, a bigger knife, and his trusty pistol. The reason this review was short is because I wanted to explain how to fix the Broken head problem. First, run some hot water over the neck where the peg is stuck in the socket, next get needle nosed plyers (while the plastic is still warm) and pull the peg out of the socket in the neck, and last but not least, pop the eye patch head into the socket and run under cool water (to harden the plastic again). The thing about this teqnique is that you wont be able to use the regular head anymore, but i'm sure most people want the eye patch head on anyway. This teqnique should save you a lot of time sending it back and getting a replacement. (: (: (:

product_title: KidKraft 53227 Vintage Kitchen,Blue
review_headline: Nice kitchen...KidKraft could incorporate some electronics...
review_body:
First off my 16 month old has really enjoyed her kitchen. It is essentially all wood so it is extremely sturdy and I am quite confident it will last. The assembly wasn't too bad. I would say it took about 2.5 to 3 hours although I wasn't in a huge rush.
The white makes it look very clean...that will be hard to beat by other kitchens which my wife loves. :)
When my daughter went over my parents to play with the standard grandchild kitchen that has made it through a previous granddaughter we noticed a cool feature this model was lacking...electronics. My daughter is constantly trying to play with the remote, Ipads, kitchen radio, microwave, dehumidifier, or anything else that beeps or makes a noise or light flash when you push it. The grandparents had a fake radio and phone that made noises when you played with them. They also had a fake burner that lights up and makes a boiling/cooking sound when you put a pot on it. She loved those features.
So overall...I give the looks, craftsmanship, sturdiness 5 stars.
I give the innovation 3 stars...bumping the overall rating to 4 stars. I understand the electronics could be harder to incorporate into a wood model...but just a couple slight additions would be nice for the 2013 kid. We don't give our daughter electronics to play with...but they are hard to avoid in this day and age and she loves them unfortunately.

review_body:

If you live in the world of coloring books and one right answer, then avoid this toy. If you want to encourage a budding artist, engineer, sound artist, or architect, then get this toy and play with it. Don't look at the pictures of what someone else built, experiment with gravity, slope, cause and effect, speed, and whimsy. product_title: Lionel Silver Bells Train Set
review_body:
Pros:

1. Lionel Chief Remote (also a con) -- My son loves using it, esp. the horn!

2. FastTrack -- quick to put together and adds realism.

3. Railroad and Christmas Sounds/Music (also a con)

4. Die cast loco, and decent detailing/painting on all cars.

Cons:

1. Lionel Chief Remote -- if the remote goes (broken/lost/etc...) the loco will not run -- since it's tied to a unique frequency, I'm not sure if Lionel will/can replace the remote. Sure, you can wire it to a regular transformer, but it'll only run at full speed. The newer models of the Lionel Chief due out in 2014 will be Lionel Chief Plus which will allow you run on the remote + transformer properly..

2. Wow, the tender sounds are so loud, it rattles the tender car! It's honestly way to loud, sometimes to the point of distortion. It really should have had a volume control.

Other:
1. Never used FastTrack before, and while it's nice and kind of optically hides the fact of the third rail in certain angles and when you do see the third rail it doesn't look to bad at all (I'm more of a fan of S-Scale/American Flyer two rail track) but please note, it's really noisy/loud -- maybe there are tricks to dampen the noise, but as it is, it's loud.

2. A little too much green (all cars/loco are green) -- wish it had some more red/white color to the cars, but the paint scheme used on the cars are in good taste and complement the green cars.

It's a really nice set and would I buy it again, yes, if it was Lionel Chief Plus locomotive. Knowing what I know now, I wouldn't...lose the remote and the locomotive is useless even though the loco isn't broken.

product_title: NECA The Hunger Games: Catching Fire "Katniss and Peeta" Jigsaw Puzzle, 27 x 20", 1000-Piece
review_body:
So I like to start my reviews with the positives first. In that spirit, first I will say that this puzzle is a very pleasing piece of work. It features two stoic attractive young people, one male and one female with a bird of some kind (a woodpecker) bursting in flames behind them, apparently the inspiration for the name "Catching Fire." The two young people are wearing uniforms with little hexagons on them, which helps match up pieces. The pieces themselves are well-made and fit snugly together, although it is sometimes difficult to tell if one piece is an exact match or not. It works out in the end though.

One criticism I have is that there are just too many pieces. It took several days working about an hour a day for me and my two helpers (hey Lois and Maria, couldn't have done it without you!) to complete this puzzle. There are many similar looking pieces which makes it difficult to work out what goes exactly where. Also, the pieces are small and sometimes fall on the ground and you think it's lost and you look and look and can't find it. But then there it is under the chair. Otherwise, this was a very fun puzzle to complete.

Overall, I would do this again, but probably not with this same puzzle. I do recommend it for others, though. It was a very satisfying, if sometimes frustrating, experience.

product_title: Disney Advanced Talking Buzz Lightyear Action Figure 12" (Official Disney Product)
review_body:
It's got nearly everything from the films except Buzz's self awareness! The helmet opens, the wings pop out, the voice clips are great, and the karate chop and laser are just as expected! My three year-old boy had been begging me for a \\"bigger Buzz Lightyear\\" than his 4-inch tall toy he got for his birthday in May, and he definitely loves this figure...

but... it's not quite perfect. I noticed immediately, that the joints make it tricky for Buzz to stand on his own two feet - not impossible, just tricky. For the next issue, I'll grant my boy may be a bit rough on his toys, but I don't think he's in the top-ten percent of roughest kids. Nevertheless, he broke Buzz's head off in under seven hours. Clean off, as in decapitated. At least it was repairable (well, the second round of repairs seems to be holding up, still). By the time we noticed the head was off, one of the wing lights had stopped working properly, and by the next morning, less than 24 hours after taking it out of the package, the other wing light had also failed. This one is not something I am going to try to fix.

My boy still loves the toy (especially as long as he can blast his big sister with the laser!), but I will admit I had hoped it would be a bit more durable. I can't decide if the appropriate Latin takeaway would be \\"caveat emptor (leth the buyer beware)\\" or \\"cave toddler (beware of toddler)!\\"

product_title: Geomag, 30 Piece Starter Set, Assorted Color
review_headline: Comparison of Geomag and CMS Magnetics Sets
review_body:
I purchased both the Geomag 30-pc Starter set and the CVS Magnetics 108-pc Building Set at the same time, assuming they would work together. They do. Magnets are magnets, and they attract (or repel) other magnets no matter the brand. I'm happy with both products, and I hope they will help my 5 year old grandson develop his engineering skills. There are some differences between the two sets that I purchased, and I will note them in case it helps you when you are making your purchasing decision:

GEOMAG 30-PC STARTER SET: Comes with 13 rods, 16 spheres, and 1 plastic platform. The rods are about 2 1/4" long. It comes with visual instructions for making 9 different sculptures, but 8 of the sculptures require more rods/spheres than are included in the set. With this set alone, there aren't many things you can build. The plastic platform is not very useful at all. The strength of the magnets is excellent. The spheres are steel, the rods are yellow and orange. It comes packed in cellophane in a thin cardboard box, not really good for storing the set once it's opened.

CVS MAGNETICS 108-PC BUILDING SET: Comes with 66 rods and 42 spheres. The rods are about 1" long. It does not come with any instructions. The strength of the magnets is excellent. The spheres are steel, the rods are red and blue. It comes packed in a fitted case with storage for each rod and sphere, very good for keeping the set organized.

PLAYTIME: The rods in the GEOMAG set were longer, but 2 of the CVS rods coupled with 1 sphere were about the same size as a GEOMAG rod, so we could easily mix them together. So, with the CVS set we could make 33 rods of the same size as the rods in the GEOMAG set. If you buy the 30-PC GEOMAG set, I'd recommend you buy other sets to go with it because there's not much you can build with only 30 pieces. The 108-PC CVS set provided many more building options. One thing we discovered is that if you try to make yoursculptures too big, they became very unstable. The 1" rods seemed to hold out longer.

END RESULT: We'd recommend the CVS set because the storage case is awesome, and the smaller rods add to the stability of the structure you're building (and help keep the kids from becoming frustrated when it keeps falling).

review_body: First off I just noticed that there hasn't been a review done on this product in almost 4 years. With that pointlessly said I would like to go on to say that this has been one of the coolest things I've bought here on Amazon. It all started because my TV quit working and I took it apart thinking it might just be a loose cable but what I found was a couple blown capacitors. After looking at what it would cost to pay some to do it and the cost of just buying a new circuit board (power supply) I figured I could just replace the parts my self for pennies on the dollar. Problem was I have never soldered before. I picked this out for the learning process and it did everything I expected it to. It told me what's going on threw out the circuit board and how to solder and desolder components. It only takes about 60 seconds for the soldering gun to get up to heat, don't let it sit for to long or you can burn out the tip. It tells you about that in the directions which is set up like a class room textbook format. The soldering gun worked awesome, the only thing I would recommend is picking up some rosin flux to use as you're desldering or soldering. It helps the solder melt and flow really nice. I did this whole project without it but picked some up for my TV project. The flux made everything way easier. I am still using the soldering gun weeks later and have had no issues with it. I highly recommend this to any first timers that want to learn. Its very fun.

review_headline: Fine for my purposes, but not high quality work.
review_body:
I purchased this for use as a Dragonborn Barbarian, so I intended to repaint it anyway. However, I was somewhat put off by the shoddiness of the existing paint job. Parts of the armour are covered by the paint that was used for the skin, and there are metallic flakes on the head of the figure. In addition, the mould is heavily staggered, with extremely visible seams. This is most noticeable in three places:
1:The right arm, where staggering effects spine placement
2: The left hand, where the seam runs right through the fingers, splitting them at the staggering points
3: the base, where the seam running across its surface may effect structural integrity.
Salvageable, but only if you're willing to work at it.

product_title: LED Light Weight Magnifier with 5 Lenses 1x, 1.5x, 2x, 2.5x, 3.5x
review_headline: Fantastic aid for close, detailed work.
review_body:
UPDATE 04/29/2014: After about 4 months of occasional use, the LED light stopped working. The light is powered by 3 x LR1130 batteries and one of them had ruptured. I bought [[ASIN:B000W75GAK Maxell Watch Battery Button Cell LR1130 AG10 Pack of 10 Batteries]] to replace them. I had to bend the springs that hold the batteries in place, but the light fired up just fine. Another thing that happened is the little plastic piece that covers the switch fell off and disappeared. The switch works fine without it, but it doesn't look great.

ORIGINAL REVIEW 12/2013: I'm at a stage where I need 1.5 X readers for distances of 1 - 3 feet and something more for really fine, detailed work. I've tried more powerful readers, but they don't work well for me. I bought the professional Jeweler's Lighted Magnifier hoping that it would help with really close work.

So far, I'm only using the 3.5 X lenses and they allow me to see like I have bionic eyes! The frame is very light and comfortable and I can wear it for an extended period, if needed. The LED lights are fantastic for illumination, and they're even more effective because you can change the angle independent of the lenses. I've found myself using the lights as a flashlight to see into small spaces. The field of view is reasonable for such high magnification, although the depth of field is limited, as you would expect.

I'm very happy with this purchase.

product_title: Hobby Boss F-84F Thunderstreak Model Kit
review_headline: F-84F Thunderstreak by Hobby Boss in 48th scale, a build review.
review_body:
The F-84F Thunderstreak served in the USAF, a number of Air National Guard units, and a number of NATO allies. Its service life was mostly from 1954 to 1962, some being in service into the 1970s in Europe. There have been several model kits in 48th scale produced of the Thunderstreak. They are Monogram/Revell, Heller/Fonderie, Kinetic/Italeri, and this kit by Hobby Boss just released late October 2013. I received mine Nov. 2nd and did a build SFTB (straight from the box in modelers' terms) completed by the 19th Nov. This kit is the best of those available, though it is not without faults.

The good points about it are a mostly very accurate external shapes in profile and plan views, very smooth surface finish, finely engraved panel and rivet details, almost no molding flash, and no ejector pins in visible places.

Where this kit lacks is in other details that are lacking when contrasted to the exterior details. The nose gear well and intake splitter are seriously lacking detail; further they neither attach to each other properly nor fit into the fuselage halves properly. The nose gear and wheel are molded as one part which makes painting difficult and the wheel is not done correctly. The main gear wells are minimally detailed, are too shallow; though the main gear struts are reasonably well done, the main wheels are not at all correct in shape or details.

The instrument panel is quite good but otherwise the cockpit is minimally and incorrectly detailed; the ejection seat is too large for the scale and with average details. There are no cockpit details on the fuselage walls, the weapons sight is little more than a blob of plastic. The tailpipe is fairly good, but lacks the internal "sugar scoop" fairings.

There are a few detail errors on the fuselage: the suck-in doors are not correct for any of the three variations on the real Streaks; there are panel lines included that are only on the RF-84F Thunderflash (an error shared by the Kintic/Italeri kits); the gun bay hood aft panel lines are incorrect. Another significant error is that an in-flight refueling door is represented on the starboard wing; the Streak refueling door was only on the port wing.

There are two decal sheets, the main sheet includes options for two USAF Thunderstreaks, 51-9432 and 52-6675. The smaller sheet includes service badges and a decal for the instrument panel. The decals are in perfect register though the Insignia Blue shade is a bit too light.

There is one photo-etch fret that includes seat belts, external speed brake surfaces, and very nicely done spoilers; this is the only one of the 48th scale kits to have wing reliefs for the PE spoilers and, as such, are a very welcome included detail.

This first build was SFTB for purposes of posting a review of the kit as produced. There were no surprises in the build other than that the nose gear well and intake splitter would not fit without substantial filing and sanding; even then I had a difficult time getting the fuselage halves to close up without warping the ventral alignment. I did have to use a moto-tool to carve way a bit of the wing-fuselage mating surfaces to get the wings to fully insert into the fuselage. In every other case, all parts fit perfectly, assembly was straight forward without any issues. And, as this was a STFB build, I substituted no aftermarket parts.

All paints used were Testors Model Master enamels or Testers Buffing Metalizers; I used several mixes and shades of Metalizer to represent subtle differences in panels.

I elected to build the kit as 52-6675, primarily because the nose decal representing the anti-glare panel and nose livery was in one piece. The intent was to determine if that extensive decal could be made to conform to the fuselage contours. The short of it was, no, it would not conform and eventually disintegrated. One of the Monogram F-84F kits has decals with thesame livery, so I went to my decal stash and used the Monogram decals. All the other decals were applied with no problems. It is well to note that the decal instructions indicate "15 seconds" in water. In fact, that is true for the large sheet, but the small sheet requires a full 60 seconds in water before they will release.

This kit, with correct profile and plan, excellent and mostly correct external details, is by far the best of the Streak kits available as a starting point. The caveats are the lack of accuracy or details, especially so of cockpit and ejection seat, and in the case of the nose gear well and intake splitter, poorly fitting parts. Thus this kit begs for aftermarket resin and photo-etch parts to bring the interior details up to the standard of the exterior. In fact, I already have two more of these kits started and have beta releases of some resin parts to provide feedback to the manufacturer for fit into this kit.same livery, so I went to my decal stash and used the Monogram decals. product_title: 12 Days Card Game
review_body:
The game is great, well worth the money. The game's packaging is not. The packaging is befitting a $4 kid's card game from a chain store. I couldn't open the package without the thin cardboard tearing. Once inside, I found a cheap cardboard holder for the cards. Basically, if you care an ounce about your games, you'll need to arrange a separate, long-term solution for storing the game.

product_title: Tapple - Fast Word Fun For Everyone
review_headline: Simple, Fun and Challenging for All Ages …
review_body:
WHAT IT IS:
TAPPLE is a table-top game that keeps players on their toes by forcing them to provide answers starting with various letters within a brief time limit. The game itself is a plastic wheel/circle with individual letter tabs are attached to its circumference. The letters are in order and all letters are represented except U, X, Y and Z. In the middle of the wheel is a large button that starts/stops a 10-second timer. A storage compartment underneath the “wheel” stores a stack of topic cards with two topics listed on each side. The topics are color coded to indicate difficulty. An AA battery for the timer is included.

HOW IT WORKS:
The player designated to start the game pics a card, choses a topic from the card, states an answer and presses down the first letter of the answer (thus eliminating that letter from being used again in subsequent answers). The timer is pressed, giving the next player 10-seconds to provide another answer beginning with a different letter. This procedure continues until someone can’t provide an answer using an available letter within the 10 second time-frame. The last person to provide a successful answer wins the round and gets to keep the card. Reset bars on the inner rim of the “wheel” release the depressed letters for the next round. The overall winner is determined by the person possessing a designated number of topic cards.

WHY IT’S FUN:
First, it’s simple to learn. Second, it can be played by kids and adults. Third, the anxiety of the 10-second timer combined with the frustration of trying to find answers that begin with the remaining letters usually leads to people blurting out ridiculous/funny stuff before the timer goes off.

TAPPLE is a good family game that combines wit, memory and speed. For younger kids, it’s a fun way to reinforce the association of letter sounds. Another plus is that the game is self-contained with no loose parts (the cards are stored in the game itself).are stored in the game itself).

product_title: Disney Planes Franz Fliegenhosen Diecast Aircraft
review_headline: In the movie, one minute he's "Franz", the next minute he's "Fliegenhosen"!
review_body:
Franz is a big fan of Dusty Crophopper, and this unique character from Disney's "Planes" movie has a split personality! He's a German "aerocar"... in the movie, when he's in mini car mode, he goes by "Franz", but turns into "Fliegenhosen" when he's in plane mode! He's turquoise colored and pretty cool looking, but you need to keep one thing in mind... this 1:55 scale Mattel version does NOT actually convert from car to plane, while the 1:43 scale Disney Store model DOES transform from one to the other. We definitely wanted the Mattel version since that's the size of the rest of our grandson's collection, but we wish Mattel would've found a way to let him transform, even if they made it a "deluxe" model and charged a premium.

If you're wondering what "1:55 scale" means in actual measurements, Franz measures @ 3-3/8" from his front to his tail, has a wing span of2-7/8 ", and stands about 1-3/8"H at the top of his tail fins. Our younger son came into town for a Christmas visit early this year, so Grandpa & I went ahead and gave our older grandchild his gifts, which included the "Planes" DVD and as many of the characters as we could find. review_headline: Fun Surprise for X-mas or at End of Season
review_body:
I received this product to review on my blog. To use Hang’em and Hatch’em Eggs, simply remove from the packaging and place the eggs in room temperature water. The level of water should just cover the egg. It doesn’t say to do this, but I held them down to get the air out from under the egg shells. Let them sit in the water and the next day (within 24 hours) you should see cracks start to form on the shell.

My children wanted to help their little friends out so they started picking at the shells. We left the eggs in water for a total of three days, changing the water each day. They were a little slippery, but not slimy. There is material in the eggs that allows the toy to grow and contributes the slippery feel. Just grab the toy and remaining egg shell carefully. Rinse them off with room temperature water. Then lightly pat the animal dry.

The little friends feel like a hard rubber when they have dried. I thought the strings stayed with the animals, but they are just to hang the eggs initially on the tree. The animals can then be played with.

Each set comes with a polar bear, snowman, and baby penguin. I think the longer you keep the animals in water, which helps them get bigger, there can be a tendency for the colored areas to lighten up and fade.

product_title: Accoutrements Shark Attack Porcelain Mug
review_body:
There are a couple of things wrong with this cup. The least of them is the fact that the cup is very small--and the shark takes up most of the room in the cup--so there's hardly any room for liquid. I bought it so my kid could drink hot chocolate out of it, which is the only reason an 8-year-old would need a coffee cup. And you can hardly fit any in it.

But the real reason not to buy this cup is that MOLD GROWS INSIDE THE SHARK. Each time we used this cup, I cleaned it out thoroughly and put it in the cupboard. Upon taking it out again in a few weeks to use it again, mysteriously it had sticky, dried hot chocolate residue in the bottom. I would think, "That's odd," clean it out and let my son use it. But it happened time after time. Finally my husband was reaching into the cabinet to get something and was overpowered by a smell. He discovered it was the cup--with the sticky brown residue even though I DEFINITELY confirmed it was clean as a whistle before storing it. Obviously hot chocolate was leaking into the shark, then taking its time to leak back out again...and it smelled like mold. Grosses me out to think how many times my kid drank out of this. Do not buy this. Too late for a refund for me, I'm sure--but I just want to make sure you don't make the same mistake I did.

product_title: Transformers Generations Deluxe Class Autobot Skids Figure
review_headline: Looks awesome and is better after fixing the legs.
review_body:
I found mine at a local store and thought he looked like one of the coolest Autosbots and picked him up without a second thought. However he has some flaws in the articulation department.

First off, the pieces on his back make him top heavy, so he's always falling backwards. This wouldn't be a big problem if:

Secondly, he can't move his legs forward. There is a piece of detailing at the top of his legs that meets the torso which prevents them from moving. So without that being able to even out the weight, the figure can't stand up much without something behind it.

The feet also have a bit of detailing that prevents the foot from moving up. It can move pretty much every other direction but up. Same with the shoulders. They're hindered by the car doors. The sad thing is, the articulation points are there, they are just hindered by detailing.

UPDATE: As it turns out, it's a common mistake on this figure that the hips are put on backwards. All you have to do is pop them off the ball joint, slid the hip off the leg and place it on the other leg. After that, Skids is good to go in the leg department. Going to bump this up to a 4 out of 5 now.

Highly recommend, especially to families with a school-age child learning Spanish when Spanish is not spoken regularly in the home. Right out of the box there was a decent amount of puzzle dust I thought. About 20 pieces were slightly bent when I first laid them out which wasn’t a big deal. Pieces were glossy and shiny in light. I had to balance too much light and glare with not enough to see the pieces. A few pieces were separated on a corned by the end as I kept trying some of the green pieces over and over again. Lots of 4 “out” pieces that are small are hard to determine where they fit.

Overall I enjoyed the puzzle and am going to glue and mount it as a Christmas gift for a relative who likes Vermont and covered bridges.

product_title: Innovation
review_headline: Seemed to have potential, but too many lopsided games
review_body:
Innovation is pretty quick to learn and doesn't take long to set up, and there is often enough strategy involved to satisfy the more hardcore gamers who want to be asked to think. However, it seems to have some game balance issues that prevent me from giving it more than three stars.

One (usually) wins Innovation by racking up a certain number of achievements, and the most common way of attaining these achievements is by racking up a certain number of points in the scored card section. The catch is that one doesn't spend the points scored to earn the achievement, and only one person can get the achievement for a certain number of points. That means that if one person can get a few points ahead on scoring, the same person can easily get the 10 point achievement, then the 15 point achievement, then the 20 point achievement, etc. all while the players just slightly behind are almost completely prevented from making any progress toward victory despite scoring points, improving their hands, etc.

Yes, there are cards in the game that can disrupt the leader's streak and restore something besides frustration to the other players, but one has to draw the right card, have enough of the icon required by that particular card to use it effectively, etc., which means that it can easily be a longshot even with intelligent play. If you like a lot of a game's outcome to hinge on "Hail Mary" plays and occasional wild swings of fate, then you may well enjoy Innovation a great deal. If, however, you prefer a bit more certainty that intelligent strategy will be rewarded with at least a noticeably closer game, you might find Innovation a bit frustrating. Of the games of Innovation I've played so far, I've found only about 1/3 of them to be balanced enough to be truly interesting, and that's with all of the players being experienced strategy gamers. Thus, I find it hard to recommend for the true strategy game fan.

product_title: Thames and Kosmos Biology Tk2 Scope
review_body:
For a student in 4th-9th grade, I thought this was pretty good microscope. I bought it in 2010 for my 8 year old niece, and last year I had a chance to use it with her for a science project. Being a professional microbiologist and a college professor, I had my reservations as to how well I would be able to see the specimens. But for the price, I was actually surprised. We were able to see water protozoa, soil crystals, and blood cells. One reviewer remarked that the 40X objective doesn't work, but to be honest, the 40X is known as a high-dry objective and it doesn't give a very clear image on any microscope. I don't let my college students use it on the Nikon scopes we have, but for children, they will still be able to see the image fairly well. I'm glad I bought this for my niece and she's getting excited about science.

I also liked that the scope came with supplies so she can make her own slides and stain them. The instructions are easy to understand and they'll be able to use it right out of the box. Tell them to keep the objectives clean with the lens paper--don't use paper towels or they'll scratch the lenses.

product_title: NSI 3D Hanging/Glowing Solar System
review_headline: Complete waste of time and money.
review_body:
This set is completely disappointing. For starters, the flimsy design has you hang each planet from the ceiling with string and tape. Yes, tape. I had doubts that this would hold up the sun, which is the heaviest. Even though I double taped the string, and pressed down very hard to ensure it was secure, after five minutes the sun fell and smashed into pieces. Next, the set was supposed to come with 5 feet of string for hanging. MAYBE there were three feet. So now I have a set of teeny tiny quarter sized planets that are taped up and dangling about 2 inches off of the ceiling. As you can imagine, this has, in no way, captured the imagination of my three year old (although it does LOOK like she made it). Finally, this is supposed to glow in the dark?? It doesn't glow AT ALL.

I'll take all of the pieces down, and rig something up myself. But, honestly, if I was going to go to all of this effort, I wouldn't have bothered buying this in the first place. You could probably create something more impressive with old golf balls, fishing hooks and some dental floss. Don't waste your money on this garbage.

product_title: Agricola (Discontinued by manufacturer)
review_headline: Too complex for most players, standard game rules feel unfair
review_body:
This game is enjoyable, but far too complex. It seems like every single rule has exceptions and clarifications and interactions with other rules. Months after learning the game you will still find yourself consulting the manual a couple of times a game. I feel that the family game is very balanced (given that each player is the same and has the same choices), while the minor improvements and occupations added to the rules when playing the standard game are too random and potentially unbalanced to allow for fair play.

The biggest problem with this game is that your strategy can be disrupted if too many other people are planning on taking the same upgrades at about the same time as you. A single bad turn can leave you scrambling to feed just 2-3 people while your opponents are expanding their house and adding their 4th and 5th family members. Miscalculating the food required for a single harvest can also end up penalizing you for 10-20% of your final score, essentially putting you in last place with no hope of recovery. My second big gripe is that it can be too difficult to tell what your score will be, and each game is different enough and lasts long enough (2-3 hours) that it can be hard to piece together a good play style and improve your skill at the game.

product_title: Tamiya 87038 Extra Thin Cement Glue Fine Tip 40ml
review_headline: Don't Underestimate The Smell & Adverse Effects On Your Health
review_body:
As a person that had just gotten into the scale modelling hobby, I bought this glue because it had a brush, it was clear, and it is known for a good bond. I used this product for two months, and while it was everything I knew it would be; the problem I had most was with the overpowering smell of it. The other reviews don't talk enough about the truly insidious quality found in the smell that looms and lingers in the room long after you've closed it up and stopped using it. The toxic scent is that of fingernail polish remover but it clings to your nasal passages like a fume. I ventilated the room with a ceiling fan, central air and had the window up, but to no avail. After only thirty minutes assembling a model, I would begin to cough. If used for a couple hours, afterwards I would feel edgy and agitated. I was in denial of these problems due to my love of a new hobby and thinking I needed to toughen up if I was going to enjoy myself. However after I realized my feeling drained and burned out was part and parcel because of the use of this product, I stopped using it. I have not used it in two months and I never felt the way I did while using it.

The fact is the label says, "WARNING: This product contains chemicals which are known to the State of California to cause cancer, birth defects, and reproductive harm."

So if you care more about the adhesive quality than the smell and the potentially damaging quality of the chemical vapors, this is your product. Before I gave up this hobby altogether, I found an alternative, but this product made me wonder if the health side effects were worth the finished product of a finished model.

I contacted Underground Toys, who suggested that I contact Amazon. I was refunded the entire purchase because they did not have a way to just send replacement doors. product_title: Game/Play Kotobukiya Iron Man 3 Mark 42 ArtFX + Statue Kid/Child
review_headline: Great piece.... but a bit frustrating
review_body:
This Kotobukiya Iron Man Mark 42 statue / model is spectacularly sculpted and the detail is just outstanding. It looks awesome. So why frustrating? Well here is why...

1: Assembly is scary. When I was putting the figure together I was worried I was going to break it. Especially when I was trying to attach the boot to the base, I really had to muscle it in… it was not a good fit. I kept waiting for the leg to break off with me pressing as hard as I was.

2: I absolutely love the look of the water themed base…. but it is cheap and hollow. It does not do a good job of supporting the heavy Iron Man figure, and since I live in earthquake country I am paranoid it is going to take a tumble the first time it gets shaken. Really wish they would have made the base solid and not have hollowed out underneath it.

3: I love the light up eyes and chest, but the sensor does not work effectively. Also, when I did my review of the Kotobukiya Mark VII I mentioned how awesome it would have been to have the lighted effect featured on his open-handed repulsors. Well, for the Mark 42 they added that feature on the right hand… but it is dim and unimpressive. It would be better if the light matched the intensity of the eye and chest lights.

4: Okay, this one is a pet peeve… but I wish Kotobukiya would show the figure being sold on the front of the boxes. The image on the front does not match the item in the package, it is a whole different pose. I know, I know… it sounds petty. It just irks me.

I paid $80 delivered, but I see them regularly selling for around $100. Shop around for a good deal, they are out there.
If you are Iron Man fan, this is a must have. It surpasses the Mark VII in my opinion. Just be careful when assembling it, as well as picking a secure place to display it.

She would look at us with pathetic green eyes very similar to these, just begging for attention of some sort, or other times to display a streak of rebellious mischief as if to say, "I'm going to knock this off and what are you going to do about it?"  She would do the lanky belly-crawl thing to hide under the covers in her bed whenever she heard thunder or sirens or alarms, especially after she barely survived our house fire that set off all the alarms in the house not to mention the emergency vehicle alarms that came to the rescue.  The wire support inside the tail of this kitty does not extend or connect past the point where the tail meets the back, so it just lays to one side or the other. product_title: Seasons
review_headline: Fun unique game. Part luck/part skill
review_body:
We watched a few internet tutorials before purchasing this game, and were worried that there would be too much of a learning curve, but we learned it very quickly, and after playing it, really like it.

The game play takes place over 3 "years" comprising of four seasons. The point of the game is to get the most points, which can be achieved a variety of ways. Different elements are worth more in different seasons, and the game cards add a really fun game play element.

This game does have a small element of luck, but you truly win by skill, and familiarity with the cards. In the instruction pamphlet they have some recommended card sets for first time players, I do recommend you start with those.

product_title: USS Skipjack Submarine 1/72 Moebius Over 40 inches Long
review_headline: Nice Model, but be prepared for some work.
review_body:
This is an impressive model and makes a fine display piece. Fit is fair, though. The hull is assembled in four pieces. Where the top and bottom halves, both forward and aft, fit together, there is a significant bulge that requires a good bit of sanding and filling. In the model I received, there is a 1.5mm difference in diameter between the forward hull and aft hull that has required more sanding and filling. The model is molded with plenty of detail and has photo etched parts for the MSW suction and discharge grating.
Due to its size, you will need plenty of paint and filler material (glazing compound).
Decals are included for all ships of the class: this one will be a tribute to the Scorpion, lost in May 1968.
I reinforced the interior of the hull seams with epoxy for added strength and added LEDs for navigation, mast head and rudder lighting.
This will be used in parades with our local SubVets group.

product_title: Transformers Beast Hunters Optimus Prime Action Figure
review_headline: A new look for Optimus Prime
review_body:
I grew up with Transformers and love they're still around. I even love when the kids I'm around give me that look, you know that look, when I fumble with trying to transform one they're familiar with. A look of disdain mixed with triumph when they take it and make the exact right moves in fluid order.

This is a different kind of Transformer. Which was initially disappointing. I liked the Optimus Prime that turns into a Semi, a real looking truck and a daunting looking robot. The robot form is certainly daunting but the truck form? Looks like a folded up robot. Yet, the more I played with it the more taken I was. There's a storyline behind it, to be sure, and that sparks a different imagination.

The first thing I noticed, of course, was how tall this is. Pretty big. Very impressive. With great action. The cannons on the back move with a trigger, launching... projectiles of some varying sort. The transformation isn't intuitive at first, but after a couple of goes it's second nature. The priority was definitely on the action elements and the robot form, but the truck functions. It's not quite perfectly designed, the middle set of wheels don't touch the ground, but again, the action of the turret are good.

It's very plastic. That was the second thing I noticed. Doesn't feel as solid nor as well designed as other Transformers I've been around over the years. Then again, with the size of this one, if they made it more solid and of better materials, the price could easily reach three figures. So, they cut some corners, made this within an approachable Christmas or birthday toy purchase price.

One minor issue I noted: Optimus is definitely a lefty. Put the sword in his right hand and it's really difficult to pull out. Other than that, everything seemed well constructed and functional.

My conclusion? It feels cheap and awkward at first, but honestly it really grew on me. I think a Transformers fan would really value this in their collection, with this larger model dominating as only Optimus Prime should.ally value this in their collection, with this larger model dominating as only Optimus Prime should.

product_title: StelCon: Infinity
review_headline: A great space exploration / war game
review_body:
When I was a young lad I discovered a store out in Woodbridge, NJ simply called The Game Room. While it had some tabletop video games to play as well as billiards and other games what drew me in were these new games. Games with such names as Dungeons and Dragons, Car Wars and Adventurer with beautifully painted covers that promised the player something extraordinary. One of the games that I had treasured and lost as a child was a game by Yaquinto Games called Shooting Stars which sported a beautifully painted cover of two starships attacking one another and I knew I had to have it. As time passed I have yet to feel the same type of feeling when looking at covers of various games as I had felt that moment in time was long since gone... until I found Stelcon:Infinity. Could this be a game that would let me relive my childhood? We will find out in this review.

Stelcon: Infinity is a game about deep space exploration and conquest as you are looking to conquer your opponents homeworld while defending your own. Two to six players can take on roles of colorful races such as the brotherhood, vanguard and syzzlok each of these races have various modifiers (or mods). The mods gives them bonuses to explore or for combat which you will be engaging in if you want to conquer various sectors of the galaxy. As you enter various sectors of the galaxy you will need to make an exploration roll to see how much fuel that sector will produce. Fuel is a vital resource as you cannot power your ships without it.

To explore the galaxy you will need a fleet of ships and the ships that are included with this game are not just some cut out counters. These ships are made out of sturdy cardboard and look better than most of the regular counters or just one color plastic pieces that other games provide you with. The ships can be modified with other counters such as guns (which give the ship extra firepower), Engines (giving them more movement range) and squads (giving you not only extra firepower but allowing you to scout other sectors as well.) Combat is resolved by adding up your firepower (with all applicable mods) and rolling dice to to see who wins. The attacker who wins the battle must make an exploration roll as well to conquer the sector but if the defender wins they do not have to make a roll.

At the heart of this game is a deck of cards called Conquest Cards. These cards can turn the tide of battle in your favor as well as give you other bonuses to give you an edge against your opponents. Various mods include increasing firepower, adding to rolls or even sneaking a peek at your opponents hand. This brings an element of strategy into the game as having the right card and playing it at the right moment can mean the difference between victory and defeat.

Now this game retails for around $80 but you get so much for you money! The ships to me are the heart of the game and they look absolutely gorgeous but the art on the cards as well as the map boards and star docks are incredible. And it is all housed in a giant box with gorgeous box art that takes me back to the golden age of gaming where people had beautiful box art (in the days of SPI and Avalon Hill). If you are a fan of sci-fi exploration games and want a fast paced, fun and great game to play do not hesitate to pick this game up!only extra firepower but allowing you to scout other sectors as well.) product_title: Crayola See Thru Light Designer (74-7051)
review_body:
It is a bit difficult to understand just what this product is, but Crayola has a nice video explaining it in the product images. In the pack is the Light Designer, which has two clear removable plastic drawing boards, and four gel markers. The latter give a neon look and wash off surprisingly easily with just warm water. So, what do you do with this thing?

Since the drawing boards are removable, they can be placed on a picture (or face) to trace it. Want to draw something from scratch? The clear boards still come in handy, since you can trace your own work and create a basic two-frame animation, similar to what you might do by flipping between two pieces of paper. The Light Designer takes the work out of it by automatically lighting up alternating boards. The effect is pretty good, though it works best in a very dark room.

This toy is probably going to be used a lot for a little while, then forgotten, but the price is not bad for the entertainment it provides. It might even spark some interest in art that will grow over time.

review_body:
I donned this fabulous head accessory today with a brown blanket wrapped around my body, and after making horse noises enough times at the security guard, he let me past the gate, and all of a sudden, I was let onto the racetrack at the Melbourne Cup! What an honour! I named myself "Blue Sunshine", and everyone was impressed that a horse could run on its hind legs without even needing a jockey.

Unfortunately however, halfway through the race, I fell over, and people must have assumed I'd broken my leg or something, so I was treated to 5 people attempting to shoot me in the head, and that's how I worked out that the Accoutrements Horse Head Mask is also great at repelling bullets which was definitely a plus.

The product has also made me able to finally achieve my dream of being able to go to the toilet anywhere! Seriously, I've crapped on like 4 people's shoes already.

This mask has helped me realise that I do have a future in horse racing, and already 538 people have bet on me to win the next race. I'm also being heralded as the next horse superstar and they've indicated that after I die, my brain will be preserved and kept in a museum! How exciting!

Anyhow, I should go - people are getting suspicious that a horse is typing on a computer, although these people are pretty dumb so I doubt they'd kick up a stink.

Once again thanks, 10/10 would buy again!

product_title: Gund 2013 Amazon Collectible Bear Plush
review_headline: 2013 Amazon Bear by Gund - Sixth Edition
review_body:
The 2013 Gund Amazon Collectible Teddy Bear is the sixth edition in this Amazon tradition that began in 2008. Each year, a different bear with a unique hat embroidered with the Amazon.com smile logo is made by Gund as an Amazon exclusive.

This year's cuddly little fellow is twelve inches tall with dark brown fur and he sports a red plaid trapper hat with a fur lining. He sits upright and has plush faux fur. He is so huggable! I think he is the cutest Amazon bear yet.

He is free when included with a basket of $75 worth of qualifying toys sold by Amazon—over 116,000 different items are eligible at this time, from LEGO Minecraft sets to LeapFrog electronics. He can also be purchased at a discount to the usual price for a comparable Gund bear.

Some of the previous bears are being sold for many times over the original retail prices, although the [[ASIN:B0089MQW94 2012 edition bear]] in a cute little red ski cap with matching mittens is still available at a bargain price.

Don't forget to add him to your cart when buying toys this Christmas!

product_title: DON'T SHOOT THE MESSENGER Board Game
review_body: Let me guess, the name got your first, right? Me too. Well, this really is a case of what you see is what you get. My game group has played this three nights running (and plan to keep at it), which is virtually unheard of among this diverse and hard-to-please bunch. If you like edge-of-your-seat type games, you've come to the right place. If you're not fully alert, forget about it.  It won't take you long to guess an answer...quite the contrary. We're talking about mere seconds here since the expressions, cliches, sayings, phrases are extremely familiar. We use them every minute of every hour of every day. That one word is missing should cause a momentary pause at most. No, the problem is that this is also one of those Say-It-First games so, you guessed it, you need to be faster than everybody else or you get zilch. Let me restate that so there's no misunderstanding: you must be Super-Fast, along warp-speed lines. I kid you not. Each card has four questions, so you get four chances to spare your blushes. Or, better yet, the chance to win all four questions and sweep the round. But don't count on doing that often, especially if there are many people playing. You won't always be the quickest. But you'll always have fun.

She participates in choosing the next game/app and makes commitments about behavior to \\"earn\\" the new game. The latest purchase was the Brave game (22 levels). The tablet cut out. We found a video online about how to take it apart (it was nerve wracking, and it was a unit a couple of years older, so slight differences) and we managed to get it apart without breaking anything. I put it in rice and we left it there a couple of days (this had worked for me on a cell phone once). It's been a month now and everything is working fine! Thank god because it was the adults who were falling apart worried that it was dead. My granddaughter had faith in us all along. Even the cartridge is fine.

REALLY REALLY well built unit.

I highly recommend this unit, as you will get your own tablet back from your toddlers. Just be prepared to buy lots and lots of games. She's reading on her own and her puzzle solving skills are amazing. And we don't have to worry about her downloading apps on her own or making in game purchases. Worth the investment.

product_title: Melt N Mold
review_body:
Long story short: My child somehow became convinced that this thing would be the ultimate life experience and I bought it for him, thinking that worst case scenario its a teaching moment about buying into advertising hype. Got it this afternoon at a store, busted up the recommended volume of crayons, blazed it up, and sat back to wait...and wait...1.5 hours later and there are still solid fragments among some liquid wax. Obviously this thing is worthless. However, in the interest of car- and ring-shaped crayons, I threw new crayon fragments in an oven dish lined with foil into the oven at 275 for a few minutes and used the foil to funnel the molten wax into the mold. Worked perfect and that's what we'll be doing from now on, so everybody's happy.

In retrospect, if I was smarter I would've bought several of the expansion packs and not the main unit since I won't be using it anyway. The machine comes with a holder to keep the mold halves together, but it would be fairly easy to use a clamp and two small pieces of scrap wood or cardboard to hold the mold together and save yourself forty bucks and those big sad eyes.

product_title: Syma X1 4 Channel 2.4G RC Quad Copter Helicopter - UFO
review_body:
This is the best toy-grade helicopter I've ever bought. I bought it for $35 and it's well worth the price.

It has a great transmitter, I don't know the official range on it, but it's more than enough.
It's has proper 4 channel control. Thrust and yaw on the left stick. Pitch and Roll on the right.
it has a working LCD screen that shows the movement of the sticks, and hows an L or an H for the dual rates.

The button on the top left toggles the dual rates. it starts on low. This is for beginners or indoors. This affects Yaw, Pitch and Roll. Inputs barely have an effect. To make it do anything you need to move the control sticks all the way. The copter feels sluggish, it's almost trying to ignore your commands. This is good for beginners if they aren't used to proportional inputs and they only move the inputs all the way whenever they want to do something.
High is the normal mode. All of the sluggishness disappears and you realize it was just pretending to be stuck in the same spot. any slight touch of the inputs yields visible adjustments. the copter has no problem tilting and flying wherever you tell it to.

The copter has no on/off switch, instead you put in or take out the battery. Every time you put in the battery, you need to set it on a flat surface for a few seconds for the gyros to set. If you crash it or after flying awhile the gyros will be a few degrees off, just take out the battery, and reset them. It has digital trims on the transmitter. i tried to use them once and it didn't appear like they did anything, but reseting the gyro has worked fine.

The button on the top right makes it do flips. You just hit the button and then a direction on the right stick. In the process if falls about five feet so don't do it near the ground.

I've had this copter for two weeks, I've crashed it a few times, and other people that I let fly it have crashed it a few times. And so far not a single piece has broken. it comes with a full replacement of blades.

It comes with a usb charger. It's auto shut off.

I recommend getting more batteries for it. The battery life is 10-15min.

If it's the same price I'd say get one of the other bodies. The spaceship and the bumblebee both have a clear front and back. With the ufo body you can only go by the blades. The white blades are in front, the black blades are in back.

product_title: Bandai Tamashii Nations S.H. Figuarts Masked Rider Blade Action Figure
review_body:
Over all, an excellent figure. Whether it's your first S.H. Figuarts or only the latest of your ever growing collection, this one is the one to buy!
Kamen Rider Blade features several alternate hands, including one to hold cards, his signature weapon, the Blade Rouser, a holster, a kick-effect part and a broken rock part with a slot to hold the blade rouser point down.
The figure itself features a new type of hip joint that we haven't seen before, it's similar to the type-1 in the original Black and Domon Kashu, but refined even further than the Ryuki riders which also use a similar type of hip joint. It doesn't sacrifice as much mobility and the joints are smooth as silk and tight enough to hold the most extreme poses.
His shoulder pads are exceptionally well done and do not compromise any of his arm's motions, yet they don't have any visible toy-like joints to them.

The detailing on his helmet and belt and armor are all top notch and while the stickers are a bit of a novelty, they are easy to apply and are a higher quality plastic, not paper.
Once completed, he is a stylish and attractive figure with a great accessory count and wonderful articulation. A must buy!

product_title: Fisher-Price Roll N Go Get Away Garage
review_body:
[Good]

It's a pretty attractive looking toy and that will keep your kid distracted for hours.

Safety: The choice for plastic instead die cast metal was a good one. We've already had an episode where my kid has thrown one of the cars. Thankfully it didn't hit another child. If it did, the damage would be minimized since the cars aren't die cast metal.

Ease of Assembly: The instructions were pretty clear and simple to follow, with the hardest part being the precise placement of stickers.

Durability: This toy is durable enough to survive being pulled away roughly on multiple occasions.

Children under 4 that play with this toy will become more familiar with the idea of mechanical motion

[Bad]

Battery Operated: I really didn't like it that the crane was battery operated. I feel that there would be more educational value if it was hand crank operated. I really didn't see the value of making it battery powered.

While this toy is rated for 3-6 years old, I'm not sure I can see children 5 years old and older really having fun with this toy.

I don't really see any point in the retractable rubber road, other than increasing the toy dimensions on the box.

[Misc]

I didn't see this toy's price as either a positive or negative.

[Verdict]

This is a great toy for a young child.

product_title: Pinypon - Ski Lodge Playset
review_headline: Adorable Play Set With So Many Options
review_body:
So the first thing that surprised me with this set is where it says "Real Ice Rink." Now what that means is that you can actually put water in the ice rink tray and freeze it so the figures can "ice skate" on it! I didn't get the chance to do this because laying something flat in my freezer is impossible right now, but I don't see why this wouldn't work just fine although it will be cold to touch! So real ice rink, check, next up is all the figures and their skates, skis, or boards. There are so many pieces to this set that it would be hard for a little girl to get bored. I absolutely love that you can take apart all the pieces and swap them around, its like making all new dolls with just a few pieces! There are a few cardboard pieces you have to stick on to the set with these little plastic pieces but surprisingly they stayed on.

This set is for ages 4 and up and I think that would be about right. There are many small pieces so you definitely want the child to be out of the putting the pieces in their mouth stage and able to swap out the pieces themselves (although that is pretty easy to do.) My daughter is young still so I supervise her playing with it and my boys (although they wouldn't when their friends are around) like to play with it too! The set is just so kid-friendly and adorable! So much to do and change around. There are add-ons you can buy for this set too for more Pinypon Snow fun, but really this set should be good for awhile!

review_body:

product_title: Accoutrements Unisex Latex Masks
review_headline: Gives New Meaning to the Term 'Pigeon Head'.
review_body:
I will say right off the bat I have tried several different avian masks in my day, but nothing is quite like the pigeon mask - NOTHING! I have 2 other pigeon masks from various retailers around the internet and this is the best one so far. When I slip those rubbery feathers over my head, and feel my nose & mouth fill up the beak compartment, I am home. I can feel my breath begin to get labored, and my hearing dims as the non-ventilated headpiece smothers my senses, dimming my vision, but doing something so much more...it unleashes the pigeon in me. Suddenly I become what I was always meant to be - a great hybrid of male flesh and pigeony rubber. The me that was ceases to be as man and bird become one.

The latex of the mask holds up well to sweat, tears and mucus membrane as I perspire and drool from the heat of my excitement with being merged into the pigeon. The mask also holds up well against bushes and tree branches as well. It is also ideal for bathing in both mounds of dirt AND outdoor bird baths. The one drawback being that because the beak is NOT functional, I have trouble swallowing and spitting out dirty water that gags me, and it fills up in the beak like a reservoir of filth.. But, other than that, with the aid of an Exacto Knife I have bored a small hole into the beak to accommodate the swallowing of worms and other small insects.

With this mask I can now live out my greatest pigeon dreams and be the bird-like man I was always meant to be. I am so happy I purchased this mask, and never cease to marvel at the many wondrous looks it gets me from people in the park - especially the ones who's car windshields I stop to take a s*** on. Granted, I was surprised that it did not lessen my overall body weight, and my bones did NOT seem to hollow out like those of other birds so I could take flight, and there was some disappointment that I broke a homeless woman's arm when I tried to perch myself on her. But, these few small flaws aside, I find this to be an awesome mask, and am glad I bought one. get one for yourself, and you will be too.de, I find this to be an awesome mask, and am glad I bought one. get one for yourself, and you will be too.

The set comes in two resealable boxes which makes clean up and organization easy (why don't more toy makers do this?!) product_title: Batman Classic TV Series Batmobile Vehicle
review_body:
First i have two of these lugs of plastic, why because I fell for Mattel and their adult collector tricks. This car is plastic,a hollow soulless piece of plastic.

For sixty plus bucks \\"adult\\" collectible, you get garbage. Check everyone else's reviews on YouTube, same exact things I will say.

This is crap, only worth 20 dollars. How can Mattel charge $60? Because they can! No die cast metal; adult collectible means high quality, but this is cheap plastic car, with no metal, no lights, no sounds; where's my theme music.

Skip this and save 60 bucks, wait for a better quality version. Even if you waited Mattel will charge 200 dollars for their next version(ie Semi Diecast Ghostbusters car than no one preordered so they canceled), why you may ask, because they can.

When I read other Amazon reviews,I ask myself \\"what are these other guys reviewing?\\" They seem to be reviewing their nostalgia rather than the product. Look, it's as bad as claim, Mattel has taken advantage of the fans, they're probably getting a kick out of collectors and fans gobbling their garbage up. Reading peoples \\"reviews\\" on Amazon, I would chuckle all the way to the bank driving my BMW too..

I wanted this all my life but this was a real disappointment. I wish I could say go and get this, but it's so poorly handled. Sadly it comes down to cost vs worth. Is $60 worth it, and the answer is a resounding, heck no! As a fan of Adam West and Burt Ward and the '66 Batman series, I am saddened that this is what Mattel thinks of its fans; they can OVERCHARGE what they want for junk and because we have no one else to buy it from, eventually we'll break down and get it, because nostalgia is their only selling point.

product_title: Clue - The Great Museum Caper
review_headline: Clue: The Great Museum Caper Review by Dad's Gaming Addiction
review_body:
Clue: The Great Museum Caper: 2-6 Players, Ages 10+, Average Play Time = 30 Minutes Per Game

Let me start off by saying that we played three games. Normally we only play one game for review purposes, but the kids enjoyed themselves so much that we played three times. Anthony Jr (16) and Carolyn (13) got to be the thief the second and third time around and I could tell how excited they were when they saw my pawns moving in on them. They both used trickery and often didn't move their full three spaces, just to throw me off as to their possible location. Vinnie Jr (11) and Devonn (11) both enjoyed the game as well, liking the detective work involved with finding the thief. When I systematically started disabling cameras in the first game and ignored obvious targets, they began five-minute long discussions on where I probably was. It was fun watching them reason things out through logic.

With all of that said, the board is immediately eye-catching, not only due to its color but its 3D design. It's no Fireball Island, but the board and components are executed well. The board is small enough to where the detectives can move from one end to the other fairly quickly, but open enough to allow a good thief to psych out his opponents without being caught. The thief notepads perform their function well, but if you play this game a lot, save a few so that you can make copies.

If you can get your hands on a copy of this game, then by all means, do so. If you buy it used like I did, make sure that all of the components come with the game. After all of these years, Clue: The Great Museum Caper remains as one of my all time favorite games. It's easy to learn but difficult to master, making it an excellent game to introduce to kids.

review_body:
So you don't make the Same Mistakes I did -
1) The ducted fan is NOT more powerful than an open propeller. If you read up on it, these model ducted fans were originally created to allow RC modelers to build and fly scale models of jets. The ducted fan at this size is Considerably Less powerful than an open prop.
2) The landing gear, specifically the nose gear, is inadequately mounted and inadequately absorbant. I've rebuilt the nose mount and bent two new nose struts, and I'm giving up.
3) ARF is somewhat deceptive; it's Almost Ready to Fly - all you have to do is build it. If you don't have modelers tools, a workbench, and a moto-tool, you're probably in for more than you expected (note - this is common for most ARF kits, even Multiplex).

I am deducting one star only because of a flaw by the manufacturer in packaging it. There is nowhere I could find on the box that has instructions for listening to the entire lot of phrases she comes with, the various cheers. Initially she arrives in demo mode which I didn't know until I returned the original one and a second one was shipped out and arrived the same way, with only cheering two phrases. I did some research and found that there is a long white plastic pull-tab on Minnie's right side that initiates her full \\"itinerary\\" of phrases. This is important to the buyer if they are gifting this item. If you are, please attach a note, alerting the recipient or its parent to this necessary step, so they won't be disappointed to hear just two phrases over and over.

This sword is not a "bad" sword, but it's only "about" 2 feet long. The sword is basically a hollow plastic sword with some painting for detail. It's actually pretty sturdy, although I don't really recommend using it for "real" sword play. The painting detail is not the greatest as it seems like it was sprayed my a mechanical painter. Sadly, it did not come in a contained package, as it was just twist tied to a labelled cardboard backing. Some of the painted was chipped, mostly around the rounded edges of the handle part. Overall, it's an okay sword to give to kids, but not really ideal for adults as it looks like you are holding a Voltron dagger than a sword. If you plan to use this as part of a costume, it's best to give to kids. If plan to use this as a collectors item, it would look okay in a glass case on a shelf, just don't be too upset about the paint being chipped.
