product_title: Battroborg 3-in-1 Battle Arena
review_headline: solid fun but can be a little frustrating
review_body:
Pros:

Set-up is very easy. The robots come already assembled. The controllers/chargers just need to be opened up (small phillips head) and powered with batteries. Then you attach the robots to the charger (very simple), let them charge the promised 20 minutes (so far that's been spot on). While you're letting them charge, you can snap together the rope restraints around the arena--again, very simple and easy to do. That's it. Nothing to it.

Charge seems to last as long or longer than promised (20 minutes).

My eleven-year-old certainly found it fun. He had a good time duking it out with me or his mom and is looking forward to playing with his friends. It's not his favorite thing to do (he's only played it a few times since we received it) but when he plays with it, it's a great time.

Cons:
I wish they didn't take four batteries, which seems like a lot. And they recommend not using rechargeables, which is another power-related bummer.

Movement can be mildly frustrating. You move the robots by \\"punching\\" the air with your two controllers (each held in a separate hand). Do a guick one-two jab and repeat and you'll march your robot forward in a relatively straight line. You can turn by making smaller motions with only one controller (picture using one oar in a canoe). The problem is the robot often, and I mean often, got trapped on the sides or at the ends of the arena and no amount of controller movement was going to unstick them. Inevitably, a player has to reach in and pull the robot back to the center by the feet (you don't want to use the head because it will register as a hit or as a reset). This happened so often and so regularly that after a short period of time, we didn't even bother trying to unstick them with the controllers--the moment one got stuck, we immediately reached in and fixed the situation. Because it became so automatic and quick a response, I call this only \\"mildly\\" frustrating,as it doesn't take up any time and it's so simple and quick to fix. But the frequency definitely makes it an issue--there's got to be a better arena design so this doesn't happen.

Hits do not consistently register. One robot might be wailing away and clearly connecting, but for some reason the other one, who is striking less often, will \\"win\\" the round. This will only matter if players are concerned about winning. If you're just having a fun moving the robots and throwing punches and chasing the other robot around the ring (as my son was), it was a non-issue. But if you have competitive kids, be prepared for complaints and arguments.

Too Early to Tells:
Can't tell yet how sturdy these will be. One of our robots came with a piece of his arm hanging down disconnected. It was easy to reconnect and so far it's held up. I'll update if things go sour; if there's no update you can assume nothing has appeared to make me question its durability.

If the charge will hold up. Again, so far it's exactly as promised both in terms of charging time and playing time. We'll see if that holds up over time.

A tip: make sure you \\"connect\\" or \\"pair\\" your robot and controllers one at a time. One player should turn on the robot, then the controller, and wait for the pairing chime. Then and only then should the other player do the same. Otherwise one controller will end up controlling both robots.

It's definitely a pricey toy, but it's got some decent tech so it's hard to fault the price. And as mentioned, my eleven-year-old certainly had fun playing it when he played it. I'll be curious to see how often it gets pulled out. I'd say it's more fun for the running around whacking things than for any sense of a true contest and attempt to score points, especially as there really didn't seem to be a super strong connection between which robot took the most punishment and which got \\"knocked out\\" (cycling through some color warnings then flashing red). And I'd say the age-range is definitely in the sub-12 or 13 group.

product_title: World of Disney Eye Found It Board Game
review_headline: Plays well with a 3 year old
review_body:
Coming from a fairly heavy board gaming family, I've been introducing games to my kids at a young age - in hopes of working our way up quickly to the more complex Euro-games my wife and I like to play.

Still, at age three, my daughter has mostly been playing "Go Away Monster," "Candyland," and "Chutes and Ladders." She loves them, but has a little bit of a hard time following the rules and staying focused - mostly because the games are so one dimensional that she gets bored (either moving her pieces around the board gets boring, or pulling pieces out of a bag gets boring - games often devolve into a new game she makes up - which is awesome in it own right, but we still want her to learn to play a game to completion).

In addition she is a huge Disney fanatic and a huge fan of the finding things puzzles in magazines like Highlights. So I figured I'd give this a try.

For the first time, she was able to follow the games rules nearly perfectly. The variety of finding different items really held her interest (and believe it or not, mine too - even if it was just partly due to the joy of watching her). Even though it recommends ages four and up, the rules (listed on one small sheet of paper) are simple enough for a three year old. They basically involve spinning a spinner, moving a playing piece and finding things.

From a game standpoint, the different items you need to find can be easy (there are so many flags on castles, when she had to find a flag it was a piece of cake - and we were lucky that was the first thing we drew - it was a good starter) to difficult (for children at least - those mailboxes can be tiny - but all the items are fairly easy to find for adults). So it really was a perfect spread for a three year old.

The major con I have is that the game projects to take quite a long time. Take away the finding things aspect and the game boils down to moving your piece around the board (a la Chutes and Ladders), but in this case the board is huge. That's great for the finding things aspect - but tough from a we want to finish the game in 1/2 an hour with our kids aspect.

Still, we simply cut the game short - mostly because it was time for bed. Our daughter was still completely engrossed at the end and would have kept playing...

While it may not be the best game out there for young children, it has certainly earned a place on our game shelf.a la Chutes and Ladders), but in this case the board is huge. That's great for the finding things aspect - but tough from a we want to finish the game in 1/2 an hour with our kids aspect.

product_title: Loaded Questions
review_body:
Loaded Questions is a game you will enjoy most playing with people you know well, or think you know well. It is enlightening how little we really know about one another. The idea of the game is that a group of 4 or more (really, it doesn't work with fewer than that) each have a score sheet and pencil. On this they write their response to questions in one of four different categories: hypothetical questions like \\"If you wrote a horror story, how would you bump off the first victim?; no-brainers like \\"When is it not a good time to have an audience?\\"; anything goes questions such as \\"Who would not look good in a dress.\\"; and personal questions like \\"\\"What is the one question you would not want to answer?\\". There is a board with little game pieces and a single dice. The person shortest in stature starts off as the dice roller, rolls the dice and moves the number of spaces required. He then selects a card and reads aloud the question for the category of the space where he landed. Everyone except the roller writes an answer to the question. The papers are collected by the person sitting counter-clockwise from the roller (after the first play it is always the last roller), who reads the answers aloud. The roller then must guess who said which answer. The roller advances one space for each answer. And so it goes. Winning has a formula involving landing on the win space and guessing who said which answer to at least 3 times.

I found the board game part of Loaded Questions just a gimmick to start the conversations rolling, and they do roll. Everyone wants to explain why she wrote what she wrote, or guessed how she guessed. And then, as talk does, it meanders from there all over the subject and beyond until someone brings the talk back to the game and the next person rolls. It is definitely for teenaged to adult players, as the questions are a little much for younger people. It would be a fun slumber party game (if teens still have slumber parties), or fora gathering of good friends for drinks and dinner. Some ground rules about embarrassing or hurtful answers shouldn't be necessary. If you think a group may need such limiting, then it might not be the best group for the game. If everyone has their sense of humor intact, it is a lot of fun and a great conversation-stimulator!

review_body:
I have read the mostly negative reviews of this product and can't argue with the number of people who have had a bad experience with it. I would advise anyone who is worried about durability and quality to exercise caution - it's hard to ignore all of the problems that have been reported here.

That being said, I bought one of these pillows a couple of months ago to help my daughter, who was suffering from a period of anxiety about night and darkness, to sleep better and to have a pillow to take with her and provide some comforting light on the inevitable middle-of-the-night bathroom trip.

The pillow has worked fine and continues to work fine about two months after purchase. My daughter is not hard on the pillow but not unusually gentle either; it stays mostly in her bed and she taps it to turn it on at least once per night. After about a month the pillow started, more and more often, showing only red lights when turned on and only changing colors to green once before going back to red again until turned off and back on for another go. That lasted for about two weeks, with my daughter asking me why her pillow was only red with increasing frequency. Finally tonight I decided to change the batteries and now it's back to the full brightness full color changing experience that we had when it was new.

I had forgotten about how bright and colorful this pillow is when the batteries are fresh! It's also quite soft - and yes, there is a square battery pack which is hard and not comfortable to lay on, but generally you just have to choose one of the other three edges to rest your head on. I can't understand why they wouldn't have a pocket deep within the cushioning of the pillow to hold the hard plastic battery case, but they don't.

I don't know how long this pillow will last, but in the two months that we've had it, my daughter has been exceptionally happy with it and it's worked great so far. The other reviews make me worried that it could stop functioning at any time, but we'll enjoy it while it lasts.ed that it could stop functioning at any time, but we'll enjoy it while it lasts.

Such a disappointment when I bought them for children I knew, hoping to introduce them to the joy I had known with Spirograph. Those shoddy "new" ones were frustrating for an adult experienced using a Spirograph to use, let alone a child new to it. This newest version, however, is a welcome return to the classic beloved Spirograph! In fact it is even better! The pens are much better with this set, and the "Spirography Putty" included with the toys holds down the rings to the paper in a way that those  of us from the era when one pinned the rings to the paper could only dream of! Makes using the toy much easier than I remember. I  cannot wait to buy these new Spirographs for the kids in my life!

product_title: TRIVIAL PURSUIT: World of Warcraft
review_body:
While I wasn't expecting a full-sized "Genus III" version of Trivial Pursuit, I guess I was expecting something a little more from this WoW version of Pursuit.

Upon first picking up the shipping box, I thought there must have been an error. It was so light. But upon opening... yes, the game was within. And it was small! It can be picked up with a single hand across the top.

Nothing inside lived up to the expectation. The board is a four-square fold out, but so small! The normal circular wedge-holders easily cover two whole spaces! That's why you get the (molded plastic) murloc movers!

The questions? I wish I had done a little math... the Amazon listing boasts 600 questions. Do simple math... that's only 100 question cards. Most Pursuit Genus editions have several hundred cards in each of their card boxes. Oh, that's the other thing. I expected with a specialty version of Pursuit to probably just have one card box of questions. Nope. A third of a card box... and no card box! The question cards, upon being unwrapped, are going to just slide around in the bottom of the game box.

Mind you, not everything is bad about the production of the game:
1 Flipping through the cards, I did find a good mix of questions: many I got right, many I SHOULD have gotten right, and many that stumped me.
2. The sculpt on the baby murloc movers is, admittedly cute. They're newborns climbing out of their shells. When I realized what they were, I will admit it... I said "Awwww..."
3. The die has a nice murloc image with the number on each side. Admittedly, it's printed and not etched, but still, looks nice.
4. All the graphic are classic WoW, which is nice.

Overall, I was expecting a little more. It will be a fun novelty game in my collection, might even get a play or two! Just be aware of exactly what you're getting. And, keep in mind, a full version of Pursuit is significantly more expensive... with the scaled back price, you get a scaled back game.

review_body:
No idea what happened with my original review. It was posted and now it does not exist...
This product is pointed for the DJI Phantom and that is what I will comment. In my previous review I detailed all the steps but here just the abstract.
I did tried everything with this gimbal. From using two instead of the four isolators, balances propellers, used stock props (soft) instead of CF, added super lube to the servos, adding weight to the pitch section, replaced the rubbers by other more soft, and even moon gel between the camera and the gimbal. I have tried so many options during the couple of month I had this product.

My final settings on Assistant:
F2(pitch) - REV - 1000 max / -200 / -1000 min
F1(roll) - NORM - 740 max / 70 / -900 min
gain: 20 (anything else resulted in overcompensation)

pros:
- You do not need extra wires, controllers nor batteries for this gimbal. It is installed directly on the phantom and the wires connected to the F and F of the naza-M. Just remember to enable gibmal on Assistant BEFORE connecting the servos to the Naza-m.
- light gimbal
- simple to install

cons:
- price is same as some gimbals using brushless motors (way more smooth), with controllers, sensor and even voltage regulators. There is no chance a servo can compete with the smoothness of a brushless motor.
- even with the phantom kept with its engines off, this gimbal ADDS vibration to the gopro in extreme levels. The resulting video is of no use at all. Stock phantom delivers better results than this. Turn on the multicopter motors and then you get even more vibration.
- no matter all the different tests and attempts to make this work, the gimbal is totally useless considering its PRODUCTION of vibration.
- the roll servo even \\"plays\\" (does not hold the frame in solid way - you can shake it and it moves freely a degree).

conclusion:
- I cannot ask for a refund because I modified one of the plates to allow the plug for FPV. Otherwise I would send it back.
- If you want parts, then buy parts... if you want a gimbal to balance your camera and also isolate the vibrations, then this is not the product you need. On the cheap side, there are other/better options of similar price, but using way more effective technology like brushless motors. I did not find them on amazon but on ebay, searching with \\"worldwide\\". product_title: Monster High Ghouls Rule Frankie Stein Doll
review_body:
I went to Target on New Year's Day, and this doll was one of the only two left on the shelves-literally, there was only a Robecca Steam. (I already had that doll, so I didn't pick it up.) This doll is my second Ghouls Rule, and my Cleo has some serious issues. However, the Frankie is much better. She is dressed for Halloween in a strapless black jumpsuit with blue mechanical nut zig-zags and knee-length pants. The second layer is a blue knitted short-sleeved top with black stitches at the hem that lead into a sheer white-ish skirt with silver lightning bolts on the bottom half of it. On the cut-open side, there is more of the stitching pattern. Last, Frankie wears a beautiful silver vest with black stitches around the middle and the end of the collar. There is also a second smaller collar that has silver nuts printed on black fuzzy felt. All of Frankie's jewelry is silver, and the earrings are dangly nuts. The bracelets are also made of nuts and have holes in the side. They extend to her lower arm stitches. My favorite part of the outfit are the boots. They are black with no heels and a platform, and have stitches on the sides. The toes are covered in black glitter, which I LOVE. Her bolts are shiny, but her stitches are a bit duller. Frankie's hair is done up like the Bride of Frankenstein's, a tall curly updo with two white streaks on either side. Her bangs are gelled and have one white streak. My doll's 'do is more fanned out than the other ones I've seen recently. Frankie's makeup is absolutely wonderful. She has light blue lipstick and eyeliner on her lids, and above it is gray, which you almost can't see. On the lower lids she has simple sparkly silver. Frankie's eyes are the usual, one green and one blue. The work on the left side of her face is the real masterpiece, though. It continues her mask, which only covers one eye (more on the accessories later). Extending from Frankie's left eye are eight blue lightning bolts, which look fantastic. Her accessories are a blue mask stitched together that covers her right eye and has two lightning bolts coming out of the end. She also has a blue trick-or-treat bag with slime dripping from the top and bolts sticking out on the sides and flat all over the back. It also has her skull symbol in the front. Her blue pennant also has a skull with bolts on top and a lightning bolt in the middle. Her party treat is green slime with lightning bolts and regular bolts in it. It is in a silver bowl that has rivets holding it together. She also comes with a trading card, like all of the other GR dolls. As far as durability my only trouble was that Frankie's left boot has a huge hole running the length of her toes on the inside edge, so keep your eyes out for any holes in the boots, which are made of a soft rubber. Also, the masks cannot be held very well by the dolls, either.

Mattel really hit the nail on the head with the detail in this doll. Everything is so intricate, especially the accessories, which could be less detailed in the hands of a lesser toy company. I'd recommend this doll for collectors and younger girls alike, and it will look great in any collection. The Ghouls Rule line of dolls is great, but I'd recommend looking on Amazon or somewhere that it's less than $25. (When I wrote this review, it was $20.)

product_title: Bang 4th Edition
review_body:

There's a lot of annoying \\"take that!\\" mechanics that I despise and the whole game is about screwing people over with gunplay and random wild west craziness. The worst part is you can die super-fast and be out of the game early, sitting around bored while the other players play on for another hour or so. How is that fun? It isn't, at least not to me. I don't hate this game as much as [[ASIN:161661238X Wiz-War]] or [[ASIN:B0043T96X6 Robo Rally]], but it's close. These kind of games do nothing for me.

UPDATE: Just played [[ASIN:B00DH8D0HC Bang!: The Dice Game]] and have to say it's much better than the original. Without all those cards (including ways to block hits), the game plays much faster and with less confusion. If you get killed early, you'll only be sitting around maybe twenty minutes with nothing to do, as opposed to the hour or more with the annoying card game version. The art is much nicer in the dice game too. That said, I still don't really like it, but would rate the dice game a full star higher than the original (three stars).

product_title: The Noble Collection Hermione Granger Illuminating Wand
review_body:
Yes that's correct, I'm 22 years old and I bought this toy for myself ;) I've always been a huge fan and I grew-up with the characters, but I'm usually only ever extremely nerdy in my own house. This toy is wonderfully fun, I bought it, believe it or not, because I'm aways waking up in the middle of the night to get a drink or use the bathroom, and I thought this would be much sweeter than a flashlight or a night light.
It is larger than the collectable wands, and much less in quality than them too, but that's because this is a toy. It's larger because two batteries need to fit in there, and quite obviously made of plastic.I can't stress this enough to those negative reviewers, you're paying for the Harry Potter name, the price is not going to go down. I'm an avid collector, and yes it's as much as the collectable wands even though I myself would consider it less of a collectable and more of a toy, but it's also ten times more fun since it really does light up with just a flick of the wrist, and off again in the same manner, which is better than any other light-up wand you'll find out there.

My conclusion: If your'e willing to spend the dough, this really will be worth it, you or your child will go bonkers for it. To you it may look too fake, but to your kid, they are a real wizard! How big of a price tag can you put on that kind of joy? By far the most fun thing I've added to my collection of HP items. And I plan to use it constantly.

product_title: Teamson Kids Wooden Doll House
review_headline: A Darling House but some Damage to the included Furniture
review_body:
This is a doll house that any little girl would love. My daughter age 5, simply has adored playing with this house since we gifted it to her. Some days for hours on end even, I find her playing with it. She's hugged me nearly every day thanking me for her lovely house. It's pretty large and makes a great home for a Barbie sized doll or those just a little shorter than Barbie. There's even a really cute white linked balcony for your child's dolls to play upon!

I would give this house 5 stars though there are several important things that need to be mentioned that caused me to dock a star. My parenting loves however are that the Doll house is FSC certified, environmentally friendly, made from quality wood, and that it's a fun make believe prop that encourages imaginative play.

Upon opening the package, three of the furniture items were broken or damaged. One chair the arm was completely separated, on the bed one leg was bent (and eventually broke off by a little brother) and one of the couches was dented on the top edge. The former two my husband mended with super glue. The latter will just have to stay that way. If packed better this would probably not have happened.

I'm not sure if replacement pieces can be sent out or purchased separately but that would be something to look into if by any chance the item ships and gets damaged before it gets to you. I hear the company this Dollhouse is from has very friendly customer service.

The house pieces were in good condition, no issues whatsoever. The bright & cheerful colors and illustrated interior as well exterior are very nice. Assembling wasn't difficult, but it did take a while. The picture instructions are clear and finding the correct piece wasn't an issue. It even reminds you to check the facing on some pieces so you don't put it backwards.

The final construction feels pretty sturdy and I believe it will hold up to general use for years the years to come.

product_title: LEGO Bricks & More Blue Suitcase 10659
review_headline: We love these and are happy legos is helping the in between duplo but not ready for huge sets!
review_body:
I am a parent to numerous lego sets and minifigures (lego city to super hero ones) that I put together with my child. Finally I found one that my son can put together without my help at four years of age. It is this one!

I really don't mind helping him put others together but to see the accomplishment on my sons face is worth it!

We have the 10659 set and are super happy that Legos is coming out with more of these \\"young builder\\" sets. These are not Lego Duplo's. These are everyday legos with larger bases for example the car base. The car base helps a child in the age range of 2 years of age plus start building and being creative with everyday legos.

Inside this very sturdy bin with great yellow/orange latches that my four year old can open on his own. The blue box has been in and out of the car multiple times and for some reason no matter how much my son seems to non intentionally harm it, it does not break. He has sat on it a few times, dropped it, and for some reason this bin is great and holds all the pieces in there spaces!

Inside there are handy dividers. So for instance if you build a car and want the bricks in a different compartment you can do this. It's so neat to be able to separate the legos by color and have completed items stay in there space at all times. The dividers are great and WTG Lego's! Inside there are 5 blue dividers that you can use or put aside- they simply slip in or out at your discretion.

Additionally the booklet is 17 pages long. I have taken the staples out of mine and laminated it just to kid proof it a little more. Don't be discouraged with the 17 pages though most pages only have two steps per page thus making it easy for a child to see what they may want to build and be successful in building it. The pages show the steps on how to build the items on one page and the other page shows the item completed thus giving a child/parent confidence in building the set.

I am buying more of these!

product_title: ITALERI 550225 1/35 Sherman M4-A1 ITAS0225
review_headline: Actually a decent model kit - NOT A TOY!!!
review_body:
This kit from Italeri is several years old and not as detailed as the latest Shermans from Dragon and the other top names, but with a bit of work, this kit holds its own (I've built a half dozen of this guy). First task, ditch the tracks as they are as stiff as my old drill sergeant's spine. I usually get the rubber tracks offered by AFV, available at online shops. I keep my stiff tracks to use for impressions in mud and slush on dioramas.
I usually replace the barrel with an aftermarket one that are available at several online model shops. Just watch the price and types. Now, once the hull and road wheel assembles are don (they are really pretty basic) and stowage is added (I use items from Black Dog, Verlinden but there are several good companies out there if you search) and any additional hull armor add ons - planks, spare tracks, sandbags etc... a nice primer coat and the finish OD coat. Now the fun starts, splashing on mud, brush, twigs, clumps of dried dirt, leaves and the plethora of stains and filters you can have a pretty decent kit. Toss the kit figures as they look like scarecrows and add in some Dragon figs with Hornet heads and presto! Ready for the hedgerows.
Four bogie wheels for this inexpensive Sherman

product_title: Transformers Construct-A-Bots Optimus Prime Vs. Megatron Construction Set
review_body:
We received this toy as part of a BzzCampaign from BzzAgent (which basically means we got it for free in exchange for giving our honest, thorough review on the product). When we were selected for this BzzCampaign, I was a little hesitant at first...I mean, come on...a transformers toy that would actually transform into from a bot to a vehicle and back again without having to remove or disassemble anything? I'm glad that I was wrong. This toy arrived yesterday and my 6 year old son has been playing with it non stop.
Pros:
* Instructions to build each figure are very well illustrated. My child was able to lay his pieces out in the correct configuration and assemble each bot pretty much on his own from the beginning.
* Pieces snapped together easily and stayed together until you truly wanted to disassemble the piece. And then, pieces snapped off easily without fear of breaking or bending something.
* Imagination is a huge piece of the puzzle here. Once the skeleton is put together, the possibilities really are endless with how you can assemble the bots.
* Fine motor skills play into this toy in a big way. The pieces need to be put on in the correct way and some of the ball/socket pieces need a little "oomph" behind them to get them in properly. If you have a child (like I do) that lacks a little in the fine motor skill area, this is a great activity to help them with that.

Cons:
* Transformation - the instructions in the booklet that came with the toy are a little unclear when trying to follow the steps to transform the Bot into a vehicle. However - after figuring it out and doing it a couple of times, it becomes much easier to do.
* App - the app for iphone is a little confusing. You have to "purchase" the pieces you need to build your bot with points. When you download the app you automatically receive an allotment of points and it looks like with each toy you purchase, you receive a voucher for more. This was a little hard for me (and my son) to grasp. You build this bot on the app but may or may not be able to build it with your pieces (in real life) because you may not have every single piece that is a choice in the app. I feel like the app has a lot of possibility, but it's not quite the best part about these toys.

Overall - a great toy that will provide many hours of fun and creativity.

product_title: Crayola Ultimate Crayon Collection, 152 Pieces, Art Set, Gift
review_headline: This COULD HAVE BEEN a great product...
review_body:
As a marketing professional, I bring a critical perspective to products that others might see in a much simpler light. Take a crayon case, for example. Crayola, the KING of crayons, thought consumers would love a case to hold 152 crayons. I thought my kids would love it, too. After receiving it and trying it out, I cannot help but think of all the cool things this case could have been, rather than just a yellow hunk of plastic that holds crayons.

I normally like to point out all the great things about products, but this is an exception. Other than holding 152 crayons, this case really does not offer much. Instead, I will focus on all the things YOU WILL NOT FIND with this product, that would have been really neat.

THINGS I WISH THIS CASE OFFERED, BUT IT DOES NOT:

1. Spinning/Carousel Base: It is impossible for a little one to see all the crayons that are arranged to face 4 different directions around the center of the case. So, why not make the case rotate, rather than making the kid walk around it or pick up the entire case?

2. Grouping/Organization: Rather than 152 colors dispersed somewhat randomly, why not use the case to help bring some sort of organization to the colors? For instance, there is one box that is full of metallics. There is another box full of glitter crayons. However, the only way I knew this was by pulling out the individual crayons and using deductive reasoning. Why not label the groups and do more groups to help make sense of such a large assortment?

3. A Lid with a Clasp: There is a very cheap plastic lid with this case that I am certain will be discarded by most purchasers who think it is simply packing material--not worthy of keeping for the long haul. However, if you don't keep that cheap piece of plastic, then you have NO LID AT ALL. It would have been nice if they had thought about a case of crayons that will almost certainly be transported by a little one who might drop it.

4. Cooler Sharpener: This case has a sharpener, but it is inconveniently located in the middle of the case, and it is sunken down low. It really isn't even all that easy to see. Then, to sharpen a crayon, a kid must hold the crayon vertically and turn it. Sure, all of this is possible, but with a big case like this, a better solution could have been designed that is easier to access and use.

5. Refill Friendly Design: My kids use washable crayons, which do not come with this case. However, the only way that I could put their crayons into this case would be to buy 16-count boxes of crayons, as this case is really only designed to hold that size of box (actually, there is one box in the case that holds 24, but the rest hold 16 crayons). Practically speaking, the life of this case is going to be pretty short if it is not easy to refill with one's own crayons down the road.

In summary, if you are just looking for a throw-away plastic case full of 152 crayons, then this product is for you. If, on the other hand, you are hoping for a case that is designed to stand the test of time and provide some unique and useful features and benefits for your little ones, you'll be disappointed like me.it.

product_title: Android Netrunner: The Card Game
review_body:
I recognize a *lot* of people love this game. So I kept trying to learn to like it. But in the end, I just don't get the appeal. I suspect (but have no evidence) that people who like this game also like Magic The Gathering, a game I never played. There are similar game mechanics here, so perhaps that is part of the appeal for those who like it.

Problems:
First, the game is very complicated. To me, that's an upside -- it means the game has the potential to be very interesting. The problem is that the rule book is absolutely terrible. You simply cannot learn to play this game without consulting many different online videos, fan-made rule books, or forums that discuss the rules. The rule book is horribly organized and neither walks you through learning the game in a logically progressive way nor serves an adequate reference book when you have questions. I'd rather do my taxes than deal with the rule book for this game.

Second, the base game has decks (identities) and functions that are nearly worthless. Perhaps these identities & functions make sense when mixed with expansions for the game (which I never bought), but if that's true, then the base game should include those expansions from the get go.

Third, and this may be an intrinsic problem with deck building games of this type, players can win or lose very quickly depending on luck of the draw (especially early in the game). Yes, there's skill in building a smart deck (once you have the expansions to make many cards/identities in the base game actually worth something) and yes, once you play many games, better players will more often win. But if you just want to sit down and play one or two games with someone, it can easily feel like the major points are won/lost by luck of the draw. And that's just unacceptable for a good game.

For my money, deck building games like Dominion are leaps and bounds better than Android: Netrunner.

product_title: Step2  Tropical Island Resort
review_headline: Kids love it but VERY hard to keep algae from growing in the island
review_body: Wonderful toy for a three year old from the kid's point of view, but the construction makes it impossible to clean.  Water accumulates in the island shape (that is attached to the main toy by a large screw) and even when we emptied the toy each day, algae and other unappealing things grew in the island and would leak out bit by bit into the main water area.  It took me a while to figure out what the problem was.  I finally took the whole thing apart and cut three large drainage holes in the bottom of the island with a knife (the underside where it doesn't show) and cleaned it out with bleach and a bottle brush.  Hopefully that will keep things from growing down there in the future.  It is an example of lack of product testing in a real life environment.  Too bad, because the overall concept was lots of fun, the people, boats, etc. were a great addition for imaginative play.  It's not a question of durability or educational value (as per star categories), but complete lack of foresight of design feasibility over more than one time use.  As a UX design person (and someone who likes kids' toys to be cleanable), both surprising and disappointing.

product_title: Disney Planes Wing Control Dusty Crophopper Radio Control Plane
review_headline: This is NOT a flying toy
review_body:
If you look at the pictures on the box, it seems to show Dusty flying thru the air, in front of the boy with the controllers. On bottom of the box, however, in eighth inch letters, is written \\"This is not a flying toy\\". My first response was \\"ahh!\\", but if you look at the body of the plane, it would be aerodynamically impossible to fly, unless you were in a zero gravity. Since the boy I got this for is only 5, its actually great that it doesn't fly. Those flying planes require big open space, no electric wires or trees, and they STILL crash. If you want to introduce a child to radio controlled toys, this isn't a bad place to start. The box recommends age 10 or older, but with a little bit of supervision, you can start them out younger. If the kid forgets to turn off the plane when done playing, there's an automatic shut off to conserve battery life.

When it comes to operation, I had a few problems. First, you need a large, flat area to play upon. It wont move thru grass, and any obstruction before the \\"flight path\\" of Dusty, will cause him to tip over, or stop. I tested it on a car port, but had to sweep it first. A sidewalk wont work, cos the plane tends to waver in its flight plan. IF you tilt the controller off level, the plane turns. So unless you have a child who keeps their outstretched arms perfectly level to the ground, the plane turns. The thumb button on the controller gives it forward motion, but there are no breaks. So its way too chaotic in motion, to work in a small to mid sized play room, unless you don't mind turning the plane a lot. (and kids don't) It has all kinds of crazy sayings in the DUSTY character voice. \\"Bank left!\\" or \\"Hi, I'm Dusty, well, my name is Dusty.\\" There are some preprogrammed flight planes if you hit that button on top of the plane, but not for in the house.

As long as you don't expect too much functionality, or control with the plane, and you have a flat, large play space, this is a really fun toy. It helps if the child intended loves that Disney show, PLANES. It also helps if you give this to the child WITH BATTERIES, cos they are not included. Buy 4AA and 2AAA alkaline batteries, and have a Phillips head screw driver ready, to set up the toy when its unwrapped. Happy Flying!ps if the child intended loves that Disney show, PLANES. product_title: LeapFrog LeapPad Ultra/Ultra XDI Kids' Learning Tablet
review_body:
If you have kids who have been using Leapfrog's various game platforms, especially the LeapPad, the Ultra extends the usable life of the platform for your child a bit longer by making it more tablet like. A larger screen with higher resolution and wifi to connect to the internet (what appears to be a very limited browser was still in development when I last checked) give older kids more to play with.

A notable difference between the Ultra and regular LeapPads is that the Ultra has a built-in, non-changeable rechargable battery. It generally lasts a long time and charges relatively quickly (several hours) but could present a problem for long trips.

As a parent, when setting up the Ultra you are prompted to log in with a PIN so be sure to write this down or use something memorable. This allows the parents access to the store but keeps kids from making unapproved purchases and changes to the account. In essence, this step takes the place of downloading and installing LeapFrog Connect. Once connected, you have access to apps for the Ultra as well as any other applicable apps that may have worked on the smaller LeapPads. This is a nice touch - some companies might not allow something as simple as sharing apps like this. What bugged me was that there is no way to tell what has been already downloaded or is downloading. All apps available in your account are simply marked \\"Download\\" and don't change once chosen.

As an adult, I find I'm annoyed by some things kids don't seem to care about - so take these from that angle. The on-screen keyboard is *very* sensitive and lead to many mistypes, which was especially frustrating while setting up our wifi password. Swiping between screens is a hit and miss affair. Sometimes you get it to swipe, sometimes not and you wind up opening an app.

These issues are minor. As an adult you expect more - you would rip Apple to shreds for behavior like this on an iPad. Your kids will love it, however, just like mine do - they don't notice these minor problems. It's bigger, brighter, bolder, better in almost every way. product_title: DC Collectibles Batman: Arkham Origins: Series 1 Bane Action Figure
review_body:
The main reason for me to get this figure is because it reminds me of my late overweight Uncle Kelley but, extremely kind freelance luchadore. In fact, I do not recall him ever winning a single match. Most of his wrestling matches were solo acts for children's birthday parties and Bar Mitzvahs that he would always manage lose at to the cheers of many youthful onlookers.
With me being the middle child of four brothers and five sisters, our parents ran a small business stocking claw machines at Mexican grocery stores. Often times, they would stock a machine and then have to completely refill it in under five minutes after highly-skilled Mexican with a couple of dollars would entirely \\"grab\\" everything with the claw. This would cause my parents to be gone for days to weeks at a time as they ran their modest business.
Uncle Kelley would fill-in for them while they were gone. To us, he was always a hero. He would show up at our door dressed in one of his one-size-too-small white unitards with corresponding mask, douse his body in whatever kind of oil we had (such as baby oil, suntan oil or peanut cooking oil) and wrestle us in the back yard where our empty ground pool doubled as a wrestling ring.
One night after watching an episode of 'Survivor' in Spanish, we all decided to go into the back yard for another wrestling match. We lit up several tiki torches around the ground pool for a nice tribal effect while playing the music from 'Jock Jams' on our boom box. Uncle Kelley covered his body with buttery cooking oil as he entered the ring. What should of been a fun wrestling match turned into one of the most horrific things I have ever seen.
Uncle Kelley got too close to the flame and ignited himself up like it was Cinco de Mayo and the Festival of San Fermin combined.
Not having a phone or knowing the number to nine-one-one in Spanish, all of us just stood there and stared as we helplessly watched him flail about as a headless chicken until he collapsed on the mat and eventually stopped moving.
A few days later, our parents returned home and we held a small funeral for Uncle Kelley. What was left of his remains went into a trash can on the curbside. It pulled out at the last second, probably realizing something wasn't right, flew to a nearby tree and kept his eye on us.  A super cool moment for us both. product_title: Bandai Tamashii Nations Sailor Moon S.H. Figuarts Action Figure [Resale Editon]
review_body:
I have to admit I haven't been this excited about a collectible in a long time. Sailor moon is all about nostalgia for me. It was the first anime I ever got into. That being said, I have never been this disappointed.

I checked out the reviews before placing my order for the figure and noticed the various complaints about damaged boxes. As a collector this is a HUGE deal breaker. I went ahead and made my order anyway and selected 2 day shipping hoping that the less the package was handled the better it will be upon arrival. Boy was I wrong. Once I completed my order I called Amazon to voice my concern about the figure's original packaging being damaged in transit. They assured me they would take every precaution to ensure the it arrives in good, undamaged condition.

It was very upsetting to find the mangled box that arrived on my door step. The Amazon box looked like someone had just stomped on it. The entire bottom half was smashed. I had no doubt of what condition the actual figure packaging would be in upon seeing the state of the outer packaging. There was no bubble wrap or anything remotely protecting the interior. Only a single sheet of defeated bubble at the bottom of the box. I didn't even get an invoice inside the box. Not to mention it sounds like something is rattling inside of the box...maybe some of the pieces came loose. I didn't know I chose not to open the figure just incase.

I called Amazon again and told them what happened. I was treated very nicely and promised the issue would be resolved. They said that they would ship a second figure through one day shipping and email me a return label to return the damaged one at no extra cost to me. I was pleased with this but I'm still concerned with the fact that I have yet to receive the email regarding the return or a confirmation of the new shipment. Perhaps they need more time, but If I don't receive some kind of notice by Monday I will be calling them again.

This is all very disappointing considering I plan to order the rest of the sailor scouts as they are released. I would not like to have this problem with the rest of the figures. PLEASE FIX THE PACKING AMAZON! a BIGGER BOX with maybe some bubble wrap and packing peanuts would help!

*update

Amazon has given excellent customer service. I got my return label and a shipping confirmation for the new figure. Hopefully, there are no more issues with the shipment/transit of my figuart and moreso I hope this solves future issues for other collectors that order these figures. I definitely can not complain about amazon's customer service they have been great every step of the way.

product_title: Flinch with FREE Playing Card Deck
review_body:
Flinch is a game that fills a niche in my gaming collection. For the 9-12 years old crowd and the not so interested in games gang, this is a good transition game. (I have a lot of gamer friends and a lot of non-gamer and professional associates that get uncomfortable when the gang breaks out \\"Apples to Apples.\\") Flinch gives me a middle ground, way out.

This game reminds me a great deal of [[ASIN:B008NZ3QVE Dutch Blitz Card Game [GAME-DUTCH BLITZ] [Other]]]. In both cases you are trying to get rid of cards in a particular pile by quickly playing cards in sequences on other piles. Flinch is a turn based game, and Dutch Blitz is a raucous, no holds bar, blitz game with everyone playing at the same time. I've given away a few Dutch Blitz games, because my main objection is that it is super easy to cheat at it, and Dutch Blitz always devolves into a meta-game. The players quickly gravitate into one of two camps, those that don't cheat and those that push the envelope further and further until one half of the group is doing nothing but watching the other group in an effort to curb the cheating. I know a lot of folks that love Dutch Blitz.

Flinch eliminates the cheating loophole by ensuring that everyone must pay attention to every turn by every player, because if you see that a player has made an error then you can score points by correcting the mistake and calling \\"Flinch.\\" (The original title was probably filch for obvious reasons.)

This was likely quite scandalous back in 1921 when a giggling flapper pointed out that a starched collar business man failed to make a correct play. Oh chucky dorn!

Some older games like Sheep's Head, Hearts, Spades, Napoleon, Oh Pshaw!, and others have aged well and are just as exciting today as they were in their salad days, but Flinch really feels like a parlor game.

If you have a timid group of players or kids on the cusp of 9-11 years old then this might be a game that satisfies the needs of your group.

If you often host games at your home and have a new group, or you are looking for new alternatives, Flinch could be a good pick.

product_title: KRE-O CityVille Invasion Marina Madness Set (A3249)
review_body: My son and I received the Kre-O Cityville Invasion Marina Madness Building set for free for review purposes through BzzAgent. If I had to give this set a rating out of 10 stars, I would give it a solid 8. The only complaint I really have is that some of the pieces are super-duper tiny, and I have a semi-clumsy/forgetful son which means we end up missing small tiny pieces that never get found. That being said, we have had this set since the end of August and none have gone missing just yet. Also, if your child's fine motor skills are not very fine-tuned this can be a bit of an issue. There were a couple of pieces that I had to help him put together and he is 8 years old. Everything else I have to say about this set is absolutely positive. Let me start out by saying that my son is not one of those building set geniuses who can look at the display on the front of a box and whip it up in a matter of minutes without using the instructions. I think the reason he enjoys sets like this so much is because they do provide a bit of a challenge, but are not out of his league. He also was so surprised and excited by the fact that this set provides movement and noise, whereas most of the traditional sets like these do not. It allows him to still use his imagination, but have more real noise and excitement at the same time. He has already added some of the other sets to his Wish List so I know they are a big hit with him. Additionally, whereas most toys find themselves collecting dust in our house, this one does not. It honestly is a toy that he plays with very often. While we did get this set free for review, I do know that the sets are very reasonably priced and available at most stores, and you can grab an even better deal here on Amazon.

review_body:

The deck itself is good enough to be played against several experienced players, however, I would recommend touching it up a bit. It has a few high costing burn cards which can be easily substituted for burn cards that deal more damage for less the mana.

I tested this deck against my Tournament Burn deck and though it was able to put up a fight, my Deck annihilated it. The person using this deck was one of my friends and also a very experienced player as well. So it was the deck, not the player. So again, I recommend breaking this deck down and building it up burn cards that suits your gameplay. Its a great deck out of the box, but if you want it to be a true burn deck, it needs some touch ups.

IE:
-4 Artillerize for 4 Lightning Bolts
-1 Infiltration Lens for 1 Curse of Stalked Prey
etc etc.

Might want to change up the Creature a bit too. However I highly recommend keeping the Goblin Grenade combo strategy. I'll let you figure out how to use that if you don't already.

product_title: ALEX Toys Active Play Monkey Balance Board
review_headline: Sturdy and well made, able to take rough play
review_body:
I purchased a balance board for my very active (then) 3 year old for Christmas. She was a bit intimidated at first, especially since we tried it on a hardwood floor--it slipped when she tried to step on it, and she was afraid she would fall. We eventually got her to try it out by putting on a carpeted floor, and she's been using it almost daily since then. She is very rough on her toys, and the balance board still looks brand new 8 months later, which is unheard of around here! She has gotten very good at balancing on the board, and often invents games that involve jumping on/off, twirling, trying to stand on one foot, etc using the board. It is difficult to keep her occupied AND burn off some excess energy when we are stuck inside--the balance board is definitely our go-to toy for rainy afternoons!

Update 4 years later: Yep, this still gets played with. Still in great shape, too! My now almost 8 year old keeps it in her room for using as a fidget-board when she's working at her desk: she stands on it while she draws or reads. She is still awfully hard on her toys, and this balance board has held up beautifully to years of being used as a table/'skateboard'/doll bed/TV watching accessory/desk tool. Her 4 year old sister now borrows it to balance on as well, and it's great to see a toy being used so much--definitely, DEFINITELY worth what I paid for it 4 years ago, and the price has dropped dramatically since then. I'm buying a second for my nephew for Christmas!

product_title: Dungeon Twister 2 Prison
review_body:
Having played [[ASIN:B0024H7OF6 Small World]], [[ASIN:B003L5CXW4 Defenders of The Realm]] and [[ASIN:B006473RZS Super Dungeon Explore]] recently, I can certainly say that this game is quite enjoyable in their midst. Unlike the other games, this game (without any expansions) is designed specifically for two players (or one, if that's your thing), whereas the others are 2+. Unlike DotR (a coop game) you are playing versus in an attempt to kill the other player or make it to the other side, all for precious Victory Points.

Directions are decent to read, they introduce you to concepts through five tutorial scenarios. You can play through them adding complexity as you go or, like we did, just read them and jump in to a full game afterwards. Rules aren't too bad (SDE has the worst rulebook I've ever read, others are fine) and are easy to pick up. The game seems decently balanced and weighted well between each characters. There is just enough strategy to keep it enjoyable, guessing what your opponent will do next, but not so much that your brain bleeds. Five stars in design, in my opinion.

The only docked star is on durability - the models are a flexible plastic which, while good for preventing brittle breaks, caused one character to arrive in a Matrix-like back bend. Still stands, it's all good.

Overall I'd say this game is worth it. Seems like there is a decent amount of replayability, fun to be had and strategy to keep you on your toes. Plus the expansions if you get bored, so who can complain?

product_title: Set of Seven Vampire: the Eternal Struggle Beginner Decks VTES Jyhad Starter Deck
review_headline: Some cards have different backs, some are scratched/damaged.
review_body:
First off, I haven't played enough of the game to rate the selection of cards or the synergy of the decks, so this brief review is simply going to point out a couple major issues with the decks themselves.

First off, some of these cards are old. Very old. I understand that this game isn't exactly flying off the press by the hour at this time, but many of the cards look old, straight out of the 90s, and have many white flecks on them where the ink and finish came off, which leads me to my 2nd (more important) warning.

For those of you that do not know, Vampire: the Eternal Struggle was originally named (and branded) Jyhad in its first run(s), and later renamed to the title you see today. \\"Why is this an issue?\\", you may ask. The problem with the product I am reviewing is that these cards come from various versions of the game, so some are from Vampire: The Eternal Struggle, and some are Jyhad. ON THE BACK OF THE CARDS.

This simple fact gives a very inconsistent look to the decks, as well as granting a strange transparency and possible metagame advantage: You might know which of your cards are from Jyhad, and which ones aren't; therefore giving you knowledge of what's on the other side of the cards.

Though I am not that experienced in this game yet, my experience with Magic: The Gathering and its players is enough to know that serious Collectible Card Game players are walking Wikipedias of card information, and would totally use the inconsistent card backs to their advantage, whether consciously or not.

Overall, a serious player or collector may not want to go with this bargain bundle for the above reasons. You have been warned.

product_title: LeapFrog LeapReader Interactive World Map (works with Tag)
review_headline: Six Stars! Learn World Geography the Fun and Effective Way
review_body:
My Five Year Old is playing and learning nonstop with the LeapReader Interactive World Map. Basically, you get a two-sided map of the world. One side has just geographical borders and the games center around finding the countries. The simple map structure makes it easy to discern country locations and relationships. My daughter tends to need help with this side. The other side includes continent names and includes graphical representations of climate, topography, landmarks, and cultural distinctives. This side has many activities and games centered on teaching about the countries. The pictures allow the LeapReader pen to direct her more independently to find and understand the geography or other information being taught.

It is incredible to see how much she has learned and the passion she has developed for learning about the world. A few days ago she didn't know the difference between states, countries, and continents. Now she not only understands this but can quickly find Djibouti, Japan, Madagascar, Norway, Chile, Mexico, and more. I can't imagine a more effective way to introduce a child to basic world geography.

I highly recommend you pair this with [[ASIN:B003GIS8TS LeapFrog LeapReader Interactive World Map]], which does just as good of a job of teaching about the United States in a similar manner.

My daughter has begun augmenting her LeapFrog learning by wanting and playing with geography apps on her iPad.

product_title: Nerf CS-18 N-Strike Elite Rapidstrike
review_headline: A Vast Improvement Over the Stampede and Vulcan
review_body:
Among the very few fully automatic dart guns Nerf has ever made, this one is simply the best. It is smaller, lighter, quieter, and shoots at a faster rate than either the Stampede or the Vulcan.

It has a well-made feel to it (as most of Nerf's dart guns do), it feels comfortable, and there are no parts that creak as if they're going to fall off. It's also nowhere near as finicky about being used as the Stryfe, which I think set the high bar for being annoying about having a zillion-and-one ways and so-called reasons for stopping you from firing it.

It is possible to do single-shot firing, as well as just holding the trigger to spray darts. The only caveat is that you have to disciplined enough to remember to continuously hold the lower trigger to keep the flywheel motors running -- if you don't, then single-shot firing can easily result in jamming on a dart.

It is a shame that they're selling this with just an 18-dart clip -- at least the Stampede was shipped in an elaborate kit that included multiple clips and a bandolier belt to carry them. This gun deserves to be provided with a similar set of equipment. But, to be honest, this gun doesn't really come into its own unless you use the 35-dart drum magazine with it. I've tried this combination, and it really makes this the complete keep-your-enemy's-head-down kind of gun.

There are only three complaints that I would put against it...
1) The motors driving the flywheels really are noisier than they need to be -- the motors in the Stryfe are definitely quieter.
2) The ability to attach barrel extensions to the front of this gun is not well implemented -- almost all of the barrel extensions wobble in place a bit when attached to the front. On the other hand, this gun is already sufficiently long that it's hard to see why you would want to make it much longer -- maybe Nerf has some other forthcoming barrel extension in mind?
3) The battery compartment really should have been put towards the rear of this gun -- with the battery compartment being built in up front, this gun is a bit nose-heavy, which makes one-handed operation a little unrealistic -- if the battery compartment had been put towards the back, the weight of the four C-cells could have been supported by a fore-arm.

Only the first complaint is what I would call a significant one -- the noisy flywheel motors take away any possibility of sneaking up on somebody with this with the motors running. It's the one advantage that the Stampede and Vulcan have over this gun -- neither of those guns needed to make a sound at all until you were ready to pull the trigger. If you carry this dart gun with you, you'll need to have a simpler manually-operated spring-type dart gun for that initial sneak-attack shot -- and then you can use this dart gun to spray darts when everyone already knows you're there.

I recommend this.

An update -- 11/6/13...

I still recommend this dart gun. However, I also recommend setting aside its 18-dart clear plastic clip and picking up one of the 35-dart drum magazines to use with it, instead. Having had this dart gun for a while, I'm noticing that the spring in the 18-dart clear plastic clip seems to have become somewhat weaker, and the something about the plastic that the clip is made from somehow causes or enables a great deal of friction between the tips of the dart and the interior of the clip. As a result, the darts don't immediately move up the clip as they are fired, which appears to be leading to frequent jamming.

The 35-drum magazines seem to be made of a plastic that doesn't suffer from this weird friction issue -- I don't know if it's actually a difference in the plastic material or maybe a slight difference in smoothness of the interior that causes differences in friction -- but the darts do seem to stick more to the interior of the new clear 18-dart clip. Also, frankly,the 35-dart drum was always the better choice for a dart gun like this, anyway. It can go through darts so quickly with its rapid rate of fire that an 18-dart clip is used up too quickly.

product_title: Be Amazing Toys Big Bag Of Science +70 Activities
review_headline: This is a toy, not a science kit, and it's not a very good toy.  If you want a science toy, there are better options
review_body:
I love science. I'm an engineer and a father, and science fills our lives. I am always looking for great science projects to do with my kids and things they can do on their own. The problem is that chemistry and science kits today are dumbed down from the kits when I was a kid - they tend to be mostly toys, lacking some of the cooler experiments I remember. Want to know why kids want to be lawyers rather than scientists and engineers? I blame the dumbing down of science through programs like STEM, but I digress - this is a review of a product, and I want to make sure you know if it is something to buy your kid. I will review it for what it is - a kids toy science kit.

So you hand this to your kids and tell them to have fun with it. First problem, the activities are really for a 5-7 year old, but the instructions are written for a kid who is at least 9 or older. My [[ASIN:B004OYYAUE The Magic School Bus - Chemistry Lab]] came with colorful cards each with an experiment. This \\"Big Bag\\" comes with a black and white instruction book filled with dense text and instructions. You can't just hand this to your kids and off they go - you need to read it with them. Not much of a toy if the kid can't even play with it themselves.

The first \\"experiment\\" is to put 3 different color alka-seltzer tablets into one of three different test tubes. Yes - you've colored water. If your kid has made lemonade, they've done this one. The second is to hold the test tubes up to light to \\"mix\\" the light color (ever held up two balloons to the light? I thought so). The third is to mix the colored water with a pipette. Yes - if your kids play with paint, they've done this too. Lots of the experiments are various types of hygroscopic chemicals (powder, marbles, shapes) that you get wet, watch swell, and then color with the alka-seltzer.

Even for these, the powders and hygroscopic shapes come in relatively poor quality plastic baggies that can't really be resealed. Other similar kits I have bought have resealable jars or bottles. These cheap baggies just make a mess and really only let you use them once.

The coolest was the calcium chloride and sodium alginate - make a solution of calcium chloride and drizzle in sodium alginate and you get cool long streams of worms. Okay - it was fun, but once you do it once, you've used up all the material for it.

Some of the more interesting experiments require things not included. Yes - the first page of the kit tells you things that \\"you get it\\" yourself (meaning you have to search the house for it), including a nail, bowl, cup, string, spoon, ruler, straw, battery, ziplock bag, mixing tray, etc. Lots of the experiments require 2-liter bottles of soda. So after coloring water and making slimy shapes, you will be running out for 2-liter soda bottles.

70 activities is also a bit of an exaggeration.

For example:

Activity 62: Flower Holder. Fill the test tube with water and use it as a flower vase.

Activity 64: Message in a Bottle. Place a message in the test tube and seal it with a cap. Put it in the pool and float to a friend.

Activity 69: Rhythm Tube. Fill the test tube with beads and pebbles and shake it. Yes - this is \\"Life Science\\".

The worst... Activity 57: Time Capsule. Use the large test tube to hide a message to open in the future.

In other words, this is a toy, and not a good one at that. My kids all agreed that the Magic School Bus was a better overall kit. It is more colorful and fun - neither has really advanced chemistry, but the Magic School Bus was at least more interesting for them to do on their own.

product_title: Flutterbye Flying Fairy
review_headline: Fun Flying Fairies Will Take Over Your Home!
review_body:
One of the first things I noticed with this toy were the details that the toy company put into the fairy itself. The toy was beautiful, and my daughter thought so as well. The toy itself takes 6 AA batteries (which is a lot), but what these batteries make the toy do is pretty unique and cool. Seeing that the toy itself does take a lot of batteries I might recommend using lithium batteries for longevity if use. I did not try this with rechargeable batteries so do not know how well they would work with this, but it is a possibility that these may also work well. The batteries are placed in the docking station (as I call it) for the fairy and charges the fairy itself. This station is also the launching station for the fairy too. By charging your fairy and then hitting the button you are able to launch the fairy into the air and then by placing your hand underneath the fairy you can control where she goes and how high she flies.

I have to say that my daughters loved controlling heir fairy and they thought this was a very fun toy to use. As mentioned above I decided to use lithium as I surmised that I could need them, and so far they have been working great. My five and nine year old girls were able to control the fairy with no problems and the biggest problem that we had was having the girls share the fairy!

All-in-all this was a fun toy and one that I am sure that your kids will love too!

product_title: WayWord
review_body:
Why surprising? Because it was a \\"free with your order\\" game I received and therefore didn't expect much.

There are a bunch of hex pieces, each with a letter on them. Depending upon common frequency of the letter, it has 1 to 3 points. A number of tiles are randomly set up to start the game. During his/her turn, each player tries to make a word using the tiles in play, but only by \\"walking\\" his/her token from tile to tile. For example, \\"BET\\" is a word only if the \\"E\\" is adjacent to both the B and the T! The word must start from the tile the token is currently at, and if a tile is currently covered by another token, it may not be used in the word. You will quickly hate your co-players, believe me. \\"Why did you have to end on the S tile?\\" \\"Sure, block the only E on the board. Thanks.\\"

To add to gameplay, some tiles are special, allowing the player who walks on them in the midst of his/her word to jump elsewhere on the board, double or triple the points for the word, or other goodies. After a given number of turns (depending upon player count), the highest score wins.

We play this regularly, and it continues to baffle us while putting smiles on our faces. Winning this game gives a player a true sense of accomplishment!

product_title: Bachmann Trains Pcc Trolley Los Angeles Railway
review_headline: Bachmann has changed/upgraded in the running mechanism. Excellent move Bachmann!
review_body: This review is on the HO scale. Bachmann formerly used a very low, low, quality motor to run their trolleys. They have reconstructed their configuration to a stand alone real motor. This is an excellent upgrade. I believe the stand alone motor type will be in their new \\"Blue\\" style box. If you see the old white box, it is not the up graded version. I believe this is true. I have purchased 4 new Bachmann (Blue Box) new style, and they run great. They also are very quiet running, because all those plastic gears in the old style are gone. As far as cost and \\"new\\" design, you will be very pleased. The only thing I wish Bachmann could consider is one more light inside the trolley. It still is a great buy, and with the new design, would purchase and would recommend Bachmann Products. I have run my trollies for several hours at a time, and have had no problems. They are not meant to run for days at a time. If you wanted to run them all day, you would need to go to a good train store and upgrade the motor to a higher quality motor that can withstand a longer running time but for running for several hours or so, I have had no problems. It is a good idea to take your trolley, even if it is new and have it lubed and oiled at a train store. You can oil your trolley. I believe instructions are included, or you can find it on line, or u-tube. Use a minimal amount of oil. Easy access to motor, and interior. You can feel the underside. If it is hot, you are running them for to long a period of time, or it just may need to be serviced. They also need to serviced (oil and lube) periodically, depending on how often you run them. I would say at least once a year, depending on your running time. Out of he box, they run very well. The price and the quality are excellent for the price you pay [[ASIN:B0013K4QZG Bachmann Trains PCC Trolley Los Angeles Railway]]. The detail is excellent. Interior lights, tail lights,and a headlight. I wish they had 1 more interior light towards the rear of the interior, but it still is very nice. You cannot run the power thru the pole. product_title: Takara Tomy Transformers Masterpieces MP-12(Japan Import)
review_body:
Not realizing that the newest verion of MP Optimus Prime is much smaller than the one I have (doesn't even reach the top of my version's shoulders), I expected Sideswipe to be considerably bigger (as the size comparisons I've seen have him standing next to Optimus). In fact, he is not much bigger than the Generations version of Sideswipe.

Sideswipe is also entirely plastic. No diecast metal at all. He feels a little flimsy as well.

On the bright side, his transformation is intricate, without being too complex (the only problem being that I was afraid of something breaking off the first time I tried it).

Not a bad Transformer overall, but I would only recommend to die hard MP collectors, or to collectors that are looking to have a complete collection of every version of Sideswipe.

product_title: LEGO The DeLorean Time Machine Building Set 21103 (Discontinued by manufacturer)
review_headline: What a great set!  Great fun, great investment!
review_body:
First, let me say that the photos do not do this set justice. I saw the original prototype model and was initially disappointed that this didn't seem to look as good. However, after seeing it in person and a side by side with the prototype, I can say that not only is it better in every way, this is a great looking kit!

It feels accurate to the show, and it's got enough room for Marty and Doc Brown to fit in the DeLorean and go on adventures, so there's a lot of play opportunity here. Whether you're a collector or a kid, not only is it a fun build, it's great to display and fun to play with. I've bought a lot of LEGO and I can't remember the last time I was this satisfied with a kit.

Plus, if you're a collector/investor like me, this is going to be a great set for investment. This comes from the same line as the Minecraft set, which jumped 400% in value the day it was discontinued. LEGO started making it again, so you can still buy it, but the fact remains that these are low production sets with huge demand and appeal. I think this will do better over time than Minecraft, because Back to the Future is not only a classic, but there are some very unique bricks in here that will be useful for other Back to the Future builds. Not to mention Doc Brown and Marty are pretty unique licensed characters that won't be found anywhere else, it's not uncommon for figures like these to sell for upwards of $20 a piece!

No matter why you're thinking about buying this set, you should stop reading this review -- and all the others -- and just buy it already. I can't think of a better LEGO set for the price in the past 10 years.

product_title: DC Comics Classic TV Series Batman and Robin Action Figure (Discontinued by manufacturer)
review_headline: Some days you just can't please all toy collectors.
review_body:
As someone who grew up loving the 60s show as a kid, then hating that it was the only way the world at large could conceive of Batman during the gritty \\"Dark Knight\\" 80s, particularly when those same folk were aghast at how \\"dark\\" the character seemed in the now-campy-in-retrospect Tim Burton films and later 90s sequels, then coming full circle and loving the nostalgia of the colorful, on-purpose campiness after being grittydarkknighted for one super serious Miller/Nolan Batman tale too many, just out of the novelty it now had exuded, I feel I can comment on the experience of finally owning these figures, as we have a history that is as long as this sentence.

I felt the likenesses were pretty good (especially Adam West's Batman) and the articulation is more than adequate to get them into the contortions required for the wall-climbing scene they were designed to acheive as their preferred display. I even secured the very cool building facade base to a vertical \\"building\\" (i.e. a cardboard box spraypainted gray) to test their ability to stay on their pegs when at a true 90degree angle and they never came off, even when I picked up the whole building and moved it around. The \\"batrope\\" is really just some black paper-twine, not proportional, but the thick size fits the molded grip hands (only with the clear rubber bands, if you lose them it will slip out easily) and the wires in the cape don't really function for their purpose (to keep the capes at an angle parallel to the building, even when the base is parallel to the ground, as was actually the case when they obviously - and humorously - were filmed standing up with the camera turned sideways for the TV show) because the ends are not secured to the collars to keep the wires in place on at least one end. Also, those horsey sized tags on the capes are as ridiculous as they are probably government-mandated, but can and should be cut off immediately.

I could go on, but to cut it short, I had more to like about finally getting this modern-quality version of a childhood favorite than to dislike. It is not perfect, and I may have had no issues where others did, but Holy you can't please everyone!
