product_title: Playskool Sesame Street Elmo Junction Train Set
review_body:
The Amazon shipping box was pretty big, larger than the toy's box, but for once that was a good thing, and I'll get to that in a moment.

Time-wise it took me about 11 mins 30 seconds to unpack everything. Part of the reason for this length of time was that most of the track sections were tied down with those annoying string ties which were taped to the back of the inner carton. Still, at least they didn't go with those wire ties... Sorting out the parts and applying the stickers took about another 14 mins (so we're about 25 mins into it so far). It's probably easier applying the stickers before you start assembling it. Then putting the track together took about another 20 mins. So all told it took me around 45 mins from the moment I started opening the box to being able to play with it.

Looking at it, and noting the battery requirement, I assumed (wrongly) that the train was mechanized. Unfortunately not - you push it around the track by hand. The batteries are to make the Elmo train sing, talk and make noises. The ingenious part about the design of this train and track is that the train has a couple of wheel sensors under it, while a number of different track sections has different \\"bumps\\"....at first I thought it coincidental that Elmo would sing the same song over a specific section of track, and then I realized that the different \\"bumps\\" would signal Elmo to sing that corresponding song. Like I said, it's ingenious.

There also comes with it a little Grover taxi, as well as a carriage to pull behind the Elmo train. When you're not playing with the train, the Grover taxi sits neatly in the carriage, and there's even a fold-down door on the carriage to keep the taxi in place.

The track itself is quite large and you can either use it folded down as a straight train track, or you can fold it over so that you have both a train track and a car track. I'm guessing that most kids will want it folded over so that they can play with both the trains and the cars at the same time. The kit only contains 1 train, car and carriage, however I noticed on the box that there are additional Sesame Street cars and trains which you can use with this kit.

The kit is educational - there are letters and numbers on the track itself, and the songs that Elmo sings involve counting and ABCs, so there is great potential for a toddler/kindergartner to learn as they're playing, particularly as they will most likely sing along with Elmo.

The entire ensemble seems fairly durable. The track pieces push together and do pull apart with a little tug. That being said, it doesn't completely break down again (or if it does, I was too nervous of breaking something to try harder than the force I was already exerting. So putting it back in the kit's box might be problematic as some of the assembled parts which were too stubbornly held together (in particular the train station) were too large. Well, remember how I said that the Amazon box was a little larger? Well, as luck would have it, everything went in the Amazon box just fine, and the packaging paper does a nice job of protecting everything from dust and keeping things fairly well in place. I know this wasn't intentional, but it was just a lucky bonus.

Overall, I'm very impressed with it. It's tough enough for young kids, it's fun, educational, interactive and well designed. I highly recommend it, especially for Elmo fans!with both the trains and the cars at the same time. I do not regret this purchase one bit. NECA once again creates an amazing new addition to their Predators line that continues to amaze me. The figure came with his joints already un-frozen and with extremely well detail in the paint job.

product_title: Thomas the Train Quest for The Crown Set
review_headline: One of the best Trackmaster sets
review_body:
Our 2-year-old son loves Thomas (as does his 6-year-old sister, though she may not be as quick to admit it), and he's accumulated several of the Trackmaster sets, including a few large ones that he received as gifts or we were lucky enough to find cheap. Usually, the sets have one, maybe two, features that usually work, but not always. The Quest for the Crown set has three or four cool features (depending upon how you define where one feature ends and another begins), and all of them work perfectly and consistently.

Although this isn't the tallest set, and it may not have the longest track, it's pretty huge. The instructions are a bit easier to follow than is sometimes the case, and set-up was a snap. Over the course of the track, Thomas closes a castle gate, descends into a mine, finds a crown (that lands in his car), and encounters a section of missing track that is quickly and automatically replaced by a crane. (The gate and missing track features have to be manually reset on each trip around the track; however, the gate can be locked in the open position and the set comes with an extra piece of track to fill in the gap for younger kids who may not be able to, or forget to, do this each time--a very nice touch for adults who don't want to closely monitor a train doing the same thing a few dozen times.)

As with other Trackmaster sets, the pieces are brightly colored and durable, perfect for kids. The set includes a motorized Thomas, but it's compatible with other engines and tracks. Trackmaster sets can sometimes be hit or miss, but this is one that I'd have no problem recommending for any young fan of Thomas or of trains in general.

product_title: Stare! Junior Board Game - 2nd Edition
review_body:
This is a five-star game if ever there was one. Use any criteria you wish and then check off those boxes. Many others have described how its played, the skills it fosters, how good a time they have. But I would like to pass along a few things about the cards themselves.

During a game the other day, my youngest (age 7) came up to me with a card and said something like: \\"Look, that's what you are always telling us\\". He was holding a picture of a boy who typed \\"I can do anything\\" on a computer. This left an impression on me, as it did on my son. When the game was over I decided to sift through the cards out of curiosity. Such positive messages pervade the whole game. Take the Superhero on parade with the sign saying \\"Reading Is Fun\\". Or the scene showing children of different races and backgrounds in a group embrace with the text \\"Let's All Get Along\\" scrolled across the bottom. I also like the card with the three kids sitting around a table discussing a test they took, with one admitting that he \\"should have studied harder\\". Then there is a cartoon with a funny circus scene with the caption \\"Always Obey the Rules\\". There are many more such messages (\\"Be Active Play Sports\\", \\"School Is Fun\\", etc).

Then there are the cards that are just downright adorable, funny, or both. I defy anyone to suppress a laugh when they come across the image of a tied up dog frantically looking at a group of ducklings swimming in his water bowl (I can't do it justice with words). The picture card which has now been taped to our fridge door shows a kitten atop a fishbowl, holding a fishing rod and staring down at a goldfish, with a sign marked \\"Gone Fishing\\". I smile every time I reach for the fridge door. Maybe I'll scan it and send it off to my fishing-crazy brother. I love this game and, best of all, so do my hard-to-please youngsters.

product_title: Yomega  Pro Speed – Non Responsive, High Performance Pro Level Yo-Yo with weighted metal rims – Featuring a ten ball, C size, 10 roller bearing For Ultimate Spin Time
review_body:
I'm not a yoyo expert. I have been into yoyos off and on for several years now and I can do the basic stuff. I have owned several of the yomega yoyos across the years, the clutch type and the ball bearing yomega Raider. I have also had my fair share of fixed axle(metal and wood) Duncan brand yoyos. So this Yomega Pro Yomod is the first unresponsive yoyo I have purchased.

I ended up purchasing two yomega yo mods. The black \\"pro\\" version and the green \\"G-R\\" version. Without interchanging the parts, the pro yomod contains an unshielded, C-sized bearing. It also weighs 70 grams, and has a wide gap between the two yo-yo inner sides, with a recessed set of rubber grips. All of those features makes the pro version of the yo mod very unresponsive.

This is intentional, unresponsive yoyos is the newest development in yoyos, so it works pretty well in that regard. In order to make the yoyo come back, it has to be done with a \\"bind\\" trick. I find that doing the bind works, but there has to be enough spin left in the yoyo otherwise it will not work.

After using the pro version for an hour, I ended up bruising my hand, this is due to my lack of experience and my hand not being used to the weight of a 70 gram yoyo. I purchased a \\"G-R\\" version of the yomod changed the G-R parts for all the pro ones. So now I have an unresponsive 60 gram yoyo, which is noticeably lighter, and a lot less stressful on my hand. I will eventually go back to using the 70 gram weighted yo yo after I get comfortable enough with the lighter 60 gram one, and when my hand heals up.

If someone bought the pro line as their first yo yo and they are unsatisfied with the non-response, the easiest remedy is to apply the appropriate type of yoyo oil to the ball bearing. A well oiled bearing will be more responsive than a light oiled one.

Yomega does not recommend the yomods for beginners. All three versions of the yomods, the Pro, G-R and the BX2 are consideredadvanced level yoyos. The product packaging has a numbered dial pattern along the front with an arrow indicating the level of play. 1= beginners and 5=most advanced players. These yoyos are listed around 4, meaning not for beginners.

The yoyo in its packaging is not assembled, unfortunately there is no instruction manual which is a problem. Problems I foresee are people incorrectly assembling the grip pads, and spacers, as well as not knowing how to properly maintain the ball bearings. There is information on this at the yomega website, but this should have been in the packaging regardless.

update: Some people maybe wondering how long can the prospeed sleep for? This varies by skill and technique, and usually isn't going to be practical in a situation like a yoyo competition or performance, but my personal best is 5 minutes 22 secs.

product_title: Win8Fong Acrylic Dragonball Replica Ball (Large/1 Star)
review_headline: It's like I pulled it right out of the anime!
review_body:
This replica is so good it might as well be called the real deal. I honestly thought that I held the one-star dragonball within my hands! Any fan of the series absolutely needs one of these dragon balls as an amazing display piece. Many people worry that because the description says that the balls are made of acrylic that it will have a plasitcy feel or be a lightweight prop; let me put an end to your fears, it doesn't. I was a bit skeptical at first, but If no one told me that the ball was acrylic, I wouldn't have been able to tell that it was not crystal. The ball has a nice glassy feel, it's very shiny, and is about the size and weight of a baseball.

The question everyone wants to know is does it have a visible seam? The answer is yes, it does, but it's really only noticeable if you at it directly, especially under light. Originally I thought that the seam would make the ball look tacky, but honestly I don't mind the seam one bit. These dragonballs look and feel so amazing in every other aspect that I don't think it matters if it has a seam, it's awesome. This product is the official Bandai product and NOT THE STRAPYA WORLD VERSION!! The larger balls are 1:1 scale unlike the set of 7 smaller dragon balls sold by Bandai. The only difference between this ball and the smaller set is that the star(s) are not three-dimensional in the full sized balls, only the small ones. The stars in the full sized balls are less than paper thin.

It doesn't get any better than this people, It's an offical Dragon ball Z product by Bandai, it's the same size as the Earth dragon balls in the anime, and it looks and feels amazing. If you decide not to buy it, you're missing out big time.

product_title: Rio Grande Games Dominion
review_body:
**We received this from Rio Grande Games for free for this review**

The initial setup for the basic Dominion game is quite lengthy, as should be expected, because the 250 cards are wrapped in decks that need to be separated. Once the separation is complete a thorough reading of the rules is absolutely necessary in order to even complete the first round of turns, again as should be expected. The setup of the first game took roughly 30 minutes of reading the rules and placing each card in its location. After the first experience setting up the game each subsequent setup was much quicker.

Understanding the design of Dominion is a difficult process initially. Again we advise thorough reading of the rules and how each card and effect works. Before the game starts treasure, victory, curse and kingdom cards need to be placed on the playing space. Treasure cards are what each player uses to purchase other cards consisting of copper (1), silver (2) and gold (3). Victory cards are what are required for winning the game. Curse cards are a form of attacking other players that are dependent on other cards for use. Kingdom cards are the player's means of increasing their abilities with a large variety of effects. In the base game there are 25 different types of kingdom cards, each having their own specific effect such as drawing more cards or attacking other players. Attacking other players usually consists of giving other players curse cards with \\"Witch\\" card which takes away a victory point and takes up space in your deck or the \\"Thief\\" card which forces other players to reveal cards in their deck and allows the player to take a treasure card if revealed (this card was the source of many office rivalries). The kingdom cards effects are incredibly varied and fun to experiment with. Once ten kingdom card types are placed on the field and the victory, treasure and curse cards are placed the game begins with each player getting 7 copper and 3 estates which areworth 1 victory point. Each player shuffles the \\"deck\\" and draws five cards and the game continues from there. Each players turn consists of the \\"action\\", \\"buy\\" and \\"clean-up\\" phases. The first round of turns in a game does not include the \\"action\\" phase. The \\"action\\" phase consists of the player using the kingdom card/s in their hand. If the player has a kingdom card that increases the amount of actions a player can take then multiple kingdom cards may be used in a turn.

The \\"buy\\" phase consists of using the treasure cards in the players hand and any +treasure gained from a kingdom card to buy more treasure/victory/kingdom cards (typically only one card can be bought in a turn but more may be bought through the use of kingdom cards). Each card has a price listed on it and can only be purchased if the player's funds are at or above the amount shown. The \\"clean-up\\" phase is simply taking all purchased, used and unused cards from the players hand and placing them in the discard pile to later be shuffled into their deck. The game ends when 3 supply cards (kingdom, victory or treasure) are empty or when all of the \\"Province\\" cards which are victory cards worth 6 points are gone. Each player then counts all the victory points they have and the one with the highest wins. This usually takes roughly 30 minutes or more.

Dominion is a fantastic strategy game that certainly takes some time to get used to. But once the players understand the rules and each cards effects the game becomes incredibly engaging. We here at The Gaming Experience have played the game nearly 30 times and have used multiple action card configurations that have resulted in many very interesting games. Most notable is the optional victory card \\"garden\\". This card adds a single victory point for every ten cards in the player's deck so changing strategy to acquire multiples of these before other players is key to winning when they are in play. Depending on which action cards are in the game individual strategies will change as well. The only problem we have with the game is that certain action cards, if they are in the game, are simply better then others and it usually becomes a race to get those cards. There are also some action cards which are completely undesirable outside of very experienced players and extremely specific situations. With one standalone and seven expansions outside of the basic game, Dominion is a game every table top gamer should have in their collection as well as those who simply enjoy strategy. Dominions publisher, Rio Grande Games made a great decision in publishing this title and bringing it to the customers.

There are surfaces on the bow and stern areas, for instance, that have what appear to be a comical, out of scale \\"diamond plate\\" molded in. This is actually an accurate representation of an anti-skid surface developed by the IJN! This kit is not set up for motorization like the other ships in Nichimo's 1/200 line (mine did not include a gearbox or a motor/motor mount) but can be converted to R/C and I have seen it done with a great deal of skill. Imagine having a museum quality model ship sitting on your shelf that can also operate like the real thing and be realistically propelled in a pond or swimming pool...

product_title: Citadels
review_headline: Citadels is a fantastic game for 2-8 players!
review_body:
Citadels is a card game that, simply put, is a mix of deductive reasoning (Clue, Love Letter, etc) and civilization building (Seven Wonders). Each turn, you play the role of one of 8 characters (9 if you have 8 players), each with a specific ability. The King, for example, gets to choose first on the next turn, while the Magician can swap hands with other players, and the Assassin can effectively "murder" one role (that player loses their turn). During your turn, you can choose to use your character's ability, take either gold or building cards, and/or build a structure that you have in your hand. Building structures increases your total points and gets you closer to ending the game - the last round occurs when a player has built his or her 8th structure.

A large part of the game revolves around predicting which role your fellow players choose each turn, while picking a role for yourself that won't be a target for the same players. Do you attempt to pick the Merchant (special ability: extra gold for that one turn) to build up your gold stockpile, allowing you to to bigger and better structures, or play it safe, knowing that the Thief (special ability: steal all of a character's gold) lurks in the shadows?

It's difficult to find a card game that balances skill and luck evenly, but Citadels manages to hit that sweet spot.

review_headline: Princess Sofia Castle, Royal Family and Bed Playset
review_body:
I preordered the three items above and was very excited in giving them to my granddaughter, who is 3 1/2 years old. My son helped put the castle together. Like many here, I was disappointed in the quality of the castle and how easy it is for the staircase, doors, etc., to come off. The Royal Family is very attractive. However, like many here, their heads do come off very easily. Again, a concern for choking or just breaking in general. The bed set was fun because Sofia is in her pajamas and gives her a different look then the doll who came with the castle and the family set. I'm happy my granddaughter loves these toys, but I feel I spent a lot of money on the castle and Royal Family set and didn't live up to what I was expecting. Thankfully she is young and doesn't fully understand. If your little girl loves Sofia, then she will love the toys. I just question if more testing or better quality materials should have been used on the castle before preselling.

product_title: 4-in-1 Stroll 'N Trike
review_body:
After reading the reviews of the Radio Flyer 4-in-1 Trike and the Little Tikes 3-in-1 I decided on the Radio Flyer. While I had some speculation from reading the reviews, I am more than happy with this product (and I am a hard person to please). The assembly was quite simple, about 20 minutes even with the help of a 15 month old. I thought my 15 month old wouldn't mind being put in this to go for dog walks...turns out I can't keep her out of it! If we walk less than a mile in it she refuses to get out. We have to hide it because if she sees it she wants to go for a ride.

Pros -
-Color is superb
-The basket while small is still enough to hold a few diapers, doggy pop bags, a bottle of water, or whatever other little things you may need on a walk
-The umbrella I didn't think would be useful but in reality does a great job protecting her head, face, and shoulders
-Love the wrap around guard, also has a cup holder for her water cup
-The foot peddles can be locked so she can rest her foot on them (still a little short...she manages to rest her feet on the fender as it is big enough).
-Handles are adjustable
-Wheels - I was worried about this. I really wanted some nice rubber wheels, no trike product offered this. These wheels are made of a "soft plastic" and are surprisingly quite quiet.
-I love the fact that it grows with her.

Cons-
-There is no way to lock the handle bars so if she grabs ahold of them you have to over steer the bike back...not necessarily a bad thing as it teachers her cause and effect.
-Handle bars and steering became "loose"...not responsive. While going down a straight road the handle bars may be angled slightly. Haven't figured out if this can be adjusted without pulling apart the frame.
-No drink holder on the handle bars. You can put stuff in the bucket, but will have to stop to reach it.
-The lock to disengage the peddles doesn't always stay put and will make a clicking sound...easily corrected by turning the nob on the front wheel.

product_title: The Hunger Games: Training Days
review_body:
When I was looking for a Hunger Games game, we got several, but this is the family favorite! It's got enough strategy to keep everyone interested, from teens up to adults. The game is fair and balanced. And there's plenty of \\"wiggle room\\" to allow for your own permutations and modifications!

In a nutshell: pick a Tribute to be. Each has a special ability as well as ratings in 4 characteristics. Put out cards (as many as there are players), and each person has 3 tokens to place face-down on the cards. The cards are modified by one or more characteristics. You win the card based on your value for the characteristic plus your effort token(s), plus your die roll. The person who wins the most points (based on the point value of each card you win) is the winner.

Even my 5 year old loves this game, because it allows him to practice addition (characteristic plus effort token plus die roll), so it's a win-win for the entire family!

product_title: UNO Blast Card Game
review_body:
We love Uno in this house so we were very excited to get the chance to check out the UNO Blast Card Game. The game changes up some of the rules of UNO while keeping the basic premise the same - but is it really a fun game?

PROS:

-A new way to play! It's always fun to have a little change when you have a classic game, and the UNO Blast definitely changes up the rules, requiring that you put any card you have to draw into the Blast unit, and adding a few new cards that definitely make the game different.

-Blast unit is fun! The unit is actually really fun, even when you're not playing! My kids spent a half an hour (or more!) putting cards in and watching them pop out, as well as trying to guess which slot was the one that triggered the pop up!

CONS:

-Fast game - all of the Blast games we've played so far went much faster than the regular UNO games, taking 10 minutes (or even less in one occasion!) to finish the game. Good if you want to do a number of games, bad if you want to have a longer, more involved game.

-Missing old UNO - While we liked playing the new game, we did admit to missing some of the facets of the old game. Not having to draw until you get a card that you can play is likely the biggest reason why the game goes so fast.

VERDICT:

While UNO Blast is fun, I don't think it's going to be replacing our regular UNO anytime soon. It's definitely fun for a little bit, and I have a feeling it'd be a blast during a party, but it's not something that we'll be playing all the time.

product_title: Plan Toys 3-Piece Car Set
review_body:
My three cars came as part of the Plan City Train Station set and are the same as these separately sold ones. They are tiny, as other reviewers have noted; from bumper to bumper about the size of a golf ball, but shorter from base to roof and hence a potential choking hazard. My one year old finds them a little on the small side and has a bit more difficulty gripping them as they have smooth, rounded edges, unlike say, the Plan City train cars. The advantage of this car is that it can 'drive' along the standard (Plan City, Thomas or IKEA) wooden railroad. It also doesn't scratch our hardwood floors because of the rubber wheels, unlike the Melissa & Doug cars or IKEA train cars which have plastic wheels and metal hubcaps.

The reason I am writing a negative review of this toy is to caution parents that the wheels are detachable. I wouldn't consider my 21 month old particularly savvy with small toys, yet I found him sucking on two of the apparently removable rubber wheels earlier. The cars are small to begin with, hence the wheels are even smaller, about the size of M&M chocolates, so some may not consider them of choking hazard size. Still, the notion of a toddler chewing on or swallowing (toxic) rubber is less than ideal. While the wood seems hardy enough as with most Plan Toys, and the paint has stood up to some toddler gnawing, I cannot consider the toy durable since the wheels are removable, tiny and liable to get lost. It's going back into the china cabinet together with the automoblox toy cars whose wheels are also removable, and more easily so. As I have most of the Plan City Train, Road and Station set, I have found that the wheels also come off other vehicles as they are all similarly made. For instance, the Plan City bus wheels are also detachable, albeit requiring more manual dexterity to pry off than these littler cars. But it is just a matter of time since my toddler now knows that rubber wheels come off, and he figured this one out ina day. My mistake in equating small with age appropriate for a toddler. It is too small, and now, unsafe. When my youngest is past the age of putting things in his mouth, I will take these cars out again, but that will be in some three years' time.

Meanwhile, if you are looking for small cars, I have found Sevi's mini (car, train, truck, helicopter) series reasonably good, although note that they are European toys made in China, and in my experience, the quality control is a bit weak with Sevi: 20% of the time, the axle may not be drilled accurately through the body of the car and all wheels may not sit on a flat surface (not an issue with Plan Toys, but hey, no perfect toy out there!)

P.S. I wanted to add that you can find plan toys for a third less at utoypia online.

product_title: LeapFrog LeapPad1 Explorer Learning Tablet, green
review_body:
My daughter loved the Leappad for the first five months she had it. Then the screen froze. My daughter's Leappad has been frozen for several weeks, so I followed the steps to \\"tune\\" the Leappad. Every time I power it on it now goes to yellow triangle \\"!\\" screen. When I connect the Leappad to my Windows 7 PC via the USB cable, the Leappad Connect program starts the tuning process, which gets to 8%, then freezes. I've repeated this multiple times. I've let this run for hours and the process is just frozen, not making any progress.

The answer I got from Leappad support was to \\"do a reset,\\" i.e. exactly the same steps I had figured out on my own by searching the net and product site. Guess what? It's the \\"reset\\" that is getting stuck.... They really had no other answer for my problem. I can see that hundreds of others on the Internet have had similar problems, but zero success in fixing them.

So, all hope exhausted, I gave up.

The vision of this product is very good (my daughter still asks about it). The execution & follow-through are exasperatingly lousy. Don't buy it.

product_title: Dungeons & Dragons Fantasy Roleplaying Game: An Essential D&D Starter
review_headline: he skulked the dingey crypt corridor which reeked of decay and then...
review_body:
I think the mr higbee's statement that 'you don't need the core rules' should be revised to something more of you needn't worry about them early on. you may want them as you get more involved.

the fact is the products were designed as stepping stones: first this starter, then the essentials, finally the hard core stuff (and yes you will want the hardcovers if you are to have any edge in this game be you PC or DM)

I also recommend 'players strategy guide' for a tactics -how to- and the 'DnD 4e/DM-for dummies' to get you on the right track to 'power gaming'

also wizards character record sheets for 4e while being sparse give you enough blank power cards for one PC so you can add-on powers from other sources such as essentials or core products.

and I recommend you picking a campaign setting if you are a newer DM they give you options for adventure ideas when you aren't experienced enough to build your own, plus you can grab elements to add to your own worlds or creation.

finally if you feel too intimidated when deciding products or want to add flavor without a hefty price tag then try dnd insider at [...] the forums will help you make all the right calls and the $5.95/mo subscription gives you cool tools and tons of game product dirt cheap.

good luck all you fledgling gamers and game on

product_title: World of Warcraft UDE Official WOW Gaming Card Deck Protector Sleeves - (The Alliance) - 75 Sleeves
review_body:
While I'm not a fan of WoW (and have only ever played the game for my boyfriend and another friend for a total of maybe 30 minutes), I do like the designs of classes and races in the game. Being a fan of lions, though, is what makes the \\"Alliance\\" faction of WoW stand out to me. I personally even bought the WoW Creative wireless headphone set for myself just because it was color-modifiable and came with a set of \\"Alliance\\" Lion inserts for over each ear.

These deck protectors seem to be nice quality. They are made by the Upper Deck company (which no longer makes the decks or deck protectors for the WoW trademark. Compared to \\"Deck Pro\\" or other solid-back deck protectors, they seem to be a little less 'thick', but are well made enough to handle constant games of Magic the Gathering. They have a very nice design (blue and yellow: who can go wrong with the colors of UofM? Am I right?) and every sleeve in each deck was made without any flaws. This is nice, because even in MtG deck protector sets: you can have imperfections in the printing or manufacture of each sleeve that could prevent you from using around 10% of each set (for rule's sake of 'marking cards' and therefore stacking the deck). Since all of these were obviously quality checked for flaws, I feel it's a great set of deck protector sleeves.

My feeling is that they are worth it--and will fit an average built-deck of MtG cards (which is between 60 and 70 cards) plus some extras to change from time to time. I ordered two sets for my purposes of replacement as they would become worn from use--but I don't see that happening easily (unless you are brutal to your decks or play daily).

Buy them before they're gone. They come in both Alliance and Hoard--and are pretty cool. They also help you more easily know what cards are yours if you're going out and gaming in tournaments or game shops, making it easy to spot if someone is trying to swipe a card of yours that they wouldwant... Remember: stealing is wrong, but it happens.

Happy gaming!

I havent been able to find the name 'Bret' in connection with this even with the help of the internet today, but who knows.  Something may come to light some day.. product_title: Melissa & Doug Trunki Sunny
review_headline: Great product for kids on the go!
review_body:
These Trunki suitcases are super cute, and a great idea for kids who travel a lot! It's clever that each different suitcase design has a different name. I also like that it is made of a strong material so it can take a beating at the airport and keep on working.

It's very handy that a child can sit on it and even be pulled along on it when walking through an airport. The instructions say that the child should hold onto the \\"horns\\" at the front of the suitcase while being pulled, however, they really aren't handles and would not be enough to keep a child balanced. So that should only be done by older children, not small children.

One side of the interior has straps to keep items in place. The suitcase \\"locks\\" with little keys attached to the straps. If your family is going to be doing a lot of traveling, though, it would be nice if there was a way to lock it with a suitcase lock.

It is easy to convert it from a shoulder strap to a pull along strap, and there are also two small handles shown in the picture. Lots of options. There are 4 \\"hidden\\" compartments but they are so small your child could only store the very tiniest items in them.

The only real disappointment I had was when I really looked at it with my little girl, it looks like it needs to have a \\"face\\". There are horns, and the lock on the front kind of looks like a nose, but it needs eyes and a mouth. I was sorry to read on the brochure that there are face stickers available to purchase for an additional charge. I wish the company had thrown in one set of stickers for free with purchase - a sheet of stickers are not that expensive!

Otherwise I think this is a very cute and practical suitcase for children and I would recommend it.

product_title: LeapFrog Read with Me
review_headline: A Toy that Promotes Print Awareness and Reading Readiness
review_body:
Violet has quickly become one of my son's favorite toys. Besides being educational and promoting reading readiness, Violet is very soft and cuddly. Even when he is not reading the books with her, he loves to have her come on his adventures camping under the dining room table or exploring the cave under the bed. I have found it is very rare to have an electronic and educational toy that is also cuddly.

As far as the educational aspects of this toy, I started off a little skeptical. Many toys that claim to teach reading comprehension do nothing of the sort, or they have one set of questions that the child hears every time they read the book. Read with Me Violet has many different questions, and I have not had the same experience reading a book with her yet. The questions she asks encourage the child to make connections to their own feelings as well as asking the child to look closer at the book and interact with the pictures and context of the story. I like that Violet reinforces the correct answer after she asks it most of the time. I did find it a little odd that when she asks you to pat her back if you feel happy, she will not accept any other answer before moving on in the story. What if the child is not feeling happy at the time? Other than that, I felt that the educational portion of this toy was very well done.

As for ease of use, when I first introduced my 3 year old son to Violet, I handed her to him with the books. I showed him how to turn her on and off (that's always his first question), and showed him how to choose which book he wanted her to read. Then I let him explore on his own. He was quickly able to follow her directions and even started answering some of the questions verbally (something that he doesn't usually do with inanimate objects like TV shows).

Overall, I think that this toy definitely does what it advertises. I would definitely recommend this toy to other parents who want to encourage their child to love reading, especially if they are not a family that reads together every day. As a teacher, I would love my students to come to me with the experiences they get from playing with this toy.

product_title: Mighty Morphin Power Rangers Ninja Megazord Deluxe Action Figure
review_body:
I've said it before, and I'll say it again: this was one of the finest Christmas gifts I've ever received. It wasn't the most expensive, or the most sentimental, but what makes it memorable is that it was a total surprise, not to mention my reaction after ripping open the wrapping paper as a kid. It was the Christmas just after the movie came out, so it was big on my radar.
My family was gathered at my grandma's, and I opened it entirely right then and there. I received the Falconzord as well, but you can read my other review for that.
I can't remember whether the box I received was the movie or TV show version, but it doesn't matter as the product inside is the exact same thing.

Opening the box, the Zords sat nicely in Styrofoam, each in their own little compartment. That box and Styrofoam insert are long gone, but I still have the figures to this day. The stickers were fairly easy to put on, but I remember only because the stickers, which are still on, don't seem to be crooked or too out of place.

Obviously, I've lost pieces over the years, and even gave away the red Ape Ninjazord to my cousin, but have re-acquired them all in some way or another. The transformations are fairly simple. I don't have the instructions anymore, but they're not necessary. I still remember how to transform them from memory, and I'm sure any new buyer could them get right away.

The figures separately are some of the most articulated out of the Megazords (the other being the original dino Megazord). The only one that has the least is the red Ape, but that's only in the legs. It can still move the arms to wield its swords. The frog has nice big moveable legs (which are necessary for transformation, anyway), the bear and wolf have moveable legs and jaw, and the crane has sliding wings and a two-jointed neck (one at the bottom and one at the neck, for transformation).

When in Megazord, you can move the arms 360, and...that's about it. The frog can still move the legs, but only backward, and crouched, but it ruins transformation as the arms flip out of the shins. There are caps to put on the heads of the ape and wolf which gives the Megazord its fists, which leaves me to wonder the purpose of the swords the ape comes with. It's not useable at all with the Megazord, so it comes with no arsenal. I haven't seen Kakuranger yet, so I don't know if that's all there is. There is also a bit to put in the bear's mouth.

All in all, this was a childhood favorite, but I admit it's not as great as the other Megazords. I like the look of the original one, and the Thunder one is hulking, but it's probably my favorite in terms of aesthetics. The Tigerzord, Red Dragon, and Dragonzord Megazord combos are probably my favorites.frog can still move the legs, but only backward, and crouched, but it ruins transformation as the arms flip out of the shins. There are caps to put on the heads of the ape and wolf which gives the Megazord its fists, which leaves me to wonder the purpose of the swords the ape comes with. It's not useable at all with the Megazord, so it comes with no arsenal. I haven't seen Kakuranger yet, so I don't know if that's all there is. There is also a bit to put in the bear's mouth.

All in all, this was a childhood favorite, but I admit it's not as great as the other Megazords. I like the look of the original one, and the Thunder one is hulking, but it's probably my favorite in terms of aesthetics. The Tigerzord, Red Dragon, and Dragonzord Megazord combos are probably my favorites.

review_headline: Awesome Blaster, NERF is on it.
review_body:
So this is probably tied with the Rampage for my favorite Nerf Wars primary.

Pros:
Smooth operation, accurate, decent stock range, good looking

Cons:
Slightly unbalanced (because of flywheel), jams frequently (fixed with a couple super simple mods)

So one of the first things I did when I got the blaster was remove a bar that blocked the firing rod when there was no dart in the clip. It just caused a lot of unnecessary jams. However, I had still jams rather frequently. I realized that it was because of a couple doors in the barrel, they pushed back on the dart and it would get caught up pretty often. I was able to remove one completely and break off the other with a pair of pliers and that fixed the problem.

Range is just a little lower than the rampage, but I love the operation. It's a breeze to reload, and I can always depend on my shot location up to 30 feet or so. Blaster is a little front-heavy, but a stock helps to offset it if it seems like a problem for you.

Overall, NERF's whole elite line has been fantastic, couldn't be happier with the direction they are going.

product_title: Diamond Select Toys Universal Monsters Black-and-white Legacy Series 2 Figure Set : Dracula, Frankenstein and the Bride of Frankenstein Numbered SET
review_body:
Ok, I'll cut right to the chase for a change, as I review a lot of these types of items. The best one of the three figures here is Dracula, though he looks nothing like Lugosi, more like the Dracula in the Marvel 70's magazine. But this isn't necessarily a complaint. He's got a very cool and fierce expression on his face, with great menacing fangs. AND his base is MUCH better than the color version released last year, and he's lost that stupid wolf that never sits on the base properly. AND his cape stays on better than the color version due to the gravestones it's balanced on.

Frankenstein is Karloff-like, but his arms don't sit in their shoulder-joints very well. His base is castle-stone floor with chains and cuffs and a rock or two. The problem with all three is there are no real points of articulation except the arms moving from the shoulders only, and the hands swivel a bit, so not so poseable. Frank's kinda wooden, but so was Frank. I like 'em.

The transgression here is The Bride. She looks nothing like Elsa Lancaster, too cupie-doll or Barbie-ish for my tastes. It's insulting to Elsa and her legion of fans. Her body and base are OK but, truth be known, all three are just recycled versions of the color versions, with Drac having the most re-working and best outcome. He's the real keeper here, as long as you're not looking for Bela.

I'll give it 3 1/2 to 4 stars 'cause I like Drac + Frank, the B+W classic tone and the affordable pricepoint at the time of this review.

product_title: KidKraft Star Table and Chair Set with Primary Bins - 26912
review_body:
I didn't buy this from Amazon, my mother did. She thought it would be a good table for our kids and it was a very sweet gesture. However, I'm only holding onto it long enough for her to visit my house once and see it before I pitch it in the trash. Putting it together was a nightmare; the screws didn't fit properly in the holes of the crossbars and when I tried to used some force to get the screws in, the part that receives the screw pushed back in to the pole itself, making it impossible to screw it in. (I am a veteran assembler. Being a military wife, I have to do a lot of this kind of work when my husband's job takes him away. So, I know what I'm doing, for the most part.)

Once my husband used some pliers and brute strength to pull the little pieces back to the ends of the poles and we managed to get the table assembled, we realized that children HAVE to sit on either end. If they want to work on something together and move a chair to the side of the table, they can't do it comfortably because the baskets get in the way.

We owned it for a few months before the top popped off while my husband was carrying it outside to do Easter eggs. Keep in mind that we keep it in a room that our kids only have access to when I'm on the computer and so it had only been used about 4 times at the point which it fell apart. The chairs are decent, but oh my goodness I absolutely, positively HATE this table! Mom, come visit quickly so it can stop wasting space in my den! lol

product_title: Coast Guard Rescue RC 3.5CH Gyro Helicopter Mini Infrared Remote Controlled SYMA Heli S111G
review_body: I added the \\"but\\" at the end of my title for only one reason. The way this little helicopter is designed, it is impossible to get to any of the internal components should they ever need to be repaired. The body is molded plastic and there is no way to take it apart without destroying it. At least no way that I can see, and I am very good at taking things apart, as I'm an autobody repair technician by trade. You can't even get in there to replace the battery. I'll fly it until the battery wears out, then it'll make a very cute decorative ornament. These little LiPo batteries do not have the \\"memory effect\\". If you over discharge this type of battery it will ruin it. Fly the helicopter until you start having to give it full throttle to stay aloft, then land it and shut it off, and always wait at least 10 minutes before recharging, to allow the battery time to cool off. If you do those two things, the battery should last a long time and you should be able to get 7 to 9 minutes of flying time, consistently. If you want a mini helicopter that you can repair, or replace the battery, then get the Syma S107G instead. I also have two S107GS. I bought this one because it's so awesome looking, I don't care that it can't be repaired. I've only had this helicopter for two days. It has 10 flights logged so far, each time I'm getting 9 minutes on a full charge...yes, I time each flight, and I keep a log of the number of flights each one of my helicopters has done. I just want to see how long they last. None of my three little birds has died....yet. You should get many hours of fun out of this little helicopter if you take care not to over-discharge the battery and try not to crashed too much.

product_title: Integy Steel Front Universal Driveshaft (2): Slash 4X4
review_headline: Junk - Just like every other Integy brand part
review_body: These are complete junk.  I thought that since they weren't aluminum like most of Integy's horribly products, that a set of steel parts might be good.  They came newly installed in a Rally I just purchased.  One was bent when I received it.  The Integy driveshafts looked new and they didn't show any indication that they had ever been run, so I chalked it up to the seller telling me the truth that they were brand new and that maybe it happened in shipping somehow - I stuck a stock plastic driveshaft on that side for the time being so I could take the truck for a test run... Well after one battery pack with the other driveshaft in my 4x4 Rally, the vehicle developed a horrible wobble in that side front wheel.  I knew immediately what it was unfortunately.  Took the wheel off and sure enough, I had a bent outer axle.  Right where the hex pin hole is, like the other one.  I didn't have any ugly flips or anything on either run. A few small jumps off a speed bump, but that's about it.  I was just driving on asphalt and grass.  And only on 2 cells!  I run 17mm adapters for buggy wheels, so maybe that adds some extra leverage on the outer axle - But I've never bent a stock outer axle before, and I've driven on those much more aggressively.  So what that tells me without a shadow of a doubt is that the Integy axles are total junk.  The outer axles bend way too easy and I haven't found a place to buy them separately.  Spend the extra money for the Tekno or MIP ones.  You'll be glad in the long run!  Purely based on Integy's track record, I would have bought either of those brands instead, bigtime.  My Rally just happened to come with these driveshafts unfortunately.

product_title: Gundam Seed Frame HG 56 Civilian Astray DSSD Leons Graves Custom 1/144 by Bandai
review_body:
This was my third Gunpla I've ever built, and I really like the design of it. I was disappointed it didn't contain any polycaps, which hindered some of the articulation, and prevented some it could've had, but the joints overall work fine without. I'm still a little bummed about the stiff legs (since they don't have polycaps, they can't stretch very wide).

The color is different than my other Gundams, and I like it a lot. Any change is always welcome. It comes with two different heads, though only one face and mouth piece, so you have to remove those every time you want to change the head. Kinda annoying.

What impressed me the most was the jetpack (or whatever it is). It can open up to reveal boosters inside, and those are individually articulated.

A nice and easy Gunpla to build, though it could've benefited from polycaps.

She loves putting the Pollys to bed, sometimes in their separate little areas, sometimes having a sleepover in the convenient little two-doll sleeping bag. The \\"elevator\\" swing is a constant source of entertainment as is the slide. Some of the parts are super small and not very useful, but still fun. We love how both the camp set and this tree house have \\"secret\\" compartments (for this one, it's the barrel table with the chessboard on the top). And the surprise trapdoor area rug is a hoot too. Long lasting play that stays off the floor and out of everyone's way? Can't beat that!

product_title: Elenco  AmeriKit Learn to Solder Kit
review_body:
I have been soldering electronics for years, both professionally and as a hobby. Recently I was asked to teach the Electronics Merit Badge to some Boy Scouts. I found this kit and ordered one from Amazon. I was impressed by what arrived. Not only does this kit include a soldering iron and all of the parts needed, but it also includes a very well done tutorial. I ended up strongly recommending this kit to the Boy Scouts. The main reason is because of the tutorial. The circuit board includes pads whose sole purpose is for practice. The tutorial in the manual walks you through basics like tinning the soldering iron, proper technique, advice on avoiding heat damage, and how to avoid a cold solder joint. Each of the parts is clearly labeled and the instructions are easy to follow.

Putting this kit together will not make you an expert at soldering. Like most things in life, proper soldering takes practice. The soldering iron included is not a top-of-the-line model, but it gets the job done. If you are serious about getting into electronics you will want to upgrade your equipment.

If you want to learn to solder this is a great starting point. Don't skip any of the tutorial, and pay close attention to all of the safety precautions. Before too long you'll have yourself a working siren and have gained a valuable skill.

product_title: Melissa & Doug Sunny Patch Happy Giddy Toy Binocular for Kids
review_headline: Sort of cute, but smaller than expected, and the neck strap is a hazard
review_body:
I had seen several other brands of kid binoculars in our local toy store, so was familiar with the competition. When I ordered and received this pair of binoculars instead (Melissa and Doug is always a reliable bet, right?), I was really surprised at how small it was. Its okay, since they are for small kids with small faces, but its not really a "substantial" item. I guess the compactness and lightness can be considered a "pro" since it doesn't take up much space and it actually folds down even further.

I do think the neck strap is a danger however. I understand that part of the fun of having a pair of binoculars is wearing them around your neck -- but kids know that too and thats the first thing they do is to put the string over their neck. My issue is that it really is more of a flimsy string, and not a real thick safe strap. Its the kind of cheap string that twists up around your neck as soon as you put the binoculars on and start to move around. Total strangling hazard in my eyes, and this is for an item that is recommended for as young as 36 months.

The string is also cheaply done, and is threaded from back to front, rather than left to right, which means that the binoculars don't really lay flat on your chest, but rather twists to one side, even further promoting the twisting and the choking of the neck.

I'm going to be removing this "strap" with a pair of scissors. Total negative.

The binoculars themselves are fine, and are sufficient for my 2 and 4 year olds having fun with them.

product_title: BUILT IN VIDEO CAMERA! Ready-to-Fly RTF Super Micro Helicopter with Spy Camera WLTOYS S215 for iPad iPhone Android tablet
review_headline: How to set up the IPad
review_body:
This is a great little gizmo, but, if you want to pilot it from your IPad, there are some things you need to know.

1. Set aside the instructions that came with the helicopter, because they're written in worthless pigeon English and make no sense.

2. Nothing will work unless the chopper and controller are fully charged. Put the USB cord that came with the helicopter, and has the yellow ending, into any active USB port you have available. (I used my regular computer.) Plug the yellow ending into the helicopter's receiver port, which is located just to the left of the helicopter's on-off switch. It takes about an hour to charge the helicopter's receiver. Make sure the helicopter's on-off switch is turned to OFF while charging.

3. Do the same thing with the controller, which is that gizmo that says \\"WLtoys\\" on it and has what looks like a headphone jack. To the left of this jack is a little port where the USB charger cable (the same one you used to charge the helicopter) inserts into.

4. While you're charging these two items, go to Apple's App store and search under \\"IPhone Apps.\\" (I know, you're not using an IPhone, but that's where it can be found -- don't know why.) Search for \\"WLtoys,\\" and you'll find the app from UPRtek. Download it.

5. OK. So now you've got the helicopter charged, the controller charged and the software downloaded to your IPad. You're (almost) good to go.

6. Plug the WLtoys controller into the headphone jack of your IPad. Push hard, so that it's all the way bottomed out on your IPad. Go to the IPad's volume control and turn the volume all the way up to the fullest volume you can get. THIS IS SUPER-IMPORTANT!

7. Activate the UPRtek software on your IPad and find your type of chopper. The camera model is labeled \\"Spy Cam.\\" I clicked on this and it brought up a display that showed the throttle as a slide-bar on the left. At the top of the throttle slide-bar, just to its right, is an ON-OFF display. Making sure the throttle is all the way to the bottom, tap the ON-OFF display to ON.

8. Turn the ON-OFF switch on the helicopter to ON.

9. If you've followed these instructions to a tee, the controller on the IPad should turn blue, which means the IPad is now talking to the helicopter. Again, that's because the helicopter's receiver is fully charged, the IController is fully charged, the software version is correct and turned ON, and the IPad's volume is all the way up.

From here on out, it's a matter of learning how to fly, and you're on your own. My only caution is to warn you that the throttle is VERY sensitive. Go in small increments, increasing the throttle thrust bit by bit. You'll see all sorts of posts telling about how the chopper just jumped up, flew to the ceiling and crashed on first launch. Don't be one of them. You need to baby the throttle until you get the hang of it. The helicopter holds about 10 minutes of flight-time charge.

The software has a \\"DEMO\\" button. If you goose the throttle just a bit, so the helicopter has just enough thrust to be barely on the ground, the DEMO will march the copter through some precision maneuvers and give you an indication of how precisely this baby can fly.

As you'll see, you have two choices about how to control the craft in flight -- manually or via gyroscope. You'll get a far better knowledge about the copter's flight traits if you start out by manually controlling it with the circle-in-a-circle piloting mode displayed on the right side of the UPRtek display. Once you're confident you know what you're doing, you can graduate to the gyroscope mode, which essentially turns your IPad into a Wii. That mode is activated by pressing the software display button that looks like a nuclear symbol, two orbiting circles.

Once you understand these fundamentals, pick up the original instructions to find out how to \\"trim\\" your helicopter, correcting any tendency the craft has to drift one way or the other. Unlike the other instructions, this part of the setup is fairly well explained by WLtoys.

Good luck! Hope this helped, and thanks to my daughter Jane, who got me as far as this.

product_title: LeapFrog Disney Pixar Monsters University Learning Game (works with LeapPad Tablets, LeapsterGS, and Leapster Explorer)
review_body: Let me start by stating that the 6-year old that received this game was instantly hooked on it.  It is great to see the loveable monsters from Monsters Inc. in a new game based on the sequel.  While this was inevitable, not all licensed properties live up to one's expectations.  Thankfully, that was not the case here.  The game play is just the right level of difficulty for the recommended age range. The levels are challenging but not overly frustrating for the little ones.  The best aspect about games such as these is that kids are learning without even knowing it.  To them, they are having fun playing with some of their favorite characters in fairly easy to understand and fun activities.  The graphics are not overly impressive but again, since the game is fun, it hardly makes a difference.  The only quibble is the need to connect to the internet to download additional features of the game.  This is a re-occurring theme with LeapFrog and even Innotab games that simply is unnecessary.  It is just an excuse to get users to create an account with the company website where one will be enticed into making additional purchases.  A shameless marketing ploy that undermines the value of the games, in this reviewer's opinion.  Overall, this is a fun game that should keep the little ones entertained for quite some time.

product_title: Grimm's Color Charts Rally Building Blocks Set
review_headline: Grimms Blocks a pleasure for adults and kids alike to play with
review_body:
Like all Grimms blocks, these are stained and unvarnished and still have the feel of unfinished wood. The vibrant colors are gorgeous. You will not find colored blocks more attractive than those made by Grimms. Rectangles are 4 cm x 8 cm x 1 cm. They are very light weight but the unvarnished feel makes them less slippery and easier to build with. A few larger blocks (4 cm x 4 cm x variable height) are also included.

This set is great on its own and also makes a fabulous addition to a tabletop set of unfinished blocks. Adds a gorgeous splash of color. I noticed my kids were drawn to colorful plastic toys whereas I often purchase natural wood toys. Now the kids and I alike love to play with these beautiful blocks. Two of each color of rectangle is so many shades makes these fun for Montessori color matching. I was surprised my 5yo could detect the subtle differences.

Note that the nature of the stains (unsealed with varnish) means that sometimes one color rubs off on another block. This is rare, but it does happen and they may arrive that way. I've seen reviews of Grimms toys that were negative for only that reason. I've seen this with Holztiger too -- it just comes with the territory of the more natural finishes. I can tell you that my 18month-old sometimes sucks on the blocks (not recommended), and the colors don't seem to bleed at all.

We also have and love the 4cm stepped blocks (100 blocks) and several other Grimms blocks. We just love them!

review_headline: A decent addition to any Zombie deck.
review_body:
I bought this to add to my Zombie World deck for a strong monster that exceeds the seemingly standard attack for Zombies, which is 2400. It's effect is also pretty useful, if you manage to normal summon it you can use it's effect to return cards on the field to the owners hand at the cost of the cards in your hand.

It's nothing super epic but you know it might just help you out in a pinch, for a Zombie deck it's decent, combine it in a pure Zombie deck with Solidarity or a primarily earth Zombie deck with Gaia Power to strengthen it's attack and add Mezuki and Card Destruction.

Using it's effect to discard Mezuki let's you special summon a zombie in the graveyard, using it's effect and then using Card Destruction lets you return cards on the field to your opponents hand and then destroy them as well.

Really it all comes down to preference I do enjoy having this card in my deck though and I've used it plenty of times to clear the field of high level monsters or fusion/ritual/synchro monsters and then land an attack.

review_body: I've been into these awesome and beautiful Pullip dolls for a long time, and I gave this as a gift to a friend and started her obsession as well. Pullips are obviously expensive fashion dolls from Asia, and are more collectibles to be displayed on a shelf with their stands and/or used to dress/redress, carefully customize, and in photography. I cannot recommend these dolls, which aren't for play, to anyone under the age of 13 unless they are extremely careful. They tend to be fragile, especially this model from 2006 and is on the worst possible Pullip body, the type 3; this body tends to break at the wrists and is not very poseable, not to mention the squeaky sound when the joints are moved. This is usually remedied with replacing the body with an obitsu body, but unfortunately a replacement body in Nahh-ato's color shade is very rare to come by. If this is something you don't want to look forward to, you should look into the newer Pullips with the improved body type. Other than that, Nahh-ato is stunning as all Pullips are. product_title: Crazy Chalk: Rolling Stamper
review_body: I work for a small city police department that puts on a \\"Bike Rodeo\\" for kids every year. We struggled the first two years to draw chalk lines for the bicycle obstacle course. Drawing with street chalk is exhaustive, time consuming, and you usually skin your knuckles. The traditional line drawers with powdered chalk tend to just dump the chalk out all over, making a mess that gets all over everybody's shoes, and they're to bulky to maneuver easily. We didn't even consider spray chalk that comes in a can because it would be way to expensive. Then, my sister recommended this little tool that she found at a yard sale and use at her daycare. It's child-sized, so us adults have to hunch over. It makes a clicking sound that is sure to delight children while annoying the adults, and the attached bucket has to be refilled frequently....but this is still awesome. The chalk only goes where you want it to go, it makes a nice even line, and it just uses the cheap line-drawing chalk that you can get at a local hardware store for about $6 for 50lbs. I've borrowed my sister's for two years, but now I'm going to make my department buy our own. Definitely recommend! If they made this in an adult size, it would be five stars.

The puzzle pieces are well cut and sturdy. I hate puzzles where the pieces aren't cut through all the way and you have to tear them apart -- sometimes tearing the pieces. This is not one of those puzzles.

The puzzle comes in a sturdy box with magnetic closures. It includes a ziplock bag for storing the pieces. There's also a leaflet with a picture of the puzzle which is easier to handle than the puzzle box.

The puzzle picture has fun details that make it challenging. This one is from one of my favorite vacation spots. I get a kick out of the artistically stylized details.

I recommend this for puzzle lovers, Hawaii lovers, and those who like good simple fun.

review_body:

If the owner follows the directions the frogs can live quite happily in the aquarium provided. Mine sang, mated, molted and thrived. I have my tank on my desk where I'm entertained daily by the little cuties. Especially when I had a male and female, now I have two females.

I now have another frog and a few tetras in my 5 gallon tank that are doing fine but it took quite awhile to stabilize the new tank. The eco system provided by Natural Aquatics was very efficient and self sustaining as long as I followed the directions. I did, however, change the water a little more frequently than twice a year. I still feed the frogs the food provided by Natural aquatics, it sinks to the bottom of the tank so the fish don't eat it before the frogs can get to it.[[ASIN:B003XKNA5G Natural Aquatics Frog Aquarium with 2 Frogs]]

review_headline: Unbeatable value for a tube, don't pass this up
review_body:

I weigh around 250, and this has no problem keeping me up. I'm sure it could keep 2 of me up.

PROS:

The vinyl is thick feeling, and the design is top of the line. The 'back rest' portion inflates separately from the tube, allowing you the option of using it or not. The handles are in just the right spot and easy to grab, and it offers 2 average size cup holders which do a great job. The mesh netting is sturdy, and the inner hole is 'just the right size' for adults. You can easily paddle with your arms, or kick-off using your feet. The inflation orifice is a high quality screw-down device, guaranteed to not accidentally popoff.

Other notes: The inflation orifice is about 5/8" in diameter (eying it), and is meant for the 'hand' or 'foot' pump units, or anything with one of the larger inflation hoses. I didn't know this when I got it. I use the air system in my shop to inflate things like these, so I simply used a piece of vinyl tubing inserted into the orifice and connected to my air system, to inflate it quickly.

product_title: Voltron Lion Force Collector's Gift Set
review_body: Let me start by saying that I always wanted my very own Voltron Lion Force when I was a kid and now I own two. Yes, I said two. I first bought the die-cast version of the Toynami Masterpiece a few years ago. Later, I just had to have the plastic version. The die-cast Voltron is nice but very heavy. Every time I lift it I feel like I'm at the gym pulling a dun-bell. Also, when transforming the die-cast lions much care must be placed on not chipping the paint or wearing away the chrome on the legs. Not to mention the die-cast version is $100 to $150 more then the plastic version. My die-cast is typically for display only and when I need my Voltron \\"fix\\" I pull out the plastic one. I would like to think that the die-cast version is a homage to the original Voltron Lion Force toy released in 1981 by matchbox. The matchbox version was boxing and not really posable. Both Toynami versions are slimmer, which makes them look great and their very posable too. You can handle the plastic Voltron more frequently then it's die-cast counterpart without the fear of causing any damage. It's lighter in weight and you can pose it with ease. I've transformed the plastic version more then fifty times and I must say it's holding up very well. No chipping or signs of wear. Now, these Voltrons are collectables intended for the adult collector and I wound not recommend them for a child. But if you insist on getting your child one of these, go with the plastic version for sure.

product_title: Campaign Cartographer 3 Map Making for Gamers
review_headline: A stellar cartography suite (with a steep learning curve)
review_body:
I will preface this review by saying that if you do not love the creative process, mastering new skills or learning - then you should probably walk away from this product. In order to get the most from this product I devoted more than 6 hours over the course of 1 week watching YouTube video tutorials and practicing with the software.

However; that being said...after I invested the time to learn the software; it is an absolute joy to use. I can create beautifully illustrated, lush maps in very little time which has been immensely valuable in designing worlds for the tabletop roleplaying game that I run. The best part is that using the Layers and Sheets features of CC3 I am able to change and manipulate my map from source very easily; and then export it to a more useful format (such as PNG or JPG) at any time.

The bottom line? CC3 is a very powerful tool with a fairly steep learning curve. You will learn a lot about autocad software, best practices in layers-based graphic design (if you've ever used Photoshop, Paint.NET or GIMP you know what I mean) and cartography in the process of getting to know this tool. If that sounds great to you; spend the money on this software. If that sounds awful; walk away.

PROS

CONS

- First play-through normally requires a quick game without the zombies.
- Games can last up to an hour, depending on how often/crazy the rules change.
- Can get overwhelming as lots of new rules are introduced.

Very happy with this zombie-themed card game. It's fun and constantly keeps you thinking and planning ahead. The cards explain themselves, making the rules very easy to understand. A must have for anyone who enjoys a quick, fast-paced card game.

product_title: Wise Alec: Civilize This
review_headline: Civilze This !  Who's the Wise Alec in your family!
review_body:
When I first opened up the package after receiving this game, I was immediately struck with how sturdy and well packaged it is. The box is quite thick and even has a magnetic closure and a plastic cover to go over the card slots to keep it well packaged during travel.

Wise Alec: Civilize This! is an expansion pack for the original Wise Alec Game

We love to play board games as a family, so were quite eager to receive and play Wise Alec: Civilize This! after receiving it. We have studied ancient civilizations quite in depth in our homeschool and felt that this game would be great to reinforce some of the things we have learned.

Included in the game is one colour coded plastic die as well as 4 decks of 50 cards each. Each card has a 3 point question and a 7 point question. Obviously, the 7 point question is harder than the 3 point question, but they are on the same topic on each card. The card decks have themes that are Ancient, Medieval, Modern and Wise Alec. The Wise Alec cards are ice breaker questions such as performing 20 squats, or naming 5 countries in a certain continent and I think are meant to level the playing field between younger players and older players. The game also offers other ideas on how to level the playing field like staggering the points needed to win. One idea is that Mom and Dad need 75 points, Older children need 50 and younger children need 25. Another idea is to make all questions worth 5 points, but the older children and adults only get to answer the 7 point questions. Both of these are a great idea!

The instructions for the game are printed right on the inside front cover of the game box. This is perfect, not only for a game that children are going to be playing, but also for a travel game. Not sure about everyone else's children, but mine always lose the instruction sheet of their games LOL! I know, that is only my children, but surely there are some somewhere else that do this too

There are a couple of different play methods to choose from. One is to go to a certain point level before ending the game, for example, the first player to get to 50 points wins. Or, you can choose a certain time limit, say, 20 or 30 minutes and the player with the most points wins. We found that the game can actually be played with as many players as you want, you are not limited to the 2-6 that the game specifies.

product_title: Chinese Checkers and Traditional Checkers
review_body:
This is a piece of junk. If I could give this a \\"0 stars\\" rating, I would. It is shameful to even waste trash bin space on this one. Seriously. Yes, it really IS that bad.

1) Chinese Checkers: The board size -- at 11-1/2 inches diameter -- is ridiculously small, which renders it frustrating to all parties of all ages who attempt to play. It is next-to-impossible for even the most adroit and nimble-fingered adult to play. And even our children at ages 6 and 7, with their teeny tiny fingers, cannot move one ball one space anywhere on the board without disrupting at least a dozen other balls and sending them scattering to the four corners of the Earth. And believe me, this has nothing to do with motor skills or eye-hand coordination!

2) Chinese Checkers: This set does NOT utilize real glass marbles which look aesthetically pleasing in their soft pearlized hues and feel pleasantly organic to the touch. Oh no. Rather this set comes with cheap, pathetic little lightweight plastic \\"balls\\" in obnoxious primary colors. The pathetic plasticness of these \\"balls\\" renders them utterly useless for anything other than annoyingly rolling to the four corners of the Earth -- at every touch, turn, hiccup, and/or breath!

3) Chinese Checkers: The holes are not set deep enough into the board; therefore, the pathetic little lightweight plastic \\"balls\\" proceed to roll annoyingly to the four corners of the Earth every time someone even minimally touches the playing table, board, or any marble on the board. In fact, if anyone even closes a door in the house, turns on the radio, or a car backfires in the street, all of the pathetic little lightweight plastic \\"balls\\" on the board WILL indeed roll annoyingly to the four corners of the Earth.

4) Checkers: First, the checkers are about the size of Sweet Tarts and trying to play the game on a board this small will nearly drive you mad. Second, the checkers will not stack and stay put whenit comes time to \\"king\\" someone. Third, there is something about the sound of plastic checkers banging down in repeated movements on a tin board that is akin to nails on a chalkboard in the realm of one's auditory sense. And last but certainly not least, similar to the Chinese Checkers side of this maddening duo, if you can move your checkers on this eensy board without disrupting every other checker on the board and sending them sliding toward the four corners of the Earth, well, you have some mad playing skills that no one who has entered our home of any age, gender, race or religion -- be it man, woman or child -- can master!

5) Storage: The pathetic little lightweight plastic \\"balls\\" and maddeningly unstackable checkers cannot be sandwiched for storage inside of this two-sided tin (even though this is touted as a \\"feature\\" of the product) when/if kept in the nylon netted bags in which they come. We had to separate \\"balls\\" and checkers out into several ziploc baggies in order to spread them out in a \\"thin enough\\" layer to actually get the tin to stay sandwiched closed. So essentially, we had to repackage all the playing pieces immediately in order to simply get the tin to stay closed for storage in between play sessions.

Bottom Line: This set is ill-conceived and poorly executed on so many different levels it's appalling. \\"Cheap junk\\" is the best thing I can say about it. My mother bought it locally for twice the price it is here on Amazon as a Valentine's gift for our children. Within three days, they were frustrated beyond measure, and my husband and I went online looking for something better.

For a good quality, aesthetically pleasing, useable, properly-sized Chinese Checkers set at a reasonable price, please consider the **15\\" JUMBO CHINESE CHECKERS WITH MARBLES BY CHH** here on Amazon. It has a lovely, solid wood board with deeply drilled holes and real glass marbles in gorgeous pearlized colors... feels great tothe finger, sounds right to the ear, looks much nicer in person than it does online. It has been worth every penny, complimented highly, and well received by all who have played.

Because there's so much more to playing a game than just winning.... ;)
