product_title: Go Goddess Game
review_headline: Thought provoking and female bonding at its best!
review_body:
I purchased this game several years ago on a whim. I liked the box and figured, hey, why not?

This game turned into a bond with my girlfriends that has been incredible. It has thought provoking questions that are multiple choice, fill in the blank or simply answer what's on your mind and in your heart.

It started out with me and two friends who turned Go Goddess into a weekly get together that truly helped grow our friendships as well as each our own person giving us clarity on things that would come out in the game that would also be something we were dealing with at that current time in our lives.

Then we grew. Adding other friends to the group, we gained other insights that made our group more open minded and whole.

I started playing this game when I was in my early twenties. I'm now in my early thirties, married, small child, and my friends and I still yearn to play this game. (Living several states apart makes it tricky.) It has made life more full simply by talking to each other. It also has been a game we have been able to grow with since what we thought early on has changed now that we're married and have children.

I've read the other reviews on this game, and I'm understanding of their concerns, but a little saddened as well. I don't think this game promotes alternative medicine simply by suggesting it in a multiple choice question. This game is designed to include ALL women regardless of race, sexual orientation, religion, or medical choice. What if there was a card that discussed at home birth over traditional birth at the hospital? Or c-section versus vaginal birth? Would that turn someone against the game simply because it's a woman's choice/preference either way?

And for the question about one's daughter being a lesbian and not having a multiple choice option to accept her for who she is, I agree. That should be an option. But that's also part of the beauty of the game. I could go through all of the different cards in this review and suggest why one question is complete or incomplete in some fashion. But that's something else I love about the game. The conversations that we had not only about the question would turn into, \\"Why isn't 'accept and love her for who she is' an option?\\" Then we'd discuss why, and I can't tell you how many times an A B C D multiple choice card turns into an A through ZZ option card because of all the tangents we go on discussing ONE card.

Perhaps the women who designed the game could include new cards to include some of these thing that are very important to many women. Can you imagine what the cards would have said 30 years ago based on the ideals back then? What about 50 years ago?

At the end of the game, players collect the cards they chose throughout the game. There's the ROYGBIV rainbow as part of the game, and each player counts to see how many card of each color they have. Once a player determines that she has more red cards or indigo cards in her hand, then that is her color for the game. There is Radiant Red, Optimistic Orange, Intelligent Yellow, Growing Green, Balanced Blue, Intuitive Indigo and Positive Purple (though I'd love to see Vivacious Violet....) Each color in the booklet has a list of power words to walk away with. For example, Radiant Red lists Enthusiasm - Every day, in every way, live life to the fullest.

Sometimes the color one gets at the end of the game fits perfectly to where she is that day or week. Other times it's something to strive toward. Then sometimes it's a kick in the kidney to look in the mirror and say, \\"Hey, lady, get your stuff together cause this is so you. You're not alone, we'll get through this.\\"

I give this game an overwhelming stamp of approval. My girlfriends and I have grown so much and become stronger by strengthening our bond with each other and working on improving ourselves knowing we have women friends to support us. I think giving the game a try or pulling it out of the garage sale pile and giving it another try is definitely something to consider. It's also very interesting to include some men in the conversation. Made my husband join the ladies one night, and he brought a new perspective to the table!

I would also like to add that I am in NO way affiliated with the game in any way. Fridge pins are strong. They're small, but incredibly powerful. Their small size lets them easily compress several pages together to hold them to the fridge (something I've found magnets with larger surface area, but less concentrated strength have trouble with).

product_title: Ideal School Supply Tactile Letters Kit
review_body:
I think these will be useful for us but are smaller than I had expected. I should have read the product description more closely so that's on me--they're just smaller than I was picturing.

The cards themselves are about 3 1/2 by 2 3/4 inches. The letters are 1 1/4 by 2 inches and fairly narrow--the sandpaper is only about 1/4 inch wide. They are made out of cardstock, but it's a heavy duty cardstock and feels fairly sturdy. They're heavier than what you'd get on a playing card or a flashcard. The quality is reasonable for the price.

At any rate, I think they are a good tactile tool for learning letters and phonics. My son likes tracing the letters with his finger. Today we played memory with the capital and lowercase letters. I was also able to get a good crayon rubbing with them. Although they are smaller than I had thought they would be I think they will prove to be worth the purchase. It's a good choice if you don't want to invest in the higher quality but more expensive Montessori style letters.

product_title: Monster High Picture Day Cleo De Nile Doll
review_body:
Picture Day Cleo de Nile

Finally completed my collection of the picture day dolls! Now I have to wait patiently for wave two to hit the states, OK before I digress further, I'll get into the doll. Like all of the Picture Day dolls, Cleo comes with a stand, hairbrush, binder, purse and Fearbook.

This is actually my first Cleo, so I have no comparisons to offer on any of Cleo's other outfits. That being said I really love her Picture day ensemble. She has cute gold and blue wedge sandals on. The heels of the shoes have feather and Egyptian detailing that I'm quite fond of. Her knee-length leggings are metallic gold and black stripes, paying homage to her Mummy ancestry. Cleo's top is exceptional a tunic length, royal blue with metallic gold detailing, replicates mummy wrappings. Soft blue and gold gems printed onto the fabric, give the top a nice touch.

Cleo comes with minimal jewelry accessories. A gold belt with a black scarab buckle in the same detailing as her shoes accompanies a cuff bracelet with a similar design. My particular doll did not come with earrings, though I have heard rumors that some of the picture day Cleo's did come with scarab earrings of some kind. No necklace of any kind adorns Cleo's neck which makes me slightly sad.

On an up note, Cleo's translucent blue purse has a beautiful gold scarab design on both sides. The purse also opens for play. Her gold Binder has feather detailing and will hold all of her Screamology homework, as it too opens for play.

Cleo's wig is thick and full with her trademark black and gold hair covering an underlay of turquoise. Her bangs are heavily hair sprayed but the rest of her wig is easily brushed and restyled after unpacking.

Overall a lovely doll to own!!

product_title: My Pillow Pets Hungry Hippo - Large (Lavender)
review_body:
Different from any other, this pillow pet is no typical stuffed animal. I have been through countless stuffed dogs, bears, cats and more; yet none compare to my beloved hippo. Many Christmases ago, Hippy came into my life wrapped clumsily beneath the lit tree. It was love at first sight as I squeezed my fluffy friend close to my heart. From that moment on we were inseparable - well, except for the time I spent with other humans, homework and sports. Hippy was indeed my partner in crime, or more like my partner in watching innumerable movies, studying and sneaking food into my room. He was always there for me, the only stuffed friend I'd ever need. Every night as I headed to bed, I knew his soft, fuzzy self would await me. I can't even begin to think what I would have done during a terrifying storm without my thunder buddy. I could depend on Hippy to let me hide under his silky, purple belly for the loudest cracks of thunder. After a while of owning my stuffed friend, I refused to wash him for the mere chance that we wouldn't return the same. I was mortified when my mother decided it was time for a swim in the washing machine without telling me. I sighed of relief when he returned just as cushiony as before.

When it was time to move on to college, you bet Hippy came along with me, just as excited for our new surroundings. I was fortunate to have a piece of home to get me through such a transition in my life. College can be a lonely place, you know, but lucky for me I had my shaggy friend to rely on. The few nights I struggled to get to sleep were spent clung to my Hippy instead of counting sheep. Many may think that continuing to sleep with a stuffed animal in college is considered childish, but my response would be: Not only is this hippo my cuddle buddy, but he's a pillow - how multifaceted my friend is! There is no worse feeling than those long, cold nights when Hippy would fall from my lofted bed onto the floor and I was faced with the difficult decision to sleep solo or climb down from this zenith of a bed to retrieve him. For the times I felt homesick, just seeing Hippy's gigantic smile reminded me that home was still with me.

Since college has been such a busy period, I have had less time to devote to my pillow friend. To prevent his loneliness, I bought him the perfect surprise - his own pillow pet friend, Herky! These fluffy creatures are best in multiples so buy as many as your heart desires. Obviously from my experiences, these pets are perfect for any age and can warm anyone's heart. I highly recommend my friend's counterparts to anyone looking for a quiet, but loving companion.

review_body:
Big bubble wands are hard to do well at a good price. Unless you make your own, there's not a lot of quality choices out there. Glad I found this one (after trying some of the lesser ones) after making bubbles for many years since it's perfect for consistently large bubbles.

I wish that I had this wand at the beginning of my learning curve since it is better made and larger than others I've tried. Would not hesitate to recommend this to anyone serious about making giant bubbles.

It could be a little longer so as to create larger bubbles, frankly. There's another wand on the market that's longer/larger so if you want maximum bubbles without crafting your own, then look around.

Some basic tips for beginners:

Technique and maintenance are the key things to observe with any wand (that has a cotton lasso). Technique is more than just how you open/close the wand or the weather you make the bubbles in: bubble juice mix is part of the equation too. Here's the basic recipe: 1 gallon hot water, 1 cup yellow JOY detergent, and 1 tablespoon baking powder (not soda) blended vigorously. You could double the detergent for better viscosity but it's not necessary in decent weather. I use a 3 gallon pail filled with 2 gallons of the bubble juice per session.

When starting a session, allow your dry cotton lasso to be submerged entirely in the bubble juice for at least 30 seconds before beginning. It still might take several dips and attempts before you reach total saturation, but be persistent.

Maintenance of this (or any cotton lasso wand) requires you to rinse the lasso. Then gently squeeze the lasso as your run your hand down to the end, removing excess moisture. Now it's ready to store and should be fine for the next session.

product_title: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles Classic Collection Raphael
review_body:
Having grown up with the Turtles, I was ecstatic to see these \\"collector's\\" versions announced by Playmates. They look just about perfect, having popped right out of the cartoons series. Mind you, Playmates was famous for bringing the Turtles to plastic life with the explosion of the cartoon series, so I wasn't expecting any comic renditions. In any case, we have NECA to thank for the comic releases.

But with the resurgence of the Turtles through Nickelodeon--which, if I may be so bold, is better than the original cartoon--Playmates decided to cash in with the older generation, who adored the '80s cartoon with persistent whining to their parents for the Technodrome and blimp (both of which I owned, both of which are now long gone). These collector versions are geared for that crowd; though, with the durability of the plastic, I wouldn't hesitate to give them to children 7+.

These are as great as you can get with the classic TMNTs, though they aren't exactly perfect. I'll start with Raphael here.

The articulation is overall fantastic, having a little more than necessary. He's even got individual finger and toe articulation, like his brothers, though I found that the finger articulation doesn't provide for great grips for his sai. They dangle a bit loosely in his hands. If you can get the fingers to tighten just so and not move him they don't look as bad. So, while it's great to have finger articulation, it does detract from the strength of his grip.

Also, I'm not a fan of his blank stare. Playmates seems to have tried to mimic the toothy clench from their older figures, and I appreciate that, but I don't like the blank stare. Maybe a more menacing frown, like the Nick counterpart, could have served better. That being said, his face isn't as bad as the other Turtles; I wish Mikey had a grin and Donatello have the contemplative face. A sterner look for Leonardo could've been better, too. But those are my opinions. I'm not a toy designer, so what do I know?

The color is great, as each Turtle has a different shade. The big \\"R\\" on his belt buckle, not to mention his colored bandana and pads, is a dead giveaway that these are designed off the cartoon look. Which is great. If you want the definitive versions of the comic Turtles, if not the only, the now-expensive NECA line is the way to go. If you want the definitive '80s cartoon look, these Playmates Classic Collection line is the way to go. With Bebop and Rocksteady next, let's hope Playmates soon releases April, Krang, Splinter, and, most importantly, Shredder.

My final complaint is the size. While I'm not too upset that they're a bit larger, they won't fit in scale with other 6\\"-ish scale figures, should you desire to cross over. I plan to pose these by themselves, so it doesn't detract too much for me; still, it would've been nice to see some shorter Turtles.

They all come with sewer stands with their names, which is nice. And the colorful packaging makes me almost wish I didn't open them. But what are you going to do?

All in all, a great addition to any toy collector's hoard, especially if they grew up with TMNT.oy designer, so what do I know?

product_title: Polly Pocket Wall Party Ultimate All-in-One Playset
review_body:
This Polly Pocket Wall Party is an innovative way for my daughter to play with her Polly Pocket toys and it gets the clutter off of the floor. Since these toys can be attached to the wall, I don't have to worry so much about stepping on the pieces or vacuuming them up.

Assembly was a bit tricky as there were not a lot of written instructions. The pieces for each item were sorted into individual bags and some of them had instructions in color. Those were easier to assemble than the ones in grayscale. One of the pieces holding the adhesive was put on upside down in the factory and that threw me for a loop, but once I figured that out, I took it apart and put it back together the right way and popped it into place with no problem.

Most of the pieces don't have a level bottom, so you can't easily play with them on the floor. They really are designed for the wall only. We'd considered putting the Wall Party on the marble surrounding our fireplace because we thought the adhesive strips would stick better, but after looking at it we thought there wouldn't be enough space to fit everything. We ended up putting it all on textured walls. We pressed the strips on really hard and they've been sticking fine.

My daughter has a lot of fun playing with this set. She has some other Polly Pocket items she can incorporate too. She seems to be pleased about how novel this toy is compared to other floor or table toys and she really likes the slides and zip lines that connect different areas. I'd recommend this as something that's a change from the usual doll sets.

The others from ALEX we have tried, include some big craft kit/box, which was awesome. Tons of variety, and just a great activity for a rainy day with your kid or kids. We also use at least two of their expandable art folders, which are great, and finally we tried a kit with crumpled paper that you make into pictures. Pretty great, hands on stuff for our age kids (3/6/9).

I cannot recommend this one though, because 1. the bits for the automatic screwdriver don't stay on, which causes great frustration (to parent and kid). But more importantly perhaps is 2. it's just not any fun. There a PLENTY of great \\"drilling\\" toys/kits out there that I would recommend, like pretty much anything from Battat, for instance.

Sorry, ALEX, you make some good, to very good kits, but this isn't one of them.

product_title: Disney/Pixar Brave Merida Doll
review_body:
I am so happy that Disney made a Celtic Princess (Scotland is part of the Celt belt.) with their new movie Brave! Being obsessed with all things Celtic, I had to get a Merida doll.

I bought the Mattel version of Merida because she was all I could afford with my budget at the time. I liked the Gem Stylin' Merida too but was worried about the gems that come with her getting lost. I bought the plain Merida doll because she didn't come with accessories that could get lost.

There have been mixed reviews about this version of Merida. Some have hated her, said she wasn't accurate at all compared to the Disney Store version, etc. Others have loved her. I fall somewhere in the middle. I don't hate her, but I don't think she's the greatest thing ever either. I just don't see the stink some people are pitching about her not being \\"official.\\" I don't think it's bad she's dressed in her formal dress. There is a Disney Store version of Merida where she wears her formal gown.

When I was growing up, before we got a Disney Store, the Mattel version of the Disney Princesses were all we had. I made do with the Mattel ones.

My favorite detail of her costume is the golden celtic knotwork on the bottom of her dress. I love her circlet too.

I am glad I got Merida because she is different compared to the other princesses.

Zoomy is a handheld digital microscope from Learning Resources that eliminates all that frustration and provides a fun, easy science experience for kids of all ages!

The egg-shaped microscope is easy to hold, whether you are three or forty-three. It plugs right into a computer USB port to provide a full-screen shot of whatever you want to place under Zoomy to explore in depth. It comes with a tiny disc formatted with the viewer that provides up to 43x magnification.

The lights are built-in to the bottom of Zoomy digital microscope and the button on top swirls for focusing or you can just move it around with your hand. The top button also allows you to take a picture that pops up on your computer so you can save the photo if you want. What a great way to get photos for a science fair project!

I placed a white piece of paper on my desk and grabbed a beaded bracelet. There are also two stabilizer domes you can attach to the bottom of Zoomy if you're so excited that your hands won't stop shaking!

You can capture photos or videos with Zoomy and the online viewer allows you to add special effects and picture frames too. This microscope is so much fun to use and it's so simple even preschoolers can use it on their own.

Wanting to play some more, I pulled a leaf off a dandelion in my front yard and was amazed at the magnified details. I absolutely love the fantastic experiences that new technology provides, so our children can have more positive and more exciting opportunities today.

review_body:

My husband and I took about 2 hours to put it together and the instructions were pretty easy to follow but be sure to have a few extra tools handy. You're going to need a wrench, ratchet, hammer, ladder and philips screwdriver. You're also going to need 2 persons which is the reason why I had to help hubby set it up. Usually he's the one doing all the work.

We also bought the [[ASIN:B001P5GRF6 Little Tikes 2-in-1 Snug N Secure Swing-Pink]] since at 14 months our daughter is too small for the swings that came with it.

It doesn't mention it here on Amazon but it states that 4 kids can be on this with the maximum weight of each child being 80lbs. It was one of the reason why I chose the Lookout over the clubhouse since the clubhouse was only 60lbs.

The climbing ladder though is a little difficult for my daughter to maneuver but once we put her up she loves sliding down the slide. My daughter should have fun with this for at least another 3 years I would say. It's durable, weatherproof and we love the colors.

Would I recommend for a toddler I definitely would. Anyone over 5-6 definitely not although my 8yr old is able to swing along with his sister without any problems. For older kids I would get something that would last a much longer time.

product_title: Hansa Teutonica
review_body:
Hansa Teutonica is a Euro-style game with a lot going on. Hansa Teutonica has a great amount of many ways to score Victory Points (the goal of the game), and has open enough game play that at a table of 5 everyone will likely be trying a slightly different strategy. The game play itself is described well in some of the other reviews here and I recommend watching one of the teaching videos on BoardgameGeek if you do want to learn how to play if no one in your game group has played before. So therefore I will make this review short and to the point.

Good things:
Lots of variety every time you play someone will try a slightly new strategy since there are so many ways to score Victory Points.
Excellent game play for 3-5 at about 90 minutes. (sorry I don't recommend playing 2 player.)
Quality components, either wooden bits or thick cardboard
The game progresses at a rapid pace, so even if you start with one plan you must be flexible.
It is a pure strategy no luck game, with perfect information so everyone knows the same things at the same time.

I highly recommend this game in fact it is one of my absolute favorites. If you have never played any modern board games it might not be the best place to start but if you have played Ticket to Ride and enjoyed it or want something deeper this is an excellent choice. It is a fairly easy game to teach someone to play (for a Euro), but it may take anywhere from a half a game to a couple games before the learner has a grasp on it, but stay with it your patience will be rewarded. It really is that good.

[[VIDEOID:moOBEYP8LVSLWE]]I've owned this pair of ladies for many years now. I bought them at a Suncoast Video in a local mall. I haven't even been to a mall in at least four years now and even then the store had been long closed down. I was lucky enough to get them for around 15 dollars. They are a couple of pretty ladies. They both have cute little tails and as another reviewer says one is a cat and one is a monkey I guess. Also of note for collectors like me is the exceptional box they come packaged in. You can keep them in it and still enjoy looking at them by simply opening the front door like cover of the box. It has a small piece of velcro that holds it closed. I've actualy kept it this way until now so I could make the video. I plan on placing them back in it.
Well anyways I would recommend a purchase if you can get them for a fair price and if you are a fan of anime figures of cute girls.

product_title: Fisher-Price Thomas Wooden Railway - Water Tower
review_body:
If your wooden train set -- with its bridges, tunnels, switch tracks, and curves -- is still lacking something, this might be the perfect addition to your setup. The Thomas & Friends Wooden Railway Water Tower is pretty simple -- just move the black tube/lever, and the tower appears to fill with water. Move the lever the other way, and the water seems to disappear. Okay, so the liquid doesn't look exactly like water -- it's bright blue -- but little kids probably won't mind.

I brought this to a preschool playgroup and set it up with the tracks the children already had. The playgroup has collected at least three different wooden train brands over the years -- Melissa & Doug, Brio, and one other brand. The track piece on this water tower was compatible with those others. The children in the playgroup -- ages 2 and 3 -- had to be shown what the water tower did, but they were quickly interested in it and seemed to enjoy pretending to give water to the little trains.

Overall I think this is a fun, interactive toy that can add a little extra something to your wooden train setup. My only disappointment in it is the price. However, I have heard good things about the Thomas & Friends line as far as durability, so perhaps it may be a worthy investment/addition to your set.

Out of the box, this figure wears a helmet that can be removed with the front pack. The face underneath the helmet is the one of a clone trooper. The rest of the body is well sculpted, but the best details are on the \\"hard parts\\" like the helmet. This figures also includes a blaster.

This figure has:
- ball-jointed head,
- ball-hinged shoulders, elbows, knees, ankles, and
- swivel forearms, waist and hips.

There is nothing overly impressive with this figure. It offers good likeness and posability.

review_body:

Each card has four riddles represented by four symbols - a square, circle, triangle and star. It's all random, no degree of difficulty and the symbols don't represent any categories. They just determine which riddle gets read when you roll the die. Getting a correct answer wins the card the question was on. The first person or team to collect 10 cards wins.

I found the board game version to be a bit confusing when you had to switch pieces with another player, so I actually like this version a little better.

product_title: Polly Pocket Wall Party Ultimate All-in-One Playset
review_body:
This amazing toy actually brought out the kid in me, a 31 year old mom. Once this was all put together and ready to play with it provided hours of fun for my 8 year old daughter and even my 4 year old son. I love that there are SO many different areas for them to play with and it's kind of like an entire town, tree house style. I must say, I prefer Polly Pockets over Barbie's and they are only getting better and better. We have some older ones but these new ones are slightly larger and more durable. The clothes are easier to put on as well, which is nice since my 4 year old likes to remove them but in the past had trouble dressing them. This set also comes with loads of accessories. It has dishes and cups and all that good stuff, but there are extra shoes and other fun accessories as well. And the shoes (and other things that need to stand on their own) come with little suction cups so you can actually stand the Polly Pockets up and they don't fall over. Major bonus since they don't stand or even sit very well on their own. I also love that the hot air balloon has a storage compartment in it. So all the accessories can be stored in there and there's plenty of room. There are a few other places to put stuff as well, like under the tent. So you don't actually need any storage containers for all the little pieces. This toy definitely makes for plenty of fun playing time for my kids and their friends.

The one negative thing, which isn't a negative once it's all said and done... is that this is a pain to put together! It has LOTS of pieces and you have to put each little section together. It comes with directions for each piece, and you can be a little creative in how you arrange them, but you want to make sure to think ahead and consider how they'll all come together cause there are 'zip' lines for the Polly Pockets to get to each section. You want to make sure it's the right distance and all that. So it wasn't terribly hard to put together, but it was extremely time consuming. It took me at least two hours to get it done but once I did it was worth it.

We've had this now for maybe about two months and while the kids aren't AS enamored with it, they still have fun playing with it. And the stickies that attach it to the wall have stayed sticky cause nothing has fallen down yet.

I definitely recommend this toy and one MAJOR bonus is that it's a toy that's off the ground. What mom out there isn't sick of toys covering the floor? This toy doesn't touch the floor!but it was extremely time consuming. It took me at least two hours to get it done but once I did it was worth it.

review_body:

The case is handsome wood with a starburst inlaid pattern on its top which looks beautiful. The interior is lined with nice flock felt, and holds the tiles tight when closed (some of my sets, after you lay the tiles in it orderly, and pick it up, all the tiles tumble around inside because there's too much room inside the case for the number of tiles).

The poker chips it comes with are basic, as are the TWO! prevailing wind indicator dials. For such a nice set, these accessories are under-quality, but I wouldn't pick a set based on its chips. Short of buying a collectable set of tiles, you won't find anything nicer.

product_title: TOMY Gearation Building Toy
review_headline: A solid, fun magnetic gear set.
review_body:
My toddler (28 months old) loves gears. We bought this set to supplement our refrigerator set ([[ASIN:B00004U95L TOMY Gearation Refrigerator Magnets Building Toy]]) with more gears. This set exceeded our expectations. Like the other set, the plastic gears and decals are colorful and fun. This set includes eleven gears, including two sound-making gears (a \\"clicker\\" and a \\"ringer\\", with a tiny bell).

We liked that the gears' teeth are smaller than some of the other play gear sets, giving this one less of a \\"little kid toy\\" look. Our toddler, like most, is drawn to things that aren't toys first and foremost. The magnets are strong enough to keep the gears where they need to be, but even a small child can still easily nudge one across the metal surface to mesh the gears.

All is not perfect, though. The gear with the rotating arm sometimes touches other gears instead of gliding over them, making the gears stick and stop rotating. The gear that has a sold-colored cutout top with the teeth that spins over a fixed base with a colorful sticker has a similar problem. It's a mid-sized gear and the principle is good, but the execution is lacking. The cover wobbles sometimes, making the gears stop spinning and the motor click painfully. (Poor motor.) Then the kid (or you) has to figure out which gear is causing the problem, interrupting play. Or enhancing problem-solving, if you want to think about it that way.

The powered backer board is a good idea, but with the batteries, it's very large and heavy for even a tall two-year-old. It's in the closet until he's bigger, but by then I doubt he'll be playing with this toy anymore, unless Tomy comes out with new gear expansion sets. If you're buying this for an older child, I think you'll get more use out of the board than we have.

Bottom line: If your kid likes the Gearation refrigerator set, you MUST HAVE this set, too, so you'll have a respectable number of gears for play. Be aware that each of the four non-powered gears in the refrigerator set is duplicated in this set, though they have different decals.

product_title: Academy F-86F-30 "Sabre"
review_body:
The 1st impression one gets from this box is it's an excellent product. The pieces come bagged, the instructions are well done and easy-to-follow, and the canopy and clear parts come on their own sprue protected from the other parts.

I did the cockpit, engine, and painted the internals of the model first. The cockpit was assembled and painted as per the kit instructions. There is not one bit of flash on the parts. The J-47 engine is well done. One may assemble the F-86 with it in \\"pieces\\" like there is maintenance being done in a shop. I didn't build my jet that way to the detailed engine is hidden in the fuselage where all a modeler can see is the tail pipe. I really liked the duct work on the intake. I've ran into too many models that don't have any ductwork it looks like crud.

The decal sheet is a dream and there will be hours of work putting the decals into place. I use sov-a-set to keep my decals in place and will give the model an overspray of neutral clear coat. That way decades later the decals will not peel off over time.

Note, I did not follow the USAF model for this kit. I had some left over decals from a Canadair MK6 Saber and built it in standard mid-1950s day fighter colors for NATO. Generally the F-86F-30 and Canadair Sabre Mk6 are identical fighters from a modeler's point of view. There is a vent on the Canadair that missing from the F-86F-30 but 99% of the people in the world don't know the difference.

I really highly endorse this excellent kit. I got it off Amazon for a better price than I got from Squadron(.)com for the same product. The shipping was fast. All in all this was a very positive experence.

product_title: Aluminum Main Rotor Hub: MCPX
review_headline: Metal main rotor hub, designed to protect your dog bones!
review_body:
The plastic main rotor head that come with the mCPX Helis does a pretty good job but one continual problem is that due to the design the dog bones attached to it are often broken in a crash. They get over flexed and snap. This Microheli design has an enclosed channel for the dog bones to fit into, with this simple improvement, they are kept from over flexing and rarely break now. Yipee, one less thing to repair!

I've been really happy with the MicroHeli brand. Each of the many upgrade components I've purchased from them have been reliable and worked well.

A brief mention of why you should consider trying this mCPX heli: I really wanted to find a way to get my skills up to the level of inverted flight and some fun flying (loops rolls, flips and so forth). The problem is that the cost of learning on a larger Heli is really high. To avoid the damage that a single crash costing $50 or more does to my pocketbook, I tried this micro collective pitch heli. I have been VERY pleased and have been able to conquer inverted flight and some tricks.

The pros of this Heli are simple. It's low cost (relatively speaking for a Heli) and very crash resistant. When you do break something the pieces are low cost and easily available. There are a few cons with this Heli. #1, it's very small, and easy to lose orientation with distance, it takes good focus to learn how it looks at anything past 25'. #2, the tail is a bit weak relative to the main motor and you can get tail washout with full energy rotor actions. There are mods for this and the Heli is still very flyable in spite of this. Depending on your eyesight and budget it could be easier for you to move to a larger CP Heli, I have friends who love the130 for this very reason.

The typical method of learning heli flying is to start with a coaxial heli which has 2 sets of counter rotating blades (Blade mCX2 ). That will help you learn orientation and the basic stick movement. Next, I went to a fixed pitch Heli to learn more control and stick management (Blade mSR). I stayed on fixed pitch too long and should have moved to this Collective Pitch Heli sooner since it wasn't that hard of a jump for me to make the change. I'll be sticking with this Heli until I have inverted flight and additional tricks down without damage. Next. I"ll move up in size since by avoiding crashes I'll be able to afford to fly the larger Helis. The great part about flying with this collective Pitch Heli is that I have it all programmed up on a DX7 with the very same controls and switches I'll be using on larger Helis, which helps me as I step up. Everything I'm learning and doing now carries forward.

review_headline: Fun, motorized engine and coal car set.
review_body:
My four year old nephew is a big fan of \\"Thomas & Friends\\". Likes:
>Die-cast metal engine and coal car feels hefty, robust, and more durable than the wooden and plastic \\"Thomas & Friends\\" engines and railroad car sections.
>Electric motor drives four rubberized plastic wheels provides plenty of traction along the wooden tracks.
>Easy magnetic connectors to add on other magnetized train sections.

Slight Dislikes:
>Hiro has no problem pulling along several wooden/plastic train sections but has to strain to pull two metal cars over the elevated bridge sections.

>Kids will want to add more accessories such as [[ASIN:B000TLW3NC Thomas & Friends Wooden Railway - Musical Caboose]], [[ASIN:B001PAKU0O Thomas And Friends Wooden Railway - Zoo Car]], [[ASIN:B000J53Z12 Thomas And Friends Wooden Railway - Deluxe Railroad Crossing]], etc. Parents be prepared to spend some $$$.

Overall:
A fun toy for kids 3 and older with some educational value in teaching kids how to assemble the wooden tracks and imagine/design different track layouts. We'll undoubtedly be buying more accessories to add to the kids' \\"Thomas & Friends\\" collection.

product_title: Venom 25C 2S 10000mAh 7.4V LiPo Battery with Universal Plug (EC3/Deans/Traxxas/Tamiya)
review_headline: 1 of my 6 of these batteries has already died after two months.
review_body:
I purchased 6 of these batteries for Traxxas Stampede brushed motor RC vehicles. I have three trucks and 6 of these batteries (2 per truck). Each of the batteries was used twice as the weather turned cold in my area and we could not go outside as it was too snowy and cold. I have 2 Traxxas chargers and properly charged the batteries each time using the 2S setting (7.4V and 5.0A current). After two months in storage, one of the battery is now giving me a low voltage warning and will not take a charge. I find that unacceptable. I'm waiting to hear back from the supplier and/or manufacturer of the battery and see how they respond. These batteries are $87 a piece and not cheap to say the least. As I have purchased 6 of these, I will update my review once the manufacturer responds.

Now, the positives: When the batteries work they work well. Runtime in excess of 45 minutes each (the average temperature outside was 25F). Also, make sure to run these batteries in the correct voltage mode (green on the Traxxas stampede truck - there is a little button on the truck, not on the battery). The instructions state this. Another very useful feature of this product are the additional connectors. My chargers did not come with the correct converters but these batteries did and they made connecting to the battery a breeze.

This particular battery will not fit in the Traxxas stampede's battery slot properly so I took a velcro strap and secured the battery in place with this modification. I spoke with a Traxxas rep who assured me that these batteries were compatible electrically with the brushed motor but that I would have to come up with a way to fit them inside the chassis.

In sum, right now this battery has 3 stars with me due to the 1 failure.

My major beef with this product is that it does not come with an adapter (it uses AA batteries), which was surprising to me, but also I could not find anywhere in the material which adapter to purchase. I had a similar one, but the part that plugs into the unit is just a bit too large. Maybe the information is there somewhere, but it is not easy to find. So for now, I am using batteries and making sure to turn the unit off at the end of the game.

One other small problem has been that one of the buzzers does not stay plugged in properly. It eases its way out, so that it seems that that buzzer can't buzz in. product_title: Killer Bunnies and the Quest for the Magic Carrot; Blue Starter Deck
review_body:
My friends and I play games very often - Bang, Munchkin, Catan, Dominion, Fluxx, Guilliotine, etc. I was looking for another game that would allow for more than 4 players, and happened across this one.

Gameplay is is a lot of fun. There is a unique mechanic in this game - you have to put out your next two plays at all times, so you are always planning ahead. I've never seen a game do this, and it makes for a nice change of pace. The overall mechanics are pretty straightforward, and the manual walks you through gameplay, gradually building ideas. It isn't too complicated, and a group can pick up the rules within one or two games. Games last about a half-hour.

Nearly every card is unique, so it takes a while to learn how each one works. There are plenty of explanations of how the unusual cards work in the manual. There are more than enough cards in the base set to keep things interesting, so no need to buy any boosters at the start.

The quality of these cards is the best I've ever seen. They are a really tough plastic-type cardstock. You can tell that they will last a very long time, making this a better value for your money than most card games.

Overall, ths is a great additon to your game collection.

product_title: Round 2 AMT ST Enterprise Set (3 in 1) NCC1701, 1701A, 1701B  1:2500
review_body:
Years ago (read 1990s) I bought the \\"Three Enterprise kit\\" 1:2500th scale model.
It came with the TOS, Refit, and E-D. There were registry decalsand a stand and the rest was up to the modeler. A few years back, I dug what was left out of storage and bought a new one (same ships at that point). I game them much better/more detailed paint jobs and was VERY happy with the results, even if hand-painting the \\"aztec\\" on refit and E-D was tedious.
I also bought the alternate three enterprise kit with the E-B, E-C, and E-E giving them detailed, \\"aztec\\"ed paintjobs as well.

I wanted to build these slightly differently.
I didn't plan on using the aztec decals but once I tried them out, and saw how (surprisingly) well they went on, I knew that I had to.
I actually built the TOS-E as the Yorktown (using dry-transfer decals for the registry), the Refit as the self-destruct version from Star Trek III, and I retrofit the E-B into the Excelsior.
The hull decals are amazing and as I mentioned, comformed to the hulls surprisingly well.
The only REAL drawbacks to this kit is a lack of alternate registries for the ships and perhaps the lack of a base for the models (although that isn't an issue for experienced modelers, it could be for someone newer to the hobby).
overall, I'd give the kit a 9/10. I'd love to five it a full 10 but those two issues hold me back.

The pin vise has 4 components, the hollow metal tube body; the collet (in this case, double-sided), which is essentially a smaller metal tube that tapers at both ends, and is inserted into the tube/body and has the 4 prongs that tighten against a drill bit to grasp it; the binding nut that is placed over the collet, and is screwed onto the body (with the nose of the collet sticking through it), pushing the collet's 4 prongs together as it is screwed on/tightened; and the swivel piece on the back of the pin vise's body that just spins, making one-handed drilling easier.

The problem:
The binding nut never reaches maximum tension against the collet's nose when tightening, allowing you to continue screwing/tightening the binding nut way past the taper of the collet and onto the middle of the collet's body. So when you unscrew the binding nut, the collet is lodged in the binding nut, so you must completely unscrew the binding nut off of the body of the pin vise so you can pull the lodged collet out of it (and retrieve your drill bit from the collet, too). I have to use 2 pliers to grasp both the collet and binding nut to pull the lodged collet out.

Also, since the binding nut never reaches a stopping (tightest) point against the collet, the collet never grasps the drill bit tight enough, so enough force against the bit when drilling causes the bit to turn within the collet, and thus not drilling into whatever you're trying to drill into.

This happens regardless of the size of bit used, and on both sides of both of the double-sided collets (a secondary collet is stored in the body). The collets are also made from weak metal, so they bend out of shape easily.

Either the binding nut's nose hole needs to be a smaller diameter, or the collet must taper into a larger diameter body, so the binding nut reaches a point at which the collet is too thick for the nut to continue screwing down over it (a maximum tightness point).

product_title: Fisher-Price Thomas & Friends Wooden Railway, Tidmoth Timber Co. Deluxe 8 Pack
review_body:
We have quite a collection of Thomas tracks and trains and I wasn't sure this would be anything noteworthy to add to our collection, but my 4 year old son has been playing with it every day for at least a week now. I'm pretty space conscious and this has not been a waste of space at all. I'm so glad we got it!

Highlights include:

1. A huge mountain that can be put together a few different ways. We have a spiral mountain set (I forget the official name) and two other bridges. I wasn't sure this would be different, but he likes to connect them in different ways, so he gets quite a lot of play out of it. I think his favorite thing about it is how high it is.

2. A lumber mill that you can put little logs into, rotate and have them fall into the back of a train car. My son has found this way more entertaining than I expected, even though the mechanism for putting the logs in and turning it is a little awkward - especially for young children.

3. A really sturdy, oversized crane that trains can drive under. This has also gotten more attention than another smaller crane that we have. We have a few magnet pieces (similar to the logs) that can be lifted by cranes but I've never seen him touch them until we got this crane.

I'm always impressed by the quality of Thomas products - and this is no exception, but I am perplexed by why they don't include a few more logs. There's an engine (of course), a bed car and two logs. You can buy the trains separately but you can't really buy extra logs. I would love to see Thomas products come with a few more of the easy to lose pieces. I can't imagine it would increase the cost that much.

I also think the "decorated" curves (with the plastic on the sides) are not much of an addition to the experience. In my opinion they just take up space. These and one from another set don't see a lot of action from my kids. I also think the drive through tree trunkdoesn't fit with the rest of the set well. It literally doesn't do anything and is just for looks. I'd rather see extra logs or an extra flat bed train car, or something that could specifically be played with.

Another thing I don't love about the painted scenery is that it chips really easily and looks worn pretty quickly. We've had issues like that with other painted Thomas products.

One reviewer said they'd like to see less plastic but I have to say that the plastic and wood are integrated beautifully. I thought the same thing when I took it out of the box but the pieces really grew on me. They keep the look and feel of the older pieces really well for using plastic.

Overall this is a fantastic product. The picture makes it look small but it's really quite large and a great set whether you're just getting into Thomas or already have a boatload of Thomas tracks.

product_title: Bandai Hobby #28 Gundam Age Clanche 1/144 High Grade Model Kit
review_headline: A must have for anyone who liked Gundam AGE
review_body:
Gundam AGE is a series that fans have very mixed opinions about. Some love it, some hate it.
I personally enjoyed the series from beginning to end, mostly due to mechanical designs like this one.

The HG 1/144 Age line makes use of a lot of clever yet simple engineering that allows these models to both look great and pose great. Little to no paint is necessary unless you want to bring out the finer details on the majority of these kits.
The High Grade Clanche is no exception. As the grunt suit of the show's 3rd Generation, the Clanche is a transformable mobile suit used by usually nameless pilots.
In terms of construction, it's relatively simple with very few foil seals to be seen, mostly minor detailing as mentioned before. The kit includes the completed model, a small shield that can attach on either arm as well as store a single beam saber handle, a DODS Rifle as it is called in the series, two beam saber blades, landing gear for it's transformed state, and a unique stand that allows it to be displayed in both modes for some aerial posing.
The kit's articulation is fairly standard so you can pull off some of the poses on the manual rather easily or even get creative on your own. The transformation is very simple, it essentially consists of pulling the whole torso onto it's back and while functional, doesn't look quite as good as the mobile suit mode.
The kit is very well designed and looks great out of the box, I recommend it to anyone who enjoyed Gundam AGE or is looking for a hobby in these plastic models.

review_headline: Thirty Years Later, Still Love this Game
review_body:
I played this game when I was a kid and I still enjoy playing it. The game I have is 30+ years old and still looks brand new. The quality of Ravensburger games are superior to any games I've bought recently.

We changed the \\"rules\\" a little to help make the game go quicker:

If they roll doubles, they can go directly to the key room regardless of where they are on the board.

We also play that if they are in the key room and make a correct guess, they can keep guessing until they guess wrong.

We don't play the \\"send someone home\\" rule if you land on the same space. (Although as they are getting older, give them a choice at the beginning if they want to enforce this rule or not. After all \\"it is just a game.\\") These simple tweaks in the rules make the game go much faster.

It's a great \\"memory strategy game\\".

product_title: Monster High Travel Scaris Café Cart
review_body:
I got this for my daughter who LOVES Monster High (as do all her friends in 1st-3rd grade). I really wasn't looking for anything in particular other than just something new that she can use with her dolls. Here's what I found:

1. She loves the cute accents like the little hanging skull lights on the table umbrella
2. She loved playing with it and pretending her dolls were someplace amazing
3. It was easy to assemble with normal durability for a plastic toy accessory - thin, but durable enough
4. NO sticker accents - thank goodness! Those #$^^$ stickers always end up everywhere but where they should!
5. Nothing special as far as play time - it needs your child/children's imagination! They can make it into anything that they want it to be, but there are no whirling parts or buzzy bits or flippy switches that spit out candy or money or a glamorous lifestyle -- UNLESS your child imagines it does.
6. The colors were the normal girlie colors and not goth-y like some of the Monster High stuff seems to be. I like that it has more of a neon/day-glo accent to all the toys in this line.
7. The chairs (as to be expected from EVERY type of doll playset ever!) do not fit the dolls well. Honestly, the only way that they would fit the dolls and hold them into the seat worth anything is if they added seatbelts or some sort of torture-device type clamps. Personally, I get it: I don't want some clamp attaching to a doll's legs - it just doesn't look right!

Overall, my daughter likes it so I'm happy. It isn't dark, there isn't emphasis on death or goth or anything like that (more like mythical/paranormal beings), so I like it. And really, can we expect anything different with the age of Vampires, Werewolves and Zombies we live in? Yeah, right.

review_body:
This figure is from The Vintage Style figures in The Saga Collection; Leia as seen in the film Return of the Jedi. The face has some resemblance to Carrie Fisher and the body is very detailed as well.

Out of the box, this figure wears a fabric poncho, a plastic helmet and a belt with holster. The holster can actually hold the blaster. All of these can be removed.

This figure has:
- a ball-jointed neck,
- ball-hinged shoulders, elbows, knees and ankles, and
- swivel torso, but

As such, this figure offers a lot of options for posing. It has to be noted that this figure is small, measuring 3 1/4\\". These seems to be to scale when compared to other figures, but it caused a few problems. Two things I have issues with are a bit too slender and long neck, and blue colored hinges behind the ankles. product_title: Crazy Aaron's Thinking Putty, 3.2 Ounce
review_body:
This Thinking putty comes in a great huge metal tin that before you even see your putty makes you love it. Although it can be a little difficult to get out of its tin if you practice it quickly becomes easier. It is a lot of putty! At 3.2 oz it is way more than you get in a little plastic egg. Now for the color. At first when I took mine out of its tin I thought \\"this is not grey-black! This is dark green! I soon saw that I was mistaken. Under different lights at different angles the color changes from dark green, to graphite-oil grey, to a emerald green, or a greenly yellow. If you roll it up in a coil and let it sit in its tin it will soon take on a oil look. It seems to have little glittery sparkles in it, probably that is what makes it change its color. Also if you put it in its tin or a clean surface like its tin and press down on it and lift it will look like a beautiful marble smooth sparkly surface. This putty does not seem to stick to things as much as silly putty does and has a very nice texture to it. The only problem is it can easily pick up dirt and grime. You can not wash the grime out so you just have to knead it back in. If you are in a bad mood, or you want some stimulation then take it out of its tin and begin kneading! Sculpt it, knead it, stretch it, Anything you like, it really does help! Overall I love this putty and I think I shall get some more soon.
P.S. I found, a useful way to get the putty out of its container. If you use a Popsicle stick or a craft stick and insert it underneath the putty and push up you will be able to easily get the thinking putty out.

product_title: The Magic School Bus -Blasting Off With Erupting Volcanoes
review_body: I bought this kit for my daughter's 10th birthday.  She's above average in intelligence, and she thoroughly enjoyed this kit.  I think the age range on this product is appropriate.  It's simple enough for younger kids to do with help, and has enough of a \\"wow\\" factor for older kids to enjoy.  The kit comes with a guide, which walks kids through several learning activities and experiments.  The first activities are simple (reading volcano and earth science facts, and matching description stickers to the headers in the booklet) but effective.  We did these on the first day, learning our background material and finishing up by painting our volcano.  The volcano is a thin, black plastic cone with rivulets molded into it, that you can paint to look like a volcano.  There is a cheap water-based paint palette included for this.  My daughter half-heartedly spent 15 minutes on this, and told me it was too tedious.  Children who are more artistically-inclined would probably enjoy this part more than she did.  The next day, once the paint was dry, we were ready to make our volcano erupt.  You'll need to supply water, baking soda, vinegar, baking powder, and lemon juice to do all the variations.  From this point on, the experiments are all about acids and bases.  I appreciated the fact that the child is invited to use trial and error to determine which proportions of baking soda, vinegar, and water produce the best results.  My daughter enjoyed wearing the safety goggles and using the test tubes, pipette, and measuring cups to make chemical reactions (just like a real scientist), and recording her results in the lab booklet.  We got some good reactions--nothing too crazy, we didn't need a mop but we did need to put down some paper towels quickly.  If your kiddoes are just looking for dramatic, foamy explosions, this kit is probably way too low-key.  We learned a little about volcanoes, a little about pH, and spent a couple of cool \\"unplugged\\" hours together.  All in all, definitely worth the money.  I plan to buy other kits in this series.

product_title: Pathfinders Hydraulic Machines 4-in-1 Wooden Kit (Cherry Picker, Platform Lifter, Excavator, Scissor Lift)

Definitely a good intro to how hydraulics work. And no batteries, bad switches, cheap crappy plastic. If you're tired of poorly made toys, this one's a good bet.

product_title: Barbie 3-Story Dream Townhouse
review_headline: My Little Barbie Is Very Pleased
review_body:
Barbie's new digs arrived quickly & in perfect condition. As others have noted, it ships in the manufacturer's packaging replete with enormous full-color picture on one side, so have a strategy in place for diversion & distraction should the future mistress(es) of the realm be around when it's delivered.

The structure itself is surprisingly robust for being 99% extruded plastic, and all circuitry for the various powered items is embedded in the parts that come pre-assembled, so no worries there. Plan on a pretty solid hour to get everything put together, plus some more for applying the graphics and arranging the voluminous array of loose items. The elevator functions reasonably well out of the box, but as mentioned in other reviews, plan on a bit of filing & perhaps a tiny bit of silicone on the rails if you wish to avoid future kiddie frustration. PROTIP: Test all powered items prior to presentation and then let your child discover them on her own.

The assembly instructions themselves are as horrific as one would expect these days - 2 point font, tiny low-res greyscale illustrations, lots of almost meaningless arrows & very few actual instructions. Seriously guys, I'll pay the extra 2 cents in paper & ink costs to have legible assembly instructions that make sense. Fortunately, it's pretty much impossible to assemble it incorrectly, but you'll have to endure a bit of unnecessary confusion.

Now to brass tacks. My 4 year old daughter was literally agog, and approached her new Dream Townhouse as a pilgrim might approach a shrine after a long journey across the Kashmiri Himalayas. In minutes, no less than 5 Barbies (and a pony) had taken up residence and were making heavy use of the accoutrements. She then spent the next 4 solid hours playing with it, and has played with it every day since. When I tucked her in that night, she told me she was so happy, hearts were coming out of her. So... yeah - old dad belts one out of the park.

product_title: Eze Dope, 250ml by DELUXE MATERIALS
review_headline: I Don't really regard this stuff is a toy.
review_body:
Easy Dope is a top coating for tissue-covered flying models like an aliphatic resin. There are warnings on the bottle about the hazards of ingesting this product. At first I was skeptical about this product so I really can't call this a toy material. It's winter here in the Mid-Atlantic and the product had the consistency of Cream of Wheat when it first came out of the packing box that was left outside my door for who knows how long. I removed s teaspoonful of the paste and mixed it with some water and it then had the consistency of white (Elmer's) glue. It said to thin 50-50 to apply tissue so I did that but I overdid it and the results were horrid. I let it dry and removed it where it was worst. I sanded the entire plane till it would accept another coating and used another produce I ordered, Tissue Paste, and that worked great. After the covering was dry and taut I applied a thin coat of the Easy Dope to finish the project. I thinned the coat since it is a small model (approximately 1:32 Piper Cub by Guillows).

It's been a long time since I put a flying model together and I thought I'd get back into a hobby that I haven't visited since the early Sixties. With the new super glues and products like Easy Dope I may start reading up on R/C electrics!

product_title: Sanei Super Mario Dry Bones Plush Doll
review_body:
Well, I don't know what the first reviewer was talking about when the person wrote a really negative, yet nonsensical review about this toy. San-ei products are usually high quality, accurate, and cute, so I decided to buy this toy and discredit that reviewer even more.

For starters, the toy arrived at the expected date. When I opened it, I saw this Dry Bones in a plastic bag, which is a huge plus because the bag protects the toy from dirt and stuff. When I took it out, the toy felt very soft, just as any other San-ei toy. The toy is not flimsy at at all, and it feels very durable, as if it can withstand some throwing around. The details on the toy is very accurate, with the tail, arms, and legs having a black band to indicate its segments. Its belly's contours feel much more defined compared to Koopa Troopa from the same brand which is supposed to be like that because... well, it's a skeleton. I do wish the head and the arms be a bit paler, but I can't wish for everything.

One thing that is a huge plus for this plush is that every part of it is stitched; there are no cheap stuff inside there, and again, the material just feels well-made.

There's another Dry Bones plush I bought earlier, and it's from a lesser-known spot, and I love it too, but it's a tad big compared to this one. This one is more to scale with the Koopa Troopa plush, which is around 17 cm (6.5 in) sitting. The older Dry Bones plush is good, cute, and cuddly, but this one is another great Dry Bones plush to add to your colorful Mario collection. Dry Bones fans will love this little pile of bones!

product_title: Elenco Snap Circuits Green - Alternative Energy Kit
review_headline: Good even for a Kindergarten-age child with Lego experience
review_body:
This was one of our son's "big" Christmas presents from grandparents. It is a great product. Our child had just turned six when he received it and is just learning to read. However, after building a few layouts with adults he grasped how the instructions worked and he hopped to it with a will. As with a lot of other kids, Lego really helped him understand schematics and step-by-step instructions.

We have tried a number of science kits, even those theoretically more appropriate for children my son's age, and this is far and away the best one. Chief reasons:

--The snapping mechanism for building circuits is brilliant, clean, and safe. The parts are attractively colored and quite durable. (I've had to Super Glue the little green fan, but this is not a big deal.)

--No mess. Volcano and "magic science" kits often have some horrifying component that could destroy clothing/floor/the universe, and are particularly unsuited to household like ours with a younger, mobile sibling. Our son plays with this circuit kit alone in the backyard and I have zero worries.

--EXCELLENT storage tray. Other science kits have proven impossible to store. Bits, pieces and lumps sit about forever. This kit has a place for everything, to the extent that our son really likes cleaning it up.

This is a great kit.

product_title: Play-Doh Elmo Shape and Spin Playset
review_headline: A Video Review of the Play Doh Elmo Shape and Spin Playset
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:mo3F6PNKP189KOA]]Our 3 year old daughter enjoys both Play Doh and the Sesame Street character \\"Elmo\\". What could be better than a toy that combines Elmo, Play Doh, and learning shapes? The Play Doh Elmo Shape and Spin Playset is a fun toy, but it does have a few negatives.

The toy is pretty straight forward - you place a small amount of Play Doh on the shape. You then push down on Elmo's hands (with a fair amount of pressure) you release Elmo's hands and then push up on the release handle and remove the shape. The Shape comes out as a bit of a *blob* so you must trim the edges and then place the shape on the appropriate spot on the mat (see the video). At this point you rotate (to a different shape) and repeat!

Notes -

- Elmo does not have a volume control, which is unfortunate because the toy can be kinda annoying.

- It can be difficult to get the shapes out of the mold

- Clean-up is a little less difficult than the average Play Doh Toy

- Compared to many Play Doh toys this one is very educational.

- Elmo sounds like... Elmo

- A picture is impressed on both the top and bottom of every shape.

- The picture mat is a fun scene and is similar to what you find in a lot of Sesame Street books.

Final Verdict - While there is room for improvement the Play Doh Elmo Shape and Spin Playset is both fun and educational for children ages 2-6. Be warned.... while children will like the toy; parents may become pretty annoyed with Elmo's voice!

4 1/2 Stars

product_title: Water Shooting 3.5 CH RC Helicopter Gyro V319 (Colors May Vary)
review_headline: Only one problem: very short (8 min) battery life
review_body:
I can't describe how happy I was, like an 8-year-old, when I took this thing out of the box and started flying it. I'd always wanted a remote control helicopter and was amazed and surprised how easy this is to fly. Even more fun than a Vertibird, the previous champion in my toy world.

In the Aerodynamics and Fun categories, this bad boy goes to 11. But it has one serious drawback. I've been flying it for only a few days and the battery life is already down to 8 minutes. (I'm talking about the battery in the actual helicopter unit; the controller is powered by six AA batteries.)

I thought maybe Einstein's Theory of Relativity was at play here -- and that the battery life just SEEMED short. So I flew it last night until the battery was completely drained, charge it overnight, flew it again this morning, and timed it: 8 minutes total flight time before the battery died again.

OK, there's an upside: I might actually get some work done. Because if it flew for hours...well, it would fly for hours. Still, 8 minutes? I'm barely getting warmed up by then.

***UPDATE (six months later): I've now bought and flown four different remote control helicopters (both radio and IR) and can confidently say that they are all a blast to fly, but that Syma makes the most durable models.

product_title: HABA On the Farm Large Portable Take Along Play Set with 22 Wooden Pieces (Made in Germany)
review_headline: Amazing illustrations and high quality;  4.5 stars (taking into account price)
review_body: This is a really adorable play set.  The pieces are larger than I thought from the photo (in a good way).  They are nice and blocky and about half of them (all of the animals except for the chicken/rooster, but not the trees or fences) have different illustrations on both sides -- for example, there is the pig's face on the front side of his block, and you see his little tail and his back on the other side of the wood.  This is great for conversations about front and back and differences/etc. - but it does make it a little awkward in terms of play.  It's hard to explain, but if you're playing with the pig whose front faces to the right, you can really only make him \\"walk\\" to the right; if you have him walk to the left, his backside is to you.  The wood quality is the absolute best and the paint will not come off (like other, less costly, brands).  The cardboard is sturdy and of very good quality with a nice magnetic snap to keep it together and a red handle -- but within minutes of receiving this gift, my 2.5 year old immediately wanted to climb into the farm (and it obviously will not withstand unduly rough treatment).  The illustrations are the cutest -- so captivating! It was a little annoying that mine came with stickers from the company on the side and back - as I was nervous to unpeel them - but when I did, I was so impressed with the illustrations on the sides and back of the box...so many details and talking points!  Clean-up is very easy and the colors are bright.  The guide that comes with the farm has some great ideas for involving children from 1+ in different age appropriate imaginative play (with stories, keys to find certain hidden items, etc.).  It is an expensive set, so you will want to make sure none of the animals wander off (!!), but the quality is so high and it's something you'll want to hold onto for other children/grandchildren/etc.  Although this is a great toy, if you are under any sort of financial strain, I would recommend foregoing it -because there are other similar style (although maybe not as high quality) toys out there (see Janod's farm for half the price).  If price isn't an issue though - or if you are more organized than me and able to keep track of pieces....and have a calmer toddler than mine... I highly recommend it as a very high quality, adorable, imagination-provoking farm.

Even the dress forms included to insert into the dresses so you can color them are cardstock, instead of cardboard. The markers don't allow for detail work and the stickers don't stick!

I was trying to relive our happy Fashion Plates memories. Instead...Remember \\"Rub Ons\\"? This toy is very similar, even down to the \\"pull up an edge, check it, put it down and rub some more\\" feature.

Sorry, Barbie, this is an EPIC FAIL!py Fashion Plates memories. Instead...Remember \\"Rub Ons\\"? This toy is very similar, even down to the \\"pull up an edge, check it, put it down and rub some more\\" feature.

product_title: Hero RC H911 2.4GHZ iRocket 4 Channel Fixed Pitch Ready to Fly Helicopter with Battery, Balance Bar, Main Blade, Connect Buckle, Tail Blade and USB Charger
review_body:
I just received the H911 last week, quick delivery, packaged well for shipment. After unboxing and thoroughly reading the instruction manual I charged up the batteries and started to play. The only minor problem when getting ready to fly is the way the manual describes how to \\"bind\\" the rc transmitter to the helicopter. It reads like your supposed to put the charged battery into the heli, the receiver light on the circuit board flashes rapidly, then blinks slowly and the manual then tells you to turn on the transmitter which will beep three or four times and bind or connect with the heli. I did this several times and it didn't work. I googled a video that I saw online posted that showed a guy getting his ready to fly and he put the battery in and while the light blinked rapidly he turned his transmitter on right away and when the controller stopped beeping the heli light turned to a solid glow, no blinking and he could fly. I tried this and it worked the first time. I checked the control surfaces, the rotor toggles up and down like it should, goosed the power to make sure the rotor turned and then gave it about half power....it came up, I freaked and cut power and it dropped like a rock. No problem. Turned it upright and throttled up again and had very little to do to trim it out and be able to come to a hover. Let me tell you, talk about feeling like a kid again this thing is a blast. I read some comments about getting a used product, it could happen I suppose but not my experience. And there is no question about the durability of the H911. For the short time I've had this the first couple of times I flew it in the living room. On a couple of those flights when getting to know the flight characteristics I throttled up too fast and came up to the eight foot height of the ceiling, and as a new pilot would do and from watching numerous videos online before purchase, I did what everyone said, I cut throttle and it drops slowly af first, the blades are turning a bit but comes down the rest of the way fast. This is something I don't recommend doing often but it hit on the skids and didn't break a thing. Picked it up and examined it, not a crack or break, probably a little lucky on my part. I've had it up doing slow circles in the living room and drifted one way or the other and into a sofa (soft) and a wall (obviously hard) several times and doing what I saw so often in video's, cutting throttle, it falls, you set it upright and take off again. I've since resorted to pulling the cars out of the garage and flying around in there, more room to practice and have fun in. Nice flight characteristics, once you have it trimmed unless you are out of control coming in you can level off with throttle and drop slowly in place on the skids, a real kick for just 15 to 20 flights so far. You can really tell when the battery is low, at full throttle it will only hold hover and power a couple of feet in the air and will not go any higher, time to land. A battery lasts about five and a half minutes so far and they charge in about thirty minutes. I'm already thinking about ordering the five battery pack on Amazon. That way you could charge and rotate the batts. to keep flying for quite a long time. I decided to get the H911 instead of the Syma S107G. The S107 probably would be easier to fly right away but this challenges you more. Also being able to change batteries and keep flying attracted me to this bird besides the reviews of it's reliability. Get one and have some fun.
Edit: Just a little update. Ordered the five pack of 200Mah batteries to fly longer and rotate/charge batteries in the process. Working out great. The new batteries seem to give you almost a good ten minutes of flight with better throttle response. This being my first chopper experience bypassing the twin rotor 3 channel type of copter I continue to learn something new every flight. A soft touch on the sticks is definitely better than ham fisting it if your losing control or getting close to something. The durability of the H911 continues to amaze me. Got too close to a lamp and drifted into the pole sending the 911 from about two feet up crashing to the hard wood floor. Didn't notice it but the tail rotor popped off, when I tried to take off after the crash the chopper just spun around on the floor. Checked it out, found the rotor and pushed it back on and took off again with out a hitch. Can't wait until it warms up a bit to pull the cars out and fly in the garage again. With the speed of this thing you need the room to anticipate direction changes until you get better at it.

product_title: Catan: Seafarers 5&6 Player Extension 4th Edition
review_body:
A fun and interesting addition to Settlers of Catan. I think this expansion pack is far better than some of the other expansion packs (such as Cities & Knights). It gives opportunity for several players to interact and the element of ships add a new dimension. In addition, there are a variety of ways to win the game, which keeps every game a guess.
The addition of \\"gold\\" - meaning if you settle there you can take whatever resource you want - is quite the advantage but still overcome by skill of the other players. For this reason this expansion pack might encourage targeting of certain players more so than other expansion packs.

This expansion pack is not too easy and not too difficult - perfect for a mixed or an advanced crowd. For a group just learning Settlers, I would recommend learning the basic game first.

The actual materials appear to be well-made and durable, although some of the smaller pieces are almost too small and could be easily lost. When you put the \\"sea\\" together it can be hard to tell where the hexagonal tiles meet and thus where it is acceptable to place the ships - if they were outlined in black that would be better.

Overall, a delightfully fun and interesting game that is not terribly difficult to learn, intriguing enough to play again and again, with quality materials.

His mouth can open and close which is something I liked in the Beast Wars/Beast Machine toys. pretty darn poseable but I wish his tail had a little more pose ability so he doesn't look like hes going to well...use the bathroom in every pose. Im very very happy with the size. Compared to the RID line the bots are scaled up a little more thank God. Thank God hasbro was listening on that note. One other problem I have with his beast mode is that his head becomes separated from the yellow \\"feathers\\" behind his head. I don't know if I got a bad mold or what but the other Beast Hunters figures I have, have the same problem. They don't hold together as well as the RID line. Over all I like the beast mode. It's nice to see the Predacon's return.

Transformation is SUPER simple. 95% of the transformation is just moving is beast head inside his robot chest. the other five percent is just posing him in a humanoid pose. Simple for kids and parents alike. Parents I highly doubt you'll get to play with this one. Your child should easily be able to transform by him or her self.

Robot mode looks rather intimidating. He looks like he could really tear a bot apart.The head sculpt for some reason really reminds me of rhinox from Beast Wars.Maybe Im just seeing things. Pose ability is great in robot mode. The weapons do not make him backheavy or front heavy at all.And like the First Editions the tail whip when attached looks like it transforms from his arm.

Overall This is an ok figure. Im glad Hasbro scaled them up a bit but I feel like Hasbro made this one a little too easy.Im really hoping to see Lazerback in the show.Parents this is a prime choice for your children because its pretty durable and easy to transform.hildren because its pretty durable and easy to transform.
