product_title: Mega Bloks Halo - UNSC Cryo Bay
review_headline: Very nice little set from Mega Bloks
review_body:
I had not had any Mega Bloks sets for a very long time (mid 2000's). Back then most of the sets had cheaper plastic, loose fitting bricks, and the minifigs were pretty bad. When I saw they were doing Halo, I had to pick up a few to see if the quality had improved and I was pleasantly surprised. The minifigs are very well built and sturdier with great articulation. The blocks are a much better fit and might start to give Lego some competition. I still love Lego, but I have to say that Mega Bloks have gotten pretty good. I can do so much more with the Mega Bloks minifigs than I can with my Lego ones.

Now to focus on the Cryo Bay set. This is a nice little piece of Halo history that I was surprised to see made into a set. It is not your typical battle terrain, but it is a scene that most gamers have etched in their heads as it was an important moment for the franchise. It did not look like much at first because it is a smaller set of 72 pieces, but it turns out to be a lot of fun for the size. This is also one of the more inexpensive ways to get Master Chief (John 117) and Cortana since they are only in the very expensive TRU ship as of this writing. This Cortana does not have a light up base, but she looks good and is in a decent scale if you want to have your McFarlane figure holding her. She is very thinly attached to a round stud by her legs, so I would be careful removing and attaching her as would be the most likely spot for breakage. She feels a little fragile there. Master Chief is nicely detailed and he has three weapons to choose from: an Assault Rifle, a Battle Rifle, and the new Sticky Detonator. The scene displays well on any Halo shelf and you can have Cortana watching over the sleeping Chief or him thawing out to start Halo 4.

As far as price, personally, I would not go too much over retail. This is a set that will be popular if only for the minifigs, even though it's a great set as it is. Keep an eye out for Amazon sellers that may have it for a reasonable price. I only paid around twenty one for it shipped. Would I pay thirty for it? Probably not because there is not enough there to justify that price, but that's just me. I would still keep an eye open because you can find it without breaking the bank, and it is a set you would probably enjoy if you are a Halo fan or collector.azon sellers that may have it for a reasonable price. review_headline: Ignore the age suggestion, it's great for ANY age!! Hands down the BEST purchase I've made recently!!!!!
review_body:

We got this for the kids for Christmas (ages 7 & 10) and we have had a BLAST!!

I was looking for something for the 7 year old because she is fairly competitive for her age & gets disappointed when games are too complicated for her to win.. and she knows if you "let her win". (She's way past Candy Land, but not quite to Monopoly) This game is PERFECT! She kicks our butts at this game sometimes and it's not our choice haha!

The best part is that we're all getting better! It's a great game for kids who can't find milk in the fridge when it's right in front of them... they learn to spot things & it literally improved after one night. She even plays with her small cousins who are 3 and 5! The game is obviously a bit slower, but they keep getting better!

I recommend this to ANYONE with children, or even adults who like games. Just a hint, if you're playing with a very small child (like under 7), Just have the older ones close their eyes a second or two to give them a head start. Before long, they won't even need the head start!! They're learning & don't even know it!

This game is worth every penny... I never review things like this, but it just doesn't get any better than this game... Do yourself and your children a favor and get this game! When the kids are gone, I can't deny that we sneak it out of their room with some adult friends and laugh our butts off playing it, too!

product_title: Fisher-Price Laugh & Learn Click'n Learn Remote
review_headline: Durable and fun for baby, but does get a little loud if you don't do a little easy tinkering.
review_body:
This remote has been one of my baby's favorite toys since we gave it to him at 8 months. We've had it almost 2 months now, and he's thrown it, stepped on it, sat on it, drooled puddles into it, and it's still going strong and singing its little toy heart out. It plays tons of songs, lights up at the top, and says numbers. My son really enjoys putting the end in his mouth to chew while mashing the buttons with his thumbs to make the music play.

The only problem with it is that it has \\"volume up\\" and \\"volume down\\" buttons. When your child pushes the volume all the way up, it is a little annoying, but not so loud that you can't live with it. It's not gratingly loud or anything, but a little fix can make this toy so much better. As a previous reviewer said, all you have to do to fix this is grab a screwdriver and pop out the little white rubber piece underneath the \\"volume up\\" button. For us, that made the button sag, so we took the little black bead out of the white rubber thingy so that the button couldn't make contact with the circuit board anymore, put the white rubber part back inside, and that fixed everything. The button was still technically pushable, but it no longer raised the volume. I HIGHLY recommend this fix. Once you do it, you AND baby will love this cute little toy.

Review. This is the sculpture of the Kenshin revoltech figure, is an awesome addition to your collection. It has plenty of articulation, the color scheme is very accurate to the Samurai X series. I grew up watching this series. I do believe that this is a very good figure to add to your collection. For me it means one of the hero embodiment of my youth.

product_title: Playskool Sesame Street Let's Rock! Elmo Guitar
review_headline: Didn't buy it for myself...it was for my toddler
review_body:
On one hand, if your kid loves Elmo, your kid is probably going to love this guitar.

But let's be real here...when reviewing electronic kid toys, you're not looking to read how much someone's kid loved it. You want to know things like battery life, volume control, if it's truly age appropriate, and any other gripe a parent could come up with.

There's no volume control--pack up and go home. Okay, it's not THAT bad...except I can hear my daughter playing with this from another room. But hey, it makes her happy, and eventually she moves on to a quiet activity, like jumping off the couch, sticking things in vents, or maybe even coloring on the walls.

Have you ever had that annoying ringing in your head when a TV was turned on, and most people can't hear that frequency? Well, Elmo guitar knows that frequency and any time it is switched on, you get the annoying ringing on top of the migraine you get after listening to the lack of volume control.

Hey it's a pretty good toy, even if my 3 year old is still figuring out how to hold and play with it properly. I just make sure to keep Excedrin in the house for myself. And oh...you brave souls who bought the Rockin Elmo(or whatever it's called) to go with this. I can't imagine.

product_title: Dungeons and Dragons: Castle Ravenloft Board Game
review_body:
I would recommend this game to any fan of fantasy themed board games. I've always enjoyed the dungeons and dragons universe and this game is no exception. While it may seem daunting to some, keep in mind that the game contains outlines for different adventures with varying difficulty levels.

There are a lot of pieces but not all of them will be used for each adventure. Also, the rules can be flexible. Its kind of like landing on free parking in monopoly. Depending on the house rules you may or may not get $500. Not everything is black and white where the rules are concerned. Let your imagination run wild. You can also use the pieces available to custom make you're own adventures. Or combine the other adventure system board games and dungeon command skirmish games to this and get even more creative. They all interconnect.

The miniature figurines are not prepainted so have some fun painting those as well. If you dig deep enough you can find user generated content online to add to your game. There are additional themed cards for monsters, heroes, encounters...etc. You can even find user created adventures.

Now if only I can find friends to play this game with. I'm only kidding. My wife enjoys playing and I've even played a few games over FaceTime with my brother and his family. That takes some extra preparation though. All in all this game has brought us hours of enjoyment with a lot more to come.

product_title: 1/25 Roscoe's Dodge Monaco Police Car Model Building Kit
review_headline: This is a re-issue of an old classic, some skill required
review_body:
This has been re-issued about 10 times since 1975, it was even a two door twice! Look at the box art, you can see the two door coupe taillights. The kit inside will be correct though. Keep in mind, this will reflect tooling from the 70's, but still a good old 4 door dodge. The detail is modest but it's easy to build. I will go over what it comes with: It has a chrome revolver, an M-16, an M-14, a shotgun, some radios and a radar unit. A lightbar with red and blue and some lights for front and rear. Really fat tires with steel wheels and chrome moon caps, way too wide but they do look like cop car wheels. The chassis pan has everything molded in like the exhaust and suspension. MPC did it this way back when they tooled their kits.

This kit has been issue in the following editions: The 1975 Fury (2 door) 1976 Road runner (2 door), 1976 Monaco (2 door), 1977 Monaco 2 door Force 440 cop car, 1977 TJ Hooker cop car 4 door, Batman Gotham City cop car 4 door, Dukes 4 door Cop car (shown here), one or two others which escape my memory at this time.....

This is not modern tooling. It can be built and painted to look great on the shelf, and worth the money. This represents one of the most common police car platforms ever, which makes it of significant historic value.

product_title: Super Soaker Switch Shot Blaster
review_headline: Shoots far, low volume, lots of shots
review_body:
A Super Soaker is great if it does what you want it to. I've seen huge Super Soakers that will drench a person in one shot, but their tank empties in a few shots unless you're wearing a backpack.

1. This water gun shoots further than the 25 feet it claims. It shoots 30-35 feet on the single stream setting, and at least 25 feet on all the others.

2. I get around 30 shots per refill of water.

3. It's way better than a pistol for getting people wet, but it's not going to soak someone in one shot. You'd need four or five shots, on any of the settings, to get a t-shirt completely wet.

4. There are four settings: one stream, two streams, three streams, and a wide stream. The three stream setting spreads out about 6-8 feet by the time it has traveled 25 feet. You could hit three people, one with each stream, and give them each a fist-sized, very wet spot, if you aimed it right.

5. It does not pump up for extra velocity. The pump goes out, and then when you pull it in, it shoots. No trigger. I've seen a lot of water guns like this. Works fine.

6. It seems pretty safe. It says not to shoot people in the face, and I suppose it would hurt pretty bad if you got shot straight in the eye, but it's not going to send you to the emergency room unless you're really close.

7. The gun seems really well made, and the two parts that come off, the water tank and the shoulder rest (for easier storage), go on and off very easily. The water tank did not leak at all, and it was easy to fill and to empty. Like I said, it seems to be put together well.

If you need to drench someone in one shot and win every battle by having a storage tank on your back, then get something bigger. However, this is a well-built gun that shoots over 30 feet on the best distance setting. The thirty shots seemed like a lot for a water gun battle, so it's good for that, too.

My kids and my wife all wanted it as soon as Iwalked in the door, but I explained to them that I had to test it out to write a review for Amazon, LOL. My wife got it afterwards, though, because she'll share it way better than the kids will. Of course, she's not as afraid to shoot me as they are ...

product_title: Chaos Space Marine Terminator Lord Warhammer 40k
review_headline: Great model, great scale, great options, but suffers from the same problem as the rest of the earlier GW chaos models
review_body:
The scale on the Terminator lord is fantastic because he is much larger than the standard chaos and space marine terminators, and he comes with his own textured base. The boxed set includes the following:
-right-handed and left-handed pre-heresy lightening claws (larger than standard terminator lightening claws and keep in mind that the chaos terminator box set does not come with any lightening claws)
-4 heads (a chaos terminator helmet with four tusks, a honed helmet with a t-visor, a sorceror helmet with a t-visor and four prongs, a bare head with a snarling visage, and a head with a respirator in the shape of an eye and some signs of mutation)
- 2 front torsos (one for a lord depicting the top of a chaos star and one with the librarian-standard horned skull)
-1 set of legs that come in three parts so they may be positioned standing on the textured base that comes with the kit
-1 left-handed power fist with a middle finger that is a protruding claw
-1 left-handed chain-fist with a unique 2-chainsaw design
-1 left-handed outstretched arm with an attachable force staff for creating a terminator sorceror.
-1 left-handed power-awe
-1 right-handed combi-bolter
-1 right handed combi-bolter-melta
-4 spike bits
-2 hanging trophies, one being a skull and fang/claw, the other being a spear-head and fang/claw
-1 book hanging from a hook
-3 options for loincloths (a set of chains with a skull and hook at the end, a very long cloth with chaos star desing and hanging skull, a torn cloth with the chaos star visible and a claw/fang
-3 shoulderpads, 2 left, 1 right. The options for the left are either a fanged skull in the center of a chaos star or the eye of Horus, symbol of the Black Legion. The right shoulderpad is blank
-1 cape designed for terminators
-1 back half of a terminator torso
-4 shoulder trophy racks, one containing a tyranid skull, one containing a veteran Dark Angel helmet, one cataining a skull, and the last containing a small sack
-a demon familiar bearing a small sword
-1 buckle with a fanged skull to go over the top of the loin cloth and cover the mid-section of the torso

Overall, there are many options and if you're planning on building a terminator force to accompany the lord, you have some options you can mix and match. The model is very easy to assemble and the pieces fit very well with no real need to file anything down. This is also the only kit to get your chaos terminators a set of lightening claws.

The only negatives are the same complaints most people have with chaos kits: the only chapter-specific should is for the Black Legion so if you're planning on making a Lord for any of the other chaos chapters or you want to make a Lord dedicated to a specific chaos god, then expect to kit-bash and customize this model.

review_body:
I was disappointed in this because I thought the drive-thru headset really worked. It's just a plastic, pretend headset that doesn't even make noise and doesn't really even fit on my 22 month old's head, let alone my 4 y/o's. When you push the button on the speaker piece (NOT the headset), it says, "Welcome to McDonald's, can I take your order?" but that's ALL it does. The cash register is basically like a calculator but has some buttons on the side for items. When you push them, it repeats the item you pushed. It does not display a price for that item (I was hoping to teach my son about money with this, but this doesn't help much).

Also, the coins are 2 plastic pieces that each look like 3 coins stuck together. And it comes with a pretend $5 bill and 2 $1 bills. Again, not really great for teaching about counting with money.

The food items are fun, but they are the same one that come in other, less expensive sets. So while this may be fun pretend play for some kids, my 4 year old was done with it in 10 minutes. Now he just plays with the food, and isn't really sure what to do with the rest.

product_title: Magnetic Go Board with Single Convex Magnetic Plastic Stones Game Set
review_body:
This set is a bit on the scaled-down side, for portability. Nothing wrong with that...just important to know. The dimensions are listed, so there shouldn't be a surprise. But just be aware of it.

But don't expect great things from the magnetic features. The stones stick, but relatively loosely. Sneezing probably won't jostle them, but a big bump in a car or plane probably would. They are even less likely to stay in place if the board is placed vertically as the product description suggests.

Still, it is a completely adequate board, with completely adequate stones, and given the price it makes for a completely adequate set, and even with at least above-average resiliency in the face of vibrations and jostling, as compared to any board with no magnetic features at all.

But rare-earth magnets, these are not.

product_title: Tsuro: The Game of the Path
review_body:
One of my biggest gripes in buying board games is opening the box and thinking to myself that "Really? this games cost this much and all I get is a bunch of cards and maybe a board and some misc. game pieces" I know in the end however, a great game is a great game regardless of the cost or amount of items in the box. But still, more time than not I feel somewhat ripped off. Now Tsuro isn't cheap, and it does suffer from what I talked about above, but the designers of the game really went all out on the presentation, going a long way to make you feel like it was worth the money. You open the box and your are presented with a sheet of vellum that appears to be an old calligraphy styled painting of a dragon.. The Instructions underneath are gorgeous as are the tiles, all done in a rich Chinese art style. The presentation is just top notch. I would have liked the game pieces to be heavier, to better simulate stone.

The game is fun and easy to pick up making it an excellent choice when non "gamers" are over. As others have noted, the games are quick, making a perfect game when you have a little time to spare. My 10 year old son loves playing and I can see kids as young as 6-7 liking this game. A shout out to Will Wheaton and his Table Top show for introducing the game to me.

product_title: Constructables Motorized Building Dinos Playset
review_headline: The Surprise Hit of the Birthday!
review_body:
My son received this for his 4th birthday. He loves motion and physical activity as well as pushing buttons/opening things, but building things that are more complicated than stacking isn't really a passion (yet). He has played with this toy non-stop since receiving it yesterday, ignoring all other gifts and actually sobbed when he had to stop playing with it to go to bed last night.

It's a very clever product. A set of four different main dinosaurs can be easily assembled by a small child using the main motorized \\"body\\" and a set of different pieces/parts. Variations on the four dinosaurs are limited only by a child's imagination. The pieces are simple and sturdy and uncomplicated. I walked him through making a couple of the first dinosaurs using the sketched instructions and then he was off and running.

Different dinosaurs open/shut its mouth, wag a tail, etc. Simple but charming. All of the dinosaurs have forward and backward motion and \\"walk\\" across a floor (better on un-carpeted floors.)

There is a noise associated with the turning gears within the motorized body, but I don't think it is excessively loud or annoying (compared to many other toys with beeps, whistles and squeaking.)

We're charmed by the toy! Highly recommended for ages 4-10 (as many older daughter is desperate to play with it too, once her younger brother takes a break...if he ever does.)

product_title: Accoutrements Yodelling Pickle
review_body:
Will kept telling me about this christmas present that he kept forgetting to send me and I was like 'dude, Will, it's OK. I didn't get you anything either\\" then the other night Will texted me and was like \\"Archer premieres tonight!\\" next text message \\"oh wait, that's next week!\\" next text message \\"I keep forgetting to send your christmas present!\\"

and then i rolled my eyes and was like, whatever Will.

Then today I was having the worst day. I finally pulled myself off the couch and grabbed ten dollars and opened the door to head to the liquor store and then a small brown box fell on my foot and I knew immediately what it was.

Well ... like I knew it was Will's present. I had no idea what was IN the box.

SO I opened the box from the bottom with a knife and vigor. There was another box inside! and it was wrapped! and on it it said \\"to Halley <3 Will\\" and immediately I felt better. I took a picture of it. Then I tore the paper opened (damn, Will used a lot of tape FYI) and my eyes didn't really process what it was. I didn't read the packaging, I just focused on the product that was visible through the transparent cellophane and thought

Will ... sent me a vibrator?

product_title: Robotic UFO 3 Channel I/R Flying Ball Remote Control Helicopter
review_body:
First off I will say that this is the first negative review I have ever written on Amazon. I have submitted a several positive reviews but no negatives until now. We ordered this toy for our daughter 1 week before Christmas. When the package arrived 2 days before Christmas it contained an RC car, not a helicopter. The package had no invoice or packing slip in the box, I had to look at the tracking number and match it to Amazon to even be sure it supposed to be the helicopter and not just a lost package. I disputed the shipment immediately and the seller sent a boiler plate response. I contacted them back after Christmas saying I wanted to return the item and did not hear back from them for about 7 days. Then they just sent me a 1 line response saying ship the item back to this address. I responded back and asked them if they could provide me a shipping label to return. A few days later and they said just keep the car, and we will ship the helicopter. Then nothing for over a week, so I asked them for a status. Then a few days later they said they would ship it out tomorrow and send me the tracking number. Then nothing again for over a week. When I was about to dispute with Amazon I finally got the helicopter, almost a month late.

And it turns out it is a piece of junk! the controller is cheaply constructed, and the controls are constantly getting stuck. Flying one of these helicopters takes finesse, and half of the time the throttle gets stuck on full or off. Either way the thing is impossible to fly, either it is bouncing off the ceiling or crashing to the ground. Every once in a while the throttle will work for a few seconds and then it actually flies pretty well, but then it will just go haywire again and crash. So I would assume that if the controller worked better it might be OK, but it is hard to tell. Other than the controller it is still not well made, the wires are exposed and just taped on in a few places and the cage is very flexible so it doesnot offer much protection. I don't feel like fighting to return this so I am stuck, but don't make the same mistake and but this.

review_headline: Nice tool set, but could use some improvements
review_body:
This was a recent gift for my daughter, who is almost 3 years old. She's always interested in my tools, so I wanted something safe for her to play with.

This isn't one of her favorite toys, but she does really enjoy it. She has found many uses for the hammer (which may or may not be a positive thing).

I love that the plastic is safe and sturdy. However, I wish the bolts were designed differently. There are three places where the bolts fit: the holes on the toolbox, the small plates with two holes, and the plastic nuts. The nuts thread perfectly on the bolts. However, the bolts slide right through the other holes. I wish that the bolts would thread through the toolbox holes, too. My daughter always tries to use the bolts with the toolbox, and it doesn't work properly. We can put a nut on the other side of the bolt, but then the nut needs to be held while the screwdriver turns the bolt. That's a little too complicated for a toddler.

Otherwise, I really like this tool set. We have other Green Toys, too, and they're all great.

I do agree that a few points could be confusing (at the beginning it tells you each player gets $2500 to start but, the \\"standard\\" rules still say $1500). However, most people have played Monopoly before and just need to see what the differences are. It does say \\"Rules of Play Standard Edition (for your reference)\\".

It was also mentioned that the Chance/Community Chest cards were not updated. However, on mine the skycraper and train depot are added on them. So, maybe the very first one's weren't changed but they realized this and changed them.

I think it is a great update to the original game and look forward to many games with my friends and family.

product_title: Revell P-51B/C Mustang
review_headline: A good model for the price.
review_body:
This is a model that I had really anticipated building. The P-51B/C Mustangs are often overlooked by the P-51D, and this seemed to be a great way to build an earlier Mustang at a reasonable price. My experiences with the model were almost entirely positive. The instructions were clear, the parts were molded well, and there were two sets of well done decals allowing the builder to choose either a P-51B with a bird cage canopy based in China (what I built), or a P-51C with a Malcolm Hood canopy based in the ETO. All told the only flaw I had with the model was the canopy, which took this from a great looking model to a great looking model if viewed from more than a couple of feet away. No matter what I tried the canopy just would not fit the model. The windows immediately behind the cockpit were molded in such a way that they would pop off the moment I took pressure off with my fingers, while the front was loose and bulged over beyond the cockpit except at the corners which would also pop off. It took me two days of tinkering with it before I managed to find an arrangement where the canopy would stay on, but it still looks crooked, which is really just a shame considering that the rest of the model is absolutely superb for the price. I sincerely hope that this was just a problem with the kit I purchased, since I'd really like to have another go at building this oft overlooked variant of the Mustang.

Pros:

Detailed panel lines and rivets.
Landing gear tires with detailed tread.
Excellent decal selection.
Clear and easy to read instructions.

Cons:
Ill manufactured canopy.

product_title: Mega airplane battery operated with flashing lights & sounds just like a real airplane
review_headline: Very cool product however the quality is lacking and the sound failed within a couple of hours of play
review_body: This is a very cool airplane with lots of lights and at one point sound. The overall quality is subpar. There are color smears on the body of airplane. Several stickers for windows, doors, etc are crooked and can not be removed or replaced. The sound mechanism for the plane, sounds like a plane taking off, failed within a few hours of play. The wings are installed by sliding into the side of the fuselage and held in place with a pressure fit. There are no tabs or other type of retainer to keep them installed so any bump of the wing will result in the electrical circuit disconnecting and the lights on the wings will go out. Its an easy fix but annoying. I could glue them in but it is nice to be able to remove the wings for storage. Overall, my son loves it because it is a huge airplane. He doesn't mind so much that the sound doesn't work. I wouldn't recommend this product.

review_headline: Not Very Durable, Charge Does Not Last, Hot Battery When Charging, Poor Range
review_body:
I bought this as a gift for a nephew and we were all very pleased with the looks of this RC car. I received the red model. The lights are very bright and have many different colors within the wheels. + Looks very nice with good graphics and light display.
- Easily becomes stuck. Have laminate floors and cannot travel from laminate up onto the throw rugs.
- Poor turning radius. Have to go get is just to turn it around.
- The remote is so lightweight that is just feels cheap.
- Poor range even with the antenna fully extended. Between 10-15 feet it starts to cut out.
- The battery pack becomes very hot while charging and has a strange very strong odor, almost like plastic melting.
- One of the clips that secures the battery pack charger to the power cord broke off the first time I plugged it in. (Not User Error)

_Bottom Line_ No I definitely would not recommend this to a friend and wish I had chose something else for my nephew. Will update this review in a few weeks to see how it holds up.

product_title: Flying Super Grover 2.0
review_headline: Awesome for Super Grover Fans...Otherwise, It's Just Okay
review_body:
My husband, who grew up with [[ASIN:037582913X The Monster at the End of this Book (Sesame Street) (Big Little Golden Book)]] and made sure that we had it for our children, LOVES this toy. It calls to those Super Grover fans who love the overzealous, overconfident, furry good guy. For me, it's a fun enough toy, but the reality of the toy didn't quite measure of to the cuteness of the story (but by all means, the story is definitely one to get for your little one!).

Flying Super Grover is a \\"stuffed\\" toy in the same vein as [[ASIN:B000UU7LOS TMX eXtra Special Edition]] or [[ASIN:B006BMM75W PLAYSKOOL Sesame LET'S ROCK! Singin' Cookie Monster]]. He's got a furry exterior that covers a bulky, heavy, mechanical body. And he's wearing plastic armor on his feet and chest, with a moveable visor on his head. It's really cute, and very true to character, just not especially huggable.

Super Grover sort of flies--when your kid holds him in a flying position, his arms are supposed to go out in the direction you're aiming him. Unfortunately, I've found that Grover's arms only seem to go straight out in front of him when we're aiming him downward, as it's simple gravity which moves his arms. As my little guy is only two, Grover's not experiencing much arm movement. He's just too heavy for a toddler, and I haven't noticed that there's much else mechanical about him to make the weight worthwhile. My 6 year-old can handle him much better, but she doesn't have as strong an interest in him.

Grover IS cute. You press the button on his belt to get him talking, and his first words are always, \\"Helllloooooo Everyboddddeeeeee!\\" Then he says things like \\"Going up! Going down!\\" and lots of other phrases to tell you what he's doing. To be honest, I'm used to tuning out toy noises, but Grover is a little louder than some of the other toys my kids have. I don't mind his constant talking, but he definitely needs to be turned off at nap time, and I can see how he could grow tedious to some (especially if he became a favorite).

My kids have taken an on and off interest in him. I think if he had a lighter body, my son might enjoy him more, but there are so many other toys out there that just capture his imagination for a little longer. Having said that, Grover is definitely worth owning for Sesame Street fans, and he's adorable just standing guard in the room. I'd rather have him than any of the gazillion Elmo toys out there any day.

product_title: Melissa & Doug USA Map Wooden Puzzle
review_body:
This is a good educational toy. My daughter who is 4.5 plays with it on a daily basis ( we bought it this past Christmas) and is learning about states as well as the capitals. One thing I like about it, is that the inside of the puzzle has the capitals and the puzzle pieces just has the name of the state. So, once you do the puzzle, you have to have an idea of the capital before you can place it on the puzzle board (unless it's just obvious such as Texas), which helps kids learn the states and capitals.
The only complaint I have is that small states such as Maryland, Connecticut, etc., do not have an actual puzzle piece (it's combined into one) but other than that, it was a good investment. I am glad we have it.

review_headline: Terrible instructions and pole attachment, poles broke during first use
review_body:
First the good: when we finally got this tent set up, my kids jumped about and giggled hard. They loved it despite its flaws.
Then the bad: Complicated, unintuitive, and possibly unsafe setup: Like other reviewers, I couldn't work out how to set this up, because the setup system is so flimsy, it doesn't seem like it could be right (and the instructions are misleading). You just poke the two poles through four flimsy loops and four flimsy ties (eight connections for the entire tent, not for each pole) rather than actual pole sleeves, even though the instructions tell you to use the pole sleeves and the picture on the box appears to have the poles put through actual sleeves. If you've ever used a real tent, it doesn't seem like this is a real way, or a safe way, to pitch a tent.
And, poor quality: The quality of the product was so poor, one of the four loops was already half unstitched when we received the tent. After my kids jumped inside the tent (and onto the pole) once, the pole broke, and the poles came out of place, rendering the tent unusable after around 5 minutes.

product_title: Munchkin Deluxe
review_body: I've been interested in this game for years now and finally bought it as a joint gift to my wife and myself from Santa and I have to say, I'm sorry I waited so long. I'd been on the fence because of the price more than anything else but after seeing the quality of the components first hand I feel more justified in my purchase. The addition of a board and pawns that would otherwise have to be bought separately as well as the box, which has room for expansions, make this the perfect entry point into the series. As for number of players, I play regularly with my wife and the game works great with two players though it really shines with a group of at least four.     The game itself is fun and humorous, even the rules are in the spirit of being a 'Munchkin' (a derogatory term for Role-players that regularly use loopholes or otherwise power play or cheat) and state right off, \\"Any other disputes should be settled by loud arguments, with the owner of the game having the last word.\\" The previous quote comes from 'Contradictions Between Cards and Rules' which is not as confusing a scenario as it sounds but that is the only real fault of the game, learning the rules. It may take a game or two, but once you've gotten the rules down the game play is usually fast and fluid.     One thing I have to warn you about is that the game is addicting and the urge to buy expansions (or promotional materials which also come with cards or in game bonuses)is almost guaranteed after you've become initiated.     If you're on the fence over gameplay, the official site offers a 'rigged demo' in flash format here, [...]     If you're on the fence over price try the demo above and see if you think it could be fun, if you find yourself enjoying it and have someone to play with I can assure you the price is well worth it.

product_title: Hot Wheels Criss Cross Crash Track Set With 10 Car Pack Bundle
review_headline: Looks great but the novelty wears off. A real hit and miss.
review_body:
This is certainly an expensive and rather loud track set up from the Hot Wheels series. Immediately the cars fly off in all directions until one gets used to which cars go on the track. It does not suit all types of cars. Some get stuck and others spin off the track after one lap. The cars that came with it are of course best suited but there are other cars that will suffice.

The noise of the track motors is rather intimidating, much louder than expected, roaring away incessantly, and this becomes irritating after a short time. My little boy could not handle the noise. It takes a lot of batteries and if these run out it may well find itself sitting under a bed gathering cobwebs.

All in all this is a track suited to the older age group, unless one can put up with the noise. The speed of the cars is exhilarating and very hard to control. It is difficult to master getting the cars to crash at all as they seem to miss more than hit. In any case, it works well enough but is best on hard surfaces.

It is also not as huge as the packaging looks, trick photography I believe. It will excite the Hot Wheels fanatic no doubt. I am just not sure that it delivers enough bang for the buck as it is very expensive for what it actually achieves.

product_title: Godzilla Destroy All Monsters Battlezone Collectible Figure Godzilla
review_headline: Looks great on a dresser or desk!
review_body:
I ordered this figure in unopened condition and was the first to ever open it. It was still crisp and new but by golly, the Big G himself was very well sculpted and detailed. Astounding quality for such a seemingly inexpensive and small item. He's posed in a very familiar battle stance but the coolest part about him is that he actually has a single sound effects sequence (two roars, a blast of his breath, and a quick yelp) and believe it or not, they even added the effect of having his spines light up from within in a lovely radioactive blue glow. Even more so, a blue light shines from in his throat, lighting up the inside of his mouth. It really is a very nice touch and looks even better in low-light situations.

What's really neat about this line is that, from what I understand, it was intended to include the whole set of monsters from the 1968 film "Godzilla Destroy All Monsters". However, the company went under during production and thus, only Godzilla and King Ghidorah ever made it to market (only 1500 King Ghidorah figures made it out!). The King Ghidorah figure is equally neat!

If you're a Godzilla goof (like me) and just want to add a small touch of Godzilla to your room or a whole army of monsters, this is a good place to start. Very modest on price, great quality and detail, nice extra effects, and personally, I think it's very collectable. GET IT! JUST DO IT!

review_headline: SYMA 031G Helicopter -- 5 star, if you get a good one.

Even while holding the helicopter in my hand with the RC on a table, the motor would stop and run at random, like an old Evenrude. This defect has been noted on many other reviews. My helicopter has been flown 3 times this weekend and is already near ruin. The motor just cuts out at random. I am sending it back to Amazon for a replacement. My Bro in Law has the same model which runs well. Apparently there are QC problems; some units good, some bad. I would suggest caution buying this brand. Other than that, it is great. I am sure the kids and I will have great fun after we get the bugs worked out.
UPDATE 1/8/13 We received a replacement for the bad unit. The new one is much better than the last one. The throttle is much more responsive and the motor has not even sputtered. I believe there is a QC problem, but good units can be had. Just do not hesitate to send them back if they are not right. Amazon does a great job of making sure the products you get from them are good. That is a big reason I buy from them. I am giving these a 3 star just for the QC aspect; some are good, some are bad. If they were all good I would give them a 5 star. You have a lot of fun for the price.

product_title: Dixit Journey
review_headline: Fun Family Game & Fun Party Game
review_body:
This game is sort of like Balderdash with pictures instead of definitions. 4-6 players. Each player has a handfull of pictures. The active player for the round selects one of his pictures and announces the clue. The clue can be anything from one word to the line from a song or movie. All the other players choose one of their pictures that best matches the clue. Players vote on which picture is the original picture. You get points for choosing the right one and points when others vote for your picture.

the twist: As the Active player, if no one guesses the correct picture, you get 0 points. If everyone guesses the correct picture, you get 0 points. Your clue has to be easy enough that at least 1 person gets it, but hard enough that everyone won't guess it!

We have played this game with all adults and with our children ages 8-12. It is fun for everyone. We allow lobbying for the pictures and talk about why each one might fit the clue. Lots of fun

product_title: MJX F645 F45 4ch LCD 2.4GHZ Large Single Blade Rc Helicopter (Colors may vary)
review_headline: Nice but not so happy with a few things.
review_body:
I'll get straight down to it.

Pros. Very stable. You can literally hover for at least 3 secs in the same spot without moving an inch due to its large size. You can customize the controller to suit your preferences. The two sticks can be adjusted for all modes of movements, meaning that you can make either the left or right stick for throttle or navigating.

Cons. Lets just say that the overall construction of the body is not so good from an engineering stand point. Its like a chair in which the legs is made from wax or plastic and the seat and back brace is made from metal. Parts that should be metal such as the landing gears and battery bay is plastic and parts that serve little or no function is made from metal. The rotating blades flexes when the heli is flying which suggests that the heli is a little too heavy for the blades to support. If you land too hard, there is a strong possibility that you will break the landing skids. Another thing some people might not like is that this Heli is VERY loud, Its like a small vacuum cleaner. It might not be a problem for outdoors but it might be for indoor flying. Taking off the canopy helps with the noise a little because it reduce the vibrations. Also, the motors gets very hot, around 80 degrees after a full flight. (measure with an Infrared Thermometer)

Seller (RC Toys Village) did not ship me the red version which I specifically ask for. They told me they would ship the red version in an email but I got the green version instead. Either they don't really care for their customer or they just didn't have the red version in stock.

I will suggest you get extra parts if you are a new pilot. If you know how to fly, then I recommend you get 2 extra batteries with extra charger for a good 20-30 minutes of fun. Dead Batteries takes a full 3 hours to completely recharge which is a good thing because the batteries would be damage from high charge current.

Overall. 3 out of 5.

product_title: Melissa & Doug
review_body:
As soon as I opened the package the box and blocks had a strong paint or chemical smell. I expected it to have a wood smell but that's not what this was. Not only did this toy have a strong paint smell upon opening but the paint on the blocks comes off when my daughter mouths them which I believe all babies/toddlers tend do. It's comes off way too easily with little effort or wear, it started coming off the first day we opened it.
It might be good to let it air out a while before giving to your child as far as the paint coming off...well I don't know about that one.

Pros:
Made from wood
Strong design
Fun for baby

Cons:
Strong chemical/paint smell when first opened
Paint on blocks comes off easily in child's mouth
Heavy and could hurt a little foot if dropped on it

review_headline: Cheap and Under-Engineered, Not a Lot of Fun

Just like the other reviews said, the cars don't fit in there right, the top of the panel that holds them in is too hard to open for kids. Ironically the bottom part of the panel which is supposed to be the hinge comes off easier than the top which is SUPPOSED to open. The ramp is completely non-functional, there's not enough tension on the joint to keep it up, the cars just knock it down and fall out. It does launch the cars very well if you learn to pop the launcher fairly hard, it took my three year old a few tries before he got the hang of that. The cars themselves are \\"meh\\". Just a tiny piece of plastic with a marble in the bottom for them to slide around on, but the marble isn't even lubricated so it doesn't roll very well. It amazes me sometimes what kind of cheap junk Disney will put their name on, definitely one of the worst offenders out of all of the IP-heavy companies.

The strategy involves knowing where to place your card in your rack so that as you are switching cards your sequence is most quickly completed. Each turn you can switch one card; you can choose the discard from the previous player or choose to draw from the deck.

This game takes about 10 minutes to play (or less). The rules are easy to understand for small kids. It's not overly exciting, nor does it require a lot of thought except during your turn. product_title: Step2  LifeStyle Custom Kitchen II, Brown/Tan/Green
review_headline: Was worried at first, but it looks great!
review_body:
So after watching what had to be the 50th cliche robot/solider/superhero/truck/action figure toy commercial for boys and barbie/fairy princess/baby doll/tea set/sparkly art project toy commercial for girls, I decided I wanted my son to have a little more variety in his toy box.

I decided a kitchen set would be appropriate since my son is always watching his grandmother cook and is always interested in helping her. I didn't want anything too big but wanted something interactive enough to keep my son's interest. I was WORRIED about this product at first, because I had seen a few complaints elsewhere from people who had taller kids or had children older than 2. My 4 year old is pretty tall for his age, so even with the measurements given, I thought it might be too tall for him, or he's outgrow it quick.

Well, we have it and my son loves it! It is a little below his waist but he doesn't seem to mind. He LOVES the sounds the microwave and the stove makes and even though he's only received it yesterday (on Christmas) he's made enough watermelon and pizza stew to last a week!

Pros - Very nice to look at, doesn't take up too much space, easy to put together, my son loves the frying and boiling sounds.

Cons - Hope you don't have kids that like to climb things. This is good up against the wall but be wary if you have climbers. My son was disappointed the frying noises don't work on his red pans, only on the pans that came with the set. Also, while easy to put together, I would use an electric drill instead of a screwdriver. Makes the job go so much quicker.

So I would recommend this product to anyone looking for a girl or a boy. And when my son gets tired of cooking, he just pretends to fix the oven with his new tools. :->

Pros:

-High level of detail with a figure of high scale.
-The ability to swap out hands and weapons to recreate some of the most intense moments of the \\"Devil May Cry\\" series.
-High level of articulation allowing any number of battle stances and poses.

Cons:

-Paint job can be rushed and causes bleeding effect (hair paint on neck).
-Extremely fragile. Not meant for extended part and stance swapping.

All and all if you are a hardcore DMC fan like myself then this figure is just what your looking for but if you are looking for. If you're looking for something more sturdy I would suggest one of the PVC figures.

product_title: Lionel Trains Polar Express Train Set - O Gauge
review_body:
After reading all of the reviews on this train, I decided to purchase it for my boys for Christmas. I thought I was making a wise investment considering the price and quality of the brand name, Lionel. In fact, the delivery by Amazon was great -- packaging and timeliness of delivery. The box was even sealed inside a "Factory Seal" plastic that gave me every bit of confidence that the quality of the product I was buying was very good. Little did I know that after spending several hours on Christmas Eve assembling it, that it was going to be a train wreck of a Christmas.

Unpacking everything and putting everything together was quite easy and laid out. BUT, after connecting the power, much to my surprise, I could not, for the life of me, get this to work. The light on the transformer just kept blinking. I did everything to troubleshoot: looked for a short on the track, examined the engine, took the tracks apart and back together again, replaced the wires, tested the wires -- nothing worked. After several hours I decided to head to the internet and typed in, "polar express o gauge transformer blinking green".

Wow.

I didn't realize how many issues these transformers had. I knew there were a few bad reviews here on Amazon regarding issues with the transformers, but had no idea there were many more outside the company. I thought what were the chances I was going to get a bad one? Well, chances were good.

Alas, Amazon was great -- I immediately got on my Amazon orders and quickly processed an exchange and they sent me out a new one with no questions asked. It arrived two days later (today). Although it was a heartbreak to see my kids disappointed on Christmas Day, Amazon (i.e., Santa's elves) fixed it up a few days later.

I would recommend to anyone buying this, if you are buying it for a special occasion, assemble and test prior to the occasion. This Dad learned his lesson the hard way. I'd say 5 stars to Amazon for getting it back to me so quickly and making the process of exchanging seamless and smooth. 1 star for Lionel on the issues with their quality. I'll be holding on to the receipt the next few days to see if it goes out again and plan to return it for a refund if the same issue arises.

product_title: Dowdle Folk Art Alpine Christmas 500pc 16x20 Puzzles
review_body:
This puzzle was so completely bizarre. You can't see this in the small image on this page, but this is one of the most \\"unintentionally\\" wonderfully weird puzzles we've ever put together...and we put quite a lot together. The snowmen on this are psychotic. The people are psychotic. There is a small child at the bottom who has built a fire just below a snowman to melt him. There are hunters up at the top--one is aiming a gun at a deer...and the other is in line with a couple of hikers. Snowmen are lurking in dark corners. There's even a snowman who looks as if he's devouring a gingerbread man by smothering him in his belly. Then, there's a guy in the bottom left corner packing up gingerbread men to sell and other gingerbread men are standing around in horror. Up near the top, there's a snowman saluting the flag--and a guy with a bow getting ready to shoot him. Then there's the deer on the right at the top about to get attacked by a bear.

This is based on Alpine, Utah where I once lived and worked (at Kencraft) and I've got to say that I don't remember Alpine being that much like an acid trip gone wild...but I really enjoyed finding everything as we put it together. I have never laughed so hard at a puzzle. I'm considering gluing it and framing it...and dragging it out for Halloween.

Oh, and the pieces on this puzzle were very bizarrely shaped but I liked that. It was a really fast puzzle to put together and a lot of fun since you weren't sitting around agonizing over a couple dozen pieces that all looked the same. Great puzzle. Great fun. Possibly not for the nostalgic grandparents who want a sweet puzzle to put together. This one bites. ; )

product_title: Symphony in B Music Toy
review_headline: One fatal flaw for littler kids
review_body:
This is an amazing toy with one serious flaw, and that's the DEMO button.
My two year-old instantly realized that to hear the music, just push the DEMO button.
This cancels out the PLAY button and any ability to add/subtract instruments, which is the entire point of the toy.
So, if you're handy and have size small and extra-small phillip screwdrivers, razor knife and pliers, then here's a \\"hack\\":
1. Flip it over and remove the batteries for safety.
2. Remove every screw on the bottom except for the ones appearing to hold the speakers.
3. Carefully lift the base off and you'll have access to the little circuit board that holds the DEMO button.
4. Remove that little circuit board and the DEMO button will fall out.
5. Take a razor knife and cut out the guts of that button, like you're taking the seeds out of a melon. I cut the four lines of plastic, then used a pliers to twist it out.
6. Put everything back together and Voilá! the DEMO button is deactivated.
And it is now a perfect toy!
One criticism-
The batteries included with the toy last about two weeks.
So if your toy starts glitching and you think it's broken, it's probably the batteries.

product_title: MOTA 6036 iPhone/iPad/iPod Remote Controlled RC Helicopter (Extreme Edition), White/Silver
review_body:
Gave the toys as a present to my 11 year old on Christmas day, was ordering parts for it on the day after. The counter weight and top rotors broke after about 15 mins of flying time (indoors), most of the time was simply trying to hover to get the trim set.

Had 2 soft crashes, no problems getting the unit back into the air. On the 3rd crash (running it into the couch) the counter weights came dislodged from the top rotor. After that, the unit will crash within 3-4 seconds when the counter weight and top rotor hit each other.

I have another one in the box for my daughter (10 yrs old) but may send that one back and just buy something else for her birthday.

I like the idea of using the Ipod Touch, controls seem to be responsive but sometimes the unit would not stop turning unless the off button was hit.

Giving the toy a 2 star because of the durability issues with the rotors and counter weight. Parts were not that expensive (~$5) but in the long term I may be buying a lot of parts to keep this flying. Not sure how it will do outdoor, too cold right not to try.

review_headline: Nice looking boat, good price but does have issues
review_body:
The boat looks quite nice but I've already had a few issues. First, one of the propellers came badly smooshed, no problem I just used one of the spares. Problem was apparently they have opposite pitch and I used one the opposite of the one I replaced......the boat just ran in circles until I figured out what was going on.
Second is the boat badly listed to one side, this required putting a old lithium AA battery on the light side, under the deck, now it floats upright.
Finally the battery compartment hatch isn't water tight(or anything near) so any water that splashes over the deck gets under the deck and on the battery. At one point the boat totally stopped working until I emptied the water and let it dry out overnight with a fan pointing under the deck.
I have mixed feelings about this boat, price was good and it looks quite nice but it's not the best designed. I'm going to keep it though, warts and all because of the decent price and it does look nice. The speed and power is quite good, I haven't used it long enough to have to charge the batteries which is a good thing I guess.

product_title: K'NEX Atomic Coaster
review_headline: Definitely Has Issues, But Still Looks Awesome
review_body:
K'NEX have certain advantages over LEGOs and certain disadvantages. K'NEX give you more bang for your buck. A set of LEGOs that's four feet tall will probably run you about 700 bucks. But LEGOs have much clearer instructions and are a lot easier to work with.

The main problem I had with this set was getting all the moving parts to work. Assembling it took a long time, and there were some places where I got confused and stuck, but overall the assembly wasn't too bad. Once I turned that switch on to watch the roller coaster cars run though, that's where things went downhill. Even though I followed the instructions, the chains kept getting caught up on the track. So I did a lot of things to try to correct this problem. I tightened the chain, I loosened it again, I rearranged the support structures to keep the car wheels from getting caught on any parts of the track, and just when I thought I was all good to go, I'd do a test run and the cars would get all the way to the top of the track but the track wasn't sloping enough to bring the cars back down. And when I rearranged the chain to bring it past the tipping point for sure, the darn chain kept getting stuck again. So either I had a chain that kept getting caught, or I had cars that couldn't reach the other side of the track's peak to get the momentum to roll down. It was an absolute mess.

So I took the batteries out of the motor completely and I just let my son push the cars up manually. That way I don't have to worry about the track breaking. I think he likes touching the cars while they're on the track anyway, so the automatic motor isn't even needed.

I think the main problem with this set is the top of the track is just too flexible and it's easy for the cars and chains to get caught up and messed up when a motor is pulling them. If the top pieces of the track were solid pieces that didn't bend so much, the motor and chain might have functioned better.

I think this is a good toy if you don't get hung up on trying to get the motor to work right. It's still pretty fun to move the cars manually, and it looks really impressive. Lots more impressive than a $60 LEGO set, that's for sure. Probably more impressive than a $260 LEGO set even. It's just extremely frustrating trying to get the motor and chain to work. And that's kind of a disappointment. It might have been better if K'NEX didn't even include a motor. There'd be a lot less frustration and, as a result, probably more fun. If I wanted the track to work with it I'd probably have to use scissors and tape.

product_title: Kid Galaxy Morphibians Stingray
review_headline: Durable and versatile -- for a remote control toy
review_body: This toy uses 2 AAA batteries for the handset and 3 AA batteries for the vehicle. My biggest complaint about remote control toys is their battery sucking capabilities. This Morphibian Stingray is no different. In order to work properly, the batteries must be replaced in the handset after it has been used for any length of time and the vehicle every other use, provided it has been turned off after use. The handset is easy enough to use. My 4-year old grandson figured it out. He played with it for about an hour then lost interest. We took it outside to try it in puddles. It can go through puddles, it can withstand getting wet but that's about the sum total of it. He's been playing with it off and on for about a week and the handset hasn't worn out or broken yet but he doesn't play with it for long periods of time. I can see where this would be a fun beach toy. Perhaps we'll put it away until we can take it to the beach. This is a great toy for a group of two or more 6 to 8-year old boys, provided they each have one. As remote control toys go, the Morphibian is more durable and versatile than others in this price range. Overall I'm impressed with the Kid Galaxy brand. I'm just not that impressed with remote control toys.

product_title: Lionel Trains Polar Express Train Set - O Gauge
review_headline: Awesome product from Lionel.  The kids LOVE it!
review_body:
I'm an adult, and this is my first real train set. I obviously have no perspective on some of the comments regarding declining quality for Lionel, but I can say that I'm thoroughly impressed with this unit! If this is "low quality" for some folks, then I have to question just how high they are setting the bar!

First, the train and tender are metal...and HEAVY! All pieces are incredibly well made and detailed, and the unit works without issue. It's perfect for around your Christmas tree and the kids will definitely love it (mine do!) Some pros & cons:

Pros:
1.) Quality. Incredibly detailed and sturdy engine & tender units.

2.) Features. Love the realistic smoke stack, lights and whistle.

3.) Set-up. Extremely easy to set up and get going. I had it running around our tree in about 15 minutes.

Cons:
1.) The only real con (and it isn't really a con with this set per se) is that Lionel doesn't offer multiple levels of this set. I for one would have paid more for an ALL metal set (the passenger cars are plastic) as well as a set with more features. It would have been nice to have more lights, a working bell, more steam features, etc. Again, I think the value of the current set is good, but if Lionel had offered a more expensive set with more features, I would have purchased it.

2.) Noise. As I said, this is my first train set so this may be normal, but I find the train to be fairly loud while it is running. With a large room and all hardwood, the noise resonates quite extensively and can get annoying. As a result, I only find myself running it for short periods.

product_title: Bandai Tamashii Nations Fire Rodan "Godzilla" - S.H. MonsterArts
review_body:
I got this figure for my birthday, and I have got to say, it was a great choice! The sculpt on this figure is fantastic, though the beak is slightly different than the prototype. The extras that this figure comes with really sell this figure, as it comes with the red spiral ray for the S.H. MonsterArts Godzilla and Godzilla (1995)/Burning Godzilla, and a damaged head for the S.H. MonsterArts Mechagodzilla. The articulation on this figure is great, with the wings being able to turn full 360, the head has a great range of motion, and the legs hold up pretty well. The wings also feature full flapping action! While the tail is movable, it should be noted that the end balljoint has the tendency to pop off if overextended, which is easily done due to the small size of the joint, and can cause a small piece of the sculpt to fall off. Please take care while doing so, and note that the figure would not be broken if this happens; just realign the sculpt and the socket the ball fits into, and you're good to go! The only improvement that should have been made would be the addition of an ab crunch.

All in all, a fantastic figure that any fan of this line should pick up!

product_title: ALEX Toys Rub a Dub Jungle Waterfall, color may vary
review_headline: Smiles all around with this one!
review_body:
Santa just brought this toy for my 3 children (all girls ages 3.5 years and twin 2 year olds) and we just played with it in the bath tub. Overall, I don't have any *real* complaints about this product.

Pros:
sufficient suction cups hold fast on plastic backed tub wall.
Easy to remove by slipping a fingernail under the suction cup to break the seal.
Works as advertised, many variations optional and can be spread out to several feet if so desired.

Cons:
I might have to get another one, my twins were fighting over it!
The monkey wheel did occasionally get stuck, but only for a moment or two and corrected itself.
My twins could slide the pieces across the wall while still suctioned on, thereby, making the waterfall effect void. But that is a problem with my children, and not so much the product, so therefore, I did not hold it against the product. It's just something I hadn't anticipated.

Overall, my children had a blast with this product. My 3 year old really enjoyed moving the pieces to see if it would still work or work better or what not, she had more fun with it the way it was meant to be played with than my twins, who really enjoyed the monkey the most. Did I mention, the monkeys eyes spin around as the wheel does? They thought that was hilarious! I would recomend this product to my friends and family, and would buy it as a gift to give also. Another great product by Alex Toys!

product_title: The Crazy Chicken Game
review_body:
I purchased this game for my daughter for Christmas through another retailer, so my review has no reflection of amazon at all, but the product (like these reviews SHOULD be!)

My daughter begged for this game for a good month before Christmas and I decided to get it for her as a gift. It was one of the first things she started to play with because she was so excited to give it a try. I will tell you this, it took us longer to get it out of the package than it did for us to play the game, and she immediately said it was lame and probably won't touch it again. I'm going to return it in a few days after the post Christmas return rush slows down just a little. This game is a waste of space, plastic, batteries, etc. I would give it negative 5 stars if I could.

On top of it being a lousy game, I also feel that it is a hazard. My hand got stuck twice in the \\"doors\\" inside of the chicken.

The point of the game is to not get the \\"third gut\\". Well the \\"guts\\" and other pieces are just little round pieces that kind of look like Skittles candy. You are supposed to put them in the bottom of the chicken but when you turn the chicken upside down to do so they just come out of the top because the doors have a hole in the center.

The sounds do not work properly. Sometimes they work, sometimes they don't...and they are pretty annoying when they do work. This is coming from a mother that has in the past purchased a drum set, guitar, karaoke machine, etc...so I am not an \\"anti noise\\" mom like a lot of parents can be.

All in all, this game isn't even worth $5, and will probably get no play time from any child above 3 yrs old. And you won't want a younger child to play with it because like I said, the game pieces look like large skittles and are a huge choking hazard.

product_title: Air Swimmers Remote Control Flying Bass Fish
review_body:
I bought this and the shark for 2 nephews. It's a cool concept, and once assembled I was pleased with it, for what it is and what it cost.

But I HATED putting it together. The instructions are very poor. I did better with the Bass, but only because I had already assembled (and messed up) the Shark. Read the instructions VERY clearly. Don't look at the diagrams at all (not that you can make much sense of them, the print quality is so poor, like a multi-generation copy). Don't assemble while tired or stressed, you will make mistakes. Even if you handle the parts very carefully, odds are one or more of them will break at a (cheap) glue joint, so have some super glue handy.

I've put together many hundreds of presents over the past 30 years for various siblings, cousins, nephews, and kids. These were some of the worst instructions I've ever seen... and that's saying a lot.

product_title: DC Collectibles The Dark Knight Rises: Batman vs Bane 1:6 Scale Icon Statue
review_headline: Mediocre Paint Job, But Still an Iconic Pose
review_body:
I was giddy for this statue because it represented one of my favorite scenes in The Dark Knight Rises, the type of scene that makes your inner fanboy squeal. Perhaps having the moment of impact would've been more apt, but I understand that would be almost impossible to balance Batman AND Bane on Bane's one leg given how top heavy it would be. This statue is fairly sturdy and is heavier than it looks. No chips or cracks on it. The cape is felt, which was probably done to reduce weight.

I have knocked off a star because of the fairly mediocre paint job. Given its price, it should have been better. On my statue, there was white porcelain showing on Bane's chest that wasn't painted. Luckily, I had some flesh tone acrylic paint that could touch it up like new rather than go through the hassle of requesting a replacement. From afar, the paint looks fine.

I'm also not a fan of it not being numbered. I am not sure why DC Collectibles aren't doing limited edition runs anymore. I would like to know the edition size of this piece. If I could do half star ratings, I'd bump this piece down to 3.5 stars, but what the heck, I'll round up to 4.

product_title: Battlestar Galactica
review_headline: Best Board Game I have ever played!
review_body:
The game says you can play 3-6 players. If possible play with at least 4. 3 player games are not that fun.
This is a great game and it has the total feel of the show. There are 1-2 cylons in your group and so there are several accusations going on. Some one may make a move to sabotage the fleet or they may of just made a bad choice without knowing it. The game is difficult to understand how to play at first. It took my group two games to understand what is going on and how to play the game when looking for the cylon or what to do as the cylon. If you just have one player that knows how to play it makes it a lot easier explaining everything to the new players. So it is very difficult to learn at first but the beauty of that is its that much more unique. Basic games get boring quicker vs the complicated ones.

I have had the game for a week now and have already played 4 games. My friends and I are super addicted and can't wait to purchase an expansion

product_title: The Learning Journey Techno Gears Marble Mania Extreme 3.0 (200+ pcs)
review_headline: Fun for the kids, frustrating for the adults
review_body:
Bought this toy several years ago, and gave it to our 9yo son last year. My wife spent an hour or two a year ago trying to put it together with him, but didn't get very far. So I stepped up yesterday and started working on it (our son is 10 now!). Being a software engineer and pretty handy at building just about anything, I figured it couldn't be THAT hard, right? But it didn't take me long to see why other reviewers give it a bad rap. It is HARD to put together. Not that the pieces don't fit -- they do. The problem is that the instructions are very often too vague, and the pictures, which should provide information about part orientation, are either too small, photographed from poor angles, or are covered up by the part numbers, making them hard to see. I was doing fine until I got to the point where we had to assemble the tower. Nothing I tried worked. I thought, \\"these are the right parts, but they sure don't fit together like they do in the picture.\\" So I started to Google for things like \\"marble mania parts/instructions wrong\\" but found nothing. That's when I saw the Amazon reviews. An \\"Ivy League Engineer\\" struggled with it, and I wondered, \\"another engineer couldn't do it either?\\" Well, then this is not a child's toy...it's a parent's nightmare! Not finding any help on the Internet, I went back to it, and after looking at the pictures and pieces again for another half hour, I finally realized that we had the base part of the tower positioned upside-down.

Long story short, this is not an easy toy to assemble. It took me 3-4 hours to assemble (after which I noticed that the instructions say to allow 3-4 hours -- or I might not have even started the job!). As others have said, it is not a build, play, and take apart toy -- the time it takes to put it together is just too long, and no child is going to build it on their own. If a child has a long attention span and plenty of patience (which does not describe any child I know), then maybe, just maybe, they will experiment with it by moving things around. But honestly, I don't see that happening.

Be prepared to scrutinize every step and every piece for proper orientation, as that is the key to successful completion.

In the end, our son (and our 5yo daughter) enjoyed it. They both had fun overloading it with too many marbles to see what would happen (the balance bucket will get stuck in the wrong position and stop the whole thing from working) -- but they didn't care -- it was fun for them.

product_title: Barbie I Can Be... Paleontologist Doll
review_headline: Adorable--needs to come in more variations
review_body:
My daughter loves dinosaurs, bugs and animals in general. We jokingly call her \\"nature girl.\\" This Christmas she asked for her first Barbie so I went on an adventure to find one who fit her personality. I was delighted to find this one. Her outfit is neat. We *love* the boots and hat. I'm sure they will come off in 3 seconds as it's a universal law that Barbies are naked 70% of their plasticy lives, but my girl will appreciate them anyhow. The accessories could be a little more plentiful and realistic (glittery dinosaur bones? *really*? HAHAHAHAHA), but they are still fun. The packaging is even educational as it gives basic facts about fossils. I also like how this Barbie is associated with the Smithsonian as I spent many a happy visit to their Natural History museum during my childhood--and would like to believe a little money from it goes to them.

My only gripe is that the doll only came in blonde (there's also a dark skin/black hair one, but it wasn't at our store)--even though her face was *adorable*. This may come off as nit-picky, but I care a lot about hair/eye color as my daughter is a brunette with brown eyes, and I don't want her growing up thinking she is \\"less\\" because 99% of dolls have blonde hair and blue eyes. This doesn't mean she won't have blonde dolls (she currently owns and *loves* her 12\\" Disney Store Rapunzel doll), but I wanted her first Barbie to look more like her.

I ended up buying an inexpensive brunette Barbie (from the Mermaid Tale series) and swapped the heads. I thought of just swapping the clothes, but swapping heads is less work as I didn't need to remove the dolls from the packaging. Popping off Barbie heads is a little more involved than when I was a silly kid who played jokes on my little sister. These days it helps to use a hair dryer to warm/soften the head and a small flat-head screw-driver to gently pry it off or you risk breaking the piece that secures the head to the neck. Once you have the heads off, they are easy to swap. They slide right back on the necks easily. Now I have an adorable brunette Paleontologist Barbie ready to be wrapped and stashed under the tree on Christmas eve.

Probably TMI for anyone reading this, but if you have a child with a different hair/eye color and want to get make one of these cool dolls look more like her (or him--if it's Ken or a GI Joe), this is a way to go about it.

This review is technically not complete as my little girl hasn't played with (or even seen) this doll yet, but I expect her reaction will be a joyful gasp and followed by a squeal on Christmas day. :)

Update: Paleontologist Barbie is a hit! My daughter calls her \\"Adventure Girl\\" and has her go one many adventures with Rapunzel, Tiana, Merida, and the She Hulk. They go hunting for bones and treasures--which they store in the trunk of their purple Beetle (handy for speedy getaways from live dinosaurs and dragons). She has held up fantastically from lots of TLC and the boots surprisingly have not gotten lost too easily as they stay on most of the time and are large enough to be easily found. The hat, on the other hand, tends to disappear more (it would be nice if it fit a little deeper or had elastic to stay on), but that's okay. This doll has turned this anti-Barbie mom into a fan, and I am investing in a few cute outfits for \\"Adventure Girl's\\" future expeditions. :)

product_title: 11" Santas Secret Elf Boy and Girl Set Christmas Plush Stuffed Animal Toy by Fiesta Toys

If you are in the market for an \\"elf on the shelf\\" or Santa's \\"secret elves\\", this pair made by Fiesta is a great buy. They do not come with any Elf On The Shelf story, so if you are looking for that experience, you may want to go with the product that is accompanied by a book.

These two elves are adorable though. They are plush and are both just shy of a foot from top to bottom. They are NOT pose-able, however, like any plush toy, may be propped up against other items to \\"stand.\\" They are also stuffed well enough to \\"sit\\" on their own.

You get two elves in the set, a girl and a boy. They have nice detail and are soft and cuddly if used as a toy. They are soft and do not have any real small parts on them. Each has a jacket which is removable, and closes in the back with Velcro.

We do not use our elves as toys since they are magic.

They appear around Christmas time, right around when we begin to set up our decorations. Their job is to watch our children and report back to Santa. They may not be touched, as this prevents their \\"magic\\", which is that they become animated at night while everyone sleeps. They tend to get into all sorts of mischief, from going into the cupboard for snacks or sugar (to make their favorite drink, sugar water), to leaving notes for our youngest, to watching TV and playing video games, and some times , alas, they \\"TP\\" some of the rooms in the house. After Christmas, the elves return to the North Pole.

The price for these elves can range greatly, particularly during the height of the Christmas season. We got two so we'd have a boy and a girl, and two elves can help each other get into mischief that maybe one elf cannot alone. The price for two was only about $5 more than one elf. At the time (right around Thanksgiving) we paid just under $20. Again this will vary based on season. I do think I've consistently seen that the price on Amazon is always the best, and often significantly less than some other retailers.

If you are looking to start a nice Christmas tradition, or just for a cuddly Christmas toy for a youngster, these are really nice.antly less than some other retailers.
