product_title: Lords of Waterdeep: A Dungeons & Dragons Board Game
review_headline: Awesome game but some improvements could be made
review_body:
I bought this game today and took it to game night. We played it all night and ignored everything else, 3 games in about 6 hours (with a short break to eat, probably about 1.5hrs/game). Once everyone got it down, we were really having some fun. It's really a great game! Not too complex and you can really get into it. I highly recommend it to everyone!

Now, I'm going to talk about why it only got 4 stars (although it would be 4.5 if I could):

-0.25 stars:
11 lord cards. Cool, you think, some variation on bonuses. Wrong. Only one card (6 points per building) will offer anything other than 4 points per any quests from 2 random types. It really is a waste. The first game through, we got wrecked by the guy who had the card for building control, all of us unknowing that it existed. Afterwards we went through the deck...it's the only one of it's type. Seriously?! I understand it's a DnD type and therefore quest-based but I want to be able to do something other than quests to get VPs. I always hope for the building perk, and honestly it's a good one to get. The buildings really benefit you (allowing completion of small plot quests easily) and if you take the 4 gold from Aurora's Realms Shop or 2 from Cliffwatch Inn you can easily buy one per turn. It's so much easier to not have to focus on quests, which is disappointing. I want options. More building benefits. Maybe some lords get more than 4 points for the quests. Maybe some 5 for Arcana and 3 for Commerce...change it up! Make it more intense!

-0.25 stars:
The intrigue cards. An awesome part of the game, yes. However, often I could only help myself if I helped others. Hurting others? Played those cards every chance I got. But helping others? We usually ended up with a few cards we refused to play for this purpose. I don't want everyone to get an orange/I don't want to give away 4g/I don't want to discard a quest, etc) There wasn't anything that really stuck out as an awesome -power- card to get. Maybe include 1 or 2 strong cards (Take one [?] from every player, take 1G from every player, etc). Even better, set a few cards in a power deck that you can trade buildings for or something. I want more options. More depth. It was frustrating for one player to get 3 terribly, terribly useless intrigue cards when others actually got useful stuff. And the Mandatory Quests...make them harder/more unique! We could usually get them out of the way in one turn. I dealt two to a foe and he did both easily same turn, without actually having the pieces already due to plot quest perks. I'd say make them increase in difficulty based on level in. Same with the other better intrigue cards! At round 5, they become somehow more powerful. It would make the intense endings that much more intense knowing someone could turn the game with one card!

Despite all of this, it is still quite a good game. If anything, I'm tempted to make my own cards. If I could match them perfectly (so you couldn't tell them apart by the material/colors/etc) I would make my own Lord Cards, and I still might. This would be a cool option to include also. Either way, when the expansion comes out (August 20th, 2013 according to Amazon) I'll be buying it immediately if not pre-ordering it. Buy this game, you won't regret it!

product_title: Tenergy Syma S102G Night-Hawk 3-Channels Mini Indoor Helicopter
review_headline: Would be nice if it worked.
review_body:
My wife and I bought one of these for our son for Christmas. We even bought a spare parts kit because we knew that he would probably slam it into the wall/chair/cat/sister and break the blades or the main shaft. We figured it would be something easy to fix if necessary. Well unfortunately for us the Heli came with two major issues. The first being that even with new batteries, either the remote or the heli itself drops the signal randomly. So when the heli would actually lift off, the signal would just cut off and it would come back down. Very dissapointing.

Another issue we noticed immediately was that the secondary shaft gear was not meshing with the drive gear properly. So, on top of the heli randomly losing signal, it was a crap shoot on whether or not the gear was going to grab and the heli was going to actually take off or not. Overall we have had a very poor experience with this product.

My son really likes it and was able to fly it easily when it did work, so I will probably keep it and repair it, but another issue I found is that the two lower screws near the landing gear, which need to be removed to take the plate out that protects the gears, are set very deep into the plastic. I have several jewelers screwdrivers and they are either not long enough or too thick to get to these screws. I believe its unnecessary to have these screws set up in such a hard to reach manner and due to this I will have to buy something else to repair it.

Hopefully once I get to the gears I can repair them so that they mesh. I am going to order a spare receiver and controller as well. If that doesnt fix it I will still probably buy the 107.

product_title: Pan for Gold Science Kit – Learn Gold Panning and Become a Prospector!
review_headline: Great Gold panning Kit - Highly Recommended
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:mo12VCV2HNLKEPL]]This Dr. Cool \\"Learn How To Pan For Gold Kit\\" is about the coolest thing I have seen in a long time! We have always been fascinated by gold panning but never had the ability to do it where we live. This kit allows us to try our hand at it using pyrite \\"seeded\\" sand in-place of real gold sand, but the technique is the same and the results are fun!

The set includes all of the basic items need, including: a 10\\" black Pan, Rookie Sand, Advanced Sand, Glossy Adventure Guide and Activity Guide, plastic Tweezers, plastic magnifying glass, collection jar, drawstring bag, and a fairly large pyrite nugget. See video.

You will also need a larger basin of water to wash the sand, we used a slop sink in our shop. My 10-year old \\"test subject\\" enjoyed panning for the pyrite in the beginners sand and my wife panned the advanced sand, with both saying it was a little harder than they thought it would be from watching several popular TV shows. With a little practice they both were able to extract the pyrite and were thrilled with the results.

My family now wants to try their hands at the real thing, so will have to look for an opportunity to go \\"out west\\".

Highly Recommended!

CFH

Note: kit provided for review by the manufacturer

product_title: Maisto R/C 1:24 Scale 1967 Ford Mustang GT Radio Control Vehicle (Colors/ Mhz May Vary)
review_body:
People ask me constantly - how do Vine reviewers hone their skills of criticism? Do they meet with other Vine reviewers, and drink upscale teas while chatting about the latest books? Or perhaps, just meeting with the local literati, or subscribing to esteemed journals like The New York Times Review of Books, or what?

The model car goes hurtling down the hall, with my stuffed pig attached by a rubber band on the roof. It enters the living room, where our two cats sit, pretending boredom. It stops in the middle of the carpet, and moves back and forward a few inches. Finally one cat climbs off the chair and goes forward to sniff the intruder.

As soon as it does, the car moves back, and so does the surprised cat. The cat sits down, afraid to come too close. Good move, because the car suddenly turns around, and the piece of wool attached to it spreads out as the cats attempt to chase it down the hall.

In ways like this do we selflessly try to find the essence, the je ne sais quois of the product. It is relatively small, but fast and maneuverable. In the beginning, I had trouble making it drive straight ahead, but there is an adjustment for that under the car, and now it goes exactly where I want it to go.

It does just what you expect it to do. It seems strong enough to resist bangs and crashes, and I'm sure it will work outdoors. It is a load of fun, especially for the cats, which are getting tired of chasing the laser spot.

So if your cats need the diversion of Monty-Python's Confuse-A-Cat, but without the expense, this is what to get. And you might even find yourself having fun. That happened to me, but I squelched the feeling, reminding myself that I was here to conduct an investigation, not just laugh at the cats. Even if you have no felines, you'll still get a charge from it. Talking of which, the car requires two AA batteries, not three as part of the Amazon page says.

This game will keep your mind sharp because you have to add your card values as you throw down your cards. Then at the second stage, you have to add up your points. This takes some thought, but it's a lot of fun finding all kinds points in your hand and in your crib.

The game of spade uses partners. You could use the board to keep count. Use your imagination and you can come up with any number of additional uses for this Cribbage board.

This board will make the game A LOT of fun. Get this Cribbage board wet and you'll enjoy it as much as I do. But, most of all, HAVE FUN!

review_body:
I bought this to play with my 6 year old son and it is a blast.

The plastic pieces are durable and fit the grids perfectly. The ships have some neat details on them. The game itself is contained in 2 separate boards that have a closing lid which keeps the pieces in them for storage. It also seems like you could easily play the game in the car because of the way the boards are created.

There are two small negatives, but not really that detrimental. First, there are more pegs than will fit in the game board peg holders. This is good in case pieces go missing, but it leaves pegs loose in the box instead of the game boards.

Second, the labels on the grid are somewhat hard to read because the letters and numbers are the same color as the plastic (they are raised letters). Not necessarily a huge issue, but my 6 year old had to count across at times because he couldn't read the grid.

Overall this is an awesome game and I'm so excited to play it with my son!

product_title: Ravensburger Master Labyrinth - Family Game
review_headline: Fun and quick game, suitable for kids, little text involved
review_body:
The Master Labyrinth is a slightly more beefed up version of the original The aMAZEing Labyrinth. There are slightly more rules but the concepts are the same. Best with 2, 3 players. Recommended with 2, 3, 4 players. Each game takes about 60 minutes to play.

It is played on a board with maze tiles (Straight's, L's, and T's) arranged on it. Perhaps the most novel aspect of this game is that players mutate the maze by sliding a tile onto the board from the side, which hopefully will enable them to travel to the next ingredient.

Players are represented on the board by little wizard pawns. Players are wizards-in-training and they are charged with running around the maze and finding all the ingredients (numbered chips) needed to become a Wizard. The trick is that the two chip cannot be taken until the one chip is taken, and the three chip cannot be taken until the two chip is taken, etc. Once all twenty-one items have been taken, the highest total score wins. But the 'Master' part of the game gives each player three ingredients which will give the player bonus points for grabbing.

The game is fun, but pushing the modular board could get a little tricky. Therefore, on the one hand, the game is child friendly due to its lack of complex rules and texts, but on the other hand, those with less delicate fingers might get annoyed. If the base board provided wider tracks of movement for the modules, this problem could have been less prominent.

product_title: Portal 2 Bookends for Shelf and Books - Officially Licensed Portal Collectible
review_body:
Found these on Amazon by a random search and quickly purchased them for a Portal-loving boyfriend who was delighted to receive them. I'll go through with a numbered review to divide information for you!

INITIAL REACTION:
5 stars! "Oh my god! Where did you find these?! They're amazing!"

DESIGN:
5 stars! Unmistakably a piece of "Portal" memorabilia. Great concept, good choice of color. These pieces look great just sitting out, acting like bookends on any geek's shelf.

CONSTRUCTION:
2 stars. They hold books just like they should...but their construction is not quite as durable as I expected. The thinner metal won't hold anything more than stacks of paperbacks. If you're planning on using them with heavier books, choose something else...or you'll need to double up with a pair of flat metal bookends (like the type you can purchase from WalMart or Staples). Otherwise, these pieces tend to warp and bend.

VALUE:
3.5 stars. Because of their slightly flimsy construction, I don't feel that they were worth $26.00. I would have paid up to $20 for them, mostly for the design.

Hope this review helps you make a more informed decision!

product_title: Magic The Gathering: 2012 Magic Return to Ravnica Holiday Gift Box
review_body:
Bought this for myself because, what the heck, it's the holiday seasons and I needed a box for my growing collection. The box itself is quite sturdy. If you've seen or owned a fat pack box, I reckon the construction material for this box is the same as the fat pack boxes.

As for the price, you're basically paying $4 for the box, 6 VERY nice and sturdy thick plastic dividers (thicker than credit cards!) with great RtR Lands art, some stickers, and the alternate-art foil Dreg Mangler. I think this is a really good deal, especially if you need a box for your collection anyway. I've also heard that game and comic book stores are only getting limited supplies of these, so these Holiday Gift Boxes may become rare soon in the future - all the more reason for getting one while they're around at base (or close to) price.

The 4 RtR booster packs that come in the box are basically at MSRP price of $4 each. As with any booster packs, they're random. You'll get good pulls some times, and you'll get less-than-desirable pulls most of the time. I happened to be lucky with the packs in my Holiday Gift Box: Rakdos Lord of Riots, Chromatic Lantern, Blood Crypt, and a foil Mizzium Mortars. The current going prices for these 4 in total already exceed what I paid for the Holiday Gift Box! (The other rare was Volatile Rig, boo...)

review_body:
When searching for ways to get my 2 1/2 year old into anything that educates him, sometimes I try to go beyond just a book. He LOVES this toy. And it is completely durable, made of solid wood. I have actually seen it help my toddler learn the letters of the alphabet and learn to spell, and he is more engaged in this toy than just a book that teaches the alphabet (I have more than one, by the way). He started with assistance from me, picking out all the letters for him and putting them near the slots they would fit in. (Of course I would tell him what letter it was, tell him what sound it made and what word he was spelling, too.) Now, he is sounding out the letters himself when he grabs them, and he is finding the letters he needs to spell with all by himself from the greater pile they're in. He is also much better at putting the letters into their appropriate spots on the puzzle. As anyone will find out, this requires your child learning to rotate or flip the piece over until it fits.

review_headline: You have GOT to be kidding me!

P.S. I am perfectly capable of reading and following directions. I followed them! And when they failed me, I also googled for answers. Two FULL large containers of Morton's salt later, I only managed to make the goop angry. It only managed to make the pieces smaller so that it was even more difficult to catch. product_title: LeapFrog My Pal Violet
review_body:
My daughter got this as a gift from my mom. My daughter is 7+ months old, and Violet is still a little too big/bulky for her to really play with, but she loves the different pressure points to press.

We customized is online (which was a breeze) and Violet sings songs that includes my daughter's name (Ava), her favorite food, color and animal. So while she has no idea what's going on yet, it still cute, and she likes to hear Violet speak. I assume it will be more fun when she understands it.

Some of the very minor complaints I have are: 1. The USB cord is maybe 1 foot long. Didn't affect me, because our computer is has easily accessible USB ports, but it could be an issue for others. 2. The name used (Ava) sounds like the animal is asking a question when saying her name. The phonetics are not perfect, and it's a fairly simple name. I read a review where someone with a son named Christian had a similar issue, so it may be that way for all names...but it's certainly not horrible. 3. You would expect Violet the purple dog to be a female, the voice sounds like that of a young boy. Not the worst thing in the world...just something to keep in mind. None of these would detract from a 5 star rating for the toy though.

Overall, I would DEFINITELY recommend the toy. It's under $20, and you can continually change the customization it with the different songs/foods/colors/animals...there are probably a million combinations. You really can't go wrong with this toy, and it will probably last your child a number of years!

product_title: Propeller Racer: Green Science
review_body: This is a pretty basic fun toy. When I asked my son (5 yrs)his opinion about it for this review he said he really liked it, but currently didn't know where it was. With my limited assistance he was able to assemble it as it just screws together. The following are my observations. It is not the most durable toy as the rails are easily bent; for that matter they are easily straightened - but you never get them back quite right. Works best on a hard floor - doesn't like rugs. Eats batteries fairly fast(two batteries - AAA) with continuous play - because of that its hard to see how it could be part of a 'green' science project as the advert suggests. Interestingly my son took off the supplied propeller and tried other propellers off other toys. Amazingly enough they fit the shaft, probably because they all were connected to similar type motors. All were smaller in diameter and didn't drive it very fast. One was a propeller off a cheap toy fan which had LEDs that lit up when it rotated, but again not large enough in diameter with its small rubber blades to get it going very fast. In spite of the slow speed having the LEDS made it the most fun for him, running it down the hall in the dark. Playing with the different size blades was probably the most educational part of the toy for him. Too bad they don't supply alternate propellers with it. Price was very reasonable $12-$13 as I remember. Should package two together for racing.

product_title: LEGO Cars Mack's Team Truck 8486
review_body:
I got this for my son's 4th birthday. I bought it on clearance, which made it all the sweeter. It was the first big set that I have ever put together. It took me about an hour and a half. I am pretty sure that if I was in the target age range of 7-12, I'd have had it done in half the time.

Like other large sets, the pieces come in numbered bags so you can build a part at a time. My son was enthralled as he watched Lightning McQueen emerge from what moments before had been a pile of random bricks. To tell the truth, so was I!

The instructions are fairly clear, though some of the fiddly little pieces are a bit hard to recognize in the drawings. I made it through the whole thing without any major mistakes, which speaks volumes for the quality of the instructions. And I actually found myself enjoying the process once I figured out that I needed to separate the pieces by type as I opened each bag.

There was only one part that I didn't enjoy. I'll just go on the record saying I hate stickers, and this set had a lot of them. With most, there was some room for error, but the larger stickers fit their respective bricks \\"just so.\\" I might have had an easier time if I hadn't had 3 cups of coffee beforehand.

This set is very sturdy. My son is currently curled up in bed holding it, and nothing has fallen off. The detail is amazing. The whole trailer opens up to show the inside. The parts are well-made, too. The tires are thick, thick rubber that will last forever. I think it's something we'll enjoy for awhile.

I don't know if kids in the target age range would enjoy playing with the completed project since it is based on a Pixar film. My 10 year old would have enjoyed the challenge of putting it together, but he would have broken it apart not long after and cabbaged the pieces to build something else. If you're just looking for a Cars 2 toy, Mattel cars may be a better value.

review_headline: Great bath toy for hours (and years!) of fun!
review_body:
I bought this bath toy for my son when he was 2-3 years old. He is now 7 years old and it's still his favourite bath toy!

When I first got it and set it up, I was also disappointed (like other reviewers were) with the fact that some pieces didn't \\"snap\\" together as I thought they should. At first, when my son tried using the pump (by far his favourite part of the toy!), it kept coming out. I fixed this problem VERY easily and inexpensively by buying a piece of non-slip rubber (the kind sold sometimes as shelf liners, which has non-uniform holes in it) from a dollar store, cutting it in a strip about 1.5-2\\" wide and maybe 5\\" long, and wrapping it around the bottom of the pump very tightly before pushing the pump into the hole where it belongs. After this, the pump stayed in place extremely well with no problems at all, and I haven't replaced that piece of rubber for years! The rubber doesn't even show, so it doesn't affect the look of the toy.

This is expensive but worth it -- it has stood up very well for years, and is not made of very cheap plastic.

product_title: The Elf on the Shelf: A Christmas Tradition with Blue Eyed North Pole
review_headline: What Drooling Halfwit Would Buy This?
review_body:
Here's a test of how empty and meaningless your life really is.

You can either lead a productive life during the holidays, wrapping up things at work, helping the poor, and a host of other things that actually are in the spirit of the season.

Or you can buy an elf and, while the kids are sleeping, have it make messes around the house. Messes that you will have to clean up.

Seriously? Who dreams up this nonsense? More importantly, what idiot would actually look at this on Amazon or the toy store and say, \\"Oh, this sounds like a good idea because I don't have enough to do as it is!\\"

I mean, isn't the glittering mound of presents beneath the tree enough? I mean if you really want to build anticipation for Christmas morning, why not buy a freaking Advent calendar instead?

So if you are having a hard time filling up your day as it is with manicures, tennis lessons, and your book club's in-depth discussions of Fifty Shades Of Gray, then knock yourself out. But rather than this incredible make-work book, why not use your bottomless reserves of energy to hie thyself down to a soup kitchen or start a toy drive for underprivileged children? I think that would be a far better use of your time than this ridiculous thing.

product_title: Bananagrams Word Game
review_body: If you like scrabble but can't stand the long wait while the deep thinkers try to find the "best" word with the most points, then this game is for you. It's a quick game that can be played with several people (2-4, even 1 works). You take 21 letter tiles and everyone begins creating his or her own words which can be changed every time they pick a new letter. This way you don't have to wait and you don't have to worry that your spot will be taken by someone else. You basically create your own scrabble words and try to be the fastest person to do so as this is a quick game. You keep picking tiles one by one until they are all gone and the first person to finish using all their letters is the winner. Be careful though, you will be a rotten banana if you claim to have finished first but one of your words is not in the dictionary. The game comes with a lovely cloth banana-shaped holder that zips closed. I highly recommend this game if you like words and creating words.

product_title: Star Wars The Clone Wars The Vintage Collection Ahsoka Figure
review_body:

This figure is Ahsoka from The Clone Wars era. This one was sculpted with a realistic look based on the animated series.

As such, the sculpt of the face is amazing. The rest of the body is well sculpted as well and not as slender as the animated counterpart. The clothes in particular are well detailed including actual fabric from the hips down.

This figure has:
- ball-jointed head,
- ball-hinged shoulders, elbows, knees and ankles, and
- swivel wrists, waist, hips.

This figure has great grip with both hands holding both lightsaber well. It also includes two unlit sabers that can be attached to her belt.

Overall, this figure offers great likeness and good posability.

This puzzle is a a truly unique one. It reminds me of some of the Rubik's line of manipulative puzzles in how fun it can be when you finally break through an figure out the 'trick' to solving the particular puzzle. My kids(son=9 and daughter=6 at the time of posting) had a lot of fun getting into this puzzler. The beginner levels were easy enough for my six year old and the others were challenging enough for my 9 year old. This will be a great addition to our puzzle / game collection.

Only a few slight drawbacks that keep me from rating it 5 stars overall. The limited # of puzzles reduces the replay-ability, but I'm sure that after putting it down for a while it would be fresh and fun to retry the puzzles that we've already finished. The product durability is a little tricky. If you don't twist it and truly only FLIP the tiles you'll have no issues, but I could see an overzealous younger child twisting and breaking this toy, so definitely no smaller kids without supervision. A suggestion for increased stability might be to use metal rods to hinge the corners instead of the plastic hinging. These issues aside the puzzle is a fantastic mind game and great for a car trip or bus ride as you could have many people give each puzzle a shot and maybe even make a game of timing solution time for a challenge for multiple people. It also takes up very little room and can fit in a man's front pocket with ease.

Another great toy by Thinkfun. Keep the great ideas coming!

review_headline: A big hit for my 3 year old
review_body: We just got this for our son, who is two months shy of 3. He \\"bought\\" it with his allowance savings (all 8 quarters and a few pennies). We don't usually spring for expensive toys like this as our kids rarely play with toys enough to make it worth it. In fact, we hardly buy them toys at all. They love nothing more than a shovel, bucket and dirt. But my son would stop, as if hypnotized, every time he saw the Batman Batcave Imaginext set. He would be captivated for several minutes, until I pulled him away. After 3 or 4 encounters like this at the store we decided that we may have actually found something that would hold his interest. When we went to get it, he again stopped, practically skidding, as he passed it on the shelf. Adorable! It was in the cart and ready to go when we saw the castle for the first time. Now, I know he wanted the Batcave, but we also know our kid well, and swords, castles and things like that are a favorite. We showed him the castle and he was totally into it, and it seemed to have more replay value than just Batman, so we switched out. This thing has been awesome! He wants to play with it every day (it's been over a week) and I'm sure at this rate it will keep his interest for a long time. Better yet, his 4 year old brother and 18 month old sister love it too and they can all play together. And even their 5 year old cousin will be able to enjoy it when he comes over. As a frugal mommy who doesn't buy stuff like this, I am VERY happy with this purchase and may even consider springing for the ogre or the dragon after Christmas if they're marked down ($30 is too much!!). And I know that getting the accessories will rejuvenate any waning interest, prolonging the value of the castle. I highly recommend this toy.  :)

product_title: K'NEX Nintendo Mario Kart Wii Mystery Bags
review_body:
What I like the most about these figures is that they are a step up in terms of quality compared to most typical pose-able Mario branded action figures. The figures stand approximately a (Lego) head higher than a Lego figure. I received Donkey Kong from my package, but I also own the Mario figure. Both figures are made up of three detachable pieces: the head, the upper body, and the waist/legs, and stick together tightly, The arms are able to move 360 degrees if they are not stopped by the legs or the head (this varies by character). The legs move backwards and forwards but not entirely in either direction. Finally, the head is able to move a full 360 degrees as well, but some figures like Donkey Kong have large heads that fit perfectly into place in a groove between their shoulders and can hardly be moved at all.

The pictures give a good idea of what the figures look like, but don't give a true representation of how the figures appear in three dimensions. For example, some of the figures look flat faced in the pictures although all of the figures are rounded and faithful to the actual art of the character. The quality of the art on the actual figure, such as Donkey Kong's tie and eyes, are printed finely without any bleeding or odd marks. However, the construction of the head piece is by no means perfect and may contain one or two hardly noticeable imperfections in some obscure areas. The Donkey Kong figure also has a noticeable line across his chin below his mouth because his head is large in comparison to the other figures and that is the way it is constructed. Both figures stand properly on flat surfaces despite their legs not being perfectly straight.

Despite having reviewed these figures as a collector they are a great quality toy for children who enjoy Legos or K'NEX. These figures are primarily meant to supplement the K'NEX Mario Kart Wii building sets. There is also a Wario figure that is currently only available from a track set, butnot obtainable from these bags. If K'NEX products are anything like Lego's, you will want to pick these up before they go out of production.

product_title: Nerf A0419 Lazer Tag Set, Twin Pack
review_headline: Fun Laser Tag, iOS Optional but Recommended
review_body:
Cool: This is a pretty cool laser tag set that can use iPhones or iPod touches for added \\"heads up display\\" fun. Recommended, especially if you have two compatible iOS devices.

Description:

- the iOS add on is optional. Out of the box, this is ready to play. (Well, technically, each gun needs 6 AA batteries, not included, but once you add THOSE, you're ready to play.) You can mount a frame for the iPhone/iTouch or leave it off.

- A bubble sensor on the front of the gun registers \\"hits\\", so when your gun is out and ready to shoot, you're vulnerable. The good side of this is that you don't have to mess with sensor vests or hats, but the down side is that it's a little less realistic. There's no point hiding most of your body behind a tree or standing sideways -- your body can't be shot, only your gun.

- These are LOUD. Part of the noise is to communicate with the iPhone, I think, since it only connects via the headphone jack and doesn't have bluetooth, so any input to the phone must be coming through the microphone. But at any rate, you won't have much luck sneaking up on your opponents. (And, as noted above, you probably can't reliably shoot them in the back, anyway).

- There are three triggers. One fires shots, one reloads, and one raises a \\"shield\\" that prevents you from shooting or getting shot.

- The guns are a little heavy, but the weight and balance is good.

- Adding an iPhone is really fun. Once you download the free app, it shows you the camera view, but adds battle info, shows your shots, and shows you an explosion when you hit an enemy. As you take hits, the screen appears to crack.

- Note that this isn't compatible with all iPod touches or iPhones, so make sure that yours are compatible. We used an iPhone 3g and an iPhone 4S, and they both worked great, but the iPhone 3 is too old, and the iPhone 5 is currently too new, so we were lucky that we fell in the sweet spot.

Conclusion: I like these a lot, but make sure they're for you before you invest. They're loud and don't work with all iOS devices, but if those limitations don't bother you, they are very cool and highly recommended.

review_body:
Master Chief, he is very awesome,he doesn't say a word, but he doesn't have to. He is more of an experience than a character. But, anyways, let's get talking about the to-, I mean Action Figure (It isn't JUST a toy).

Pros:
A very good sculpt, nothing was made lazily, and it feels like he's really a miniature Master Chief in your hand.

So much detail. His color, pieces of armor, everything is there, looking at him in-game and figure, it's like there isn't a difference (except one is pixels, other is plastic).

He stands very well on his own. He doesn't come with a stand, but he doesn't need one, his feet are like their own stands, I even shook the table he was on (pretty hard, even) and he stood their, unfazed.
*********

Cons:
His gun is a challenge. It took me about 15 tries to put on his gun, and I became slightly frustrated, but I eventually got him in a cool two-handed pose. The gun can be held in both hands, but I found his left hand easier.

Movement is stiff. His arms and knees move fairly well, but his feet, waist, and legs move pretty stiff. And it seems the Chief has gotten Chronic Depression after being made into action figure , because his head is almost always down, even if I try to move it, kind of annoying.
*********

This action figure is almost perfect, except the 2 problems I could actually find. I bought Dutch (from ODST) along with the Chief, and they look great next to each other. Also, he is a very durable toy, I've found myself \\"playing\\" with him a lot, so it might be good for a teen age Halo fan, who isn't afraid to \\"play\\" with some awesome \\"toys\\".

I would recommend this to almost anyone who likes Halo, either if you play or pose, it's great fun.

product_title: 4 First Games Children's Game
review_headline: Good FIRST game box for little ones
review_body:
I brought this box of games with me when I went to my daughter's house recently. My 4-year-old granddaughter was excited to play. She punched out all the game pieces from the cardboard and we separated the ones used for the different games. My granddaughter has played a little CandyLand, but otherwise, she's new to game-playing. We played two of these games - The Bird's Nest and Garden Party.

We played Garden Party first, and this was fun because you're collecting flowers to plant in your \\"garden\\". She enjoyed rolling the dice and collecting the flowers, and it's a short game, so we played it several times. Then we played The Bird's Nest. According to the rules, you can't move ahead until you roll the color of the spot immediately in front of you. I thought this would make for a long game, and lots of rolling and not much moving, so I decided to change the rules so we could move up to the color spot that the dice shows, even if it wasn't the very next spot. Then we had to roll white to enter the nest. This made the game go much faster. I do think that it would've taken too long and been frustrating if we played it according to the rules that came with the game.

Garden Party was more fun because there was something to collect (the flowers) and you put them on the matching flower in your \\"garden\\".

The game comes with two double-sided boards, making 4 games in all. I do feel that the outer box is very sturdy - more durable than most game boxes. I think the box will hold up for a long time, but I would recommend putting the game pieces in separate baggies (maybe the snack-sized ones?) according to which game they are used with, so you can start playing right away rather than spending time separating which pieces are with the game you want to play.

Size/Design/Construction:
As said the very small helicopter has a weird 2 blade on top design & a very tiny topside tail blade. Becasue of it's size, it doesn't fly for long (about 5 or so minutes) & switching it on requires a finger with a nail. It at least has a LED indicator when it's calibrating in the beginning & when the battery is low.

Charging
The helicopter charges through a small plug attached to the controller. It takes at least 30 minutes & you get to fly it for a little over 5 minutes. There are no antennas because it uses infered.

Controls
The Controller has the basic 2 stick design. The left for altitude & the other for fwd/back/left/right. Once you move a stick it seems to takea full real 1-2 seconds to respond which makes flying very difficult becasue you have to plan ahead long before it gets to the area you have to change directions for. The altitude stick is VERY sensitive though again, slow response. It can't slide to the side, only turn to the left or right. It does have a trim control on the side of the controller so it doesn't rotate forever on it's own.

iOS App

One is the same as the sticks on the controller, the other is using tilt control (which was even harder to use). I had a lot of issues using these controls to the point they seemed broken. (BTW, make sure you turn your iPhone to airplane mode so an incomming text/call doesn't freeze your controls.) The app also allows you to record 3 short flight patterns, though I'm not sure how that's needed. Works on an iPhone4 using iOS 5. When I read this had a \\"cam\\" & smartphone app, I thought it was a bigger helicopter with a small camera on it so you can see where it's headed. I was very disappointed.

Decent charging time

product_title: Revell X-34 Landspeeder
review_body: Any toy-like issues with this kit are easily remedied. The snap assembly is tight and with minor clean-up of sprue attachment points, goes together cleanly. Not a huge fan of the pre-painted kits as a rule, but this one is more than acceptable. I would have like to have seen the large gouge/scrape visible on the nose of the 1:1 subject replicated, but that's just a pass or two with a brush loaded with steel-colored paint. I'd be interested in seeing a non pre-painted version of this kit with options (new engine pods and a full canopy with rollbar) to recreate the sportier XP-38 version of the speeder - the reason Luke couldn't get top dollar for his when he sold it. All in all, an enjoyable build.

product_title: Thomas & Friends: Thomas and Charlie 24 Piece Floor Puzzle in a Shaped Box
review_body:
My nieces and nephew (3 1/2 years old) loved this puzzle because it's brightly colored and very engaging! All Ravensburger brand puzzles that I have purchased in the past, including this one, are high quality and durable cardboard stock that snap into place with no small gaps in between like other puzzles I've purchased. The pieces are thick, large, and are perfect for small hands to work on fine motor skills and spatial reasoning while lining up the pieces. The images on the pieces are firmly attached so they won't peel off either.

Even the box is engaging - it's shaped like Thomas and my nieces and nephew even enjoyed playing with the box and rolling it across the floor like a toy train. The finished puzzle is about 27\\" by 19\\" and I'd highly recommend it for little Thomas the Train enthusiasts!

product_title: Zombicide Base Game
review_headline: Great zombie apocalypse game but a bit buggy
review_body:
Pros:
- Really fun game to play. It has really tense moments in which you don't know if you're going to survive. It adds to the excitement in playing.
- Production value is great. The figures are top good and there's plenty of them. Cards and board tiles seem durable.
- Varied scenarios you can play. You can probably come up with various scenarios if you're feeling creative. There are some online that people have created that they make available for free.
Cons:
- Some mechanics do not make much sense in some contexts.
- There are no trays for the figures and other bits so I just piled them all in ziploc bags.
- The zombie kill markers that go along the top edge of the player boards seem like they can scratch the player boards in the long run.

product_title: Mayfair Games Replacement Card Set Settlers of Catan
review_body: Settlers of Catan is my favorite game in the world. We wore out many of the cards that originally came with the game, so I bought these. There's nothing wrong with the cards, but I do have a little problem with the lack of consistency in printing. With every expansion, each set of cards seems to have a different hue of blue on the back. These particular ones looked a little washed out. The problem here is when drawing cards from another player you might be able to tell the difference between, say a slightly lighter blue resource card from this deck and a slightly darker blue commodity card from the Cities and Knights deck. It's pretty obvious the difference. It's almost like taking all the aces from a deck of red-backed cards and putting them in a deck of blue-backed cards, then playing blackjack with them. I just wish the manufacturer could be a little more consistent on the printing color quality from here on out.

product_title: Takara Tomy Transformers Masterpieces MP-12(Japan Import)
review_headline: Great engineering marred by a rushed paint job
review_body:
The hallmark of a great Transformer is its ability to form both a perfect rendition of vehicle AND character form, without a transformation that kills you in the process (think ROTF Leader Prime). Lambor succeeds beautifully there, providing both a lovingly crafted car mode as well as a dead-on Sideswipe character model. The transformation is clean and easily repeatable without a lot of fuss. Engineering wise, this is highly recommended.

The glaring downside however in a piece this expensive, is the paint apps. The difference in red color between the body and cockpit is obvious (due to the material they're layered onto). And worse, in my particular model the silver paint that lines his shoulders was already severely chipped off in one spot, and bubbled in another. FRESH out of the box. As they say, always take caution with a Takara first run. Fortunately a little touch-up with my Elmer's silver paint pen did wonders here so it's livable.

review_body: I saw the signs at the store for the new Furby the 2nd week of September. I was shocked at the price of almost $60 at the store and thought there was no way the toy would be worth that price. I was wrong! My daughter got the teal Furby last Sunday. We downloaded the app on our iphones (free) as well. This toy is so much fun that even my 14 year old starts laughing at it. It has so much personality and so many different ones that you can't get bored with it. It sings, it dances, it babbles constantly. Evil Furby is hysterical and the first time it changed to Evil mode it made my daughter cry (which caused my son to love the Furby). I had to rock Furby and treat him like a baby for several minutes before he changed back to a happier mode. We quickly discovered over and under feeding Furby makes him mad as does rough housing him too much. After a few days we got a 2nd Furby the plum colored one. It is a deep purple and very pretty. The Furby's instantly liked one another and began babbling. Now they sing together and dance even when we are not playing with them. This is a geat toy and I am recommending it to everyone I know, young and old. Well worth the money as there are so many different things it does. Furby falls asleep and starts snoring and wiggling like it's trying to get comfortable. It will be completely silent after a minute of snoring. If you pick it up Furby instantly wakes back up so be sure to let Furby fall asleep where you plan on leaving him for a while. Lack of rest also brings out evil Furby.

product_title: Sinful Suzi Variant Edition Statue
review_headline: A Five Star Statue In A Four Star Variant Edition
review_body:
Sinful Suzi first appeared in a variety of sketches by renowned artist and premiere pinup painter/illustrator Joseph Michael Linsner for a series of online auctions, and fans went wild. Shortly thereafter Linsner brought Suzi into her own with the 'Linsner Girls Portfolio 4: Sinful Suzi', leaving rabid aficianados frothing at the mouth. He then thrilled us with the penultimate statue that captures every leather-clad curve and unclad contour of her fetishistic frame to perverse perfection. Only 1200 of those statues were made and quickly sold out, and then there came this variant edition in matching red corset, thigh-high boots, evening gloves and thong. Voluptious in the extreme, she's the epitome of the succubus that every red-blooded man would let escort him to Hell in a hotrod and a heartbeat. Hell yeah.

Unfortunately, no one knows how many of these exist as they were made to order, and the prices asked for this edition here on Amazon at the time of writing are steep. I paid less than 1/3 of this price at an auction, but demand fluctuates with these collectibles. Personally, I much prefer the first edition over this one; maybe 'cause I sexually prefer my women in black over red any day, maybe 'cause she's got on even less clothes (no corset), maybe 'cause the red mixed with the blue hair (which is a brighter shade in this version) and blue base (the first one is grey and resembles a stone mausoleum pedestal) makes this more garish than sexy, at least to me. I'm well aware that this is a statue, but she looks like a cheesy Vegas neon-lit hooker than the original depiction did. But to each his own, right? One man's meat is another man's poison...

Amazon usually drops the ball on details and specs on such items; this statue and it's predecessor are approx. 15 and 1/2 inches from bottom of base to the tip of her devilish horns, Suzi's exactly 12 inches tall, and it's about 8 inches in length from one end of her pitchfork to the other. Comprised of cold-cast porcelin and hand painted in great detail, it's a welcomed addition to any collection, regardless of edition. But I'd definitely recommend checking out both versions (think ebay) for better pics and pricing. And I still think the first statue blows the lid off this one. (When is Amazon going to list these items as 'collectibles' and not 'toys'? product_title: Baby Alive Wanna Walk Doll Hispanic Speaks English and Spanish
review_headline: Works well & my toddler loves it!
review_body:
As a parent, you have to take the bad with the good. Quite often, you're going to be buying toys that are extremely annoying, but your kids will love them. This is one of those toys. There's something a little eerie about watching a doll walking on its own in that stiff, dollish way. However, when it brings enjoyment to your kid, that's what matters.

product_title: Step2 Whisper Ride Buggy
review_body:
The buggy is good. My child enjoys riding in it. What I have an issue with is the assembly instructions. They are horribly illustrated and way too many for a simple buggy.
Pros:
1. It is spacious enough for a 1 year old, though I am not sure it would fit a 3 year old.
2. My son definitely likes riding in it and keeps pointing to it all the time to push him around in it.
3. It looks cute enough for a toddler
4. Light weight
5. This is way better than the lightning mcqueen push car which has a very unsteady handle for pushing

Cons:
1. Awful assembly instructions. Step2 must have a better instruction manual. The pictures are not informative enough to make assembly easy. It takes a bit out of the joy of buying a new toy for your child and makes for a lousy first impression for the parent.
2. Noisy. Be prepared that the pedestrians along the block would be looking at you.
3. Cheap plastic-y feel - but you already know that when you buy a plastic toy

Overall, my son loves this and since the assembly is a one-time thingy, its not too bad for the parents.

product_title: Last Night on Earth: Timber Peak Expansion
review_body:
I have played LNoE for about a year now, and I absolutely adore this addition to the game.I've collected every expansion so far, excluding the ones only available on Flying Frog's website.

In Timber Peaks, we are introduced to a brand new town, and three new Heroes (three returning ones, now \\"Survivors\\"). We are given Alice the Waitress, Nikki the Bush Pilot, and Ed the Lumber Jack. These newbies are still awesome cliched stereotypes from B Horror Movies that fit right in with the cast from previous games. Speaking of which, the board this time around (one center tile, 6 L Shaped Boards) is made to be able to have the characters from before, as Twin Peaks also has a High school, Diner, Police Station, etc, for them to start in.

I am a little disappointed by the decision to include 3 surviving Heroes (Sally, Sheriff, and Jake) as I would have preferred to have all new heroes. I mean I can understand the direction, it is also a common element to have survivors return in sequels, but I feel that establishing a definite continuity is pointless since there is unlimited possibilities, and still would have liked to see new heroes.

The artwork is once again stunning and enjoyable. I even had to stop and look at the pictures every now and then because they were so impressive. One that pops into mind is \\"Terror at Timber Peak\\" which features a beautiful blue mountain with that unique filter LNoE uses.

There is also new rules for an experience system. As you slay zombies or wound heroes, you collect experience points that you use to buy upgrades for your characters. Although these are a cool idea, I felt that some of the bonuses we kinda lame, and really not helpful. This was kind of a bummer after gathering enough to buy an upgrade that wasn't helpful, and having to collect again.

The cards this time seemed really powerful, but I couldn't tell if either deck (Zombies or Heroes) was stronger than the other, which means I can assume that they're pretty even. It was nice to have guns for survivors that were able to fire multiple times per turn, even if it drives the Zombie Player(s) mad. They of course would strike back with cards like \\"Vicious Attack\\" which would deal two wounds as opposed to one. This cranked up the fear and unpredictability a little when your youth characters could die in one hit.

The objectives also seemed more difficult than the original base game, which is not necessarily a bad thing, but I don't know if I would necessarily tell people who are interested in playing LNoE to pick this expansion over the original, but I don't think that it would be too big of an issue if they did

Also, as you know if you've played FF's games before (or if you haven't, fyi), LNoE returns with the same super quality materials. The figures are well detailed and sturdy. The boards are thick and shiny. And the cards are thick too, made from superior quality paper. They have a glossy and plastic feel to them. It really is a shame I have to sleeve all my cards, but you could totally get by without them. I just have nephews who are prone to spilling soda, so I have no choice!

Overall I really enjoyed this expansion and cannot wait to play again. Also a new center board is awesome as my fellow players have discussed maybe creating a game using both of the boards and 8 L shaped boards and having twice as many heroes and zombies, and two missions to play out. Possibilities and creativity are infinite on this game!

Buy it if you love LNoE! But if you're just starting, I kinda would recommend the original LNoE base game to begin with.

product_title: Blokus Game
review_body:
I am an instructor for the Summer Institute for the Gifted and at SIG I teach game strategy to 5-6 year old gifted children. One of the games I use in this course is Blokus. I highly recommend Blokus to any parent who wants to help their 5-7 year old have fun learning to be smart.

The beauty of Blokus is that the rules are incredibly simple so a young child can learn them quickly, in under two minutes, and yet the strategy and thinking levels needed to get increasingly better at this game are quite complex. This combination is exactly what makes a great game to teach critical thinking skills to young children. Specifically, Blokus helps children develop spacial reasoning abilities, problem solving and perseverance. It also can begin to develop thinking ahead skills. But, this game is as hard as your child is ready for in that a child can play it and have fun before these capabilities are fully developed and have a blast while improving these skills and as their skills increase they can engage the game at higher degrees of complex thought. With repeated play, you will see your child's thinking skills improve.

My oldest daughter just turned five and we gave this to her for her birthday yesterday. We have already played four times. She loves it and we love seeing her work through the spatial constraints and opportunities the board gives you each turn. You will hit a homerun if you give Blokus to your child as a gift both as a fun parent and a parent who helps to raise a smart child.

product_title: Elefun
review_headline: Kids love it, parents hate it
review_body:
My 4 year old autistic son loves this toy, but it takes a lot of work and supervision to help him enjoy it. It has been great as far as getting my son to participate and interact with us. He calls out the colors of the \\"butterflies\\" as they come out, he picks them up and puts them back in, he asks us to \\"turn it on\\" etc. The problem stems from the way it absolutely drains batteries and the long plastic snout that the butterflies float through. Because the snout folds closed, you have to manipulate it every time you start it, or the butterflies will never come out. Sometimes the butterflies just hang out in the tube, so even my son knows how to tap it to get them to pop out. And, it turns into a very expensive toy when you have to replace the 4 C batteries all the time. We always use Energizer or Duracell, which are not cheap/weak batteries. And, because I'm participating with my son every time, I make sure to turn it off as soon as possible to save battery life.

I saw that another reviewer mentioned cutting the snout shorter, which I have thought of doing. That might save some battery life, because the butterflies will spit out faster and you can turn it off more quickly.

Also, we have not used the nets, but I haven't seen them as being dangerous. They provide 4 nets (green, red, yellow, blue), but there are only 3 colors of butterflies (green, red, yellow). I don't understand why there is a blue net, but perhaps it's in the directions I haven't read.

Overall, I'd only suggest it to those parents who are willing/able to play with their kids every time they use it and can afford a lot of expensive batteries.

product_title: K2 Game by Rebel.pl Publishing
review_body:
This is a great game that is very simple to learn. Via a very limited hand of cards, some of which allow you to move up or down the mountain and others that give you oxygen, you try your best to climb one of the highest mountains in the world. You begin at base camp where the oxygen is rich, but as you move up, the air thins and the cards in your hand may not give you all of the oxygen that you need, causing you to repel back down, if you can. There is a limit to the number of climbers that can be on one spot as you climb up, and that number decreases as you climb higher. The goal here isn't necessarily to reach the top, though that does give you the most points, but to survive 18 days on the mountain. Each of your two climbers gets a tent that you can use to acclimatize, but other than than, you need to strategize your way up, or down, without running out of oxygen. The weather plays a huge role, and it varies each game depending on how the weather tiles come up.
I really love this game, one of my favorites. You really feel the tension as you try to battle the weather and others for climbing spots to win. There is an easy side with good weather and a harder side with more severe weather, and the combination of weather tiles compounds these conditions. Wear your warmest jacket and bring lots of energy bars, you're going to need them!

product_title: Electric Tricycle Color: Blue
review_body: I have to agree with the negative reviews on this product that I've seen on Amazon. I purchased this trike in March 2012 and have nothing but trouble with it. It is a cheap Chinese made product without quality control. As previous reviews have stated their support is a joke. YOU, THE BUYER, ARE THE SUPPORT! Problems I have had are as follows, the pedals broke first because they are cheap plastic ones, the support center did send me some pedals, the same plastic type, I threw them away and went to WalMart and bought some good metal pedals. The rear basket does not fit to the frame well, fortunately there are holes drilled in the clasps so I was able to use cotter pins to hold down the basket. The front tire that came with it must have been a bad spare because shortly after receiving it, I had to replace it and the tube when the tire blew out. The fuse overheated and melted part of the plastic box containing the battery. I had to remove the burnt out fuse holder and replace it and the fuse. Later the battery connection broke off and I had to solder a good replacement connection to get the bike running again. Finally the bike literally broke. I was not racing or going fast (Thank God I wasn't), just making a left turn after the light changed and the frame broke throwing me up against the curb. It cost me $117.70 to have it welded and a lot of aggravation trying to deal with E Wheels Support (still haven't been reimbursed). Except for the plastic pedal I have not gotten any support even though the website states the EW 88 is guaranteed for 1 year. My advice is DON\\"T BUY FROM E WHEELS or their suppliers.  Update Oct 18, 2012, finally received a check from E Wheels for the welding I had done ($117.70).  However, now I have a NEW problem, the bearing on the offset axle went out.  I noticed when riding I heard a thunking noise and upon investigation it was the bearing.  My calls to E Wheel Support have gone unanswered.

product_title: Citadels
review_body:

The amount of strategy does depend on who you play with, however, with the right people the possibilities are endless.

This game requires observation and a good memory to figure out the favorite strategies of your competitors, which in turn forces you to attempt to remain as unpredictable as possible. The expansion pack is a healthy addition to an already great game, as you can completely revamp your strategy and change the game significantly just by swapping out a few cards.

This game is a delight and if you enjoy games that are majority skill, and only a small part luck, you NEED this game!

product_title: Wood Folding Chess Set with Beveled Edges - 11.5 inch Walnut Board
review_body:
Seriously, worst chess set ever. Now let me tell you why.

The wood was nice but the craftsmanship was terrible! The squares were offset and uneven. The board was smeared with dust from the fabrication and because they threw on a cheap clear coat I can't clean it off! Very lazy.

The pieces were a decent design, but the fabrication was horrid! The tops of the rooks were cut so uneven that the some of the cuts didn't even look made. The base on some of the pieces were flat on one side like the machine cutting them was off calibration, making them uneven and ugly.

The hinges on the bottom of the board were not receded enough so when the board was unfolded and set down the center of the board stood higher than the ends. This created a small gap in the center of the board and really made it hard to lose myself in the game.

The felt on the bottom of the pieces were so off centered that some were climbing up the sides! I had to peal them off and re-felt the pieces myself. So lazy!

Finally, when I went to open the box the first thing I noticed was the glue had seeped in from the box and was stuck on the board. I had to rip the box away from the board and then peal off the glue and paper from the end of the board. It's still stuck on in certain areas.

If this were an $8 or $10 dollar board I could live with it and wouldn't complain, but I didn't buy this to have another cheap set lying around the house. I bought this to upgrade from the plastic set I've been using; I still use the plastic set. For $30, do not buy this set!

product_title: Casa Grande Family Game
review_headline: A fun, lightly strategic family game
review_body:
As cool as this game looked, it frustrated us at first. I'm a smart guy - I write technical documents for a living, yet as with the other two Ravensburger games I played, I was very confused by a couple of subtleties in the directions. As with the other two, the game is actually pretty simple and once we started playing, we figured out where we had misinterpreted the directions. And, admittedly, for the first 10 minutes or so, we didn't quite see the appeal, as though we were still missing something, but as we continued, and the board started filling up, and we better understood the goal, and started picking up on the strategies we began to see the simple attraction of the game and we quite enjoyed it. By the end of the game, I was looking forward to another round in the near future. So my point is, if the relatively sparse instructions confuse you a bit at first, hang in there. It's really a pretty good game, The game took a while to play - close to an hour, but I think it will go faster in the future, and there is the option of playing a shorter game with fewer pieces, but the most fun is when the board starts getting full, so I'd encourage you to go for the full game.

The object is to strategically place pieces that form a foundation of a building, on which you can place platforms ('floors', or 'stories') for which you get paid. The strategy is to try to build multi-floor structures as your payment is multiplied by how high the building is. You can bank bonus points that allow you to do things like alter your position on the board, 'rent' a space to build a foundation piece on another player's building, or trade for cash. Whomever has the most cash once the pieces have been played, wins.

Like their other games I tried, this game will appeal to younger kids as well, but the older you are, the more complex the strategy and overall game play will be. It's also a very attractive game, but I had to mark it down for durability since the \\"money\\" is very flimsy and half of the playing pieces are cardboard, but they should still last many, many years if not mistreated.

Give it a try, I think you'll enjoy it.very flimsy and half of the playing pieces are cardboard, but they should still last many, many years if not mistreated.

Give it a try, I think you'll enjoy it.

product_title: LEGO Friends Advent Calendar 3316
review_headline: Lego Friends are Great and this adds to the positive impact for young ladies.
review_body:
Legos are great and fantastic toys. One long standing problem that legos, and other popular building toys, have had to deal with is a lack of interest from young girls. Of course, this is not universal, but largely this is true. This lego set is not all that \\"rich\\" in unique and valued pieces. However, because it is the only one available in this type of set (the Friends sub brand), it is hard not to bring up this larger idealism in the review. As more sets are added in the future, and as more sets are added to the line up, I think the quality discussion will be more important. We all are familiar with Lego's quality. Is this set expensive related to other toys, yes, like all legos. But try to find a better 3 dimensional puzzle that can be played with and built .... that is another discussion for another place.

For now, we must understand that Lego chose a safe route with this Advent calendar and also chose a limited run not to have lots of these sets hanging around later to diminish the \\"Friends\\" image after the holiday season. Lego has a lot vested in this line, and as a father, I loudly applaud their efforts. My daughter loves the lego friends line and plays with them side by side with my son and his star wars sets.

In this case, it comes down to the fact that I can, for the first time, this Christmas, set aside a calendar that is for my daughter and my son. It doesn't have to be some half hearted attempt to make Lego City more interesting.

People may complain that Lego should not be making gender specific sets, but I firmly disagree. If young girls need the different toys to engage and be interested, then we need to understand that difference and celebrate it, not rail against it. I have never pushed or steered my kids in any direction, the reality of the situation is that when I take my kids into Walmart, or TRU, or Target, then my daughter likes looking at (and asks for) the Friends line, and my son likes the Star Wars line.

product_title: Ravensburger Giant Stow And Go
review_headline: Does the job, but not stellar
review_body:
We do so many puzzles in our house, so I was interested to see how a puzzle storage system would work. This particular system is a large piece of felt and an inflatable tube.

The felt is very durable and the pieces don't slide around, and the inflatable tube is a great toy for hitting other people with.

The first couple of times I tried to roll up my puzzle and move it to another location, everything was fine with the rolling and unrolling, until I got to unrolling the last piece of felt that was around the tube. The puzzle pieces tend to slip out while the fabric is still on the tube, so the last five or six inches get ruined. A way to prevent this would be to keep a border of 6 inches on the edge that would be rolled first, so that part wouldn't be jumbled.

Pros: you can (very carefully) move the puzzle successfully.
the product is very sturdy

Cons: The puzzle pieces are not on a perfectly flat surface so the puzzle tends to buckle. I prefer a very flat surface for puzzling. There's a reason why I don't put puzzles on fabric.

Bottom line: I wouldn't buy it again.

product_title: Thomas & Friends: Thomas and Charlie 24 Piece Floor Puzzle in a Shaped Box
review_headline: Thomas & Charlie Floor Puzzle Is A Winner...
review_body:
Ravensburger's \\"Thomas & Friends - Thomas & Charlie\\" is a wonderful floor puzzle which toddlers may enjoy assembling. Thomas the Train and Charlie are familiar characters for most children; they should have fun putting this puzzle together. Thomas the Train fans, in particular, will find this a wonderful puzzle.

Ravensburger's \\"Thomas & Friends - Thomas & Charlie\\" floor puzzle is sturdy and the picture is firmly attached so that little ones will have quite a bit of difficulty if they are prone to \\"peeling\\" items apart. The die-cuts are smooth which allows for easy assembly. Pieces fit together well. They are not so tight that a child will become frustrated, nor so loose that the puzzle will fall apart if jostled slightly. Even the box Ravensberger has used is sturdy; the \\"engine\\" shape is unique and clever.

Although recommended for ages 3 - 6 years, I think younger children with whom an adult is \\"playing\\" can enjoy Ravensburger's \\"Thomas & Friends - Thomas & Charlie\\" floor puzzle. I question whether children at the upper end of the age range would find this puzzle much of a challenge. For those older children, I would recommend choosing some of the Ravensberger puzzles that consist of a greater number of pieces. Ravensberger's \\"Thomas & Friends - Thomas & Charlie\\" floor puzzle is definitely a 5 star toy - not only for its fun factor, but also for its durability and its educational value.

product_title: Batman Dark Knight Rises Exclusive Vehicle Batmobile with Batman
review_headline: A great, simple Batmobile for kids
review_body:
I was disappointed with most of Mattel's Dark Knight Rises line. Other than their Movie Masters figures, the Dark Knight figures were all lifeless and gimmicky. They didn't even seem like they'd be fun for kids, let alone adult collectors and Batman fans. On a trip to a store looking for decorations for a table I was decorating for a charity event, I happened across this Batmobile and Batman set. The point of the event was to decorate tables based on recent movies so I jumped at the chance to decorate a table inspired by the Dark Knight Rises,thus I needed a nice Tumbler Batmobile for the table. This is what I found, and here are my thoughts:

The Facts:
Articulation: Batman has a swivel neck, swivel shoulders, and swivel thighs.
Accessories: None, unless you count the Batmobile as an accessory.

The Positives:

*If you're looking at purchasing this toy for a child, you'll be pleased by how solid it is. This feels like the kind of toy that a kid could drop, play with outside, roll down the stairs, and crash into other toy vehicles without breaking. It seems quite sturdy, as the Tumbler should be.

*The included Batman figure, while not super poseable, has a really nice, detailed sculpt and a permanently attached cloth cape. He isn't a bad figure and fits nicely in the Batmobile.

The Negatives:

*The paint work on the Tumbler Batmobile is pretty minimal. There are a few more details which I wish were painted, as overall this is just molded in black plastic with a little bit of gold paint.

Overall: For adult collectors wanting to drop lots of money on Batmobiles, there are better options from Hot Wheels or Hot Toys, but for kids, this is not a bad option. It worked great for my display and is a fun little model to pick up and mess around with every now and then. The fact that you get the Batmobile and a Batman to drive it makes this an excellent gift idea for any child who loves Batman.an.

Bendaroos are essentially pipe cleaners coated in the world's stickiest wax, so they pick up every bit of fuzz, dust, hair, fur, crumbs, etc AND leave a gross sticky residue behind on everything they come in contact with.  If they happen to get dropped on carpet (and possibly stepped on), you will need the fire department to remove it from your shag. I also gave it time to \\"power on\\". Nothing helped or worked. Not that I was going to keep that hunk of junk I was just curious. I immediately sent a frustrated email to Amazon/Yagazoon about the sorry state of the Mr Robot and my son and my disappointment. I was relieved to find that Yagazoon replied back within the hour letting me know that hey had actually had a handful of these complaints and that they had purchased the Mr Robot and had it sent directly from the manufacturer to their customers. Basically letting me know that it wasn't them that had sent the shoddy toy. I did think it was nice though because when they offered me two choices 1) I could re-order with them but they would not be able to guarantee that I wouldn't receive another toy in the same condition. I was glad to have that information and then allowed to make a decision with that knowledge. I found that very forth coming of Yagazoon. My other choice was 2) That I could return the item to Amazon for a full refund and that Yagazoon would also provide a $30 credit to anything at their store via Amazon. I took the second offer which I though was very generous.
I waited until Mr Robot was being sold by another seller and once it was I purchased through them. The toy came in a box that looked exactly the same so I had no expectations of it working. review_headline: Needs a modification...get out your Dremel
review_body:

Coming from micro copters like the V911, the greater inertia makes this puppy less nimble, and the oversized flybar exacerbates the issue but always fighting the controls. product_title: VTech Switch & Go Dinos - Attila the Ankylosaurus Dinosaur
review_headline: Fun with VTech's New Switch & Go Dinos
review_body:
Have you heard of the new VTech Switch & Go Dinos? \\"Switch & Go Dinos(tm) offer an exciting play experience by fusing easy transformations with cutting-edge electronics. Boys will love the unique animations and roaring sound effects that bring the toys to life. With their awesome personalities and fierce designs, they're dino switchin', racing fun!\\"

Currently there are four starter Dinos available for purchase on VTechkids.com: Sliver the T-Rex, T-Don the Pteranodon, Tonn the Stegasaurus and Horns the Triceratops - and VTech has just added three new dinos to the collection. I recently had the opportunity to review two of them with my boys. We received both Brok the Brachiosaurus and Attila the Ankylosaurus, which are two of the newest dinos in the collection.

What I love about VTech's new Switch & Go Dinos, is that they combine two of my boy's favorite things - dinosaurs and vehicles. The Dinos can morph into a vehicle and then back into a dinosaur again. My little guy is five years old and had absolutely no trouble switching the toy back and forth between the vehicle and the dinosaur - at all. We've had similar toys in the past that were almost impossible to transform and it's so frustrating for both the kids and myself when they have toys that they can't use the way they're meant to be used. Not the case with the Switch & Go Dinos, though!

You know me, I'm always on the lookout for toys that will get my boys thinking (it's all about the brain power, folks) and keep them entertained at the same time. This toy is definitley the best of both worlds. The gruesome twosome have been playing with their new Switch & Go Dinos almost non stop since they arrived last week. They are geared for children ages 3 to 8 years old, which is perfect since my boys are 5 and 8!

review_body: I purchased the 9116 as a step up from the co-axial easy to fly Syma S032G.  It definitely is a step-up... but very fun to fly.  There are a few things that I don't like; first, the throttle takes a lot of coaxing to get it to run, second the manual is useless, third the copter fly's leaning to the right and fourth the charger fails to recharge the battery.  Some reviews said the battery doesn't last long.  Well I don't think that it is the battery, but the charger.  After about 10 recharges the charger will not charge the battery at all.  I switched over to my ElectriFly Triton (which is not my preference for a charger, but it's the one I have) and its charging just fine and the run time is a little longer.  The battery's balance charge connector is not compatible with the Electricfly Equinox (I am looking for an adapter cable) so I am charging through the power connector for now.  I think the throttle issue is the copter has an automatic shutoff if it is out-of-balance.  So when you get it spinning initially you have to just re-advance the throttle to keep it running. I shifted the battery and connectors to the left and that has help with the leaning problem.  I moved most of the furniture out of my family room to fly indoors, but the 15 X 20 feet space is very tight for hover training. I can't wait to fly outdoors...  All-in-all, this is a very durable machine that is a lot of fun for the money.  Just don't start with this one.

product_title: 20Q (Colors May Vary)
review_body:
Not Smarter and only Spooky that they would put out such a lame new version of a fine classic game.
My original, several year old 20Q game has finally worn out after hundreds of hours of use. I would play it most every night for a 1/2 hour or so to put me to sleep (weird I know). The buttons finally gave out.
So, since it was so successful in putting me to sleep, I wanted to get a new one, thinking it would have improved logic.
I never understood the reasoning of the original, and this is worse, asking questions like: \\"Does it weigh more than a duck\\"?, and later asking: \\"Does it weigh more than a pound of butter\\"? Or asking \\"is it small\\"? How do we define small? Does a duck weigh more than a pound of butter? I imagine some do, some don't. Then the crazy questions it always asks, like: \\"Do most people use this daily\\"? How can we define use for something like a cloud or paint? Supposedly you win if you pick an item which the game can't correctly identify. However, it always seemed more of a challenge to pick something which the game could identify.
The new version is so oddly laid out. The buttons around the edge are poorly marked, all run together so you need to be careful what you push, and are not always useful. Your choices are Yes, No, Sometimes, Rarely, Skip, and Undo. There is no Unknown button like the original. It often thinks it has the answer by Q 14 or so, and wastes a question with a wrong answer. It also won't go to 25 Q like the original if it misses by 20. I think it's right about 20% of the time, even with easy objects. The original was right at least twice as often. It doesn't always tell you what question number you are at and suddenly it starts giving random wrong answers. Dumb logic! I was expecting this new spooky version to have better logic, but it is totally illogical. Maybe they want the kids to think they are smarter than a computer? And did I mention that it burns through batteries? Too many lights around a hard-to-readscreen.
