product_title: Underwater, 1000-Pieces Augmented Reality Puzzle
review_headline: (4.5 stars) Life is the bubbles....Under the sea
review_body: The gorgeous undersea motif is what drew me to the puzzle and not the augmented reality app that is only available for iPhone and iPad owners, neither of which I own. I like a good challenge and at 1,000 pieces with such a difficult design featuring much sea life, I certainly got that! The pieces are thick, well-made, and while there's still glare, it's reduced so it's less of a distraction than most other puzzles unless the light is directly overhead. They interlock well and I had no trouble fitting the pieces into their proper spots. Unfortunately there were two bent pieces included in my box, one not so bad but the other I'm worried will break in time, even if I don't plan on re-working the puzzle that often. Although out of 1000 pieces (plus five duplicates), that's not a bad ratio. The biggest problem I had was with the box, while well-made, the design is blocked by a hand holding a phone and the words \\"video-animation\\" in the lower left hand corner and a bit in the lower right hand area as well. While I prefer to work a puzzle mostly without looking at the box, at least at first, after a while I need some hints and help. I had to squint into the phone to see what that corner looked like. Also, I think the design could have covered more of the box than it did, a lot of wasted space was taken up. Still, the colors are vibrant and crisp and most of the pieces stick together very well. After completion I was able to pick up the puzzle on one side, fully expecting it to totally fall apart, lifting it totally up and only one piece fell out. Incredible. I had a bit more trouble taking it apart and accidentally peeled up part of the picture on one piece which I fixed using a glue stick, so I'd recommend being very careful dismantling the puzzle. Overall, I'm very happy with my first experience with Ravensburger and would definitely buy from them in the future.

product_title: E-flite Blade mCX2 RTF
review_headline: Junk, Not Stable Or Easy To Fly At All!
review_body:
I know a lot of fan boys say this is fun and easy to fly, that it will hover in place endlessly and you can land it in a tea cup but they are LYING! This is not a high priced precision made model with micro processor controls and a GPS, it's made of loose fitting inexpensive plastic parts. It's a bit more controllable than the old 2 ch. models that couldn't steer since you can make it go forward and back, left and right and you couldn't do that with one before but it's still not stable enough to fly indoors unless it's in a really big room where you can keep from crashing into the walls and get out of the way when it tries to hit you in the head. They claim it can hover in place and has a gyro to stabilize it with the tail rotor but there's no tail rotor and I don't think there's any gyro either. The only one I know of that can actually hover is the much more expensive Parrot AR Drone. Mine tends to take off and veer to the left or right most of the time. It will only go up and hover for a second or 2 some of the time but otherwise you never know where it's going to go and it tends to take off to the left or right. Since it's not very stable I had to fly it outside and if I use the biggest part of the yard it won't get lost over the fence but that's about the best it can do and it always heads for the nearest tree. It is durable and well made though (except for the flimsy plastic frame). In all the times it's crashed so far nothing has broken. Maybe someday they will make one that is really stable enough to fly indoors with precision but this isn't it even though there are a lot of fake videos on Youtube showing them being flown with precision indoors. product_title: Nirvana Radio Controlled Model Sailboat, Red
review_headline: 2007 NIRVANA II still sailing perfectly - a great value!
review_body:
Upon retirement, and after watching many RC models sailing in Manhattan's Central Park (Conservatory Water) over the years, and having once painstakingly built a planked 30\\" sailing model of a Dragon, I started looking at 1-meter long RC models that I could purchase and sail, planked or whatever. But most seemed to start around $400 to $500 to start, and often running quite a bit higher. That, plus safe shipping issues nagged at me. Also, I didn't know myself well enough to know how much I would LOVE sailing my boat, you know, was it just a passing fancy, and if so, should I put a lot of money on a boat up front?

Solution? I ended up buying the Megatech NIRVANA II for about $211 including S&H in 2007. It seemed that I could \\"eat\\" the $200 if I didn't like sailing it. But in any event, I couldn't have made a better choice for my needs. It took me about 4 hours to put it together, because I went really slowly and carefully. Like they say, the hull is one integral part, so most of the work is rigging the mast and sails, main and jib sheets. I've ended up sailing it about 3 to 4 times each spring through summer season for five years. I use rechargeable batteries for the hand controller, and charge them once each season. I love the boat. I even sailed it once on the 1.2 mile wide Hudson River in gusty winds, and it never capsized. In fact, it's never capsized, and never taken on more than about 3 tablespoons of water in the small aft controller compartment even though it has frequently been knocked down briefly by small gusts. I now sail it on a reservoir and have sailed it out maybe 500'-700' from shore without losing control. It tacks nicely into the wind, and loves to reach. One has rudder control, and simultaneous control over the jib sheet and main sheet, so that both go out, or come back in, together. Good luck!

product_title: Slushy Magic Slush Cup
review_body:
I bought 3 Slushy Magics from Walmart and then read reviews here on Amazon. I was concerned what I'd get. We used them and are confused why some are having problems with them. It seems like the ones that were bought at Walmart got good reviews, lol. I can only tell you what we do to make them work well. Remember, these are not going to be rock hard icees you get at Ritas or someplace. These are done at home so they are thick but will have some liquid in it as well at times. It works fine for kids. You don't get a ton of slushy but it's enough for kids and a nice treat.

Make sure the drink you choose is COLD, not cool, and not make fresh from the tap. If you just made a pitcher of lemonade, pour out some in small cups and set them in the fridge as those will get cold faster. Toss an ice cube in it to get it colder if you want, just take the cube out before you make your slughy. But the drinks MUST be COLD first.

When you open the box, there is a paper in there telling you that there will be condensation in the ice cube bag, which we had, and was not leaking! It's salt and water in the cubes. Has never leaked. I'm wondering if the condensation was mistaken for leaking which is why they now add the paper to explain that they're not leaking.

Put the cubes in flat on top of each other.

Pour your drink to the fill line. I pour slowly directly on the cubes. We've used pink and strawberry lemonade and apple juice. All worked and tasted well.

We found that you ust keep your finger over the hole and little or no nails works better as long nails get in the way and it will leak a bit through the hole. It has never leaked through the lid on any 3 we own or in all the times we've used them.

We shake side to side with the cup on its side. I've done one in one hand and one in the other at the same time.

We found that the harder you shake the faster it slushes up. I can shake harder than the kids so it seems to slush faster for me.

It takes us about 3 minutes to shake. It's not as long as it sounds. I shake, the kids enjoy watching the time tick down and letting me know each minute that passes by. Sometimes it takes shorter if the drink is even colder. If my pitcher of lemonade is full it won't be as cold. If there's not much left the lemonade will be a bit colder so it can take 2-3 mintues to shake. Time flies!

When time is up, I take out the 3 cubes, shake the slush off and back into the cup and then rinse them immediately to go back into the freezer. Pop in their straw/spoon and they go watch a movie! Granted, they don't get a full cup like the picture on the box shows. You don't get much because the 3 big cubes take up space but it's enough for kids for a summer treat. We take out the cubes before eating so the kids don't accidently punture the cubes by jabbing at their drinks.

We have tried a lemon/lime pop. We keep water, pop, canned teas in a mini fridge which is kept much colder than the big fridge. When using the pop so very cold to start it took literally seconds to slush up and it slushed up really firm! My kids couldn't even get the timer to the first minute when they were done. So the colder the drink the better. You could pour some of a drink into a big measuring cup and set it in the freezer for a bit first and then add it to your drink.

You cannot put these in the dishwasher or microwave. We rinse them during the day and I hand wash them at night for the next day. My triplets each have their own so I don't worry about germs.

In the end, these work great! They are not rock hard icees if that's what you're expecting. They're slushy, sometimes with some liquid in the bottom, but are a great and fun treat for kids. If you're an adult I'm sure there's a better way to get what you want. But what I listed works for us and is quick and easy and fun for my 7 year olds!

I'm buying one for my granddaughter when she comes for her birthday in a few weeks!daughter when she comes for her birthday in a few weeks!

product_title: Spy Net: Secret Mission Video Watch
review_body: Here's the deal with this watch and I hope it helps anyone thinking about buying it in the future. After reading all the negative reviews I almost didn't buy this thing. I bought both styles the one with and without night IR vision. But I wanted it for work, and the price was worth the risk. This is a DVR camcorder, and parents need to remember that. Also no toy is kid proof. When I got a wind up tractor as a kid for my 4Th B-day, my dad told me. \\"Wnd it up to tight and you'll break it\\". This is a real digital recorder, And if Johnny is wrestling the bad guy to the ground and his wrist slams into the coffee table, that's the end of the watch. Just as it would be for your cell phone, and most any other electronic device. Yes it's a toy, but just like an old wind up tractor it has intricate parts inside. I use mine to see up under dashboards and for bolts dropped into an engine compartment. It seized up on me when I took it off the charger (PC) and I was not happy, no watch, no video, nothing, I didn't bang it or anything, just took it off the charger. But there's a reset button on the back and it hasn't happened since. About the snake cam, The snake cam does not have it's own light source. And even if you buy the watch with IR night vision the Snake cam doesn't have IR on it's own.  Recording video with this uses up a lot of juice. It stays charged about 3 days on stand by (as a watch only). But I keep it on the charger as much as posible, when I need it, I it need it to work so one stays on the charger at all times. You can record steady for about an hour. But it tells you to put it on the charger when the battery is getting low.  When you buy this, inside the package is an external battery pack that takes 4 AAA batteries. It plugs into the back of the watch. When at work and not in use I leave it hooked up to this as a portable charging unit. A handy Father could solder longer wires to this battery pack and have it in a pocket or put a velcrow band on it to be wornon the bicep. This would give you extended play time. Just an after thought, for when the 30 day warentee runs out. I gave it 4 stars mainly because of battery life, tha band could be better. Hope this was helpful.

product_title: Ravensburger Snail's Pace Race - Children's Game
review_body:

At the beginning of the game each player predicts which color snail is going to be the fastest and which is going to be the slowest. Then the players take turns rolling the dice and moving the snails along the board until all of the snails have crossed the finish line. When this is done, you can see if anyone guessed the fastest and slowest snail right. Pretty simple.

It is great for color recognition, 1 to 1 correspondence, introducing the idea of predictions, taking turns, etc. We really like it.

product_title: LeapFrog LeapPad2 Explorer Kids' Learning Tablet or Bundle
review_headline: Excellent Kids' Tablet with High Educational Value
review_body:
LeapFrog sent their new LeapFrog LeapPad2 Explorer for my family to review. We checked out some of the differences between this device and the original LeapPad and tested its functions and apps. If you are wondering whether to get a LeapPad2, just let your kids use your iPad, or skip tablets for kids altogether, here's our take:

My educational philosophy is that outdoor activity and play is key for very young children. Despite being high-tech in my professional life, the early childhood teaching techniques I advocate are decidedly Pre-Industrial. Yet there are places where a thoughtful use of technology can enhance learning.

Initial studies show that using a tablet can boost literacy scores in Kindergarteners and help children on the Autism spectrum improve their communication skills. The idea that tablets can help reluctant learners or provide a reliable and safe learning interaction for children makes a lot of sense.

What doesn't make sense to a lot of families, however, is handing a $400 device over to a young child, even with a super-rugged cover. Also problematic is sharing a device the adults need for work and communication with a kid who is just beginning to grasp the concept of taking turns. Another concern is an Internet connection that lets your kids veg out on the entertainment equivalent of junkfood, see inappropriate content, or \\"accidentally\\" rack up bills buying game points or new apps.

The LeapFrog LeapPad2 Explorer restores parental control to the equation. To download apps, the LeapPad must be connected to the computer. All the apps and games are created by LeapFrog, a company that is practically synonymous with educational tech toys. And the LeapPad 2 is even more durable than its predecessor so your three year old can hog it without you worrying about getting it back destroyed...or not at all.

Here's what you get with the LeapPad 2. I've highlighted the main differences between the original LeapFrog LeapPad and the LeapPad 2:

* LeapPad2 Explorer Learning Tablet (4GB Memory, double the original)
* 2 Built-in Cameras & Video Recorders (the LeapPad 2 has a front and back camera; the original has only one camera in back)
* Extended battery life (about 1 additional hour)
* Faster processor (550 MHz, compared to 393 MHz on the original)
* LeapFrog Learning Songs App (5 Songs Included)
* Pet Pad Writing App
* Cartoon Creativity App
* Art Studio App
* Free App Download
* USB Cable

There is also a recharger available separately for purchase, a welcome change to the original since these devices are total battery drainers.

Just about the only drawback to the LeapPad 2 is the cost of cartridges and apps. To someone of my generation, this is not a deal-breaker. Younger parents, used to cheap and free apps on smart phones, might balk, however, at the recurring cost of purchasing additional games. Plus, the cartridges can be traded or resold.

The games available on the LeapPad is what truly distinguishes it from the pack, however. Although there are definitely winners out there, a lot of free and cheap apps for smart phones and adult tablets are hastily thrown together and provide little educational value. With LeapFrog, parents know they are getting appropriate and pedagogically correct content for their kids.

Plus, some of the games \\"auto-level\\", adjusting the difficulty to challenge each child. A few games even allow parents to customize the device with math sets and spelling lists from school.

As with adult tablets, kids can play LeapPad games using the stylus, the touch screen, and the built-in motion sensor.

Kids' interests are often character-driven and so my daughter's favorite is the LeapFrog LeapPad Ultra eBook Adventure Builder: Disney Fairies: Tink's Midnight Tea Party: in this game, she can read the story at three differentlevels, make choices that affect the story, and play games. There are different modes (read the book to me, read the page to me, and read it myself). You can also record yourself reading the book, a great option for parents and grandparents who live far away.

The ever popular Pet Pad app comes with the LeapPad and allows kids to practice writing while playing with their virtual pet.

My kids are also big fans of the Disney Pixar Brave Cartridge, a first-person adventure game in which the player moves Merida to solve science puzzles. The variety of different science activities (learning about life cycles, experimenting with physics) is very engaging.

My personal favorite is the LeapPad Creativity App: Disney Animation Artist: Mickey and Friends. I really enjoy trying to draw Mickey and his buddies with the stylus and think this is a great game for future artists and Disney fans of all ages.

The addition of Little Pim language videos is the start of a beautiful relationship and I am hoping the two companies will develop some interactive language learning content.

The bottom line is that you will get an excellent learning tool with plenty of high quality content if you are willing to invest in apps and cartridges.

As stated above, we received this tablet from LeapFrog for review. All opinions are my own.

product_title: Radio Flyer Classic Red 10" Tricycle with Push Handle
review_headline: as much fun for grandpa as for the grandkids!
review_body: We purchased this trike just prior to a visit with the grandkids, It arrived on time (actually, two days early)and in good shape. The bike has a cream and red paint job and looks new-vintage. It was easy to put together. We all loved the look (including the parents). I was glad to find a tricycle built from metal instead of plastics as my grandson is quite the little demolisher. Grandpa took him for a ride atleast 5 times each day that we were there. Although very tall for his age, our 20mo. could not quite keep his feet on the pedals when in motion but had no problems keeping his feet up during the ride. He did steer a lot and sometimes cranked the wheel to the left (out of the blue) making us roar with laughter. A light push down on the bar corrected the movement quite easily. We chose this trike over the ones with the adult steering simply due to the free ratcheting pedals on that other style. We wanted the kids to be able to learn to ride as normal, with the safety of an adult near the helper bar. The other style is free wheeling; meaning if the child goes down a hill (even a slight grade), the bike takes off with no means of controlling the speed. They cannot pedal backwards in that type, or put pressure on the pedals to slow down the speed. I didn't want our grandkids rolling into the street at a fast speed with no means of stopping. This is just my opinion and a major reason we chose this particular trike. All in all, we feel we made a great choice and this radio flyer will be in use for a long time then passed down to the next child when out grown, rather than thrown in the trash when worn out.

product_title: Doctor Who Dalek Projector Alarm Clock - Digital Timer with Dr. Who Sound Effects
review_headline: It was nice while it lasted.
review_body:
I got this alarm clock a few days ago and I have to say I really liked it.

The visual details are great. The design is just like the new Daleks from the new Doctor's series. You have the right larger base, the more prominent band around the arms, and the yellow for the eye stalk as well. The base is dotted with the orbs, even the clock is there!

Durability wise it's a bit on the light side and feels a bit flimsy, especially the arms which almost feel like they are meant to come off and might any second.

As a alarm clock it works great. The buttons are concealed in the orbs on the base and it projects the time on the cealing when you press down on the Dalek. There are three alarm sounds plus the classic shout of \\"exterminate\\" if after 50 years of life with The Doctor that doesnot get you moving, nothing will. product_title: Hasbro Furby
review_headline: Multiple Personalities but a Successful Reboot!
review_body:
I am an owner of one of the original Furbys so I pulled it out (a couple of them actually) to give a good comparison.

A quick crash course in Furby: Furbys are interactive robotic pets with various modes of interaction to which they respond, Furbys are loud and have no off switch (You have been warned!!!) but will go to sleep if you leave them alone for a bit. To wake them simply tilt them. Furbys begin to speak in \\"furbish\\" which is their own simplistic language. As time goes on they learn English one word at a time replacing their own furbish vocabulary. These take 4 double-A batteries which are not included and have 9 methods of interaction: Shake Furby, tilt Furby, feed Furby (with your finger or a free I-pod app), pet Furby, tickle Furby, talk to Furby, pull Furbys tail, introduce two furbys to each other, and play music for Furby.

First the original gen furbys had specific differences: stripe mane or poof with tail, pitch of voice, names, eye color, etc. The new gen Furbys come in different colors but there are no real differences between them... that is until playtime starts.

How you play with Furby will change it's complete personality including the tone of it's voice and it's LED eye shape. The personalities have a huge range from a \\"tough guy\\" Furby to a \\"Valley girl\\" type, and everything in between. The personality is triggered by how you treat them, for example you can overfeed Furby and I've found that when I do so he always changes into the tough guy mode soon after, if I pet my Furby a lot it changes to a sweet and cuddly personality, and so on. Changes are very obvious, it will wiggle, close it's eyes and emit a seizure-inducing series of flashing lights while exclaiming \\"Me change!\\". When it opens it's eyes it's a whole new Furby. It shifts personality very quickly at first but seems to shift less frequently as time goes on.

So how good is it? Well it's fun! It was fun then and is arguably better now.
Some of the improvements include the new LED eyes which are very expressive and highly visible, new animatronic animations that allow it to stretch scrunch or wobble (the original could tilt back and forth only), an expanded vocabulary of furbish terms (original furbish dictionaries will still work for most basic words as those have not changed), and new interactivity such as dancing to music, and working with the I-phone app.

The materials are also very soft and Furby is surprisingly sturdy unless you're really rough with her. I think she could stand up to most heavy play just remember that electronic toys DO NO LIKE WATER. Water = dead Furby.

I would recommend for most ages as it would be very useful as a \\"pet\\" for kids, or to help develop skills in young children for translating from other languages. Also makes a good desk toy for adults as long as you're okay with the level of noise. Makes a good gift for those who grew up with one of the originals, as it has that nice level of nostalgia about it. :) It's an A+ toy and not too pricey at retail (do some research on price before you buy)>Some of the improvements include the new LED eyes which are very expressive and highly visible, new animatronic animations that allow it to stretch scrunch or wobble (the original could tilt back and forth only), an expanded vocabulary of furbish terms (original furbish dictionaries will still work for most basic words as those have not changed), and new interactivity such as dancing to music, and working with the I-phone app.

That makes them more challenging for my four and six year old, but still robust enough that my three year old doesn't ruin them like he has some other, flimsy puzzles. The edges and tabs haven't broken or peeled in the slightest.

You can see by the stats how big these are, almost 2 foot by 3 foot, so they really are floor-puzzles, like they say. The colors are exceptionally vivid and haven't faded or worn off at all. As advertised, the pieces fit together crisply - thick enough and precise enough that they don't separate like some of our other thinner, flimsy floor puzzles. Despite the differences in thickness and texture, both puzzles seem equally sturdy. This puzzle has a normal, square shape, and my three year old puts it together all by himself.

Bottom line, from now on I won't be buying anything but Ravensburger floor puzzles for my kids. product_title: Fisher-Price Laugh and Learn Stride-to-Ride Puppy
review_headline: This toy stands the test of time - 1.5 years and going
review_body:
(See update for long term impressions)
This toy doesn't move well on either carpet or hard surfaces. The wheels are small, cheap, and don't rotate well. They also don't have any tread so the toy just slides instead of rolling.

The other major problem is the locking mechanism for the seat that allows it to switch positions. The mechanism requires large hands so a small toddler can't do it. The build quality of the mechanism is very poor because it doesn't securely lock the seat - there is a tremendous amount of \\"play\\" in each position and it just doesn't feel durable.

On the positive side, the plastic shapes have been fun for my 2.5 year old to play with and stick into the puppy's belly or into its mouth. She can reach in on the other side of the belly to pull the shapes out.

The music is fun and pleasant (not annoying to parents) and the sound quality is actually very impressive with good intelligibility. There are 3 buttons in addition to the nose button which all light up and are easy to press.

Overall, I would say this puppy is fun to interact with but the construction quality is poor. The distinguishing feature of this toy is the ability to ride or push it. Unfortunately, this feature doesn't work well. So what you are left with is a pretty bulky stationary toy. If you have plenty of room in your house, this may not be a big deal. But for most people, a more compact interactive toy would be preferable.

UPDATE: I am upgrading this toy to 4 stars because despite the lousy wheels, my 10-month-old who is on the verge of walking has been having fun pushing it around the house. It works better than I thought it would as a \\"walker\\" and my baby uses it much more than I expected. The music is also motion activated so the dog \\"sings\\" and shakes its head while being pushed. There have been no issues with durability to date.

UPDATE May 2014: After 1.5 years of this toy, my kids (2 and 4 years old) still enjoy playing with it and pushing it all over the place. This is somewhat amazing since they usually get bored of a toy (or break it) in no time. Despite my concerns about the build quality, nothing has broken on this toy and it is in near perfect condition. review_headline: Great for kids, time-consuming for moms
review_body:
My daughter LOVES this set. It has lots of cookie presses and we ultimately have a great time together baking.

I took note of previous reviews before buying... this is not a terrible toy. It's just a little messy and involves a lot of parental involvement and clean-up. If you go into the purchase expecting that this is going to be a family activity, you'll be much less impatient and disappointed when you get to the making cookies part.

I made my own sugar cookie dough. It has to be cold and firm. The more we handled the dough, the warmer it became and thus started sticking in the molds. I followed advice from others. Use lots of flour to dust the molds before each use. Spray things with cooking spray (Pam or Baker's Joy). Pop the molded cookies into the freezer for a couple of minutes before baking and they hold their shapes much better.

If you're buying for older kids who are completely self-sufficient, then you should be able to hand over the box, set the oven and let them go to it. If you're buying for a little one, know this is an activity you're going to be very involved with.

product_title: Forceball Futuristic Hockey / Lacrosse Card Game
review_body:
Kickstarter, for those of you who don't know, is a web based company that lets you donate money to people that want to do something, but don't have the money to do it on their own. Forceball started there, and was fully funded because people thought the game would be fun just by reading about it. You can no longer donate to the Kickstarter campaign, but now you can buy it. Independent companies like this one need our support to keep coming up with new and fun ideas. Big corporations are only interested in giving you the same thing that they have before because it makes money. How long has Monopoly been around? How many versions are there? How different is the latest version from the first one you played as a kid? That one I'll answer. Not very much. Indy companies work hard to come up with new and incredible games, and this is easily one of the best I've seen in a while.

Why would you care about indy companies like this one? Forceball is a why. The setting is a little silly, hockey with lasers, and the art could be better, but the game play is great (That's why we buy games right?). 55 cards are all you get, and all you need. The game is set up into 3 periods, which end when the empties and you try to draw a card. So, the number of cards ties to the length of the game. It's quick to play, and a lot of fun.

I said that it has a high educational value because it is a great way to teach tactics. If you try to win every fight, and go all out to win them all, you could fall short and let the advantage to the other team.

Overall, it's a lot of fun to play, and for the price, can't be beaten.

product_title: Crayon Rubbings
review_headline: Fun and entertaining for preschool-age kids
review_body:
When I was little, I loved to draw. However, I didn't always know what to draw. I'm sure my parents and grandparents got tired of me asking them for creative ideas.

Now that I'm a parent, I too have been asked the question, \\"Mommy, what should I color?\\" After you've been asked this about 100 times, you start to run out of ideas. That's why I love this this Crayon Rubbings set from Creativity for Kids. Each kit comes with 20 pre-drawn coloring pages that are ready to use. The set also comes with 20 blank coloring pages in case your child wants to draw his own masterpiece.

Additionally, the set comes with a box of 15 Faber-Castell crayons. The crayons are short and somewhat stubby, so they are the perfect size for small hands to hold. And unlike some crayons we already owned, the Faber-Castell crayons are not waxy, so the color goes on smoothly and evenly the first time. This is great for my son because he doesn't have to press hard to get a bright color and the crayons don't break. Another great feature is that these crayons don't have the traditional paper wrapping around them, so my son doesn't have to stop his art project to ask me to peel away paper to keep using the crayon.

One thing I especially liked about this set was the pre-made coloring station. The coloring pages fit neatly into a plastic stand so his drawings stayed in place. There were little indentations at the top of the station to display the crayons, so he could easily pick and choose the colors he wanted without making a mess all over the kitchen table.

For the rubbing portion of this kit, there were five different textured plates to choose from including stars, waves, dots, swirls and scales. The plates were a little on the thin side, but they functioned well so it didn't really matter.

To make a rubbed picture, all you have to do is select a plate, set it in the center of the drawing station and place a coloring sheet on top. Next, you rub acrayon over the plate and paper and voila! You have a fun, textured image!

After the main drawing is complete, kids can use one of the eight markers included to outline their image, or add additional details. After your little artist is done creating a master piece, you can display their work in one of two self-adhesive picture frames that come in each set.

As a parent I really enjoyed the creativity this crayon rubbing station offered. It's a simple concept that provides hours of entertainment. It can be used in so many unique ways that it really held my son's attention because he didn't have to do the same thing over and over.

review_body: The Aston Martin brand is all about craftsmanship and attention to detail.  I think that fact sets high expectations for a die-cast bearing the name.  Considering the scale and modest price, I'm happy to say I wasn't disappointed.  The doors and hood open revealing a reasonable level of detail and the interior is all black with paint or decal instrument gauge cluster.  I think they attempt to emulate \\"Carbon Black\\" editions of the real V12 Vantage.  Fit on the left-hand door could be a bit better.  I noticed the same small misalignment on photos of  different colored models.  Don't expect the same precision as larger more expensive reproductions and you'll be happy.  The one I purchased was made by Motormax.

product_title: Nerf Nstrike Elite Hail-Fire Blaster
review_body:
We have yet to go wrong with a Nerf blaster. The Hail-Fire is the Quantity over Quality model: it's not the most accurate or the longest-ranged Nerf gun (although it's certainly accurate and powerful *enough*), but it has a huge magazine capacity.

The mechanism for advancing to the next clip works nicely, with a solid-feeling handle. Holding the gun with one hand on the top handle instead of supporting the barrel from beneath is a little awkward at first, but you get used to it quickly, and the unique hybrid pump/ bolt action is pretty cool.

I'm going to list the negatives, which are fairly minor. Aside from these few issues, this is another example of a great toy gun from our pals at Nerf.

* Initial assembly of the gun is slightly tricky. It takes a fair amount of force to fit the parts together, which took awhile because I was afraid of breaking it. Thankfully, once it's together, there's no need to take it apart again.

* Due to the large round clip holder, the gun is very wide and kind of awkward to store.

* Although the gun holds 8 clips and the box lists the maximum ammo capacity of 144 darts, only four 6-dart clips are included (along with 24 darts). So unless you already have a bunch of clips and darts handy, you'll be very tempted to spend more money to fill this up. To maximize it, you'll need to buy 8 18-shot clips, which will set you back nearly a hundred simoleons. On the lower end, they do sell a [[ASIN:B0083TXZ6G N-Strike Elite Hail-Fire Mission Kit]] that gives you 4 more 6-dart clips for around fifteen bucks. (In addition, the gun looks a little goofy with only 4 clips attached and all that empty space, but nobody's going to notice that while you're pumping 24 darts into them. ;) )

* Build quality issues: Although my gun has been problem-free, I notice that some other reviewers have reported issues with the motor trigger mechanism. Be aware that you may need to attempt a fix or returnthe gun for a replacement.

* Batteries! Not a huge deal, but be aware that some excellent spring-loaded Nerf guns are available (notably, my personal favorite, the [[ASIN:B0083TXWXC N-Strike Elite Retaliator Blaster]]).

product_title: Fisher-Price Little People Disney Princess Songs Palace
review_body: My hubby and I bought this palace, the additional princess dolls (set of 6 sold at Target) and the additional sets with the princes (sea carriage with Ariel and Eric is adorable!) all for our 2 year olds birthday. We opened the palace and she has not stopped playing with it since. This has become a toy that gets played with every single day. Our 5 year old loves it, too! This castle is a HUGE hit in our house. It has so many cute phrases and song clips from each of the princess movies. When you place the dolls on the center circle of the dance floor, each princess introduces herself, says a few character phrases and then sings a song clip from her movie. Our girls adore this feature. Our two year old claps in excitement and dances along with the songs. It's so cute. The palace also encourages the girls to be creative and use their imagination while playing. It came in a few easy to screw in and snap together pieces. You will need a small Phillips head screw driver to assemble some of it. Nothing major. No defects with our pieces. It took us about 10 mins to assemble, including peeling the stickers off the sheet and placing them on the pieces. This is a classically sturdy Fisher Price quality toy, it is colorful and fun. Each room or accessory has a sticker that incorporates parts of the Disney Princess movies. Example, Rapunzel's tower has the floating lanterns and a baby Pascal (her chameleon) painted on the wall. Another room is about Cinderella, the bedroom has the three good fairies from Sleeping Beauty. Our girls totally love the castle and all the dolls that we purchased to go with it. Their little imaginations run wild making up stories about being invited to the ball etc. Seeing our little ones happy makes us happy parents. No complaints from this family. If your little one(s) adore Disney Princess the way ours do, our advice is: buy this castle! :-)

product_title: Learning Resources New Sprouts Cure It! My Very Own Doctor Set
review_body: As a childcare provider, I've owned many doctor kits in the past 25 years and the New Sprouts Cure It! My Very Own Doctor Kit from Learning Resources is superior to all the others. Designed for little hands ages two and up, these durable pieces hold up through constant pretend play. My preschoolers found no flaws in the design and no way to destroy the pieces. The doctor bag is a soft bag that stands up on its own, has a wonderful velcro closure, and easy to grip handles. All the pieces fit easily inside and even my two year olds can clean up it quickly. It has \\"cured\\" the kids in my group countless times and is one of their favorite toys. It is so essential that children have role playing toys like this doctor kit, especially since they all visit the doctor often and must sometimes even go to the hospital. Being as curious as Curious George, they are willing to explore the doctor tools and become more comfortable with the \\"real\\" doctor visits. I highly recommend the Learning Resources educational toys! Disclosure: I received this product at no charge in exchange for my honest review.

The pegs stack onto each other as well as peg into two of the foam shapes. The individual puzzles are nice and sturdy.

My only dislike about the toys is that the larger shapes puzzle is very thin and flimsy, which makes picking it up intact to put back away a pain, as the pieces barely stay in. All in all a great toy, though!

review_body: If you have a 1 to 2 year old don't hesitate to buy this. We probably own most of the age appropriate toys (our first child!) and I would say this is the best toy we own for several reasons. It has plenty of activities to keep baby entertained and engaged in a relatively small, compact package. There is a volume control which I appreciate and two modes, one of which is \\"opposites\\".

product_title: Melissa & Doug Folding Princess Castle
review_headline: Great Fun for Your Princess (or Prince!)
review_body:
My daughter received this castle, along with [[ASIN:B001ENH3WU Melissa & Doug Princess Castle Furniture]] for her 6th birthday. She has played with it for at least 30 minutes every day since she received it, and that's saying a lot since she also just started first grade (so she's got nightly homework) and she has a room full of other toys to play with.

Let's be honest, you can hardly beat a castle for a six year old girl. But this one isn't just for show, it's quite playable. My daughter doesn't use Melissa & Doug pieces with it, rather she uses pieces from various miniature Disney playsets ([[ASIN:B000J5NVNY Disney Sleeping Beauty (Aurora) Poseable Figurine Figure Set]], [[ASIN:B000PM1KC0 Disney Princess Favorite Moments 4-Pack Gift set-Styles May Vary]]). The size of the figures and the openings in the castle doors and arches are perfect for these figures.

I'll admit that the furniture doesn't all fit into the castle perfectly, but this fact actually seems to make it more fun for my daughter as she is constantly rearranging the castle and setting it up for various play modes.

My 22-month old also seems to dig the castle and likes to sit in front of it and put various toys in the different rooms. And the castle is sturdy enough that we can let him do it without worry that he'll damage the castle or injure himself.

I was impressed enough when I saw the castle online, but was even more so when I saw that the drawbridge can actually be raised and lowered and there is one room with a sliding door. They're just little things that make this castle even more playable. I also love, love, love that it can fold up so that it takes half as much space when it's not in use or when it needs to be moved.

review_headline: terrible, with lots of small plastic parts
review_body: I'm an adult who has enjoyed slurpees, although it was a very long time ago. I was hoping for a sturdy machine that would be simple to use and put together. I didn't get either of these in this machine. In addition, the recommended ingredients include a soft drink with very high sugar content; you also have to add lots of salt and crushed ice to get it to work. There are so many easily breakable parts that I wouldn't recommend this to anyone under age six. Bad design all around. Use something like a smoothie maker or even a Vita Mix, so you can make something healthy instead.

product_title: InnoTab 3 Plus The Learning Tablet
review_body:
We received the InnoTab2 for review and I was excited to see how this would compare to our other tablets. Though the technology is not the same, this tablet makes a lot of sense for kids, versus a more expensive model.

Cost: The InnoTab 2 costs the same as it's predecessor $79.99.

Durability: This toy will handle a lot more wear and tear than the more expensive tablets. We have already had scratches to screens, drops, more drops and had to replace the charger more than three times. Right now we are waiting for yet another charger to arrive because now the charging unit on one of the devices has been broken. All this stuff ads up to a lot of money and a lot of stress. The InnoTab 2 is more durable and a lot less fragile, and if for some reason they completely wreck it, you won't be out $250 or more!

Educational: They have lots of game apps on their tablet, but only about 40% are educational. I would much rather the children play games that will teach them something and this allows them to practice everything from vocabulary to math. This is also an ebook reader, which is neat because now they are reading more and more books.

I can definitely see spending this money and it being very worthwhile. The rotating camera, expandable memory and so many educational apps, make this a great device for kids.

I have received a VTech InnoTab 2 to facilitate my review.

product_title: LEGO Star Wars 9678 Twin-Pod Cloud Car and Bespin
review_headline: Cloudy with a chance of AWESOME
review_body: The LEGO Star Wars Miniatures line is easily one of the most interesting sublines LEGO has developed, combining rare or unique minifigures with mini-scale ships and a related planet.  The Twin-Pod Cloud Car and Bespin set is one of the best from the line so far, as not only is this a first appearance for the Cloud Car in a miniature scale, but the included Minifigure (Lobot) is all-new and only the second time the character has gotten a minifigure at all.  The Cloud Car is a rather iconic Star Wars vehicle, despite only appearing for a few brief scenes, and this miniature definitely does it justice.  Sturdy and well-designed, the ship is fun to play with and swoosh around, and the included stand makes it great for display alongside the new Lobot figure.  The included Bespin is simple, but effective, and looks great as a backdrop or a Christmas ornament for those planning a Star Wars-themed tree this year.  In my opinion, this set is easily worth the cost and is the best set out of the new subline so far.

product_title: Electronic Labyrinth Family Game
review_body: When I first sat down to play this with my husband, there was a bit of a learning curve. product_title: Power Wheels Dune Racer
review_body:
We bought this for our 7 year old and 2 year old who share the same birthday and weigh 60 and 30 lbs. Shipping took about a week, which was great. We also purchased an extra battery so they could go and go.

We do not live on flat land(sigh)nor dry land(sigh again) and we have a LOT of rocks(very huge sigh). We read the reviews that were available at the time of purchase and watched the youtube videos and were very impressed.

The first day we got it my sons were driving it and went to go up a slight incline. Total power loss. Thought, okay, grabbed the uncharged battery. So told them it had to charge and put it away for the night. I had two VERY sad boys that night because it was their early birthday gift from their dad who was getting ready to go out to sea.

Over the next week or so, no problems with it going up and down the inclines in our yard. It goes over pretty much every nature obstacle and some man made. As noted above, we have wet land (more like soggy yuck that sometimes steals your flip-flops) and it goes through it. It also goes on gravel and over bumps with ease. My 7 year old is in love with this thing.

So imagine my horror when a few days ago the boys are driving up the driveway, a 10-12% grade, on a fully charged battery hot off the plug, and all of a sudden it starts rolling backwards at a very fast speed. I am yelling to step on the gas and my 7 year old is yelling HE IS! They crashed into a tree, which is a good thing, and a bad thing. Good because they stopped before going down over the hill behind them, backwards. Bad because it hit hard! Thank goodness they were not hurt and the buggy only got some scrapes. product_title: Diggin Rigs Power Crane
review_headline: Good for anyone who likes Play Doh
review_body:
I got this for my 6 year old granddaughter because she loves all things Play Doh. I was concerned that the truck would be too young or boyish for her but she took right to it.

The wrecking ball works better if you put a ball of Doh inside it to weigh it down. The Doh has glitter on it, which is a major plus for her, but the black Doh actually looks like pavement because of it. You have forms to make blocks like Lego and they fit together. The forms on the truck will spit out 3 forms, one of which look like steel beams. Even my 11 year old grandson had a good time with it. There's a pizza cutter that comes with it to help make the roads even on the sides and a roller to make it flat. I thought the roller was a little useless because you need a lot of power to flatten Doh unless you've already done so with your hands. A good buy, anyway.

review_body: I received these quickly and in perfect condition. These were great for the fairy land my grandkids and I created. They love play with them every time they come over. These fairies are a perfect size for their fairyland.

review_headline: Alot of fun for Lego Hot Rod fans
review_body: The Racers lego kits are alot of fun.  My 2 young boys like the different Hot Rods they can create.  Generally you can build the Hot Rods shown and/or combine the bricks for a HotRod mashup vehicle and/or combine with other Lego Racer bricks for even more combinations.  As a dad I tend to favor non-licensed Legos because the cost per brick is always alot lower then licensed sets (read: Star Wars, Harry Potter, etc.).  I also feel that the non-licensed sets spark more imaginative play as kids won't be so tied to just \\"build it once\\" so it looks like what they see in the cartoon or movie.  But that's nitpicking.  At the end of the day this Racers set and the others in this series offer a whole lot of fun, a whole lot of rubber tires, and some cool highway sections for the kids to apply stickers so Win, Win, Win.

product_title: Thinkfun Daily Puzzle
review_body:
Oskar van Deventer and Wei-Hwa Huang are two of the best puzzle creators in the world, and this is one of their most approachable creations. Just flip the six smaller, 2-sided tiles to make the month, then the four larger tiles to make the day.

Each tile has holes and black bars, and the surface under the tiles is also black. To make a 5, you might need 2 black bars on the top tile, 2 bars showing through holes on the second tile, and the surface showing through 2 holes.

I have a few thousand puzzles, but this is one of the best on my desk. The logic method to solve a particular month or day can be tricky, but it never takes too long.

Highly recommended.

product_title: Forbidden Island
review_headline: Forbidden Island: A great door opener for cooperative games!
review_body:
First of all, let me say Forbidden Island is the first cooperative board game I have ever played. That said, I enjoy the genre immensely. Don't get me wrong, I love me some competition! But every once and awhile working with other people is great as well.

Forbidden Island is an incredible board game to play and deserves every one of the 5 stars I have given it. It has you on the edge of your seat the entire time as tiles begin to flood around you, some sinking into the abyss as your standing on them! It is a very exciting game and has yet to feel too easy or boring to me and my wife as we play. We have won only twice in our first six times playing it!

The rules are pretty straight forward, but it does take some time to master a basic strategy. At some points it does feel like you are just waiting to get the cards you need, but it is still suspenseful as tiles continue to sink despite your efforts to save the important ones. Each character is fun to play and changes the game every time. For example, I like to choose the Navigator and move other characters around, and my wife likes to be the diver and swim through flooded tiles.

If you are reading about this game and considering buying it, just go ahead and get it already, you will not regret it. Its fast, fun, challenging, as well as extremely rewarding for anyone looking for a good time with a board game.

product_title: Thunderstone Advance Caverns of Bane
review_body:
I've been a big fan of the Thunderstone line of games and have enjoyed most of the early run. When Thunderstone Advance came out, I thought they fixed quite a few problems that I didn't even quite realize I had with the original set up of the game. I loved the new cards, the tokens for experience points, and even the way new Regulars worked rather than straight out Militia.

With a new expansion, Thunderstone Advance becomes an even better game. More variety is always nice, and Caverns of Bane provides plenty. A plethora of new heroes mixed with some really great spells and more useful villagers than the original game, the expansion seems to have a lot to offer to enhance game play. I love the new treasure gimmick, making some monsters both harder and more rewarding to beat.

If there was one tiny little complaint, it would be that the new monster dividers do not have the Level of the monster group on them. I really like the leveling system that Thunderstone Advance utilizes, and not having the dividers marked is just an irritating inconvenience in an otherwise lovely expansion. But overall, if you like Thunderstone, you'll like this. It doesn't add anything game changing, but it's more of the game you already love.

Our family enjoyed this game. My oldest (age 12) and my middle child (age 11) enjoyed it quite a bit. My 9 year old did not enjoy it at all. This is something even my engineer husband enjoyed sitting down to play.

Enjoy.

product_title: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles Classic Collection Donatello
review_headline: My review in brief: "I like it!"
review_body:
The Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles have a way of popping up every few years with fun new ideas while still maintaining their original charm of being four, fun loving teenagers which are quite proficient in the martial arts. I still remember first discovering the TMNT on the shelf of a toy story my grandmother always took me too and for some reason they captivated me. Maybe it was the numerous weapons they came with, the colorful packaging, or the weird variety of characters in that first wave of action figures? Whatever the case, I'm thrilled the TMNT are still around and making a huge comeback. With IDW publishing an excellent monthly comic and reprinting nice collected versions of the original black and white comics, a new cartoon from Nickelodeon premiering soon, and a movie on the horizon, this seems like the perfect time for Playmates to jump in and play off of the nostalgia of adult fans who first encountered the turtles as children. With the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles Classic Collection, Playmates has done much what Mattel has done with Masters of the Universe Classics, Bandai with the Thundercats vintage collection, and Hasbro with the Star Wars vintage collection, the G.I. Joe 25th anniversary line, and certain Transformers releases: Recreate beloved vintage action figures in a larger scale with modern articulation and detail. These turtles are recreations of the original action figures with a smattering of detail from the cartoon series. I think Playmates has been highly successful in their endeavor, but read on to learn more!

Positives:

*I love the look of this figure! The size, the colors, the detail: all of it comes together to make a beautiful blend of style and nostalgia. Most likely, this is the image of Donatello that jumps into your mind. I mentioned it above, but with this collection Playmates has successfully blended the style of the original toys (look at that facial expression) with elements from the cartoons (brown belts and pupils on the eyes). By himself, Donny is great; with his brothers, he is amazing.

*Donatello does have 34 points of articulation, just like the package proclaims. Besides the expected double-jointed knees and elbows, Donatello also has articulated toes and fingers. He can easily hold his included bo staff in a variety of poses.

*Donatello comes with a stand that looks like a manhole cover. It features the TMNT logo and Donatello's name. Stands are always welcome in my book.

Negatives:

product_title: Dragon Models 1/400 Air Force One 747-200 ~ 28000/29000
review_headline: Great for collectibles, not for use as toys!
review_body:
I've been collecting Gemini Jets and the Dragon Wings NASA/Space collection for some time now, all in 1:400 scale. Remember the size of 1:400 planes - a large plane is around 6\\" long, smaller ones can be 1 1/2-2\\", with other sizes in between.

The difference between Gemini and Dragon airplanes is that Gemini is all metal (save for the landing gear), Dragon is a metal body and vertical stabilizer (rudder), wings and horizontal stabilizers (tail fins) are plastic. They are not noticeable unless picked up, Gemini Jets are a bit heavier, being all metal. Gemini does not offer the NASA or space items and they have a smaller selection of planes (airlines and airplane types) than Dragon. They are both highly and impressively detailed, especially considering their size.

These are great collectors items that will maintain close to original price (newer releases tend to drop in price for awhile), older models and smaller releases can go up in price over time considerably - of course, assuming they are well taken care of, same for the box.

And, once again, these are collectible models, they are not toys. They will break easily unless handled gently (don't pick them up by the tail fins, they can break off!) I don't know why many of these are listed under toys but they are definitely not appropriate for small children (smaller parts can break off and be a choking hazard), and they are not meant to be played with, so please don't buy it for Johnny expecting he can \\"fly it around\\".

Each turn represents a year of life and you pay your mortgage, car payment, expenses, and interest on loans before you move on the board.  It's very realistic with promotions, college, children, houses, cars and vacations.  The board is divided into four sections and it's up to you which section you enter: education, business, love, or adventure, unlike the original version of Life where you go through the whole board with little choice.  For example, if you want to make money, you don't ever have to go to any other section than business.  I was disappointed the first time I played it as there are only 4 credit cards and we had 6 people but two of us took partners and it worked out well.  It seems to work well with mixed age groups - we played a 19 year old, three people in their mid-twenties, and older adults in their 60's at the same time. product_title: Lords of Waterdeep: A Dungeons & Dragons Board Game
review_headline: Engaging resource-management game with a fantasy theme
review_body:
Thematically based on the Dungeons & Dragons Forgotten Realms setting, Lords of Waterdeep is an engaging resource-management game on a par with Settlers of Catan and the like. Each player takes on the role of one of the titular Lords of Waterdeep, keeping the Lord's identity secret from the other players. The overall goal is very simple: high score, measured in victory points, wins. Players earn victory points primarily by completing quests dealt from a deck of cards and, to a lesser extent, by building new buildings in Waterdeep. Each Lord also has a secret agenda that brings additional victory points. To complete a quest, a Lord will need to commit some combination of adventurers--clerics, fighters, rogues, and wizards, each class represented by a colored token--and gold. On their turns, players assign agents (not the same as adventurers) to recruit adventurers, collect gold, and do other things that advance their interests. Intrigue cards held by each player present additional options.

Lords of Waterdeep is a big game in a big box. The first time you play, give yourself half an hour or so to punch out cardboard components, and two or three hours to learn and complete your first game. The rules are quite straightforward, and you'll have them mastered by the end of your first or second game. Thereafter, games can run an hour or two, depending on how many people are playing, how familiar the players are with the various components (buildings, intrigue cards, quests, and Lords), and how much time the players take to make decisions on their own turns. The components are very high-quality, and even the injection-molded tray in the box has been very carefully designed to hold all the components perfectly.

Most importantly, Lords of Waterdeep is fun to play! My sons, ages 14 and 8 at the time of this review, both love it. We're always on the lookout for a couple of free hours--not so easy to come by during the school year--when we can play.

review_body:
I'm disabled and decided to play solitaire dominoes for therapy. I've ordered a few other sets, and they are all working well. This set gave me a surprise. One of my disabilities involves vision, and working on that also helps with some brain damage. I figured out a few years ago that colors are effective and important for me to use. These red dominoes are teaching me something else.

Because they are a bright color and have white dots and my vision is all over the place, I have to work at counting the dots. Every color, size, and type of domino gives me a different vision experience--and that is excellent.

The first time I used this red set, it didn't come out right at the last move, so I knew the set was either mixed up or I had misread one or more pieces. I played again, and found myself recognizing them faster and the game ended the right way. Good for my eyes and for my brain--and the red makes me smile, too.

I like the velvet case, and the dominoes are lovely. I can't comment on using them professionally, but they are certainly very nice.

product_title: Electronic Labyrinth Family Game
review_headline: Not overly complicated but has enough strategy to keep the brain cells busy
review_body:
I heard such good things about the original Labyrinth game that I jumped on the chance to get this. Having never played the original, this review will not include a comparison between the two. I will start off by saying my husband and I are somewhat into gaming though not really hardcore. We play Settlers of Catan, Citadels, Blokus, Qwirkle, Chess and Go. We've also played Agricola and Puerto Rico and while many people love the complexity of those games, my husband and I tend to be turned off by too many rules. We love something cerebral but simplistic. Elegant.

That said, I liked this game. I think I liked it more than my husband did. When I opened the box, my initial impression was the game was very attractive with quality pieces. There's a slot for each kind of piece and everything is well organized. The fact that you can shift the maze and change the game board was pretty neat to me and the high fantasy element was fun.

The first time we played it took over an hour because of reading the rules and understanding the game. The second time was a breeze because we had already figured out some shortcuts and cheats to manipulating the maze. I think it's not so complicated that going through the game is laborious, but there is just enough strategy involved that you're plotting and scheming though most of it.

The electronic book is nice. It has the option of \\"fast forwarding\\" through the intro so that the characters aren't always introducing themselves. It was also fairly intuitive to use and blended seamlessly into play.

Definitely will get lots of use out this game.

Edited to add: I'm not sure why the Amazon product specs say this is a 2-6 player game. It is actually for 2-4 players.

product_title: LEGO Ultrabuild Green Lantern 4528
review_headline: Green Lantern Lego figurine = short diversion
review_body:
As an adult, perhaps it's not really fair that I would be writing this review, but then again I've long been a fan of Legos and also have long been a fan of the Green Lantern character and many of his Justice League type friends, so perhaps this is the right kind of \\"toy\\" for me to say a few words about.

I put toy in quotations back there because in reality this isn't so much a toy as it is just a collectible figurine, or at least something that might eventually be a collectible. Assuming this is part of a limited time release and won't be an item that remains readily available in the marketplace, I could easily see it as a collector's item that appeals to both Lego collectors and collectors of DC Comics Heroes action figures.

In terms of fun, I based most of my detailed sub-rating on the construction of the figure. It builds fairly simply just from following the included manual. There are approximately 8 detailed steps that show how to put the figure together if you wish to stay within the lines and build the set as designed. Of course this is a Lego set and as such, you can mix and match the pieces with other similar Lego sets to create something different -- for example, if you wanted to build a two headed Green Lantern you could mix pieces from two of these sets to do just that. The manual that comes with the set and/or the online advertising here even suggests that someone could combine pieces of this set with one of The Joker to build an even bigger Green Lantern.

Unfortunately though, the fun is fairly short-lived as once someone does build this figure they aren't likely going to just tear it apart and start all over again. They could, but in reality the pieces are designed to be used for building this type of figure. They aren't the typically more generic Lego blocks and won't mix in with those types of blocks, at least not as anything other than perhaps a giant character that has been imported into the smaller Lego world (assuming you have some mini-fig type characters to go with a typical Lego set). Picture perhaps a Gulliver Travels type scenario, with the figure you build with these pieces as the Giant among the little chacters (mini-figs) from the normal sets.

Children could play with the figure after building it if they wanted to, it does flex at all of the joints and can be made to sit or stand in various poses, so yes, it can be played with as an action figure, but then again the pieces in this set are not as durable (at least they don't seem so) as the more generic Lego blocks. These are a bit more fragile as they are larger, more open pieces. If one of the bigger pieces were popped off and left on the floor and stepped on, I suspect it would snap quite easily. Never mind what might happen to it if the family dog or feline got ahold of it.

For the relatively low (current) every day price, I think there's plenty of value here and can easily recommend this item. If the prices skyrocket a bit later on, then not so fast. product_title: VTech Switch & Go Dinos - T-Don the Pteranodon Dinosaur
review_headline: Keep your little boys & girls entertained for hours of creative play!
review_body:
I have 3 boys in my household - ages 8, 6, and 2. Upon receiving our T-Don and Tonn Switch & Go Dinos, the biggest downside is that my kids had to share the two toys between the three of them! Right away my older sons were in awe of the toys and how they morphed from vehicles back into dinosaurs with ease. Of course my 2 year-old loved that it seemed like a \\"big boy toy\\" and even HE could easily manipulate the toy to morph back and forth. The very audible (but not over disturbing) roars and sounds the toy makes were also fun for my kids. All three of my sons enjoyed incorporating the Switch & Go Dinos into their regular creative play, even making their own voices and noises to emulate the dinosaurs. This may not be what you would think of as a typical \\"learning\\" toy because it does not enforce reading or math, necessarily, but it is a learning toy in my opinion (as a mom) because my kids are presented with the opportunity to use their imagination and creativity when incorporating these toys into their everyday play. They are learning about sounds and developing fine motor skills while they switch the dinos back and forth into different toys altogether.

The toys are very interactive and my kids enjoyed the little bits of educational information that came out of the toys as well. My kids were so excited to receive these and I also think that for the price -- you can't beat it! For about the price of a movie DVD you can get this 2-in-1 toy which has far more potential for creativity and learning. These would make an excellent gift idea for any boy or girl on your gift list. In saying that, I should add that I have a niece whom I plan to get these for as well since I think they are very educational and creative for both boys and girls. I like that they are pretty gender neutral since both boys and girls are fascinated by dinosaurs and I also think it is great for girls to have a type of toy that morphs into some other type of toy, yet isn't exactly\\"girly\\". Bottom line, I think this toy is a good value and a unique choice for your kids if you are looking for something that encourages creative play.

{I have received VTech Switch & Go Dinos to facilitate my review.}

product_title: LEGO The Lord of the Rings Hobbit The Mines of Moria (9473)
review_headline: My favorite of the initial LEGO LotR sets!
review_body:
9473 The Mines of Moria is a 776-piece LEGO set initially released in May of 2012 with a LEGO store price of $79.99. It is part of the first wave of Lord of the Rings-licensed sets, and includes Legolas, Gimli, Boromir, Pippin, a giant cave troll, two skeletons, two orcs, numerous accessories, and a ton of grey bricks to build with. It is my *FAVORITE* of the LEGO LotR sets so far.

Why do I like it so much? Two main reasons: 1) it is a BIG, exciting set and 2) the pieces can be used to build a lot of different things. With the first part.. the set contains an excellent selection of good guys (The Fellowship), bad guys (orcs, trolls, and skeletons), and interesting things to build. There's a treasure chest that can be hidden, walls that collapse, a tomb that flip open, and an opening and closing door/gate. This set is DYNAMIC. You're going to want to build it, play with it, alter it, and play with it some more. The pieces can also be used to build a lot of different things. When you're done playing in the Mines of Moria, you can build a castle with all of the grey pieces (the mine gate is now a castle gate!), or use them to build up other LotR, Castle, or Kingdom sets. The bad guy minifigs will fit right into other Castle sets, though the good guys have a slightly different skin color than normal LEGOs (cream-flesh colored for the LotR characters rather than LEGO yellow). The weapons, treasure, and skeletons will also make a nice addition to any LEGO Kingdom or Castles collection.

Rating: 5 out of 5 Stars. This is one of the best LEGO sets I've seen in a while.

product_title: Super Soaker Clip System Canister
review_headline: Awesome idea, but no real advantage
review_body:
I own (and am reviewing) several Nerf Super Soaker models because this line of guns (blue and white with orange accents) offers the best combination of durability, ease of operation, and affordability that I've come across. They are much more durable than the flimsy plastic used in most other squirt guns, and their water reservoirs have nice screw-on caps that don't leak! If you shop around, you can also find great prices on the simplest models, which are some of the best in the line up.

About the Super Soaker CLIP SYSTEM CANISTERS:

The reloadable clip is a super-cool idea, and it works great in my Tornado Strike, for which I own three clips. My gripe is that the clips are so small in capacity that they don't offer a major advantage over simpler, cheaper, non-clip-style super soaker guns in the same line up. In fact, they end up adding weight, cost, and even a little inconvenience as you try to swap clips in the midst of battle.

For example, with my Tornado Strike, I get exactly 12 shots per clip. So with my three ammo clips, I get a total of 36 shots. The problem is that this means I have to run around with two on my waistband and one in the gun, then take the time to reload as each clip empties. While I'm carrying all that weight and capacity, the cheaper, simpler Scatter Blast puts out a more effective stream (slightly further and noticeably wetter per blast) and gets 40 shots on its single built-in reservoir. The Scatter Blast is also smaller, lighter, easier to pump, more rugged, and MUCH cheaper since the Tornado Strike costs more even before you factor in the cost of extra ammo clips.

If the ammo clips had a higher capacity, they might offer an edge in battle. As it stands, however, I've found that they are more \\"cool\\" than effective. Everyone always seems to want to use my Tornado Strike because they like the clip feature, and I always let them borrow it (I grab my Scatter Blast instead) because I know I'll be able to out-gun them while they run out of shots and fumble around trying to swap clips. I guess in that regard it is my secret weapon.

The only clear reason to prefer the ammo clip system and the associated guns (Tornado Strike and Lightning Storm) is if you have several of these guns and a large supply of clips. Then you could have someone volunteer to constantly reload clips while everyone else has a long, uninterrupted squirt battle (thanks to a steady supply of clips). Since none of my friends ever want to volunteer for reload duty, I don't find any clear advantage to the clips, and I even think they fall short of the simpler, cheaper models with a large built-in reservoir.to out-gun them while they run out of shots and fumble around trying to swap clips. product_title: Blade mCP X V2 BNF (Transmitter not Included)
review_body:
The Blade mcpx is by far the best sub-micro CP heli in the market. This is not a beginner's heli, but it will teach you proper collective management. If you are already familiar with FP (fixed pitch) helis and want to take it to the next step, then look no further. The mcpx handles moderate winds quite well, but it becomes quite twitchy and bumpy when exposed to gusty winds.

Tail hold could be better, but it does a decent job. Some users will modified the tail boom by using a longer, solid carbon fiber rod. I have not done this mod yet, but I have seen modified mcpx's and they hold the tail better than the stock form.

The provided batteries are ok, but I recommend you get some aftermarket packs to add more juice and flight time. I can squeeze about 5 minutes out of the stock batteries, and about six minutes when using Hyperion's 250mAh batteries.

One of the advantages of owning an mcpx is that many hobby shops carry plenty of parts. If you crash, you can easily get this little guy back in the air after a quick trip to your LHS. Parts are not too expensive, and if you can't get them locally, there are hundreds of online stores carrying parts for the mcpx.

Overall, I am very satisfied with this heli and highly recommend it to anybody who is ready to jump into CP helis. I think this is the best \\"real simulator\\" you can get since it can fly very similar to bigger choppers.

product_title: Robert Kiyosaki Rich Dad How To Get Out of the Rat Race Game
review_body:
All I have to say is this: I have two decrees from accredited universities, and this game has taught me more about the BASIC financial principles of investing than any of my school classes. Yes, it's BASIC information, but it's a game. It's only meant to simulate investing and is in no way a substitute for solid investing education (which is not always available in schools). It's meant to change your mindset about how to raise and invest money, and how you can get comfortable with borrowing to leverage your money and NOT spend it away on \\"doodads\\" and things that are NOT assets.

After playing this game, I got an education in financial investing and then put what I learned into PRACTICE. Without the additional education, the game playing would have been useless. Without putting my education into PRACTICE, the education itself would have been useless as well. I spent 12 years of my life as a recruiter for HR and staffing agencies, and I can tell you many a person who went to school and got a degree, and didn't put the degree into PRACTICE. Those were the people who were always complaining about the lack of opportunity and they were always bouncing from job to job, usually at less than what they expected. Now I will say that nowadays, traditional education will not guarantee you a job, which is why this game is so valuable. It teaches you that you need to start a business and how to do so by leveraging your money so you won't end up in the situation I just mentioned above.

A large majority of people do not take the time, energy or financial effort to educate themselves on the levels of financial literacy that it will take to earn a living or be wealthy. If you are one of them, do not waste your money and buy this game. But if you do want to learn BASIC principles and have an extreme amount of FUN doing it, then go hard or go home!!!
