product_title: Lords of Waterdeep: A Dungeons & Dragons Board Game
review_body:
LoW is probably the most complicated \\"euro-style\\" game I've ever played, but it's also one of the most fun, and one of the most replayable. The setup of the game takes around 10 minutes alone. Play takes roughly an hour, give or take a little depending on the familiarity of the players.

I won't go into how to play, as it's a fairly complicated game. Suffice to say that you have only a handful of actions per turn, but copious amounts of choices to make per turn. Do I try to acquire adventurers so I can complete quests? Do I play Intrigue cards to derail my opponents? Do I try to claim the First Player marker so that I go first next round? Do I build a building and hope to cash in on other players using it? Do I claim more quests? Lots and lots of choices, but limited resources to execute them.

Strategy in the game revolves around doing quests. Your \\"Lord\\" (randomly chosen at the start of the game) determines which types of quests give you bonus points at the end of the game. However, because the quests available are randomly determined as the game progresses, it's often difficult to capitalize on this bonus. Since the quests vary greatly in the resources required to complete them, you end up spending your turns debating whether to acquire resources, play (or gather) Intrigue cards to either hinder your opponents or gain resources yourself, or set up plays for future turns. Generally, the more resources a quest requires, the bigger the payout. Though the big reward quests are tempting, it's often better to complete multiple smaller quests of your lord's speciality to acquire the bonus points. You also have to plan ahead to ensure that you're not found wanting a specific adventurerer type or gold in order to complete a quest.

I still haven't completely identified a routinely successful strategy to playing the game, though playing at least one agent into Waterdeep Harbor seems to be effective, if you don't require much resources for quests. The Harbor allows you to not only play an Intrigue card, but also to redeploy your agent at the end of the round. With good planning, you can play your card AND get the resources that you need. Too many Intrigue cards end up wasting your time, however, as you won't gain as many resources from playing them as you will get from buildings on the board. I could go on for pages about various strategies, but ultimately you have to play the game for yourself to determine what works for that particular game.

Production quality is very good for the game. All pieces are either ~2mm thick plastic-coated cardboard or wood. The Quest and Intrigue cards are plastic-coated as well, much like good playing cards. Most impressive to me is that the game box contains an insert which neatly stores all of the pieces in various wells dedicated to those pieces. This allows you to quickly distribute materials and set up the game without having to dig around the box and sort all of the little tokens. It also makes the box \\"tip-resistant\\", where flipping it upside-down won't cause all the pieces to go flying around the box. Granted, some will lose their places, but they're easily retrieved. My major complaint is with the victory-point tokens and the 1 gold piece markers. They take some doing to get them to fit in their assigned spots in the insert, but I don't really know how one would improve upon the design to ease the problem.

Overall, this isn't a quick or simple game. It requires some time dedicated to setting up and playing it, and requires a fair amount of thinking and strategizing to play well. It is absolutely worth getting and playing though. product_title: Arkham Horror
review_headline: Not the Best Mythos Board Game, but Probably the Best Known
review_body:
This board game is a retread/rethink of an older game by the same name that attempted to capture the feel of the RPG Call of Cthulhu experience in a board game format.

The good:

The artwork is superb and the cardboard pieces are very sturdy. The replay value of this game will be high provided you can live with the \\"almost always lose\\" philosophy of the design. The mechanics are not difficult (see explanation of why people think they are under \\"the bad\\").

The Bad:

Losing all the time. This is really a matter of luck, but a few bad die rolls at the game start can make the game thoroughly uninteresting from the get-go as characters spiral uncontrollably into uselessness. More thought should have been given to breaking the game into initial, intermediate and end-game phases when it comes to the mythos threat.

Need for high player-character count. Play with two and you'll see what I mean. Solo play? Fergeddaboutit! Waste of time unless you field many characters. See \\"footprint\\" for why this is inconvenient.

Rulebook: Horribly disorganized. In the post RPG world game companies have forgotten how to write rules so you can jump into the game and figure it out as you go (like the old Avalon Hill games used to work). You'll be clawing all over the bedsheet-sized rulebook (about 2 square feet when open) looking for that vital special case even if you have an indexed version of the rules since stuff can be in sidebars instead of the main text. Epic fail.

Footprint: The game takes up acres of space what with cards decks and card displays and the board. I've heard that some people have played with all the expansion boards too. I envision them using a banqueting table to do so (though later expansions have smaller rulebooks).

For the money it isn't a bad deal if the milieu floats your boat, but this is a \\"dolls house\\" game in which the temptation to keep adding expansions to see how it improves the play will be expensive and irresistible.

If you are looking for a game that offers a more \\"realistic\\" Call of Cthulhu game feel and gives the players a chance to actually win (losing to the mythos threat is something that can be judged to take place over geologic timescales, it doesn't mean every encounter is fatal for Azathoth's sake else Inspector Legrasse never gets out of the swamp with the statue and the story never gets told) I'd advise saving your money and buying \\"Mansions of Madness\\", which has been much more popular with my gaming friends (albeit costing about twice what Arkham Horror does).the play will be expensive and irresistible.

product_title: LeapFrog AC Adapter (Works with all LeapPad2 and LeapPad1 Tablets, LeapsterGS Explorer, Leapster Explorer and  Leapster2)
review_body: To those of you looking for a current review and to answer some questions, I wanted to make a few comments.  First of all, as many other reviewers have mentioned in their five star ratings and to answer some of you that have left one or two star ratings, this is an AC Adapter, as mentioned in the product description and the box itself.  This is not a charger, not a docking station.  This is merely an electrical plug that works with the Leap Frog products.  Whether you have rechargable batteries or not, this item is not intended to charge those.  This is to be plugged in while using the unit, as you would a television.  If you want a portable unit, put in the batteries.  We use this ac adapter when we are at home, since most kids sit in one place while using these toys, it is no problem to plug it into the nearest outlet.  We put in fresh batteries when we head to an airport or when we are in the car.  That being said, the second issue, which actually made me wonder whether to order this or not, is whether it works for the LeapPad or Leapster Explorer units.  It does.  In fact, the version we received is exactly as shown - a white adapter with a rounded/domed plug - and the box actually says on the front and back that it works for ALL Leapster Learning Systems - explicitly stating that it includes the Leapster Explorer and the LeapPad Explorer.  We have a Leapster 2 as well as the LeapPad and this works for both of them.  Why the product description mentions that it isn't compatible with the Explorer systems, I do not know.  The only reason I can think of is that Leap Frog has updated this item since it originally appeared and now includes those systems.  Of course, what you receive could always vary from what someone else received, but we just got ours this week (May 6, 2012) and the pictured item is what we recieved, even if the description doesn't match. product_title: Revell 1:72 SR-71A Blackbird
review_headline: Good model of an SR-71 Blackbird
review_body:
I ordered this because I Love building models of all kinds and I wanted a large aircraft. Its huge! 18 1/2 inches long and has a wing span of 9 1/4 inches wide. I am also a fan of aviation and Lockheed Martin, the company who developed the Blackbird project back in 1964 for the U.S. air force and the C.I.A. First off the shipping was fast, it came a day ahead of schedule and the box and its contents were all there and undamaged.

It includes a D-21 reconnaissance drone which has an option of being on a cart or on the top of the SR-71. Its a great model for the price. I got it at around $24 (save $25 to be safe). Model kits of this size can be $70 to $100 if Tamiya America made something like this kit. It comes in black so it would look good unpainted and with decals applied. The only thing that was a bit challenging was the rear landing gear if you want to build it with the gear down for a desk display. It's the reaction rods (landing gear hydraulics) that you would have the most trouble installing so keep a set of tweezers and a good light source handy and try your best.

It does include a pilot and radar systems operator which I didn't bother installing because I built my model with the canopies closed and you can hardly see the cockpit through the small view ports. But if you build yours with the canopies open then you can see the pilots, instruments, and controls in the cockpit Better. I wish it came with an access ladder for the side then I would have left the canopies open with pilot and radar operator in To give it that getting ready for flight look. Overall I wold recommend this to someone looking for a model kit of an SR-71 Blackbird that is of good size, quality, and not to spendy.

Robot mode is excellent. Holds together well. Nothing really get's in the way of his poseability like the Cyberverse Optimus Prime shoulders.This is another area where I'm really wowed by this guy. He's is pretty friggin screen accurate in robot mode too. Essentially all you have to do to imaging the look of the upcoming powerizer Dreadwing...just imagine the Cyberverse Robot mode bigger. Seriously he looks that good. I know a lot of you would rather wait for the Powerizer but the Cyberverse figures are really growing on me. I asked Little Tikes if this is a common problem with their bounce houses and of course they denied it. They said that if they sent me another bounce house and it happened again, only then would they give me a coupon to buy another Little Tikes product on their website where they mark the products way up!!! product_title: Green Toys Jump Rope
review_headline: Perfect Jump Rope and MADE IN THE USA!
review_body:
I seriously can't say enough about the quality of these jump ropes! I purchased a green one for my 2 year old and a pink one for my 4 year old.

- The handles are SO comfortable! The colors are vibrant.

- The rope turns with ease.

- The rope is cotton, not plastic, so no whipping your legs! Wow!

- The rope length is sizeable to fit your child!

- Gets your child moving.

- AMERICAN MADE TOO from RECYCLED PLASTIC! Way to give Americans jobs and save the planet at the same time!

Note: sizing the rope takes some muscle to get the top twisted off. It has a locking notch that you have to force past and then it untwists with ease. When you tie the new knot, don't trim the rope. Just let the excess rope fill in the hollow handles (so smart!!), recap it and twist it back on. Use some force until you feel it click over that notch again to lock back in place. It's not hard, just takes a little muscle to unlock and lock it again. Well made! Won't fall apart once locked!

They have all the bases covered with this design. What a wonderful toy to own! I LOVE them! My children LOVE them! Will definitely buy another if these ever bite the dust. Being a child powered, not battery powered, toy I will certainly be getting them for gifts too.

Green Toys is a great toy company! We own their teapot set, dishes, and two of their sand box bucket sets. I have never been disappointed with anything this company puts out. My kids love and use every toy they own from Green Toys, which really says it all.

product_title: Fisher-Price Octonauts Gup A Deluxe Vehicle Playset
review_body:
Got this for my son's 5th birthday. He loves the Octonauts and I was elated to see it available on Amazon. I was worried about the delivery time since it was coming from the UK and they said it could take up to a month to get to me. I went ahead and ordered it anyway knowing he would love a real Gup A. To my delight, it came in a week and we were able to present it to him on his birthday.

It is larger than you think...about the size of a small football...so he needs two hands to hold it unless he grabs it by the antenna. However, he doesn't seem to mind and he has been playing with it every day. He loves taking it into his bath and to school for show-and-tell. Aside from its bulkiness, the only other design flaw is the propeller/wind-up motion aspect. It takes too many cranks of the propeller to get the toy moving and even then it can only propel itself on smooth surfaces (i.e., hardwood floors). It doesn't work on carpets or even in the water.

On the plus side, the addition of play figures like Captain Barnacles and sea creatures made the playset super fun for my son. The figures are cute and Barnacles has movable arms and legs so you can get him to sit or stand and hold things.

Overall, I (and my son) give this toy a BIG thumbs up!

Using cards to direct parts of a person's body is not a common activity, so the participants have to be willing enough to try new things and keep adjusting their methods until they find what works. Generally, I'd stick to pulling this game out with close friends who don't mind a bit of a laugh and are ok with occasionally looking a little silly.

review_headline: A Blast of a Euro-American Combo.

We have played only twice, but can see a great future ahead. I don't usually take time to write reviews, so pardon the erratic nature, however, I felt I needed to at least mention how fun this game is.

Basic game is one of;
Exploration (of expanding the board by turning over tiles);
Battle with a great ship mechanic (your ships are what you make of them based on ...)
Research (your race starts to focus on Military/Exploring/Tech)
Adaption -- So much can change in one turn that you have to be on your toes.

Be prepared to spend a few hours in the beginning just getting set up and learning the game. After that - The recommended time of 30 min/player seems a little light, but not too inaccurate.

Not going to get bored of this one any time soon.
Enjoy!!

PS: There are not many games that make 2-6 players so fluid and fun for all.

product_title: Air Swimmers Remote Control Flying Shark
review_body: Gave it as a gift and then had to have one myself. I will share some points to consider when using and building your Air Swimmer. Helium, I discovered is sensitive to heat. Where you fly your Shark and the room's temperature will effect how firm the balloon will feel.It doesn't lose helium it just expands differently in the balloon. Allow balloon to adjust to room temperature before adjusting weight for neutral floating. Watch the instructional (you tube) video several times before building your Shark. Use pure helium. Try not to handle the sticky side of the tape too much. Take extra rubber bands just in case you lose one or two. Securely stick all your taped attachments. The tape does cure in time and the fins will hold strong in a few days. In the beginning repress your taped items often until the tape's glue sets. Remember if you fill the helium in a warn environment and fly the Shark in a cool place he may feel a little soft. That works the reverse and maybe could over expand. I haven't tried that.

product_title: Syma S110G Infrared 3.5 CH Micro RC Helicopter RTF w/ Gyro orange and red
review_headline: Let's tell it like it is
review_body:
Ok, I'm just fed up with all the rediculous complaints in so many reviews for this, it's just silly.
First, to the people who say it's not durable enough. Well, if you crash it (or ANY other low cost toy)enough times or have a bad crash (due to lack of flying skill, no doubt), guess what? It's going to break! Just because you can't fly the thing without having a bad enough crash to break something, that doesn't mean it's not durable, it means you need more practice. And I also saw one reviewer give it a low score because \\"IT SEEMS LIKE IT WILL BREAK EASILY.\\" Are you kidding me? It SEEMS like it would break? Give ME a BREAK.
I even saw one reviewer complain about how it spins and there's no trim knob. Huh? How about this: Read the manual. Then, actually LOOK at what you're holding in your hand. Observe the TRIM WHEEL? Give that a shot before coming on Amazon to bash something that you're clearly not knowledgeable enough about to even review in the first place.
There's even a couple good reviews that have some absurd claims in them. Concerning runtime, there is no way whatsoever that anyone gets 10 minutes or more of flight time. It's IMPOSSIBLE to achieve. The motors draw a certain amount of juice, the battery has only so much to give, you can't change the laws of physics. Maybe you can get the rotor to spin for 10 minutes, but actually flying for that long? Not gonna happen, sorry. I guess some people think it's impressive to be \\"that guy\\" who's got a heli which defies the laws of physics and works better than anyone elses does.
Think of this as a micro s107g, but as size decreases things get more sensitive and twitchy. If you suck at flying then don't buy a heli that's the size of a large insect. You're gonna crash it then come here and cry about it not being durable enough. Yeah, the transmitter exaggerates the already sensitive flying characteristics of such a tiny heli, but you will overcome this with practice, and then come to appreciate it as being responsive.

product_title: Syma S107/S107G R/C Helicopter *Colors Vary
review_body:
I don't care if you're 8 or 88, this helo is one heckuva lot of fun!

First read about these in the Wall Street Journal and that they employ gyroscope technology from today's smart phones making these little guys very stable and much more enjoyable to fly. This is very, very true!

Had mine now for 2 months and have flown it pretty much every day, twice a day - once before work and then after dinner. Maybe when I first got it I flew it 3 or even 4 times a day. Anyway, when first flying it you easily become overconfident because it IS VERY STABLE. It's a snap to fly.... you start buzzing around the room and then you crash it. I've crashed it countless times and it still just flies again and again without issue. Now, I've grown proficient enough to fly it low between and around chairs and tables. I buzz around from room to room annoying my wife I might add. No problem :)

Several reviewers have commented on how long it flies with a charge. Well, today I get just about 8 minutes on mine each and every flight. Perhaps it's because I let the battery cool down before recharging. Anyway, it was 8 minutes when I first bought it and it's still 8 minutes. A replacement battery is just a few dollars, but the original is still fine so no need to change it yet.

The only mod I've done is to take the return spring out of the controller controlling thrust (up and down) which makes it even easier to fly.

This is so much fun and for $20. Truly, I don't think you could get a guy something better than this just as a fun gift. These will be this year's stocking stuffers for some of my better buds.

product_title: The Settlers of Catan 5 & 6 Player Extension
review_body:
I was introduced to the Catan series of games through the Cities & Knights expansion. I instantly fell in love with the game, but hesitated to purchase my own because of the high price. I then thought of checking Amazon, and was pleasantly surprised to find it for so cheap! I bought this at the same time I bought a great card game called Bohnanza. I bought the main game, and the player expansion, for less than I would have paid for just the basic game at my local game store.

The game is a fun boardgame style take on some of my favorite PC game series, such as Civilization and Age of Empires. The game does take a while to play, so needs to be started early in the day if you want to get one, or more, rounds in. The gameplay and rules can be a bit overwhelming for a first-time player; however you are able to gain a strong grasp on the \\"how-to\\" once you start playing. This game is not for the whole family (if you have younger children), as younger children may have a difficult time grasping the concept of play and applying strategy. This is a great game to play/introduce to families with older children, friends, or colleages on game nights or at parties/get-togethers.

product_title: Syma 3 Channel S013 Mini Infrared Black Hawk RC Helicopter
review_body:
This helicopter isnt as bad as some people like to say but it is flawed.

Pros
Not zippy(fast,almost uncontrollable movements)
The control's frequency does not lag very much
Durable body and rotors
Replacement parts are easy to obtain and are not costly
Charges relatively fast
Safe Packaging(Good for those lazy delivery personnel who like to throw stuff)
Radio Control is very durable.

Pro/Con
Comes with only a charger straight from the controller no wall or USB charger.
5-9 minutes of flight time
Not kid friendly(14 years or older is recommended to fly this.

Cons
The Dead Zone on this thing takes a little getting used to(has to be adjusted so that it does not fly in circles, but once adjusted stays pretty stable)
Controller needs 6 AA batteries to function.
The plastic wheels on the bottom aren't very strong
Can only be used indoors(Will function outside but a small breeze is enough to take the blackhawk down)-No pun or joke intended.
Takes 20-30 Minutes to charge for about 5-9 minutes of flight time
Instructions can be understood but Chinese to English translators get a couple things wrong

product_title: Nanoblock Bottlenose Dolphin
review_body:
This is my second Nanoblock purchase (My first was the Panda). This is a great Building toy, but needs some getting use to. The instructions are harder to follow than LEGO's and Mega Blok's. It takes more time to read it and follow than L&MB. Also you build in a very different way. The pieces can be swallowed or lost so be careful.The pieces are easy to grab but sometimes harder to connect. The end product is very cool, its more for display though. The details are great but this Nanoblock set is easily breakable(Just the flippers). The Panda I got was very sturdy and strong. I would suggest it as a starter set.

Recommended age 10-15
Younger kids might have trouble with assembly and its breakable and not for play.

Fun factor *** Stars. Its fun to build but that's all.

Educational value *** Stars. Might teach about building,coordination,animals, and maybe shapes?

Durability ** Stars. Its very fragile. I picked it up gently and the flippers came off.

Pros
-Fun to build
-Great looking
-Good detail

Cons
-Fragile
-Sometimes confusing to build
-Not the greatest instructions

That concludes my review. Its an awesome toy and I would recommended to buy it.

product_title: Toy Vault Godzilla Talking Keychain Toy
review_body:
I just received this item and it's pretty cool but not quite as fun as I had hoped it would be.

Button 1. Supposedly this sound is King Ghidorah, which it probably is but it is the post 1990s King Ghidorah, which doesn't sound a whole lot different than versions of Rodan. I would much rather have had this be the classic King Ghidorah sound from the movies of the 60s & 70s.

Button 2. Baby Godzilla. Yeah, This one makes me think that the manufacturer had a very limited contract as to what they had access to for sounds. I mean, out of all the unique sounds in Godzilla movies over the years and you pick \\"Baby Godzilla\\" as one of your 4 sounds? To me it sounds a little bit generic and not significantly different than the included King Ghidorah sound. It's not bad, or annoying but seems like a missed opportunity to include something really cool. FYI, I think it's Baby Godzilla from Godzilla vs. Mecha Godzilla II.

Button 3. Godzilla. What can I say. Probably the main reason anyone who even thinks of buying this item. :-D

Button 4. Mothra. I'm not a fan of Mothra but this is a pretty good sound. It has a brief Mothra shriek followed by the sound effect of Mothra flying. Not a flapping sound but one of those old school monster movie sci-fi \\"flying\\" sounds. Which is great but once again makes me really wish they would have used the classic and very distinctive King Ghidorah sound for button 1.

product_title: Panic Station
review_headline: Great board game fun, especially lovers of the move "The Thing"
review_body: First important thing: Get the new rulebook from board game geek.  [...]  On the bottom of the page there is a Files section with v2.2 rules.    This game is great fun.  Someone is not human and is trying to infect others. The humans can only win by having 3 gas cans and going to the hive.  The \\"board\\" is random and is made of cards from a deck. You explore by placing cards down to make the station larger.    If you enter a room with another player pawn, you must trade or attack. The host may infect (everyone starts with 3 infection cards) and the only way to avoid infection is to trade a gas can. The host needs to be careful because a blocked infection card will result in the other person claiming you are an alien. (Timing is important)    If your group may be interested, check out the rulebook v2.2 at board game geek.    The game comes with a nice tin to hold it together. I prefer tins because they are waterproof and do not degrade.    Definitely a favorite of mine.

product_title: Last Night On Earth - The Zombie Game
review_headline: cooperative competitive an oxymoron that works
review_body: Lately I have been branching out into the board game world of zombie survival horror. I haven't played them all but I was really taken away with this game. Almost every board game is competitive in nature with the exception of Arkham Horror and Hero Quest, to name a few. It is always hard to create a game that breeds true cooperation. When I say cooperative I mean your team wins not any individual players. In order to survive, and if the zombie plays is anyway descent, you will need to work together. Almost all cooperative board games still foster some sort of competitiveness with resources. This game is no exception, however you will most likely fail. It is difficult to pass over a weapon or item and jeopardize your own well being for the good of another player and the group but it needs to be done. With this game if you pass away one weapon you almost feel naked against the zombies. If you are selfish you will almost always fail. In defense of the people I played with we were playing a bunch of competitive board games over the weekend and thus we kind of foster this kind of attitude. It was really refreshing playing a true cooperative game.  About the game: The game utilizes cliche scenarios with cliche heroes but the game is anything but a cliche. While reading about the game a lot before I played it I thought I knew what I was in for. My biggest surprise that no one ever seemed to mention but you will realize quickly is that all houses pretty close to zombie spawn points. While it is absolutely necessary to get Hero Cards you are never completely out of danger and only a few turns away from getting cornered in a building. This game really feels like like you are watching a movie.  The only problem I have is with the audio cd they gave me. I happened to be so lucky that I had the Resident Evil 1 and 2 video game sound track and that works a ton better.

product_title: Mattel 1 Vs. 100 DVD Board Game
review_headline: Better than most, but that's not saying much.
review_body: As DVD games go, this is up there with Banzai as one of the best as one of the best DVD games yet. Unfortunately, some things keep it from being quite as fun as it could be.  Good things first. The game works like the first season's game, and rather remarkably (for a DVD game) it keeps the score for you. The set's there with a real mob and audience, plus Bob Saget himself. The questions are well written, and for a 16 year old boy can be kind of tough, though I've found adults find them rather easy. The helps work like they do on the show, save for the fact that you can choose whether to use the studio mob or the home mob, and the helps work slightly differently for each.  The game comes with some sets of cards, used by the mob members to lock in answers and identify themselves as in or out. In fact, the home mob is where the game really falls down. First of all, having to sit there while the One ponders on there answer is incredibly dull. Secondly, with no money at stake, there's no reason to want to be the mob. That's also an issue for the One. Why walk away in the first place? Finally, no One is ever going to use the home mob. The studio mob is almost always right, and the few amount of people in the home mob makes it more likely you'll get a wrong answer.  Last few complaints are to do with the editing. It's VERY repetitive. You'll see the exact same shot of a large, black girl in the audience bouncing in her seat constantly throughout a game. You'll here Bob make the same nonsensical statements every time. The tension (what little of it there is) is drawn out the exact same way throughout the entire game.  Basically, it's not bad, it's not great, and I'm too tired to really finish this review.

product_title: Discovery Kids Animated Jellyfish Lamp MULTI
review_body: My 6yo son recieved this as a Christmas gift. He was excited to set it up, but we were disappointed once we finally did. Plus, the jelllies hang near the top most of the time, unless they're being pushed around by the water jets, so their movement is of little interest  Educational Value: Litte to none. This is basically a fancy nightlight with 'swimming' jellyfish. The various colored lights are nice and soothing and do make a great nightlight, but that's about it.  Durability: We didnt experience any leaks, and the product looks and feels pretty well made. Its nice and hefty, especially once filled with water.  Overall: Disappointed, and im not sure how long my son will leave the tank on his shelf. We cleaned the jellies before inserting in tank, and waited patiently for 24hrs in the hopes that everything would start working properly and the jellies start 'swimming' somewhat naturally, but it didnt happen. We even gave it another day, but the jellies stayed towards the top of the tank, only to be pushed somewhat violently and unnaturally by the 2 water jets. I took the jellies out a few times to clear the small air bubbles out form under their mantles, in the hopes that would help make them neutrally buoyant, but the bubbles created by the water jets would get back under there, so it seemed like a loosing battle. Batteries havent been an issue yet, as i turn the tank off after my son falls asleep, so its not running all night (he has other night lights).

product_title: Bounceland Magic Castle Bounce House Play House
review_body: I bought this for my daughter's 3rd birthday (we also have a 1 year old). The packaging is surprisingly compact. I found the product mostly well designed and great value since renting a bouncy house would cost about half the price of buying this. The kids absolutely loved it. One complaint-- there is a side entrance that closes with velcro. This is a hazard since the velcro isn't strong enough to hold a child if they jump into it (one kid fell out, but was ok). After this happened, I tied the \\"door\\" closed with 3 shoe strings and now it is fine. There's really no good reason for the door and the manufacturer should remove this. I set up the bouncy house on our concrete patio and put a blue tarp under it to prevent abrasion. I also bought a box of 500 no-crush balls. The kids enjoyed these, but they really aren't necessary and actually make it harder to jump around. They also take up a lot of storage space so not sure I would recommend those although I think having an occasional ball pit will be nice for variety. In terms of size, we had at least 4 or 5 toddlers in there without any problem. 1 adult can lay down or sit inside but I wouldn't recommend jumping. The kids had a lot of fun on the slide, but it is also a bit dangerous if they aren't careful. I put some padding around the slide just in case. Wouldn't be a big deal if you had the unit on grass or something softer than concrete or if you have adults 'spotting' the kids on the slide. It's not as big as the commercial rentals, but it is super easy to set up and I've already used it about 5 days this month since her birthday. I'm really glad I bought this and highly recommend it.

product_title: Aurora World Esmeralda
review_headline: Honestly the best toy I've ever bought.
review_body:
When my senile grandmother's cat died last month, my entire family was convinced that it would be the last blow before she...you know...donated herself to the worms. Haha! Just kidding. I love the crazy broad. Anyway, since my grandpa died back in '04 she had spent every ounce of her tenderness and love on her Manx cat. Even though this provoked jealousy and other hard feelings among her children, I always understood. She and the cat had so much in common. Both were losing hair, both were over the hill, both had bladder issues, and both smelled awful to mention just a few. I encouraged this bond that they shared and this is why I had to think fast when we found old Silverwing stiff as a board on the kitchen floor.

This is where Aurora World Esmerelda comes into the picture. I hopped online and bought this cat with one intention: to hold my grandmother's attention until we could find her another really old Manx cat. After a couple of days (I had no fingernails left after waiting for shipping), the silly old woman started to notice the cat was gone. \\"Oh, it's nothing,\\" we told her. \\"Silverwing'll turn up!\\" And, boy, did she ever.

As soon as the stuffed cat came in the post I snuck into my grandmother's room while she was taking a little cat nap (pun intended!) and placed the new Silverwing on her lap. It made me sick to get so close to her, but I knew it had to be done. After a couple of hours, none of us had heard a peep and we were starting to worry. I went back into her room fearing the worst, but when I cracked open the door Grandmother was petting the stuffed cat as if it were Silverwing in the flesh! I mean, I've seen some funny stuff before, but this was a gas. One by one, I called the rest of the family upstairs to see the spectacle.

Turns out this additional laugh at my grandmother's expense wasn't a once in a lifetime experience. She's talked to, pet, fed, and even groomed the thing since the day she got it. As a result, thisbad boy gets 5 stars all the way across. I wouldn't, however, try to buy this for your girlfriend or wife. It's life-like, but only stupid people are going to fall for it (i.e. children and old people).

product_title: Melissa & Doug Wooden Shape Sorting Clock Educational Toy
review_headline: best melissa and doug toy I have bought.
review_body: I bought this toy for my daughters second birthday.  I was not expecting her to tell time with it yet, but she loves shapes and the rest of the melissa and doug puzzles.  I am glad to finally have found one hard enough that it takes her a while to finish.  I like that the shapes don't have the colors underneath so she has to think about the shapes instead of just matching colors.  I am excited that it will be able to teach her numbers, shapes, colors, the color wheel and time and that it is a toy that she can grow with over the next few years as we revisit it.  I really like this one better than most of the other melissa and doug products that we have.  The slot that the shapes go in is very deep so you can't bump the shapes and have them fall out.  I have some peg wooden board puzzles where the depth of the shapes location is simply not deep enough and pieces fall out.  I love that these pieces are really deep and hard too so there is no way that they can brake if they accidentally get stepped on.

product_title: Quadrilla Basic Set
review_body: My almost two year old got this for Christmas a couple of months ago after he played with it in a toy store for over an hour and a half.  NOTHING holds this child's attention for a hour and a half!!! I was a little hesitant to buy my toddler a toy that uses marbles as he seems a little young (we put them up). But this is his FAVORITE TOY EVER!!  He carries the box around the house yelling, \\"Marbles!!\\" at the top of his lungs most of the days so that I have to hide the dang box!  And, honestly, he is so absorbed in watching the marbles go down the run that he doesn't seem to even think about putting them in his mouth (and everything goes in his mouth) and he tries SO HARD to not knock it down--he is just still young. It is a little frustrating that I have to build the runs each time (it is a little confusing until you get the hang of it, but directions are easy) and that the runs are easy to knock down (I have thought about hot glue lol).  My five year old loves this toy, too, and is finally starting to build her own runs.  And it is so educational as you have to reason out how to put what pieces where and how to get the marbles to have enough speed to make it on the runs (physics and spatial reasoning).  But it is the best money I ever spent.  And definitely get the spiral (think how kids love the penny spirals at the mall) and the wooden ones--they last a almost two year old's daily play and occasional throwing.  The plastic ones do not last!  I am going to buy the marble pads to collect the marbles today, too!

product_title: YuGiOh 5D's Spellcaster's Command English Structure Deck [Toy]
review_body: i didnt buy this from amazon, i got it in store from a hobby store. This deck alone doesnt get you very far, hence why its called a \\"Stucture\\" deck. but if you have a few good spellcasters this is a HUGE improvement for you. all of my cards were outdated/old, so i got this to update my deck. i got this with a few synchros/tuners and now im VERY effective against my friends. NOTE this doesnt come with any tuners/fusions/synchros of any kind. you need to get those seperate. i kinda like the fact that it is that way because with no tuners/fusions/synchros you can make this deck to whatever you want. it comes with a guide that tells you how to use this deck, which is nice. theres a lot of good cards in this deck, except giant trundae is in this and thats banned so realistically you have 39 great spellcaster cards. i recommend (you dont have to, but this is what i did) that you get arcane apprentice, flamvell magician (2x), explosive magician, and supreme arcanite magician, polymerization( if you dont have one), dark magician. theres a lot of 4 stars and a few 2 stars so a 6 star synchro is best. with these you can make a magic wall then build up ur monsters then level you opponent. this deck is spell counter heavy. i use about 30 arcade tokens and thats barely enough.

product_title: I'am a Little Teapot * Singing Doll with 2 Teacups & Spoons Set

I expected to receive a baby as pictured, but we received a brunette baby with green eyes (same dress).  The baby has a cute face and nice hair, but the rest of her just looks kind of cheap.  I like that her body is soft (although of course, you can feel the hard speaker inside her).  The dress and booties cannot be removed, and the dress barely covers her in the back.  She sings \\"I'm A Little Teapot\\", and that's it...so she's a bit limited. review_body: I ordered this puzzle for my daughter. She immediately wanted to play with it when I opened the box it was shipped in. She is 9 months so everything still goes in her mouth, so I was cleaning it off before I let her have it. Good thing I did this because the finish was NOT sanded smooth. product_title: Battle Cry (2013 Version)
review_body:
Battle Cry is a two person Civil War game. I feel like it is somewhat of a cross between Risk and Settlers of Catan. The board is flat, and you place hex pieces to map out the battlefield with the appropriate terrain. Then, you place your pieces down. The rule book has a vast variety of different battles to choose from, and it maps out each one, telling you where to place terrain and troops. It also lets you know of any special rules for that scenario, how many cards you get, and who goes first. Setup time can be long, but oh, is it worth it.

Like I said, it is sort of like a cross between Settlers and Risk. It is like Settlers because of the hex-pieces determining terrain. It is like Risk in that you have your troops move around dice to determine if you roll a hit or not. You are given a set number of cards at the beginning of the game, and those contain the command orders you may play. You draw a new card at the end of every turn. When you play a card, you give orders to the appropriate \\"units\\" and that activates them to move and battle. Once battle is over and you've drawn your card, it is the other person's turn.

The goal of the game is to collect \\"flags\\" which are connected to units. As you kill off units, you get the last man standing who is holding a flag and that counts for one victory point. Each scenario has its own rules for how many flags it takes to win, but the typical number is six.

Each game takes around an hour to play after setup is done, and I have played around three games now. I have lost two out of three...but I don't really care because of how much fun I was having. Seriously, I cannot recommend this game enough and I cannot wait to play more. :)

review_body: These things harden very quickly, and you have to mix the cement/mould yourself (I wouldn't let a kid do this as it hardens really fast and requires some measurement). I mixed mine in a metal mixing bowl and had a terrible time getting the hardened paste out of my bowl. I recommend washing your mixing bowl immediately before the paste can set. If you are going to use the included strings to make ornaments, put the string in the plastic molds BEFORE you pour the paste in; it literally starts to dry in seconds and we didn't have time to get the string in some of ours before it was too late. The included magnets DO NOT stick to the back of the ornaments once they are dry - it's just a waste. But, it was a fun project for the kids, and if you take my advice on the timing of the mould and string, you should be fine.

product_title: Melissa & Doug Giant - Lifelike Stuffed Animal
review_headline: Got a faulty lion, but Melissa & Doug made it right!
review_body:
We got this for Christmas for my 3 year old son who is fascinated by lions. We already have the Melissa and Doug big Tiger for our five year old daughter who loves tigers, and it has been great.

That being said, the lion arrived with a hole in the furry part of the tail that needed to be stitched up. In the past month and a half another hole has opened up at the stitching in the \\"arm pit.\\" These were easy enough to mend, but things went from bad to worse as more and more of the stitching failed, eventually resulting in the tail falling off.

Needless to say, \\"Daddy Lion's\\" tail falling off was of real concern to my 3 year old.

I am going to contact Melissa and Doug, and will update this review to reflect what their customer service tells me.

EDIT - I spoke with a very helpful person at Melissa & Doug and sent them some photos, and a new lion is in its way. The customer service rep was surprised about the issues, and said that M&D might request that I send the original back (at their cost) so they can see what went wrong. I have updated the review from one star to three, and may bump this up more if the replacement is high quality.

FINAL EDIT - Our replacement lion arrived yesterday, and it appears to be the high quality that we have come to expect from Melissa & Doug. I am bumping my review of the lion up to 4 stars because of M&D's great customer service, and th apparent high quality of the replacement.

product_title: Banzai Falls Original Water Slide
review_headline: AVOID BANZAI BLOWUP TOYS - ANY POSITIVE REVIEW IS FROM A PAID EMPLOYEE OF BANZAI!
review_body: This is one of the worst designed $500 toys you will ever find and dangerous too!  The first one I bought about 4 years ago.  Shortly after the 30 day warranty expired, I noticed that when my son was at the top of the climbing wall (8-10 above the ground), that the top of the slide was starting to collapse.  I poured water over the entire slide and only found small air bubbles leaking at the seams.  Almost all the seams were leaking air, but by the manufactureres own admission, this was normal.  I went along with it.  A few days later my son fell off the top of the slide and was shaken up, but not seriously injured.  The top had collapsed and he fell nearly 10 feet to the lawn.  Upon closer inspection I discovered that it wasn't the seams that werer leaking, but the entire inner shell of the inflatable that was tearing from underneath the outer nylon fabric.  You will see upon close inspection, your slide will delaminate and the air will seep throughout the shell of the slide.  I tried to return it but the manager at Target said it was past warranty.  I called the manufacturer and they never called back after dozens of messages.  I called our state attorney general product safety department and am waiting to hear from them.  This is a truly unsafe toy and I only wonder how many kids have broken bones from collapsing the top of the slide.  Eventually, I bought another one, wrapped up the old one, put it in the box within the 30 day period and Target gave me my return.  Within a few weeks, the new had also started to tear from the inside.  I still have this one and will pack it into a new purchase and return this one as well.  It is a fabulously fun toy for the kids, but never would I expect the manufacturer to believe this is a $500 disposable toy after 1-2 months light use.  Save your money - by your kids an ATV or a pony!  May many others return their purchase as I have done - this company needs to do right by their customers and allow the return after more than 30days.  If anyone has written a positive review on this company or this product, I am convinced it is because they are working for the company or have otherwise been rewarded by the company to make some lame positive statements.

product_title: LeapFrog Leapster Learning Game Disney Fairies
review_headline: One of our favorite Leapster cartridges
review_body:
My daughter got this for her birthday, and it quickly became her favorite game. There are a few activities to choose from, each with its own level, so she can start at level one and make it harder as she masters the steps. She loves the butterfly game, where she has to match numbers to paint a butterfly different colors. There is also a number and letter game to catch baby fish in a water bubble and help them over a waterfall. My older son has also enjoyed playing this game (even though he says it's for girls!). His favorite part is steering the grumpy fairy, Vida I think, into flowers to gather pollen. You are supposed to steer her into letters or numbers the game asks for, but if you steer her into a tumbleweed she falls on her bum, which he thinks is hilarious.
Overall, it's a great addition to the Leapster games, and I am sure we will be playing it for months to come.

product_title: The Game of Life Zapped Edition
review_headline: A necessary paring down of a classic!
review_body:
I'll start by saying I've tried, on multiple occasions, to get my kids (ages 7,8 and 10) to play the old fashioned Life board game. They like the idea and enjoy it - but only for about 20-30 minutes before it really starts to drag. It's tough to even start a game you know will require their focus and an hour to play.

Enter the zAPPed version of the game! The iPad interface engages the kids, navigates you through the play and makes the overall experience much more interactive. The videos are a minimal addition that don't add much, but the kids liked them and they keep them focused on the game so I guess it's worth it! The guidance the app provides really streamlines things. The options to choose wedding type, baby gender and other silly graphics that get added to your avatar were very entertaining to the kids.

Overall they loved it and I enjoyed it and avoided the headache usually involved in forcing my kids to play something I used to play!

review_body: My son loves stealing our remote controls. I took the batteries out of a lesser used one for him to play with, but that was only a short term solution. I found this toy remote, and we've been very happy with it! I like that it's somewhat realistic looking, silver and not some bright color, so it's like Mommy and Daddy's. I was also happy to learn that the volume button does actually turn the volume up and down; at first I thought this toy was rather loud, but turning it down helps a lot! Yes baby can change the volume, but so far he hasn't turned it up more than a notch or two on his own. I also like that some of the songs feature a pleasant man's voice; the cartoony girly voice found on so many of these toys gets really old. The only improvement I could ask for is a lights-only setting, because when Mom and Dad are trying to watch TV, the toy remote's sounds can be distracting, but turning it off completely is more boring for baby. product_title: Star Wars: Saga Legends 2010 Galactic Battle R2-D2 SL14 3.75 inch Action Figure
review_body:
I saw this, and was intrigued by such a small R2 figure with electronic sounds. I took a look at it, and noticed that this time around you can tilt the three treads so that they all touch the ground flat at the same angle. This is an improvement over previous R2D2 figures that allowed you to extend the middle leg, but not adjust the feet to sit flat on the ground. The sounds are cute, and the light is nice, if not accurate to the movies.

There are a few drawbacks to this edition though. One is that the dome does not swivel at all. No doubt this is because of the electronics, but it would be nice if this was made clear on the package. Another drawback is that the third leg is permanently extended, so you cannot display R2 in his familiar two-legged stance. But the biggest letdown is that you CANNOT replace the batteries. This is marked on the package, but not in a large, noticeable typeface ( I misread it and bought the toy thinking they were replaceable, but I guess that's my fault for just skimming the small type ). This is a bit of a bummer, because once those sealed-in batteries are dead, that's it for the electronics. Then you or your kid will be left with a cute, but not very poseable, R2D2 statue.

Overall it's nice, and pretty accurate sculpt, but I don't know if a child would enjoy it as much as one of the more adjustable, non-electronic versions.

product_title: FurReal Friends Hop `N Cuddle Tan Bunny
review_headline: For The Bunny Crazed Child in Your Life
review_body:
The Furreal Friends Hop 'N Cuddle Bunny (Tan color) is a nice toy for a young child. Rabbits are one of the more popular animals with little kids, and a stuffed animal like this that the child can control is a great idea, particular for a young girl like my niece who is completely bunny-crazy, and may be too young to own the real thing.

The bunny has a switch with three settings located on the bottom hidden by a velcro slot. \\"Try Me,\\" for temporary activity, \\"Off,\\" and \\"On.\\" The \\"on\\" switch activates the one minute sequence of crawling in a circle approximately 3 feet in diameter (going clockwise), with occasional stops, sitting up, and various noises that I suppose to the right young person could be considered endearing. The sequence lasts long enough for the bunny do do a little more than one circular loop. It worked just fine on our carpet. I haven't tried it on the hardwood.

The \\"on\\" sequence will stop after about a minute, but if you gently brush a switch located on the bunny's lower back near the tail, the sequence starts again. My niece quickly figured out the mechanism, and sleeps with the bunny next to her, occasionally pushing the button if she wanted some motion or sounds. It stops after a short while if she does not.

The construction seems reasonable. The faux fur has been sewn over a hard shell animatronic body. There are pink pads on the bottom of the bunny feet. So this bunny is not squishable, and may not give the best hugs. I clicked four stars on the durable, but of course it hasn't been in action long enough to judge this.

However, I have noticed that she prefers her animals to make friends with each other and converse. After quickly learning the geometry of the pattern, she sits another animal where she expects the bunny to be at the end of its circular path, then begins narrating the important commands, statements, and then, when the bunny finally gets to the other stuffed animal, friendly greetings are exchanged between the two stuffed acquaintances. Adorable.greetings are exchanged between the two stuffed acquaintances. Adorable.

product_title: Palco Beast Water Balloon Launcher
review_body: First off, I love this slingshot.  It perhaps may not be able to shoot 300 yards, but it can probably come pretty close to it if not make it in absolutely perfect conditions.  My two friends and I, who are all big guys, manned this slingshot, trying to make it go 300 yards, and I'm not so sure how far it went, but it was far.  We were shooting on the top of a hill that was probably 200 yards away from a football stadium that can seat 6,000 people, and we were launching the balloons over the wall of the stadium and landing 2/3s across to the other side of the field (from sideline to sideline, not from endzone to endzone).  So we were higher up than the ground on which the balloon landed, but I'd say it could've been 300 yards.  Anyhow, it definitely can shoot over 200 yards pretty easily with some strong handlers.  One thing I don't like about the slingshot is that the balloons often bust in the pouch when you let go.  I think it's because the pouch bunches up after a few launches, so I always unbunch it before launching.  It still busts balloons even after doing that, but I think that's somewhat expected with a slingshot that has so much power launching fragile, thin balloons that are meant to pop when touched.  The balloons are pretty small, but that's by design and necessity.  The portable water bottles that are to be used to fill the balloons seem pretty worthless although I tried them maybe once.  I just use the hose end converter that works much better.  The product is durable, although I'm thinking that the elasticity of this product may lessen over time due to the fact that latex and rubber gets brittle over time.  We'll see.  Everything wears eventually . . . except McDonald's food. haha  Oh, and I suppose that this product is educational because you learn about Newton's law of, for every action (pulling back the sling), there is an equal and opposite reaction (a balloon going really, really far).

review_body: The ShockWave 26 Brushless RTR is a pretty good boat for a newbie.  The boat is FAST! It's so powerful, you can get it to stand on end and pirouette!  Likewise, it can be flipped, but only if you drive it wreckless!  I purchased a POV MAC-10 4 GB Mini Action Video Camera and we attach it with Velcro to the top deck. I like to chase the ducks and geese, so watching their reaction is interesting. Actions shots of the other boat is pretty cool too!  My son and I both have one and we've learned a lot.  Lessons learned:  - Get at least one extra battery; highest mAh rating you can afford. I purchased two extra Dynamite 7.4V 5300mAh 2S 25C LiPo Battery Pack, Hard Case: TRA, and I've been pleased with their performance.  - Secure the cockpit and hull opening cover better than it is out of the box. Between the two of us, we've lost three cockpit covers and two hull opening covers. They come off pretty easy and sink right to the bottom of the lake! I opted to screw mine on to secure it. My son went the velcro route, and glued a piece of styrofoam inside the cockpit cover.  - When the boat starts to slow, get it to shore. My son has a small boat we use to retrieve the boats when they run out of power or otherwise get stuck.  - Becareful lubricating the shaft. I followed the instructions, but have had a heck of a time securing the shaft back to the motor coupling. It seems to be tight, but once I run it a minute or so, the shift slips and I'm DIW.  I have a new shaft and coupler on order, so I'll see if I can get it fixed with that.  It's a fun boat. I highly recommend it!

review_headline: This toy just keeps us buggin
review_body: Be aware this toy is not for little ones. It takes time to prepare and fine motor skills to clean up your bug. A couple of tips; give things plenty of time to warm up and cool down, while your waiting for the eggs to warm up, put clear tape around the sides and bottom of the mold before you put it in the frame, this prevents the substance from leaking, just in case it doesn't seal. Put some petroleum jelly on the plug if you want to fill your bug with goo, this makes it so you can pull out the plug with ease. If you want to keep your bug remove just the top mold and set it out in a cool dry place overnight, then lift it from the mold, clip and trim it up, voila, a creepy crawly to last. This is like an art and science project combined, there will be some mess, but it is so worth it. Have fun!

product_title: A Game of Thrones: The Board Game Second Edition
review_headline: The Rules Aren't So so Bad!
review_body:
So like everyone else, I recommend the game, both to players of deep strategy games, and people who just like Risk. I played this with some old friends of mine. Historically we would just play Risk together, but they were all up for something new. Everyone had a blast. The game is so much mor complicated, but it's so much fun. No one felt overwhelmed by the team all of the rules had been read.

The four of us who originally sat down to play the game chilled and ate while I read the rules and we made sure that we could comprehend them. That part took 3-4 hours. It's a long rule book. BUT then someone's brother showed up, right as we were getting ready to play. So we cleared off the neutral pieces for House Tyrell's territories and I regurgitated the rules back to him. With the help of everyone else, it only took 25-30 minutes. Then we played one round and my other friend came over. So we decided to reset everything and give him House Martell. This time it only took 20 minutes to explain the rules. Granted he's a smart guy, but still.

After that, we got down to playing. We only made it to the end of round 6 and it got to be midnight, so we decided to end the game there and House Baratheon, who still sat the Iron Throne influence track, chose the winner. The game is amazing, and really, rules that can be explained in 20 minutes aren't so bad. We kept the rules handy while we played, just for clarification, but we didn't need them very often (just to clarify what could and couldn't be done to, in, or from ports) and everything went fast enough that we never got bogged down by the rules.

The opportunities for deception and alliance are a lot of fun, and it's nice to have a game that has unofficial alliances built in to it. Whoever starts as House Baratheon is going to at least be guaranteed fun in the beginning, also, because they decide all non-combat ties until they're knocked off their claim to the throne. That element was a lot of fun, even playing as House Greyjoy. It was always interesting for everyone to turn towards Baratheon to hear his verdict. It keeps everyone involved in the game, and the way that turns are played out meant that there wasn't a lot of downtime between any particular players active times.

House Martell won our first game of only six rounds without even battling anyone. He was tied with two others for first and Baratheon (who was still in position to decide ties) picked him for being a good neighbor. Mr. Rogers was right!

Honestly, I think I would recommend this game to anyone who enjoys strategy games (simple like Risk, or complex), A Song of Ice and Fire, or someone with 5 good friends who want to have some good wholesome fun.

product_title: Beyblade Stealth Battlers -  Tempo Hammer Hit
review_body:
My son was very eager to try some of the new Beyblades that jump and have arms or projections that pop out. Tempo Hammer Hit was near the top of his list. He has enjoyed Beyblade Metal Fusion for a few years now and wanted to see how this new Beyblade stacked up to his favorite Pegasus Beyblade.

Tempo Hammer Hit has two hidden hammers at opposites sides of the plastic disc that makes up the Beyblade. When contacted during a battle, the hammers will pop out and hopefully knock the other Beyblade over, thus winning the battle. Our main concern was that having just two hammers would unbalance Tempo Hammer Hit preventing it from spinning easily or continuing to battle. Another worry was that the hammers getting hit by the opponent Beyblade would cause Tempo Hammer Hit to be knocked over and stop spinning. Indeed, this seems to be the case some of the time. I'm assuming it depends on the angle in which the released hammer hits the other Beyblade. It seems to be about 50/50 whether it helps or hurts the opponent. With those odds, Tempo Hammer Hit is not a go-to Beyblade if you want to win, but it's a fun twist on the usual Beyblade battle.

product_title: Taj Mahal
review_body:
One should not ever put the words \\"Taj Mahal game\\" and \\"fascinating\\" in the same sentence.

This games lacks a lot when compared to other Knizia designs, like AMUN-RE.

But the game has a different purpose. It is meant to be a fun, fast and entertaining card-based game for 3-5 people. And it works on that level.

Each player visit (or not) 12 provinces in Northwestern India. Each provicne has a number of cities. They fight, by using their cards cleverly, to get Influence Points, by controlling military, religious, economic and social forces (amongst others).

Good game, but simply not breathtaking like DOMINANT SPECIES or really engaging like STONE AGE or POWER GRID, or even LANCASTER and SHOGUN.

review_body: We did a lot of research when it came to purchasing our son a battery powered vehicle.  We decided on the Power Wheels F150 because of the monster traction and all the great reviews. My husband, a machinist, took it apart and noticed a gear in the rear drive motor is stripped.  He also noted that it appeared the motor was not mounted straight causing extra wear on the gear.  Unfortunately, we have to take it to an authorized service center to have it fixed and it is impossible to get anyone from Power Wheels on the phone to discuss the issue.  Every time we have tried we get the same message, \\"all switches are busy\\" and the phone hangs up.  Extremely poor quality and customer service.  We'll be replacing it with a gator.

product_title: Zone 60 Special Metallic Edition Video Game System
review_body:
I bought this because i wanted the experience of the Wii's motion sensor, but i didnt want to pay $250. After buying this, i would gladly pay the 250 Dollars for Nintendo Quality, or any quality really. Do not be fooled by looks, this is NOT motion controlled. thats right, this IS NOT A MOTION controller.

There is a sensor inside the controller that detects when your controller is moving suddenly, similar to a wireless gamepad sending the response of the \\"A or X button\\". the game then reacts. the game does not actually capture any movement, or show your movement on the screen. thus, it is as motion controlled as the buttons on your TV remote.

To give you an idea of how bad it is, Imagine repackaging 60 Sega Genesis non-licensed games into a $30 system, 49 of which are as shallow as Pac-Man, the other 11 being So Called \\"motion controlled\\" which half the time doesnt pick up movement.

Simply put, DONT BUY THIS. if your a parent, don't buy this unless your children are blind. Buy them a Wii or dont. Getting this for your kids will make you look like the failure of a parent in the neighborhood, as well as subject your children to ridicule.

product_title: Rummikub -- The Original Rummy Tile Game

product_title: 1:18 Dukes of Hazzard General Lee
review_headline: A Great Re-Pro of a Classic TV Show
review_body: Friday nights in the late 70s/early 80s had many watching the \\"two modern-day Robin Hoods\\" battling corruption in a place called Hazzard County. Their famous car, the General Lee, carried them along on their adventures. The car is so well known enough now it goes down in TV/film fandom history alongside the 1966 Batmobile, the Black Beauty, Chitty-Chitty-Bang-Bang, and the Munsters' car, just to name a few. This die-cast reproduction of the car is almost perfect in every detail with the exception of possibly the plates being bare. On other versions the Confederate flag is on the front and back (probably because they never really said which state the show took place in, although it is common knowledge they originally filmed on location in Georgia). It would have been a nice touch to have a flag or something instead of just empty plates. All-in-all a great die-cast model to have if you or someone you know is a true-blue 'Dukes' fan.

product_title: Crosswise Transformers RID R.I.D. Robots in disguise Tiny tin 2003
review_headline: A Transformer even Hot Wheels fans will love
review_body:
In 2001, Hasbro revamped Transformers by bringing back a story originally from Generation One in the 1980s: the heroic Autobots fighting to stop the bad guys--the Predacons, in this case--from stripping planet Earth of its fuel resources. For the series, they imported molds from Japan while also using a few different molds from different prior series to create new characters. Among them was a group of Autobot mini-cars called the Spy Changers, each of them (save for four molds originally planned for Generation 2) being repaints of figures from a Generation 2 sub-team called the Go-Bots (no connection to the Tonka series from the 80's). Crosswise is one of them.

Sculpt/Paint
Crosswise is a reuse of the Generation 2 mold used for the characters High Beam and Bumblebee, along with the 1995 Botcon exclusive female Decepticon Nightracer. Here, he is molded in translucent plastic, with blue highlights inside most of the parts. The wheels are molded in black plastic with vac-metallized hubcaps. The underside (which is also his chest) is molded in red solid plastic. The only paint details on this figure are silver (on the engine in the back, his head, and the tampographed X on the hood of the car mode), black (on the windows), and red (for the spoiler and the bottom of the doors (which become his arms in robot mode). Overall, this is an interesting color scheme, and it gives the bot a distinct look and feel.

Transformation
Transforming the guy, like the rest of the figures in this sub-team, is very easy: first, pull the back of the car out, so that the legs are seen. Next, pull the doors out until they can freely move. Finally, flip the hood downwards until it becomes the chestplate. Then stick the red gun in either of his hands.

Playability
These types of Transformers aren't exactly poseable, as they can only move at the arms. However, in vehicle mode, they can be compatible with some Hot Wheels or Matchbox race tracks (as evidenced by the size of the vehicles and the axle configuration). These are definitely for the younger set of Transformers fans.

Conclusion
This is a TF that you can give to a younger fan-to-be to give them their first taste of the fun and exciting world of the Robots in Disguise.

product_title: Barren Glory (Magic the Gathering : Future Sight #3 Rare)
review_body:
This card is a final act of desperation to win a game. While it may be a powerful enchantment, the conditions it requires to trigger its effect very rarely seem to come about. To get this card out you need at least two land on the field and some way of adding four more mana to your pool, which will likely just be four more land. From that point you must have no permanents on the field, meaning you need a way to get rid of that land you already laid down and some way to either play all your cards from your hand or something to discard your hand.

I would definitely not build a deck around this card, especially when you consider having more than one of these on the field would mean they cancel each other out. The only way this would be worth having in your deck is if you know you'll be up against decks that run cards that destroy permanents and keep the field clear.

Suffice it to say that my friend runs this card in his white/green deck as a fail safe and he has never won a match because of it.

product_title: Thunder AC6 Smart LiPo Balance Charger/Discharger w/ AC Adapter for 1-6 Lipo/ 1-15 Nimh + USB to PC Software
review_headline: Great all around charger at a great price
review_body: I've recently gotten back into the RC hobby after a long while  I used to love operating RC cars back when I was young.  Having purchased a couple of hobby grade cars and batteries to go with them, I knew I would need a hobby grade charger.  The wall warts that come with most models or batteries are next to useless, being that they take upwards of 4-5 hours to charge a battery.  This is due to a low charge rate, sometimes as low as 0.5 amps.  After some research, I decided on the Thunder AC6 charger.  It charges all types of batteries, such lead-acid, Ni-Cad, Ni-Mh etc.  Another great feature is the fact that this charger has an integrated balancer.  This is convenient because you don't need an external one.  I've used this charger to charge a variety of packs so far.  4200/3000/1200mah 7.2v NIMH, 2300mah 9.6v, and 7.4v 2S LiPos.  It has performed flawlessly on each pack.  You can set the peak capacity or the charger will auto detect it.  It has a temp sensor, to make sure your packs don't get too hot while charging, and a USB cable to connect to your computer so you can see the details of each of your packs as it charges.  My 4200mah NIMH packs charge in under an hour.  Its great being able to charge so quickly.  You are able to enjoy your model more, instead of waiting and waiting to recharge.  The only drawback is if you have some high capacity multiple cell LiPos, such as a 6S pack.  The charger is limited to 50 watts, so when you have those larger packs charge time will take a while.  But for the majority of street and offroad hobbyists, this charger should work just fine.    It includes a variety of plugs to accomodate most any pack.  Tamiya, banana, alligator clips, glow plug, receiver etc.  The only two notable plugs that it is missing are Deans and Traxxas, but they are both easily and cheaply available here on Amazon or on the web.  Enough rambling.  The Thunder AC6 is a great charger for most any hobbyist who needs a versatile unit to handle all their charging needs.  The price cannot be beat either.

product_title: Spin Master Games Quelf Board Game
review_body:
\\"Quelf\\" is pretty much the ultimate mixture of [[ASIN:B004YDFG12 Candy Land]], [[ASIN:B001RNAAIG Guesstures]], [[ASIN:B0036RNWPY Trivial Pursuit]], [[ASIN:B004LYP0HY Gotcha!]], and some other game that hasn't been invented yet. However, if you haven't heard or played all of those games, you're still going to have a fantastic time Quelfing.

The game starts out with each player (there can be up to 8) choosing a character the play with. All of the possible choices are extremely out-there and zany, already warning the players that this won't be a serious game in the least. Characters include Super Ninja Monkey, Biscuit Farmer, Queen Spatula, Mrs. Pickle Feather, and more.

Once you've selected who you will be playing as, a roll-off ensues to determine who goes first; the players then continue their turns in a clockwise fashion. After the first player is chosen, he or she will roll the dye and obviously move forward the number of spaces that the dye lands on. This is where the heart of the gameplay begins.

There are 5 different colors on the board, representing 5 different kinds of cards you will pick up in your turn:

BLUE = ROOLZ CARDS ~ These cards put a rule into play that either everyone must obey or just the person who picked the card must obey. They last until the end of a game or until a new card specifically says to remove them. Examples would be \\"everyone must end their sentences with 'izzle'\\" or \\"you must snort every time you laugh\\". Breaking a rule gains the rule breaker a penalty.

GREEN = QUIZZLE CARDS ~ Whoever lands on this color turns to the person to their right and waits for them to read them a quiz question from the card. Some of the questions are trivia (What word in the English alphabet rhymes with no other word?), some questions are based on guessing the correct answer (From the following options, choose the height of the shortest man who ever lived.), and some answers are puns (How far did the cow walk into the woods? Answer: Halfway. After that he was walking out of the woods). Getting a main Quizzle question wrong results in a penalty, but if there is an extra credit question, you may be able to still move forward.

YELLOW & PURPLE = STUNTZ and SHOWBIZ CARDS ~ These cards are a bit crazy and had all us players groaning in anticipation of what our card would have us do. There really isn't a difference between the two cards except Showbiz is more of a performance while Stuntz is more a silly challenge. A Showbiz example would be to yodel while sticking your finger up your nose. A Stuntz example would be stuffing as many items down your shirt as you can in a certain amount of time. Not completing or failing your card results in a penalty.

RED = SCATTERBRAINZ CARDS ~ There are two topics on these cards such as \\"Breeds of Dog\\" or \\"Foods Vegetarians Will Not Eat\\". The player who drew the card must choose one of the topics. Then, that player names an item that fits under that topic, and you go player-by-player, each naming an item that goes under the topic. This card is over when someone repeats an answer, gives an unvalid answer, or takes too long to give an answer. That player who loses gains a penalty.

The winner is the person who makes it to the end of the board first.

The age recommendation is for 12+. I could honestly see some kids who are only 10 playing the game. There doesn't seem to be anything inappropriate in it, although some challenges include kissing or serenading someone with Shakespeare.

The first time I played this game, I played with three people. We had a blast and much preferred this game to another game that we played that same night. The next time I played, I played with six people. We didn't finish the game, because after about 45 minutes of playing it we were a little bit tired of silliness. However, I can almost promise you that each of those people would love to play the game again someday.

Do I recommend getting this game? Absolutely! Unless, of course, you don't like silly, fun games and would rather sit around watching the news instead. The only negative that I have about Quelf is that after a long time of playing it in one night, it's easy to get a bit sick of it; but isn't that true of most games? There are many cards for each color, making it definite that I won't start reusing cards for a long time! After having it for only about a month, this has quickly become one of my favorite games. I Quelf as much as possible; what about you? Have you Quelfed today?
