product_title: CitiBlocs 100-Piece Natural-Colored Building Blocks
review_headline: Great Fun for All, Inspiring Imaginations
review_body: We tried these out at a Maker Faire booth and our little one (~14 months old) spent the majority of her time playing with these blocks! We promptly went home and purchased some! At first we built towers for her to knock down, now she can stack them and build basic things on her own. product_title: Spy Gear Night Goggles
review_headline: pretty fun, but for little kids

Especially with a small child.  The Pros are: They are fun, they are cool for a kids to have, they are durable for the most part,but remember,   THIS IS A TOY! product_title: Hot Wheels Monster Jam World Finals Stunt Stadium Set

product_title: Creatures - The Card Game
review_headline: Lots of fun for all ages!!
review_body: This card game is a riot!! My friends and I had an awesome time mixing and matching animal sections. The coolest part is that there are animal facts at the bottom of each section of the cards. If the animal is all put together, it reads a true fact about that animal. If it's mixed up with other animal sections it creates whole new types of animals that can do all kinds of amazing things. The pictures are made simply and each section matches up almost perfectly with every other animals' sections. The rules are simple, build an animal from one head, one middle and one tail end. Then, battle them against the other animal creation. Whoever has more animal points wins the round. product_title: Blink Card Game The World's Fastest Game
review_body: Sort of like Bejeweled with cards -- the one minute version of Bejeweled that is!  You could also compare it somewhat to Uno, but its a head to head race, and it actually has more strategy than Uno.    You get 3 cards, each with one to five of several possible shapes, in one of several colors.  You try to make matches to two running piles with any card in your hand by color, number or shape, and also plan runs to get rid of multiple cards in your hand in a row. For example, if you see 1 grey tear drop, you might put down put down 1 green tear drop, put down a card with three of a different green shape, and then put down a card with three of a different shape/color.  All the while you are drawing cards as you play them so that you constantly have 3, and continuing to plan to get rid of as many as you can, as quick as you can.    Its not quite as deep as Bejeweled because you'll rarely run out of moves regardless of how good your strategy is (remember there are two active piles and your opponent is quickly placing cards) and speed of recognition is therefore more important than deep strategy, but its basically the same type of game play as one minute Bejeweled -- make matches, make em quick and plan a little if you can.  Having an opponent makes up for the perhaps slightly more shallow game play than Bejeweled.    I wish the shapes were a little less exotic.  Tear drops, moons and the others take more getting used to than basic shapes like squares and circles would.  However, this is a very minor quibble, its a great game.    As many have said in other reviews, the age range on the box is silly, and kids younger than 7 can play easily, and play well.  My six year old is pretty good (doesnt need a handicap, or at least not much of one) and doesnt cheat.  How cool is it to play a skill game that uses the brain with your 6 year old and have them beat you?  With some other thinking games he gets intimidated and will cheat or whine, but Blink is so easy to get that he justblazes with it.  There is a modest luck factor, so if your reasonably close in ability, different folks will win.  Plus, as many have said, its super easy to give a handicap by having one player take one or more extra cards.  You can very easily invent 3 and 4 player variations, but the gameplay does suffer a tad from the logistics of more people trying to slap down cards and fewer cards per player.  Still fun, but if you want to routinely play 4 player you may want to buy two decks.

product_title: North Star Games Wits & Wagers Family Card Game
review_body:
I really loved the game itself. It seemed that North Star Games had done a wonderful job of presenting a cute, eye appealing game. I personally enjoyed the fact that it was a trivia game, as I tend to know lots of strange, useless trivia. 6 year old daughter's thoughts-She loves the little cards to write her answers. She thinks the questions are funny. The game is technically for age 8 and up, so she played on my team. She understood HOW to play, but the questions werent things she would have known the answer to.

The husband's thoughts-Well, he didnt like it. He likes trivia, but more history type trivia. Trivia he deems 'useful.' When the first question was: 'How old was Miranda Cosgrove (iCarly) when she started her show?' and it was followed up shortly after by 'What year did Barbie get a belly button?\\", DH was completely turned off by the game. And, I guess the cute little Meeples are not as thrilling to a guy. YES, the girl's team won, so maybe that had something to do with it? :)

So, sadly, he wouldnt play again and it left me unable to play again since, though she was interested, Mustang couldnt play alone. I am looking forward to the holidays and hope that others at the family gatherings will want to play, because I really did like the game and would like to play it more.

product_title: Fisher-Price Kid-Tough See Yourself Camera
review_headline: A great hands-on camera for little ones
review_body:
My two-year-old is obsessed with my digital camera. He loves to take pictures and videos and then watch himself. Unfortunately, I'm a little nervous letting him handle an expensive digital camera. This Fisher-Price-Kid-Tough Camera is the perfect solution to my problem. It's definitely durable enough to take the drops and bumps that will inevitably take place. It's easy for him to use. It didn't take long for him to figure out how to take a picture. The See Yourself feature is fantastic. He loves watching himself on the screen.

CONS:
*It is SUPER easy to delete pictures and videos on this camera, so if your little angel takes a great picture you may want to upload it as soon as possible. I think my son had just as much fun deleting pictures as he did taking them.
*It does NOT include a USB cable, so keep that in mind. They're not very expensive, but with the price of this camera, I wish one would have been included.

All in all, it's a great little camera for little ones. It's easy to use, durable, and my son really enjoys using it. Picture quality is decent, the images on the view screen are not as clear as those on my own camera, but they definitely get the job done. As a mom, it's great to have my own camera back again :-) Everyone is happy.

review_body: It looks like Amazon Prime is no longer available for this product, which is a bit of a downer.  My family really enjoys Futurama, and my dad often quotes bender, so I bought this as a birthday present for him and he loves it. With Prime it got there right on his birthday and everything.  It's of solid quality, great colors, and great packaging but leaves me wanting a bit more:  His arms and legs are a little flexible (and his arms rotate at the shoulder), which is nice, but I kind of wish they had ball joints where they connect to his body for more posing options.  It would be pretty sweet to have him sitting on something instead of just standing all the time.  Also worth noting is that his arms come out of his shoulders at about a 45 degree angle (not straight in the picture)  His quotes come in loud and clear, but there's only 12, so admittedly they've gotten a little stale.  I'd like to see \\"neat!\\" or \\"abandon ship!\\"  Comes with three sets of eyes: open, half-mast, and angry.  He could be better with a little bottle of LöBrau or BendërBrau, or a head in a jar, or cigar... something.  If you take a corner off of one of the sets of eyes you can also get Bender's excited face.  I still think it's pretty great, even though it could be better. Certainly the best reasonably-priced Bender figure around, and as such I highly recommend it for fellow Futurama fans.

product_title: LeapFrog LeapPad1 Explorer Learning Tablet, green
review_headline: So Far, So Good! (Realistic (and Somewhat Sarcastic) Point of View)
review_body: Soooooooo, I Bought The Leap Pad For My Sons 4th Birthday. Of Course Like Many of Us, I Have Read Reviews Over and Over Again and Contemplated About The Price, Etc. This Is Review Is For The Realistic Parent...  1. GRAPHICS - Let Me Just Say My Son Is 4 and Like Most Kids HE DOES NOT CARE ABOUT GRAPHICS OR HD! So If You Are One of Those Parents Who Want A 1080 Resolution For A Child's Toy, GOOD LUCK. The Clarity of The Product Is Good. The Pics Are Clear and That's All That Matters. The Animation Is No Different Than A Kid Would See On Nick Jr. 2D Basic Stuff.  2. DURABILITY - I Have A Very Rough Son. He Throws His Toys, He Steps On Them On Accident, Etc.  This Is A Pretty Durable Product. I Have Read That Parents Would Rather Buy There Kids An IPAD. Sorry, But This Single Mother Doesn't Have $400 To Waste. I Barely Had The $100 For This Product. But I Can Guarantee That If My Son Steps On This Leap Pad, It Will Be Just Fine. I Can't Guarantee That w/ An IPAD! LOL.  3. PRICING - Yeah The Pad and The Apps Are A Little Steep. But $20-25 Isn't To Bad If You Ration It Out. No One Said You Have To Buy 10 Games Right Away!   4. Everything Else. He Has Been Playing w/ It For About An Hour Now and He Has Already Learned How To Take Pictures, Has Went Thru The Alphabet and Paint Tools. So Obviously He Is Enjoying The Chance To Explore His Toy. It Was Fast and Easy For Me To Do The Registration and Download The Games. I Can't Believe People Complain About Things Like That. 20 Minutes Out of Your Life Shouldn't Be That Bad. And You Don't Have To Sit In Front Of Your Computer As It Downloads The Apps. Can We Say MULTITASK?  Overall, I Am Happy w/ This Product. I'm Happy He Is Enjoying Learning How To Write His Letters. His Happiness Is All That Matters...  FYI - Mine Came w/ 4 Standard Apps and One Free Download.

product_title: Wireless Gaming Receiver for Xbox 360
review_headline: Great, but need to manually install driver for 64bit computers
review_body:
Ok this is pretty solid receiver and feels like it is a legit product. I like to save money as I hope you do as well.

The only problem I found is the drivers, they don't load automatically, you have to install this manually. Which is easy to do.

I am posting this so you do not have to dig through all the links and forums to get this to work.

\\"Googling will bring up a few solutions for this issue, but I found only one works. These are the steps I took to install the drivers for the device:
- Install the official software: google \\" Xbox 360 Wireless Controller for Windows \\".
- Start -> Search for \\"Device Manager\\" -> Open it
- Find the \\"Unknown Device\\" -> right click -> properties
- Driver -> Update driver -> Browse my computer -> Let me pick from a list of device drivers on my computer
- Double click \\"All devices\\" -> Search for \\"Microsoft\\" in the left pane and select it -> Search for \\"XBox 360 Wireless Receiver for Windows Version: 2.1xxx\\"
- Choose \\"Next\\" and complete the install

The \\"Unknown Device\\" should then disappear from the devices list. I was then able to sync my existing wireless XBox 360 controller (which came with my XBox 360 console) with the adapter by pressing the large \\"X\\" button on the controller to wake it (it should start blinking), then pressing the button on the adapter (its light should start blinking), then pressing the receiver sync button on the controller (a small button in between the left shoulder button and the central top port of the controller). After a few seconds, the controller and adapter lights stopped blinking, leaving the top left light of the controller lit (the Player 1 state). Viola! Done.\\"

After the install, I played with the newest games, Skyrim, Deus EX: HR, RAGE. You will want to check if your current game supports a game pad.

Using Xpadder made this work for any game that has to use the keyboard, even flash games.

Have fun playing games.

review_body: These planet marbles are beautiful and nice to display, but they don't get played with very often.  I'd say they are better for looking and learning than actual play, but cool none the less.

product_title: Kid Galaxy RC Bump 'n Chuck Bumper Cars
review_body: The first complaint I have about this toy is that it requires 10 batteries. That seems extreme for little bumper care. The second complaint I have is the ability to steer these cars with the remote. They did not turn well or go over anything. They are however cute, and the little men shooting out is cool, as well as the ability to switch channels to control the other person's car. The colors and presentation were good. The educational value is nil in my opinion, as this seems more for just fun. My son liked them but he gets frustrated by not being able to control them well, but he is younger the the recommended age group. Over all an okay toy, but I would not have been pleased had I paid for this toy, especially with the amount of batteries it takes.

product_title: Mega Flier - Clown Fish Giant Inflateable RC Flying Fish
review_body: I'm very disappointed in this toy.  We bought one for my 5 year old son and filled it at the local grocery store.  It cost $10 to fill it with helium, and the very next morning we discovered it has a slow leak.  My son has played with it for less than a day and now the tail keeps falling off because it's loosing so much helium.  I can't express how disappointed I am in this toy, and for the price it should last much longer than it has.  I am going to try and exchange/return it to give it another try only for my son's sake, but will have to incur yet another cost to fill the new one.  Overall, the assembly is complicated, filling the helium is cumbersome and costly, it does not have the same fins as pictured,  and it's not very durable.  On the positive side, it is fun to play with and easy for my 5 year old to operate.  In the end, don't purchase this unless you have $50 to kill on a balloon and can deal with the complications & disappointment.

product_title: 100% Compatible with Pink Lego - The Princess Carriage
review_headline: It would have been great if it was Lego
review_body:
My daughter opened this set right after she got it for her birthday. She commented that it was really pretty and she loved the horse but \\"it doesn't stay together\\". My son's response was \\"that's because it's not made by the Lego company.\\"
Often times you get what you pay for. The problem is that if this set had been a genuine Lego set, you would still have paid about the same price for it as you are paying for this generic knock off. The quality on this set is what you'd expect to get at the dollar store. The helmet popped off the driver's head continually. The wheels fell of as the carriage rolled forward. Then the back of the carriage followed soon after...every time. The princess didn't stay put on the horse's back but kept popping back out of position. The princess is solid white and the set comes with two paper doll dresses that you layer over the neck before putting the head back on.
The set is indeed Lego compatible, as they claim. That is something anyway.

product_title: Tomb Raider: Lara Croft 12-Inch Action Figure
review_body: Lara Croft is amazing!Other than BloodRayne,Tomb Raider has always been a favorite game and Lara has been done with exact video game detail of the character.Lara has outstanding articulation from the boots to the great facial features.Her shirt even shows wrinkles of being worn while the gun holders and belt are realistic as can be.Lara also comes heavily armed with 2x pistols,1x shotgun,1x grenade launcher,and 1x excalibur sword.The sound chip in the back can be loud,but that's better than not being loud enough in my opinion.She has sayings that match from the video game using an electronic voice box.This version of Lara is more of a statue than a figure in the fact that it does have some poseability but it can be fragile if you are to rough with it.I would recommend Lara more for collectors who know more how to handle a display piece.Lara has a ball-jointed head piece,swivel wrist and feet,while her arms can also be moved up and down.The cool thing is that Lara has a more solid,non-plastic build to the body and legs for a more realistic look.Lara is one of the sexiest video game characters around and this 12-inch version does her justice.Bottom line Lara is a well-made,high quality,10 out of 10 figure/statue that is well worth the time to get.This is a great addition for any Lara Croft and Tomb Raider fan.Lara Rocks!!!

product_title: Phoenix R/C Pro Simulator Version 3.0 with DX5e
review_headline: This is where you start to learn to fly an RC Helicopter(Get Non-Radio Version)
review_body:
IIf you want to learn to fly a RC Helicopter this is where you start. Welcome to the adventure. The first thing you need to do is get the version of this that doesn't come with a radio. You will want to buy the [[ASIN:B001OYDG8Y DX6i Transmitter Only MD2]] radio. This radio will carry you through the Blade 450 and you can bind up to 6 aircraft to it and it only cost 160 buck which is dirt cheap for what it does.

When you get this program download, make sure you download the Blade mCP X as this is what you are going to buy further on down the road (Just go ahead and down load everything but especially this aircraft). Next download the mCP X Spektrum DX6i setting from the web (Something to note, on the helo, the collective channel is reversed. In the sim you need to set it up in the normal direction).

Now you have the radio you are going to use to when you get your helo, you have it set up the same way as you will use it, and you have the helo modeled in the sim. You are pretty well set up for success now. One thing to note, is the sim is easier in some ways and more difficult in some. Also, there is a big difference between sitting in front of a screen and having this little angry bee flying at your head. So keep that in mind.

Before continuing, I will answer your question about why the [[ASIN:B0058IOEF6 Blade mCP X Bind and Fly RC Helicopter]]. There are really 3 main reasons, the first is it doesn't have a stab bar. To compensate for that, this helo is actually comparatively stable. The second and most important is damage resistance. I will tell your right now. You are going to crash. Even after hours in the sim, you will crash. Got that. If you, use your throttle cut before you actually hit anything, it is very likely, this helicopter will be flyable after the crash. This is because of the light weight and lack of a stab bar. Almost any crash with the 450 is going to put it out of commission (weight and stab bar). The 3rd reason is repair costs are very cheap. If you think I am off the mark on this, try flying the Blade 450 or Trex 600 in the sim. See how many times you crash)

I tried to learn to fly a RC helicopter twice before the mCP X and came away frustrated and significantly poorer both times (Hirobo Shuttle and TRex 450).

Start with the sim and you are going to save tons of money and frustration. With your radio hooked up to the computer and the Blade mCP X running, practice your hovering (The sim has hover training but I personally did not find it very useful Hover nose out until you can stay in one location. Hover nose left and right until you can do the same. Hover nose in. Now do all of the same upside down. Practice 30min a day every day. After a few months, maybe sooner, you should have your hovering down. Don't get frustrated, these little things are incredibly difficult to fly. The biggest thing you are going to do is make your control movements to big. If you are conscious of the stick moving, your movements are too big.

Once you have that down, get yourself a Blade mCP X BNF and start your practice all over again. Move slowly Don't expect to be able to do in real life what you can in the sim but you will be able to move rapidly because of your practice.

Ok so I talked about how to learn to fly, but why this simulator. The main reason is it has the Blade mCP X. Period. However, I will say I have a very old computer and this program runs very smoothly on it. So that is another plus. I have seen some people knocking this sim because it has picture environments instead of 3D. My response to that is big deal. I really don't care that much about the environments and picture allows this to run smoothly on a slower computer. Everything I have seen and read about this sim says it is realistic. I would agree with that statement as much as any sim can be realistic. (Blade mCP X experiences tail blowouts and nose rotation during autorotations which does not happen in the sim)

As far as the training and lessons go, I am not really impressed. There is a ton of work that needs to be done to make these more useful learning devices. The programmers of this program should look at what was done in any of the Gran Turismo to see how they could make the training much better. You will need to come to this program with your own training syllabus. As I said before, there is an autorotation and hovering training mode. The hovering mode gives you 1 control at a time. Maybe useful for starting but you will quickly outgrow it. Additionally, there are some demo lessons but the instruction goes far too fast to keep up with. The training part really needs to be re-thought and improved.

The extras can be useful and fun. One extra is balloon pop. The nice thing with this is it takes your conscious mind off of flying and put it on hitting the balloons. As they said on Last Samurai, some times you have \\"too many minds\\".

Overall, this is a great program which is an invaluable tool to help you learn to fly RC helicopters. product_title: Kotobukiya Star Wars: Darth Vader "Final Battle" ArtFX Statue
review_body:
This is the fourth time Kotobukiya has produced a Darth Vader statue in the ArtFX line (five if you count the smaller ArtFX+ version). At some point you have to wonder if there's any point when there are still so many worthwhile characters Koto has yet to tackle at all. To be fair, this statue does make some improvements over the previous versions, but it has a couple flaws holding it back from greatness.

The previous Vader statues have been based on Episodes III and V, whereas this one is meant to depict the final battle in Episode VI. That's where the light-up feature comes in. The lightsaber and belt panels light up, but also one of the helmets glows to simulate Vader being electrocuted by the Emperor. The glow effect works well, although it's a bit of a hassle to activate. The switch is located underneath the head, forcing you to remove and replace it every time. By comparison, the Darth Maul ArtFX only requires you to twist the hilt of the lightsaber.

The biggest improvement with this version is build quality. Koto's older ArtFX statues sometimes feel a bit cheap. My Episode III statue even has some fraying plastic slivers in spots. This one feels much more sturdy and has better paint application and texture. Also a plus is that the display base is actually useful. On the Episode III version, the statue becomes completely unstable when you attempt to insert it into the base, forcing you to either reinforce it somehow or just display it without the base. Though this base is just as light and hollow, it supports the rest of the statue nicely.

However, there's one significant problem, and it'll probably affect whether most people buy this statue or not. The pose is slightly bizarre and not very accurate to the film, or even very Vader-like in the first place. The pose shows Vader simultaneously attacking with his lightsaber and preparing to leap. Or maybe he's simply buckling from the Emperor's lightning. Whatever motion the sculpt is trying to convey, it's not well suited to the character. Vader isn't meant to be flexible; all four of his limbs are prostheses, after all.

Update: A couple other points worth noting now that I've had the statue displayed for a week. First, the pose isn't exactly as it appears in the promo shot. The lightsaber is held at a different angle and faces more forward. This is true with all statues, but it's best to either view the statue in person or at least seek out some pics taken by actual owners before buying. Also, Vader's size is a little off. The ArtFX statues are supposed to be 1:7 scale across the board, but this one seems closer to 1:6. The difference isn't that notable, especially since Vader is a large fellow anyway, but some collectors are sticklers for consistency. Granted, it worked out better for me since a lot of my other Sith Lord statues are from Gentle Giant and are 1:6 scale.

Build quality has improved, and the light-up function is neat, but the sculpt is a definite step backward. Perhaps this pose will make more sense when the inevitable Palpatine companion statue is released. I'd recommend this piece if you can find it for a discount (I bought it for $65 from Thwipster). But I wouldn't bother paying anywhere near the $150 MSRP.well suited to the character. Vader isn't meant to be flexible; all four of his limbs are prostheses, after all. ASSEMBLY:  * For the first few months, we had to help my daughter assemble the tracks, but at 2.5, she now does it on her own. product_title: Estes 2157 Saturn V Flying Model Rocket Kit
review_body:
One of my All Time Wants for model rockets, the Saturn V is a nice, large and gorgeous rocket. And, depending on the time you put into it, a very nice piece to keep on display.

First recommendation - save EVERYTHING! Typical of most (I hope!), I did not thoroughly read the entire instruction set before starting construction. There are several steps that use what would otherwise be thrown away. Centering Ring center punch outs and styrene trim need to be saved for later use in the build.

To keep the price down, Estes incorporates a couple steps that I'm not overly pleased with. One is that this model a single engine rocket mount - D class. I would have much preferred a 2 or 3 C cluster option and let this thing fly higher than 150 feet. This is the rocket that put man on the moon after all.

Also, assembly of the angled Body Tube step down sections just doesn't feel sturdy. They are party why this rocket is rated as a Skill Level 5 build. Precise alignment is manageable but aggravating. I 1/2 expected these parts to be pre-cut balsa instead of thick paper edge glued to centering rings. I was wrong.

Guaranteeing a Skill Level 5 build are the styrene molded parts. Perfect cutting of these parts is almost impossible. Keep plenty of fine sand paper around - I actually used several metal files for trimming. Gluing styrene to the BT is an adventure at minimum. Keep liquid plastic cement and\or Super Glue nearby as the ends typically lift during drying and need more attention. At the bottom of the rocket, the bell housing fairings and fins are combined styrene forms - the fins being 2 halves glued together and sanded.

Overall this is a very challenging and time consuming build compared to other Estes models but also very enjoyable. You will feel a sense of pride and accomplishment when completed.

It's a Stetson and it goes oh so well with a bow tie and braces.  Likeness is up to par with past 11 figures.  And it somehow manages to get past the horrid curse of a figure with an accessory molded to its head...whether it is a pair of glasses (tell me ONE figure with glasses that looks good in this scale) or a hat.  Looks like it came off perfectly to me.  Ready for the showdown at Lake Silencio.

product_title: Fisher-Price Topzy Tumblers Twirlin' Tumblin' Fun Park
review_headline: Interesting toy.  I was entertained for a bit even!
review_body:
This is an interesting toy to watch. The little characters are irregular sized, kind of like two spheres squashed together on top of one another and weighted in such a way that they tumble through this toy, where other figures wouldn't - so beware - don't lose them!

Assembly is easy and quick, don't be daunted by that. I think it took me longer to get it out of the packaging than assemble it. Batteries are included which is nice.

The thing I like best is that this thing does not play endlessly. It will go through one \\"cycle\\" which is fairly short actually then it shuts off until the button is pressed again or the bar on the front is rotated, and then it will do another cycle and shut off again and the processes is repeated as many times as the child activates the toy.

My only complaint with the toy is that after the characters slide down the slide they don't always make it up the \\"stairs\\" on the buttons that pop up. For my toy the rate is about 50% for this. I think it's they just don't have the momentum from the slide and they don't quite make it all the way onto that first button on the stairs that will pop them up to the next stair. This is a minor complaint though because normally my 13 month old won't let the characters GET that far anyway. He's grabbing them at the midway point and repositioning them somewhere else or doing something with them. Rarely he just watches them go all the way through.

product_title: Small World
review_body: Smallworld manages to get pretty much everything fun about conquest games absolutely nailed, while doing away with a lot of the tedium and adding in a delightful sense of humor.  The scaling map sizes are designed perfectly so that no matter how many you're playing with, the world really is just too small for the lot of you and somebody is going to be getting conquered.  Simple but fairly deep gameplay, massive variety of race/power combinations means every game plays out different (with a few exceptions) and a genuinely charming visual aesthetic have made Smallworld probably my current favourite board game.  The only real gripe is that some combinations (flying sorcerors, for instance...or nearly any power attached to Trolls) are bordering on imbalance and can, especially if attained early on, weigh the game so heavily in one persons favour that it would take an equally ludicrous combination to close the point gap.  Fortunately the sheer variety of powers and races means that the insane ones show up rather rarely, and most games are that perfect balance of silly and competitive.  Highly, highly recommended.

product_title: Crayola Model Magic Jewelry Studio
review_headline: Beautiful beads in a short time but it stains
review_body: We gave this set to our 8 years old daughter. She loved and enjoyed every minute playing with it.  All you have to do to make jewelry is to take small pieces of the dough and roll it in your hands. You cal also twist many colors together then use the manual bead spinner to create beautiful, colorful beads. Let the pieces dry for few hours then glaze them. Our daughter enjoyed using the glaze because it gives the beads a nice shiny surface. I played with her and I was amazed at how easy it was to work with the dough. It is not as hard as regular play dough so it is easier to mold.  The set came with plenty of modeling dough and pendants to make lots of beautiful pieces of jewelry.  It did come with only two pair of earrings, but my daughter hates earrings so that was not a problem.  I wished that the packaging was bigger and that there was more space to hold the dough; the instructions suggest that you keep the material in Ziploc bags to prevent drying.  Also, be very careful with the dough, it does stain almost everything (walls, furniture, clothes.) The playing area has to be protected to prevent any damage.  It is a very nice set that keeps my daughter busy for a long time.

I'm sure as both grow the gloves and length will fit better, at least until age 8-10, depending on how big the boys grow how fast.

I honestly have no clue why I was prompted to rate the gloves \\"education value\\". They're gloves. Superhero costume gloves.

Ultimately we are very happy with these gloves.

product_title: The Thanksgiving Game
review_headline: Now I'm Thankful for My Elders
review_body:
With Black Friday Eve -- aka \\"Thanksgiving\\", in some circles -- approaching, I decided to get into the gobbler day spirit. It may not have the sugar-fueled mania of Halloween or the raw consumerist frenzy of Christmas, but I still found plenty of opportunity to get my turkey-themed freak on.

I'm always looking for something -- anything -- to liven up the Thanksgiving dinner experience. If I wanted to sit in a room staring at the family for four hours, I'd stage another intervention for Uncle Pete. Lord knows the last one didn't take.

So I picked up this game to play at the holiday table, after we're stuffed on stuffing. In the description, the makers suggest \\"a prize be offered to the official winner, such as candy, a plant, or a new Christmas decoration\\". Those don't sound much like 'prizes' to me -- we'll be playing for cold, hard Thanksgiving cash. That's how my family rolls.

Good thing, too. We played a practice round over the weekend, and I cleaned up. I scored eighty bucks and a gravy boat off of Grandma alone. And I've been practicing in the meantime. Assuming she's got any dough left by the time Thursday rolls around, this is going to be the best Thanksgiving EVER!

product_title: Zhu Zhu Pets Deluxe Playset Giant Hamster City Sky Mall Includes Pinkie YoYo!
review_headline: Lots of Fun, Assembly Manageable - INSTRUCTIONS HERE
review_body:
Contents: This comes with the garage/car and drive-in movie-theatre (each sold separately), 2 hamsters, an elevated room, a floor-level room and lots of tunnels/ramps.

I'm glad I took the chance and let my daughter use her birthday money for this - she had her heart set on it so I decided to take a chance in spite of the other reviews. She's been playing with it very happily non-stop for the last 3 hours.

My six year old and I put it together in an hour and 15 minutes, including re-arranging to interconnect it to her existing 2 rooms and castle. If we had gone just for the mall itself, we'd have been done in an hour. It was a little tedious but not too painful to assemble as far as kids' toys go.

Assembly Instructions:
- Print out a copy of the color-coded picture provided by another reviewer. The text probably won't be legible, but the colors help. Consider printing out these instructions as well (copy & paste into Word or Wordpad then print)
- Unwrap everything in the box, keeping the instructions but throwing away the plastic & paper wrappers
- Match up colored covers with white floor pieces of the same shape & size (great kid contribution), snapping on covers as you go (kid can hand off to adult if the snapping is too difficult). There will be a few short white pieces without covers left when you're done.
- Assemble the garage (it has its own instruction sheet to help)
- Put 3 supporting legs on the elevated room - one on each side. Add on the signs.
- If you are building the sky mall approximately as shown on the box, use connectors to assemble sections of 2-4 pieces each (one of the instruction sheets has tips on how to use the connectors). Pay attention to which direction each piece of tunnel curves. If you look at the original Sky Mall instruction sheet carefully, you can see which sides the hinges are on. But don't sweat it if you can't tell - for most of the pieces, the curve is obvious enough. Use the color-coded printout to help figure out which pieces to put together.
- Lay out the sections in their approximate positions in their final destination (you won't be able to move this intact). Do not hook in the other connectors yet - just let things rest against each other loose. If hooking in other rooms/kits, re-arrange things now to figure out how they're going to fit together. If something that should fit together has a big gap, check to see if a tunnel section needs to be reversed. The \\"straight\\" pieces are slightly curved, so flipping one around can solve a 4\\" gap at the other end of the ramp.
- When everything is positioned well, go back and add connectors to all the in-between pieces.
- Add the remaining support leg to the flyover ramp.
- When all connectors are in place, go back and look at the connections again since putting in one connection can loosen another. They need not be perfect, but if there's a gap of more than ~1/8\\" on the floor of the connection the hamster is likely to get stuck.
- Take a picture of the finished product from up above so you can replicate it later after you child takes it apart and wants you to figure out how to get it back to the way it was. :-)

product_title: Puerto Rico
review_body: First of all, let me start by saying that this game is longer than your average game. When we play it we anticipate about 2 hours, sometimes a little quicker and sometimes a little slower depending on how distracted we get and how much discussion we get going. If you can accept that fact that the game will last longer than Uno, or Yahtzee, or Clue-then you can have one of the funnest game experiences of your life (yes, I know \\"funnest\\" is not a word). Many other people have posted some wonderful and in depth reveiws of what this game is like, so that is not my goal. I simply want to state that it is amazing! I love other games, like Settlers, Stone Age, Pirate's Cove, Dominion and Ticket to Ride. This game is my favorite and it is because there a still some luck (based upon what other people do for their turn), but your brain can get blown away with trying to figure out your best move, while not helping the people after you. My favorite experience with this game was with my wife's friend and her husband. We were on vacation and played games until 4AM. This was the final game and it took about 2 1/2 hours to teach and play through the first time. After that we were all super beat so we went to bed. The next morning the husband and wife practically jumped out of their room and said \\"I kept waking up thinking about what buildings to buy and how to make more money and ship more goods, we need to play again right now!\\". I am addicted to this game and my only complaint is that I dont get to play it often enough. This game honestly isn't for everyone though. We have some friends where the husband loves it, but the wife needs a little more \\"stimulation\\" for her gaming desires and she gets bored with it. My wife and I love it and teach to it everyone that we can because it is crazy addictive and almost always spawns some good talking afterwards and is a GREAT way to spend time with friends and family.

product_title: Lionel Little Lines Polar Express Train Set
review_headline: A great train set for smaller children
review_body: I had trains when I was a kid, and so did my dad. I still have my trains and will give them to my son when he's old enough, but not yet. For now, there's Lionel Little Lines. The box says ages 2 1/2 and up, and it's true. This is a real train set, but made of plastic and way more durable than the big boy trains.    Our house is completely tile, and I fully expected the Little Lines engine to be smashed in days or weeks. In fact, I watched my son bounce the engine off the tile many, many times. It just keeps on working. Easy on batteries, simple remote control, and the track snaps together extremely securely. While certainly not the kind of toy that becomes a classic, it is indeed a toy that will last.    Like another reviewer said, it is quite loud and there is no means to adjust the volume. I'm thinking the speaker covering technique is a simple and effective idea- if that doesn't work, I'll solder a 100 ohm resistor in series with the speaker. That will definitely reduce the volume.    I'd rate this toy a best buy, if your kid is interested in trains. It is tough, simple, fun, and cheap.

product_title: Melissa & Doug Deluxe Wooden Railway Train Set (130+ pcs)
review_body:
I have never taken the time to write a review for anything I've purchased, yet I use reviews all the time to determine items that I want or don't want to purchase. I was so extremely pleased with this purchase I felt I needed to share.

We bought the M&D train set, table and Suretracks for my son's 2nd birthday. I was fairly certain i was going to be pleased with these items based on the reviews, but I was more than pleased! As other mention, the train set doesn't have a lot of fillers and it takes up almost every inch of the M&D trainset table. I cannot imagine we will use the table for anything other than a train table because the train set isn't something you want to take apart and put together a bunch of times. I would HIGHLY recommend purchasing the Suretracks with the train set. One box of Suretracks will secure about half of the trainset (that is suspended), so we had to purchase another box to secure the whole thing. The suretracks really help as little hands and bodies can easily tip over the suspended sections leading to major meltdowns. Another poster commented on the height of the table. My son is 2 and is extremely tall for his age and i think the height is perfect, simply because the table is long and wide, therefore he has to lean over to reach the middle of the tracks. If it was much higher he wouldn't be able to reach the center. The tracks are also compatiable with Circo (target brand wooden tracks and trains) and Thomas (wooden).

I did a lot of research and in my opinion this is without a doubt the best deal for your money. My son LOVES playing with his train set. As far as the table is concerned scratching easy, etc... we haven't had any problem with that yet, but i am not too worried if it does. I don't expect any children's toy to remain in mint condition, that is just me. I also think the drawer is a nice feature. Is it huge? No... but you can definitely store several items in there and it is a nice perk in comparision to other tables..

review_body: If you plan on purchasing any of the other Perplexus game balls, I would definitely recommend the Perplexus Rookie as a starting point. The original Superplexus is exactly that, SUPER it's built like a bowling ball, they are extremely rare, but with some persistence and the will to pay the price (you should be able to get the old Superplexes for around $50 US and that's including shipping), they can be found and purchased, my experiences, most of them are available from England. The original Superplexes has basically the same maze, as the new Perplexus Original, the maze walls may be a little shorter or not there at all, in some locations, and the original Superplexes has an electronic timer with sound effects (the sound effects could very well drive a normal person insane, fortunately they included a button to turn the sound off, if you prefer. Be warned once you pick it up it's next to impossible to put down, and another warning is, beware your sanity may be at stake.

review_headline: Not as good as I was expecting
review_body: Tygra is my favorite Thundercat and I was really looking forward to get this figure after it was announced. Also, they are very difficult to snap and keep in the arm peg.  * The hands joints are blue and the feet joints are flesh instead of the other way around.  * The arm and leg accessories look bulky.    I was expecting a better figure akin to the Masters of the Universe Classics line. Instead, this looks like a regular toy for a kid and not a collector's figure as I read somewhere that it was supposed to be. I guess kids will have a great time playing with it because of the articulation which makes possible lot of action poses. I also have the Lion-O figure and that's better than this one. Even the old 80s figure was more representative of Tygra than this one. Do not pay more than retail price for this.

product_title: ThinkFun Shape By Shape
review_body:
Thinkfun is leading the pack in producing excellent games and/or puzzles for all ages.You may remember the name Binary Arts;well it is the same company,just a new name.
This game is a first cousin to another one of their games Square by Square;see my Review dated September 15,2011.It is a little more challenging however.It consists of 14 geometric shapes which must be placed in a tray.It comes with 60 cards in the drawer.Each card is a different challenge.There are 6 red pieces and 8 yellow pieces.Each card gives a figure shape that is to be made with the red pieces.Once that is done,the remaining 8 yellow pieces must be placed in the tray filling the tray.This game is quite similar to that classic Chinese puzzle Tangrams.
Tangrams has 7 pieced while there are only 6 red pieces to complete the figure;therefore a little easier.The larger challenge is to fit the remaining 8 yellow pieces into the tray.Another difference is that of the 6 red pieces there are 3 pairs of shapes, and with the 8 yellow pieces there are 4 pairs of shapes.None of the red pieces are the same shape as the yellow ones.There is no differentiation shown as to the difficulty of any of the cards,although I found that some cards were a little more challenging than others.You will also notice that on the back of each card there is a hint, as well as a solution.You should be able to solve each card quite quickly ;well under a minute each.I found it interesting to check the solution after I got all the pieces in;as quite often my solution was different.You will also notice that there is a fair amount of symmetry in some solutions and none in others.
A game that will be a lot of fun for all ages;and it can even be played by more than one by shuffling the cards and keeping times for each to complete a challenge.One can even compete with themself by choosing a number of cards and tracking the time to complete them all.There are numerous ways to use this game and all will provide lots of entertainment.How about competing in teams? There you go;a great game where you can use your imagination.ent.How about competing in teams? There you go;a great game where you can use your imagination.

product_title: Classic Beanbag Chair - Cotton or Hemp
review_headline: chair is not white like in photo
review_body:
This is a classic bean chair. I purchased it as I thought it might make a comfortable TV chair. It's very well made and Eco which is wonderful.
The color is actually a natural looking kind of beige, not a pretty as the white in the photo. I ended up sending it back because when u sit in it, it's very low to the ground & it was like doing a squat every time I had to get up. Hey, I love exercise , but not when I'm relaxing after they gym. WARNING, it cost me almost as much to ship this item back as it did to buy it. Even though it only weighs 13lbs it's over sized and everyone from FED-EX ground to UPS wanted 99.00 to return. This is a great fun chair for the right person. The chair is SUPER comfortable , well made, and doesn't stink of any nasty smelling toxic beads or fumes. It has large stitching which reminded me a bit of a baseball & it has a huge zipper which would have looked nicer if the color of the zipper actually matched the bean bag and was not a dark brown. product_title: Project Runway Rockstar Style Compact Fashion Design Sketch Portfolio
review_body: I bought this notebook for one of my nieces (age 8) and she loved it.  I had already bought a couple for my daughter (also age 8) and she's been entertained by them for hours on end.  We took them on vacation with us this summer and they worked out great.  With one of these and a box of colored pencils, my daughter had a great portable form of entertainment that she used in restaurants, on the plane, in the car, and at her cousins' houses.  I give them five stars for portability and entertainment value.  If you're shopping for a child who's interested in art or fashion, these notebooks are great because they allow endless creativity and combinations while at the same time giving some guidance (in the form of stencils and the pre-printed models on each page) so the young designer is not completely on his/her own in trying to draw something he/she can be proud of.  So I also give them five stars for creative value.  I would say these notebooks are educational in the sense that they can help develop drawing skills.  My daughter often uses a combination of the stencils and her own freehand designs now.  And if they can make her forget about the TV or computer for even an hour, they are certainly worth the $5-$10 purchase price.  The plastic (vinyl?) stencils are pretty durable, and another idea is to make some copies of the pages with the models printed on them, so that when the notebook pages run out, your child can continue to design with the stencils.

review_body: Just thought you all would like to know this:    He saved six soldiers' lives -- with a child's toy  Remote-control model truck checks for explosives -- and triggered a deadly bomb  [...]    ....    In 2007, Fessenden and Guy sent Fessenden's brother, Staff Sgt. Chris Fessenden, a radio-controlled (RC) model truck outfitted with a wireless video camera to help him check for bombs under trucks and search for improvised explosive devices (IEDs) on roadsides in Iraq. product_title: Star Wars Episode II 12 Inch Ultimate Jango Fett with Missile Launching Backpack Figure
review_body: I bought one of these Ultimate Jango Fett 12inch pack years ago to add to my collection since I bought anything Jango Fett related I could find at the time. This is easy to use and assembly can be a bit tricky since some of the armour pieces like the knee gaurds warped, so they don't stay attached. The chestplate is two pieces that snap together but with constant use it can break. I suggust once you have all the armour on you do not remove it, that way you won't wear out the velcro or any of the snaps. The paint job on mine was pretty decent, with only a little bit of the facial stubble appearing to be \\"off\\". There are two sets of hands that you can pop off, however I found these very hard to attach and reattach, so I left the orginal arms on and did not change them after that. Lots of little pieces that tend to fall off or don't seem to fit anywhere like the Kamino dart--I just set that off to the side since there was no clip or anything for it. Shin gaurds and other leg pieces do fall off if they are warped or if the velcro is loose. Overall I wouldn't give this to a child because of the small pieces and I would be afraid of the pieces being broken by \\"play\\". Quality isn't as high as I was expecting, but it's about the same as any other action figure you might find. Good gift for an older Star Wars fan or Temuera Morrison fan like myself. Not too posable either, can only do a few different poses. I suggest using a doll-stand to prop this guy up since he'll probably just fall over.

product_title: LeapFrog LeapPad1 Explorer Learning Tablet, green
review_headline: Almost worthess; not worth its price.
review_body: My family bought this toy as a surprise birthday present for my younger brother.  However, I think he found his new pair of pants more exciting.  Out of the box, before setup, it's useless.  How would your child feel if he clicked on the \\"My Books\\" button and saw no books on the shelf?  After setup, it's not much better (we still have no books...).  In our experience we have had many good products from LeapFrog, but this is not one of them.      Long Setup Process  --------------------  The setup process required a Ph.D. and a computer scientist about 45 minutes of pain.  In fact, we encountered errors in the software when we first installed it.  We had to reconfigure our firewall for no aparent reason.  The actual syncing/updating process took about 20 minutes.  The software is for Windows and Mac only; open source users are out-of-luck.     Slow Speed  --------------------  The pad is sluggish.  If you push a button you will have to wait for a second or two before the next screen loads, at least.  The software that you install on the computer is just as bad.  This does not even slightly compare to any tablets recently on the market.    Extras start at $10  --------------------  No games/books come pre-installed.  You can only get one for free.  After that, it's $10 for each game/book, at the minimum.  That means if you want 100 games, you're out $1000.  There are also no books pre-installed either.  That means unless you buy more this is worthless.  How much did an iPad cost again?  The iPad and iPod Touch (which is not that much smaller than this product) come with plenty of free games available.     Fraudulent Reviews  --------------------  It seems that many of the 5-star reviews are written by people who were given Leappad Explorer with games pre-installed.  I quote Jared Castle who wrote \\"We also purchased the LeapFrog Explorer Learning Game Star Wars: The Clone Wars, not knowing the tablet would come pre-loaded with apps for the review.\\"  These reviewers didnot have to fuss with installing the software or paying for them.  This provides them with a fundamentally different experience with the product.  Perhaps for $100 this would be a decent product if it came with games and books, but it does not.    Also, beware of reviews outside of this site.  NPR says that this is an iPad for kids.  In our experience, this is just not true.    Poor Packaging  (difficult to return)  --------------------  The packaging was difficult to open, and was designed to be torn.  This makes it almost impossible to return.  You can say goodbye to your $100+shipping now.

product_title: Playskool Step Start Walk 'n Ride
review_headline: Not as sturdy as it looks

Your child has to already be pretty well-balanced in order to use this toy because otherwise it tumbles over since it's so light weight. My son was 10 months and was extremely eager to stand up and hold on to this toy while walking, but every time he'd get up and hold on to it, it would fall over causing him to get extremely frustrated. He got another push and walk toy that was a fire engine and was MUCh more sturdy that he had no problem at all with(it didn't tip over easily). I don't really recommend this product unless your child is extremely steady on their feet and good with their balance already. But for me, that's the purpose of this toy...to help them with their balance, which I didn't feel it did for him. NOw that he's a bit older and steadier on his feet it's fine, but like I said before it just made him really upset that it kept falling over.

product_title: Game Matt Variation
review_body:
I've been using Chessex battlemats for several years. I have yet to have one wear out on me. I now have four of them for various situations. The smaller ones are good for small dungeons/lairs or even doing encounter by encounter. They make bigger versions, the megamat and the mondobattlemat. The latter is HUGE. You can fit many a dungeon completely within its borders meaning the party can just explore and go.

Tiles? Pfft. What a pain. With the Chessex mats you can map anything, any time, anywhere, any genre. I wouldn't trade a single battlemat for every tile collection in existence.

You want the double-sided version, because one side is 1\\" squares, and the reverse is 1\\" hexes. I use the squares for dungeons and the hexes for outdoor encounters, towns, etc.

Use ONLY Wet Erase Pens! As other reviewers have noted, the dry erase markers will not come off.

product_title: Nerf Vortex Vigilon Blaster
review_body: Just got this blaster, the latest in my ever-growing collection of Nerf blasters, and while I do like it, there are several cons.    But first, the positives.  It's a solid blaster, and I love the design.  It has a very durable feel to it, not that I plan on pistol-whipping anybody with the Vigilon.  The clip release is quick, and the disc eject switch for jammed discs is a good feature. The discs do travel a bit farther than the darts, maybe an average of five feet farther.  It also has the tactical rail for attachments, and unlike in some N-Strike blasters, the rail is not located in an awkward place.  It's right over the barrel, so it won't interfere with the slide-loader.  There's a slight improvement on accuracy, in that the discs don't fly as wildly as Nerf darts will in a pitched battle.  Also, they still don't hurt if they hit you, a plus for little Nerf warriors.  The discs are more solid than darts, so they won't get destroyed as easily (a major plus considering the cost; see cons).  Now to the negatives.  The discs fly farther, true, but they seem slower.  If you're firing from a great distance, your target, if he can see it coming, can easily dodge the disc.  But when you hit your target, the disc may ricochet in a more random direction than a dart, and farther too.  I wouldn't recommend this for office Nerf wars, since the discs are more easily lost in the nooks and crannies of the cluttered cubicles.  A major negative point, considering these cost a lot more on Amazon.  Looked at the refill price, and it's almost the same as a blaster (the refill costs more than the Proton!).  What's up with that?  And they do cost more than darts, so losing them is a big blow.  Not sure how to rectify this, except maybe making the discs much brighter, so they stick out.    So while the Vigilon may now occupy a space in my Nerf arsenal, I think the old reliable Maverick will still be my sidearm of choice.  I may use the Vigilon in a sniper's role, considering its range.  But before I do that, I'll be sure to stock up on extra ammo, anticipating major losses.

product_title: Marvel Superhero Squad Series 19 Mini 3 Inch Figure 2Pack Taskmaster Deadpool
review_headline: Two of the best figures in this line!
review_body: Once my daughter started playing Marvel vs Capcom 3 with me, she quickly got some new favorite superhero characters- Deadpool and Taskmaster. When I went to see if any Marvel Superhero Squad figures were made of the two, it turned out that they were both available in the same pack...and they just got re-released! Needless to say, I ordered these guys immediately. There's a tiny problem with them that's common of the figures in this line, but the bottom line is that these two translated to Superhero Squad form perfectly.    Deadpool has more articulation than I expected. You can move his head, hands, arms and waist, making for some pretty fun poses. They did a great job with adding little details to him, like the wrap on his katanas, buckles on the straps on his boots, and even some grenades on the back of his belt. They sure didn't skimp out on this figure! He stands up perfectly and looks pretty cute for a crazy moonwalkin' mercenary. Taskmaster looks really good too, though you can only move his arms up and down. Just like Deadpool, the detail is all there, like the little pouches on his belt. He can stand up without falling over as well (I bring this up after the Sentinel problem in my review for that toy). Unfortunately Taskmaster got the short end of the stick in the paint department, and while Deadpool looks perfect, Taskmaster has some missed areas like on his boots, and too much paint on other parts, which caused little globs. If you're an adult collector that cares about the paint, don't order these- just go to a store that has them and check for the best ones. However, I ordered these for my daughter and she loves them! She already played Don't Break the Ice with Deadpool in the place of the ice skating bear, and then had Deadpool fight her MODOK and Iron Man Superhero Squad figures shortly after.    These are great little toys to get, and I wish something like this were around when I was little. Deadpool and Taskmaster are fan favorites, and I can see this pack selling out once again. Get them while you still can, before they end up being another Beast/Iceman pack.

product_title: Barbie Collector Pirates of The Caribbean: On Stranger Tides Captain Jack Sparrow Doll
review_body: To start with I am a collector of Jack Sparrow figurines, and this little guy was my twenty-fifth Jack!   Quibbles first----He does not have the long string of beads that hang from the left side of Jack's hair. His hair is pretty well detailed so it seems like they could have added them. Of course, I do realize that they might be more of a choking hazard for smaller children. He doesn't have a compass or a pistol, but then again they would be choking hazards. And personally, I wish his beard braids were a bit longer.     But on the positive side---His vest is beautiful, I love the details of the buttonholes and the gold toned pattern. He has his little shrunken head! The best thing is his hair.  It looks just like Jack's hair looked in \\"On Stranger Tides\\". And his hair is long, nearly to his waist. He is very easy to pose, but I do not think he would endure being played with. In my opinion he is a shelf toy. To be loved and admired. His head can be tilted in different ways to make him look more expressive and he does look like Johnny Depp, but to me more like Johnny looked in \\"The Tourist\\". :-)     All in all, I would recommend this Jack Sparrow to any older child or adult who loves the witty Captain and Johnny Depp.

product_title: Pool Vacuum from Polaris - ATV All Terrain
review_body: Bought this to replace a Hayward Navigator. Thus far, it works well. One problem, it gets stuck on the pool drain. I just ordered a drain cover from Polaris to resolve this problem. I'm a little ticked that I had to spend another 60 bucks for the drain cover, since, from what I've been reading on the web, this is a very common problem with this cleaner. My Navigator did not have this problem.  UPDATE: Well after a year of service, I cannot recommend this product. It consistently gets stuck on the drain cover. I bought the cover for the drain provided by Polaris. It's just a circular piece of plastic. When it stays on the drain, the system works. Unfortunately, after only a few hours, the cover moves and no longer covers the pool drain. So now I'm stuck with a system that I have to check on several times a day to make sure the cover is on the drain so the sweep doesn't get stuck. Bad design. I don't have an unusual drain cover, so I'd bet this happens to others. I just bought the tune-up kit for my old navigator, which never had these problems.

product_title: MOTU Masters of the Universe Classics Man-E-Faces Action Figure by Mattel
review_body: Just like his vintage and 200X counterparts, Man-E-Faces the Eternian Actor's addition to the line is a welcome one - and one eagerly anticipated since the start of the Classics line.  Man-E-Faces sculpt is very true to his original figure, and his rotating head features the same three faces - that of a man, a robot and a monster.  This time around, however (*SPOILER ALERT*) Man-E-Faces, as a secret accessory, includes another head with three faces bearing the likenesses of He-Man, Orko and Skeletor!  It's little added surprises like that which makes this line extra special for He-Fans and She-Ravers.  In case I didn't clarify above, Man-E-Faces entire head doesn't come off, only the top which lets you remove the cylindrical piece that bears the faces so you can change them. product_title: Hot Wheels RC Nitro Speeders Ken Block Ford Fiesta Rally Car
review_headline: Great for Kids, Adults, and Cats! ;>)
review_body:
We picked up this little machine so my partner's grandson could play with it when he visits. He's 7 years old, and though this toy says \\"8+\\" for age usage, he had no trouble figuring out how to control it. (I think most young kids, let's say 7 yrs. and up, are tech-savy enough to handle it.)

product_title: Through The Ages
review_headline: The quintessential civilization game for the modern euro gamer
review_body:
I confess: I've always liked civ games. And I've long been hunting for the ideal medium-weight civilization type game that is playable in 4 hours or less, and I've been on a quest for economic, military and technological bliss.

I'm pleased to report that with Through the Ages: A Story of Civilization, my quest is virtually over. It's not a perfect holy grail of civilization games, because any game that plays in under 4 hours has to sacrifice something. Through the Ages lacks a map, and arguably the down time can become an issue when played with four players. But as far as medium weight civilization games go, Through the Ages is stunningly good, and perhaps the very best.

The game is primarily driven by cards, but there are player boards and tokens, because you'll need to be managing a variety of things in your civilization, including population, food, building resources, science, strength, culture, happiness, and government. On your turn you take actions to slowly build up your civilization by inventing new technologies, building new buildings, producing building materials, all the while making sure that you have enough to feed your people and keep them happy. There's also significant player interaction, and not only are you competing with other players to have the most advanced civilization in terms of cultural development, scientific progress, or military strength, but you can even use your military to attack your opponent - although the cost of doing this can be high!

Through the Ages certainly meets most of the criteria I'm looking for a civilization type game: strong historical flavour and theme, economic and military elements, civilization technology, playable in 4 hours or less, a solid game without being overly complex, and decent components. Now excuse me, while I go and build myself a civilization! - EndersGame @ BGG

review_headline: Best pre-school game I've seen in years
review_body: I got this game for my 4 year old daughter and her 2 year old cousin to play. Turns out my 10 year old had just as much fun as they did.    Red Rover is a great Rainy day game that keeps kids moving and learning at the same time. My only recommendation on changing it would be to sell additional \\"bones\\" so learning choices can be expanded. A quick recommendation for other moms, to make the game harder for kids spread the bones out further from each other. Red Rover has a time element built in if no one is able to find the bone he is looking for. We found that by spreading the bones around a room the memory portion of the game kicked in even more.    Beyond the hours of giggles and learning, Red Rover is a perfect game for parents that don't want to keep track of a million pieces of \\"stuff\\" after the game is over. Red Rovers backpack holds the 12 bones securely.    Kudos for Mattel on this one. I would love to see more games like Red Rover.

product_title: Bandai Hobby EW-03 Gundam Heavyarms Custom Endless Waltz 1/144 High Grade Fighting Action Kit
review_headline: A Nice Replica For Gundam Fans
review_body:
This Heavyarms model was fun to put together, but a little to easy compared to more modern Gundam kits. The building process will only take about an hour or two. The main body colors are fine and the set comes with stickers for the detail colors, though I would strongly advise using paint for the details instead though. The stickers look passable, but painting the green lines and face are quick and easy remedies to make the model look much better. The finished product is pretty sturdy. His chest and shoulders flip open to reveal missiles and machine guns, whiles his legs and hips have pieces that can be replaced with additional missile openings. This model also comes with two large machine guns (displayed on box) which are light enough to keep the Heavyarms from being top heavy. He poses fine without any worry of breaking, but when trying to make more complex leg poses his back has a strange angle to it. My main concern was that his antennae and jets for his back are very delicate.One of the jets was already broken before I recieved mine, which was a little disappointing, but not a deal breaker.

In conclusion, I was very pleased with this model kit. The Heavyarms looks great, and despite needing a little bit of detail paint, is immediately shelf worthy. This simplicity of this model kit would be perfect for a first time builder. Whether you love the Heavyarms model, love wing, or just love the Gundam franchise in general, this is a great model kit.

product_title: Feature So Soft Pinkie Pie
review_body:
When Andromeda was very small, she learned her first two \\"sign words,\\" More Please. While she speaks fluent \\"people\\" now, those are still two of her favorite words. So as soon as I saw those were two words that was said by Pinkie Pie, I was sure she would be a hit.

From the moment the box was opened, Andromeda was entranced. Before Pinkie was out of the box she was squeezing her hand, listening to her, and giggling with each new response.

She was especially excited that putting the bottle or pacifier in Pinkie's mouth made her suck. With a little help, she realized that using the spoon would do the same thing. From that moment on, she and Pinkie were inseparable. Although she has never slept with a doll, she had to have Pinkie in bed with her, sucking the pacifier, of course.

She is just the right stage, where she enjoys treating things like babies, so Pinkie Pie is perfect for her. Having the verbal interaction just makes it more fun. As you can tell from the video, her favorite thing is feeding her. She thinks it's just hilarious that she burps after eating ... and that she sometimes says \\"excuse me.\\" Even when Pinkie forgets, Andromeda chips in for her. She enjoys her feet moving, whether she is seated (as she is in the video) or standing - where Andromeda has to hold her hand to help her walk.

The Horse/doll itself seems very safe as far as choking hazards. No buttons, eyes are painted on, nothing to come loose, and even the batteries are screwed in, meaning little fingers can't get at them. My only concerns are the extras that come with it - the spoon especially. I do want to mention that the pacifier and bottle are both 'solid' meaning that nothing can come off of them to cause issues.

With Pinkie being Andromeda's new best friend, I hope she has time for her Grandma. :-) Kid tested, Grandma Approved!

product_title: Agricola (Discontinued by manufacturer)
review_body: Agricola is an excellent game for 1-5 players.  It is a little hard to learn at first, but is well worth the effort because it has loads of playing and fun potential.  It is challenging enough for hardcore gamers like me, but simple enough to still be fun for more casual gamers.   Two game modes (family game and normal game) allow for further customization of the game to the players' skill level and to the desired complexity.  Overall, an amazing game!  I've already played it many times since purchasing it and plan to play many more.    The only downside (for some anyway) is that the playtime is a little long.  The game's estimate of 30 minutes per player is a bit optimistic.  It would probably take 30 minutes per player if each player was very skilled and had played many times before.  When playing with people who are still learning the game, play time is closer to 45 minutes per player.  Still, if you have the time, the game is definitely worth playing and will be fun for the whole duration, however long it is!

product_title: INTEX 15' x 48" Easy Set Pool Set w/ Pump, Ladder, Kits
review_body: First of all my husband and I just love the pool.  We are in our 60's and just wanted it to float around in on a hot TN day.  The picture shows 7 people in it, but I can't imagine that many, however it's just perfect for the two of us.  The set up was NOT as easy as they make it sound.  First of all finding a perfectly level space large enough for it was not easy for us.  We had to dig some on one side and add some dirt, which we had to purchase, on the other and that in itself was a job that took a lot of time and energy.  The ladder took my husband an hour or so to put together.  Filling the pool took parts of 2 days....guess our water pressure isn't so good?  Doing the electrical work and filter, adding chemicals and all the other stuff you have to do took time also.  So don't plan on putting it up and swimming in 30 minutes.  After we finally got it filled and ready to go, we had rain, rain and more rain and then it took another week to get the sun to shine warm enough to get in it.  Now we're back in the 90's here and the wait and time was all worth it!!!  It's sturdier than I imagined it would be and we just hope that it lasts us a couple of years because it is just what we wanted it to be.....a cool, refreshing oasis on hot country days.  Oh....ps.....after putting it up and everything, we saw it for a LOT less at Academy Sports, but still glad we bought it through Amazon as it is always easy to return if necessary and we didn't have to try to fit the big box in our car and lug it out.  The box is heavy!  Buy it and you will enjoy it!

product_title: LeapFrog Tag Junior Bundle
review_headline: Interesting toy saddled with arduous setup and tiny memory.
review_body: This device has some major issues.  As someone who works on computers all day, the last thing I want is to come home and futz around with downloading whatever book my child wants to read.  The real deal killer for this product is the tiny memory.  I was only able to fit some of books that it came with on its memory.  8MB is just a tiny bit of memory these days.  My child is playing with it.  So far it is not much different than our Story Reader.  The Story Reader is much easier to use, however.  The chances of me hooking up my computer and jumping through hoops each time we want to change books are tiny.  Summary: 2/5 stars.  Not worth the trouble in my opinion.  If you want to know more.. keep reading.  * Unpacking and Setup *  First thing you need to do is get a computer and download the Leapfrog Connect application.  I did this on a mac.  After a fairly long download, you're given a long lawyer talk EULA (end user licensing agreement) to agree to..  So far, this is not how I like to play with a toy.  I connected the device via USB and it recognized it immediately and started downloading an update for its software.  Next I'm told I need to provide a bunch of personal information and create a Parent Account.  Name, email, and year of birth are required.  I opt of of advertising emails and get an annoying Are You Sure dialog.  Yes, I'm positive.  Next I need to create a profile for who is playing with the toy.  Age, month and year of birth, and name are all required.  I'm told this is to \\"create age appropriate learning program\\", but I'm feeling like this could be simplified.  Next I click Finish, but am asked more questions.  Email addresses of family members to email learning updates to.  Optional survey questions about what types of smart phones I use...  Now I'm given two choices  Personalize Tag Junior (name of child), or Download Audio (for the books you purchased).  I'm surprised we didn't already get the audio download with our software update... but I clickon that one.  Now I need to manually find every book I have and download the audio.  Unfortunately I have quite a few books, and the application has a bug where every letter you type into the search field shows up three times.  I finally find an audio file and download it but the device has powered off.  I turn it back on but it is not recognized.  I try again and it works.  Now there is Another update available.  Huh?  I just updated.  Now I need to manually drag each manually download audio file to the device.  Ugh.  Turns out the device only has 8MB available on it.  So only two books fit on it.  This is in the age of 8GB flash costing about 10 dollars.  This device has  one thousandth that amount of memory.  Wow.  * Use *  Of course my 3 year old picks the book that didn't fit in the device's memory.  \\"Sorry, we can't read that one right now.\\"  We try Megs Pet, which stresses learning the \\"short E sound\\".  Basically she sets the reader on the page and it reads and or sings the story for her.  There are some interactive aspects where she is asked to place the reader on certain parts of the page.  So far thats about it.  I'll update this review if anything else is discovered while we play with this.

product_title: Crayola Colored Bubbles Wand Set
review_headline: Cool to see, but not worth the mess
review_body: I was so excited when I saw this in the store that I immediately bought the wand set and an extra bottle of bubbles.  I read the directions and warnings about avoid wood, concrete etc.  So we did the bubbles in the middle of a large grassy area, which saved us from some of the horror stories I have read in the other reviews.      I had no idea how long it would take to clean up my son however!  My son had green splotches in his hair, blue and orange splotches all over his face, arms, legs, shirt, and shoes!  I was able to get most of the bubbles off his body with wet paper towels.  I thought I was basically done after I cleaned his face, arms, and legs, but that wasn't the case.. when I took of his shirt, the bubbles had gone through his shirt and he had green spots on his chest too!  I gave him a bath to finish cleaning him and get it out of his hair.  Then I started a load of clothes because the bottle recommends immediately washing clothes, and everything came out.  Then I cleaned his shoes and my shoes in the washer which came clean as well.  So for us, everything came clean, but it took about an hour of my time to clean up from 20 minutes of fun.    I feel like the wand set itself was a little useless too.  The bubbles are all still going to be round, and now you are changing out these messy used wands with new ones.  In the process, you get the colored solution all over your hands and you have to clean the wands after you use them.    Bottom Line: In hindsight, I would not have bought this product.  But if you want to try it, I would recommend buying just one bottle of it instead of the wand set.  Wear old clothes (not just the kids, you too).  Do it barefoot, so that you don't have clean any shoes.  Do it the middle of a large grassy area.  Have a bunch of wet paper towels with you to clean up so that you don't have to walk inside covered in colored bubbles.
