product_title: Set: The Family Game of Visual Perception
review_body: This pattern-recognition card game is deceptively simple, extremely ingenious, and totally addictive. (And it's easy to see why it's won so many awards.) Took me a few plays to realize what the \\"all the same or all different\\" rule actually meant, but once I did, the game became fast-paced and endlessly fascinating. One thing they don't mention on the box or in the instructions is that no matter what two cards you randomly pick from the deck, there is always -- always -- a unique third card that forms a set. (Using this idea as a test is a great way to learn the game.) Once I realized this, finding sets became easier and utterly fun. Very highly recommended -- and I'm no pushover!

product_title: Pirates of the Caribbean At World's End Disney Exclusive Action Figure Captain Jack Sparrow
review_body: First of all, be careful when buying this, I would suggest communicating with the seller to make sure they send you the right one. I ordered this expecting the one in the picture, where Jack Sparrow is wearing a coat, but when he arrived, he's in the same box with the same items, but he's NOT wearing the coat. So I am disappointed about that, but it's not going to affect my rating of the product, it's just a seller mistake that I've resolved with the seller.    Anyway:  Other than the missing coat, he's a very nice figure. The fabric parts of his outfit are made of soft rubber/plastic so they don't get in the way of poses. His baldric is not functional, you can't put the sword in it. It's not attached to his body in any way so you can adjust it any way you want though.    He comes with a cutlass, flintlock pistol, removable hat, and Captain Barbossa's pet skeleton monkey. The cutlass looks nice and is sorta bendy (I guess because it's a kid's toy) but not too bendy. The flintlock looks like a real flintlock and made of hard plastic. You can stick it into his belt to carry. The whole monkey is made out of soft rubber/plastic stuff, so it's flexible and you can make him grab onto stuff. It also has nice detail and he's holding a doubloon in his hand. The hat is hard plastic.    Jack is super poseable, with elbow, wrist, leg, knee, and ankle joints, plus a rotating joint right below his knees, and two different joints on his head and each of his shoulders for a wide range of movement. It's easy to make him hold the weapons. The leg and hip joints are really loose, but maybe that's on purpose, to make posing easier. He can stand on his own really well.    The sculpt is detailed and looks a lot like Johnny Depp. There's tiny stitching on his boots and realistic metal effects on his belt and baldric buckles, and the hat looks like leather. The hair is layered and has all his trinkets in it. The paint is really good and accurate also.    Overall great, but I took a star away because it seems like they could've used a more durable plastic. It seems like if a kid played with this, his joints might not deal with a lot of strain. He seems more durable than an average Final Fantasy figure, like he might be ok if you drop him, but it just seems like the plastic could've been higher grade, because it makes the joints seem a bit weak.

product_title: 123 Learn 'n Play 36 Piece Boxed Floor Puzzle
review_body: We recieved two Crocodile Creek puzzles for our 2 year old last Christmas, (ABC and 123), and she has really enjoyed playing with both of these.  The pieces are a great size for her (she is now at age 2.5 getting better at putting them together), and they have held up well to the typical young hands that try to force pieces together when they don't fit.  There are some fun and different animals on the ABC puzzle that we typically don't see on alphabet items.  Both puzzles are great - wonderful pictures - and she tends to pull them out at least once a week to play with.  Another nice bonus is that the boxes are very sturdy - she has even been known to sit on them and they still are in great condition.      We loved those puzzles so much that we requested another Crocodile Creek puzzle from her grandparents a week ago.  They purchased the Dance Studio puzzle for her at B&N, but the puzzle pieces didn't fit right.  The package had been opened, and we weren't sure if pieces had been mixed up, or the diecut was just not done right.  Either way, I contacted Crocodile Creek through their website, and asked what could be done about this - expecting them to tell me to return it to the store.  Instead, I got a UPS delivery today with a brand new puzzle.  They didn't ask any questions, just sent a replacement.  I was really impressed to receive such good customer service and now my daughter will be able to enjoy another great puzzle.  I plan to buy more of these as her next birthday rolls around.

Not even a paper towel can be placed under it to decrease the noise because then the wok won't shake at all. product_title: RC Radio A-10 Thunderbolt II Electric Remote Control Plane
review_body: Bought this from a different website, but it's the same kit.  First the problems:  1. It is not Ready to Fly.  The term \\"ready to fly\\" or \\"RTF\\" is overused these days.  You will need to spend several hours assembling it, and overnight waiting for glue to dry before you can fly it.  At best it is ARF, or Almost Ready to Fly.  Definitely not \\"Ready to fly in minutes\\" as it says in the description.  2. There is no Rudder control.  Although it says \\"Aileron, Elevator, Rudder, Throttle\\" the rudder is fixed.  You can steer it on the ground with the nosewheel steering, but no rudder controls.  3.  Severely underpowered, out of the box it is UN-FLYABLE because it does not have enough power.  All you can do is taxi it around. (I ended up using a much bigger battery just to get it airborne).  4. The nose wheel steering is so unstable, it makes taxiing very difficult.  And since all you can do with this model is taxi it, that's a problem.  Not a concern when airborne.  5. The controller included is very shoddy, and barely gets the job done.  If you have another 4 or 6 Channel transmitter, us it.  This one is junk.  6. The servos included in the kit are junk as well.  Very noisy (chatter), and they do not trim out very well, although I couldn't tell how much of that was the fault of the transmitter.    Now for the good comments.  (Once I upgraded the battery system to a 11.1V 1300 mAh):  1. Very stable once airborne, handles crosswinds up to 7 or 8 mph nicely.  2. Inexpensive. But you get what you pay for...  3. Looks pretty cool, and it is fun to fly, but I'd spend a little more and buy a good radio, battery, and better motors.    Overall, I dont think I'd recommend this kit to anyone without experience with RC due to the amount of tweaking you'll have to do.

product_title: Melissa & Doug Trunki Sunny
review_body:
I purchased two of these for my two little grandsons for the weekends and holidays they spend at my house. It made it much easier to see that each boy has all of the supplies that he needs for the weekend, instead of just a jumble of clothing since they are roughly the same size. Plus, an advantage is that one side has a cross of elastic bands across it to make it easier to fold blankie and their favorite stuffed animal onto that side to make sure they are in the suitcase at both ends of the weekend.

They lasted about two weekends before the latches on the handles started to cause problems. The first weekend, my husband was able to get the right orientation on the handles again so they would slide upward to release them. It was extremely difficult and I broke several fingernails.

By the fourth weekend, the handles basically won't move anywhere so they have to be snapped on and off for every use. They are extremely tight and this is very difficult to do. It is very frustrating for the children and for me.

This is NOT the quality I have come to expect from Melissa and Doug toys. One star is generous.

product_title: Star Wars Episode 3 Electronic Lightsaber Obi-Wan Kenobi Lightsaber
review_headline: Appearence leads to frustration, frustration leads to 'hate', hate leads to buyers remorse, pass on this
review_body:
I bought the Anakin version of the electronic light saber. The only difference is the hilt. These are not good. You want to pass on this one. The hilt on both are passable and the sound chip is pretty good, but they way they do the blade is awful. It is not lit up and down the blade. It is only thinly lit at 3 spots. In a room with any kind of light the effect is awful. Doesn't looke like a lightsaber at all. You get blue light that fades...then it gets blue again then it fades. In a pitch black room, it looks better but still pretty bad.

I am sure, other than price, the only reason someone would look at these are because they are the only 'rectrable' version. The bottom third never retracts. And the other pieces if you hang it from a belt blade down will also start coming out. The overall design with the poor lighting is just a really cheap, bad-looking toy. There is no Obi-Wan version in the 'Ultimate' collection. But if you want a blue blade you can go with Anakin (pre darkside blue blade) [[ASIN:B004SGRW6C Star Wars Ultimate Anakin FX Lightsaber]] This does not retract but looks a million times better. It glows very relastically up and down the blade in a nice pale blue color. It looks great.

I normally write reviews on products I really like. They are well designed, good value for the money, often better than expected. I am very glad I purchased them and want to share. I also write when I want to alert people that to me in my honest experience this is a product I think they will regret getting and certainly will not live up to expectations. Sadly this is the later. The ulitmate FX one is the former, go with the ulitmate one. The idea of a retractable blade was so appealing to me I bought an electronic one. But it just looks so bad that even if it was fully retractable it would not be worth it. Buy the ultimate one, even if you can not get an Obi Wan hilt, you will be happier. And if you want to go up to the metal hilt you can get an Obi Wan ultimate version.

product_title: Megabloks 80pc Lrg Mega Bloks Bag
review_body: Who doesn't remember playing with Lego when they were a kid? I know I spent many hours and beyond making worlds with mine in my youth and naturally want my own son to have the same fun. With Lego Quatro being discontinued, we opted to start him off with Megabloks. On one hand these are great. They are big enough that even a young toddler can handle them with ease. They are also easy to put together and take apart. Unfortunately, they are far too easy to take apart as my son quickly became frustrated when his towers would consistently fall over. Being not quite two he's really in that stage where he just wants to build towers, and that is hard with these blocks as they don't lock together at all, but rather just \\"sit\\" on top of each other.  As much as I wanted to like these, I have already had to put these away and replace them with Lego Duplo. The Duplo lock together nicely and my son can finally build the towers he wants. A younger child might have problems using Duplos (putting them together and pulling them apart) though and so these Megabloks would still be the best option in that case. Just be aware that the \\"play span\\" of these may be disappointingly short.

review_body: This magnetic drawing board is inexpensive and great! We keep it in our diaper bag, so that our daughter only gets to play with it when we're out. The pen thing falls off the string pretty often, so we have to tie it back on every now and then, but overall we just love this magnetic board. We were also glad it came in pink! It would be nice if you could choose the color to have sent to you, but we wanted pink anyway, so we were happy :)

product_title: LEGO Star Wars Freeco Speeder (8085)
review_headline: Another quality Lego Star Wars set!
review_body:
I have noticed a bunch of the reviews for this product are from moms saying that their six year old son enjoyed it. I have enjoyed Lego since about that age, and twenty years later I still get so much joy out of a simple toy. I enjoy them b/c they are novel, quality products and allow for imagination at all ages (while helping develop/practice skills such as problem-solving and following directions.) I have noticed over the years, how much Lego emphasizes making the instruction book the best it can be by making the steps easy to understand. Overall, I think they have really improved how \\"user-friendly\\" the instruction books are. They really break it down well. I enjoy the innovation of Lego and have been really impressed with how they handle the movie franchise sets, esp. the Star Wars sets.

I have a bunch of the more recent Star Wars sets, \\"Darth Vader's Tie Fighter,\\" \\"Plo Koon's Starfighter,\\" \\"Luke's Landspeeder,\\" etc. and this one goes along great with all those. This model is based off a model from the Star Wars Clone Wars series and you can find out more info about it here:[...]
The likeness is definitely there! The build was pretty straight-forward, and the end model is sturdy. Looks sleek. Comes with two mini-figures, pretty standard. The two figures are detailed and unique. The minifigs are always one of the best parts of a particular set. Another solid Star Wars Lego product.

I payed $20 for this set on Amazon (at time of posting.) I think that is a great deal. It is $27.99 at Toys R Us and $24.99 at Target (at time of posting.) I love Amazon and think they have great deals and selection on all toys, esp Lego. I have also been impressed with Amazon's service, packaging and delivery. Keep it up guys. I appreciate it.

product_title: My First Lab  Microscope
review_headline: Would be great except that it's optics are useless
review_body: Purchased the first one for my Daughter for her Birthday last month.  She was pretty excited when we unboxed  it. During setup of the first slide, the unit seemed pretty sturdy and well made for a low $$ plastic scope  (I have an old metal Tasco scope in a higher price bracket and it's quality is outstanding for a 4 decades old unit).  At first we thought that the slides were defective due to a blotch that appeared while viewing the first one,  but after the second slide went into place, we realized that the lens was dirty (or so we thought).  After cleaning  both sides of the removable 10X piece, the blotch was still there.  If there was some way to ignore it, the quality  of the optics (for the $60 price point) would have been acceptable. But having a permanent fuzzy blotch/blob directly in  the center of the field of view was beyond annoying.  I have to believe that it was a defect in the internal mirror  system.  After receiving the SECOND unit days after filing for a replacement, I am certain that defect is a consistent  factory defect.  2 scopes with nearly identical blotches in the field of vision?  If it been to one side or the other,  it would have been a liveable condition.  Direct center of field distraction pretty much takes the fun and usefulness out  of this scope.  I wish that I could have had one long enough to properly evaluate, but the second scope is going back  for a refund.  Hopefully Amazon will pull this item as to not cause any more disappointment to customers.  I will have  to either give my Daughter my Tasco (still working great after all these years) or spend a bit more on a better scope.  On to the other scopes reviews to see which will be next.

product_title: Nanoblock Giant Panda with over 150 Pieces
review_body: I've done a few of these Nanoblock miniatures now and believe that the Panda Bear is the best animal one to get. It is a beautiful piece when completed and actually built quite solidly. My 3 year-old daughter played with the finished piece for a while without messing it up (contrary to what would happen with the Koala Bear).  The pieces are quite small and typically in sizes of 2x4, 2x2, 1x1, 1x2, 1x3, 1x4. If you have large hands, it may be difficult to put together some of the pieces, especially the 1x1s which may require tweezers.   Contrary to some reviews, the instructions are actually quite good, thorough and easy to follow. It may take a little getting used to, but I never found any confusion with them. The directions break up the process into 6-8 sections with prior completed segments grayed out to distinguish from the pieces being worked on. When your Panda is completed, you will have lots of extra pieces (not sure what this is for -- possibly to enhance the design). If you're looking for a fun one to start out with, get this one!

product_title: LEGO Minotaurus Game (3841)
review_body: We bought this game for my son for his birthday, and it proved to be one of his favorite gifts.  It has all the elements he loves: the LEGO brand, the ability to create and design your own game layouts, the ability to create your own game rules, and hours of fun.  My son is quite the inventive and creative sort - which is largely why he loves LEGO products so much.  I was a bit concerned that the LEGO board game would be a bit too defined and simplistic for his tastes, but these concerns were quickly alleviated.  While the game does come with a basic suggested design/layout, and basic game rules; the real magic and fun of the game comes from the ability to design your own Minotaur worlds, as well as the relatively easy adaptability of the game to developing your own rules.  With that, my son played the game repeatedly with his friends.  I played a game with my son and two others and really enjoyed it.  The game is exciting, fun and sometimes frustrating to play, in that, just when you think you are about to win the game the minotaur can show up to send you back to home space.  In my case, the game took more than an hour to complete!  But it was so much fun, and my son really enjoys it.  Highly recommended!

review_headline: Quit working after a day, not that great when it did work
review_body: Ours, like most others, quit working after the first day. On ours at least it appears that the bubble liquid gets into the electronics. The liquid is pumped up the same side as the batteries are on and when I went to swap out batteries (thinking that was the issue) they were coated in bubble solution and one had begun to rust already. Kids used it for two half hour sessions the first day and the next morning when they tried to use it again, it was already dead.   When it did work, it was not that great. The bubble solution cannot sustain the larger size bubbles this machine is meant to produce. Smaller ones created with the wand did OK, but the ones the machine produced using it popped either as they were being created or with-in a half second or so. They wanted to chase them across the yard but end up just standing over the top of the thing trying to pop them before they popped themselves. The kids have used some smaller bubble generators that worked great and filled the yard with bubbles but this one was disapointing even when it did run.   Bubble generators are a great kids toys toy when done right. This one fails on several fronts and I cannot recommend.

product_title: Do A Dot Art: 5-pack Shimmer Markers
review_body: These are great. We have three sets (all but the fluorescent ones) and use them often, they always work and aren't showing any signs of running out soon. We usually use them on newsprint with a second sheet below, and that's sufficient that they don't bleed through to the table. The ink dries in minutes, even if an area is saturated. We've left them open for ~30 min, they're still fine. Some of the other reviews mentioned staining, but I've had no trouble - ink may leave a little colored residue on the skin after gentle washing, but just for a day and it's no worse than any other marker or paint that we've used.  They really are glittery, too. The ink goes down without much shimmer, but the glitter is more evident as it dries. You can layer different colors while the page is till wet, they don't get muddy. Good toys.  Update in late 2015 - they're still going strong! We still love 'em. They've come out a few times a month for more than 5 years!

product_title: Hasbro Beyblade Metal Masters Triple Battle Set Action Figure
review_headline: Love Beyblade, but the stadium's no fun...
review_body: My 9 year-old son is a huge Beyblade fan. He has more than a dozen tops and a couple of stadiums, and has had hours of fun over the last year customizing his Beys and battling with his friends. Needless to say, we were very excited to get this new Triple Battle Set. Unfortunately, it hasn't been as enjoyable as we hoped.  The two exclusive Beys included with this set, Galaxy Pegasus and Meteo L-Drago, are fantastic. Pegasus spins right, while L-Drago spins left, making for some spectacular battling action. I was pleased to see that this season's tops have been redesigned to eliminate some of last year's less desirable features. There's no easy-to-destroy rubber tip on the bottom of Pegasus anymore, and the stickers that used to be put on top of the Beys and rippers have been replaced by screen printed character logos. These Beys can spin long and hard, and we love them.  The problem? The stadium isn't really much fun. In theory, it's designed with three interchangeable centers so that you can customize your battle arena, but it only took us a few minutes to realize that all three centers produce the same result: the Beys get stuck in the grooves in the center and stop prematurely. No long, tense battles, and fewer dramatic collisions between tops. My son quickly put the Triple Battle stadium away and went back to his older stadiums.  Though we love Beyblades, I wouldn't really recommend this product. The stadium is a disappointment, and the MSRP of $35-40 is way too high when you consider that most of the big box retailers sell basic stadiums for $10 and 2-packs of Beys for $15. Buy wisely and have fun battling!

product_title: Playskool Poppin Park Elefun Busy Ball Popper Toy
review_body:
This popper is absolutely adorable and - for the most part - my two year old LOVES it. My big problem is that it's loud. My little guy is also scared of loud noises, so as much as he loves it, every time he turns on the popper, he runs away in fear! So it's set on automatic: turn on, run away, and then watch (from afar) as the balls go out the nose, into the ear, and back out the nose. Thirty seconds or so go by, the music and blower stop, then run over, turn it on, and run away again...

The fully automated mode isn't foolproof. Sometimes the balls fly in unexpected directions. That's fine though: it's a toy, not a piece of precision equipment.

One special note: I've been extremely impressed at the durability and safety! All sorts of things have been put in the elephant's nose and ear, and we've been able to get them out safely, and never had an injury from putting a little hand or finger where it shouldn't be.

review_headline: Great Figure. A few gripes though.
review_body: This is a great figure/statue, but there are a few things you need to be aware of:    1. First, the cape is completely yellow, not black on the outside. The black would have been cool, like in the picture for the promotion, but it's different enough that it could change your mind on purchasing this. I'd recommend checking actual photos out on ebay or online to get an accurate picture.    2. the peg for her leg to stand on the base is in the middle of the base, not like it is in the picture (unless I got a defective one) so Batgirl stands with her right leg on the stand and the other foot off to the left. This also makes the statue look a little off. I wish someone at DC would have caught this particular mistake because now you need like 4\\" of extra space for the stand or else she can't stand at all (the peg in her right boot is permanantly attached).     Still looks cool, but seems like they messed this one up with the final design. Also the red stripe on the helmet, in the picture, is not there either, which kind of makes the helmet look like it's not really part of the costume. I think the blue/gray version did this too. Not paying attention to these little details hurts the look of these figures.    On the positive side, the colors work well and the semi-transluscent hair is a cool effect.     Maybe I'm too picky, but I can't be the only one bothered by some of these little details. I loved the Batman statue and definitely wanted this one to have a set.    My two cents.

Children learn the difference between herbivores and carnivores. They learn that dinosaurs had to protect their eggs from predators. They learn that if you dig into the earth, you can uncover dinosaur bones which can be put together to form a skeleton. They learn traits of several dinosaurs. These are all good things to learn, but there could be so much more to this game. To me this was a game that could have been as involved as Animal Genius, but wasn't. To me Animal Genius is the best game available from Leapster, and this game is about a fifth as educational as Animal Genius. If my son already loved dinosaurs and knew something about them he may have been disappointed with this game, because it doesn't have much to offer.

product_title: Wits & Wagers
review_headline: Great Party or Game Night Game
review_body:
Over the past 2 years I have had the enjoyment of playing this game with friends and family. The first time we played it the game was a little slow-going, but after that the game really picks up. I have played this game over 40 times and I still have a blast playing it. I will say that after playing so many times I have found that I will need to buy the expansion pack as we normally come across a few cards that we have already used and other players remember a ballpark answer. I will also need to buy a new set of dry-erase pens as the ones that are provided with the game dry out after a few months of use.

When playing with new people it is best to have one or two people in teh game that already know how to play. Don't try explaining all of the rules up front... instead I have found it's easiest to explain the main rules before playing and then explaining the betting and payout during the first round. This game is overall a great game to play, especially for parties that have new people that might not be aquainted with the entire group.

product_title: Little Tikes Baby Tap a Tune Piano
review_body: When our daughter was born, we had a strict no-noisy-toys rule. That lasted until she was about about 6 months and go so much fun and education out of toys that made sounds that we relented. But then we discovered that most electronic noisemaking toys have a button to play autonomous music when the baby isn't playing with it. I don't understand -- it's not like she would sit there listening. She would hit that button and then lose interest and crawl off, and I'd be stuck listening to the same four bars of something annoying over and over. We looked for a toy that didn't do this, but all of them not only had this button, but they considered it a selling point.  So I decided to try to find some mechanical noisemakers for her. It's a bit tricky, since at 9 months, she's really too young for something like a xylophone with a choking hazard mallet. This piano is the most fun thing we've tried. All four notes are chosen to sound nice in any combination, so she can bang on it to her heart's content without giving me a headache. And I've been able to see her grow and develop. First she would turn it over and bang on the bottom. Then she would smash on the keys to get maximum sound. Now she plays each key individually.

product_title: Crayola Crayon Maker
review_body: [[ASIN:B00296QV1K Crayola Crayon Maker]]!  [[ASIN:B002VY06IO Crayola Crayon Maker]]  [[ASIN:B004Z1JUJ2 Crayola Crayon Maker with Story Studio]]  Thought this would be cool fun for my kids but what a big disappointment. Firstly the timer switch kept getting stuck so had to turn it manually to get it going again (You try sitting there for 20 minutes kick starting the timer every minute). We made 3 batches of crayons and the kids were bored after the first batch. Only ½ actually came out Ok. If you pour too fast or too slow the top gets blocked and none will come out. Many crayons you get from family restaurants etc. are cheap and don't melt well and tend to bubble with a film on top which again blocks the top when you pour and they don't come out. Crayons didn't have colored swirls they just melted all together to form one color.  Crayons are only ½ the length of normal crayons. Then there is the clean-up, after 2 times you definitely won't want to be doing it again. All in all, no matter how much they slash the price it's a big waste of money!  To be fair I thought I should make an additional comment. This machine does work if you use good quality crayons like Crayola. But, there is the rub, I want to recycle all the crayons we get from family restaurants, not use good ones. The rest of my comments still stand.

product_title: Monster High Clawdeen Wolf Doll
review_body:
I wasn't much of a fan of the original Clawdeen doll, at least, not enough to spend $20 or so on one, so I passed on her, while my collection grew full of other dolls.

Then I got lucky enough to find this version of her on the shelf! I really, really love this Clawdeen, and she's easily my favorite by far of all the Clawdeens that have been released. For starters, I absolutely adore her hairstyle. The ponytail looks cute, but also a little classy, and it works very well with her considering she has the ears to work around in terms of what hairstyles they can give Clawdeen in general.

Her earrings are really cute as well, with a little chain hooking multiple piercings together on one ear.

Her outfit just smacks of 80's style (like quite a few of these dolls) which for me, an adult collector who grew up in the 80's, is a selling point. Her sweater has leopard spots on it that are actually glittery, and I don't think pictures pick up on that sparkle too well.

Her boots are some of the most amazing ones I've seen in the line; the heels meant to mimic claws are very subtle, but a nice way to keep her \\"animal\\" theme. This Clawdeen also features claw style hands, instead of the older style regular hands.

She also comes with a functional purse that opens and can hold a few small items! Very awesome.

While I can't ever rate these dolls very high in terms of their educational value, they are some of the most amazing dolls I have ever seen, and any kid would be truly lucky to get one.

product_title: Sea Ventures, Battery Powered, Diving WWII Submarine
review_body: We know subs were sunk in wartime so if you want one that will realistically plunge down to Davy Jone's Locker and remain motionless on the bottom, this is what you want. This sub is actually 12.5\\" long, separates into top and bottom pieces for access to the single AA battery and has an external on/off switch that is waterproof. The sub is free-flooding so it will float until its deck is about even with the water surface. If left undisturbed it will cruise around on the surface for quite some time in lazy circles or in straight lines, depending on how you have the rudder positioned. However, if the sub is jostled enough the remaining air pocket will escape and then it will lose all bouyancy and completely sink. The sub will not dive with the bow planes angled down nor will it cruise underwater once I took it there. Once filled with water it becomes too heavy for the tiny propeller to have any effect and it will land upright on the bottom. I will try adding more styrofoam inside the sub (there is already a small piece in there) so it will retain positive buoyancy and it might work best as a non diving sub. As a motorized pool toy it is mediocre if you can keep it on the surface that is. The deck guns, conning tower and rudder are all made of flexible plastic so they won't snap off, a wise feature, and yet it still looks like a Gato Class sub. I really wanted this thing to work as advertised despite other older reviews but it was not to be (at least out of the box). I didn't think they still made simple toy subs like this anymore and was surprised to find something this \\"old school\\". It is overpriced for what you get; it's more like a $5 item.

product_title: Jacquard Tie Dye Kit
review_body: I was skeptical about tie dye - all of the buckets and dipping I've heard of in the past intimidated me.  I tried this out with my 10- and 8-year old cousins, and it was amazing!  From start to finish, everything was easy.  Be sure to cover the table you're using with plastic, have plenty of rubber/vinyl gloves handy, and wear old clothes.  The DVD was short enough to watch just before we started, but clear enough that we understood exactly how to do everything.  We had just enough dye for 6 adult-sized t-shirts, 3 pairs of boxers, and a few pairs of socks (ran out of one color as we got to the socks - no big deal).  My only advice is if you're doing it with kids, tie up all the clothes in the patterns they want, let them soak in the soda ash, and take items out as you go.  I did the clothes in batches, and the kids got bored waiting between sets.  The DVD tells you that you can leave the clothes in the soda ash for more than the 20 minute minimum period, so don't worry about leaving everything in for too long.  The next day when we washed and dried our clothes, we were SO HAPPY with the results!  The colors were vivid and the patterns exactly how the DVD told us they would look.  We're doing this again the next time they're in town!

product_title: Revell Proto Max RTF 4-Ch Heli
review_headline: Great Beginner Fixed Pitch Heli - Great Support
review_body: I've flown some of the smaller coaxial heli's, and they got boring quick. Among limited control and low flight times were the reasons I decided to upgrade. This heli is AWESOME. It is amazing what technology they've fit into this model.  Thoughts -   1. This is indoor only, unless you live someplace where this is no wind at all, and I mean 0MPH. It is only about 1 ounce, and even the slightest wind will make a big difference in flight. While it does have a low/high option, even the high option has a hard time fighting any kind of wind at all.  2. If you're new to flying, go with low mode at least a few times. You'll know when you're ready to move up to the higher mode; it won't take long.  3. Blip the throttle (left stick) to get it off the ground - otherwise it will pull across the floor and undoubtedly crash. Once it gets some height, you have far better control.  4. Give yourself some room. I realize indoors that can be a problem, but perhaps a garage or other larger area to start. Once you get comfortable with the controls, you can easily fly in smaller areas.  5. Until you're comfortable - if you're flying and think you may crash - pull the throttle down. That has saved my butt many times just starting out. This thing is durable, but if the main rotor is spinning, you have a much higher chance of damaging something.  6. I had a problem with the control board - a quick call to support and they had a new one on the way, which I easily replaced myself.  7. Get an extra battery!  8. When the battery gets low, the chopper will let you know... Generally, when I give it full throttle and it barely goes up, it's time to be ready to catch it or land it. You'll also notice limited control of the tail, as that motor loses power pretty quick. Once it reaches a certain level, it shuts off - be prepared.    Awesome heli - great support - good fun - would buy another!

The first time I tried it with a full clip,it jammed and the dart got mangled extensively. Thankfully though,I also got extra darts. It hasn't jammed up since but I noticed a few things.    Good Points:  -accuracy:The accuracy is ok with just the gun. It is better with the barrel extension though.  -usability:I normally roll and dodge when I have wars. Some guns slow me down but with this gun its easier than some.  -range:This gun has a good range of about 20-25 feet. It shoots farther though without the barrel extension.It also shoots a little farther with the stock attached.      Bad Points:  -accuracy: accuracy is good but it has a downside. If you are looking for a dot-on shot, this isn't the gun for you.  -rate of fire:This gun has a decent rate of fire. Against a one shot pistol. If you try to shoot it faster than 1 per second or so,it will jam. Or make a funky noise.  -range:The barrel extension which is supposed to make it a sniper gun,fails majorly. I used the barrel extension and the dart fell 5-10 feet shorter than without the extension.    Overall,I like the gun, but if you want to shoot fast,this isn't for you.

product_title: Miko Monkey
review_headline: Fantastic, terrific - best huggable monkey ever!
review_body: I could not have been more excited to learn that Ingri Von Bergen is back in business as House of Ingri making her signature dolls! Of the eight characters featured in Me, Me, ABC, five are available now and the other three will be coming later in the year. We really wrestled with our decision, but chose Miko Monkey over Moki Monkey, Picco Panda, Francis Love Bunny, and Marty. It was a tough choice as each character has his/her own personality and are so weirdly cute in their own way. I love the eyes and sweet heart on Francis, Marty's vivid scarlet body and Picco's little panda likeness. But Miko has his his own unique attributes that won us over.     I was pleasantly surprised when Miko arrived for two reasons. He was quite a bit bigger than I was expecting him to be (even though the dimensions are clearly stated - I'm not too good at visualization) and the quality was amazing. Miko's body is made from soft, no-pill fleece - the good fleece, not the cheap stuff. His face and eyes and bum are done in a brushed faux suede, serged onto the body with a solid zig-zag stitch - no chance of these accidentally coming loose. His hands and feet are weighted with beans, a necessity considering his oversized noggin.    Those are the technical details. The overall result is - he's awesome! Just the right size for hugging and as soft as can be. Predictably, my six year old loves him every bit as much as the alphabet book. I should mention that Miko's most prominent asset is actually his butt. That tan faux suede really stands out against the blue fleece, doesn't? We're not lacking for any monkey butt jokes at our house.     House of Ingri has done an amazing job of bringing these characters to life. I'm more than a little excited to see the rest of the characters come out in December.

product_title: Bubble Bellies II with 8oz Bubbles - Hippo by Imperial Toy
review_headline: BOGUS DESIGN! Doesn't work. Stay far away.
review_body: Received as a gift for my 2 yr old. Right out of the box it never worked. Leaked solution all over and never blew a single bubble. Took it apart to diagnose problem and found that the soap-supply line had a HOLE burned through it by the hot glue used to secure the internal parts. Repaired using heat-shrink tubing around the hole, and despite all my efforts, the supid thing STILL didn't work. Now at least the bubble-blower was receiving solution like it was supposed to, but due to the HORRIBLE DESIGN (as many other reviewers point out), it doesn't blow bubbles because the solution never flows over the wand-tip sufficiently, and when it does, the air current is too strong and pops the bubbles before they ever leave the wand. Bottom line = cool idea, horrific execution. Should never had made production. My feeling is most people are buying these in brick&mortar stores and then coming online to report their bad experiences. Online shoppers - don't buy this!!!

product_title: Pokemon Jumbo Shadow Lugia Promo Card E3 Nintendo
review_headline: Yes, this card is fake. But you should know that already.
review_body:
This Shadow Lugia card has 300 HP. The most HP I have seen for any legit Pokemon card is 200 for a Wailord. That card had other disadvantages like a retreat cost of four energies. 300 is a lot more than 200, and there are no real disadvantages. Moreover, the \\"Shadow Storm\\" attack does ONE THOUSAND damage. The most damage I have seen done by any legit attack was 200 by the Articuno, Zapdos, and Moltres card (a single card), and even that card I don't think you are allowed to use in tournaments or anything. 1,000 damage is a joke, an insult to the whole card game. For four psychic energies, an attack should do about 60-80 damage. The main reason this card is obviously a fake - and not a very convincing fake, either - is that the artwork is lifted directly from the regular Lugia card from Unseen Forces. Granted, it's cool artwork, but many people on the internet are very skilled at creating Pokemon fan art. If you are going to create a Pokemon card, even if only for you and your friends' personal enjoyment, please put more effort into it. And if you are going to sell it on Amazon, for your own dignity's sake, you might as well just tell us that it's a fake.

I would not recommend spending over $10 or $20 for any kind of single Pokemon card, and if you are, you should make sure it is legit first. I will tell you up front that this one is not.

product_title: Backyard Safari Lazer Light Bug Vac
review_headline: A Bug Vacuum for Suckers Only
review_body:
I'm done with this company. Every spring they release this great looking kids stuff on to an unsuspecting public. I have to assume they do this with the hope that maybe 50% of the people who purchased their - I hesitate to call it junk, but it's kind of junk - products will either be too lazy to return it or might give it as gifts and forget to include a gift receipt.

When I initially picked this up in the store I could not even feel the suction when I turned it on, it was that weak. I knew right away that the suction this device provided would barely pull down a dust mote, but I assumed the weak suction had something to do with the plastic wrap packaging covering the exhaust and bought it anyway.

So today I busted the thing out of it's packaging and tried it on some ants. Sadly, as I feared the suction was so meager they were just annoyed and kept on about their business. In the end I was able to nab a few by knocking them loose from the wall with the nozzle but it was really unsatisfying to do it that way as you might imagine.

So now I have to tell my 4 year-old daughter, who is just beginning to have that sense of excitement whenever she encounters new things like science, paleontology, or insects, that we have to take it back to the store because it is simply \\"not good\\". What I'd hoped to encourage, a sense of wonder at the natural world, will now become a lesson in dealing with disappointment.

product_title: Fisher-Price Disney's Dance Star Mickey
review_headline: A Popular Toy.... but not as Popular as we Thought
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:moKRGSMM4FBDHE]]At Christmas 2010 we thought that Dance Star Mickey would be the highlight of the holiday. Really, what could be more popular than a talking, singing, and dancing Mickey Mouse!?! Well apparently several things can be more popular... because while this Mickey is a dancing machine he doesn't offer up much in terms of imaginative play. Mickey dances and sings several songs, but he is not soft or cuddly, he can not easily be taken outside or for rides in wagons.

Things that our daughter likes

- He sounds just like Mickey Mouse (as you would expect)

- Very energetic dances

- Great (happy) dance songs which usually get our daughter dancing along with Mickey

- Very easy to turn on

- Not too loud.... we can all hear Mickey, but he isn't so loud that we worry about waking the dead

A few other things to note

- Mickey need 6 AA batteries

- He only moves so-so on carpet - he is a much better dancer on wood or ceramic floors

- I mentioned it earlier, but he is not soft or cuddly - and due to all of the electronics he is kind of heavy.

Final Verdict - While Dance Star Mickey is a *fun* toy he is not a *must have* toy. In our daughter's closet she has 6-8 things she plays with on a more frequent basis than Dance Star Mickey with number one being [[ASIN:B003TO4YYC Kidkraft Suite Elite Kitchen]] so while I will give it 4 Stars - I will issue you a little caution, remember some of the other toys that turned out to be rather costly fads....

4 Stars

The only real downsides to this card is its low attack for it's level, it is a 6 level monster and has a 2100 attack and the other bit of it's effect which states that when this card is removed from the field to the graveyard so are the cards that were special summoned with it's effect so make sure you have something like \\"Tutan Mask\\" or \\"Sakuretsu\\" armor facedown and \\"Giant Trunade\\" can also clear your way for a safe attack.

product_title: Can You Imagine Pocket Plasma with Clip, Green
review_body: Ok, so I'm a Trek nerd.  Years ago, I bought a larger cousin to this device (called a Lumin Disk), and when I saw this little beauty I had to have it -- in green, of course!    It's important to remember that 2 of these units can perform very differently from one another.  For example, unlike the one in the reviewer video, mine seems bent on creating a thick \\"whisk broom\\" outer end of the \\"lightning\\" bolts at all times (in constant-on mode), whereas the one in the video review is much cleaner looking, with the lightning presented in a more modest and random fashion.  Unfortunately, there are no adjustments on the product (only a slide switch for off/on/sound modes).  It's possible that display behavior could be altered by modifying internal circuitry (e.g., output drive level), but I suspect variety is primarily due to tolerances in pellet phosphor coatings and thus behavior cannot be changed in a given unit.    The sound mode is nicely implemented.  I had a guinea pig.. er! I mean a relative sit about 4 feet away from the unit and speak in a normal voice.  The device triggered appropriately, so it has a reasonably sensitive mic but isn't overdone to the point where minute SPL's (Sound Pressure Levels) trigger it.  If one gently runs his/her fingernail over the relatively smooth case, the display is active pretty much the entire time the finger is in motion, so it's likely the unit would be generating \\"lightning\\" most of the time it's in motion and attached via its metal clip.  I haven't tried walking around with it attached to myself, as that wasn't my purpose in buying it.  Sensitivity drops markedly as batteries drain.     I gave it 4 stars for durability because it's a fairly thick chunk of glass which seems like it would handle a fall from a decent height onto carpet -- hard surfaces like wood floors or concrete I have my doubts about.  Also, the battery cover is held on by two screws (nice!).  The manufacturer, however, doesn't seem overly confident, as they provide a meager 45 day warranty.    I rated it a 2 on educational value because, well, just looking at the thing doesn't tell you much about the physics behind it, and the included manual doesn't delve into theory, either.    There's definitely a fun factor associated with this item.  The novelty wears off soon enough, but it can be mesmerizing if one is tired and stares at it too long.. tooo.. looonnggg... (((@@))) whoa! hey! ok, I'm back.  I suppose one could hook it up to a 3VDC wall wart (AC adapter) and run it all night, if one were inclined to do so -- unfortunately, there's no adapter jack, so one would need to solder the adapter wires to the battery terminals or use small alligator clips (both of which would likely void the too-short warranty).    As I mentioned, I have a larger disk and, basically, if you've seen one, you've seen 'em all.  After the initial \\"wow, so cool, never-saw-it-before\\" factor wears off, size becomes the most impressive feature of these disks (be they huge or tiny ones like this model).  For those who won't be using it in artsy projects -- the green one would be perfect for a Borg regeneration chamber diorama -- its lasting value comes primarily from impressing people who haven't seen a Lumin Disk up close and personal and/or those who haven't seen it miniaturized to such a degree and made portable.    I suppose these small ones would also look great near (or inside?) speaker cabinets -- Boogie Borg?  er.. yeah..  Anyway, I enjoy mine and will probably order more for various projects or to give as gifts.

product_title: Nerf N-Strike Raider Rapid Fire CS-35 Dart Blaster
review_headline: The gun is good but has its defects.
review_body: My brother gave me this gun for christmas and my dad got one from amazon at the same time. In the first battle we had, his gun jammed at least five times. I've realized a lot that this gun shoots at least 4-5 feet farther Without the stock on, which isn't very fun for me. I enjoy having the stock on the gun.    Good things about the gun  -rate of fire: I can get it up to about 3-4 per second which is pretty fast. Until it jams,but I'll talk about that in defects  -range: without the stock, this gun can shoot up to around 30 feet depending on the level of the gun tip when you shoot.  -big clip: the clip holds 35 darts,but I normally fit in 36 or so. This is good as it gives me more ammo,so less reloading.  -reload time: If you have an extra clip ready, the reload time is much better than reloading the whole 35 shot clip.    Defects  -jamming: the gun jams every once in a while. I find this annoying because I have to unload the gun and fix the problem; less time to shoot. It tends to jam more when I use the slam fire mode.  -range:the range is good,but also bad. If you are out in a large field,this is not the ideal weapon for long range firing. As I said,without the stock it shoots farther, but someone using a longshot could easily shoot you as you try to move in so they are in range.  -weight:the gun can get kind of heavy what with the big clip on one side, making it tilt. Also, all the weight is in the front of the gun.  -reload time: the clip that comes with this gun has 35 darts in it. That takes a while to reload and gets annoying. Even if you have extra clips,it still gets kind of annoying.    Overall I like the gun, but Nerf should really make a modified version with larger range and no more pumping the handle really fast.

product_title: KRE-O Transformers Starscream Construction Set (30667)
review_headline: The rest of you will have to wait until September
review_body:
June 2001 Update:
Apparently the release dates have been brought forward from September and are available her on Amazon now! Why wait?

Original Review:-
It's a little difficult to review a new line of toys, when even the link to the product page here on Amazon, ends with a 404 error.
If you're wondering why that's the case, a simple web search will reveal that the KRE-O line of toys won't be released until later this year (2011)

Fortunately for some lucky ones like myself, we have the Amazon vine program to thank for this tasty early release

In response to consumer feedback Hasbro have come up with, or rather gone back to a different style of construction toy.
Lego it isn't, but it's very close, in fact it's actually compatible with Lego, so potential add ons will only be limited to your kids imagination.
The KRE-O Starscream has just over 300 pieces, and is a little fiddly for younger fingers.
The 8-14 age range is about right, but if you're on the lower end of that scale, some adult supervision and assistance will be required.
There will be three main sets released in the fall of this year, including this one here, an Optimus Prime set of similar size, and a smaller Bumblebee set.
The full line eventually will range in price from under ten dollars, to over sixty.
A word of warning, as versatile and compatible as these sets are with other brick based systems, they have an either / or aspect to them.
Starscream can be the stand up Autobot as shown, OR the Jet fighter, but not constantly switched between the two.
During construction, on whichever you choose, there are some pieces that once in place are not intended to move, a potential flaw maybe, but the finished item looks impressive.
The pieces although small are well made and very durable, so some of the snapping plastic that was prevalent in the more one piece Transformers toys has been improved.
Starscream also comes with two Kreon mini figures, while in Jet mode the canopy of the fighter can be opened to accommodate one of these figures.

All in all a nice change of direction for this popular theme of Hasbro toy, sure to be a big seller................when it finally gets here later this year.r can be opened to accommodate one of these figures. product_title: Gundam 00: Masurao Robot Spirits Action Figure
review_body: I just got into the Gundam franchise a few months back, but I wasn't quite ready for model kits, so I turned to the excellent Robot Damashii (Spirits) line. Despite the small size, these figures are very high quality and extremely poseable, as well as much more durable than most model kits, due to the lack of a need for assembly.    The Masurao, while having a very unique design, is no different in terms of quality. Piloted by Graham Aker (aka Mr. Bushido) for a short time in Season 2 of Mobile Suit Gundam 00, the Masurao is Graham's Flag heavily customized into a samurai-esque mobile suit. The figure translates the very neat design almost perfectly into plastic. The figure has a gorgous glossy black finish with nice burgandy accents, making it look like it flew right out of the show and into your display case.     Like all Robot Damashii figures, the Masurao has great articulation, with 30+ ball joints and swivel joints. Any pose you want to put this guy in, he can pull it off excellently. Unfortunately, the small ball joints (and the largeness of) the pods at his hips cause them to pop off occasionally, but not enough to be considered a problem.    As for accessories, the Masurao comes with three sets of hands: a closed fist, open hands, and hands for holding his two beam swords, designed to look like giant laser-katana (which fit very well in both his hands and his hip-mounted pods for storage). The hands are set on tiny ball-joints and are very tight, so care should be taken when swapping them to prevent possible breakage. The Masurao also comes with two belt-like attachements that plug into the back of his head, just like on the show.    And as a bonus, the figure comes with a personalized display stand! The base of the stand is adorned with Japanese lettering that really completes the feel of the samurai-themed mobile suit and bumps this Damashii up to \\"Highly Recommended\\".    Pros:  -Very accurate to the anime.  -Very detailed and well-painted.  -Nice selection of accessories.  -Extremely articulate.  -Sturdy joints.  -Good price.  -Bonus display stand!    Cons:  -Ball-joints for hand-swapping seem fragile.  -Some parts seem a bit fragile.  -Difficult to stand on its own.  -Not so much a con, but this really isn't a toy for kids.    Note: There is an almost-identical version of the Masurao called the Susanowo, with white instead of red and different accessories. As far as I know the two are identical, so really whichever color suits your taste.

review_headline: Arond the World in 80 Days - up to 6 players!
review_body: We boardgame a lot and sometimes we have exactly six players. I can think of only a handful of perfect boardgames for six and 'Around the World in 80 Days' is one of them. You start in London and instead of trying to get as many victory points you are trying to use up as few days as possible to travel (the track is around the outside of the board). Journeying from city to city generally take two train cards (numbers on them represent days travelled), two boat cards, or a combination. More if you are on the last leg of the journey. Player turn order gives you a pick of one of the cards but it's also associated with a special action (e.g.: first pick next turn; move a day-stealing detective; get money; special action card). And special actions are where it's at. An action card deck can give special aid or set all or nearly everyone back when a storm takes place. I fully recommend this game for all.

There are so many effects you can do with this gimick and it is easy to do, not much practice needed but practice always make things smoother.    -Mike

product_title: Blade 120 SR RTF Helicopter BLH3100
review_body:
First flight: It fell from about 12 feet, found a small gear lying next to it. Put it back on. Flight time: about 15 seconds. Second flight: went out of control, fell from about 15 feet and one entire side of the body is cracked, and a piece the size of a dime is missing. Flight time: about 8 seconds. 3rd flight: lasted about 10 seconds because I still couldnt get the adjustments tuned in right, but nothing broke. 4th flight: Before lift off I discovered the tailfin was missing. Went to previous crash areas but not there. Must have blew off in "flight". Liftoff was very noisy, and found that the tail rotor is the reason. No idea why. Spent the next 5 mins trying to dial in the adjustments. HEY! Got it to hover! Great! Hovered for 10 seconds and battery went dead. Total flight time: less than a minute.

Pros: Love the transmitter..
Neighborhood cats like to chase it.
Cons: Not a thing about this copter justifies the price tag.

I have plenty of experience with the Syma 107. While learning to fly it, it has hit walls, ceilings, me, outside trees, plowed into a neighbors roof, and yet..not one thing is broke or cracked. That is a durable chopper with many hours of use.

*update* Bought replacement parts fixed it up. Took it out....flew good for a while then a servo locked up. Busted my body pins and servo is still locked up Completely useless..... When it rocketed forward and to the left, it was after adjusting the trim. This proves that this copter does not react correctly to the commands. When you give it throttle, it should go UP.....not forward. While others try to discredit my review, they don't know the amount of time I took to read the manual, and even bring it with me while trying to fly this flying money pit.

review_headline: If 100 Pennies Equals $1 Then Why Are There Only 62?
review_body: I have been happy overall with my purchase of this play money set.  I do wonder why the set did not come with enough pennies to make a dollar though.  When I'm teaching my son how many quarters, nickels, dimes, pennies make a dollar he gets frustrated when there aren't enough pennies to show me he can make a dollar.  I think that the company probably just didn't think to provide adequate numbers of each coin needed to demonstrate the very basic concepts required to teach counting money from square one (i.e. 100 pennies = $1).  In all other aspects this play money set is a wonderful educational tool.

product_title: E-Flite Charger, 1S 3.7V LiPo Charger, 0.3A: Blade mCX
review_headline: Blow up all your lipos with this little gem
review_body: No auto-shut off, which means, if you don't catch that the little red light went off in about 5 minutes, You poof and ruin your battery.  I watch fairly closely, but i miss it to change a diaper, or to take out the garbage to the curb and i've ruined another battery.  No big deal when batterys are only $5 a pop which is what I'm guessing they count on when they sell you this, but after you've had it a little while, puffed batteries and waiting for additional batteries to come in the mail put a real dent in your flight time.  Just spend the money and get a balanced charger with auto shut-off and don't waste your money on this!  Also, just throw the one that came with your Blade away, it is garbage.

product_title: Toy Story 16" Buzz Lightyear Plush Doll
review_body: My grandson received a hard plastic Buzz Lightyear as a holiday gift. Deeply in love with Buzz, the child carried Buzz everywhere, and of course wanted Buzz to nap with him. Being two, the child also likes to throw his toys around, and when Buzz went \\"to infinity and beyond,\\" well, it just didn't bode well for the rest of the family to have a hard plastic Buzz hurling through the air.    Soft Buzz to the rescue. Soft Buzz looks just like hard plastic Buzz, is durable, cuddly, nap-able, throw-able (within reason, though, presumably, to infinity and beyond also)--an entirely acceptable replacement, in the eyes of this two-year-old. Creative parent gently guided hard plastic Buzz to a safe place in the attic, explaining to the child Buzz was going on some sort of interplanetary mission, and he would return when the child was closer to four years old, and could play without hurling Buzz through the air. This explanation was intriguing to the child and new Soft Buzz is the favourite constant companion.    Soft Buzz arrived with lighting speed, too, to thankful parents, grandparents and child. We are all very happy, and Soft Buzz is a welcome family member. Thank you.

product_title: Wonder Forge Richard Scarry's Busytown, Eye Found It
review_body: Finally a kids game that Mom and Dad will like to play!  Reach the picnic island before \\"Pig Will\\" and \\"Pig Won't\\" eat all the food.  There are a number of \\"Goldbug\\" cards, which compel the team to search the board for objects found in Busy Town: barricades, traffic cones, hot dogs, kites, numbers and more!  There are enough objects to find that players (even adults) will not remember where things were the last time you searched for them.  Each player then moves the number of spaces that equal the number of objects found while searching.  Kids will learn and read new words, team work (everyone wins or everyone loses), and game skills.  Comes in a nice box with lid that hinges and folds onto the box and a very durable game board.  You'll find yourself playing the Busy Town game over and over.

review_headline: I expected better from Dinosaur Train merchandise...
review_body: We purchased the Dinosaur Train set with the track and station. It said it came with the nest and time tunnel. These were flimsy cardboard and didn't even last one day. My 2 1/2 year old even recognized they were 'not good' and 'flimsy.' I expected something he could actually play with and that was impossible, they wouldn't even stay together OR stand up. Further, the dinosaurs will not stand on their own, even on a flat surface, which is a source of great frustration for my son. They will not stay in their train cars (even propped up) when the cars are moving. It appears they have a little 'peg' that is supposed to go into a little hole in the car, but that is impossible for either my husband and I to accomplish, so no child would be able to accomplish it. The train that comes with the set will not pull any extra cars without spinning it's wheels and going no where. Then to add insult to injury, we purchased lights and sounds Dinosaur train hoping to help the original train along (by splitting up the cars) without realizing that although we spent MORE in lights and sounds train relative to the set, it does NOT move. To a 2 1/2 year old, it appears broken and he doesn't understand that ONE train won't sing and the OTHER train won't move. Very disappointed.

He loved it but broke soon thereafter (wheel wouldn't stay on).  I bought a different brand with thicker plastic for about $20. My son is very active, but not destructive, so my goal was to find a truck that could keep up with him at 2 -  and grow with him into boyhood.  I found it here!  This truck is rugged, hard wearing and strong. I wish I had invested in it in the beginning and not wasted my money on the other two cheaply made alternatives.

product_title: Little Tikes Seek & Explore Expedition Climber
review_body: I was really excited to get this for our soon-to-be two year old for the backyard. He generally loves to climb and we thought this would be endless entertainment throughout the summer. First, it's much smaller than it seems in the picture, so that is somewhat disappointing. The slide has a very abrupt curve at the bottom, so his feet hit the bottom of the slide and stop him before his bottom hits the end, which means he basically slides for about 8 inches! Also, it's just held together by screws in plastic, and at times it seems a tad less sturdy than I would have liked. Our little guy is a bit above average in size (27 lbs) and when he stands on the orange landing to climb up, you can see it bow in the center, so I'm not sure how it could handle a 6 year old, as stated.  I'm also not sure how it will hold up in a move (we are a military family and move often) - I fear the stress on the plastic where the screws are may not withstand the summer from moving it weekly to mow the lawn. Otherwise, it was rather simple to put together by myself and took less than 30 minutes. I would not buy again.

product_title: Life Cycles Blu-ray
review_body: I'm going to start by saying this is one of my favorite movies that I own, definitely my favorite bike movie. I currently own The Collective, The Collective Roam, The Collective Seasons, ordered Follow Me the same time I ordered Life Cycles, and want New World Disorder 10.  The others are very good bike movies, I still like them but to me, in my opinion don't compare to Life Cycles in Blu Ray. Some say that the movies has too much slow-motion, too many scenery shots and that it doesn't make them want to ride.  It isn't all slow-motion and the scenery shots are pretty cool.  Life Cycles was shot in ultra HD and when you're watching it on a 120hz flatscreen all I can say is wow... With their cinematography, the riding, and the scenery it motivates me to go ride. Even if someone doesn't like mountain biking I think they would enjoy watching it for the scenery in ultra HD.  This movie shows a certain elegance a rider can have with mountain biking, not always just plowing down the trail and hardcore hucking. If that's what you're in the mood for then NWD movies would probably be better for you.  Follow Me was good but the production quality looked as though I shot it myself with my 4 mega pixel camera and I just picked music off of my Itunes, it just didn't flow to me. I bought that in Blu Ray too and it almost wasn't worth the exra money for Blu Ray. The storyline, the music and the riding in this Life Cycles flowed very well.  I recommend this movie to anyone who rides a mountain bike and can appreciate great production quality.

product_title: Playskool Musical Activity Ball and Gear Center
review_headline: Matching, Stacking, Turning, Pushing, Placement, Cause and Effect
review_body:
This is a simple toy but my nine-month-old granddaughter gets a lot of action out of it. She likes to re-arrange or stack the gears before pushing the big red button on the right to turn the gears. (The big red button has eyes on it) She has learned that there are several ways to make the gears turn. The attached extra gears on the upper right corner make the circular face near them spin when she turns those gears manually. The two balls snap out of their holding spots (holding spots are the two hollow circles on the upper body and these help keep all the pieces together for clean up time) and she has to figure out that she can drop them into the top (out of sight) and they will spill out of the front shoot and onto a little turn table. When she turns the gears by pressing the big red button, this little turn table spins also and eventually pops the ball out for a surprise action. Each of the lower gears can be moved, removed or stacked. They each have a pattern on the center which can be matched with a pattern on the gear mechanism itself. That would be appropriate for older siblings. The whole toy is lightweight enough that she can lift it, turn it over and generally explore it. It is colorful and exciting to look at. She has had it for several weeks and plays with it every time it is close enough to grab.

If you have a baby who enjoys exploring how things work, this toy could be engaging and fun for them. If your baby is one who is entirely focused on other things (making faces, making noises, moving instead of sitting etc.) and NOT interested in manually exploring how something works, this might not be the toy for them. It is colorful and interesting enough to catch their curiosity but they should be in that \\"I want to know how this works and know everything it can do\\" stage.

To happy babies everywhere !!!!!

product_title: Discovery Exclusive Frog Pond Terrarium
review_headline: Save your money, buy a real aquarium and a pet from a local pet shop.
review_body: My son was given this product as a gift for christmas.  He was so excited at the prospect of growing a small creature to an adult and keeping it/caring for it.  I have seven fish tanks of my own with several different aquatic species, so thought this would be a good \\"beginning\\" experience for him.  I was wrong.     Immediately I saw major flaws with the container itself: it wasn't easy to clean, too small, many areas that could entrap a small creature and kill it, no filtration/aeration.  Basically, it is not suitable for a small aquatic creature to live in, nor an adult frog if you manage to raise one to adulthood because it is far too small for the species they recommend it for (the Northern Leopard Frog).    Which brings me to the next complaint...  [...]    This company was recommended by the Discovery Kids product, and has shipped two tadpoles to me.  The first swam in circles for two days, wouldn't eat, then died.  We just received the second shipment after waiting two months.  The second tadpole arrived already dead, and apparently for some time, as it smells very bad.    Please, keep your money.  Do not spend it on this product as it is a waste.  Buy a nice five or ten gallon aquarium kit from a local store (Walmart sells them), have fun decorating it with your kids, cycle it and your filter for a month, then buy a pet from your local fish store as well.  A good choice would be an african dwarf frog (not the clawed species), or just a couple of nice guppies.  Do a little research on setting up the aquarium and your animal beforehand so that you can minimize untimely deaths.  This is a much better choice for your children and the poor tadpoles being tortured and killed in these containers shipped by ribbitsgalore.    I hope that my experience and my information will help other parents to give their children a REWARDING experience rather than the FAILURE provided by this product.

product_title: James Bond 007: The Golden Gun Limited Edition Prop Replica
review_body: I'm an avid collector of movie memorabilia, dating all the way back to the SD Studios version of this golden gun.  When I saw there was another company re making this golden gun at a quarter of the price I was very excited. But there's a little Sang \\"you  Get what you pay for\\" in this case, when I purchased the golden gun, I was very upset when I received the pistol. The gold plating on the gun was actually very thin and very cheap. The plating was not even one micron thick. Over time the plating will wear very fast. Not only that but there were several casting defects and air bubbles in the metal itself. The company who makes these doesn't tell you they are manufactured in china.. But they are mass produced there. Also, these are not a true limited edition item. These are open numbered which means the company will continue to make these golden guns until they can sell no more and they will stop the over seas production. The plaque that the golden gun comes with is numbered with a black magic marker that someone wrote in by hand. I had gotten number 714. There was no 714 out of 2000. It was just 714... I strongly incurage anyone not to waste 500 or even even more depending on sellers on this gun replica. You will be very disappointed with the product. I'm a member at the replica prop forums and some other members there confronted the company about the poor quality of these guns as everyone was eagerly awaiting there pre order arival, the company replied by saying \\" our guns are half the price of the sd studios version, we tried to get it as close as possible, but this gun give collectors a chance to own this item at a more affordable price\\" so all in all there saying you get what younpay for... Back in 1998 the SD studios version sold for 1200 but the quality was un touchable. Steve from sd studios is a good friend of mine for years and this pistol is not even in the same universe as sd's. I was very upset I spent over 500 buck on an item that looked to be 50 bucks.Base metal components with cheap mass plating like they use one those fake purses hardware  you see on the street for sale, parts of the pen like the clip are super glued in at the top.  I hope no one falls for this trap. I want people to really know what they will get before they buy. The pictures look great but the product is terrible. I would never take the time to write this long review if the product was not that bad. The only thing that was amazing was amazons excellent customer service and getting me my refund. Also there are several people out there with defective pistols and the company never got back to them to fix the pistols. Also one last thing I forgot to mention is the gold 007 bullet that comes with the gun which is the most important part, it's plastic and it's spray painted gold. They couldn't even make it metal...

Obviously, if something is of value, you're not going to have your kid paint in it.  I just put one of my husband's old shirts over my son's shirt and that works fine as a smock. product_title: Gundam 00: GN-X III A-RAWS Type Robot Soul Spirits Side MS Figure
review_headline: Not the Greatest of the Robot Spirits Mobile Suits.
review_body: I must first note that I am not the biggest fan of the GN-X III mobile suit's design, so I'll admit this review may be slightly biased. The figure is an excellent interpretation of the on-screen enforcer of the A-LAWS from Gundam 00, with all the accessories expected and accurate sculpt and colors.    The articulation on the GN-X is probably its biggest point of contention, as the strange hip armor pieces severely limit hip and leg articulation. The figure has around 20 joints in total, which is slightly less than usual for a Robot Damashii Gundam, but still allows it to pull off decent poses. The head in particular is very expressive despite the seemingly-limited collar.    The GN-X comes with a GN Beam Rifle which he can gold very sturdily, though the forearm peg just barely squeezes into the slot, as well as a transformable GN Lance. The lance can be extended to be nearly twice the height of the figure itself, who does hold it rather well in lance mode, but is very loose in rifle mode. The GN-X also comes with a very nice shield with a rotating center, as well as a very cool crimson beam saber. Unfortunately, the beam fits very tightly in the hilt, and it feels like you're going to break it unless you take care when removing the beam. Also, he only comes with two sets of hands: open and weapon-holding.     There really is nothing that sets the GN-X too far back from other Robot Damashiis, other than the slightly limited articulation and accessories. If you like the design of the GN-X, then this is a great representation of it and, due to the low price from most retailers (some even going for $10 plus shipping!), could be considered for army-building. I'd lightly recommend this figure.    Pros:  -Accurate sculpt and paint apps.  -Nice assortment of accessories.  -Excellent articulation nonetheless.  -Lovely head design.  -Often very cheap.    Cons:  -Limited articulation in hips.  -Somewhat cheap-feeling plastic quality.  -Accessory count small for a Robot Spirits.  -GN Lance can barely be held in Rifle mode.  -Beam saber very fragile.

product_title: Hunting Zone Pump Action Shotgun, 4 Shells Included
review_headline: Pretty good prop for Engineer cosplay.
review_body:
If you play \\"Team Fortress 2\\", you like to cosplay (Dress up) and you're thinking of cosplaying as an engineer then this toy gun is pretty close to what the engineer uses as his vanilla (Original) primary weapon. The color and design of the stock are the only fairly glaring differences. You can find this exact gun under different manufacturers (Kidz Toyz) and \\"series\\" (Outdoor Hunter) names at K-mart, Family Dollar, Fred's, Maxway and possibly Big Lots. You can get them as cheap as $10.99 to $14.99 at those stores. I bought mine's at Fred's for $10.99.

As indicated on the packaging, it makes a shooting noise when the trigger is pulled. It's not too loud, but if you don't like hearing the sound repeatedly then there is a battery hatch in the stock where you can disable it. The shells might also be an annoyance factor since they'll probably be littering the floor.

I have no idea how well this gun fares with kids or air/car travel (I have yet to go to a convention that allows toy guns), but it has fared very good with me and, just recently, with a cross-country move where it was packed in a box by a bad moving company. Only three shells will fit into the chamber of the gun, so you'll need to put the extras in a container so they are not lost, chewed up by a pet or possibly swallowed by a child. The shells get stuck in the chamber when you slide the forestock backwards or forwards sometimes, but they are not too hard to remove. The \\"spent shells\\" are ejected out like you would see in a shotgun, so make sure you're not anywhere where they can fall into a hole or underneath something.

However, the cockpit is a bit cramped and will require you to sort of \\"scrunch\\" your figure up to get him in. Once there, it's not bad and the cycle's cockpit will close. As for sound effects/light effects, my cycle only lights up when you touch the button on the side which causes the front wheel to light up.
