product_title: LeapFrog Explorer Learning Game: Wolverine and the X-Men (works with LeapPad & Leapster Explorer)
review_headline: Great game but not until they are ready.
review_body:
This game by itself is great. I will say though, that we have always bought LeapFrog products a little too advanced for our son. He plays around with them and then figures out what they are teaching. We've gotten just about every LeapFrog product for him since birth. He is now in his 8th week of Kindergarten and is at a 2nd grade reading level, and plans are being made to test him out to third grade this week. I owe this entirely LeapFrog, because our son has really latched on to learning without us having to push it on him. This game however is one that didn't work with our usual formula. A child must already be spelling words on their own frequently not to get frustrated. This isn't the usual \\"buy it and they'll grow into game\\". It more reinforces currrent skills and knowledge. We will probably be putting it away and trying again in 6 months. Overall I highly recommend this game if your child is already spelling (or being required to spell) many words, because it builds upon that.
I can't comment on durability because we've only had this game for a month. I will say, however, that I was disappointed that the gold metal contact plates on the back that go into the Leapster are exposed on all Explorer games. They are not covered like on previous Leapster games. We'll see if this is a problem in the future as far as durability.

product_title: Mattel The Sing-A-Ma-Jigs - Hot Pink
review_body: My grandchildren loved these toys--and so did their parents.  When you push their tummies their mouths open as they make their particular sounds.  I bought 5 of them so we were able to produce quite a concert.  I thought it was a annoying that you have to push their tummies for each individual sound.  When the toy is in song mode I wish you could just push the tummy once and the Sing-A-Ma-Jig would play the entire song.  Another concern is how to keep these toys clean.  There are no instructions included for their care.  I suppose you have to surface clean them.  They won't stay clean long with toddlers.

product_title: Star Wars 94254 R2-D2 Interactive Astromech Droid, 17.1 x 11.7 x 11.5-Inch (Discontinued by manufacturer)
review_headline: Worth the Money!  Our new family pet!! :D
review_body: I bought this product 2 months ago for a Christmas present and was so excited for my son to open today today (christmas morning)... after playing with it I decided I had to immediately write a review!  First of all, if you have no patience this is NOT the toy for you, this is what I get from the people with bad reviews.  You have to get to know him, learn what makes him happy and what makes him sad/mad.  When I first turned him on, he seemed almost scared/sad but he cheered up just by talking with him (really I didnt even give him commands) just let him beep back at whatever I said to him, he likes to talk!  Then I started with commands of people I knew would make him happy! If he does get in a bad mood, you may have to tell him several times to \\"behave yourself!\\" and then \\"reset system\\" brings back to normal.  You get used to his beeps, and if you are boring or annoying him he'll walk away lol.  He heard a movie on the tv and rolled in front of it, turned towards the tv and watched it (no command used, he just sensed the noise from the tv).  Make sure to pause and give him time to respond to the steps in the manual and he responds to much more than is listed, I already had him doing several other songs & dances.  I think his stubborn nature makes him a little more fun, if he did only do just what I wanted him to then he would be kinda boring and we'd be bored of him. My son calls him his \\"pet R2D2\\"... my son has more trouble controlling him, but hes only 4 and doesnt get yet to pause to get him to understand commands but he loves just talking to him and seeing what hes up to lol unfortunately my son likes to upset R2 by asking him about Darth Vader! but I have quickly learned how to fix this problem!  I love this toy, it really has a personality of its own!

product_title: Toy Story 42 Inch Bop Bag (styles may vary)
review_body: We got this for our son, put water in the bottom and it wouldn't bounce back.  My husband then picked it up and realized there was nothing keeping the water in the bottom, it was sloshing around in the whole thing.  We'll try to rig it to work with something but it's disappointing to see your kid run around excitedly when they receive the gift and then be unable to play with it.    UPDATE:  I have had really wonderful communication with the company and they are sending a replacement.

product_title: Cars Toon El Materdor Track Set
review_body: This toy was easy to assemble and seems durable.  It comes with two cars from the El Materdor toon--El Materdor and the bulldozer.  There's just not that much to the play of it.  You place El Materdor in front of the spring release, push the button, and he zooms around the track.  The idea is that he'll \\"jump\\" over the bulldozer and land on the small unattached track piece, thereby triggering the \\"roses to fall.\\"  My son seems to have fun with it but not for a long time at at stretch.  He plays more with just the two cars.

product_title: Fisher-Price TRIO DC Super Friends Batwing
review_headline: Lots of Fun, Better than Legos for Under 7s
review_body: Both of my sons love Batman.  We have the Imaginext(?) Batout and my kids love it as well as the other toys.  We recently discovered Trios and are big fans.  The pieces are much larger than Legos--which means that kids are less likely to lose them, plus they can build bigger things more easily.  Both my 5 and 7 year old have had great fun building all sorts of different flying contraptions from the Trio BatWing set.  We've bought Lego sets designed for 5+ before, but honestly, many of them are too complicated for my kids to put together by themselves.  With Trio, both my 5 and 7 year old can follow the directions in the manual and easily create whatever it is they want to create.  Then they have the option of creating all sorts of other creations as well.  This is a great gift for a Batman fan!

product_title: VTech - MobiGo Touch Learning System
review_body: Got this for our nieces and they absolutely love it. It's even caused a few fights.Battery life is good and they tell me it's perfect for long car trips. The screen is bright enough to use in the car. They love the games and enjoy competing with each other and sometimes helping each other out.

product_title: Connect 4 x 4
review_body: I bought this for my 5yo...guess I should have waited a little longer.  Anyways, it is a fun game if the children are old enough and is very colorful.  I like the way the game tiles store in the game rack.

product_title: Great Eastern Naruto Mist Village Logo Headband
review_body: My son bought this and he loves it! It is a pretty good fit, just a little bending (carefully) will do the trick. Great product, pretty fast delivery! Good product!

product_title: V-Cube 7 Multicolor
review_body: I haven't been cubing for very long - just one summer - but I still know that this cube is an amazing cube. After hearing so many people telling me how theirs have popped and exploded, i was timid about buying one. Now, however, i see that the cube is very high quality. Out of the box, the layers slide very smoothly and very solidly. It doesn't feel like it is going to fall apart. Curious, I wanted to see how it popped. So i made it pop on purpose and surprisingly only two pieces came out. I haven't had it pop on me accidentally at all. I recommend this cube, by far, over any other cube in your arsenal. However, do not jump from 3x3 to 7x7, i read that in another review for this product and they are completely correct. It is like a 5x5. I reccomend learning the 3x3 first then going on to the 4x4, then onto the 5x5. After that, you can choose to go to a 6x6 or 7x7. Best cube i've ever had.

product_title: Glass Go Stones JangStone No.1 - 9.5mm (Size 34)
review_body: These seem like nice stones, however, my life is boring and so I decided to count the number I received.  My box was short 1 white stone from what was advertised.  I contacted Amazon about getting an extra stone and was told that I could only return the item and try a new set.  Well...the new set is short a couple black stones...so I guess I'll just combine the two sets to form a complete set and send back the rest.  Regardless, somebody should be checking the quantities in these packages.  I'm sure I'll never need that one extra stone but I still feel like they should at least include as many stones as advertised and even throw in an extra or too.

product_title: Bead Bazaar Medium Bead Barrel
review_headline: Want a big bunch of beads and bead strings for kids?  Get this!
review_body: Huge assortment of beads, mostly with fairly large openings for stringing and a bunch of colored strings.  Some charms and alphabet beads.  Nice assortment, great condition, well packed in separate bags and boxes.  If you have small kids that want to make some bracelets and necklaces or make other bead projects, this is the best bet.

product_title: Nintendo Luigi
review_body: I bought both Luigi and Mario for my nephews (ages 4 and 5) and they LOVE them! The younger one likes to pull on his toys and usually rips them but, once he discovered that his Luigi was indestructible, it became his best friend! A little pricey but a very durable toy!

product_title: Trouble Game (Amazon Exclusive)
review_body: I'm 33. This game is made like crap compared to what I had in the 80s. Why is it so small? I had to assemble the game myself. It's made of extremely light plastic. The bottom is even a poor excuse for cardboard. Its more like a heavy weight paper. I tried to sell it at a consignment shop, and the store didn't even want it. It ended up at the dump and I bought a vintage version off ebay.

product_title: Dr. Freud's Therapy Ball
review_body: The idea is great.  The tag lines are funny.  But the delivery is off.  I could barely see the writing in the triangle.  It takes the fun out of it.  :(

product_title: Melissa & Doug Trunki Sunny
review_headline: Not sure what happened to the Trunki
review_body: I purchased the Trunki by Trendy Kid for my older son last year.  It is great.  So, I now have another son and thought \\"why not buy a trunki for him too!\\"  I was excited to see that it was Melissa & Doug, made in the USA, and that they had other colors available.  Well, it is a piece of junk.  I received it and one of the latches was already broken off.  I tried to follow the directions for the other latch to see if I could fix the one that fell of, but it simply didn't work.  It didn't slide up as the directions stated.  I couldn't get it to do anything and then, it fell off too.  At least then I could open the trunki.  I tried to put them back on and they pop right back on.  But, with simply removing the latches entirely (whether locked or unlocked) there is nothing secure about the closure.  Plus, they eliminated the handy accessory pocket from the original so there is no longer an organized pouch for little kid socks or underwear.  This costs less than the original, but it is totally useless.

product_title: US Toy Child Feather Angel Wings Costume
review_body: Delivery was awesome... Very fast... But--- However beautiful these Angel Wings look, they should NOT be advertised as 'Child\\" size... They are tiny... TODDLER size ( about the size of a notebook)... The online picture of the Angel dress, halo and wings show them as being much MUCH larger... My granddaughter is 5 and they look lost on her... Maybe my expectations were higher because of how beautiful they were shown in the picture with the dress...  Instead of these huge, beautiful, angel wings, they are simply tiny and do not really show on either side of her when facing forward... Totally ruined the look as compared to the pictures online... Trying to return them... Wish me luck!

product_title: Schylling Mini Wire Puzzles 12 pack Brain Teaser
review_body: These are fun.  They work the brain & can really get people going.  Great to leave out on the table, sparking curiousity with guests.  The best surprise is when someone unexpectedly gets it.

product_title: Scene It? Comedy Movies Deluxe - Adults Version
review_body: We have many Scene It games and really enjoy the quality of the product. So we were excited to see this game as our whole family loves comedy films. It hard to describe how disappointed we were with this edition. Poor film selection, poor scene selection and a bad user interface. We used a blue ray DVD player and it had a long delay every time we needed the remote, which is often on an interactive game. In our opinion, the company did not pay up for clips of more popular classic comedies. Move on to your next choice...

product_title: Black-suited Spider-man Kids Boot Covers
review_headline: A little disappointing/not what I expected
review_body: These boot covers are pretty much just socks with a treaded/rubbery sole.  Kind of like baby socks that have grippers on them.     There is no room in them for my son to wear shoes, but they are not substantial enough to wear on their own.  I assumed by \\"boot cover\\" they would fit more like spats and be open on the bottom or have an elastic that goes under the shoe like I've seen on other Halloween costumes.

product_title: Rugrats the Movie Watch Tommy Burger King
review_body: I bought this expecting to get the blue electronic Tommy watch they had sold at Burger King when the first movie came out, the very same watch I had adored as a young boy. I literally counted the days for my watch to arrive so I could hear that lovable baby say \\"A baby's got to do, what a baby's got to do.\\". When I opened the package and saw none other than Chuckys nerdy face instead of Tommy's bald-headed charm, I went ballistic. Nonetheless, I am extremely complacent and am wearing it right now.    Other than being completely disappointed, it is a pretty standard watch. The batteries were dead upon arrival which makes it unusable, but those can be replaced. The scratch and sniff banana print on the watch smells like a combination of plastic and bananas, a bit pleasant if you like odd smells. If you're a fan of Chucky from the series, get it. If you're a casual shopper looking for some items that cause massive amounts of Tommy related nostalgia, be prepared to be disapointed.

product_title: Educational Insights Eggspert
review_headline: Best bet for group trivia games
review_body: I do a lot of training at work and got a lot of stares when I pulled this out. Staff were rolling their eyes looking at it and getting huffy. Then I asked the first question and buzzers started ringing in. Staff loved it!! I've used it for family feud, jeopardy, wheel of fortune, and other games. Staff don't dread training as much now and get more involved in the training. It also builds team spirit. Yes, it looks like a pre-schooler toy, but our staff love it! The options for buzzing are simple yet allow you to change the type of game you want to play, and it's great to have a very unbiased indicator of who buzzed first.

review_body: This is a well constructed backpack. The compartments are roomy and it handles well.  My only complaint is that there is only one zipper per compartment so he has to zip it ALL the way over to close it (so he doesn't).

review_body: Costume arrived in perfect condition much quicker than the estimated arrival date. Costume fit well for the size range 8-10. All the essential pieces for your child to pretend to be a Pokemon trainer.

product_title: Playmobil 4141 Transport Set GoCart Race Compact Set
review_headline: Amazing quality and detail for the price
review_body: This was given to our almost-3 year old, and the recommended age of 4 would probably be more appropriate -- we removed the little traffic cones, not so much because we were seriously concerned about choking as we didn't think he'd get the concept.    But I have never been so impressed with the overall quality and design of a toy. The little figures fit beautifully into the carts, with their \\"hands\\" snapping onto the controls, and the cars themselves roll better than anything in the house (matchbox, Thomas, you name it). The cars will easily roll over 20 feet on a flat surface before they finally stop. The details, particularly for a toy at this price, are also amazing: tiny helmets that can be removed, a flag, a trophy, and the aforementioned traffic cones.    I've now scoured the Playmobil site and read other rave reviews from parents, and I'm a convert. I look forward to exploring the castles, circuses, Egypts, fire stations etc. when our boy is in the 4-6 year range!

review_body: My one year old daughter absolutely loves this chair.  Now she can sit in the living room with the rest of the family in her very own big girl chair.

No idea what caused it to die, but it's not as if it was dipped in water or dropped or anything.  Terribly disappointing.  At about $15-20 I'd consider myself satisfied with what we got out of it.  At $30-40 I'd consider myself disappointed.  At $75-80 I feel completely ripped off.

product_title: LEGO Star Wars Rebel Trooper Battle Pack (8083)
review_body: I purchased this as a gift for a five year old boy. He immediately opened it and tackled building it. He successfully completed it that afternoon. A big plus for Lego toys is the instructions: Lego got its instructions right. That a five year old can assemble this toy on his own, without help, pretty much says it all. The directions are clear and easy to understand. Their method is to show all of the parts needed for each step, which allows you to collect the parts needed before you start each step. They even put life-size pictures of similar parts that allow you to compare the actual piece with the picture to make sure it's the right size. The only problem we encountered occurred when we put the finishing touches on it in the final steps. It can be a little hard to attach pieces without accidentally removing others (for which I removed a star from the durability rating). It's said that getting there is half the fun, but in this case building these toys seems to be the most fun of all.

product_title: A Day Out With Thomas Game
review_body: This game has some fun, imaginative ideas, but it could use some adjustments to make it worth playing. I agree with other criticisms: the game pieces are too large for the board; and more importantly it takes too long to play and can become very frustrating and boring. Why?  Because it's nearly impossible to land on any of the 6 stars in order to punch your ticket. (and you have to punch your ticket 4 times)  Imagine using the spinner to go around the board again, and again and again, and each time missing a star by 1 or 2 points (ugh!).  I'm considering adding some stars...so that each station has at least 2 chances to enter and pick a card.  Mostly, I'm feeling pretty frustrated with the lack of consideration on the manufacturer's part.  If they would have actually sat down and played this game, they would have seen that it shouldn't take more than 20 minutes for a person to actually land on a star.  (and there's nothing but spinning and jumping until you do land on a star)  Again, I think a simple adjustment would have made all the difference (like adding more stars).  Hopefully they'll make some adjustments before printing out more of this game. My 4 year old son is now telling me that he wants me to write that he \\"only doesn't like it a tiny, tiny, tiny little bit.\\" :) (just needs to be \\"shorter\\")

product_title: Childrens Boxing Sports Set With Gloves Punching Ball Bag Kids Toy
review_headline: Seller and Manufacturer Should Be Ashamed!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
review_body: Please, please do not buy this item, it is one of the most useless poorly made products I've ever seen!!!  This is also 1 of my first reviews ever!  This was a Christmas gift for my 4 1/2 year old son.  It didn't last 10 minutes!!! The box looked pretty neat, except for poor wording (made in China), took it out of the box   and was immediately concerned with the quality of the product.  I first noticed the plug in the base looked inadequate which proved true.  It leaks water as you punch the bag.  Second I noticed very cheap quality of the washers, metal, even the funny little needle they sent to blow up the bag (made in China).  The third thing I noticed was how poorly the bag attached to   the pole (made in China)  I did get it all put together and my son started punching at it (he's 4 1/2 but very small, 35 lbs. -so he's no Mike Tyson).  The look of sheer joy filled his face, and then about 10 minutes   into punching the bag I noticed the bag was getting loose.  I checked it, and the nut that is attached to the pole that the bag screws into was rotating inside the tube.  The bag now wobbles back and  forth and is about ready to break off.  I stopped my son short of sending the bag flying though the air so that I could let the company know.  Nobody in their right mind would be proud to sell, produce, or own this bag (made in China).  I recommend researching for a more quality maybe more expensive bag!!!!!!  (maybe one not made in China)   I hope this helps!!

I do like the fact that it's elevated, not ground level, so he doesn't get as dirty.  I think its height will also discourages neighborhood cats, even when parents forget to cover the table.  It's a great toy for pre-schoolers!

product_title: Thomas Build 'n Go
review_body: I'm not a big fan of Thomas the train and we received it as a gift a few years back. This train has survived 3 kids (my oldest son got it first when he was 3 years old). It's been very durable. The small parts like the screws are not easy to lose. You use a screw driver (no drill) so there's manual turning and coordination. The train runs well on carpet as well as hardwood floor. My now 7 year old son still plays with it by putting things on the train or doing science experiments by figuring out what the maximum weight the train can push.

product_title: Athearn HO Scale RTR GP38-2, UP #625
review_body: First I will say I am new to model railroading. That being said I am a network and broadcasting engineer. I started with a junky Bachmann set around $55 and kinda caught the fever you could say. After building a layout and purchasing much of others peoples junk off of ebay I bought the Athearn GP38-2 Union Pacific #625 new. Im not doing DCC at this time and am powering the layout with a Tech4 power supply. The train runs and sounds smooth and very low speeds. It even pulls well but slow, up my newbie designed abusive 5% grade...yeah I dont know what I was thinking. However I bought a another twin to this one and together they march right up this. It works well with the momentum feature and doesnt act jerky. I dont really care for the crew-fryer light...I guess at this price level they dont care too much about that. product_title: The Settlers of Catan
review_headline: Settlers of Catan compared with Chess and Monopoly
review_body:
I'll start by saying that I grew up playing (and loving) Monopoly, Chess, and a slew of card games among other board/outdoors games that aren't similar to this game (Boggle, Scrabble, Taboo, Scattergories, jigsaw puzzles, etc.). I definitely come from a game-playing family. I see aspects of Monopoly and Chess melded into Settlers of Catan as one, cohesive and fantastic, board game. Settlers of Catan is an awesome game for people who enjoy strategy and enjoy the suspense associated with not knowing who will win until the end! (I still love Monopoly and Chess and hold them in high esteem.)

Key Differences:

MONOPOLY: It was always pretty easy to determine the winner well before the end of the game based on property holdings and cash-in-hand, this is not the case with Settlers of Catan. You begin the game with one free settlement (\\"house\\" equivalent in Monopoly), one city (\\"hotel\\" equivalent in Monopoly), and two roads. Unlike Monopoly, there are no set \\"property blocks\\" in this game. You place your pieces and build roads between them. This is how you built more settlements and cities! It takes thought and strategy since you can block your opponents and/or try to build on resources that fit your needs.

CHESS: If you wish, you can anticipate your opponents next move and plan in advance, this is not the case with Settlers of Catan. The next move can be guessed, but not necessarily likely depending on what resource, development, and/or progress cards you hold. Players may know the NUMBER of cards you have, but not their contents (unless you show them). You win the game by attaining \\"victory points.\\" At some point, the game usually becomes neck-and-neck between a few players. You never know who will get the necessary number of victory points, or if the underdog comes back with one or two strategic moves!

OTHER POINTS TO CONSIDER:
1. The board game is comprised of puzzle-like pieces (hexagons). You put togetherthe board game each time, shuffling the hexagons, and laying them out in new, unique orders each time. In my opinion, this is great. Every time you play the game, you start out with a new layout. So every time is different and ever-changing. (Imagine playing Monopoly and shuffling around the properties before each game, you never know where anything will land and no one has an advantage going into it!)

2. Similar to Monopoly, you start off with building a settlement, which you can turn into a city, and later a Megalopolis. Only 3 Megalopolis' can be built, however, and this is one competitive/strategic angles of the game.

3. You start off the game with one \\"free\\" settlement, one \\"free\\" city, and two \\"free\\" roads. Later on, you will have to purchase those items with the resources that you earn from your lands where you build your settlements and cities. So, this game is definitely based on strategy. HOWEVER, the game runs off the roll of the die. You never know what numbers will be rolled, and therefore you don't necessarily know if the properties you chose to develop will return any resources.

4. There are \\"expansion packs\\" for the game. The expansion packs add new dimensions to the game with new possibilities and new threats. I don't think they are required for advanced players and I highly recommend starting off with one. I've only tried the Knights expansion pack so far, but I cannot wait to try others!

product_title: Octi
review_headline: Excellent game for spatial and strategic thinking
review_body: As a parent and educator, I highly recommend this game for children and adults. While the game board and pieces are straightforward to understand and use, the strategy possibilities are endless. Unlike checkers, you add prongs to your pieces to determine which direction you can move. You may add up to eight prongs (to fill the octagonal pod), allowing you to move in all directions. Every decision comes with a cost, however. Loading up one pod means that you have more freedom to move around the board, but then that pod is more vulnerable to attack! (Your opponent may capture the pod and all of the prongs in it.) My experience is that kids love this game (I do too!) and that they enjoy the strategy and decision-making that is involved. Octi is like a giant spatial logic puzzle. I like that it is simple to learn how to play, but the more you play the more complex it can get!

product_title: Star Wars Flying Millenium Falcon RC
review_body: Ok, I just got this toy for Christmas and I have to say I love it.  The package says 8 and up.  I'm 38.  I have already played with similar \\"easy to fly\\" RC helicopters so I have experience with toys of this nature.  The trim settings don't \\"reset\\" after each flight.  The plastic may ballasts itself differently so they suggest trimming it out on every flight.  First rule don't fight against its initial rotation.  Mine generally rotates left on take off.  I force it more left until it does a complete 360 and then straighten her out once I have a stable forward moving hover.  I may press the trim button one way or the other but mostly I trim the thing with the left/right stick.  It steers like a cow, but on scale it's actually pretty tight maneuvering.  For the more daring you can have special mods of scotch tape to weight the thing one way or another.  Recharge times are outrageous.  I thought the thing would have a capacitor for power but it is an actual battery that you recharge with other batteries.  It has a sensor on the bottom witch is completely unexplained, but if light is cut off from it, its not going to fly.  I suspect if you are going in for a smooth landing it cuts power to the motors on contact.  I am more annoyed that it won't take off again until I lift or tilt it.  This is not really a difficult toy to fly but the learning curve is really high.  The fact that the blades are inside the styrofoam housing makes it less likely that you will crash on contact with a wall.  Still flying away from this kind of contact is near impossible.  I don't think the real falcon would have so much static cling.  In the end I don't suggest this for a young child.  Experienced RC helicopter flight is not mandatory but that kind of patience is.  I think the 8 and up was a suggestion that an 8year olds would be less likely to stick their fingers in the propellers, not that this microwave generation  would be able to fly it.  Also, indoor only with no fans.

review_headline: Excellent for kids on the autism spectrum

Yet, somehow, even though he had never played with them before, while visiting a new child psychologist's office - he immediately picked them up and began appropriately playing with my husband with them. Very cool. It is great for the visual training if you move around the room and encourage him to hit your sword in different locations - up high, down low, left and right. We have a blast with it and I know it is helping him move those eyes around and learn visual spacing. He has depth perception issues. Another cheap therapy toy!! Whoohoo! The quality is great, too. Just make sure that you use visual pictures or explain verbally if that's appropriate that we ONLY hit other swords and not people or other things. If your child is at the point where he/she can \\"get\\" that - then great. If not, buy them and PRACTICE with him/her - always making it fun even if he/she make mistakes. Never under-estimate your child. I did when thinking about him playing appropriately with these before seeing that, with a little help, he is capable. product_title: Tonka Ricochet RC Vehicle 4 X 4 27MHZ (GRAY)
review_headline: Bet this is on a lot of kid's wishlists this year!
review_body:
My 11 year old nephew who is an R/C afficianado loved this car, and hasn't wanted to stop playing with it (He's set up a big ramp on a dirt hill for to master more tricks with it). Here's the ups and downs of it for us:

The GREAT:
0 According to him, it's just cool. It does things other remote cars don't. Transforming into a monster truck (\\"awesome\\"), flipability (is that a word?)/Double-sided, and it's super fast. Plus, it's really a nice big size for all that speed. (a little bigger than a shoe box)

0 Highly durable: That's the one thing I always worry about w/ these cars - but this one has been put to every test

0 Easy-to-use remote for doing all those tricks.

THE NOT SO GOOD:
0 Battery life and access:
It's great they've made such a good toy that noone wants to stop playing it, but not so good that the longest it can be played is about 1-1/2 hours before it needs to be charged for another four hours. Then you need to grab the philips screwdriver to pull it out for charging.

MY NEPHEWS WISHLIST FOR IT:
As I said, he loves the car. He's been playing with it pretty much whenever it's not charging. But, here were his suggestions:
- Put an extra battery pack in (or sell them somewhere at a reasonable price) so that while he's playing another could be charging. That would at least double playing time to 3 hours.
- And just as a wish, he'd like to see the next version be able to transform to a monster truck whichever side is up - not just from one side.

BOTTOM LINE: A great, unique fun remote control car that I suspect will be on a lot of kid's wishlists later this year, and has lasting playing power in the sense that kids (and adults) want to continue playing with it. Unfortunately, the shorter battery life doesn't make that possible to do for too long at any one time.

product_title: Black Acrylic Contact Juggling Ball - 76mm
review_body:
First off, not all contact juggling balls are the same. I heard stories of acrylic balls being unbalanced and thus making working with the defective ball extremely tough. So I guess it would depend on which seller you purchase the balls from.

This review is of a black 2.95 inch (76 mm) acrylic ball purchased from ROCK RIDGE SALES, INC.

Scratches and tellmarks: This ball was free from any scratches and tellmarks and was received well-wrapped (first in cellophane, then with a plastic ziplock bag, and finally bubble-wrapping around that).

Balance: I rolled the ball several times on a plate of flat glass and the ball did not wobble in the slightest. The balance is perfect.

Weight: Acrylic itself is heavier than most other CJ ball materials (metal excluded), and this ball's weight is as expected for a ball of this size.

Durability: All acrylic balls are susceptible to scratches, marring, and cuts if dropped on a hard surface or banged against a wall. When practicing a new technique, it's best to use a baseball/softball or stageball, or even better, a Sil-X ball. If you wish to practice with the acrylic ball, try to do so over carpeting or on a bed (just make sure the ball won't roll off the bed), and keep low to the ground (eg. practice while kneeling or seated) to reduce the impact of drops.

Overall this ball was received in perfect condition, free of any defects, and performs admirably.

On a side note, this seller also included a two-page instructional sheet with photos explaining how to perform a few rudimentary tricks with the contact juggling ball--which was a thoughtful touch.

product_title: Cardinal Games Liars Dice In Wood Box Retro Game
review_body:
The product comes in a wood box, decorated on all sides with stickers of the Liar's Dice images and opens by sliding the lid over to one side. The contents are 4 plastic brown cups, 20 dice, and a set of instructions. Of the 4 cups 2 are smaller than the others and they fit nicely inside their larger counterparts. The dice come in 5 sets of individually sealed plastic bags that must be ripped open. 1 set of mine actually came in a miniature zip lock, while the rest had to be ripped open. Not sure if they were all supposed to come like that or not. However storing the dice and cups back into the box is quite simple, there isn't any particular layout or placement for anything. All of it can be thrown pell-mell back into the box, but sticking the five dice at the bottom of each cup and placing those cups stacked together really eliminates the need for the zip lock bags or any particular storing placement.

Overall: The durability is average. The box is sturdy and the cups will last a long while, but the dice are already losing their black spots (played at least 70 games in a 3 hour period) and I'm sure everyday wear will cause the box stickers to get pulled or rubbed off.

The game however is insanely fun. As mentioned by another reviewer, the games are fast paced, short and incredibly fun. You can make your own game, by buying plastic cups and dice. So what are you really paying for? A container that looks legit and maybe the instructions. And that's what you will get with this product, a wood container, instructions and depending on how long the stickers last, a legit look.

It also asked me to review its educational value. 5 stars depending on how you look at what it could teach you: How to lie and How to catch people lying.

--EDIT--
::How to Play::
The gameplay is quite simple, each player shakes the dice in their cup and turns the cup upside down so the dice are laying on the surface, but still covered by the cup. The cups are used to shield the rolled dice from the other players. After looking at their own dice, the players then proceed to place \\"bids\\" on how many dice there are, judging only from the amount of dice they have (or don't have. hehe). The player on the right of the bidder can choose to believe the persons bid and go an amount higher, or call them a liar. In the case of calling the person a lair, all the dice that apply are revealed and counted up to see whether or not the person was lying. Depending on the amount of players you have the bids can be quite high, or low and often times its a good idea to remember how many dice are in play so as not to be called a liar.

Example: 4 people playing there are 20 dice in play (first round)
player1- \\"I bid 4 fives\\"
player2- \\"5 fours\\"
player3- \\"7 fours\\"
player4- \\"Liar!\\"
(all fours would be pushed forward into the middle of the table to be counted, if there were 7 or more fours, player3 was telling the truth and player4 would lose a dice, if there were 6 fours or less, then player3 was lying and he would lose a dice. The game would resume (with 19 dice) and would continue until only 1 person had any dice left.

product_title: Squadron Products Tools White Putty Model Kit
review_body: Maybe I am just spoiled with the effectiveness of Milliput superfine putty, or Aves Apoxie sculpt. This squadron product, in my opinion was just not up to par with such a large array of other putty companies out there. Maybe 2-part putties can be a bit messy, but this putty just had too many problems. It dried FAST, I mean, within minutes it was next to useless for molding into place. It dried within half an hour like the tube says, but that is no redeeming factor. It was easier to sand and touch up generally speaking, but I hope if a future buyer does this they are well prepared for the putty to fall out. I found myself, on the verge on completing a very well done project, only to have the putty fall out of the model and make my work look flawed. I think if this product is purchased for a child in the beginning stages of scale model work as a hobby, it would be ideal, but even Testors brand contour putty would probably be a better purchase. Overall, if you want putty for a scale model, buy something else, you would be better off mixing your own putty out of white flour and elmers glue.

product_title: LeapFrog Reading and Writing System
review_headline: OK toy, but terrible customer service
review_body: Thank goodness we gave this as an early present or we would have spent Christmas day fighting with my computer. You need to sync this to your computer to download the audio. We're computer savvy and have other Leapfrog products on the computer, so I didn't think it would be a big deal. Our computer would not read the Tag. Leapfrog's customer support is non-existent -- it took 3 days for me to get an email reply and I waited for over an hour on the phone and never got through to anyone. I finally found the simple fix when I realized Leapfrog had a forum page on their website. All I had to do was plug the Tag into the USB port on the back of the computer -- I had already tried several ports on the front and my Leapster Explorer syncs from those front ports, so it never occured to me that the Tag wouldn't. Anyway, this really simple fix should have been prominently displayed on their support site. From reading the forum a lot of people have this problem.    If that were the only problem I could forgive them, but my Tag just stops working after reading a few words. It drives my sons nuts. Leapfrog wants me to wait 15 days for them to get a replacement out to me?????? And I still can't talk to anyone I just keep getting these canned emails. I can't believe how poorly this company is run. When your dealing with electronics you're going to get problems here and there and that's to be expected, but the Customer Service should be able to quickly handle these issues.    Apparently Leapfrog is just concerned about selling their items, not making sure kids can actually use them.

review_body: I am a Barbie collector and hobbyist, and what we call \\"a kitbasher\\". A kitbasher is someone who takes different Barbie-products to re-essamble them into something they'd like. Often, I take a collector-Barbie with a model muse body (stiff, unposeable) to combine it with something a bit more fun - like the Fashionistas Barbie here.    The fashionistas doll is not perfect, but it's the best one Mattel has come out with in years. The bigger head on the doll is still very unpopular with grown up collectors, but the body is of great value compared to other poseable body fashion dolls, not limited to Barbie. I believe it is due to the body that these dolls are nearly flying off the shelves - especially now that the new \\"pivotal\\" knee was added to some of the dolls. The knee is such a big part of this doll, that I wouldn't buy it blindly online, as you want to know you're getting the new knee - the early dolls were released with a \\"hinge\\" knee, the type found on 90's gym Barbies, but the later releases have a ball joint knee, allowing the knee to turn into more natural poses - also looking prettier.

product_title: Nerf N-Strike Stampede ECS (Discontinued by manufacturer)
review_body: The Nerf Stampede is an incredible blaster. It's not nearly as prohibitively large or unwieldy as the Vulcan, and it's much more fun in competitive Nerf matches as it is more mobile. First, the Pros and Cons.  Pros:  -Fully automatic  -Compatible with all magazines from other blasters  -Handy bipod  -Comes with plenty of darts and the new 18 round stick magazines.  -Rapid fire, compatible with all rail accessories with plenty of room for them.    Cons:  -Heavy  -Noisy  -Eats batteries  -Inaccurate  -Tendency to jam with the 35-dart drum.    The accessories that come with the gun are a mixed bag. The bipod/foregrip is useful because having a solid handle on the front is needed to balance the weight, though I've found that using a bipod with this thing is worthless as it's so inaccurate that you have no reason to stabilize it.  The shield is merely aesthetic. It's flimsy, obscures your vision, weights the gun in a weird way, and doesn't cover any part of you, so it's just made to look cool.  You'll be shooting a lot of darts with this, so using the drums is a must, though the 35-dart drum can't keep up with the feed-rate needed, and sometimes jams, either mis-feeding a dart or double-loading them. You'll definitely notice a crimp in your \\"I'm so awesome spraying darts everywhere\\" style when your barrage stops and you get pelted to next Sunday trying to clear the jam. The 18-round drum is the most effective I'd found.  Needless to say, I can't recommend it enough as a really fun addition to any arsenal, and you will surely be the most unique and coolest person on the block/cubicle farm when you whip this bad boy out. Just be aware that not only does it eat batteries for every meal, it sprays everywhere, so don't even bother aiming.

product_title: LeapFrog Reading and Writing System
review_body:
The age range on this product is 4-8, which is a pretty broad spectrum considering most kids learn to read in kindergarten at age 5 or 6. I recommend it for preschool-aged kids; 3 1/2 - 5 1/2. Once they know how to read, it's kind of useless. I have bought many Leapfrog toys and systems over the years, so I know they offer good products. Since my daughter is almost 7 and has been reading for about a year now, it's mostly for a bit of fun.

As for the Tag pen itself, I wish the pen had a cap to cover the tip. The tip does not retract, so it just seems like it will be easily damaged. The texture of the pen is somewhat textured, but not soft and tactile like if it had a silicone skin, which would have been nice. I think it's sort of slippery but my daughter seems fine with it. The volume control is nice, the fact that you can plug a headset in it is nice. I bought the Leapster headset for my daughter's Leapster earlier this year because it did not take a standard headset, and the same headset works with the Tag. The battery compartment is simple enough it is very similar to the battery compartment closure of the Leapster.

The starter book that comes with this Tag is very basic, just enough to get you interested and get an idea of how much fun your child can have. I did see on Leapfrog.com that there are other products besides books that you can use the Tag with, such as a world atlas or map of the United States, which is really pretty neat. Since my daughter knows how to read already, these types of products are still going to be good learning tools for her, and I would buy them. I see that currently Amazon only has the USA map. There are many Tag reader titles, and I have not bought one. I do know that if you want to buy a Tag book, you have to download software online. Not something I'm really fond of, but if I were trying to get my child to enjoy reading, or learning to read, I might be up for it. You will also have to sign up for an account on Leapfrog.com, which I did when I bought my daughter a Leapster last holiday season, so I am all set there.

The information your child gets from the Tag reader isn't just reading the text in the book. There are games, blended sounds (i.e. wh, th, sh), following directions, just about everything else in addition to reading. And since there are so many titles, there is bound to be a bunch of them that appeal to your child. The books are usually around $10+. The paper stock of the sampler book is very thick, because the point of the Tag is fairly pointy. It almost looks like the lead of a fairly sharp pencil.

product_title: Supersoaker Wars Shotblast  Water Blaster - Red
review_headline: Easy to use, comfortable to hold and aim, good range.
review_body:
The shoulder rest helps make the blaster easy to hold and aim. The pump operation to fire couldn't be simpler -- you pull the pump toward you to stream the water out, push the pump out to repeat. It's easy to fill the blaster with water. The capacity is good for several shots, though you'll find you have to reload often. The range is good, but not great. The velocity of the water isn't as high as I had hoped, but it does spray a good 15 to 20 feet out, if shot at the right angle.

I would actually prefer a more complicated operation, if it could provide more range. In particular I would like the pump to be separate from the trigger, so that I could elect to pump more air pressure into the system to get more range when I pull the trigger.

review_body:

product_title: Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer DVD Game
review_headline: Cute but small ones get bored fast
review_body:
My four year old nephew and I played this Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer game on a chilly and gloomy Saturday afternoon. In order to win the game, you (as Clarice, Rudolph, Santa, or Hermie) have to rescue the misfit toys before Bumble can get to them. The DVD gives you challenges that you have to win in order to get that misfit toy. The mini-games on the DVD include a memory matching game, finishing a song lyric, and a guessing whose voice it is on a sound clip from the movie, along with some other games.

My nephew liked the game for about 10 minutes but then got bored and started to make the characters talk to each other. Older children might like this game and play it all the way through a bit better. As for me, I kind of liked the DVD mini-games that we play in order to get the misfit toys the best. It's a great idea for those who have grown up watching Rudolph on TV every year. So it isn't the best game out there but I'm sure that kids 5 and older would find great enjoyment from it.

product_title: Pirateer Game
review_body:
This is a great game that I strongly encourage everyone who likes games to try.

My boyfriend met the designer of this game back when he was still producing it in his garage, and played and loved the game back then, but lost the game somehow over the years. I bought this edition for him and found I loved it as much as he did, if not more.

Pirateer's a very fun game with clear rules and a simple goal: bring the treasure back to your harbor. It's easy enough for kids to play, but definitely interesting enough for adults. The game plays differently depending on what sorts of strategies the players use, but if you want to shake it up, the instruction booklet also includes a number of \\"variants\\" which can change the game a little or change it drastically. Additionally, if you have more than four players, multiple boards can be put together for a larger game. I've only played with two boards, but I imagine three would work just as well, and four might work too.

It's a great game that's a lot of fun and endlessly variable, so it will never get boring. We play a game or two at least every couple of weeks, and everyone we've taught the game to has had fun. I've bought two copies for myself already!

I highly recommend Pirateer.

product_title: ThinkFun Izzi

Immediately I was drawn to it and knew I had to have it.  It's been years since I've put puzzles together - puzzles kept me busy daily as a child.  This is similar to a puzzle, but yet not. review_body: Bandai's Gundam 00 models are great, high quality, detailed, and fun kits. This is a transforming mobile suit, nicely detailed and sturdy (it can stand in most poses with-out assistance). Now I prefer master grade kits but these new no-grades,and high grade kits in 1/100 or  1/144 scale are great in detail and time it takes to assemble. My 3 year old daughter loves to watch me put one together, she names parts and most of the time she can tell where they go not having seen the anime from which they came. Young kids and adults can enjoy any gundam model, the experience of construction, and painting if one wants to (though is not necessary, detailing with gundam markers, and taymia paints sure so make them look nice)is truly awesome, cause once your done you have an action figure. Back to the kit, Kyrios is spot on for show accuracy, both in mobile armor (plane)mode and as a mobile suit. Excellent range of motion in the joints. I do recommend getting a gundam action base if you want to display it transformed since it has no landing gear. This is a great kit for modelers of any age and experience and if you have never done gundam (gunpla) models before I would recommend this kit along with Exia. This kit should take about 4-7 hours to assemble. It took me 2 but I have been doing this since 1999.  Buy this kit and enjoy.[[ASIN:B0010LAJ3G Gundam 00: 03 GN-003 Gundam Kyrios 1/100 Scale Model Kit]]

product_title: 5 Second Rule
review_headline: Fun game, but you gotta think fast
review_body:
I bought this game recently with a coupon I got for Borders Bookstore. The object is simple - name three things that fit in a specific category in five seconds. Not as easy as it sounds, especially if the category is not your cup of tea. Sample categories are Name Three:

Army Generals
Produce Items
Dairy Products
U. S. astronauts
Deaceased Celebrities
Beach Boys songs
Dr. Seuss books
Things you do alone

The responses someone gave to the last one I can't print here. It can be a challenge. Here's the challenging part. If the first player cannot come up with three answers, it passes to the next player, who CANNOT repeat the answers already said. This could cause problems with categories that have a limit of answers, like Signs of the Zodiac. According to the rules, if the categories gets played by all players and no one gives three acceptable answers, the player who originally got the category gets it by default. One player who just didn't follow the Beach Boys couldn't complete that card, I aced it and got it.

You can play as many rounds as you like. A round is defined as everyone being given a category to start with. Naming three answers gets the card for you and play passes to the next player. I originally thought you kept going, but a call to Patch Products said no. This isn't made too clear in the rules, in my opinion. NOTE: if more than one player misses a category, the next category begins with the next person whose turn it would be after the last player. This may not necessarily be the person who got the card. It may sound strange but once you play the game, it will be clear to you.

The one with the most cards at the end wins. The timer makes a strange noise when it's turned over. You won't be able to hear the noise in a loud environment. When the little balls or marbles reach the bottom, your time is up. Five seconds goes by quickly. I've played this game several times and it's gotten pretty good reviews. This is one of the games that is fun, but not always as easy as it seems.en pretty good reviews. This is one of the games that is fun, but not always as easy as it seems.

review_headline: Best game of the year, but gets old quickly
review_body: This is an excellent math toy for kids. Unfortunately, the game ends up getting formulaic and all of the games end up with a race for 4 or 5 of the cards out there as one strategy generally trumps all others when certain cards are present.  I have only seen two or three games where 1st and 2nd tried a different approach to winning.  After about a hundred plays, I can usually see the \\"right\\" cards after they are dealt out.  I still play because I have yet to see the same combination of decks, so until I reach that point, this will get weekly play.

product_title: Erector Radio Control Tuning Street Racer Set, 368 Pieces
review_body: My wife and I wanted to get our nine year old son a remote control car and an Erector set this past Christmas. My son isn't one to stay put and focused on one thing for very long, but the minute that we opened this and got started he was all in.  He was short on patience at first, but after about thirty minutes or so he really started to take his time and do it right.  He is really excited about taking a whole bunch of little pieces and making something actually work.  The upside to this is that the electric motor/chassis part of this does not need to be assembled, you are basically doing all of the body work.  It's great that he can build it and actually go outside and play with it, and that I doesn't just sit there and do nothing or only move slightly.  He's really getting into cars, and this project is motivating him to get his chores and homework done faster so that we can get to work on his new car.  This is a great buy and would recommend this to anyone over the age of eight.

product_title: Bandai Hobby 1/60 Strike Freedom Gundam "Lighting Edition", Bandai Action Figure
review_body:
I had just gotten back into Gundam models about a half a year ago, and I started with the Perfect Grade Strike Gundam. so when I say that I was overall unsatisfied with the 1/60 Strike Freedom, it may come from a slight bias to the detail of the Perfect Grades. I got the Strike Freedom in the 1/60 form so that it could match up to my other 1/60s on my shelf, but after getting it and getting a feel for the parts, it just doesn't compare to PGs.

The model has only a partial inner frame, where the lighting wires and LEDs go through. there is no detail on this inner frame, but you could probably take the armor off if you wanted. the lighting effect itself is sort of cool, but a big downside is that the light in the head is separate from the rest of the body. the power for the body lights comes from the stand. the pose-ability isn't too bad, the joints feel stiff though and you will be afraid to really wrench on them for fear of ripping out your wiring job.

the wings are pretty huge, and as far as weight goes they weigh about as much as the rest of the model. they also feel pretty chintzy, and one of the circular pieces of the plastic that holds the wings to the backpack actually broke, along with the peg that was supposed to keep it stationary. it was a real pain to get the wing back apart to repair this, so I would suggest gluing it in from the start, for anyone else who builds this model. it's a little gold circular piece that goes in between the 2 pieces of plastic making up each of the 4 wings. if you glue it in it will save you a lot of hassle later. the dragoons do come off, but they're pretty boring by themselves.

the model doesn't have a ton of panel lines, but the dragoons would definitely benefit from some added detail.

overall I can't give this model much more than a 3 star rating, because I didn't feel satisfied after building it, and I am not convinced it was worth the money paid for it. I have since gone out and bought the MG 1/100 Strike Freedom Full Burst Mode, and I look forward to building that. it has much more detail, and it costs less.dom Full Burst Mode, and I look forward to building that. it has much more detail, and it costs less.

product_title: Race For The Galaxy
review_headline: A tough first game, better with time
review_body: Typically when you play a game for the first time: you learn, you play, you lose but you have some fun in the process.  With this game, all is true of the above but the \\"having fun in the process\\" part.      Do yourself a favor.  Don't let an experienced player explain the rules to you, they take for granted you understand what they already know, which you don't, and can't.  Rather, take 30 minutes and actually read the rulebook if you want to enjoy your first game.  Otherwise the symbols on the cards make no sense and you are forced to act without the knowledge to act properly.    Your second and third games will go much smoother, as you learn, and the game will eventually become fun.  This game is not easy for first timers, beginners or casual gamers, but it has excellent replay value.

product_title: Snap Circuits Jr. SC-100
review_body: I've always been very inclined towards science and science related things. In my childhood, I used to do a lot of fun with science but didn't have much access to science toys except magnet so I used to depend upon more naturally available forms of science. When I had a kid, I always thought that I'd give him all the access and though he's just 7 but he asks a lot of science questions and definitely inclined so I got him various science related toys including some of heavenly priced one but he was never so interested in playing with those but he was interested in the end result. When I saw Snap Circuits Jr on Amazon, I immediately fell in love with this but I was apprehensive as it could be another toy in my kid's big toy library without much of use but somehow I thought that it should be my last attempt to get him involved in any tech toy and bought it. I opened the pack once it reached our home and made a sound activated musical bell and showed it to my kid. In my next project, my kid supplied me the stuff and from there on, I couldn't get my hands on it as he already made over 15 projects with that including some of the very complex ones. I'm completely fascinated with the neatly aligned board, diagrammatic representation in the manual, nice finishing of the parts and easy to learn approach. It's highly productive toy and it's so easy to get started with it that it becomes a toy more than a science toys and then you'll be flooded with questions about various terms and outputs which will definitely enhance the knowledge of your kids.  I loved it and I'm sure there's no reason why anyone will not like it. Highly recommended!!

He comes with a lot of accessories that are to be seen in 'Day of the Dead', like: extra arm/hand for holding gun, walkman cassette player, pail/bucket (bloody), used to contain his zombie food (body parts), men's shaver, and a REALLY AWESOME base! The base (as seen in the pics), actually has real metal chains that can attach to Bub, so you can set him up the same way as to what is seen on film.  I've been very good by keeping this bad boy in package like the rest of my Horror goodies for fear that I might knock him over and break him - trust me, it happens (haha).  Anywho, Bub is a fine addition to my zombie figure collection and looks great next to Dr. Tongue (Day of the Dead), and Plaid/Bald zombie (Dawn of the Dead).  For you Horror fans out there, buy him, he's not getting any cheaper!

review_body: It's a cute doll. My daughter liked it for a while but it didn't keep her interest for long. We like it but I think the price is too high for a simple, moving, little doll.

product_title: Playmobil Green Knight with Movable Cannon
review_headline: You Could Put an Eye Out!
review_body:
Well, almost certainly not, but you shouldn't allow your child to test it on a younger sibling! I noticed this item on clearance; a toy cannon that actually fires a cannon ball? In 2010? I knew right then I had to buy it...

for my children. (That's my story, and I'm sticking to it!)

The surprisingly sturdily built cannon works exactly as indicated, flinging a no-sharp-edges cannon ball a good three feet through the air, capable of making mincemeat out of a squad of toy soldiers.

The other pieces included, a knight on horseback and a foot soldier with assorted arms for both, were less spectacular but also well designed and well built. The only caveat I'd offer is that because some of the pieces are VERY tiny I'm a little dubious about the Age Designation of 4+; my 6-year-old was having some difficulty with them while my 8-year-old was fascinated with them.

Note: Carefully check to make sure that your set contains all of the correct parts before turning it over to your children. Mine was missing a critical part that Playmobil USA is mailing to me, but I never would have known my children hadn't lost it if I hadn't checked first.

The ages that these seem more appropriate for (7+) don't seem too interested in keeping up with them, The younger set is too rough on the little things. product_title: WALL-E Reject-Bots Action Figures from the Disney Pixar Movie WALL-E
review_headline: WALL-E Reject Robots Action Figure Set
review_body: As a fan of the movie WALL-E and of robots in general, I'm mostly pleased with this set of four \\"reject robots\\".  You get four figures in this set: GO-4 (Autopilot's minion), PR-T (Beautician Bot), VN-GO (Paint Bot), and HAN-S (Massage Bot). VN-GO and HAN-S have several points of articulation each while PR-T and GO-4 don't have any at all. These four don't seem to be of quite as good a quality as the WALL-E and EVE figures, especially GO-4 and PR-T.    I don't really have any complaints about HAN-S and VN-GO besides a slightly sloppy paint job, but GO-4 and PR-T seem rushed in both sculpt and in paint. GO-4 is painted very light gray when he's supposed to be white, and the interior of his little, red dome hasn't been painted at all.  PR-T is the worst in regards to sculpting and paint: she's too dark a pink, her off-white paint scheme is incorrect, her eye is gray when it's supposed to be sky blue, and her sides/arms haven't been painted at all (her arms are supposed to be off-white while the arm slots are supposed to be dark pink) and the sculpting sis a bit sloppy.  Also, PR-T, VN-GO and HAN-S each have a control cable attachment that is also painted somewhat incorrectly (they're completely red when they're supposed to be red & black with a yellow button). Since I am artistically and technically inclined, I shouldn't have much trouble repainting each robot to be more screen accurate, but that I have to fix GO-4 and PR-T to such a great extent is annoying.    If you're buying these for your little ones, they should be pleased.  If you're buying these as screen accurate representations of the robots from WALL-E, expect a mixed bag of two mostly accurate robots and two that will need some repainting & TLC.

It was sturdy, flat throughout to give an even play, polished wood, a wonderful table item.  No one is making this kind of toy at present.  In my tutoring program, the students have never tired of trying to beat their previous score, but, because it is flimsier, it is a little frustrating for them to \\"try harder\\".  Hopefully, sometime in the future someone will elect to make a $50 labyrinth that is sturdier and more fun to own.

product_title: LeapFrog Leapster Explorer Learning Game System
review_body: Being that we have been a fan of the Leapster 2, we were very excited to be some of the first to try out this new product. At first glance I just couldn't figure out what was so different between the Leapster 2 and the Leapster Explorer, then it arrived in the mail. Once I opened the main [...] box, the excitement grew in our house as my son immediately knew that this was a LeapFrog product! We immediately started playing with this product and I was blown away! The LeapFrog Explorer exceeded my expectations! The first thing that caught my eye before we ever turned the game on, was the size. It is such a friendly size and makes it perfect for little hands to hold. Here is a comparison of the Leapster 2 and the Leapster Explorer:Both are truly amazing products! Just because you may have either the Leapster or the Leapster 2 does not mean you shouldn't consider the Leapster Explorer as well!We recently got back from vacation and this was one product that was played with tons during the 7 hour drive to our location. It is just simple for little ones to use on their own and will keep them busy playing and learning. You can either play using catridge games or by downloading \\"apps\\" into it. My son's favorite game at this moment is Toy Story 3, but when it comes to the \\"app\\", he loves the Harmonies game. The harmony game allows him to conduct four singers while learning about harmonies and musical parts. Also, I want to point out that you can also download e-books from the Tag Library for the LeapFrog Leapster Explorer.The graphics are very fantastic for a child's handheld game on the Leapster Explorer. It uses Flash for great visual performance and a Linux-based operating system. The screen is large , bright , full-color and touch sensitive . It has internal memory of 512 MB and a download capacity of 250 - 300 MB. It has plenty of storage for gaming FUN!

product_title: Banzai   Rain Forest Adventure Pool
review_headline: Another Case of Banzai's Blatantly Misleading Photos...
review_body:
I purchased this pool knowing full well it wasn't going to be the size portrayed on the box. I have purchased enough Banzai products to know they're flat-out lying in their product pictures. This pool was only going to be used for one child though, so I didn't mind it being smaller than it appeared. The 4 children they have on the box is just insane. While my 2 year old son was playing in it, our next door neighbors little girl (whose about 3) came over and they had a great time in it. Anymore than that, and it would have been over-crowded. If you have one or two small children, I think this is a cute pool to beat the heat in, but it's HALF the size they show on the box...just a heads up.

Set up was easy enough. Blow up all the different sections (there's 7), then attach the garden hose to the water tube that sits on the green canopy and makes it 'rain'. I use the term 'rain' loosely though because it hardly does anything that comes close to rain. If you turn the water up too high, all the water pool in the front of the canopy and it starts to sag and fall over, but if there's not enough water pressure, hardly any water comes out. It didn't matter much for us though, as soon as my son saw there was a tube running up the side, he immediately set about yanking it off and playing with it.

Overall, I say 'Eh'. It's not a terrible pool, but there are better one's out there. I keep buying Banzai for a couple reasons: 1.They're sold at our local K-Mart and 2.They're usually pretty cheap (in the store), so if it gets a hole or isn't much fun, no worries cause it didn't cost much. Just know that whether you buy this pool or a different one from Banzai, what you see on the package is NOT what you will be getting...EVER. Always figure it to be about half the size of what they portray.

product_title: Flash Duel
review_headline: Lovely card game; very simple, easy and fast to learn and play; beautiful artwork
review_body: Dave's Sirlin is an expert on multiplayer game balancing and design, and on fighting games, and he was lead designer for the Street Fighter and Puzzle Fighter HD Remixes. However, I became a fan of his work through his writing, including articles about the design process, the writing process, and about the social values games instill through their mechanics. Flash Duel was the first physical card game he published, so I picked it up.    The game is very light and high variance, which means it's simple, but chance (what cards you draw) plays a significant role. Apparently you could think of it as an expansion or upgrade to Reiner Knizia's game En Garde. Sirlin added asymmetric gameplay in the form of different characters with various abilities (like in a fighting game), and a few other twists to make the game move along more quickly. I never played En Garde, personally, but I think I'd find Flash Duel a little boring without the various characters, or if the games weren't so quick, so I can only conclude Sirlin's changes were positive.    The rules are super-simple. The games are fast, though not quite as fast as Sirlin makes it out to be, at least for new players. An individual round takes less than 5 minutes (sometimes less than 1), but a full game could take as much as 15, or maybe 20 if you're both slow.    It can be a very strategic game, but only if you take the time to examine your hand and the discard pile, and think carefully about your moves. I rated it a 3 in educational value specifically because it can teach you (if you let it) to think more carefully before you act, and to consider your opponent's capabilities and likely actions. I feel like that kind of mentality is a life skill.    That said, once you have a more intuitive grasp of the game, it feels a lot like the first few seconds of a fighting video game, where you're both trying to get that \\"First Hit!\\" bonus. It can be tense and a little exciting. It's extremely re-playable.    The iconography and card design is just lovely. The art is excellent as well: fantasy characters with a fighting-game feel, slightly anime-esque. However, the flip-side to this is that two of the female characters are over-sexualized in the typical anime/fighting game fashion; if you're picky about depictions of the female form, or if you're shopping for a young child, you might want to pass on Flash Duel, or buy it and remove those characters.    I have the portable version, which is excellent for the price. The cards that make up the bridge tend to slide on a smooth surface, so put down some cloth (a shirt, table cloth, playmat, whatever) before you play. You can use small coins (or pebbles or figurines, etc.) as pawns for your characters. If packaged pieces and a more stable board are important to you, consider splurging on the fancy Deluxe version.

product_title: EyeClops Mini Projector
review_body:
This will be a mostly technical review. I had the Jakks EyeClops Mini Projector in my shopping cart for a couple weeks before I finally purchased it on Amazon. I bought it when it had gone down to 60% off, I figured, what the heck. It is a very small projector. The actual projector is 3.5\\" x 3.5\\" x 2\\". Yeah, it's that small. It's got composite in (yellow/red/white), a volume control, a headphone jack, a DC in, a focus control, and a single \\"on\\" button. It's resolution is 320x240. It makes a little bit of fan noise when it's on.
This projector is not bright, I don't know the lumens, but it's not bright. If you have a dark room, it'll go 7-8 feet, don't expect more. If it has to compete with ambient light, that number goes down fast. I can lay on my bed and project on the ceiling from my computer, very comfortable for watching videos off hulu, youtube, etc... As I mentioned, resolution is 320x240, to put that in perspective, normal standard def TV is 640x480, so it's \\"half\\". Not horrible, not great. The projector's throw (D/W) is 2. That is, if it is 2ft back from a wall, it'll make a 1ft wide image. The color of an image produced is not completely consistent. 3 of the 4 corners are tinted with the LEDs creating the image. That is, a white projection will look white in the center, a bit red in one corner, blue, and green in two other corners. This effect is evident with images of solid colors, but for normal video playback, it's not that bad, you barely notice it.
It has a standard tripod threaded socket on the bottom, but there is a layer of plastic below the threads, so some tripod mounts may be too short. It comes with a mount, though, that attaches to the huge battery compartment. Sure, you could plug it in, but where's the fun in that? Instead of the 4D batteries it recommends, I use a smaller 4xAA enclosure from Radio Shack that I wired to the correct DC jack. With 4 2500mAh NiMH rechargeable AA batteries I get about two hours of portable use. You should be able to get a cable to go from your iDevice to this projector online for under ten bucks.
This is a small, inexpensive, durable (I dropped it the first day, still works fine, but it is, after all, a projector), and convenient projector that can be powered with batteries with a low resolution and low lumens that is fun for hobbies/projects, novel ways of showing videos and slides, and can probably stand up to kids well (not personally tested). It is not the home entertainment projector you want in your living room : )
Personally, I love mine and am considering getting a 2nd, I mean, how can you not??You should be able to get a cable to go from your iDevice to this projector online for under ten bucks. product_title: KidKraft Outdoor Cottage Clubhouse
review_body:
We recently bought a Kidkraft Playhouse for our 19-month-old boy. It's not the exact same model as this illustrated one, but is very close. If anything ours is a little fancier and has a green roof. In any case, they're all obviously the same basic thing reconfigured to slightly different specifications. We found ours on display at our local warehouse store and it proved to be an impulse item that my wife and I couldn't walk away from. We thought it would be perfect for the baby's summer months.

Ours now sits on one corner of our patio slab and looks rather nice. Having it on the patio saves the need for any kind of floor or foundation and it blends well with it's surroundings. Assembly was fairly easy and took about three hours. All parts were available and fit and we ended up with a small assortment of extra screws and nuts which may come in handy in the future. The house would appear to be sturdy and child resistant, but we'll provide a test for that over the next several years.

Our boy loves the playhouse! he goes in, looks out the windows, plays with his toys on the floor and has a great time. About the only thing he doesn't care for is when we lock him in and use it as a playpen. Recently, he's been throwing his toys out the window and then going out to retrieve them for another throw. Children will be children. He had another friend over and they were both enjoying playing in the house. It looks to be a real fine addition to our backyard.

Gary Peterson

product_title: YAK 55 3D FlightFlex EP ARF 34.5"
review_headline: Nice Idea, but not durable as hoped.
review_body: I bought this with the hopes of having a more durable plane for the beginning stages of learning to fly RC planes, but found that this was even more fragile than the basic foam models I had bought prior.     1) The motor is a geared version of brushed. Requires you to buy a brushed ESC (not as common as Brushless) The gears broke after the third flight. I ordered another gear, but found that the bearings wouldn't come off the old gear, so I ended up just putting on a Brushless motor.    2) The foam is too thin, I found even picking up the plane sometimes would rip the foam. Hang launching it broke the foam, putting in the batteries, motor, servos, also slightly ripped the foam.  Crashing the plane ripped the foam. I ended up taping the whole front area with strapping tape anyway. So the concept of durability just isn't here with this plane.    When it flew the first couple of times, it flew very nicely and I was pleased, but after a 30 minute flying time with friends, it pretty much fell apart and was difficult to put to use again due the type of parts it uses. It now sits in the garage with the other pile of cheap foam wreckages.     I am only buying better quality planes now, that are strong enough to handle a little wind, are stable in flight and allow repairs when needed.

product_title: Magdeburg Hemisphere
review_body:
The \\"Magdeburg Hemisphere\\" allows for the demonstration of the power of a vacuum, as famously performed by Otto Von Guericke in 1654 for the Emperor Ferdinand III. Von Guericke's experiment used much larger hemispheres (20\\" in diameter) and involved 30 horses to show that once the vacuum was established, the two halves were almost impossible to separate. This smaller version works on exactly the same principle and is a great way to introduce the concepts of air pressure to students. Here are my observations:

+ Well Made; these are heavy cast iron with good fittings for the vacuum port
- Needs better Instructions; only basic directions are included and they do not warn about not wiping off the grease

You will need a vacuum pump in addition this to do the experiment. We have a large electric pump, but [[ASIN:B0017YC876 Hand Vacuum Pump; 15mL Per Stroke; With Gauge]] should work just fine. You can get tubing at any auto supply store.

Recommended!

CFH
