product_title: Nerf N-Force Marauder Long Sword - Red
review_body: My five year old son loves swords.  Costume plastic swords, wooden \\"practice\\" katanas, cheap two-dollar Wal-Mart foam swords, Sea-world swords, Star Wars branded light sabers (lighted, and unlighted) any kind.  To say he was an aficionado would be an understatement.    He loves to fight with swords too.  Especially with me.  Sometimes pretty hard.    Now, I've read several great reviews of the Nerf Fury swords, and \\"tested\\" them with my son at the store.  Just couldn't quite bring myself to spend 5 times as much on the Nerf branded foam sword as the two dollar cousin next to it on the shelf.  But when I saw the Nerf Marauder there, I had to buy it (along with one of the lighter Nerf Fury swords.)[[ASIN:B001LRPNBW Nerf N-Force Sword - Shadow Fury Blue]]    We've had a BLAST with them.  They are, as everyone says, QUITE durable.   The big sword is a handful.  Just like a real long-sword, it is heavy, slow, and disastrous when it lands.  The Nerf fury is just like a katana or rapier:  it is fast, light, nimble, and smarts (slashes?) when it strikes.  You can poke with it too.    My son and I have learned a bunch about swordplay.  When you own the Fury, you have to divert or step out of the way of the Maurader...it's so heavy that you just cannot really block it.  To attempt a full block usually means to allow it to power right through, and boy does THAT thunder come down!    On the other hand, if you own the Maurader, you can't just raise it over your head and beat down on the other guy.  He'll step to the side, then smack you twice in the ribs before you can ever recover.  Boy does THAT smart.      We both love that you can FEEL it when you get hit.  There is NO DOUBT about what was a good blow, and what was \\"just a flesh wound.\\"  On the other hand, no bruises have ever been dealt, excepting some heavily bruised egos.    If you love good, safe combat play with a hint of reality, and no squirming out of what really did or did not constitute a good hit, get some Nerf swords and have a go.  Everyone will know who got tagged, and who was unscathed when they watch, because someone will yell \\"Ouch!\\" or \\"Hey!\\"  Or \\"Time Out!\\"      My son has set aside the light sabers, his three year favorites for combat, in favor of the Nerf swords, and I bet you would too!  Just don't get too cocky only because you have the big ol' Nerf Marauder.  We could teach you a thing or two when facing that off against a Nerf Fury.      But you might yelp.

product_title: Stunt Devil Stick
review_headline: Cheap sticks for a cheap price
review_body: I've been using Devil Sticks off and on for about 15 years.  During that time I've owned about 10 different pairs from different makers ranging from entry level flower sticks to professional grade smooth maple sticks.  I recently decided to pick up a new set and liked the design of these sticks.  The vinyl tape wrap and stubby ends making for a nice balance between speed and tricks.  When I first received the item I had some concerns with quality.  The control sticks or handles were simple dowels with a silicon wrap/sleeve on them.  The sleeve was clearly hand cut and the edges were uneven and the sleeve didn't even cover the entire rod.  As for the main stick itself it was really light weight.    After only 2 months of light use the control sticks started to warp slightly. Based on the location of the warp I assumed it was from practice of the basic \\"helicopter\\" spin move. Shortly after the warp I was tossing the main stick in the air and heard a cracking sound as I caught it with my left control rod.  I thought it might be broken but the tape held it together for a few more days.  Eventually the tape failed and the unit cracked in half.  I inspected the main stick and it looked like they used the cheapest wood they could find.  It was either some kind of pine or poplar... not strong enough to stand up to even the lightest amateur use.  Save your money and spend $10-15 more for a Devil stick made from turned maple.  The hard wood will last a lifetime.

product_title: Johnny Lightning Buffy Vampire Slayer Xander's Blue Chevy Convertible
review_headline: The Hardest (and Most Expensive) of the Buffy Die-Cast Vehicles to Find
review_body:
According to an interview given by Jeff Koch brand manager of Johnny Lightning to Hollywood Diecast the Buffy vehicles tanked when originally released to the market. Which is the complete opposite of what they are doing today. Buffy vehicles in their original blister packs are the hardest to find and most expensive when you do (unlike Matchbox most JL collectors leave the vehicles in the blister packs as the packaging supports and enhances the display of the TV/Movie vehicles. This light blue (aqua if you like) Chevy is the rarest and most expensive one of the two Buffy releases to obtain. The blue Xander's Chevy was released in the second Buffy release along with slightly altered versions of Gile's Citroen (less sparkly greyer version), Spike's Desoto (different hubcaps) and the convertible from the spin off show Angel this time with the roof closed. The other vehicle's differences are so subtle that this is the standout different looking car from the initial release of 4 cars which is probably why it so sort after and expensive. Plus I'd be guessing they made a lot less of these than the initial 4 cars.

The Chevy is nothing special if you take it out the packaging. I don't remember the vehicles in the actual show as I wasn't looking at them but I imagine the blue Chevy was never there and that it was the red one in the show. The fact JL collectors keep them inside the blister packs is why blisters with cards with Sarah Michelle Gellar on them are so much more expensive than the ones with the other actors. Although the one's with Alyson Hannigan (Willow) have recently made some ground on the Sarah ones since How I Met Your Mother became a smash hit (and I'd love to see JL do a blister with that show's promo image of them all being squashed against the cab window on the card with obviously a New York taxi inside the blister but that's a whole different thing). Not only can you get the different actors on a collector card inside the blister pack with each vehicle but you can also get them wearing different clothing and with different quotes. The better quotes with Sarah on them are also more expensive than the ones about pep and so forth. When these do come online as loose cars they sell for a fraction of the blister pack prices. Without the pack though, you wouldn't even know they were from Buffy. If you're just into collecting Chevys JL has a lot of other options with better paint jobs and decals. Such as the original Universal Monsters release of the Creature from the Black Lagoon which is the exact same car just painted way better.

product_title: Candy Land The World of Sweets Game (Amazon Exclusive)
review_body:
Yes, CANDYland. CANDY! How did this game survive the anti-sugar movement? Sugar Pops are now labeled \\"Corn Pops\\" and my beloved Sugar Smacks are now just \\"Smacks\\". Yet Hasbro has taken a stand against the spin doctors and refused to alter their game. They know that kids and candy are a force in the universe that cannot be changed. They seek each other out like soul-mates.

My niece was raised totally sugar-free. She was given no candy, not even allowed to look at candy, and started the alphabet song \\" B E F G...\\". However as soon as she could put sentences together she began loudly proclaiming \\"I WANT CANDY\\". \\"Santa, bring me CANDY\\". \\"Is that CANDY you hide up there?\\". She was obsessed with it...it was the eternal flame she sought over all other objects on earth.

When my daughter brought her newborn over to visit, I noticed my niece down on the floor next to his baby carrier, whispering in his ear. I asked her what they were talking about, and she answered \\"He wants some candy\\". I rest my case. Even a two-week-old with zero language skills can find a way to express his inborn addiction to all things sugary sweet. Or maybe my niece thought this tiny creature everyone was cooing over had a better chance of scoring some candy than she did.

So whether it's because Hasbro took a moral stand or just couldn't figure out how to change the title AND packaging without losing their market, I say BRAVO. Bring on the sugar. And by the way, am I the only one who is confused about Splenda? \\"It's not sugar but it's made from sugar\\". What the heck does THAT mean? Were they down in the lab watching Frankenstein while experimenting? \\"Hey, he's not human but he's made from humans. Hmmm....\\".

product_title: Spring & Summer Toys Banzai Wipeout Curve Water Park Inflatable Water Slide Pool
review_body: My eleven year old son and I shopped Amazon for a waterslide last summer and were a bit confused on which one to purchase.  So we decided to read the reviews that people had made.  We were fortunate to have done this.  The waterslide my son picked out that looked the coolest in the pictures turned out to be a dangerous one.  As several reviews of the same product were consistent.  I am praising AMAZON for this method of rating products and I hope this review we are writing helps someone make a good choice. Having said that, the Banzai Wipeout Curve Water Park is an AWESOME slide.  This slide is steep with a 180 degree banked curve that gives the kids a ride.  Add a little soap and look out. Use kids shampoo that is easy on the eyes. The pool at the end of the curve fills up quickly adding a cushion after the bank curve.  The slide has been well used and abused all summer long with no problems.  A small learning curve to storing the slide after a long day.  Difficult to move when wet (heavy and bulky). I quickly learned to turn the water off, turn off the blower and the pool will empty quickly.  After that turn the blower back on and the slide will self dry quickly in the sun.  Then it is a breeze to fold and store. It is also easy to move around when it is blown up.      I HIGHLY RECOMMEND THIS SLIDE, IT IS LARGE ENOUGH FOR ADULTS  :-))))

review_body: We bought one like this for our son last year (or was it 2 yrs. ago?).  He LOVED it and used it all year. (We let him kind of learn the camera on his own, so he didn't even discover that feature until a few months down the road.) SO... fast forward to this year.  My daughter (7) just wants a camera like her brother's.  We weren't going to get one at first, but finally gave in.  My only \\"complaint\\" is that this version is even better!  Now my son doesn't want to use his anymore, he wants to use hers!  ;)  This one saves many more photos on the built-in memory, plus longer videos (a big plus for them).  My only fear is that now my son will want another new camera next Christmas so he can keep ahead of his sister.  Very, very happy with the V-tech cameras.  Never had a problem! product_title: Ertl Big Farm 1:16 Bobcat Skidsteer
review_body: Our two and three-year-old boys love anything that moves.  They fell in love with Bobcats after receiving a product video from a former contractor.  We were delighted to find a life-like version of a Bobcat to indulge this love.  We ordered the toy thinking that its quality would be commensurate with the price.  Unfortunately, we were sorely mistaken.      For nearly $30, we expected a sturdy and hard-working toy.  What we got instead is a poorly-made, flimsy plastic one.  The lift gets stuck and comes out of the slots that allow it to move up and down.  We're constantly having to snap the toy back together.  The range of motion is poor, and the attachments don't fit snuggly. In less than five minutes, the Bobcat wasn't functioning properly.     We want our children to respect the toys we buy for them and try to make wise buying choices. But even careful play with this toy is not enough.  Had we seen the toy in person, we definitely would have made another choice.      If you're contemplating buying this toy, we would discourage you from doing so.  Even with a lower price, this toy isn't a good value.  It doesn't have the staying-power to be used and loved.

product_title: Webkinz Chocolate Lab
review_body: Great seller!!! my webkinz came 2 days before the estimate delivery. Wonderful product line. Company was smart enough to combine a cute cuddly stuffed animal with a computer based virtual world. Buy rooms for your pet, and decorate them. Take care of them, bringing them to the vet when they are ill, feed them when they are hungry, and \\"work\\" at your job or at other skills to earn money to buy items. Arcade and tournament games are often educational and simple to learn, although fun. They remind me of the original atari or cell phone type games. Overall, lots of value for your money. This toy is appropriate for children as young as 5, with adult assistance. Warning for adults: Once your kid has one, they will want all of them (and the first purchase gives your online rights for one year so you'll need another one in a year anyway!), and you might as well buy yourself one now. When the parent who first gave my son one told me this I didn't believe her. Now, my children have an account, as do both my husband and I. They are great, inexpensive fun! I am not, however, a fan of the now extended line that includes clothing for your webkinz, trading cards, and hygeine products-they are expensive and not worth the money. Stick to the pets! The Chocolate Lab is very soft and well made. It looks like a lab and as it is a Webkinz, it comes with the \\"secret\\" code to use on their website. I have purchased these for my nieces and son. (Ages 8-10) They play with the dog and also log on to the Webkinz site  5 of 5 people found the following review helpful.     Each Webkinz contains a code for a community website aimed at children. The nicest thing about this site is that it is the most secure community site that I've ever seen for a child. When they go to the site, they enter the code from the doll, choose a username and password. That's it. No giving email addresses or real names or addresses. The owners of the site really have no idea what the names or addresses of its members are! Just make sure to put the code somewhere where you can find it if they lose their username and/or password, that is the only way to retrieve it again.     Additionally, children cannot--anywhere on the site--input any personal information. They can play with their friends or even strangers, but to talk to other people they must use phrases that are already put into the system. For example, if they want to tell their friend hi while they are playing a game they would click the drop-down menu and choose the appropriate phrase and click on it to send that phrase to their friend, at which point their friend is given a list of appropriate responses!     As if just the plain fact of security wasn't enough, add into it that your kids are learning responsibility, as they have to care for their pet in the online world by taking him/her out for exercise, buying food for their pet, playing and interacting with the pet, and keeping it clothed. They learn about nutrition (health points go way up when the pet eats their veggies, or down when they eat a hamburger or too much candy), and see the results of their food choices (lose too many health points and your pet will need to go see the doctor for a check-up)and other health choices (exercise makes the points go up, not enough sleep makes the points go down).     But wait, there's more! The games are appropriate, engaging, and fun. My six year old gets frustrated on some other sites when a game gets too hard or complex. Here the games are just challenging enough to make your kids try a bit harder, and very addicting with real and engaging characters. The tournaments give you a chance to try your skills against other players, and there are games for every taste. I've even caught her grandfather online playing at 2 in the morning!

product_title: Barbie Dolled up Nails Digital Nail Printer
review_headline: It Does What It Says (Very Well)
review_body: We purchased Barbie Doll'd Up Nails with much hesitancy for our daughters (ages 8 & 7). We thought, No way could this actually deliver what the commercial shows. I am very happy to admit that I was wrong. BIG TIME!    We opened the box and set up time was about the same as with any other HP InkJet printer. It comes with all necessary cables and installation software. Set up time was less than 30 minutes- including reading the instructions.    Once up and running, it took about ten minutes to thoroughly understand and execute the how to properly align the camera and the ink cartridge. (This is the most important part, and should be checked before each use)-NOT each finger, but each day you turn it on and start a session) We have only had to make adjustments one time after the initial setup.    Now, were ready to do the nails. You have to use a nail polish (included) before the printer and a clear coat sealer (also included) after to insure the designs do not rub off. This thing works like any other printer, you pick a design, either one of the 1200+ included or any JPEG image or clipart. You insert a finger, take a picture of the the finger nail with the Doll'd Up Nails, size, rotate, customize color of the image you want to print, then re-insert the finger, set it in the image of the fingernail you see on your computer screen, then hit the print button on the printer.  BAM! You have \\"Doll'd Up Nails\\"!!!!    It's so easy to use, within 10-15 nails printed, my kids had it down better than me. I have not yet turned them loose to use unsupervised, but I believe they could handle it from start to finish.    Believe the claims, it really does what the commercial shows, and it does it well. We couldn't be more pleasantly surprised!

product_title: DC Universe Infinite Heroes The Spectre
review_headline: Pretty simple figure of the modern incarnation of a Golden Age comic hero
review_body: This figure is part of Mattel's 3-3/4\\" scale DC Universe: Infinite Heroes action figure line.  The line brings a variety of characters from the rich history of DC Comics to stores as simple smaller-scale toys.  The figures are the same scale as the popular Star Wars and Marvel Universe action figures, but their simplistic design offers limited posability.    I was interested in this Spectre figure because the Infinite Heroes line encourages buyers to build their own superhero team.  I know next to nothing about the character of the Spectre, but I wanted to diversify my DC collection.  I'd seen the Spectre in pictures from Golden Age comic books (including being seated with the original Justice Society of America) and I liked his old-school costume.  He seems to have a cool 1940s look to him.  Ashen skin with a green hooded cloak, gloves, shorts, and boots.  Very mysterious.    As it turns out, this particular action figure is the recent Crispus Allen version of the character.  I wouldn't know any better, and the costume looks pretty much the same as always, but there's one big difference that is hard to make out in the product images: the figure has a gray goatee.    I don't really mind the facial hair, but the Spectre that I'd seen in pictures was clean-shaven and the beard caught me by surprise.  But it's not a big deal.  The Spectre still makes a nice addition to my modest collection.    This Spectre figure has articulation in the knees, hips, elbows, shoulders, and neck.  The shoulder joints in these DC figures are ball & socket joints, providing the greatest range of motion (and a nice touch).  The hood and cape are one rubbery piece and, I believe, can be removed if you try hard enough.    The figure is made of a durable plastic and should withstand normal playtime action.  The Spectre comes with no accessories, so no small pieces.  The toy should be fun for kids with imaginations and a nice addition for DC Comics fans.

product_title: Imaginarium Motorized Marble Race
review_headline: Grades: B+ for chutes, F for motors
review_body:
Some random observations about this product that may help you make your decision:

On the positive side, once it's set up, it's loads of fun with seemingly infinate replay / rebuild value. The kids (and their Dad) are mesmirized by the marbles tumbling through the nicely varied chutes. My 7-year-old can effectively build her own towers, one of which turned out to be taller than my six-feet. (She had to stand on the coffee table to complete it and get the balls rolling.) Little friends that have come over have all expressed excitement and had fun putting their own marble runs together. There are enough pieces for 2 separate but adequately sized towers to be built simultaneously. This set is much easier to assemble and far more steady than any wooden set I've ever encountered. It's one of the most played-with toys from this Christmas, and that includes a new electronic gaming system.

But, I also have a few gripes for the manufacturer.

1) Initial set-up is a royal pain, especially when you've got an anxious child sitting at your elbow, eager to play. Each of the chain links need snapping together (the process hurt the little lady's fingers), and the instructions are paltry at best. (We did better following the picture on the front of the box.)

2) The motors for the lift system broke within the first 10 minutes of use. Though we didn't \\"abuse\\" them, per se, my daughter did hold up the chain mechanism while attempting to dislodge a stuck marble, and instantly it started running in a jerky fashion, then quit altogether. The lifts can still be turned manually, but it takes all the \\"cool\\" out of it. Way too wimpy for a childrens toy.

3) Inexplicably, some of the pieces are of different lengths (about 1/2\\" shorter than the rest), making towers crooked and wobbly. We haven't figured out a way to utilize them effectively, so by and large, we just leave those pieces out of play. Silly, and it seems like a waste of box space.

In spite of the shortcomings, we still have a lot of fun with this set. Ours just now happens to be powered by gravity only. If you intend to buy a marble run (which I'd highly recommend for the logic building/educational/FUN value), you may want to bypass the motorized version and get something like [[ASIN:B001HZBRO0 Marble Race Deluxe]] or [[ASIN:B0000A1ZF7 Quercetti Super Marble Run Vortis, 224 Pieces]].the shortcomings, we still have a lot of fun with this set. The 360* wheels help a lot, and allow for much more mobility that riders that just go back and forth.  The seat flips up to give him a place to hide things... which leaves me looking for sippy cups!  So happy that I found this before buying one of the other riding toys!

product_title: Red-Eyed Tree Frog Wooden Floor Puzzle
review_body: My nieces love this puzzle. They repeatedly put it together and take it apart.   The pieces are big and can easily be handled by children 2-3 years old. It is colorful and fun.

product_title: Mattel High School Musical 3 Prom Kelsi and Ryan
review_body: This came in plenty of time to give as Christmas gift. My daughter loved it.

product_title: HT-ZS11M - ZOpid Electronic Sudoku with Touch Screen and Back Light
review_body: Price was right; shipment was speedy; but back light would not work so unit worthless; returned for credit which has been received.

product_title: Creativity for Kids Shrink Fun Deluxe
review_headline: Super Great Buy!!!! Just as great as they were 25 years ago!
review_body: I am very impressed with this set. First of all, Shrinky Dinks are just as awesome as I remember them being 25 years ago. Although they are even more fun now, playing with them with your own kids and watching my 3 year old looking through the window of the oven as they begin to shrink. We played with them together for almost 2 hours!!! The kit comes with everything, right down to the hole puncher needed to make the dinks into necklaces etc. Everything is right there. Super great Kid. Worth the money and will provide hours of fun!

product_title: KidKraft Pink Retro Kitchen and Refrigerator
review_body: I also, have been in love with the PBK kitchen forever, but my husband, especially, could not justify the price.  I found this one here on Amazon in November and snagged it on sale and free shipping for my 2 yo dd for Christmas.  It is adorable.  Better than I thought.  Sturdy, and yet, so delicate and pretty!  It did take a while to assemble, it wasn't \\"hard\\" just intricate, I guess.  Would definitely recommend it to anyone with a little girl!

product_title: Playskool Musical Sit N Spin (colors may vary)
review_body: I bought this for my 2 year old niece who is average in height and weight.  She barely fits on it so I'm not sure how they figure it is for use up until five years old.  Either way, she can't spin it.  I had to push her around only to have her fall off every two seconds.  What is the point of a sit n spin that doesn't move?  Garbage.  Nothing like I expected....returning it tomorrow.

product_title: Graduation Silver Balloon Weight
review_body: Very durable was a nice addition to my graduation party. Held up well will use for future parties.

product_title: Guidecraft Train Toy Box
review_body: We ordered this for my son for Christmas to go in his train themed bedroom.  We were able to assemble the pieces in under and hour, but had some problems with knots in the wood.  The safe hinges are great, and it holds a fair amount of toys.  It could have used a second coat of paint in a few spots, and there were three knicks due to poor packaging when being shipped.  We also loved that it is on wheels so our son can push it around.  Overall we are happy with the product because it is cute, but the quality could have been somewhat better.

product_title: Little Tikes Lightning McQueen Race Car Twin Bed
review_body: My 4 year old son is the envy of the neighborhood kids.  All the kids want to sit in his bed.  I would almost consider this a bad thing. One it brings all the kids to my house now and kids I am not sure of how entirely clean they are after being kids, to jump in and out of his bed.  Two now I have more to clean up and feed. I guess this is the over worry and trouble of a parent.  At least my kiddo is having fun.    As for the bed itself.  Stickers, Stickers, Stickers.  Better love Stickers, have a steady hand, and a great eye for placement.  They have an adhesive that once you put on its a pain to remove and replace.  Which we had to do a few times, as we found its hard to get proper placement on CURVED Surfaces.  So your Lightning bolt tail can end up in the wrong crevice and not line up.  luckily I read a review on here saying to: Put Stickers on first.  before assembly.  It seems logical and I found useful as moving the pieces into the position to accomplish proper sticker placement would seem impossible if all in one piece.  Also we have had for a few weeks now and the stickers seem to be curling up on the edges.  Hopefully they will last years, but at this rate we may have to rotate bed positioning so he climbs up on the other side and we will get even wear.    Really Wish they put the stickers on at the Factory.  Do they think we wouldn't want the Stickers on it?  Or am I going to Pimp My Bed?     Luckily my Wife and I tackled this together and I do recommend a second pair of hands as one will have to place and the other will have to apply pressure like wall-papering and flatten out the bubbles and trust me there will be bubbles.    So stickers done.  Assembled bed.  Real cake if you have a power tool even better. **Rar Rar Rar** (Tim Allen - Home Improvement Grunt goes here).  Now cool bed ensues.    My 4 year old went from sleeping next to mommy and daddy to not wanting us in his room, of course after a nighttime book reading, the same night.  He is now a totally independent bed sleeper.  Almost sad as he doesn't even wake up early and make the trek into our room for a few more ZZZZZ's anymore.  He just wakes us up to play back in his room.

product_title: ALEX Toys Rub a Dub Construction Squirters
review_body: I am a little disappointed...The item in the picture is not what I received.  I got a larger looking package and it only comes with 4 squirters.  Mine is missing the green one.  It does come with the storage bag though.  Anyways, I am not sure if it was just mine.  Not really worth sending back.

product_title: TYCO R/C Turbo Street Wheelie Cycle Motorcycle 27 MHz
review_body: I have yet to find a good enough pavement to run this thing. Often rolls over when I tried it on the driveway. Wooden floor is fine.

product_title: Lord Of The Fries
review_body: The game is easy to learn and is very cute. We have been collecting games for a while and we are glad to have this game in our collection. It is diffrent than most games in that it deals with food. My only gripe is the seller . They took 3 times of me emailing them to get a response and that was only after I told them I always leave feedback. I had meant to order this game expediated and hit the wrong button. I wanted to change it from standard shipping. Even tho I wrote them immedately they never responded. then i wrote them to ask another question about when it would ship and they did not respond. Then finally I wrote and reminded them I always leave feedback and they gave me a very quick response that told me very little. The game is wonderful but if you want top know you can be in touch with your seller you might want to try another vendor. To be fair it did get here on time and was new and exactly what we wanted i just hate for my emails to go unanswered. Customer service is important.

product_title: Pull My Finger Fart Finger Pen [Toy]
review_body: Well, this looked like another body part until I painted the fingernail red, then it was really funny.

product_title: VTech Kidizoom Camera - Pink - 2010 Version
review_body: My almost 4 year old loves this camera, and it has so far withstood her abuse very well.  It holds enough pictures that I don't have to worry about her following the cat and taking his picture for 15 minutes straight.  She also loves the games on it, and we haven't had to change the batteries yet (she's only had it two weeks but she's used it alot!)

product_title: Mcdonald's Happy Meal Neopets Yellow Scorchio Plush Doll Toy
review_body: My daughter LOVES neopets. You can't get them from McDonald's anymore. This seller sent the Scorchio promptly, in a cute little box, all wrapped up. It was awesome. The only problem now is I only ordered one, and my daughter wants more!! I will definitely be purchasing more of these very soon, from the same seller. Very recommended.

product_title: Monkey Pod Games Six Puzzle Gift Set
review_body:
I purchased a few sets of these in a brick and mortar, but wanted to add my review here in case it helps others out.

The difficulty spread here is pretty good, from puzzles that should take a few minutes to those that might take you hours to figure out. They're well suited for young adults onward (small pieces, so not ideal for young kids). All the pieces are made well and are quite durable, so no need to worry about wearing them out or damaging them while trying to solve the puzzles.

As others have mentioned, these are very nice puzzles just to look at. They are very, very well made and the quality on them (and the box) is simply excellent. An extremely good value for the money and something you can hang on to for a great number of years. Definitely something you can have fun with on a game night or whenever you just want to exercise your brain a bit. Replay value is pretty good too.

I highly recommend these if you're interested in wood puzzles, or think you might want to try them. There's a good selection of some classics here and it's a great starter set. I've given these as gifts and they were very well received.

product_title: Transformers Movie 2 Voyager - MIXMASTER
review_headline: Mix it up with The Master!
review_body:
Mixmaster is just one of those movie figures that really shows how far transformer toys have come since the fold in half and pull out the legs days of Gen 1. His vehicle mode is just amazing! It features a working cement funnel and some awesome detailing on the rest of the truck including those rockin' purple tinted windows. (Now that takes me back.)

In robot mode he looks so fragile but, he really is quite the durable little guy for all the moving parts that hasbro put into him. This mode really is cool with that back pack missile launcher and crazy scorpion like arms with the pincers and bulky armor plates.

Overall I'll say that Mixmaster is definitely one constructicon that you do not want to miss!

product_title: Rockefeller Center Puzzle
review_body: This puzzle is now part of our holiday tradition.  All ages work together on it and the image that takes shape is a familiar yet whimsical version of NYC all dressed up for the season.  Highly recommend this puzzle - different from most in that the cut out pieces are not standard and fit together in ways that ask you to think outside the box.

product_title: Spy Gear Spy Lazer Chase
review_body: This item is alright, but it is kind of difficult to get it to fire each time you want it to, and the adjusting wrist straps are very irritating to try to loosen.  If the product is too loose on your wrist, when you try to fire it, it doesn't work very well, but if you tighten it down where it needs to be, it is very difficult to get off when you're done.

product_title: Melissa & Doug Wooden Grocery Store and Lemonade Stand - Reversible Awning, 9 Bins, Chalkboards
review_headline: It's good for storage if you have a kitchen and need a place to keep the extra items.
review_body: My daughter received this for Christmas but it works more like a storage at this point. She is 3 and a half.  However, she really had enjoyed the cash register that she also got for Christmas.  I hope she will grow into the store concept in the next year.  It is easy to put together and pretty well built for kids toys these days.  However, it would be nice if Melissa and Doug would not have their toys made in China....which we continue to find out puts toxins in children's toys.  I would pay more if this toy was made in the USA.

product_title: Madagascar Mort the Lemur 12 inch Plush Toy
review_body: Why is this toy not available???    The Penguins of Madagascar is quite a popular cartoon on Nickelodeon but nobody appears to be manufacturing a Mort plush doll at this time. I've talked to several parents and they have noted the same situation whereby the Mort doll is not available anywhere at any price. There are a few marginal knockoffs on eBay, but they don't appear to be terribly accurate representations.

product_title: Snake Eyes Muscle Chest Kids Costume
review_body: I purchased this costume for my six-year-old grandson.  I was quite pleased with the quality; actually I was a little surprised at how well it was made.  I ordered a 7-8 for him and he is a small child anyway for six years of age.  It fit him perfectly, but I don't think it would fit an eight-year-old.  If in doubt, I'd order up a size.  He loves dressing up in it, but right now he loves anything that is GI Joe related.

product_title: Great Eastern Naruto Shippuden Kakashi 8" Plush
review_body: This is a really cool toy...all the kids in my elementary school classes love this (I teach in Japan).    So far plush-version Kakashi has withstood the beating my kids usually give to all my other things, so it was definitely worth the money. It helps that Kakashi also happens to be one of my favorite anime characters of all time.

product_title: Melissa & Doug Beep Beep Cars and Trucks Wooden Jigsaw Puzzle With Storage Tray (24 pcs)
review_body: This is a great puzzle for those kids that have easily mastered puzzles for the three year old set - you know the ones - with barn yard animals or whatever.  It's more challenging and offers great conversation in regards to colors, what each vehicle does, etc...my little guy is two and loves it

product_title: Lego City Camper
review_headline: GREAT WOULD BUY AGAIN AND AGAIN
review_body: This was a Christmas gift for my 3yr old grandson.....So you can tell it was going to get some hard use. It stands up to all the hard play

product_title: Marshmallow Fun Furniture Flip Open Sofa with Play Mat - Fire Truck
review_body: SO CUTE and just perfect for naps and play.  Our one year old son absolutely adores his fire truck couch...and so do we, I really don't know how we ever lived without it.  Only issue is that the material is the type that \\"catches\\" everything flying through the air, i.e. dust, pet hair, so be prepared to wipe it down or vacuum it everyday!  This couch has made our life so much better, before our son would only take a forty five minute nap, (if that!) in his pack and play or crib...now, he naps up to two hours!  Plus, it is super cute and love the roadway..that will be great when he gets a little bigger!

product_title: Bakers Dozen
review_body:
This game must be on every household! It's a very very good game, highly recommended!
And it's also educational!

Made by world famous Reiner Knizia, it's a rethemed version of Poison, where the twist is you must try to score LOW, or HIGH! It's more fun than it sounds.
Also because you are making sums, it provides a great value for teachers, in fact I'm buying a copy for my mom, who is a teacher and will use it with her pupils.

Great game.

product_title: JLX OverDrive - 27 MHz
review_body: 1.) You can't run two cars together on the same frequency as with any RC toy but they only made it with 2 frequencies: 27 or 49mHz so don't think that uor kids can play together or with others that have the same car.  You can't find the 49mHz version in stock.  2.) There is no variable speed control.  It's stopped or full speed all the time.  I was very disappointed with the controller as an experienced RC user.  I returned it before running it so I can't comment on the durability.  I spoke with the distributor and they said Toys R Us bought their entire stock months ago and they don't offer frequency change kits so you're stuck with the frequency you received.

product_title: LeapFrog Learn & Groove8482; Musical Table
review_headline: Fun toy and frustration-free packaging is great.
review_body: We got this for our 6-month old nephew and our 9-month old son.  Both kids are loving it.  There are a lot of buttons, and 2 modes.  I think the kids will learn a lot, and it allows them to stand while they are learning to stand on their own.  My only concern with the product is that the legs could be a little sturdier.  I think once our son gets a little more balance he will be able to pick this toy up and knock it over.  But, other than that, it seems great.    Also, the frustration-free packaging was perfect.  The toy was very easy to put together in a couple of minutes- the legs just snap on.  You only need a screwdriver to put the batteries in.  It takes 3 AA batteries and they are not inluded.

product_title: Playskool Busy Gears
review_body: My 12-month-old received this as a birthday gift and she adores it.  Every time we pull it out, her face lights up.  She is able to take the gears on and off as the machine is moving.  She loves to take all the gears off and put them back on one at a time while the machine is in motion.  She stares at it as the gears turn and I think I see the gears turning in her head!  A really neat toy.

product_title: FurReal Friends Lulu My Cuddlin Kitty Cat
review_body: I purchased this as a Christmas gift for my 6 year old daughter (not from Amazon), and I'm not sure why it cost $40. This thing is far from 'cuddlin.' Overall it just looks cheaply made and put together. The 'fur' of the cat is rough and wiry and the motor is pretty loud. The extent of the cat's movement is raising it's paw to 'lick' itself and an occasional weak 'meow.'    My daughter loves it, and thinks its the greatest thing in the world, which is really all that matters to me. But from a parent's point of view, save the money b/c the price tag is way to hefty for what's in the box.

product_title: Marshmallow Blower- Classic Red & Blue
review_headline: This toy blows..j/k, lots of fun for daughters family
review_body: Actually ordered this for my son in law for Christmas because he is a kid at heart. He and my grandson, 4 1/2 and my dtr have had so much fun with it. When I was visiting today, he kept shooting marshmellows at me, laughing heartily. I am so happy I ordered it. Such a simple toy brought so much joy.  Glad I did it.

product_title: Polly Pocket Polly-Tastic Jumbo Jet Playset
review_body: Waste of money! My daughter did enjoy playing w/ the jet, however I was always having to fix something that broke on it so she could play. Just no worth the money.

product_title: Calico Critters: Townhome
review_headline: Hours and hours of entertainment for my daughter
review_body: While this set is very expensive, it has been well worth it for my daughter. She is 6 years old - which is not too young at all considering how very very tiny the accessories are. It does not come with furniture or critters. Along with hit, she has one family, one set of baby twins, and 3 rooms of furniture. It would be impossible to fit more than 3 rooms of furniture in it. Her neighbor also has this set and they continue to spend the better part of many play dates for almost a year playing with Calico Critters. Idea to try it out: my daughter first received an animal family for her birthday and then I purchased one of the very small homes (a baby windmill nursery). When she invested a lot of time with that, we invested in the townhouse and rooms.

product_title: LEGO Bionicle Tuma
review_body: This was a Christmas gift for my 7 year old son and he loves it. He was able to build it himself with hardly any help from me (which to me makes it somewhat educational because the builder has to follow the instructions). The design is realy good because not only does it look really good (and it's quite large compared to the Bionicles you get in those little tubs) it stands up REALLY easily (the limbs and especially the legs move in sorts of differnt ways and hte feet are very large) which makes it much easier to play with.     If you like the smaller Bionicles you're going to love this one.

product_title: Wits & Wagers
review_headline: Easy to Learn - Fun for Everyone!
review_body: I got Wits and Wagers a year or two back and it's seen a lot of play-time with a wide variety of people. I can say that I have never come across anyone that this game didn't work well with. In a nutshell, it's a trivia game where anyone (even those who aren't good at trivia) can play and have a good time and have a good chance of winning.    The game comes packed with lots of question cards (all of which have numeric-value answers) which virtually no one (in our game-groups anyway) ever knows the answers to. (There's even an expansion that comes with more cards if you ever run out). The questions always have interesting answers and provides a fair bit of educational value to the game. The rest of the game components such as the timer, gameboard, and erasable pens are good-quality as well.    Highly recommended - great for groups of 6 or more players!

product_title: e-flite H2200 Blade Mcx Rtf
review_headline: A real hobby heli, not a junky toy
review_body: I have owned a few of the cheap-o foamy helicopters available at brookstone.  There is no comparison with this machine.    This helicopter is stable, super controllable and replacement parts are available in abundance.    I have an ac charger for the batteries that's available at [...]. I have 3 batteries so never have to wait to fly.      If this is your first real hobby helicopter, you'll be super pleased.  It's easy to fly right off the bat.  It's also easy to break if you aren't careful.  The difference between toys and hobby machines is really in performance, however that sophistication does mean that there are lots of parts that can break with a hard crash. Luckily though, parts are available for any damage. However, repairs are fairly simple and spare parts are very cheap.  There are great videos available from [...] with regards to common, simple repairs.      Once you get to a point where you aren't crashing the helicopter regularly, flying is a joy.  Luckily with this little copter a few flights does it.

product_title: Melissa & Doug Upper & Lower Case Alphabet Letters Wooden Puzzle (52 pcs)
review_body: This is a great puzzle for learning the letters. I have three preschool age kids that all enjoy lifting the letters to look at the picture or my oldest can now place them in the correct spot. I purchased this one over some of the cheaper ones because these puzzle pieces are in the actual shape of the letter- something I think is important while learning the letters. Some of the others have the same whitespace shape all around. Also I like that both upper and lower case letters are next to each other to help with recognition... just somethings to keep in mind while your looking for alphabet puzzles.

product_title: Scientific Explorer Mind Blowing Science Kit
review_headline: A prepatory toy for Ivy League wannabes!
review_body: I gave this gift to my two nieces(their fathers are brothers). The opening of the one I witnessed created great interest - actually her father seemed as much interested in it as she did! It brought them together on the project of trying all the experiments....I felt my job had been done! LOL

product_title: Hot Wheels 1/18 Batmobile (1989 Movie) - B6046 by Rough Trade
review_body: I have not purchased the 1989 Batmobile and at the price of $155.00 I probably never will. Why is this car so expensive when I recently purchased the 1966 Batmobile for $30.00 and the Dark Knight Batmobile for $19.00. This really sucks!

product_title: Sakar I Carly Walkie Talkie
review_body: I was really disappointed in this toy.  I thought it was an actual walkie talkie where the people could talk to each other.  It is NOT, they should change the name from walkie talkie to Morse code because that is what it does and if you do not know what Morse code is or even how to do Morse code [[ASIN:B002Y4UBWM icarly Mobile Walkie Talkies]].  I consider this false advertisement and should be renamed something totally different.

product_title: LEGO Creator Race Rider
review_body: My son(age 8) got this toy for Christmas and Loved it.  He has never really played with Legos before this, but with a little guidance he was able to creat the motorcycle.  I will continue to buy Lego sets like this.

product_title: Learning Curve Thomas and Friends Wooden Railway - Stacking Risers (3 Pieces)
review_body: Thomas the Train has provided hours of entertainment in my home. My son loves to build tracks, I think more than he likes driving one of his many trains on the track.  I would highly recommend it to anyone searching for a durable, educational toy for their child.

product_title: Fisher-Price Diego Animal Panda Rescue Car
review_body: My son loves all the new train cars, including this one, that he received at Christmas.  He likes that his train is so long now. No complaints!

product_title: Diamond Select Toys Star Trek: The Original Series Tricorder
review_headline: Enter the world of Scientific Imagination!
review_body: Back in the 1990s, certain attempts were made at making toys from Star Trek TOS.  They were ok.  I got them, but they always seemed to lack a bit in the credible department.  Then the new movie came out this year, and I came across the communicator and phaser from Diamond Select Toys.  Not only were they replicas, it was like I had just went through the backstage of filming and got the actual props of the TV Show!  My kids are into Star Trek, and since I turned out ok... I have passed on these wonderful toys to them.  There is nothing like the power of imagination!  It inspires the soul and adds a level of excitement to life that video games just can't match!  The tricorder was our latest toy, and oh boy oh boy is this one simply amazing!

product_title: Monster Jam 16" Pinata Party Supplies
review_body: Pardon the pun...this pinata was a big HIT at our son's monster truck birthday party!    The kids loved the look and the fact that the body and each tire hold candy, making the pinata whacking last longer. The pinata is, well, durable. It really took a lot of serious hitting to get it to break open. The bigger kids were able to work out some energy. The smaller kids were a bit frustrated that they couldn't hit it hard enough.    Overall, it was a good buy. One lesson learned though. I'm a first-time parent and my son who is 3 LOVES Grave Digger. I thought this would be fun for his party, but he was a little upset that his friends were breaking his favorite monster truck character. Next time I won't get one that is his absolute favorite!

product_title: iCarly Sam's Remote
review_body: I bought this at the request of my 11 year old daughter for xmas.  She really likes it, although you really can't play with it that long.  My only gripe is I wish it was a lot louder than it is.

product_title: Webkinz Lemon-Lime Gecko
review_headline: Adorable and very fun to play with!
review_body: Very fun to play with both online and offline.  Our kids will play with them for hours around the house.

product_title: Usaopoly Family Guy Trivial Pursuit (Travel Play Edition)
review_body: not for kids this is based on a show for adults would be more fun with a board for sure

product_title: Fisher-Price Laugh & Learn Peek-a-Boo Cuckoo
review_headline: Nice toy for an older baby.
review_body: I got this for my ten month old.  She loves it.  The first thing she noticed was that she could pull open the door to the cuckoo and reveal the bird which starts a song.  She loves the song.  She has recently figured out that she can push the button that holds on the clock hands for more songs and loves that too.  I actually prop this up in the corner of her crib so she'll see it when she wakes up from a nap or in the morning and play with it.  The toy still has room to grow because she hasn't yet discovered that she can spin the sun/moon wheel and that she can turn the key.  She also doesn't know she can open the bird's door by pushing the button on the top of the clock.  I've been very pleased with this.    Bottom line:  Good buy for the price particularly if you can grab it on sale.  Consider it as a crib toy.  Takes up very little room in the crib standing up in a corner and doesn't trigger easily by accident if bumped at night.

product_title: Set of 10 Bills-1792 Kentucky State Bill
review_body: I bought this fake-money for christmas fun cards. All of my friends were loved, and enjoyed.  This is a good for just fun. :D

product_title: Toysmith Busy Zoo Activity Center
review_headline: Some safty concerns about this item
review_body: I purchased this for my daughter's 1st birthday.  She was not standing, yet, so I wanted it to encourage her to stand up and she quickly learned how to stand up.  So we are pretty happy about that.  But I do have some concerns about its safty.  The beads wire goes through wooden \\"gates\\" and my daughter tries to reach for beads through the \\"gates\\". And although, she hasn't gotten her self in trouble, if she holds on to a beads through a gate and if she falls, she can break her arm.  Well, luckly, she stopped reaching for beads that way.  But I'm writing this review just to warn some future shoppers.

product_title: Star Wars Science - Jedi Projector
review_body: I do not know why I expected more from this, but it was one of the worst presents I bought my kids this year. The first one arrived DOA. When we got the replacement, I was surprised at how horrible the quality of the slides were. There are only three slide bars so it is limited on re-play value. It has become a makeshift Bat-Signal as the slides were wrecked after a day of use. Don't buy this, buy a flashlight instead.

product_title: Martian Matter Alien Maker Playset  -  Spaceship
review_body: My 5 year old son LOVES this toy.  After the first few tries, he was able to make them by himself.  I had to buy a plastic bin to store the pieces and parts in, but it was well worth it as he can just grab it and bring it to the kitchen table.  The mess cleans up easily.  The aliens eventually seem to dry out, but the fun part is making them anyway!  Great price on Amazon!!

product_title: Big School Bus: Die Cast Yellow School Bus Large 8.5" Long with Monster Wheels!
review_body: My 4 year old grandson loves this bus!  He loves any kind of cars, trucks etc.  This bus in no exception.

product_title: Great American Puzzle Factory Map Of The World 600 Piece puzzle
review_body: I was looking for a map puzzle that would teach the borders and names of countries.  This map did not do it for me.

product_title: Fisher-Price Laugh & Learn Learning Toolbench
review_headline: Cute idea, but kind of boring
review_body:
This toy is really cute, but failed to live up to expectations.

I find the songs catchy and enjoy them, and my son loves it when I sing along for him. He pulls this off of his shelf and plays with it for a couple of minutes, but he doesn't want to play with it very often and I don't think he'll still be interested in it six months from now.

product_title: Max Factory Vocaloid Supercell Miku Hatsune: World is Mine (Brown Frame) PVC Figure
review_body: I bought this figure in Japan on my last trip. I still have it in the box. I need to find a nice display case for my figures. I was originally looking for another Hatsune Miku figure but they were sold out. The sales person showed this newly released figured and I just had to have it. I totally forgot about the other one I was looking for. Simply stunning.[[ASIN:B0027PA0CO Supercell feat. Miku Hatsune: World is Mine (Brown Frame) PVC Figure]]

product_title: Shanda! Bath Toy Organizer
review_headline: Scared bejiebers out of my 16 month old.
review_body: She wouldnt get into the tub with this thing hanging. Now it sits in the closet.

product_title: Mage Knight Limited Edition Dragon Figure - Venomous Shadow Dragon
review_body: Mage Knight is a clickable miniatures wargame from Wizkids. Unlike other miniatures games, Mage Knight does not require charts and books because the stats for each mini are on the figure itself. Also, as the figure takes damage, you click the base revealing new (and usually lesser) stats.     Mage Knight is the brain child of famed miniatures designer Jordan Weisman. Weisman designed Battle Tech and other FASA games before moving out onto his own. Mage Knight was the first game published by Wizkids; and it is the best in my opinion.     Players build army using a pre-build total that they agree upon. Each figure has a point value. Players then construct their armies to create a formidable fighting force. There are many factions which gives players a lot of flair in deciding how to create their armies.     Each starter box comes with the rules, special ability card, ruler, dice and an assortment of figures. Mage Knight is a collectible game so each starter and booster is different. When buying the 2.0 starter, you will receive Kieran Starsdawn, a limited edition unique. Note: some 2.0 starters have Kieran's brother Gabriel Starsdawn instead. Both are worthy figures.     The rules for Mage Knight are so straight forward you will be baffled by why you ever tried any other miniatures game. Each figure has an attack value, defense value, move value and a damage value. When you attack an enemy unit, you decide which figure will attack and which figure will be the target. Roll two 6-sided dice. Add this to your attack value. If the total is equal to or greater than the target's defense, the target is hit. The target takes damage equal to the attacking figure's damage value. Click the base of the target that many times. Simple!     The special abilities is where Mage Knight really gets interesting. You will want figures with stackable or compatible special abilities to augment your strategies.     All Mage Knight figures come pre-painted and pre-assembled. Thus, you buy a starter and a few boosters and you are ready to play! This is head and shoulders above Warhammer. How much time must you spend painting and sculpting figures if you want to play Warhammer? If you buy Warhammer, then your hobby is painting and sculpting--not wargaming.     Mage Knight is also reasonably priced. For around $[...] you can get a substantial amount of figures and be very competitive.     Mage Knight's larger figures have nice details and great paint jobs too. The Skyguard Griffin, the MK Castles, the other titans--all of them are reasonably priced and have worthy sculpts and paint jobs.     If you are into miniature wargaming or are thinking about starting, Mage Knight is the cheapest, quickest way to get started. I highly recommend it.

product_title: Leapfrog Tag Junior Book: The Backyardigans Opposites
review_body: I own the entire Tag Junior library.  Read my reviews before buying books!  (I wish I had researched before buying them all!)    The reason why this book gets a lower rating than the others I've rated is because sometimes the concept the book is trying to demonstrate is often confusing based on the examples they use.  Here are the \\"opposites\\" they teach in this book:    -Start v. Finish*  -Slow v. Fast*  -Top v. Bottom*  -Over v. Under  -Wet v. Dry  -Inside v. Outside  -Near v. Far*  -Narrow v. Wide  -Last v. First  -Hello v. Goodbye*    Starred are the confusing ones.      Start v. Finish is demonstrated by a map where X marks Start and a finish line marks Finish.  For children who are not familiar with the concept of maps, they won't get it.  Not only that, but the example should be obvious as to which direction they are going in, but start to finish is only joined by a dotted line with a very small arrow at the end at Finish.  Perhaps it should have a dotted line with large arrows on it pointing toward finish.    Slow v. Fast is also confusing because it shows one of the Backyardigans going on a ski slope in regular skis which represents Slow and Pablo on a snowmobile which represents Fast.  The child would have to have a background knowledge of winter sports to be able to know that the snowmobile is motorized and therefore faster, but I live in a place that never gets any snow and my child didn't get what they were demonstrating based on this example.    Top v. Bottom was not clear at all.  This concept is demonstrated by two snowboarding Backyardigans, one supposedly at the top of the mountain and one supposedly at the bottom.  However, neither of them are on the mountain at all.    Near v Far is demonstrated by spaceships -- one is Near to reader, others are \\"Far\\" from the reader close to the moon out in space.  To further confuse things, they included the earth on the page, yet it's not the base for comparison, so the child at first glance will not know whatthe spaceships are near to and far from -- \\"the earth or me?\\"  The way they did this whole concept is confusing because it is the first and only concept that uses the reader as its base for comparison.    And finally, Hello v. Goodbye is confusing because Hello is demonstrated by a handshake and goodbye is demonstrated by a hand wave.  Most people use waving for hello and goodbye, and some people do not shake hands at all and given the germophobia of the 2000s handshaking is becoming a little dated in America.    -----------------------------------------------    I usually like thinking outside the box, but when teaching a concept to toddlers, LeapFrog should be OBVIOUS with it.  I mean, making the concept unclear is like writing a number backwards while teaching counting or writing a letter upside-down while teaching the alphabet.  Overall, I like the idea/theme of the race to teach opposites, but I think they should change this book to make the opposite concept more obvious on some of the pages.

If you are stuck with this toy, pull the cocking handle back and then bop it rather firmly and you might get it to work part of the time.  You could try to taper the back of the darts a bit if you are an adult and can do so safely, but if you change the diameter too much or for too great a length, you will not be able to launch it either.  I returned both units because they are defective in design and will not function as promised.

product_title: RA - A CHALLENGING GAME OF GODS MEN AND THIER MONUMENTS
review_body: This is a bidding game, where you create sets of tiles and score points for those sets of tiles.  Groups of tiles come up for bid, and you compete for them.  The game is brilliantly designed, it has a number of mechanisms working  and they all seem to fit together perfectly.  Because there are many ways to score, the different sets of tiles are not worth the same to each player.  The bidding rounds themselves can either be triggered by \\"Ra\\" tiles which come up randomly, or you can also force a bidding round -- giving you the advantage of being able to bid last (bidding is conducted openly, so the last bidder knows all the previous bids), but forcing you to buy the set up for grabs if nobody else does.  If a set is not bid on, then typically another tile gets added to it, usually increasing the value of the set further, but sometimes making the set worse.  The bidding is great on many levels -- for example, you have may have no interest in set, but if you know for certain that someone else will want it, you might want to force a bidding round, preventing the set from getting even more tiles before it is auctioned off.    There are disaster tiles which come up sometimes, as with the other tiles some of these may be very bad for one player and not hurt another player very much or at all.  There is a tension of trying to estimate when the current \\"epoch\\" of bidding will end -- important because you'd like to use all your four suns (coins) in each round (the winning bid pays the 1 coin they bid) but if you use them up too early, the other players could pick up tons of tiles on the cheap as you are frozen out of the round once you run out of suns (coins).  When you bid, your are also bidding for the sun (coin) that will replace the one you just spent, the replacement sun to be used in the next round -- a very neat mechanism.  The suns all have different values so ties in bidding are impossible.    Scoring also occurs on various levels, some short-term, some long-term.  Itbasically a game of trying to calculate what you need, what is the best way to get it with the limited resources you have, and how to prevent the other players from getting what they want at the moment, or later, by having them use their coins now and run out of money later.  The best player in the long run will be the one who can judge the odds better, and see how the tiles would help (or sometimes hurt) the different players.  Probably one of best medium-light eurogames in existence, rules are more complex than American games but after 2 or 3 plays you will have them down cold.  Games are pretty quick, about 30 minutes.  I have played the game with 2 and 3 players, it's great for both of these, though 3 is slightly better.  5 is the maximum number of players.

product_title: Mage Knight Nexus Booster Pack
review_body: Mage Knight is a clickable miniatures wargame from Wizkids. Unlike other miniatures games, Mage Knight does not require charts and books because the stats for each mini are on the figure itself. Also, as the figure takes damage, you click the base revealing new (and usually lesser) stats.     Mage Knight is the brain child of famed miniatures designer Jordan Weisman. Weisman designed Battle Tech and other FASA games before moving out onto his own. Mage Knight was the first game published by Wizkids; and it is the best in my opinion.     Players build army using a pre-build total that they agree upon. Each figure has a point value. Players then construct their armies to create a formidable fighting force. There are many factions which gives players a lot of flair in deciding how to create their armies.     Each starter box comes with the rules, special ability card, ruler, dice and an assortment of figures. Mage Knight is a collectible game so each starter and booster is different. When buying the 2.0 starter, you will receive Kieran Starsdawn, a limited edition unique. Note: some 2.0 starters have Kieran's brother Gabriel Starsdawn instead. Both are worthy figures.     The rules for Mage Knight are so straight forward you will be baffled by why you ever tried any other miniatures game. Each figure has an attack value, defense value, move value and a damage value. When you attack an enemy unit, you decide which figure will attack and which figure will be the target. Roll two 6-sided dice. Add this to your attack value. If the total is equal to or greater than the target's defense, the target is hit. The target takes damage equal to the attacking figure's damage value. Click the base of the target that many times. Simple!     The special abilities is where Mage Knight really gets interesting. You will want figures with stackable or compatible special abilities to augment your strategies.     All Mage Knight figures come pre-painted and pre-assembled. Thus, you buy a starter and a few boosters and you are ready to play! This is head and shoulders above Warhammer. How much time must you spend painting and sculpting figures if you want to play Warhammer? If you buy Warhammer, then your hobby is painting and sculpting--not wargaming.     Mage Knight is also reasonably priced. For around $100 you can get a substantial amount of figures and be very competitive.     Mage Knight's larger figures have nice details and great paint jobs too. The Skyguard Griffin, the MK Castles, the other titans--all of them are reasonably priced and have worthy sculpts and paint jobs.     If you are into miniature wargaming or are thinking about starting, Mage Knight is the cheapest, quickest way to get started. I highly recommend it.

review_headline: Wonderful addtion to any other quadrilla starter set!  (and shhh.. it's educational too)
review_body: My daughter (age 6) and son (age 3) have played with a quadrilla set in their favorite toy store, every time we've gone to the store to pick out a birthday gift for a friend.  Two years ago she told Santa she wanted a marble run for Christmas and he brought a plastic version as he was worried the quadrilla would be too hard for a 4 year old to set up.  While the plastic version has brought great joy, this was the dream for this year, and when grandma asked what she was dreaming of, I told her about this musical marble run set.      Ok, I goofed.  This should not be your first Quadrilla set, it is supposed to be an expansion kit.  But even so, it has been played with the most of any toy this Christmas.  The blocks and tunnels are easy enough for her to set up, and she loves setting up the nicely tuned sounds bars in different orders so that the marble plays a different tune as she drops it down.  Even my 3 and 1/2 year old can set up a few runs without too much frustration.      So even without any other Quadrilla set, this still worked, although it would be a lot better if it were truly an addition to another set. And we are currently looking to expand.  If money would allow, I bet she would love two of these sets, so she could create an even longer tune.      My only complaint, and the reason I gave 4 stars for durability instead of 5, is that it's one of those toys with a lot of pieces, as all creative building toys are.  Keeping the box I think is key to making sure the pieces all stay together, and although this box is nice and sturdy, it's still cardboard and doesn't have the best compartments for storing all the pieces.  At this price, couldn't that be included?  My husband's power hand tools all come in nice containers with storage for all their parts.  Surely that couldn't be too much to ask.

product_title: FOXY OPENINGS - VOLUME 37 - Morra Gambit Declined
review_headline: Must have for Smith-Morra Gambit Players
review_body: There are plenty of good books and videos out there for the accepted lines of the Smith-Morra Gambit (1. e4 c5 2. d4 cxd4 3. c3), but this is the best reference I've found that covers the lines where black declines to take the gambit pawn with 3. ... dxc3. Since the gambit gets declined roughly half the time, this lack of references is a major problem for SMG players. These lines tend to transpose into lines of the Alapain (2. c3) Sicilian, but because it's usually favorable for black to wait before play cxd4 in that opening, the lines that come from the Smith-Morra Gambit Declined move order are rarely covered in much detail, if at all, in books about the Alapin.    This video isn't a complete reference to all variations that arise from declining the gambit. Rather, it's a repertoire video for white, where IM Martin gives as many of black's options as he can, with his suggestions for how white should play against each of them. The bulk of the video deals with the lines where black declines the gambit with the most common 3. ... Nf6 and 3. ... d5. There's also coverage of 3. ... g6, 3. ... d3, 3. ... e5, and the somewhat silly looking 3. ... Qa5.     Martin's is a fairly entertaining presenter, within the limited context of these types of videos. He gives the watcher enough information to get started playing against all of these lines. The down side of the video format is that it doesn't make as good a reference as a good book. Besides the convenience of being able to look up specific lines easily in a book, there's also more space in a book, so more lines and variations can be easily covered. But given the lack of other references on the declined lines of the SMG, I'd say this video is a must own for anyone who plays the gambit as white, and is probably also good for those looking for the best way to decline the gambit as black.    Just to give a little context to my review, my current USCF rating is around 1750. I was rated around 1500 when I first bought this video and started playing this gambit constantly.

review_body: I'm constantly searching for good bath toys.  Seems they are hard to find.  This toy indeed works; but my son (almost 4 yrs) seems bugged by it and does not want to play with it.  This is a piece of foam held to your wall with a suction cup.  There are three targets.  If you squirt water on the targets, the corresponding monster makes a short noise.  One out of the three monsters makes a very annoying noise.  That particular noise also seems to be louder; though nothing a bit of Scotchtape won't muffle.  My 2.5 year old has not mastered being able to squirt the stream of water directly at the target; and I think this would be a good activity to improve hand/eye coordination - if only my 4 year old would allow it to be played!  Overall, the toy does what it was advertised to do.  However, I think it's pricey because it is just a piece of foam with some basic electronics.  If you're desperate for a new bath toy, this one works.  But for the price, I think you can find something better.

product_title: Tyco R/C Stunt Psycho Vehicle - Green
review_body:
This year for Christmas, we wanted our 4 year old to have an RC car that would stand up to abuse and was easy to use. After about 20 munutes with the controls, he got the hang of it. The car seems durable and although it's prone to scratches from the concrete, it can handle a lot of abuse.

The wheels make it perfect to run through grass, dirt, and on the street. When you get good with the controls, doing 360 spins on its back wheels is a ton of fun.

The best part is that even when you flip the car, usually you can get it turned back over just using the remote without having to run over to it and pick it up.

I highly recommend buying a 9.6V Rechargeable battery for it. It lasted a long time and seems to give it much more power! (Like other reviews, the battery cover for the remote is very loose, just use a piece of tape and you'll be fine.)

product_title: Ty Beanie Baby Boots Dora's Monkey
review_headline: I love my Boots, my Boots and me...
review_body:
I'm breaking out of my comfort zone here (I usually ONLY review books, movies and music) to review a toy I recently purchased for my daughter (this is the fourth of potentially 5 reviews). My daughter (who is 2) is IN LOVE with Dora and Diego. She already has a few Dora dolls (not to mention a bedspread) but I just couldn't resist these little Ty dolls.

I actually really like the size. She can stuff all five of her dolls in her Dora Backpack and take them around the house with her. She loves to take Boots to bed with her (I don't advise young ones sleeping with Dora or Diego, beings that their hair is a bit of a choking hazard). My daughter already had a Boots doll that we got her when she saw `Dora Live', but the doll is about twice the size of this little Ty doll and is much harder. This Boots is a much softer and thus more lovable version of Boots, so I'm happy with it and she is too.

Yes, I gave it only four stars on durability since the ware and tear of a toddler can do some damage. Boots already is separating at the seams on his legs, so I had to get onto my little one for pulling at his legs. No, his legs are not falling off, but I can tell that they are getting weak. So, just watch your little ones to make sure they don't `love these little guys to death'.

If your kids love Dora (and especially that lovable little monkey, Boots) you can rest easy knowing that they will LOVE these dolls as well!

And a note to parents, these toys are NOT educational; but the show is VERY much so (my kids speaks Spanish! Like, OMG, I don't speak a word and she converses with me in Spanish at TWO YEARS OLD!!!).

product_title: Press Your Luck DVD
review_headline: The whammies are out to get you
review_body: I got this game a couple of years ago. The game board resembles the Peter Tomarken version but has Todd Newton of Whammy hosting here. The game allows up to four people, a minimum of two is required. Players alternate being the first to answer a question to earn spins at the Whammy board. That's where the flaws are.    First off the game has THREE rounds, not two. This means you have to avoid getting four Whammies in three rounds, which is next to impossible. The first two times my friend and I played this, we both \\"Whammied out\\" and won nothing. This is anticlimatic and frustrating. You really don't have any control over where you stop on the Whammy board, the pictures showing and prizes you win don't match. It's like random spinning and hoping you don't get a whammy.    Also, when it's your turn, the game will show your score, but not your opponent's, so you have to remember that or write it down. The final downside is that you can only pass spins ONCE in each round. It's possible to win in this game, but it's very difficult to do so.    Todd goes a good job of hosting and there's a lot of questions to avoid repeats. This game has recently come down in price to about ten bucks. The board is recreated well, but this game has its flaws, so beware.

product_title: Vision Peak Ultra AC/DC Charger
review_headline: Works well with my 4600 7 cell NiMH
review_body: So far I'm digging it. At 4 amps the 4600 7 cells top off in about 50 min. The fan is a bit noisy so I have to leave it in the garage. I have compared the voltage reading on the charger to a separate DVM (no load) and found the charger is displaying about a half a volt higher than the battery is truly at. It's not a big deal as long as it is consistent. The biggest plus is the real time voltage reading vs. the peak voltage during the charge. You can get an idea of your batteries health, about how long it will take to finish charging, and how well it has charged rather than trusting a blinking light.     Pros: Real time voltage / peak charge voltage. It will charge Lipo's for when I upgrade. Runs cool.   Con's: Noisy fan, not so trustworthy voltage readings.

Anyways, I just wanted to post a few things I noticed about the model that I would have liked to know earlier:    The body is actually curved in jet mode.  It's not just camera distortion. The \\"belt\\" that helps Jetfire combine with OP doesn't have a manufactured location to fit into.  In jet mode, the legs hold it against the belly, but in robot form, the clasps hang behind him unless you get creative.      Last thoughts:    Jet form is very impressive, from the top.  I just wish it wasn't so curved.  A ton of other reviewers have talked about the poor design on the bottom of the plane.  Leader class OP is very well done, I would pick him up before looking at Jetfire.  I haven't bought any of the other LC models, so I cannot compare them with this one.

product_title: Hot Toys' The Dark Knight: 1:6 Scale Bank Robber The Joker, Movie Masterpiece
review_headline: After a Little Work, Simply Stunning
review_body: If you have read my reviews of the other figures in Hot Toys' TDK line, you know that I think they are some of the finest movie licensed products ever released.  This figure, after a bit of work out of the box, fits the bill as well.    Much was made when the first Joker was released, and while it was simply stunning in its execution and attention to detail, perhaps the biggest factor in any Joker figure--Heath Ledger's likeness in the film--wasn't quite present. The headsculpt, while exquisite in its own right, wasn't pulled off the screen like the other figure's headsculpts were.  So HT went back to work and remedied the situation by giving us a new character and the best headsculpt available on the market.    Out of the box, the figure is quite underwhelming.  The new headsculpt aside, the suit was a bit wrinkled, the undershirt not straight, and the figure looks quite plain.  After about 20 minutes of straightening up and changing out the left hand (the peg stayed in the body this time!!) the figure started coming together.  Ever since I saw the promo pics of the figure, I knew I wanted the stance that depicted for the product on this page.  Once he was there, I had to step back and say \\"wow.\\"    Unlike the regular Joker, this figure is able to \\"hunch\\" a bit better to match what we saw on the screen.  The mask fits perfectly on the additional headsculpt and the additional glove holds it tightly as well.  Again as in the other HT reviews, I don't think the figure would stand on its own forever, so I utilized the handy included stand.    So what do you get for almost $200?  A great figure, the best headsculpt available, an alternate headsculpt, the bank robbery mask, two extra hands, jokerized $1 bills, jokerized playing cards, a glock with extended clip, a machine gun used during the Batpod scenes, and incredible duffle bag, four grenades, three smoke grenades, and a foam punchout to keep the grandes separated in the bag.      While not as detailed (for obvious reasons) as the original Joker, this version is certainly worth the investment, especially if you have the regular joker and want to change the headsculpts.  In the end, it becomes a stunning addition to your collection that will have onlookers in awe.  It definitley looks like Heath stepped off the screen and into a display case.  Check out my pics to see what I mean ;)
