product_title: Beck International Beck Children's Wooden Train Set Table
review_body: I read all the negative reviews of the packaging, but decided to risk ordering it anyway.    The reviews are spot on.  The packaging for this item is awful - it's probably the most poorly packaged item I've ever received.    The cardboard is too thin to hold materials of this weight.  A few thin sheets of styrofoam aren't enough to keep the contents of the box from shifting it around.  Two corners of the box were torn wide open, and most of the hardware (which was not even in the small provided ziplock bag) had been lost in transit.    The wood pieces themselves were intact, but I now have no way of putting the table together without the missing pieces, and my son's birthday is in 4 days.    I called Amazon's customer service, and their solution is to ship me out another table.  I'd prefer that they just ship out a bag of assembly hardware, but they're not able to do that.  So now I wait for another table and have to deal with sending this one back.    The table itself appears to be of nice, sturdy quality, so my beef is mostly with the packaging - which deserves zero stars.

product_title: Maxim Wooden Train Set, 145-Pieces
review_headline: You get what you pay for
review_body: This is a fine toy; my kids of different ages enjoy playing with it. However, I wonder if this is the best option for a wooden railroad. If you can afford a more expensive brand, perhaps with fewer pieces, get it instead. The track pieces are plain wood, not covered by any stain. One of pieces of the track broke already when the kids tried to disconnect them. The painted pieces get dented very easily. Of the 145 pieces quite a few are stand-alone pieces and are not part of the track or the trains (road signs, animals, etc). The provided layout seems to be missing one support, judging both from trying to make it stable and from comparing the photo of the completed set on the box and the layout. The kids still enjoy it, but I am a bit disappointed with the whole value.

product_title: Fisher-Price Little People Airport Playset - Red
review_body: My grandson and my son was very pleased with this item.  It is played with constantly.

product_title: Star Trek Collector Series Lt. Commander Montgomery Scott 9 Inch Action Figure
review_body: This figure is well done w/ real clothing fabric. It's nicely articulated with accessories and a base stand for displaying purposes. The box itself sure is collector friendly. It has a large window that provides good viewing of the product and basic character information which is Commander Montgomery Scott from the original Star Trek series. This was made by Playmates Inc. back in the 90's. Would be ideal for display in/out of box and a good conversational piece.

product_title: Classic Alien 18-Inch Action Figure
review_headline: A Must Have For Any Fan Of Giger's Alien
review_body: This is truly an amazing figure. The sculpting is virtually flawless and the detailing is mind-numbing in accuracy. There isn't much paint (understandably so) but the parts that are painted are done so very well (especially the teeth, gums and nails). The paint on it's head, underneath the clear shell, could have been a bit more detailed, but no big deal. Also, I wish said shell was more opaque or hazy, but it's okay. I was shocked this behemoth could stand on it's own without a base, but I did experience a problem after a couple of weeks... It eventually fell off my dresser and now it can't stand on it's own. I have him leaning against the wall now, but it still appears to be standing on it's own. Also the joints in it's right hip & thigh (where all the weight is coming down) got so loose, that I had to super glue them to keep them from buckling. If you're in the market for an Alien fig., don't waste your time with any of those other figs. based on the crappy designs that came after Alien, or even Aliens (great decision to remove the clear shell from the heads of Winston's Aliens, James Cameron... >_>). This classic Giger Alien (or it's smaller version) is DEFINITELY the one to get!

review_body: My 6 months old had fun with this toy for the first two to three weeks. Once the batteries start to weaken, the \\"noise\\" of the motor tends to exceed the music which makes it annoying to the child as well as parents. It was dead in three weeks and the fault was not with the batteries. I should mention that we bought a lot of Vtech toys and this was the only one that disappointed us. Not recommended.

product_title: Dutch Blitz
review_headline: Good fun for families and friends
review_body: This game is precisely the game of Nertz, just branded with a Pennsylvania Dutch theme. It's convenient because all 4 decks are right there for you, easy to keep together, and hard to mistake for anything else.     The game itself is fun to play -- we've played with adults, who dig in and concentrate and find good strategies, and we've played with kids, who just enjoy the basics of the game.    I find myself wishing they'd done more to create Pennsylvania Dutch charm. The colors are right-out-of-the-box primaries (rather than a richer color scheme that would remind the eye of folk art), and the artwork on the backs of the cards is a missed opportunity. I'd love to see an edition of the game that makes use of the quiltlike American folk patterns that show up on the packaging.... But these are all just minor things that others may not even care about.    The instructions are well-written and easy to follow, and any question you have can pretty easily be answered on the instruction page, something that's sadly rare in games like this.     It's perfect for parties, vacations, family game night, or rainy afternoons. Colorful, fast-paced, and highly recommended.

review_body: When you first take the package out of the box, it appears as though the cling portion of the sticker is black. Don't panic.  It's clear.  Make sure your window is completely clean. The ball is NOT an actual baseball but from a distance it looks realistic enought.  My only concern is that a mischievous individual could simply peel off the sticker and walk away.

product_title: Transformers  Ultimate Bumblebee
review_body: Regrettably perhaps, I have both versions of this toy.  I would like to see different Ultimate toys (most notably Optimus Prime) in the future.  This seems like the next-generation of transformers in many ways, with the animatronics and the audio content.  But aside from that, purely as a transformer, it's still quite worthy to own.  Large, very realistic, good detail. Not so easy to transform, especially as some of the connections need some carefully-applied force to engage/disengage (a knife can be useful).  But not bad once you do it a couple times.  The instructions are much better than nothing, and half the satisfaction is figuring out for yourself how to get from one step to the next.     The car mode is fun, and of course you can spin the one wheel to keep the audio going if you want to pass on rolling it around, but the skids are easier with the latter approach.  Robot mode, as noted in another review, seems to fail full expectations.  Yes, I have the same problem with mine as mentioned - it seems unresponsive to sound or motion, and shuts down after 30 seconds or so if no button is pressed.  Interestingly, I don't have the same issue with the first model.  If I stand them facing each other and set them off, the earlier model will respond and continue interaction while the newer one obliviously quits unless prodded.   Did they leave this feature out on the newer one?      As for the content, both models reflect their respective movie roles.  I happen to like the earlier one better, but it's a matter of taste.  The doors fit better on the newer one, and the mask is cool but a hassle to get on.  The Ultimate Bumblebee is a worthy addition to a collection, and many won't care if the thing won't respond unless you push a button.  The new technology takes the transformer into a more pure \\"toy\\" mode, where it doesn't perhaps stand out from the non-transforming competition.  But it certainly opens a new dimension for the many-faceted transformers.    If you care about the responsiveness issue, might prefer a more musical, less serious audio content, and can tolerate some possible door issues, you might consider spending a few extra bucks and get the earlier model.

review_body: Cute and affordable tea set.  Plastic so it doesn't break or chip!  Color changing which adds to toddlers creativity and imagination!  Durable which makes you feel good about your purchase in this economy.  My daughter loves it.  She plays with it daily and requires water each time! product_title: Kid Galaxy Hydro Racer Barracuda Boat
review_headline: I know a boat gets wet but....
review_body: the water should stay on the outside and not in the battery compartment. The battery compartment was full of water at the end of the day when we went to take the batteries out and corrosion had already started. product_title: Playskool Step Start Walk 'n Ride
review_headline: Functional from beginning walker to toddler age.
review_body: We received this toy as a gift just when my son was just about the right age.  As he was starting to learn how to walk, he took to the toy eagerly.  He enjoyed putting things in the small storage compartment, spinning the flap-spinner, and shifting the 'gear lever'.  In our apartment, which has berber carpet, he walked behind it without any slippage or imbalance of the toy.  At Grampa's/Grandma's, where the floor is bare wood, the wheels did slip, and he did fall a few times.    Now my son is well into his toddlerhood, and he still plays with it with regularity.  In ride-on mode, he now adds his imagination and says that he's driving a race-car or even a truck.   It seems like the toy has had a good life, and I do not yet see the time when we'd give it away.    The toy is light, which makes it easy to carry (if the need arises).  It may seem that its light weight would mean that it's flimsy, but it has survived one year of good use with no breakage. This may be because of its simple design. In walker mode, the toy does not flex -- it seems sturdy.  Conversion between walker and ride-on is easy, but be sure to listen for the 'click' of the lock.      I recommend this toy if you have carpeted areas to use it on.  It's also OK on pavement, but I advise adult supervision.  I believe (but without proof) that this toy does encourage walking and did help my son learn to walk while having fun.  (I'm sure that there are plenty of other factors.  But it helps.)      My only irritation with this toy is the color.  Ugh.

review_body:

product_title: Takara Japanese Beyblade Wyborg A-36
review_body: Sadly, there are many out there who do not understand the wonder that are beyblades. First off, in order for you to have much fun, you need two beyblades and an arena. The arena is not that bad, just buy from other places than their website. Also, it's best if you have two people, though not needed.  The point behind beyblades is to launch your tops into an arena (or any other fenced off area or sink bowl) and try to be the last beyblade spinning. These beyblades do not come pre assembled, but that's half the fun of it. Customizing the beyblades with other parts from other beyblades. The instructions are simple, just look at the pictures. But if you really need help, I sudgest buying the american hasbro brand beyblades. The pictures make it quite easy to assemble your own beyblade. Though, assembling the spin gear can be a pain SOMETIMES.  Anyway, now about this particular beyblade. Wyborg is an attack type, meaning it does not focus on spinning for long periods of time to beat your opponent, and it does not just sit there and take hits like a defense type. Defense types take hits but don't get hurt as much, making the other blade the one that gets hurt more. Wyborg and other attack types zoom around the arena or playing field knocking the opponents as hard as humanly possible to knock them out of the ring or knock their spins out. Great for aggressive attackers.  I only have one complaint about Wyborg. It is so strong and so durable, that it is one of the few blades that I have that has actually broken another one. This means that this blade is beast, but don't be surprised if a slightly older beyblade is knocked silly and broken a little bit by this attacker!  All in all, a great beyblade.

product_title: LeapFrog My Pal Violet
review_headline: Lots of Potential with Online Customization
review_body: My year old son got this for his birthday and although he loves it and it is a neat toy, it really could have been technically executed a little better. I am hoping they send out updates via the USB cord to make his speech a little bit smoother and that they enhance the variety of \\"elevator\\" music available    The USB cable that comes with Scout is incredibly short and I would recommend a second mini USB cable if you do not already have one for another computer peripheral. The customization process was straight forward and we had him done quickly. My only complaint is that you have to create a user account and the Internet is required but that's a minor compliant since Scout ships able to be interactive without being customized. Additionally, Scout has volume control on his battery box and is not obnoxiously loud even on his highest volume    Scout is very, very soft and even with the battery box in his trunk, the puppy's body is soft and cuddly. My son spends a lot of his play time with Scout hugging him and petting him.     Scout has three main features - Play games, Sing Songs, and Night Songs (the fourth paw is on and off):   - The Play Games paw just chatters with your child. Asking him what his favorite color, animal and food is - Scout and Baby have the same ones after you program them. Scout also makes animal noises, talks about feelings \\"I feel happy, show me your biggest smile!\\" and engages your child in direct dialog.     - The songs Scout sings are cute and the choices you make when customizing show up in the songs he sings. Poor technical integration is shown when any of the customized items appear in the songs - Scout sounds like he has a speech problem because the tamper and inflection of the customized objects does not match the song being sung. Also, the only music you can customize in this section is elevator music. I would like to see songs with words, more known children's songs (very surprised not to see \\"Baby Beluga\\") or the ability to add yourown music to Scout.   - The Night Songs paw is pretty cool. You click it once and it does 2 mins of the \\"night\\" music you choose when customizing continuously. Press it again, you get 5; once more and you get 10. Although our guy doesn't have problems sleeping, it might be a nice touch if your little one has some problems sleeping or being alone in the quiet.     All in all, our only real concern is that Scout might be the first toy he has worthy of being \\"that\\" toy he can't live without! We have a competitors talking puppy that drives us up the wall (\\"TUMMY!\\").     If you are looking for a chatty puppy - Get Scout or Violet.

product_title: 01202 Amtrak Acela Set HO
review_headline: ACELA. The next step in railroad history.
review_body: A train set of this type is more than a toy to me. I belong to a modular model railroad club that doesn't have a home. Instead, we set up and operate at train shows and provide entertainment for the visitors. My goal is to create \\"trains of history\\", run them periodically on the module/layout, and have information sheets with facts about the consist. Some consists will be military and/or circus themed; historical steam locos: DeWitt Clinton, John Bull, Hudsons, etc. etc.; trolleys and electrics; to name just a few. A product such as Spectrum's ACELA will surely add to my historical stable while educating young and old alike by using the railroad as the central theme.

review_body: The chair is beautiful, but was difficult to put together. The holes are a little off, and some of the angles weren't exactly right, but in the end, we were able to get it together, unlike the first chair we recieved. However, customer service was awesome and sent us the second chair right away, with no problems, so I would definitely do business with them again.

product_title: Melissa & Doug Wooden Shape Sorting Clock Educational Toy
review_headline: First "Miss" for us of a Melissa and Doug toy
review_body: First off, we are incredibly big fans of Melissa and Doug toys.  Many of their great products have found a home in our house for years.  We had very high hopes for this clock, and perhaps it is partly our fault for waiting until our son was almost 4 to introduce it to him.  We truly wanted this as a teaching time toy, as he already knows his numbers and shapes.  We had two problems, first, the hands do not stay in the clock face.  I'm not sure if this is a universal design or if it's a fluke on ours.  Also, when I try and hold the clock face vertical or almost vertical for demonstrating to our son, all the puzzle numbers fall out easily.  Little things, but those are the issues my family had.  As such, it became just a puzzle of sorts, which lost my son's attention after about 1 minute.

product_title: Ideal School Supply Tactile Letters Kit
review_body: There tactile letters were exactly what I was looking for. Great for those that do a version of Montessori at home. They fit the bill and are at least $10 cheaper than what you can find elsewhere. Also, I rarely see packs with both the upper and lower case letters. A great value and a fun way to practice pre-writing skills with young children.

product_title: John Deere Sit 'N Scoot Activity Tractor
review_body: This is a great durable toy with push and ride features for a toddler.  The animals have authentic sounds and the Old McDonald theme fires up whenever the right button is pushed.  This thing is SO much fun I even let my little grandson use it (when I'm all done with it, of course). Looks like it could last for generations.

product_title: Fisher-Price Elmo Live
review_headline: Fun even for a big kid
review_body: Have always been infatuated with electronics, especially robots, but have consistently been disappointed with a number of the robotic toys that simply fail to impress...however Elmo Live is fun even for the biggest of kids! live like, funny and innovative the only bummer is that it only has a set amount of stories.

product_title: Pet Story
review_body: This was just a great \\"craft\\" project for my nine-year-old daughter.  She was able to complete it with very little assistance.  She chose to do the on-line version.  With this approach, you can add photos, text, and graphics via an on-line interface.  The drawback is that you cannot include hand-drawings unless you scan them.  Not a big deal for us.  The best part was getting the book back from the publisher.  This is included in the price of the initial product as long as you don't exceed the standard number of pages.  The book was just great!  My daughter was beaming when she opened the package and saw the book.  It was very professionally done, making it hard to distinguish from a \\"real\\" published book.  Some reviews of \\"Illustory\\" have lamented the limited number of pages included, but this was not a real limitation for us.  We felt that 15 pages were plenty for the simple book we planned.  I am not really sure what the difference is between \\"Illustory\\" and \\"Pet Story\\".  I'm sure you could write a pet book using the former and a normal book using the latter.  There do appear to be slight differences in number of pages included, so just compare the two products if you're considering them.  Overall, a great way for my daughter to be creative and get an awesome keepsake in the process!

product_title: Shape Sorting Clock
review_body: This clock helped with numbers, shapes, colors, telling time and is very durable. I like that its not made from plastic but from wood. Very durable and both of my kids love it!

product_title: Disney Bolt Movie 30 Inch Deluxe Jumbo Plush Figure Bolt
review_headline: Bolt plush is cute and cuddly
review_body: This is perhaps one of the best plush toys that Disney's made in quite some time.  It's quite cute in person and bigger than you'd think. It's also very, very soft, and is quite well made -- nothing's going to pop or tear on this plush.  The eyes and bolt marking are done in embroidery which is also a nice touch.  All in all, it's all you'd expect in a plush, and well made at that.

product_title: Harry Potter Sorting Hat Plush by NECA
review_headline: CAREFUL!!! Do you want a HAT or a TOY?
review_body: I purchased this item under the impression that it was a hat that a person could wear on their head.  I was quite wrong.  It is a puppet, not a hat.  It is probably a neat puppet, might be fun to play with, if a puppet is what you are after that is.  However, if you are after a hat, find a version of this that specifically claims to be a hat in the product description.  Unfortunately the manufacturer of this product did not include this information in the product description when I ordered it.  The return of the item was very simple.  Amazon has a wonderful customer support team and a simple return policy.  I would recommend Amazon to anyone.  I would recommend this hat only as a toy.

review_body: I got this for my daughter who loves bubbles.  First of all just to make the bubbles you have to push hard down toward the ground while pushing forward, which was hard for me and my husband much less a toddler.  When the bubbles did come out they were so close to the ground that they almost immediately popped and she had no chance of popping them herself. review_body: I was extremely pleased with this product. It was shipped very promptly and the quality of the jersey was excellent. I would definitely do business with these folks again. Thanks and Well done.

product_title: Super Cub Ready-to-Fly
review_headline: Dont waste your money on this plane
review_body: I bought this plane because of the large amount of positive feedback that it seems to get on the internet, but my experience with this plane has been nothing but bad.  I bouht it new from a hobby shop her in Arizona for my birthday. When I got it home, it had really seemed as the box had already been opened, and the battery looked as if it had been used. I called the store and he just gave me one excuse after another and ended up talking me into calling Horizon Hobby, as the wall/DC charger was bad. I had to ship the battery and charger back, at my expense, and after a lengthy wait they finally arrived. I have never managed to actually fly this plane, it always wants to veer off to the right immediately after a hand launch and go directly to ground. I have checked everything, COL, COG, everything.  Most recently, I noticed that the servo that controls the elevator has a jitter when it is turned on. I called Horizon Hobby again, got another of their semi-rude and disinterested employees on the phone, and this time he tells me that since I have had the plane out of the box and flown it, that it is not under warranty any longer. I asked him, so what you are telling me is that essentially there is no warranty on these planes, and he says that they work when they leave here, otherwise once you use it, its on you; nice.  Don't waste your time or money on this company and their products. They are cheap, they have no warranty to speak of, and when you call them for help, you just get an aggravating, time consuming run around.

product_title: Star Trek 40th Anniversary-Uss Enterprise D Diecast Ship By Corgi
review_body: I ordered it on Jan, 27th. Today is Feb, 3rd.  I live in Turkey. Whenever I purchase something from the internet (from USA, Germany etc.) it takes several weeks until the shipment arrives (via normal delivery). I had this product today on my desk. It took only one week, whereas I expected it at the end of February.    The package was in a very good condition. and so is the enterprise.  The only 'negative' thing I could say about the product is in the pictures it looks not that much like a simple toy, but a .. well maybe souvenir or something more valuable. imo the photos should be much bigger and at a higher resolution.    that said, I'm glad that I've purchased it.

product_title: Elite Force 63RD Anniversary Of D-Day "Vince" Action Figure
review_body: This was the perfect gift for my 11-year-old grandson, who is a WWII history buff and collector of all things WWII. He knew of the battle that \\"Vince\\" fought in, and is thrilled that the action figure,the weapons and other items are realistic and authentic looking. The product was described accurately and thankfully it arrived on the date it was promised. JG was very pleased and immediately deployed \\"Vince\\" into battle with his other figures. Thanks for the \\"bio\\" of this soldier,it sparked all of us to read and learn more about him,and the Ruhr River campaign,so there was an educational value to this toy. We are a military family and appreciate these types of toys. I will use this company in the future.

product_title: Metal Gear Solid Guns of the Patriots Sound Series - Snake Detected
review_body: If you look for this keychain series on YouTube, you can hear exactly what each one sounds like.  Or, you could just listen to the sounds in the game, because they are the exact same sounds!  I hadn't played Metal Gear Solid in years, and yet one push of this keychain immediately brought back clear memories of the game.  The Call Alert, Snake Detected, and Various Sound Effects keychains are the only ones I ordered, because the others feature Snake speaking in a different language, which was useless to me.  If you love the game, and want to be able to carry a reminder of it with you anywhere, these are awesome.

product_title: Transformers Animated Voyager Starscream
review_headline: Sweet toy, not a whole lot of issues.
review_body: In my opinion, this is an awesome figure.  But I did have a few minor qualms about it.    Robot mode is large.  In fact, he's taller in robot mode than Lugnut (also a voyager class figure).  All the joints work fine.  There are no loose screws that I'm aware of.  And the spring loaded \\"Mechanized Auto-Conversion\\" gimmick works without a problem.  The figure looks a lot like the cartoon character design.  I even like the translucent backing of the head to make the eyes and mouth glow when light shines through it.  It's a pretty solid toy with no balance problems.  Overall, it's also pretty fun to play with.      The only two parts of the toy I'd be concerned about as a parent are the two orange missiles that can shoot out from the arm cannons/fighter plane missile launchers.  They have the potential to be choking hazards for children who like to put things in their mouths.  Other than that there are no small parts for children to eat.    With practice (and with a good instruction booklet - the instructions suck; I'll go into this in a bit more detail) the transformation is smooth and fairly easy.  Like I said in my Lugnut toy review, many children will have a tougher time with transforming the Michael Bay Transformers the Movie toy line than this one.      This is a fan based issue, so feel free to skip it if you don't care.    I thought the paint design is fine, and it's actually like the cartoon character's paint detail.  From a G1 fan perspective, it bothered me a little that it had a similar color scheme to the other Decepticon Seeker jet named Thundercracker.  However, when I thought about how the Transformers Animated Series continuum has characters BASED ON THE G1 CHARACTERS, and THE ANIMATED SERIES CHARACTERS ARE NOT THE SAME AS THOSE IN THE G1 CONTINUUM, I quickly got over it.  The only reason I knew it wasn't Thundercracker was because it had a lot of red for certain parts of the figure.  But this is geek talk and while it may bring up issues that Transformers G1 fans may have with the color scheme of the Animated Starscream, I'm not going further with this, because it doesn't help parents at all (mostly because it's not a big deal-except to maybe Transformers dorks like me).    Here's another fan based issue...    Why are the arm cannons able to shoot orange missiles?  I watched the entire 3 seasons of the Animated Series and Starscream had arm cannons not arm missile launchers.  What happened?  Did the toy makers and the people from the cartoon not talk to each other?  What happened to teamwork (ironically, this is one of the Autobot's themes in the animated series), and making a good toy (someone seriously needs to stop thinking that people, especially children, are idiots)?    Okay onto what people really care about...    The toy's articulation.  Hasbro needs to seriously consider going the extra mile to make this an unbeatable figure (and any future line of toys for that matter) by adding certain parts or details.    While the articulation is very good, I feel that it can be much better.      For instance, Hasbro has gone as far as to make the thumbs and fingers move (actually the other fingers move together, not individually, just to clarify), which I think is awesome and has never been done (usually the fingers are just made out of one mould into a fist with a hole going through it so that the gun can be fit into it with a peg - lame, especially now that the standards for Transformers are moving up and they've proved that they can).  But they could've taken this further for such a large sized figure, why not make the wrists rotate with the range of motion that wrists normally have?  I mean, the fingers move, but that's it, I wanted to move the wrists, and it didn't budge.  What a let down. :(      As I'm looking at the Starscream figure more closely, I felt that they could've gone the extra mile and made his waist twist.  Not so much a big deal, but that would've made for an awesome toy.  But, again, Hasbro gotlazy...Oh, well.    Another thing that really bugged was, why in the world didn't they make the cockpit door open?!  The whole time, I'm staring at the thing, I wanted so bad to open it up and look inside.  Instead I'm left with the frustration of looking into the cockpit windows only to glimpse the detailed cockpit control panel and seat, but not being able to open that blasted door!  How irritating!  And don't give Hasbro any leniency on this one, they suck!  It felt like they got lazy and didn't go the extra mile (maybe 'cause they were thinking, oh, kids are the only ones buying them, and they won't care - well guess what, adults AND kids buy them and both parties aren't dumb!).  I mean, heck, the cockpits to the action figures of the G1 Decepticon Jets could open up, and there's nothing in there (no pilot's seat, no control panel)!  The G1 toys had such uninspiring interior cockpit design details (more like none), yet the cockpit doors could open to allow you to see the empty void inside!      On to the dreaded instruction booklet.  For such a seemingly easy transformation, the instruction booklet manages to mess it up for the reader.  For one thing, I feel like I have to bust out a magnifying glass to look at the pictoral details of the instructions so I can figure out what goes where.  Another thing is some of the pictures have lousy angles for the reader to view certain toy parts.  I, like another reviewer here had problems trying to figure out how to transform Starscream from robot mode back into plane mode, but I couldn't go back into the instruction manual to figure it out because none of the pictures showed how the under parts of Starscream is supposed to look like in jet mode.  This was frustrating, especially when I couldn't find anything on-line to help me!    I finally figured out after hours of playing with it that in order to properly transform Starscream from robot mode back to jet mode, the rounded portion of Starscream's shoulders (they're red), fits nicely into a pair of slots behind the underside of the nosecone.        However...    One of the things I really enjoyed about this toy is that when transforming from jet mode to robot mode, the cockpit snaps into place in the waist.  Here's why I loved this...    I remembered owning the G1 Thundercracker toy when I was a kid.  One of my biggest frustrations was that when it transformed from jet mode to robot mode, the cockpit wouldn't snap into place, and it'd just swing about all over the place on it's hinge because of how the plane's nosecone folds on it's head (it makes the head top heavy).  I hated this.      So in this respect, I'm glad they corrected the mistake that the G1 toy made.    Another mention about the transformation sequence.  Animated Starscream's wings on his back in robot mode can hook into place.  It has a hook that latches onto the underside of the folded back landing gear.  This is for all the people out there who didn't know this and wouldn't have figured it out on their own (I mention this because on-line I see a lot of people with the wings of their Starscream figures not latched onto the underside of the folded back landing gear, so it looks all loose and stuff).    Also, the second and third landing gears are on the shins of Starscream's legs.  They're the two black strips of plastic.  Pull them out.    Here's a secret not many people know about:    If you pull Starscream's arm cannons forward there are two pieces of black plastic on each side of each of his forearms that pop out.    Overall, other than the qualms I had with this toy, it is a solid toy and I did like it.  I loved how parts don't dangle all over the place like the action figures of the G1 Decepticon Jets did.  There are a lot of nice little touches here and there I loved as well.  Unfortunately, I wanted to love it even more, but Hasbro got lazy and didn't go the extra mile.    I'm bordering on an A- and a B+ on this toy.

review_headline: Wonderful way for children to learn to build and problem solve!
review_body: Usually, a toy is simply a toy... but this is so much more!  We got this for my 5 1/2 year old son for Christmas and he said immediately it was his favorite, but we figured we'd wait a few more days, lol.  About a month later and he is still playing with it daily but what I noticed more than his enjoyment was that he has used it for problem solving and many other learning exercises without realizing it.  Like the thing on top that holds different weights or whatever (I can't think of what it is called) but he totally gets into figuring out which magnet thing it would take to balance it out.  His building skills have improved and his creative side has really come out with these things.  Plus - you can't beat the price on Amazon - it is seriously double at even Walmart or other discount stores... so definitely get it!

product_title: Roll Through The Ages: The Bronze Age - The Bronze Age
review_body: This is a great little game! You build and track the progress of your Bronze Age civilization. Will you grow enough food to feed your people? Can you build a great monument like the pyramids? Perhaps you need to learn engineering or agriculture first.    And it really takes about 30 minutes to play. Turns are quick so there is not much waiting between turns. I cannot get family to play long games but THEY LOVE THIS ONE. The game fits perfectly into the small box so it is easy to take to the coffee shop for a quick game. It is great fun throwing those custom dice and IT IS NOT ANOTHER YATZY.    Some folks fear that it uses a pad of paper to track your civilization, but there are TONS OF SHEETS on the pad and the company website allows you access to the PDF file if you ever need to print more. If 30 minutes is too short then the company website has a 60 minute variation (a new civilization tracking sheet for the late bronze age) available for downloading.    Great value for money.

product_title: Air Hogs Battling Havoc Heli - Havoc vs Yellow Stinger
review_body: This was a birthday present for my 11 yo daughter.  She has really enjoyed flying them and when they crash it is just as much fun.  A good intro to RC flying since crashes are to be expected and this is a fairly durable toy.  A good idea to stay away from trees though because it can be a challenge to get them out of branches.

product_title: Scientific Explorer's Glow in the Dark Fun Lab Science Kit
review_body: Kit is small to say the least. A lot of added material you have to buy on your own. Messy too. More like a single use activity.

product_title: Fisher Price Fun Squirt Fire Truck
review_headline: Squirt fire truck is too fragile but fun
review_body: it was fun while it last which was less than one hour.  The plastic is too fragile

product_title: Melissa & Doug Classic Deluxe Kitchen
review_body: Unlike what some of the other reviews said before we bought it, this kitchen was fairly easy to put together.  We didn't have a problem with any of the pre-drilled holes.  There was one bag of screws that were the wrong type (should have been wood screws but were not), but we used some from my husband's tool box instead and it was fine.  One piece of advice -make sure there are 2 boxes when the kitchen is delivered.  The first time we only received one box and ended up having to purchase a new one at a slightly higher price.  My 2-year old son likes this kitchen, but unfortunately his enthusiasm to play with it seemed to wane after having it for a few days, which is disappointing.  He still loves playing with his friends' kitchens, but that could just be because it's something new.  Overall very sturdy construction and he can open and close all the doors himself.  Looks just like the picture.

product_title: Giant Plush Microbes - Toxoplasmosis
review_body: The picture led me to believe that I would be receiving a bunch of tiny microbes to make up a whole. WRONG!!! Only got one microbe. A little confusing, but still a lot of fun.

product_title: TABLETOPICS Family: Questions to Start Great Conversations
review_body: I purchased this for my neice after I received the \\"adult\\" version and thought she would enjoy the game with her family.  While the questions in the adult game are provocative (not in a negative way), the ones in this \\"family\\" version are rather lame, kind of boring!

product_title: Cranium Super Fort Mega Builder
review_headline: No longer made-- but get it if you can!
review_body:
This is a COOL toy. If you have creative kids (you know the type-- they're the kids who love cardboard boxes), this is the toy for them. It's expensive, but it is one of the most versatile toys I've ever seen. It works indoors and outdoors. It is engaging for a variety of ages and genders (my oldest child is 8, my youngest is 1): The older kids love inventing buildings (the ideas included, like the ship and hot air balloon, are wonderful also) and everyone, including the two year old loves playing in it. The boys like making battle forts, the girls make play houses and theaters. And there are enough parts to build two-room forts so you can have a battle at one end and a puppet show at the other. When you're done, it comes apart quickly and neatly into the nylon bag. That's a huge plus if you have space issues.

The only problem with this set is that Cranium discontinued the product and Hasbro bought Cranium so you can not get spare parts for it. What a shame. The instructions include a parts list and I highly recommend a plastic box for the connectors and clips-- one that will fit in the nylon bag (the bag is included)... we just practice our counting when we put the items away to make sure we got all our parts back.

Seriously fun. If there are any toy makers out there who read this, please bring this toy series back!!!

product_title: Sassafras Ellie Sleepwalker Elephant Bag
review_body: I actually ordered the elephant bag, but after I paid for it I was told that the elephant was sold out and to choose an alternate. I was pretty disappointed. I ended up with the chickadee bag, which is still cute....but not what prompted me to order. In the end, it is a lot bigger than I thought it would be! Great for an overnight bag. Shipping was quick.

product_title: Master Replicas Yoda Force FX Lightsaber
review_headline: Incredible, high quality, tons of fun, defective.
review_body:
When I got this, I was very excited. I opened it up, taking care not to break anything. I took out the battery pack and played with it for a few days, but the batteries began to sputter out, so I thought to replace them. I can't find any way to release the battery compartment, so I contacted Master Replicas, but after a week they still had not e-mailed me back, and time was running out to return it. I contacted Amazon, and returned it to them, and they gave me the full refund.

I don't know if it was just mine that was defective, but next time I buy one of these, it's going to be from Hasbro, not Master Replicas.

Overall, the quality of the saber was great. Extremely durable, realistic metal hilt feels great in the hand, the sound effects sound a little tinny and loud when you're holding it, but that is nothing compared to seeing the green 'blade' shoot up from the hilt.

product_title: Stomp Rocket Junior Glow Kit
review_body: I purchased Stomp Rocket for our 3-year old son's birthday...all the neighborhood kids love to come over to play with it.  Kids as young as 2 and as old as 7 have a great time launching the rockets and chasing after them.  I've not had any safety concerns with the toy - the rockets are soft foam, and the \\"launcher\\" can be pointed in different directions.  Simple set-up...(remember, it's only $[...] so don't expect more than plastic!)

product_title: Fisher-Price Smart Cycle [Old Version - Discontinued]
review_body:
We purchased this for our son for Christmas, as he is physically 8, but mentally about 4-5. He simply has not had much opportunity to enjoy it, as the batteries only last about 1 day. I refuse to keep buying batteries so we are trying to decide whether to pass the problem on to someone else, or wield a soldering iron and add an AC power adapter.

The gameplay itself is not really that stellar either. We were not expecting PS3 or XBox type video, but perhaps close to PS2 or Wii quality. We purchased two games and the graphics are really blocky, worse than I remember from the game systems from my childhood even.

On a positive note I'm glad they used cartridges instead of DVD's, as small kids destroy them really quickly.

I believe they should have built this as a controller for a better system, such as the wii or even the older PS2. I love the idea of combining exercise with gameplay, but not sure this is it.

review_headline: Most boring toy we've received yet!
review_body: This toy is completely boring.  There is 1 button to push and 1 ball gets flipped around to very short blips of music and flashing lights.  This only entertained my daughter for a few minutes, and she's within the recommended age range.  This has to be the worst, most boring toy we've received yet!  If there were more buttons or something, perhaps it would be more entertaining, but as is, it's just stupid.

product_title: Holiday Express Bakery Car
review_body: I also bought the Logger Car also can't wait for Christmas to run these together with the rest of the train. I hope my Grand-daughter notices the two new cars.

product_title: Uncle Milton Moon in My Room
review_headline: My Husband Gave Me The Moon!
review_body:
The moon has always been one of my favorite things (thanks to the book [[ASIN:0060775858 Goodnight Moon]]), so I was so excited when my husband gave me the moon to hang in our room. I know, sweet guy :)

This is actually a really cool toy - it shows all the phases of the moon, which can be changed with a remote control. It will automatically scroll through each phase slowly, or you can select your phase of choice and leave it on that. You can have it so it automatically senses when it is dark and turns on. It also turns off automatically after about half an hour.

Can't wait to put this in my son's room when he's a little older. Or, maybe I'll just keep it. It is pretty awesome.

review_headline: Super fun... Love it, but needs electronic version!!
review_body: Bought and played game for the first time, as adults, the entire family loved the game!! Played it 2x's over a few days and that's a lot considering how long it takes. I would compare this to traditional monopoly to the degree of time and money transactions - if this game came out with the electronic version like the new monopoly and life games, I would give this game a 5 stars as that would help speed up the game, and make all the math easier to handle!

product_title: Littlest Pet Shop Tail Waggin Fitness Club Playset

product_title: Precious Princess Sparkle Bag Sleeping Beauty

review_headline: Shoddy Product.... not durable at all
review_body: It is hard to imagine that this was made by Fischer Price.  I guess slapping on the Mickey Mouse name to this justifies the low quality. We've owned two of them, as one of them didn't work coming out of the box, as we were putting it together for my son's birthday.  The second one works, but it's one of those toys where you should take a picture of it working on the first day, cause it will quickly deteriorate quickly.

product_title: Little Tikes Princess Cozy Coupe
review_body: Our two year old grand daughter's eyes really lit up when she saw this car. Once inside She was all smiles.  Her older brother (age 4) couldn't wait to try it also.  The cell phone was a nice touch as well.

product_title: Hot Wheels Speed Racer Carrying Case Launcher with car (colors may vary)
review_body:
If the creative people behind [[ASIN:B001CD6FKI Speed Racer]] the movie had shown as much brilliance as the genius who licensed the toy contract to Mattel's Hot Wheels division, it would have been a box office smash rather than a box office disaster.

This carrying case/launcher is a perfect example; seven Speed Racer Hot Wheels cars can be stored and launched at the touch of a button either onto the floor or onto Hot Wheels track which can be attached to the opened door. All seven cars can be launched in rapid-fire succession by turning the wheel cover top one click in the direction of the arrows and releasing, which automatically lines up the next car. Meanwhile, the \\"movie accessory\\" attachments store in two compartments in the bottom. It comes with one car, either a [[ASIN:B0017SWZH0 Mach 5 with Saw Blades]] or a [[ASIN:B001731LXE GRX with Spear Hooks]].

Defects? The storage compartments are too small to hold some of the longer spear hook movie accessories, and a larger size that could hold more cars would have been nice.

review_body: I think this product is horrible.  I have had the same problems with the frogs getting stuck b/w the sides and even feeding them crickets and moths,they also get stuck and I had to destroy the bottom to get them out. review_body: For whatever reason you can not find a piglet anywhere.  If you have any other Disney pooh animals then you know what to expect.  Our 2 year old son loves Piglet and Roo.  This was a much have for Christmas and he loved it.

product_title: Beyblade H-92 Draciel S (Special Limited Edition)
review_body: this was a gift for my son age 9 and he enjoyed it very he loves bayblades.

product_title: Plan Toy Hammer Balls
review_body: My 1 year old LOVES this toy!! She loved it immediately and still after a few months it will entertain her for stretches at a time. When we first got it she could only push the balls through with her hands. The holes are built so that they can be pushed through like that. As she progressed, she learned how to hit the balls using another ball. And finally she can now hit the balls with a hammer. I would definitely recommend this one!

product_title: Crayola Glow Station can create with Light!
review_body: I don't get what all the negative reviews are about. We just got this for my 4 yr old son for Christmas, hung it up a couple nights later and it's been a hit ever since. Hubby and I think it's super cool! My son LOVES it, and shows it to everyone that comes over. I haven't had the issue of the drawings fading in 4-5 seconds, just the opposite. When I had my MIL over watching as he drew, she even asked what we had to do to erase it... it just didn't disappear fast like I'm now reading people have problems with! We had no problem installing it either, hubby got out his drill and that was that.    He did take away the dry erase marker before our son was the wiser. I have no clue what it's even for but just the light pen is enough for the kids to have a blast with. review_body: I got this Belle costume for my 5-year-old daughter for Christmas.  She loves dressing up (changes about 5 times a day) and loves princesses. review_body: There is no way this works. We received it as a Christmas present and tried to use it. When you put the pressure on the clay needed to form the bowl the turn-table stops. I do not recommend buying this product.

product_title: ALEX Toys Rub a Dub Sort 'n Spray Whale

The whale doesn't stay together so well, but it doesn't seem to matter. The little squirter doesn't work great, and that doesn't seem to matter either. She just loves it.

product_title: Hermit's Haven Crab Habitat
review_body: this habitat is a death trap.  gravel is absolutely inadequate for a crab.  they need several inches of sand in order to bury themselves or they will die.  hermits do not breed in captivity...you would be plucking a crab out of tropical paradise and put them in a tuperware bowl.  they also need a specific temperature and humidity level in order to breathe.  it would be impossible to achieve that in this container.

product_title: Excalibur World Chess Hall of Fame Collector's Edition Set - Classic Edition
review_body: I received this set as a gift a few years ago when it was still selling at $200.  I see the price has now dropped to an amazing $140!  This truly is a classy set with the board and pieces well varnished, the pieces well weighted and padded.  A strikingly beautiful and practical chess set!  I own many chess sets.  This set is by far my most luxurious and favorite set.

product_title: Barbie STACEY NITE LIGHTENING SET 1969 Reproduction GOLD LABEL 7,700 WORLDWIDE (2005)
review_headline: Barbie's friend Stacey is back - in all her Mod glory!
review_body:
In 1969, Mattel introduced another doll into Barbie's ever-expanding world of family and friends. Stacey was Barbie's swingin' best friend from London, complete with a wardrobe of colourful, specially-designed Mod fashions! This Gold Label collector's edition (limited to 7,700 pieces worldwide) brings back the Stacey doll along with her \\"Nite Lightning\\" fashion ensemble.

Stacey comes dressed in a bright print swimsuit, with her red hair styled into a short flip. Just like the original doll, she has real rooted eyelashes and a Twist 'n' Turn waist. The \\"Nite Lightning\\" ensemble consists of a royal blue satin \\"swing\\" coat with puffed sleeves and sparkly brooch decoration, and a metallic \\"shag\\" dress. Matching blue stockings and low-heeled shoes complete her trendy Mod look. A re-print of an original Barbie fashion booklet from the period is also included, along with the COA and dollstand.

product_title: Hellboy II The Golden Army 3-3/4 Inch Box Set
review_body: This box set is excellent. Hellboy has as much articulation as the 7\\" version, and the sculpted detail is nothing short of impressive.     Winks is also very well detailed, and comes with an alternate chain hand that pops into the right wrist.    The new character, Johann, looks very nice, although his articulation is a bit more limited due to his character design, as his joints are somewhat restricted by the containment suit. In contrast, Liz Sherman turned out to be a really nicely articulated figure, even though she is not the most striking of the bunch.

It's simple yet fun-brings out healthy competition and lots of laughing. There's a little geometry education like in pool where you learn angles in shooting. product_title: Precious Princess Sparkle Bag Ariel
review_headline: Hands down favorite of my Little Mermaid obsessed child.
review_body:
My daughter is utterly obsessed with the Little Mermaid and has the full gamut of Little Mermaid toys. This one rules them all because it's portable, poseable, and allows transformation from mermaid to human and back. I've actually just bought it for the 3rd time in 2 years. I've had to replace it because there are lot of little pieces to lose - and they do get lost. I've also had to replace it because it's flat out my daughter's favorite toy and she's miserable without it. Very simply - it's a polly pocket size little Ariel doll with a bunch of dresses and shoes, and a tiny Flounder and Ariel along for the ride. These toys are easy to carry and go everywhere (and also easy to misplace). You can remove Ariel's sparkly green tail and then (by removing Ariel's big hair) can dress her in the various dresses and shoes (mainly the pink dress she uses to make Eric fall in love with her and the white dress she gets married in). Everything is stretchy grippy rubbery plastic so it's hard to dress and undress (and Daddy ends up helping a lot). They all come in a zipper carrying case that's useful for traveling with a big bunch of little plastic toys.

All in all wonderful, and maddening (a lot like my daughter come to think of it).

product_title: Brainbox All Around the USA
review_body: How boring to learn U.S. geography facts the old fashioned way...from lists. This game is a hit with my 10 yo son who begs to make time to play with our family and who told me this is the first educational game that he REALLY LOVES. Colorful, illustrated, sturdy cards help memorization skills, along with a 10 second sand timer, making it a fast paced, highly interesting game. Ten seconds goes really quick, so we started the game turning the timer twice. Now, ten seconds is a breeze and we are covering a mountain of facts in a short period of time. Can't wait to get Brainbox: All Around The World. Highly recommend \\"All Around The USA\\", especially if your child needs to develop quick memorization using visuals.

product_title: Bandai Hobby EW-S W-Gundam Zero Custom "Special Operation", Bandai Action Figure
review_body:
I know a place where they sell millions of Gundam models for $20 a piece, but this is well worth the price, since the TV anime did air almost 13 years ago, so this model is hard to find in retail stores.

For anyone who does not know, this is the HG (or High Grade) model version of this Gundam. The levels are HG (around $25 or so), MG (Master Grade, around $50+) And PG (Perfect Grade, easily goes over $100, but is well worth it). If you are willing to spend the money, a Gundam fan, or just a hobbyist, I would suggest getting the PG or MG models. If price is a problem, stick to the HG models, they're impressive themselves.

Almost all of the pieces are colored silver so it looks cool. It is not the real color of the Gundam, but it looks okay. The only thing that I am sad about are the wings of this model; It is just one piece of silver plastic with a few movable parts. For anyone who loves this model (I do, my favorite Gundam), try to research the PG or MG models for information on more movable/complex wings, because that is the one main thing that gives this Gundam its uniqueness.

Overall, a great buy.

Our kids have a great time with it especially when we (the parents) have to sing a Christmas carol or wear a towel on our head.  It also helps us to slow down and focus on our family and remember what Christmas is truly about.  I would highly recommend it to anyone looking for a game the entire family can play.

product_title: Radio Flyer Little Red Scooter
review_body: This scooter has brought just as much enjoyment to my grandchildren as it did to me....and that was 54 years ago!  The kids just seem to always gravitate to more traditional toys, in spite of all the high-tech options they have in their toy closets and toy chests.  Everytime I have given one of my grandchildren their very own Radio Flyer Scooter, it has turned out to be the one gift they are most excited about....whether it has been for a birthday or at Christmas!

product_title: EyeClops BioniCam
review_headline: For older kids who are into microscopes
review_body:
At an incredible price and interesting concept, I really was excited about this gadget. However my six year old son and I were both disappointed.

This is a digital microscope and nothing else. You have to hold the bionicam right on top of the object. The 100x was the only view that worked well enough for us to actually use and that was only on top of SOME things with us holding the camera a certain way. The 200x and 400x were basically useless for me.

We could see our jeans, hair, and skin pretty well. That was about it for us.

My batteries did not last that long in this, so you may want to consider rechargeable batteries.

I would only consider purchasing this for an older child who really loves microscopes.

product_title: Smart Ass
review_headline: Updated questions make for fun across ages
review_body: We played this with 20+ year-olds through those in their 60's and had a lot of fun.  Because questions ranged from very recent topics to more classical history-type questions, all ages were able to answer questions and be a part of the game.  Also, given the progressive nature of the questions, we rarely had a round with a question that went unanswered.  This is a game for individuals, not teams, and you can have from 2-8 people play.  Since we'd spent much of the weekend playing team-oriented games, this was also a nice change.  Highly recommend.

product_title: 1993 World Championships Lance Armstrong DVD
review_body:
In an incredible solo effort in the closing laps of the Oslo circuit course, Lance Armstrong powered his was to the \\"Rainbow Jersey\\" in the 1993 UCI Road World Championships Road Race.

The DVD captures the wild ride after some wicked weather brought a few severe icy spots on the course; with a camera \\"surprisingly\\" in position to chronicle a wealth of spills when riders did not take one sharp descent very gingerly.

Armstrong's breakaway is juxtaposed with the refusal of the pack immediately behind him from forming a cohesive chase, as riders like Miguel \\"Big Mig\\" Indurain and Olaf Ludwig essentially concede the title to the upstart American and become content to sprint for the remaining pair of podium spots.

The coverage is first-rate and the significance of the victory became even greater as Armstrong was setting a foundation to a legendary career that may not be over. This was an icy upset that will heat up any DVD player on a cold winter day.

product_title: Blurt
review_body: BLURT! was so fun we ran through all of the cards in one night.  Oh yeah, if you have a big enough party, you will go through cards like potato chips.    The game is extremely simple.  Everyone takes turns being a reader, they read the definition of the word on the card and then people proceed to blurt out the word being defined.  The cards have two sides, one side being easier than the other.  As you get an answer correct you roll the die and advance.  But even if you are a whiz you aren't safe.  A challenge can occur when two people are on the same colored space.      For example: Player \\"A\\" is just tearing it up and is advancing to the finish very fast so he's way out in front.  Player \\"B\\" is barely out of start.  Player \\"B\\" luckily gets an answer right and advances to a space that is the same color as the one Player \\"A\\" is on (light years ahead).  Player \\"B\\" can challenge Player \\"A\\" mano e mano and if Player \\"B\\" blurts the correct answer out first, then they trade places.  If Player \\"B\\" doesn't blurt out the correct answer first, then oh well, he hasn't lost anything.    I know, it doesn't sound fair at all does it?  But, this keeps the game interesting.  The one in front is never at rest because he/she is always being challenged and the ones behind are always hoping to challenge to get a free pass to the front of the line.    Great game, the words aren't all that difficult, they just need to come out with some refills.

product_title: Phase 10 Card Game
review_body: A few years ago (I help with students at church) another leader brought a pack of these cards and suggested a few played.... I joined in and was hooked... So I purchased a pack of these cards for my game collection. I have had ages 8-88+ play this game and have never had anyone who didn't love it.    Game Play:  Phase 10 is sort of like Rummy backwards. Each player (2-6 players) are dealt 10 cards. You then lay the remaining cards face down in the middle and flip one card face up.    On your turn you must pick a card up (either the one laying face up in the middle or one from the pile) and discard one face up in the middle (covering the previous face-up card).    Your goal is to go through the 10 phases:  (*As a note: a set is the same numbers (ie a set of 3 would be 4&4&4 or 8&8&8.... A run is a numerical order (ie a run of 4 would be 1&2&3&4 or 9&10&11&12)  1. 2 sets of 3  2. 1 set of 3 & 1 run of 4  3. 1 set of 4 & 1 run of 4  4. 1 run of 7  5. 1 run of 8  6. 1 run of 9  7. 2 sets of 4  8. 7 cards of one color  9. 1 set of 5 & 1 set of 2  10. 1 set of 5 & 1 set of 3    The goal is to lay down your phase (phase out) and then get rid of the rest of your cards (go out) before anyone else.  If you do not phase out you must continue the next round on the same phase you were on. (Ie if you don't phase out on phase 1, although everyone else is on phase 2 you are still on phase 1.)    I can't rave about how much fun this game is... You can make house rules, keep points (1-9= 5 pts, 10-12= 10 pts, Skips= 15 pts, & Wilds=25 pts... person with the least amount of points in the end win), play a half game, etc...    If I could own only one card game it would be Phase 10.

product_title: Mobile Suit XXXG-01W Wing Gundam Ver.Ka 1/100 Scale Model
review_body: This model is not for the faint of heart when it comes to building a model. Although it is all snap together parts (which helps alot) it is still extremely complex and detailed. This unique version of the wing gundam is really nifty looking in my opinion (except for the extra energy pack thing, that just looks stupid). It is very posable and has extra sturdy arms/legs. I myself had a loose joint on the left arm but just replaced it (it comes with lots of joint parts to spare) and now its very sturdy. The face is extremely detailed and very hard to get two of the parts in place to stay (I involved one drop of crazy glue for them, if you buy it you probably will too, either that or leave them off, seeing as the only add a flair). That and the unit seems to have a bit of difficulty holding the buster rifle unless you rest the tip of the weapon on the ground and use it as another balance point. Those are my only gripes with the model, so I cannot willingly give it a 5 star but it is most certainly worth the price due to the build time involved (4-6 hours nonstop for advanced modelers, and 10+ for anyhting less.) and the fact that the unit itsel looks great and is extra large so it really draws the eyes.

product_title: Guidecraft Safari Collection Table And Chairs Set
review_headline: sturdy toddler/pre-K table set with secret compartment
review_body: This top quality table set is made of sturdy, thick, real wood construction that is strong and firm, with beautiful detailing. The animals are not just painted on, but hand carved. The table is a good size for 2-6 year olds and large enough for four little ones to have plenty of room for drawing, coloring, or crafts, so get the extra chairs if several kids will be around to use it. Our two chairs had a different animal on the seat, so playdate pals can pick \\"their favorite chair\\". The chairs are also balanced very well and are not easy to tip over when sitting (or standing) on them. In the center of the table is a secret compartment - the \\"sun\\" easily lifts off and the cloth pouch underneath provides ample space for crayons and favorite toys. We now have the entire line and all are sturdy and easy to put together (in less than 10 minutes with a power drill), but also easy to assemble with just a screwdriver. And Guidecraft backs their product. We needed to replace a part on another Safari item we bought (that we broke, not Guidecraft's fault) and after one phone call (to a real person) we were sent the new part within a week at no charge for the part or even for shipping! We love this heirloom set and it will be in our family for decades. (See also the coordinating bookrack, step stool, toy chest, rocking chair, and director's chair, which we also bought.)

product_title: THE ISLAND
review_headline: Great toy...but you don't get what you see in the picture
review_body: I got this set for my son, who is autistic, as it came highly recommended from his therapists (who use it at their center).  It's a fun way to teach balance and address sensory issues (and it's plain fun for his sister, who is not on the spectrum, to play on, too!)  I was so excited to see that this large set of \\"rivers\\" and \\"islands\\" cost just $50.  Ummm...no.  Apparently, all you get for $50 are the two larger \\"islands\\" and none of the \\"rivers\\" (the interlocking balance beams).  Sure, when you put on your reading glasses and look VERY closely at the fine print (and I do mean \\"fine print\\"!), you will see that this is all the set contains.   The average, intelligent person is going to look at the picture shown, read the description and think that all the pieces come with the set for the price shown.   Not so.  To buy the set as shown would cost roughly $300.   THIS NEEDS TO BE MADE VERY CLEAR!    Either the store should increase the price and sell a larger set or make it VERY clear that all a person will get for the current price is 2 pieces of plastic and a disappointed kid.  :-(    The set itself is very sturdy, really well made and quite fun to play with.  Adults can even get in on the action!   The \\"rivers\\" and \\"islands\\" are interlocking and swivel, making it very easy to configure it in just about any form imaginable...just be sure to order a full set in order to maximize this feature!

product_title: KidKraft Red Vintage Kitchen
review_body: Friends, don't be tempted by this little Chinese wolf in sheep's clothing!  Right out of the box I knew I'd made a major purchase error.  Dozens and dozens of numbered parts and two, large, plastic-wrapped piles of countless screws, fasteners, rivets, bolts, washers, nuts and other assorted and sundry unidentifiable metallic gizmos.  After about a half an hour, I had the hundred some odd parts spread across about a half an acre.  I turned to the instruction \\"booklet\\" and winced when I opened it.  The first several pages were devoted solely to the identification of the above-mentioned fasteners etcetera.  Unquestionably, the instruction manual was created by some sort of sadistic psychopath.  The thing not only made no sense whatsoever, it seemed to deliberately lead you in circles.  To make matters worse, the instructions were all multi-step illustrations with no text whatsoever (undoubtedly to cut costs!).    Folks, this adorable little hellbox took approximately 5 hours to assemble.  After the first 2.5 hours, I turned to the bottle for comfort.  I awoke with a severe hangover the following morning and returned to my project with renewed fervor.  The last hour involved fumbling with the 10-dozen or so \\"micro-screws\\" that attached the various doors to their hinges.  I kid you not, these screws are so small that the Guiness Book of World Records has decided to enter them in their \\"smallest screw\\" category.    Next time you're shopping and pass by the already-assembled KidKraft Vintage Kitchen just keep on walkin' baby!  Don't even think of tackling this monumental task...
