product_title: Decathlon Convertible Car Seat - Odyssey
review_body: I ordered this seat after reading all the reviews that infants seem to love it. I have a 3 1/2 month old who screams at the sight of her Graco Snugride car seat. We have a 1400 mile drive ahead of us next month and I pray the decathlon does the trick.   After two days with the car seat both Mom and Baby are happy.     The tiffany print is beautiful... just perfect for little girls. The pink is not an annoying shade of pink like I feared it might be. It is just a beautiful pattern. My daughter looks so cute and comfy in it.    No crying so far! She fussed a little when I first sat her in it, because I think she was so use to hating her other car seat. But once she realized how plush and comfortable she was, she got this look on her face like, \\"OH, how nice!\\" and that was the last of the fussing. She sits up much higher in this seat and can look out the windows. The infant inserts keep her sitting straight up and not slouching, and the recline of the chair keeps her head from flopping around. It seems like every measure was taken into consideration for baby's comfort with this seat. There are no pressure points or spots where baby's skin contacts anything rough or hard.     Now my only complaint... the harness adjustment strap. It is really really hard for me to pull. I have guessed this could be because of three possibilities. 1.) The seat is brand new and just needs to be broken in. 2.) With all the infant padding in place it makes it harder for the straps to go through them. 3.)With the chair in the rear facing position, I can't get good leverage to pull. Hopefully Britax will fix this problem, cause this is a fantastic car seat except for that one problem.     Bottom line is this chair is the safest and the most comfortable for my daughter, so price was no object. I will pull on the adjustment strap until I am blue in the face since she is happy now! Yea! No more screaming!

product_title: Pack 'n Play - Mocha
review_body:
I got this item as a baby shower gift and so far I have had quite few uses for it. First of all, I placed it by the side of my bed and that was pretty much where my baby slept for her first 6 weeks of her life. It is perfect for all those many times a baby wakes up at night. I really didn't have to get up, just sit down on my bed and I was able to reach my baby. Second, the changing table is very much convenient. Since my baby would usually make a number two right after every feeding, it was very convenient to have everything set up for my reach to take care of that as well.

On a third note, after she moved up to her crib, I placed the item on my living-room. Because of its color and patterns, it really look good there and it was an easy access whenever my baby would fall asleep during the day. Instead of going all the way upstairs to her room, I would just directly place my baby on the bassinet. In the same way, if she needed a diaper change while she was downstairs, I had everything there for me to take care of it. The little basket by the changing table id great to place diapers, wipes and any extra items that you need.

There are few things I didn't really like that much. When I try to use it for a trip I was going to, I realized how hard was to put it back on the bag. It is kind of big and hard to carry,since everything won't really fit back in there. I ended up leaving it at home. That was a little frustrating. Another thing is that the mobile doesn't really move. It just stays there. I saw my daughter staring at it so many times and I just wished it would have some movement or it would at least play a little song.

Other than that, she is now seven months and even though she is to big for the bassinet part, (she is now on the big kids section), she loves been there with her toys and blanket, while the rest of the family is doing other chores. Hopefully I would be able to still use it until she is at least a year old.

product_title: Fisher Price - Learn Thru Music System With Cartridge
review_headline: So sad it did not work right!!
review_body: My daughter loved this toy and after it did not advance to the next page then went crazy I took it back and exchanged it.  Same thing happened... I was really disapointed because my daughter loved it.

product_title: Disney Movie Robots Electronic Boots - Roboots
review_body: I got these boots for my son's 6th birthday. The Robots movie had come out shortly before so he was all gung ho Robots stuff. I think they are made well, and the plastic is lightweight and easy to fit around any kind of shoes. Sometimes it is hard to get them to make the noises though and he does have to stomp pretty hard. I don't find them annoying though, as some people said they do. They noises are funny and not loud at all. My son liked them a lot at first. He doesn't wear them too much anymore, but he'll pull them out every now and then and go to town!

product_title: Rallye Boys Front Wheel Scooter: Flames
review_body: We bought this scooter for our son for his fourth birthday in October 2003. It has been rode hard by many children and is still in great shape. It has been left out in the weather on several occasions with no damage done. My son has loved this scooter ever since we got it for him and will pick it up to ride before he rides his beloved bicycle. My 2.5 yo daughter easily figured out how to manuver this scooter and received a girl one for her birthday which she loves. I would highly highly recommend this scooter for ages 3-6 yrs.

product_title: Hasbro Playskool Busy Ball Popper
review_body: My son got this toy for his 1st birthday.  It took him a bit to learn how to push the plunger but once he did...oh boy!  He is now 17 mos and still loves to play with this.  He puts his shapes in there and has even put his pinwheel by the air to make it go. product_title: LEGO Racers: Night Racer

product_title: Little Mommy High Chair
review_body: Perfect little set-up for our 6yr old both the stroller and high chair are easy to assmble and sturdy  I highly recommend for your little one.

product_title: Dora's Talking House Furniture Set 4 Rooms
review_headline: DORA ANYTHING SELLS! HORRIBLE MARKETING ON THIS ONE...
review_body: I purchased the doll house at 2am, grabbing it out of the stack of merchandise in the middle of an isle in WalMart last year just before Christmas, (after looking world-wide both on the internet and traveling through 3 states). As many parent experienced the problems of getting the dollhouse, then no furniture for months, I found out at a Toys r Us along my travels that enlightened me to the fact that NO FURNITURE HAD BEEN SHIPPED TO ANYONE, as it was not to be released until AFTER CHRISTMAS. I have no idea where the people on EBAY got theirs (makes you wonder, huh???) when stores not only had no furniture, they had NEVER GOTTEN ANY period! Should be a law against someone selling a $10.00 set of doll furniture for over $100.00 but then again, guess anyone stupid enough to pay it should be committed anyway! I just think it was a marketing ploy to increase the interest and people like me, when I finally found the furniture, I was so afraid I would not be able to get it later so I purchased it all at one time. Quite an expense, one I would never have undertaken under normal circumstances. I was afraid to take the chance of having this dollhouse and nothing with it, too much to invest to just sit.You do not have to have all the sets, but almost all the children who got one and no furniture was not interested in the house at all without the \\"extras\\". After aquiring some furniture the kids were indeed thrilled and is a very cute, durable and longterm learning tool.Shame on the company, the big CEOs (look at TYCO) whose greed got ahead of their COMMON SENSE!

product_title: Transformers Cybertron Scout Hardtop
review_body:
I like the way it poses. Small problems with the gun, it can't flip out the barrel when it is pointing straight forward, but I can forgive that.

product_title: Nutcracker Kit
review_body:
Dear Ava Natov, editorial reviewer:

The story 'The Nutcracker and the King of Mice' was written by German author E.T.A. Hoffman (1776-1822).

French author Alexandre Dumas pere (father) (1802-1870) retold Hoffman's 'The Nutcracker' which is where we get the libretto (the text of the opera) for 'The Nutcracker' we are more familiar with today.

French author Alexandre Dumas fils (son) (1824-1895) neither wrote nor rewrote 'The Nutcracker'.

Amazon sells this book, translated from the German by Ralph Manheim, well-known German-language translator.

product_title: Intex Inflatable Whale Spray Kiddie Pool - Holds up to 71 Gallons (82"x62"x39")
review_body: We've had this pool now for what will be our third summer. My son has enjoyed it since he was only 5 months old and is now 2. The sides are wide and sturdy enough for him to sit/lay on without caving the whole thing in and he loves bouncing up and down on the tail. So far it's held up, no leaks and I'm rather surprised since most blow up pools don't last 1 summer. Anyways, the blow hole is a fun feature (you hook it up to the hose) that my son loves as well. Another nice thing is that the pool is large enough for me to sit in with my legs fully extended (I'm 5'7). Inflating it takes some time and massive effort if you don't have an electric pump, so we keep it inflated all year round and just store in rafters in the garage during the winter. This is a great pool.

product_title: Safety 1st neat! Diaper Disposal System
review_body: A must for all moms and dads.  If my husband does not mind changing the diapers then I know it is partly because of the Neat Diaper Disposal.   He simply loves it!   He has said that since there is no smell coming from the pail and it is easy to use, he will not complain. He loves the way it pushes the diaper right down to the bottom. We only empty the pail every 6 to 7 days only and have still not been able to smell anything.    I believe men need effective gadgets to make it more interesting.  HA!  I am a happy wife and mother.  I tend to agree with my husband on how useful the Neat really is.  Try it!  You will love it!

product_title: Fisher-Price Ocean Wonders Aquarium Cradle Swing
review_body:
When I first had my son, everyone I knew said, \\"Get a swing!\\" I looked at some, but they all seemed to take up so much room! So I didn't do it. Then my son got a cold at the age of 2 months. The only thing that seemed to soothe him was rocking. So in desperation (after 3 days in the rocking chair) I went out and bought this swing. Wish I had done it sooner! Even after the cold passed, my son loved it! I began to feel like a bad mother because he spent so much time in it, but he was very happy there! I really like the fact that you can change the direction of the swinging motion and there are a variety of sounds and music to choose from.
I only found three negatives. 1) It does eat batteries! (Especially when your little one wants to be in it ALL of the time!) I finally went out and bought a battery charger and 8 rechargable D batteries. I had to change the batteries everyday, and the initial expense was quite a bit. But, fortunately, the batteries are easy to change in this (as opposed to some other Fisher Price stuff) and in the long run, it was cheaper than having to buy new batteries. 2) When my son got older he could reach over and grab the material between the supports and stop the swing. This was my cue to take the swing away. (I'm pregnant again and I want this swing to be around for the next one too!) 3) It takes up a lot of room, but then what \\"baby thing\\" doesn't?

We have been using the Marathon since my son turned one and I just purchased an exact replacement since his old carseat cannot be used any longer.     **Update: July 21, 2005**  Even more impressed with the Britax company since we were accepted into their Crash Restraint Exchange Program (info on their website if you are interested) and they are sending us a brand new replacement Marathon in return for us sending them the Marathon that was involved in the car accident. We sent the company all of the required information regarding the car accident and they contacted us to say we were approved. All we had to do was pay the shipping charges to return the old seat to them and they are shipping us out a brand new replacement! Needless to say, I have been thoroughly impressed. review_headline: The True Nature of this Lightsaber
review_body:
This lightsaber is one of the best that Hasbro has made to date. Considering that it is just a toy, it is very well articulated. It looks a lot like the handle that is used by Anakin Skywalker in the movie Star Wars Episode III: Revenge of the Sith. The only thing that hurts the lightsaber for those that like roleplaying is that the blade does not go into the handle, a problem that has plagued this line of lightsabers for years. But the good does out weigh the bad. The light is superb, looks more like what a lightsaber blade should look like, since it is not colored plastic like the other ones. The fact that it can change colors from blue to red is this lightsabers special feature. However, this lightsaber is not really designed like the one Darth Vader will build for the original trilogy, but since Anakin's and Vader's handles have a similar design, it is like having 2 lightsabers for the price of one. The sounds are really good, sounding like the ones from the movies, which is a plus. The sound quality is better then the lightsaber line up from Attack of the Clones(Have Anakins form Clones also).
How does it compare to the other lightsabers from ROTS? Of the 3 special lightsabers(Obi-Wan Kenobi's and Yoda's are the other 2 special lightsaber and I have both), it has the better special of the 3(Obi-Wan's vibrates when it is hit and Yoda's has a \\"Training Mode\\", which is only Yoda speaking random stuff when it is activated, deactivated, and when it is hit). Highly recommend this lightsaber to those who collect them, those that want to play with them, and/or those who want a good Prop to bring with them when they see Episode III(like I did). this saber is so cool, I bought 2 of them(one stays in the box and the other I play with and brought with me to see Episode III).

Before buying this, I reviewed the online reviews on this website, and to my surprise almost everyone wrote about how defective the game is. \\"It can't be that bad\\" I thought. \\"Maybe it takes a little getting used to, but certainly the manufacturer would not have defective games in the field\\".

So, I purchased it, came home, got my son very excited about the game . . . and turned it on. The graphics were phenominal, sound was great, etc. Then, I tried to move. product_title: Cranium Zigity Tin
review_headline: Genuine fun for the whole family
review_body:
We got a promotional copy of Zigity (without the storage tin) free when we bought another Cranium game for our 4 1/2-year-old. We didn't expect to play it much as it's recommended for ages 8 and up. However, this has become a family favorite, although our daughter needs help to play.

Zigity cards are used to build four different types of sets. Each set card has one symbol in each corner: a letter, a number, a puzzle piece, and a musical instrument. You build a set by combining cards to create a word, add up to 11, complete the puzzle, or group identical instruments. A free card can be used like a wild card to complete any type of set. When you play your set, the picture in the center of the top card determines what kind of set the next player has to build. You can also play an action card, forcing the next player to draw cards, allowing you to skip your turn, or reversing the order of play. The first player to play all his or her cards wins.

The cards are clear, which makes them cool to look at and allows you to easily see all four corners of the cards. This does have two disadvantages, though. The cards are very slippery and occasionally go flying out of your hand when you're holding the desk. (Especially if you're four years old.) Second, it allows you to tell which puzzle piece is on the card on top of the draw pile or see that the card is either an action or free card (altough you can't tell which). The puzzle piece is in a bottom corner, though, so it's easily hidden once the card is in your hand.

Zigity is entertaining for adults, with lots of opportunities for strategy and the ability to use action cards to create sudden changes in momentum. For kids, its fun and educational. While it would probably require a 7- or 8-year-old to fully appreciate this game, even a younger child working on spelling and addition skills can enjoy Zigity with the help of an adult. I highly recommend this game, especially for families stuck in the Old Maid/Go Fish/Crazy Eights rut.

product_title: Snatch-It Word Game
review_headline: From the Board Games Editor at BellaOnline.com
review_body:
Snatch, by U.S. Games Systems, is a simple word game which is compact, quick to learn and fun! The game comes with 100 plastic tiles, and it is cleverly packaged in a simple tube (it sort of looks like a small, plastic packing tube).

Play is simple. Players lay all of the tiles face-down in the middle of the table. Then players take turns flipping the tiles over one at a time. When a player sees a word three letters or longer, they shout it out and snatch it from the center, setting it in front of them. Players can steal each other's words by adding a letter to them, so beware!

What's great about this game is that unlike many word games (Scrabble, for example), it's socially interactive the whole way through. No waiting for other players to take forever making their play.... it's fast-paced and fun.

review_body:
I received this chair as a shower present. I am very greatful for the gift and have used the chair every day since my five month old daughter was born. This glider has no significant problems but if I were to purchase a glider I would upgrade.

Some things to consider before purchasing:
The chair is small which works well for me (5'4\\" 120lbs).
The cushons are not machine washable.
The fabric is a simple neutral color that seems to blend in with everything.
The fabric is cleanable by hand but somewhat harsh and not very durable.
I find myself retightening the screws frequently (every other week) because they seem to wiggle loose.

I give the chair 3 stars because it is functional, comfortable and very affordable. But...If I were to need another chair in the future I would invest a little more money for something with fabric that is more durable and easier to take care of.

review_body:
I am 18 years old, and this doll got me interested in collecting Barbies again. She is GORGEOUS, and it may be difficult to tell from the picturs, but she actually has real eyelashes! I've never seen a Barbie doll with real eyelashes before, and they work so well on her! She has glittery eyeshadow and teh detail on her face is just incredible! I love how her arms and legs are subtly spray-painted lavender in parts, which gradually fades back into her skin. It gives a good diea of how well she was made, and the flower tattoos on her body add a definite touch of fantasy and imagination.

Her clothes are also gorgeous, even though they are a big skimpy. Her wings took me a while to figure out how to get on--if a child is buying this, the parents may want to add the wings first; there's really no reason to take them off once they're put on, so you won't have to worry about it again after you do it once. The holders of the wings snap two different places--the front and the back. When they're snapped to the front, they hang on the sides of her skirt, and they don't really look like a gown, but they are quite elegant and magical. When they snap to her back, you can press the button on her back to make them flutter, which is absolutely lovely. It is a bit difficult to see the doll though when your finger is on the button because of the way you need to hold her, so I usually flutter her wings in front of a mirror.

Her hair is very creative--it's divided into pigtails that are fastened with sparkly flowers, and each pigtail is twisted around tiny braids, intricate woven into her hair.

The little fairy sprite she comes with is also surprisingly well-made. You'd think that as a bonus they wouldn't care about it much, but if you look at her closely, you can see there is a lot of detail on her face, and she has tiny pink flowers around her head.

She even comes with a map of Fairytopia that's tied with a lovely ribbon, and a booklet with gorgeous artwork in it.

I LOVE this doll! It's beautiful, and a lot of fun to play with! HIGHLY reccommended!and a booklet with gorgeous artwork in it.

I LOVE this doll! It's beautiful, and a lot of fun to play with! HIGHLY reccommended!

product_title: Nerf Rapid Fire 20
review_body: I bought three of these from Toys R Us as Christmas gifts for my kids.  I decided to open one up one night to test out its performance and make sure I was getting what I thought I was getting.    The gun is fairly good sized, and smaller children (three to four years old) might find it a little unwieldy to pump and tote around, although weight isn't too prohibitive even for that age group.  It takes 23 pumps to fully pump the gun up.  There must be a release valve somewhere because you can hear it let the extra air out if you continue pumping after it's fully pumped up.  This is probably a built-in safety device to keep dart velocity at a safe level.    There is a selector switch on the side that allows you to switch between fully automatic and semi-automatic.  Actually, the semi-auto setting is sort of a slow automatic as, if you keep the trigger pulled, the gun will continue firing at a rate of about two shots per second.  On the full-auto setting, the rate of fire is surprisingly fast for a toy--about seven or eight rounds per second.  That means you can empty the gun of all 20 \\"micro darts\\" in about three seconds.  It was enough to put a smile on this big kid's face.  I quickly began scouting my house for targets and found a large-screen TV makes a great one as the darts have suction cups on the end and will stick to a smooth, flat surface such as a screen.      Darts are loaded one at a time into their individual launch tubes on the end.  When firing, the end rotates in a circle the way a Gatling gun does.  The gun produces a very audible noise each time it fires and releases pumped up air.  It isn't excessively loud, though, and I actually found it a welcome sound effect that added to the fun of shooting.  In fact, kids could play with this toy without any darts and still have some fun with just the sound it produces (which it does even when no darts are loaded).      Firing straight and level, the darts go about 15 feet before they run out of gas and hit theground.  If you angle them up a little, they'll go about 20 to 25 feet.  The previous reviewer who claimed this has a range of 30 to 40 feet either has an exceptional gun or is just mistaken.  Frankly, I think he's mistaken as the velocity required to launch a dart that far (especially if firing straight and level) might make safety an issue.  As it is, I don't think the darts have enough velocity to do damage if they hit a kid in the eye at close range, but it wouldn't exactly feel good, either.  The darts are made of flexible styrofoam and have soft rubber suction cups on the ends.  I don't see the need for any kind of eye protection with this toy, but I'll still remind my kids not to aim for the face.    Build quality seems fairly sturdy as long as kids don't drop the gun a lot.  If anything were to break, I think it would be the pump, but it should hold up pretty well with normal use.    I'd clasify this as an 'indoor' toy since kids will probably lose the small darts quickly if they shoot them outside.  Even indoors, you'll probably be finding darts in cracks and crevices every time you vacuum.  You can buy bags of 10 darts from Toys R Us, but they're $5 per bag.    Bottom line--I had a lot of fun just testing this thing out by myself.  I'm confident my kids will get a kick out of shooting it out with Dad around the house on Christmas day and for some time to come.

review_headline: Creative design, very fun to play with

PLAY: Very sturdy for \\"swooshing\\" and attacking Jedi and Republic ships alike. The fighter is easily flown through the air with one hand. Construction uses Lego clicking joints, allowing for a uniform, symmetrical shape on all three axes. There are some stickers for this set, but they do add a great deal of detail to the model.

LEARNING: All Lego sets have an advantage over normal toys in that they can be taken apart and built into whatever an imagination can create. Great for building creative skills.

DURABILITY: Very durable - click-joint construction and lightweight frame allow this to be dropped from a considerable height onto carpet without breaking.

Great toy! Very fun to play with an it always attracts people who wonder just what it is.

product_title: Hasbro Twister
review_headline: Twister: The game of adolescent physical contact
review_body:
I find it interesting to see that when you look at the cover of Milton Bradley's \\"Twister\\" today you see four adolescents playing the game: two girls and a very happy looking young boy on the mat, and another young lad holding up the spinner to indicate it is \\"left hand yellow\\" time. On our copy of \\"Twister\\" there are six younger children, again divided equally between girls and boys, with one pair actually playing the game and making their \\"left hand red\\" moves. However, if you go back to the original 1966 version of the game the cover art is of adults playing the game (by adults I mean grown-ups where the men are wearing coats and ties--but no shoes--to play the game). The art actually makes the playing mat look a lot bigger, which makes the two adults cavorting on it look a bit smaller. But while the marketing strategy may have changed over the years, the reason for boys and girls to play this game together has not (think about how many games can be said to require both genders to play it besides this one).

If you look at the game boy it tells you \\"Twister\\" is for ages 6 and up, but I have seen a suggestion that it is \\"intended\\" for ages 6-12. However, the popularity of the game seems to be mainly with college students, who bring a different perspective to the game's objective, which is to \\"Outmaneuver your opponents by placing your hands and feet on the colored circles.\\" The game box contains a spinner, the mat 5-1/2 x 4-1/2 foot vinyl mat marked with colored circles, and the brief rules, which everybody already knows. A referee spins the spinner to come up with which hand or foot has to be placed on the circle of which particular color but there can never be a circle with more than one hand and/or foot on it, which is what makes things interesting. As the game progresses, this becomes much more difficult and bodies become entangled, which we always assumed was the point of the game. If you fall, or if any part of your body besides your hands and feet touch the mat, you are out and the last player literally left \\"standing,\\" so to speak, is the winner.

The idea was that \\"The game that ties you up in knots\\" would be a good ice breaker for parties (keep in mind, the game was created in the 1960s), but it ended up becoming the raison d'etre for such festivities (I am sure many of us have memories of \\"Twister\\" parties way back then) and over 19 million copies of the game have been sold since it came out in 1966 (and sold for $6). The game was part of the golden age of games for Milton Bradley in the Sixties, when the company came up with \\"Life\\" (1960), \\"Stratego\\" (1961), \\"Trouble\\" (1965), \\"Operation\\" (1965), and \\"Battleship\\" (1967). In recent years Milton Bradley has also come out with a \\"Twisted Moves\\" game aimed at ages 8 to adult that gets players following the directions of a pair of recorded DJs on CDs, but that has more to do with dancing. The Guinness World Record for the largest \\"Twister\\" game was set by 4,160 students at the University of Massachusetts on May 2, 1987 and in 1999 \\"Twister\\" received the Dr. Toy Best Classic Toys award.nds and feet touch the mat, you are out and the last player literally left \\"standing,\\" so to speak, is the winner.

review_body: These are great, but they can be brittle, I have had escapees running around before. The common problem with ants dieing off so quick is because you need a queen ant to produce more ants as the others die off. Fortunately ants are very common in my area and i can go for a 5 minute walk and dig up a queen and a good sum of worker ants and just transport them to the ant farm. Its fun to come back day everyday and see what they have done, great value.

product_title: Primary Wood Easel
review_body: Bought this for our almost 2 y/o. While earlier models seemed to have problems with the blackboard surface, this one works very well -- virtually the same as a traditional surface. Best of all, you can wipe it off with a wet paper towel, and voila, new surface. Also, the white board on the back is very effective for drawing with the new washable crayola crayons (the regular ones have to be scraped off with your fingernail, so keep them separate) -- again just wipe with a cloth, and voila, new surface. For now, this is a great arrangement since it means no endless supply of custom paper (our daughter went through one of those expensive floor pads in a week), and she seems pretty happy with chalk and crayons, so no toddler painting mess (yet). Finally, unlike most little tike products, you don't need to hire a general contractor to put it together -- only two screws for the paper holder, and the tray snaps in. I highly recommend spending the extra bucks on this new and improved model.

product_title: Harry Potter Extreme Quidditch Deluxe Action Figure
review_body: I like this figure a lot. It was sculpted realistically and looks just like Harry Potter. It depicts Harry playing his favorite game, quidditch. He has a magnet on his hands to hold the broom, and magnets on his feet to support the weight of the broom, which I rested on his foot, to keep it in place.    He comes with a stand which can be easily assembled. He can then be placed in any number of poses. I put a rubber band around the figure's waist, and anchored it to the top part of the stand behind Harry, to ensure that he stays on it, as he will fall off of it when moved.     I am a middle aged man, and don't play with my Quidditch Harry Figure. I display it on a shelf and it looks great. It ought to provide a lot of fun for children. It looks durable but can break if played with roughly. I also don't feel it is for children under age four, as there may be a choking hazard due to small parts.     The figure looks fun, and is easily the best Quidditch Harry Potter figure I have seen. It can be considered educational, as it would encourage children to read the Harry Potter books.

product_title: Cotton Candy Machine
review_headline: Fun - and it doesn't taste bad, either!
review_body: My girls just got this toy for Christmas (ages 4 and 7) and I was surprised that it really worked!  We've got an Easy Bake Oven and a Jell-O Pudding Pop machine - and neither are as much fun as this \\"kid\\" version of the real thing.  It does take the full 10 minutes to heat up, so next time I'll get it all ready and not even call the girls into the kitchen until it's time to start making the candy.  The refill packets were sold at WalMart right alongside the machine - and they were tasty and contain at least 1/4 cup each of 2 flavors.  No, you don't get a lot for a teaspoon of sugar - but, you know what, I don't want them to eat that much anyway!  It was fun to watch it work, fun to collect it, and we all enjoyed ourselves.  I didn't let the girls eat off of the paper cones so that we might use them more than once.  My only warning would be to clear the table before you use this as, even with the \\"mess guard\\" on, we had sugar all over the table and flecks of cotton candy floating in the air - we had to rescue our fish from the table before the stuff fell into her bowl.  The age guide is appopriate - I wouldn't let a kid much under 10 try to operate this alone, as it does get hot and my 4 year old couldn't understand why - it being all plastic with no visible moving part - that she couldn't put her hand in the bowl to catch the candy as it spun out.

product_title: Sesame Street 35th Anniversary Edition MONOPOLY®
review_headline: WOW! This Edition Is Just Breathtaking!
review_body:
I am a Monopoly and toy collector plus I grew up with Big Bird and the gang. I own many monopoly editions but when I saw this version I was taken away with awe. This edition is plain and simply GOURGEOUS! I could go on and on forever telling you how beautiful and wonderful this Sesame Street Monopoly is but I will just go directly to the description. ENJOY!!!

BOARD: In the center is a beautiful photograph of Big Bird holding the 123 Sesame Street sign, The Count, Grover, Cookie Monster, Oscar, Elmo, Prairie Down, Ernie, Zoe and Bert. And it also has the 35 anniversary logo.

PROPERTIES: Purple: Twiddle Bug Windowbox & Barkley's Doghouse
Light Blue: Sherlock Hemlock's Detective Agency, Martians' Home on Mars & Biff and Sully's Construction Co.
Magenta: Charlie's Restaurant, Sesame Street Library & The Mail-It Shop
Orange: Guy Smiley's Game Show, Mumford's Magic Shop & Super Grover's Phone Booth
Red: The Count's Castle, Bert's Rooftop Pigeon Coop & Ernie's Bathtub
Yellow: Elmo's World, Oscar's Trash Can & Cookie Monster's Bakery
Green: Furry Arms Hotel, Sesame Street Courtyard & Big Bird's Nest
Blue: Hooper's Store & 123 Sesame Street

Each features a beautiful picture of a different Sesame Street character (on the board not the deeds).

RAILROADS: Oscar's Taxi Service, Furry Monster Ferry Line, Bus Stop & Sesame Street Subway

UTILITIES: Oscar's Recycling Center & Sesame Street Fire Department

INCOME TAX: $75 for tickets to Monsterpiece Theater and Buy the letter of the day 10% or $200.

MONEY: $1-Super Grover, $5-Elmo, $10-Bert, $20-Ernie, $50-Cookie Monster, $100-Oscar, $500-Big Bird. Each \\"signed\\" by the featured character.

CHANCE & COMMUNITY CHEST CARDS: Instead of Chance cards you get Block Party which features Zoe and Elmo. And instead of Community Chest you draw from Street Smarts with Little Bird. They all have great color photographs on them which is a treat other monopoly versions skip. Some examples are: Sell Bert your bottle caps collect $10, Win a disco contest with Grover collect $45, and Support your favorite non-profit organization, Sesame Workshop. Contribute $100 to help educate children around the world. Pretty cool, huh?

TOKENS: They are pewter tokens and nicely detailed. You get Big Bird, Bert, Ernie holding his rubber ducky, Oscar in his can, Cookie Monster holding a cookie, and Super Grover with his Super cape. Missing is Elmo which might not be a bad thing for the older fans.

THE BAD: Only six tokens? Why not included a purchase more tokens option like the Simpson's Monopoly has? Also the property deeds are plain unlike the Muppets and Simpson's Editions which have a color watermark silhouette on them (they do have the 123 Sesame Street logo on the back of each though). There are some MIA characters like Don Music and Roosevelt Franklin. But these are minor details that would not hurt an incredibly well done Monopoly Special Edition.

Overall this is one of the best monopoly editions ever made. This will appeal to children, adults and collectors. Educational? You bet. So in conclusion you have to buy this (of two if you are a collector). Have fun playing with your friends and young ones. Bye.

product_title: Diplomacy Board Game
review_headline: Simply the Greatest Board Game of all Time
review_body:
Diplomacy has a storied history. Former President Kennedy and Henry Kissinger are known to have played the game back in their college days. The game itself is in the category of games like Monopoly that have remained unchanged throughout the many years of it's existance. This is in part due both to the complexity and the simplicity of the game.

Diplomacy is a strategic boardgame in the same vein as Risk layout-wise which begins in 1900 Europe. The game can be played by a maximum of 7 players who each represent one of the majors powers before the outbreak of World War I: England, France, Russia, Germany, Austria-Hungary, Turkey and Italy.

Each power begins with relatively few units on the board (3-4 depending on the power) so it is of critical importance what you do with them. There are two types: fleets and armies. Each unit only has a power of 1 so in order to attack another person you need to have secured an ally to aid you in this endeavor. This diplomacy is the basis for the game.

Turns proceed as follows: each turn represents either the fall or spring of a specific year. For a certain length of time there is a diplomatic session. During this time you consult with the other players in an attempt to negotiate the moves of your units. At the end of time each person writes down the moves for their units and then play occurs simultaneously.

Either organized chaos or finely tuned play proceeds. This game relies totally upon your ability to be able to work within the various plans of your allies and enemies, to be able to recognize when to ally with certain people and to be able to recognize when that alliance is no longer needed. Backstabbing is common. This is definitely not a game you can take personally.

I have found the greatest joy of this game to be in the sheer negotiations. DMZ's crop up all over the board as powers discuss how they will aid and destroy each other. In the space of 20 minutes youcan discuss 5 different plans with 5 different people, but only upon revealing the moves will the trust come out: who is with you and who is against you.

To put it plainly: it is the best board game I have ever played and I highly recommend it.

review_headline: Teaches logic, strategy, while fun for child and adults.
review_body: My 5 year old daughter received this for Christmas.  I consider it the best gift out of my kids' extensive loot.  It is educational, but not boring for adults to play. You match the cards (pictures of animals) you have in hand with the pictures on the board to determine where you can lay down a chip.  The unicorn and dragon cards lend some additional imagination by allowing a chip placed anywhere and allowing removal of any chip on the board, respectively. I highly recommend this game.

product_title: Beyblade American G Revolution Hard Metal System Thunder Serpent Ma-20
review_headline: Besides the Attack Ring, this Beyblade is a must have!
review_body: Originaly on the Japanese model, Thunder Dragon made sparks when it's Attack Ring made contact. Hasbro's release of Thunder Serpant had this gimmick removed due to safety reasons. This Attack Ring is almost useless for battle, but atleast it looks  cool. The Weight Disk, Free Survivor, is VERY useful, as it is made to block \\"Upper Attack\\". Upper Attack is when a Beyblade with a sloped Attack Ring lifts the oppenent, e.g. Dark Effigy MS(Right Spin), Dranzer MS(Left Spin). This is a HUGE advantage to be able to defend against this, as Upper Attack is among the most deadly types of attacks in Beyblade. Just make sure and use a fairly tall Running Core to take full advantage of this. The Running core is Metal Weight Flat Core, it's almost identical to Strata Dragoon MS. The only difference is that it has a metal wieght in the center and is slightly bigger, it's generally considered better than Strata's Flat Core. Uncustomized this Beyblade is poor, but with the right costomizations it really shines. Get this if you have other HMS Blades to customize with.

product_title: SnugRide Infant Car Seat - Colby
review_body:
I also wanted to rebuff some of the posted criticsms of this car seat. First, I am a first time mom and my son is now 4-months old. We love this car seat! It is so, so easy to snap in-and-out of the car. DS sits very comfortably in it. It's got a 5-point harness, so I always feel he is as secure as can be. The straps are super easy to adjust, too.

Most car seats are unweildy to carry. Not just weight-wise, but awkward. This one is no more difficult than others. The car seat is designed to protect your child in a crash, not to be toted around for hours. I make a point of having either my stroller (which the seat snaps into) or my DH handy if I think I am going on a marathon venture.

I have no trouble snapping the seat into standard shopping carts. And it does fit onto restaurant highchairs. If the establishment has the \\"standard issue\\" wooden highchair (base has four-rungs and looks like an open square) that we see everywhere, you just have to flip the highchair upside down. A waiter showed us that! The seat snaps right in! :-)

No item is perfect. There are some tweaks I would make, but overall this is a really great car seat!

product_title: In Flight 4 Piece Crib Set
review_body: I received this bedding as a gift and I am so excited to put the entire bedroom together!!  The bedding is of great quality and will last a long time.  Great, great bedding!!!

product_title: Decipher - Megaman Power up Starter Torchman
review_body: Before they made these Nt warrior PET (Personal Terminal) Now they are making New Video games and New PET's. Capcom is on fire! the manafactuarers are really knowing which companys to help with! The card games rock and the PETS rock

product_title: Knitting Machine
review_headline: Not as durable as the original, but still love it :o)
review_body: My mother had the original 1974 Mattel Knitting Machine which I LOVED and I decided to purchase this brand/model. It is okay, not bad, but not great and you need an abundance of patience to get a project to run smoothly, because the hook system has a tendency to snag then drop stitches if you crank too fast or there is too much tension.. Still, I remember making piles of knitting back when I was a kid on Mom's machine... this brought back great memories, so I believe everyone should have one of these or have the opportunity to knit on one. Definitely have an extra supply of regular 3-ply yarn on hand and be prepared to work slowly and patiently when you use the included eyelash yarn, but knit away to your heart's content... I just made a cute striped scarf for my cat, and my husband is going to give it a try when he gets home from work tomorrow. Happy Holidays!

product_title: Fisher-Price Incrediblock Activity Center
review_body: I bought this for my 10 month old son, and he did not play with it.  He held the blocks, and then would turn to his Leap Frog Learning Table for more fun.  I returned the Incrediblock and purchased the Laugh and Learn Learning Home for $10.00 more.  He loves the Learning Home, and he plays with it non-stop.  The peek a blocks were cool, but the Incrediblock was just not fun.  The sound was not loud enough and the motor on top was too loud.  It was just boring!

product_title: Fisher Price Learning Home (Discontinued by manufacturer)
review_body: My daugter got this for her first birthday.  At first she didn't plat with it much.  Just went in and out the door but now at 18 months her and my three year old neice love it.  They play with it for hours.  It can stand up to alot of abuse.  I haven't had to replace the batteries yet and nothing has fallen apart.  My husband and I even enjoy the songs it plays.  Very much worth the money.  I am very very happy with this toy.

product_title: TeenTech Portable Color DVD/CD Player (Charcoal/Silver)
review_body: The TeenTech Portable is not worth IT.  Very heavy, doesn't hold a charge, very small screen.  Stopped working after only using it 3 times.  Don't bother with the company, I just brought mine make to Toys R Us and received a full credit!

product_title: Fisher Price Learning Home (Discontinued by manufacturer)
review_headline: Pure Delight for both Child and you!
review_body: This is just a grand toy. I have not seen anything else that comes close! It does everything! My daughter's attention was kept for and entire hour without interruption while she played and explored all the countless things it does. I purchased it when she was 7 months old. Now at 10 months, she enjoyes it even more as her motor skills sharpen and she begins to understand how everything functions. It is so exciting for her to press the door bell or open the mail I left for her from the other side and dance everytime a song comes plays (which are just the cutest songs!). Love this toy. Every one should have one!  Ok, I have had a problem tho, it was with the numbers on the top of the \\"outside\\" of the house, the number 8 would always chime \\"number 9\\" incorrectly. The manual says that this may happen if the batteries are dying but this happened shortly after putting it together. It corrected itself and was fine for a while but recently began again. It so far has only happened with the number 8 and nothing else.

product_title: Hedstrom Scooby-Doo Hopper
review_headline: FURTHER INSTRUCTIONS You Need to Know to Use This Toy!
review_body:
First: the adapter included with this ball does NOT fit flush into the valve to assist in pumping it up. Throw it away.

If you have a foot pump or hand pump that came with a cone-shaped adapter, that is the one to use. It works just fine. If you don't already have one, you will have to go somewhere (like an auto parts store) and specifically get a manual pump with this adapter.

Second: the plug provided to shove in the valve after the ball is inflated does NOT prevent air from escaping. Blow this thing up and the next morning, it will be 3/4 empty. Get an assortment of O-rings before you do this job, find the appropriate size and slide it onto the plug, all the way to the head. This will work just fine.

product_title: Playmobil Super Set Farm
review_body:
With this little farming set a kid can learn to \\"prepare the land\\" for planting and that plants need to be watered and protected, and how wild animals can help farmers. There are a myriad of pests for your garden: ducks that eat your seeds, goats that eat everything, bunnies that sneak in, a big field mouse that comes to chomp at your veggies... And natural pest control for the little pests, since the eagle looks hungrily at the small bunnies, duckies, and large mouse. The two-piece green crops allow the plant to look like a small plant, then a large plant which you can harvest from but leave in the ground, teaching that sometimes you can take only what you need. The rest of the tools and landscape are equally versatile and can provide endless fun, I've seen it first hand as the six-year-old owner of this set insists on playing with me.

If really small parts are a concern you might want to glue them in place. Any five-year-old should know not to pick the flowers from the plants and stick them anywhere awkward.

product_title: FlyWheel 19' Budnik Sphere XX Wheel Green Handle
review_headline: How the hell does it work?
review_body: No instructions, tons of little philips screws to unscrew, and we can't get it to stay on the launcher. A huge dud.

product_title: Magnetix 70-pc. Translucent Set-Ages 6+
review_body: Okay, tried this out with a five and seven year old.  Both of them tired of it within fifteen minutes.  I mean, how many \\"snowflakes\\" can a person make?

product_title: Ms. Pac-Man Plug-and-Play
review_headline: Great arcade games and improvement over the first Ms. Pac-Man Plug-N-Play
review_body:
This joystick system is much better than the first 5-in-1 Ms. Pac-Man joystick system for two reasons: 1) The control is much better and 2) it saves your high scores.

Ms. Pac-Man almost identical to the arcade version, is is more challenging than many of the \\"late-model\\" Ms. Pac-Man's with a super-fast Ms. Pac-Man and slower ghosts. The previous 5-in-1 model of this joystick had serious control problems, and it was at times almost impossible to play Ms. Pac-Man because of the controller. Namco has improved the joystick's responsiveness so that it does what you tell it to. Although I still noticed some problem with it turning DOWN unexpectedly, it's a vast improvement.

Galaga is fantasic and is easier to play on the new base. Also, Namco added memory to the game so that it will save your high scores for posterity, which was one of the drawbacks of the 5-in-1 system.

As for the other games: Pole Position plays just like the original arcade game but is not as fun as other, newer racing games; Xevious is fun for five minutes but that's about it; and Bosconian and Mappy aren't worth playing (does anyone even remember these in the arcade?). If this joystick had Dig-Dug (as the Pac-Man controller does) it would be perfect.

This is a great game for anyone who grew up a fan of these games, and it's also great for younger kids who can appreciate the simplicity and ease-of-control of the \\"classics.\\" My 5 year-old nephew loves this as well.

product_title: Megaland
review_headline: Good but not durable enough for outside
review_body: This is a very fun product for kids. The tunnels and ball pit are great. However, I really do not see how this can be easily used outdoors as it is not sturdy enough to stand on its own if there is wind etc.

product_title: Learning Resources Gears! Gears! Gears! Dizzy Fun Land Motorized Gears Set
review_headline: Looks great, but doesn't work great!
review_body: My son got this for his 4th birthday.  While the pieces snap together fairly easily, it is complicated - no way a 4 yr. old could do it.  Even following the instructions step-by-step, I found the process confusing and time-consuming.  Once I got it put together, it was fine as long as no one touched it or turned the motor on.  It is not the most stable toy when assembled, so it seems to fall apart easily - at which point, it wasn't always immediately obvious how to put it back together without consulting the directions.  When the motor is running, it's worse.  The horses on the carousel are supposed to go up and down.  In our case, just one horse not working properly causes the whole system to break apart - the gears jam and the pieces start to topple over - the carousel pops out of place, bringing the ferris wheel and roller coaster with it.  I was shocked to see how expensive this item was - especially after the 1st few catastrophes the 1st week, my son rarely plays with it now.  Definitely not worth it!  The gear thing is cool, physics-wise, but I'm sticking with the simpler horizontal versions!

product_title: Fisher-Price Deluxe Jumperoo
review_body: My daughter started out big when she was born so she was able to start using this at 4 months old. She loved it and did very well in it. At 10 months old now she is finally to the point where now that she knows she can crawl around on her own its not as exciting for her anymore. She tried out an exersaucer at a friends house but she sat so high up in it that she flopped forward. In the Jumperoo it sits nice and deep to support her really well. You will love this thing.

product_title: Baby Annabell Function Doll
review_body: My three year old daughter asked for this for Christmas.  I thought the price was high for a doll for this age of a child but she really wanted it so we bought it.  It was a little heavy but I expected that because of another review I read. She does everything they say she does but I do have a hard time getting her to cry tears.  She has to cry atleast four times and then only one of her eyes would even cry. My daughter doesn't seem to mind but I am alittle disappointed.  She was so happy to get her that it was worth the money.

product_title: Fisher-Price Pop-Onz Pop 'N Twirl Table Building System
review_body: My son is 15 months old and received this toy for Christmas and the only thing that I do not like about it is that the legs keep falling off. I keep snapping them on and a little bit later they come off. He absolutely loves to play with the table though. He also got the farm set and the table has room enough to store all the pop on pieces. I love this toy for him!

product_title: Clue® Jr. Game by Parker Brothers
review_body: Finally I found a Clue Junior version that has the original Clue atmosphere! This version comes with the famous Clue suspects and a classic looking board with differnt rooms. It's the perfect game to get my five year old daughter ready for the original Clue that she is so curious about.

product_title: InteracTV DVD System Compilation In-Pack
review_body:
Don't waste your money, I bought this item 3 weeks ago, I wished I'd tested it then instead of waiting on Christmas. It took me 3 hours to try and program it on my Philips DVD player and no matter how many attempts I could not get the button in the A position to work (all others did) until I went to the web site and found out that my DVD wasn't compatible with the system.What a big \\"oops\\" for Fisher Price and a sad disappointment to one lil 3 year old!

They had good intentions, but they sure didn't get the item tested before it was marketed!

product_title: LeapFrog Learning Table
review_body: My daughter got this for Christmas last year when she was only seven months old.  At the time she was too young for it.  But as she started pulling herself up to things she loved it.  It's nice and stable for a baby to pull up to, and she figured out how to make all the noizes very easily.  She is now 18 months old and still loves to bang on the keys and make it play music.  She has gotten hours of entertainment from this toy.  I definatley reccomend it.

product_title: Bulls-Eye Ball
review_headline: Awesome Toy for the entire family
review_body: My son just got this from his cousins for an early Christmas present.  I am online ordering another one because all of us in our family of 5 can't take our hands off of it.  High score so far is 92 but the competition is thick!  We as parents are hooked.  The kids are 14, 7 and 5 and everyone of us is having a great time with this.  You will love it.  I recommend having 2 run at the same time if you really want some fun.  We have had it playing alot and batteries are still strong and going.  There is a volume control for 2 settings and a silence mode if it gets too loud.  Watch out, you will be hooked in your firsht 5 minutes.  This was the hit at our Thanksgiving Table.

product_title: Deluxe Astro Megazord
review_body: I HATE THIS TOY SO MUCH BECAUSE I BOUGHT IT FOR A LOT OF MONEY AND TEH FIRST TIME I PUT IT TOGETHER IT BROKE IN HALF

product_title: Megaland
review_body: My two boys love the Mega Land Play tent,it provides great exploration for a good hide and seak game. It set's up very easy, and folds up into it's case, so we can bring it to grandmas, and on vacations! The Mega Land Play Tent does take up some room, so make sure you have plenty of space, or you could even make two tents out of the one. I recommend purchasing extra play balls, the ones it comes with are pretty small.But our family loves Mega Land.

product_title: Ocean Wonders Aquarium
review_body: I can't say enough good things about this product.  Our infant loves it, and even we adults find the music very soothing (despite LOTS of repeat listening).  Overall an excellent investment!

product_title: Triumph DLX Convertible Car Seat in Marimba Print
review_body:
We purchased the Evenflo Triumph DLX for our 9 month old daughter on Wed. Today, Sat, I am ready to throw the thing out the window! I can't get the release knob to move no matter what I do. I don't know if I'm doing something wrong, but I practically break my thumb trying to get the stupid thing to move. I could feel the vertebrae in my back moving, I was exerting that much pressure on the knob.

The seat is fine otherwise. It fits great in our 2005 Honda Odyssey, our daughter seems to enjoy sitting & driving in it, but I have such a difficult time getting her out.

I'll be emailing Evenflo as well to see how to fix this problem, but am seriously considering returning this seat & buying the Britax. It's not worth the aggravation & time that I've already wasted trying to get my poor baby out of the car!

product_title: LEGO Creator: Large Bucket
review_body: The grandkids love it!

product_title: Bratz: Winter Wonderland Dana
review_body: This is probubly my favorite Bratz doll i own. Her hair is silky smooth with two small braids. She comes with tons of winter accessories! Some of the accessories that you have to make sure you don't loose because they are so small are the hot chocolate, the cell phone and the lip balm. She comes with two winter jackets,a pair of ski googles,two pairs of boots (one pair is lighter than the other)a sled,and so much more! Her lip gloss and eye shadow is sparkly and so are her legs! If you kind of make a mini hill out of pillows you can put Dana on the sled and she'll actually slide down!! Anyways, this is a really cool doll that is definetly worth buying!

product_title: Scene It Dvd Game
review_headline: 1 Time Fun, 2nd time is a bore
review_body: The first time my friends and I played this game we were crying for more.  We played again a few nights later and it was basically the same game over again.  There's only like 7 different movie clips on the DVD, each with several questions based off of it.  I'd rent the game if I could but I wouldn't buy it.

product_title: Remote Control Land and Sea Hover-craft
review_body: This toy is not a true hovercraft.  It is an RC toy that looks like a hovercraft but does not move by fans.  It has a very small drive wheel at the bottom that moves the toy like a regular RC car and a prop on the drive wheel shaft that can move the toy in water.  It does not move by forced air as a true hovercraft does.  The manufacturer is very misleading in the way it describes the toy on the package.  The toy moves ridiculously slow on a flat surface or in the water.  It will not move on anything that is even close to being a rough surface.  A true ripoff!

product_title: Banzai Wild Waves Water Park (Discontinued by manufacturer)
review_body: I should have listened to others...the pool does not hold air.  The slide only held air the first time we used it and now it is worthless.  The portion that has the basketball net does not stand up...so it is useless as well.  My advice would be to find something else.

product_title: In Flight Decorative Pillow
review_body: I love these pillows (have one just like it for our daughter's bedding set).  They are the perfect little accent to throw in the corner of the crib or in the glider.  They also make a great toss pillow for a toddler bed.

product_title: Playskool Step Start Walk 'n Ride
review_body: I am very impressed with this toy, especially how durable it is and that it doesn't topple over when my son tries to pull up on it.  I like how versitile it is and feel it far surpasses the other models out there by fisher price and what not.  I am normally a big fisher price fan but this toy got me to take a closer looke at playskool toys!  Very nice toy, helping my son learn to walk and he gets a big kick out of pushing it around.

product_title: Little Mommy High Chair
review_body: It broke the first day we had it. Daddy broke it while putting it together! The whole thing is cheaply made.

product_title: Fisher Price Kick & Crawl Aquarium
review_body: My son has loved this playmat - from 4 weeks to 4 months I have used this almost every day. It's a great price and really worth the money. He loves to kick the ball and spin the octopus to make it sing. It's fun as well as good exercise for him and keeps him content for quite a while. The mat is easy to clean also.

product_title: MGA Little Tikes Wide Tracker Activity Walker
review_body: I bought this for my son when he was learning to walk, mainly becaue it had the wheel speed control. I had a walker but it was hard for him to keep up with. Like most of the other reviewers have said the doors come off way to easy. That has been the only problem I've had with it. The speed adjustment was great when he was first starting out, he wasn't falling flat on his face like with the original walker I had. It also worked great outside in the grass unlike the other walker . My son has loved the walker from day one and and even though he's walking on his own now he still plays with it...  to chase the dog!

product_title: LeapFrog Fridge Words Magnetic Word Builder
review_body: I bought this for my 4 yr old daughter who had seen the 3 letter factory/talking words DVDs.  She enjoys making up words and having them read back to her.  Much more fun than regular magnetic letters!  Even my 12 month old is trying to fit the letters into the spaces.  An easy to use product with the usual helpful advice common to all LeapFrog products.  Battery life seems OK and the product sticks firmly to the refrigerator.

product_title: My First LeapPad Book: Dr. Seuss's There's a Wocket in My Pocket
review_body: I just bought the My First Leap Pad Bus for my 28 month old.  She wasn't very interested in it at first and I thought I'd just wasted $25...... until we got \\"There's a Wocket in My Pocket\\" to go with it.   She enjoys the story  and touching the different Seuss creatures with the magic pen to hear their silly comments (we especially love the jertain in the curtain page).  It's a great book and has encouraged my daughter to give some of the other My First Leap Pad books a chance.

product_title: Gundam RX-78 GP02A E.F.S.F. Prototype Tactical Mobile Suit: Skill Level 8
review_body: This is a great model.  Its very detailed and is a blast to assemble.  Out of the box expect 3-6 hours for the average builder.  There are very few parts that require painting to make look original.  As is from Bandai this is a great model.  only downside to it is that the large boozoka wielding shield is to large for the arm to support by itself.  You can get it to rest on the leg but it doesnt rest very well.  Overall I highly recomend the purchase of this model to add to your collection.  For the price its done nicely.

product_title: Fisher-Price Deluxe Jumperoo
review_body: I love this little jumperoo.  I am a first time parent so I am very picky about what I get my daugher.  Me and my daughter went to babies r us and I \\"test drove\\"  several saucers and swings with her.  She fell in love with this one and I did too, it has just enough little gadgets on it so that she doesn't have a stimulant overload like with the exersaucer she didn't know what to do it had way too many toys this one has a few and she can zero in on specific ones, I love that it bounces, she laughs and laughs because now mommy doesn't have to be the jumperoo for her she had her own little holder, which is great for me because she is getting heavier, and when she bounces and the music comes on she gets so excited, this is the greatest piece of entertainment that I have gotten her to date, I love fisher-price.

product_title: Singin' Surprise Strawberry Shortcake with Interactive "My Rememberin' Book"
review_body: My 3 year old daughter got this doll as a Chirstmas present.  It has not worked correctly since the first day.  I would not recommed this for anyone.  Every time she tries to use the doll with the book I just get frustrated and tell her to just play pretend with the doll.  The doll it's self is very cute.  It is a shame that the technology is so poor.

product_title: 60-Sec Anti-Skip Personal Cd Player: Pink
review_body: I bought this for my daughter's 6th birthday.  We have had this CD player for less than 6 months.  She loved it at first.  Now it has stopped working.  I was never dropped or anything like that.  We tried changing batteries so many times, but to no avail.  It does not work anymore...how disappointing!

product_title: Cabbage Patch Kids Wooden 3 Piece Table & Chair Set
review_body: We bought this set for my daughter who is two and she loves it. It is the perfect size and looks much more appealing that the Little Tikes plastic table sets for the same price. My only disagreement with the manufacturer, they rate the table for ages 5 and up and I believe that is a little old for this set as the chairs most likely would not support the weight of a child that large as my six year old niece barely fits with this set, I think it is better suited for small children around 2-4 years.

product_title: Little Tikes Discover Sounds Workshop
review_body: My first son recieved this for a gift when he was 7 mos old. Loved to sit in front of it and play with all the things, especially the balls, dropping them in and pulling the lever. As he got older he really liked to use the hammer and the phone, he likes to pretend. Then my second son was born (they are 15 mos apart) and he loves it too. He likes the door: dropping things in the top then opening the door and finding them inside.(he's now 13 mos) This toy has lasted through 2 rough boys and is still played with!

product_title: Barbie as BatGirl: 11.5" Collectible Doll with Stand and Character Logo from DC Comics Super Friends
review_body: It is about time Mattel started to use there brains and release Barbie as Super-Friends.  Just like to old Super-Queens and the Mego dolls, now girls and collectors have something very different to add to there pink boxes.  I am glad to add Wonder Woman, Batgirl, Supergirl, Catwoman (not too sure about the Halle version) and now Poison Ivy to my collection.  Now if Mattel would expand the set with Vixen, Onyx, Mera, Black Canary, Zatanna, Huntress, Harley Quinn, Cheetah, and Hawkgirl.

product_title: Thomas & Friends Wooden Railway - Butch the Tow Truck
review_body: Skyler loves Butch.  Whenever a train derails we get Butch to \\"save\\" him.  Very cute piece.  Pulls trains and cars with his magnetic tow.

product_title: Ocean Wonders Aquarium Bouncer
review_headline: A lifesaver for a new mother
review_body:
Ever since the day she came home from the hospital, my daughter has used this bouncer. It has been a lifesaver for me because
she could sleep in it for hours while I did other things and I could still watch her. She loved the starfish and used the chair everyday for the first 6 months of her life!! I am now going to pass it on to my sister in law who is due next month. This product is wonderful and extremely well made. It is truly a life saver!!

product_title: FLY 1.0 Pentop Computer
review_body: yes the fly pen seems very cool. but i think it might cost a lot more than people think after you get all of the things that you have to have with it. like a recharger, expansion packs, and then all of the software that you have to have to play games and homework help. those are all seperate things. so i dont know.. it seems cool but i wonder if it might be a rip off.

product_title: Toy Story: Remote Control Racing R/C with Buzz and Woody
review_headline: Car doesnt work once in awhile it might move
review_body: total piece of junk controls don't work when they do only one rear tire works and it won't turn never buy again from amazon

product_title: Clown Bean Bag Game
review_body: This is a cheap toy that won't last long. The part with the holes and clown on it is just a peice of cardboard that is stapled to the frame. Several of the staples didn't even make it in to the wood, they missed because the frame is bigger than the cardboard. The ones that were barely holding came out after the kids played with it a couple times because when the bags hit the cardboard they push the staples out - duh. The bean bags are akwardly shaped and really don't fit through the holes very well. My 4 year old was frustrated that he couldn't get them through the holes, when I tried it, I had a hard time as well. Might be good for a one-time kids party but won't last much longer. My Kids are 2 and 4. My neighbor has the target toss which is made of netting and it is way way better - should've spen the extra cash.

product_title: Air Hogs Radio Control Defender Airplane: Red (27 MHz)
review_headline: Trash, rubbish and a piece of junk
review_body: I bought this for my son as it seemed like a reasonable buy at Toys R Us. But every penny spent on this was wasted.    The first problem you will encounter is recharging the plane itself. We were able to charge it one time, and after that no more. To charge it, you have to hold the plane firmly against a charging point on the remote while holding a button on the remote depressed.    When we attempted to fly it the first time, the wing broke. While the box states that the plane is made of \\"High-density ESP Foam,\\" it is very flimsy, and just putting it back in the box caused another part of the plane to crack.    Don't make our mistake. Save your money.

product_title: Fisher-Price Learning Patterns Rocker
review_headline: Great until baby learns how to rock him/herself
review_body: I loved this chair for my son.  It was wonderful!!!  However as soon as he learned how to rock himself back and forth, he rocked himself so hard that he fell forward.  Now the only time I can put him in it is with the kickstand out.  I really don't like the fact that he has no choice but to stay still now.  I would say that this rocker should be until they are about 6 months old.

product_title: Tamagotchi Connection DNU Use 140136Asst1
review_headline: Tamagotchi Has Returned and Won't Be Forgotten!
review_body:
Tamagotchi is a VERY fun toy. I gave a five on the 'How Much fun is this toy' Why? Because it is fun! You start out with an egg which hatches into Babytchi male or female. (After you set the time and date and stuff) Then you get to name it! Mine was named Nino, the Spanish word for boy.

Tamagotchi's are just so cute! You can play games with them, feed them, and they even preform secret actions! (For example, My brother's Tamagotchi, Twink, spits water. I still think that's hilarious!)You can also connect with friends and play games and exchange presents using infrared technology! This toy is educational becuase you have to take care of it!

You have to feed it, play with it and more, just like a pet! Plus, you have to keep it happy! This toy is pretty durable in my opinion.

I have dropped it twice (On a very hard wood floor)and it plays just like normal! I believe that this toy comes at a great price for all the fun it delivers. But it may not be a good idea for this to be the on the top present on a younger child's wishlist. Because they may find it- A: Boring and not 'interactive' enough, or B: Hard to take care of.

I reccomend this toy for ages 9 and up. Younger children may become too upset when their Tamagotchi 'dies/goes back to Planet Tamagotchi' But, all in all, this toy is great fun, and it HIGHLY reccomend it!

product_title: Jardine Madison Lifetime Convertible Crib - Cherry
review_body:
I picked this crib for my daughter due to the solid back design and beautiful sleigh features. It's very sturdy and converts to a daybed then to a full size bed. All my baby furniture came without any damage or working issues.

I actually saw the crib in the store and realized that the side does NOT come down. So, if this is a feature you are looking for- do no buy this crib.
I am 5'5 and the crib is currently on it's lowest setting. My daughter is 16mos old and I have, nor ever had any problems putting my daughter to bed.

Also, as a baby she had a mobile ON her crib. Symphony in motion by Tiny Love. It plays classical music and has zoo animals that spin around.

I didnt plan on using a bumper, as most doctors recommend not using one. But I've read that velcro can take care of the problem.

I gave it 4 stars b/c there is not a guard made for the rail, which is very thick, to prevent your baby from teething on it!

Overall, I think if you realize what your buying- it's a very good crib.

product_title: DuoGlider Stroller - Clover
review_body: This is a great stroller for the parents of either twins or 2 young children. product_title: Axis & Allies Board Game, 2004 Revised Edition
review_headline: Reminds me of "Risk" set during World War II
review_body:
I just recently pulled out this old classic for the first time in quite a while. My eight-year-old son seems to be developing an affinity for strategy games, so I thought he'd like this one. He did, and I was amazed to find that the rules were simple enough for a kid his age to grasp quickly.

My son's first exposure to strategy gaming was \\"Risk\\", and as I played \\"Axis & Allies\\" with him I realized how similar the two games are in their basic format. Both involve efforts of two or more players to conquer the world by developing and maneuvering their armies, and defeating their opponents' armies in dice-driven combat. The maps are not terribly different in their appearance and function, although the \\"Axis & Allies\\" map includes neutral territories, sea zones and islands, and also makes use of the Panama and Suez Canals.

Unlike \\"Risk\\", where all units are the same and all territories count the same for purposes of army development, \\"Axis & Allies\\" adds an economic element to the game. In this game, each player must purchase his units, which are varied in their function, combat abilities, movement ability, and cost. For example, tanks and infantry are cheap but limited to ground use. They depend on transports if they need to move over water. Battleships are quite powerful on the sea and can be used to support an amphibious invasion, but are the most expensive unit in your arsenal. Submarines can sneak attack and then withdraw unharmed. And aircraft can add great versatility to your strategic planning, but are relatively expensive and cannot be used to capture territory without the aid of ground troops. These are just a few of the rules you'll have to consider as you decide what types of units to develop.

In other words, an additional layer of realism is added to the basic \\"Risk\\" combat model, depending on the types of units involved. Armies are still developed based on the amount of territory controlled, as in \\"Risk\\", but with a different twist. Each territory has a certain economic value to the player controlling it, which in turn determines that player's capacity to purchase new units -- to be placed only where the player has an industrial complex. Thus, the player is forced to consider economics and competing production priorities in allocating his finite resources to develop his forces -- an element that is completely absent in \\"Risk\\".

Just a few practical notes, as a wargamer of many years, I can't say the excitement level of this one is particularly high, but it can be if your opponent really knows what he's doing. There is a bit of a pro-Allied bias to the game, so the stronger player should take the Axis. Also, the Russians tend to get knocked out of the game pretty quickly -- they get squeezed between the Germans and Japs. The United States starts the game as an economic powerhouse, and if this is handled well it can usually be exploited with great success by the Allied player. Overall, I'm pretty pleased with this game, especially the fact that I can play it with my young son.but with a different twist. product_title: Fisher Price Loving Family Twin Time Dollhouse with Exclusive Bonus Accessories
review_body:
My girls (4, 2) LOVE this dollhouse. For me, it was a nice compromise between pricier (and more fragile) wooden dollhouses and the smaller plastic ones in the store. We also considered the Sweet Sounds one ONLY for its room size, but decided against it since I want my girls to make up their OWN dialogue and use their OWN imaginations. I know we could've turned the sound off... but the Twin Time dollhouse was MUCH more charming in style anyway. REAL curtains in one room, a cushiony window seat, flowers in flower boxes, cloth awnings on the windows... balconies... it goes on and one. The rooms size isn't a problem anyway... just don't go overboard with furniture. Of course, that wasn't hard to do this past Chrimstas.

I was quite dissappointed that Fisher Price made it VERY DIFFICULT to outfit this dollhouse through holidays. I know there's a higher demand for toys then, but they should have anticipated the demand and kept the toy stores WELL STOCKED! I was fortunate to start my \\"quest\\" in EARLY December. I was able to get the dollhouse and SUV from TRU but the furniture was practically non-existent (around 12/1/05). I had to call Fisher Price themselves and get the kitchen ($15 shipped)... WalMart had the laundry room, kid's room and bathroom - only because a nice stock boy went to the very \\"back\\" to get them (priced $8 each)... and Ebay had the campsite, family room, parent's bedroom and dining room (got last years model that sits 4 people and plays music). All for reasonable prices on ebay. But that was EARLLY December. I felt soooo sorry for the people who didn't buy until mid-late December. Some of the furniture sets were going upwards of $40 for just ONE room! RIDICULOUS!

Fisher Price could have solved this crisis if they would have just STOCKED THE STORES or enabled parents to purchase all the furniture from Fisher Price themselves (they only sold maybe 3 different sets - THAT'S IT).

In the end, the chaos was worth it...my kids LOVE this dollhouse. It stays set up in our play room... even the neighbors love it.

A+ Fisher Price for putting together a wonderful product.
D- for not making the furniture available for parents around Christmas time.
